items.title: Vision-Language Model-Based System for Automated and Proactive Construction Fence Management to Enhance Severe Weather Preparedness
items.abstract: Construction fences can become unstable during high-wind events, particularly when attached objects such as signage, banners, or shade cloths increase the surface area exposed to wind. However, current inspection and preparedness practices often rely on manual observation, limited time and labor, and practitioners’ field experience, making it difficult to quickly assess fence stability and determine appropriate preparedness actions before high-wind events. To address this challenge, this study developed a vision-language model-based system that integrates prompt-based information extraction, computer vision-based fence condition assessment, engineering-based stability analysis, and large language model-based practical guideline generation. The system extracts key variables from user input, identifies fence panels and attached objects using instance segmentation, estimates wind-exposed surface areas, performs engineering-based stability analysis, and generates practical guidelines based on the stability analysis results. Technical evaluation showed that the instance segmentation model achieved an overall mAP50 of 0.866 in detecting fence-related objects. For practical guideline generation, the Construction Material and Incomplete and Temporary Structure 3-30E model with a temperature of 0.5 and top-p of 0.7 achieved the highest bidirectional encoder representations from transformers score F1 value of 0.853 among the tested configurations. In addition, a practitioner-based evaluation was conducted to examine the practical value of the proposed system from the perspective of potential users. The results indicated positive perceptions, particularly for practical guideline generation, system usefulness, and future adoption intention. This study contributes to automated inspection and proactive construction site management for severe weather preparedness by demonstrating how image-based condition assessment, engineering-informed stability evaluation, and natural-language decision support can be integrated into an artificial intelligence–based decision-support tool.

items.title: MAESTRO: Fine-Tuned Multiagent Large Action Model-Based GenAI Assistant Integrating IoT Sensing, Smart Control, and Extended Reality for Human-Building Interaction
items.abstract: There has been recent interest in smart human–building interaction (HBI) interfaces to improve how occupants interact with building systems. Intelligent facility management (FM) utilizes HBI principles to transform static infrastructures into dynamic, human-centric environments, where facility managers need to interpret live Internet-of-things (IoT) sensor data, consult procedures, and execute safe control actions for various building systems. These tasks are fragmented across dashboards, manuals, and control panels, increasing cognitive load and slowing down decision-making. To address these challenges, this study proposes the multiagent extended-reality and sensing-aware task-level reasoning orchestrator (MAESTRO). MAESTRO is a multimodal agentic GenAI assistant comprised of four agents that support procedural queries, telemetry interpretation, and supervised device actuation in a single HBI loop. MAESTRO integrates a large action model (LAM)-based system with retrieval-augmented reasoning interfaced in an extended reality (XR) environment and mediated by a Model Context Protocol. It uses an orchestrator, which is the coordination component that interprets each user request and decides which agent capability should handle the request, while enforcing supervised and schema validated execution for sensing and actuation. The orchestrator routes each request to the appropriate agents including a domain-adapted FM language agent trained on manuals, logs, and work orders; an IoT control agent that generates schema validated tool calls to sensors and actuators; and a vision language agent for image-based queries. MAESTRO was evaluated on various HBI testing scenarios covering safety inspection, system control, troubleshooting, and procedural guidance. The results show improved language modeling and answer quality after adaptation, a valid tool-call rate of 91%, device-execution success of 89%, telemetry match rate of 81%, and an overall end-to-end task success rate exceeding 84%. This paper shows the potential of integrating fine-tuned LAM-based agents with structured IoT-enabled middleware and XR-based HBI systems, demonstrating how foundation-model reasoning and actuation can support more intelligent and adaptive HBI workflows.
items.venue: Journal of computing in civil engineering

items.title: Few-shot semantic segmentation of UAV imagery for plant conservation: A systematic comparison of foundation models for Euphorbia resinifera mapping
items.abstract: Deep learning has transformed vegetation mapping from UAV imagery, yet state-of-the-art segmentation models require hundreds to thousands of expertly annotated images, creating prohibitive labor costs for conservation applications targeting endangered flora. This study addresses this bottleneck by systematically comparing three foundation models namely: DINOv2 (self-supervised), SegGPT (supervised), and SAM (promptable), for binary segmentation of Euphorbia resinifera, an endemic Moroccan succulent of conservation concern, using patches extracted from a single annotated UAV orthomosaic. A single-image training framework is presented where spatial diversity within one high-resolution orthomosaic substitutes for diversity across multiple images, combined with sliding window inference with vote-based fusion for full-resolution deployment. SegGPT achieved 83.74±2.55% mean IoU across 20 spatially independent test images spanning a 10.5-fold vegetation density gradient (2.01 to 21.11% coverage), outperforming DINOv2 (78.09±6.63%) and SAM (47.03±20.64%). The observed collapse in SAM’s performance, despite billion-mask pretraining, can be attributed to its architectural constraints. SAM’s fixed 1024×1024 input reduced training patches by 76.2%, and its frozen encoder limited trainable parameters to 0.1M versus SegGPT’s 316M. These findings establish that fine-tuned encoders substantially outperform frozen-encoder architectures for specialized vegetation (Euphorbia resinifera) segmentation, and that single-image foundation model training offers a viable paradigm for conservation deployment, reducing annotation costs from tens of thousands to hundreds of dollars. While demonstrated for a morphologically distinctive species, these principles may inform broader conservation remote sensing applications pending validation across diverse plant forms.

items.title: Enhancing Knowledge Management in Green Building Engineering: A Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Approach to Support Project Assessment
items.abstract: Green building assessment relies heavily on manual queries of complex engineering regulations, making the introduction of knowledge management theories crucial for improving assessment efficiency. However, the inherent characteristics of engineering regulations—dense terminology, complex clause dependencies, and frequent revisions—limit the effectiveness of traditional knowledge engineering. This study aims to explore the utilization of advanced information technologies to achieve reliable knowledge management for supporting engineering decision-making. From the perspective of acquisition, organization, retrieval, and presentation (AORP), a domain knowledge management framework is designed by integrating network analysis, information retrieval, and large language models (LLMs) with traditional knowledge management theories. A dual-structure knowledge network is proposed as the underlying carrier to characterize explicit rules and semantic dependencies, enabling lightweight knowledge organization. Furthermore, a hybrid retrieval algorithm capable of identifying and adaptively weighting domain terms was developed and embedded into a retrieval-augmented generation workflow. Facilitated by LLMs, the proposed framework supports more efficient, traceable, and scalable building assessment. This study covers regulations containing 225,604 words and validates the effectiveness of the proposed method using 132 practical test cases. The results showed that the proposed method achieves a recall rate of 0.959, effectively reduces generation hallucinations, and substantially improves the accuracy and reliability of knowledge presentation. More importantly, the experiments indicated that the performance gap among LLMs with different parameter scales narrowed after introducing domain knowledge, confirming that an effective knowledge management architecture in vertical domains has the potential to reduce dependence on large-parameter LLMs and provide a feasible pathway for low-cost deployment of intelligent applications in the industry.

items.title: Building Code Question-Answering Systems Enhanced by Large Language Models and Knowledge-Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: Building codes are complex documents that pose significant challenges for consistent interpretation and efficient compliance checking in the construction industry. Existing automated methods often overlook the interrelationships between provisions and lack comprehensive evaluation support from practical engineering perspectives. In this study, we develop a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system enhanced with a knowledge graph to interpret building codes by leveraging both the semantic content and structural relationships within the documents. We evaluated the system using 661 query-context-answer triplets from a particular building code. The RAG-enhanced model outperformed state-of-the-art pretrained transformer models and general-purpose large language models (LLMs) in answer quality. Shorter text chunks led to higher semantic relevance, while longer chunks improved precision. The closed-source model achieved better accuracy and speed than the open-source alternative. These findings demonstrate the potential of knowledge-graph-based RAG systems to support accurate, efficient, and scalable regulatory interpretation in real-world engineering contexts.
items.venue: Journal of computing in civil engineering

items.title: Automated Compliance Checking for BIM Models via a Large Language Model-Driven BIM-to-Text Paradigm
items.abstract: Automated compliance checking (ACC) for building information modeling (BIM) is a vital task in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. However, significant semantic gaps among Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) schemas, regulatory texts, and logical rules necessitate extensive manual intervention for domain-specific knowledge modeling and rule interpretation. Fully automated compliance checking for BIM models remains a challenging task. To address these issues, this study proposes an innovative BIM-to-text paradigm, which takes full advantage of the context understanding and generation capabilities of emerging large language models (LLMs). Unlike the existing mainstream methods, the original intention of our proposed method is to convert BIM semantic information into natural language descriptions, rather than converting the specification text into logical rules. First, regulatory entities and entity types are extracted from regulatory texts using LLMs with a self-correction mechanism. Second, we have designed a novel BIM parsing strategy and data storage schemes, and the LLM is used for semantic alignment between IFC entities and regulatory entities to identify BIM semantic fragments. Next, the BIM semantic fragments are converted into BIM description texts via LLM guided by the BIM-to-text motivation. Finally, the regulatory texts and the generated BIM description texts are fed into the LLM to infer the results of compliance checking. On the building BIM ACC data set and the bridge BIM ACC data set, our method achieves F1-scores of 95.70 and 96.13% in the end-to-end setting, respectively. The experimental results also indicate that the proposed framework can avoid complex ontology modeling and rule interpretation processes in the traditional semantic parsing–based BIM ACC methods, and achieves compliance checking with a higher level of automation. This work contributes a novel LLM-driven BIM-to-text paradigm for ACC.
items.venue: Journal of computing in civil engineering

items.title: An Agency-Specific Project Authoring Advisor: LLM-Based RAG System with Automatic Prompt Optimization Method
items.abstract: Despite the vast potential of large language models (LLMs) in specialized fields, their application in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) has been hindered by several challenges, including inaccurate information retrieval, limited access to domain information, inadequate customization of prompts, and hallucination. Addressing these challenges, this paper presents an agency-specific project authoring advisor that tightly couples LLMs with a curated technical document database (TDD) in an end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline and proposes an automated prompt optimization method within this framework. Using domain-specific embeddings, we first construct a vectorized knowledge base to enable semantic retrieval of AEC-specific information. We then employ domain-specific prompt engineering by combining persona, format template, chain of thought, and few-shot patterns to guide the model toward detailed, project authoring–specific answers. An automated adversarial prompt optimization method uses an LLM-based question generator and answer evaluation to iteratively refine prompt templates for comprehensiveness, accuracy, clarity, relevance, and conciseness. Additionally, we incorporate long-document handling using MapReduce, multiturn conversation memory, an integrated web search to cover knowledge gaps, and a chat-style web graphical user interface (GUI) for user interaction. LLM-assisted evaluation with 30 agency questions (scored for comprehensiveness, accuracy, relevance, clarity, and conciseness) showed that GPT-4 with RAG scored 75.7/100 versus 53.4/100 without RAG, and reached 88.9 with domain-specific prompt patterns and chain-of-thought reasoning. Gemini and Llama exhibited similar improvements. We also found that domain-specific embeddings deliver a 16.5% relative improvement in total averaged scores across the three LLMs. In expert validation, our advisor outperformed traditional search methods including Google and document search on all metrics, especially search efficiency. By formalizing an agency’s technical documents in a reusable knowledge base and coupling it with LLM reasoning, we contribute a transferable, end-to-end RAG pipeline for agency-specific question answering (QA), a systematic, automated prompt optimization procedure, and three reusable domain-specific prompt templates, advancing the LLM applications for knowledge-intensive and domain-specific project authoring.
items.venue: Journal of computing in civil engineering

items.title: Rethinking Network Foundation Models: From Bigger Models to Better Data
items.abstract: Network foundation models (NFMs) report high accuracy on traffic tasks, yet diagnostic studies keep finding that this accuracy rests on shortcuts: artifacts of how the training data was collected. The usual response to a weak model is a bigger one, and better evaluation and better architectures both hold the training data fixed. We argue that the lever is the data. A trace's network context is the set of factors that generated it: the application, the transport, and the network conditions. A good NFM is a minimal sufficient representation of network context: it preserves those factors and spends the least data and model capacity needed to do so. We show, in one setting, that better data helps. A semantically deduplicated pre-training set one-tenth the size of a campus corpus matches the full corpus and beats an equal-size random sample on context preservation (how much of the network context the model keeps). Obtaining better data is a search over which traces to select and which conditions to generate, where selection is generation limited to what was already collected. Composing real application, transport, and network components makes controlled generation cheap and produces the bytes and headers an NFM reads as in deployment. One context-preservation objective can then decide which data to keep and how much model capacity to retain; the search and the capacity choice remain proposals. For the factors it can specify, networking can pursue minimal sufficiency more directly than most domains, because it can generate traffic through the stack it deploys and check what a representation kept against the conditions it specified.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Network Traffic Classification – Reloaded

items.title: PRISM: Predictive KV Cache Discovery for Agentic LLM Serving at Internet Scale
items.abstract: Agentic large language model (LLM) workflows share prompt pre-fixes, enabling key-value (KV) cache reuse to avoid repeated prefill. Eviction or execution away from existing state can limit reuse. PRISM combines distributed cache discovery, workflow prediction, and cost-aware preparation and forwarding to prepare prefixes before demand. Compared with the strongest evaluated baseline, PRISM reduces P99 time to first token by 43.8% on a three-region GPU testbed and 79.9% in a 16-region simulation.
items.venue: Proceedings of the ACM CoNEXT 2026 Student Workshop

items.title: What Do LLM Judges Evaluate in Recommendation Assessment? Disentangling Relevance, Local Diversity, and System-Level Diversity
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges of recommendation quality, yet which dimensions their verdicts reflect is unclear. We study dimension alignment: the statistical association between LLM preferences and the winners identified by different recommendation metrics. Across 19,240 LLM calls spanning four datasets, 16 model pairs, four prompt designs, four LLM judges (7B–671B), diagnostic controls, and frontier closed-source API validation, standard (balanced) evaluation aligns strongly with relevance, selecting the NDCG winner in 86.7% of conflict pairs; 61.8% of consistent user verdicts agree with the system-average NDCG winner. Coverage and Entropy, however, are global properties of all lists, whereas the judge sees only two top-10 lists. Under diversity-only prompts, alignment with Coverage is weak (38.0%), while alignment with prompt-visible local cues is strong: category count (83.7%), category entropy (80.5%), and text dissimilarity (63.2%). LLM judges therefore do respond to diversity, but local variety must not be substituted for system-level exposure metrics. Supplying aggregate statistics forces Coverage alignment, but this is an instruction-following manipulation check, not independent diversity reasoning. A small human sanity check (330 annotations) and stronger judges show the same local–global mismatch. We conclude with a decision framework separating LLM-suitable from metric-only evaluation.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: Voltage-Dependent ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ Extraction and Modeling for Predictive Conducted-EMI in GaN Power Converters
items.abstract: This article quantifies how the off -state output-capacitance loss ( ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ ) of 600 V GaN HEMTs governs switch-node ring-down and high-frequency conducted EMI. ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ is extracted from S-parameter measurements over an EMI-relevant band (30–100 MHz) and across drain bias up to 500 V. Here, ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ is treated as a static, bias-dependent ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}\ ( {{{V}_{\text{ds}}}} )$ ; dynamic ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ effects are not modeled. A behavioral LTspice GaN model is developed with nonlinear capacitances, dynamic ${{R}_{\text{DS},\text{on}}}$ , and voltage-dependent ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ , then validated on a half-bridge using time-domain waveforms and CISPR-25-style LISN measurements up to 200 MHz. Across four devices, higher ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ increases damping, reducing switch-node overshoot and lowering resonance-driven conducted-EMI peaks in the 80–150 MHz range by up to 13 dB. Including ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ yields close agreement between simulated and measured ring-down and EMI spectra, showing that ${{R}_{\text{OSS}}}$ can be essential for predictive EMC modeling and GaN device selection.

items.title: Toward Domain-Specific Large Language Models in Construction Engineering: A Review of Development Tools
items.abstract: The architecture, engineering, and construction industry is facing the challenge of massive heterogeneous data, with an urgent demand for domain-specific large language models (LLM) capable of understanding complex engineering semantics and meeting high reliability requirements. Focusing on the four existing approaches for the specialization of general purpose LLM specialization, this paper aims to systematically review the development tools for domain-specific LLM specialization in construction engineering based on general-purpose LLM specialization. The development tools are classified into three categories: data preparation; basic LLM specialization; and advanced LLM specialization. Subsequently, their features are summarized with typical examples. Finally, the selection strategies are recommended, and the current challenges are summarized. This paper enhances the body of knowledge on artificial intelligence applications by offering systematic and practical insights into the development tool ecosystem for domain-specific LLM specialization in construction engineering.
items.venue: Journal of construction engineering and management

items.title: TimeAgent: A Training-Free LLM Agent for Time Series Foundation Models
items.abstract: Time series forecasting is pivotal across diverse real-world applications. Although time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated exceptional zero-shot forecasting capabilities, they are encountering the seesaw effect across domains due to inevitable biases in pre-training datasets, backbones, and training objectives. Given that no single TSFM universally dominates all temporal patterns, resolving this challenge typically requires exhaustive model tuning or manual expertise, highlighting the critical need for an automated and intelligent workflow to adaptively orchestrate diverse TSFMs. To this end, we introduce TimeAgent, a training-free agent that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to unlock the specialized skills of an open family of TSFMs. By framing forecasting as a scientific inquiry, TimeAgent establishes a structured, closed-loop workflow encompassing data profiling, iterative experiment planning, multi-model prediction arbitration, and outcome interpretation. Through this workflow, the agent autonomously explores the joint search space of TSFM selections and input context lengths, orchestrating a robust prediction ensemble tailored to each individual series without human intervention or model training. Experimentally, TimeAgent demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across various tasks and domains, ranking first on the GIFT-Eval and FEV leaderboards. Notably, as a training-free and plug-and-play framework, TimeAgent seamlessly integrates up-to-date models without injecting TSFM specifics or retraining the LLM agent. Beyond superior performance, TimeAgent turns opaque model behavior into transferable, human-readable insights, offering a promising way for managing an ever-growing family of foundation models. We envision this lightweight agentic framework as a meaningful step towards building autonomous forecasting systems with both accuracy and interpretability.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: SpBatch: Reclaiming Lost Sparsity for Batched Sparse FFN Execution
items.abstract: Generative large language models (LLMs) face significant challenges in deployment due to their substantial computational and memory demands, particularly under batched inference scenarios. While activation sparsity offers a promising direction to reduce resource consumption, its benefits diminish with increasing batch sizes. Moreover, existing sparse inference systems fail to fully utilize modern GPU Tensor Cores. This paper proposes SpBatch , an efficient execution framework for batched activation-sparse FFN computation in ReLU-adapted LLMs through a two-level design. At the system level, it introduces Sparsity-Aware-Division to dynamically partition large batches into smaller mini-batches, maximizing sparsity and hardware utilization simultaneously. At the kernel level, it employs a “ Load by CUDA Cores, Compute by Tensor Cores ” strategy, alongside a Bitmap-based Neuron Index mechanism for load balancing and an optimized execution pipeline. SpBatch achieves up to 8.89 ${\boldsymbol{\times}}$ × speedup over PowerInfer (a representative activation-sparse baseline) and up to 2.6 ${\boldsymbol{\times}}$ × over llama.cpp (a dense inference framework) in end-to-end inference under the evaluated settings. These results demonstrate that activation sparsity and batch processing can be jointly leveraged through a selective sparse FFN execution path, especially in small-to-moderate batch regimes and high-sparsity edge-oriented scenarios where dense execution does not yet fully dominate.

items.title: Scaling LLMs via Collaboration: Efficient LLM Inference Across Resource-Constrained Devices
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deliver remarkable capabilities but remain difficult to deploy on memory- and compute-limited edge devices. A natural question is whether multiple devices can collaboratively execute token-by-token inference with low latency. Existing parallelism schemes, designed for datacenter GPUs and batch-oriented workloads, break down on edge devices due to ill-suited partitioning and heavy synchronization overheads. We identify three core challenges: (i) per-token synchronization dominates latency in decoding, (ii) naive scaling amplifies communication cost, and (iii) Transformer operators harbor hidden heterogeneous computation–communication characteristics that remain underutilized. Our key insight is that partitioning and synchronization must be co-optimized to unlock scalable edge collaboration. We present CoSEI, a system that introduces operator-aware partitioning and synchronization-minimizing execution, guided by a lightweight planner and a tailored runtime. A prototype built atop llama.cpp achieves up to 5.4× lower latency than pipeline baselines on an eight-node edge device cluster, while enabling models that exceed single-device memory. Results demonstrate that with the right design, collaborative edge inference can make LLMs practical beyond the cloud.

items.title: Real-Time Detection and Localization of Interturn Short-Circuits in Six-Phase PMSMs With Insulation Aging Analysis
items.abstract: Six-phase permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) with asymmetrical stator windings are increasingly adopted in applications requiring high reliability and fault tolerance. However, the widespread use of wide-bandgap power devices increases the electrical stress on stator insulation, accelerating degradation mechanisms and raising the risk of interturn short-circuit (ITSC) faults. In their early stage, ITSC faults may involve only a limited number of turns and a nonzero fault-path resistance, producing negligible deviations in terminal electrical quantities while still generating localized overheating and progressive insulation damage. This article develops a simplified analytical model to quantify the impact of ITSC faults in asymmetrical six-phase PMSMs. A combined theoretical and experimental investigation of insulation aging mechanisms leading to fault-path formation is carried out. The voltage harmonic components introduced by the fault are analyzed across the machine subspaces, providing a quantitative characterization of the ITSC signatures associated with resistance and back-EMF imbalance. Based on this analysis, a control-oriented diagnostic strategy is proposed, exploiting additional current regulators in selected synchronous reference frames to enable real-time fault detection, faulty-phase localization, and electrical severity estimation without additional sensors. Experimental validation on a dual three-phase PMSM prototype confirms the effectiveness of the proposed framework for online ITSC condition monitoring under steady-state and transient operating conditions.

items.title: RTMSSD: A Racetrack Memory Based Page-Level Storage Architecture for Fast and High-Reliable Persistency
items.abstract: Current SSDs employ various expensive optimization algorithms, e.g., garbage collection (GC), wear leveling (WL), and out-of-place updates, to solve the issues such as limited device life and write amplification. Indeed, they still struggle to bridge the performance gap between host and storage due to the time-consuming erase operation of NAND flash. As a magnetic storage, Racetrack Memory (RTM) performs tape-like access with longer endurance and fast write, making it a potential persistent storage medium. However, there are still three challenges when applying RTM to the general persistency architecture. (1) Traditional three-layer space management model, i.e., block-page-sector, introduces a large number of redundant operations under RTM context. (2) The current fault-tolerant mechanism in SSDs cannot solve the position errors in RTM persistency. (3) The read-first strategy in SSDs cannot benefit from the fast write of RTM. In order to solve the above problems, we propose RTMSSD, a architecture for RTM-based persistent storage. (1) The page-level storage architecture accurately manages pages access and performs fast address translation without mapping table. (2) The fault-tolerant mechanism for RTM persistency uses encoding and rewriting to achieve commercial-level reliability. (3) The new transaction scheduling method prioritizes error correction while ensuring balance between read and write. Experiments show that, comparing to SSDs, the end-to-end latency of RTMSSD can be reduced to 26% on average. In addition, compared with the corresponding RTM-based storage configurations without fault tolerance, the PAECC method proposed in this work improves the simulated Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) by approximately four orders of magnitude even in the worst evaluated case, making RTM-based storage approach the reliability level required for commercial use.

items.title: PALM: Protocol-Aware PCIe Link Fault Prediction for Large-Scale GPU Clusters
items.abstract: As the backbone of GPU cluster interconnection, PCIe links play a critical role in supporting large-scale AI parallel computing, and their failures can trigger communication stalls, job interruptions, or even large-scale training failures. However, prior studies have primarily focused on individual-device fault prediction or system-level post-failure diagnosis, leaving PCIe link fault prediction underexplored. This task faces several unique challenges: PCIe self-recovery obscures early fault signals, topology-level fault propagation decouples the root cause from the symptoms, and firmware/driver updates cause telemetry distribution shifts. These challenges are difficult to address using telemetry signals alone and require the model to understand PCIe protocol behavior. To this end, we propose PALM, a Protocol-Aware prediction framework powered by Large Language Models. It is built upon two core engines: a Sentinel Engine, which develops a Granger-causality model to filter protocol noise and a state signature extractor to identify fault signatures; and an Arbiter Engine that translates these signatures into diagnostic evidence via a protocol-guided VLM, then fuses this evidence through an NN–VLM co-refinement predictor for reliable prediction. This detect-then-arbitrate pipeline bridges anomaly detection and protocol-level reasoning, grounding predictions in protocol semantics. Evaluated on Alibaba Cloud production data, PALM achieves 2.45 $\mathbf{\times}$ × , 7.91 $\mathbf{\times}$ × , and 6.60 $\mathbf{\times}$ × the average Precision, Recall, and F1-score of the five SOTA baselines, respectively.

items.title: MixDPT: Robust Prompt Fine-Tuning via Multi-Group Prompting and Matrix Decomposition-Reconstruction
items.abstract: The hyperparameter search for the optimal prompt length requires a significant amount of computing resources, and the method of fixing the prompt length in practical applications degrades performance across tasks, severely limiting the potential of large language models (LLMs) and large vision-language models (LVLMs). To address this issue, we propose a multi-group prompt fine-tuning method with matrix decomposition (MixDPT), which mainly consists of two modules: the Adaptive Multi-Group Prompt (AMP) module and the Matrix Decomposition-Reconstruction (MDR) module. Specifically, the AMP module divides the prompt length in LLMs into three fixed groups with simple, medium, and difficult tasks so as to isolate the task types and reduce the interference among the features. Furthermore, to efficiently adjust the model’s attention weights under computational resource constraints, we embed the MDR module, a multi-head low-rank matrix, into the Wq, Wk, and Wv weight matrices within the first Transformer layers of a frozen large model. This allows us to effectively reshape the attention weights while keeping the main body of the large model frozen, thereby significantly enhancing the model’s feature representation capability. Finally, extensive experiments on various language tasks, including SuperGLUE, NER, QA, and SRL, as well as FGVC in LVLMs demonstrate that the proposed MixDPT significantly improves the performance of prompt-based models and achieves superior performance at the same prompt length, significantly improving its stability and generalization with fixed 140-token prompts.

items.title: LyRA-FL: A Scheduler for Federated Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models in Wireless Networks
items.abstract: The distributed training of semantic segmentation models is a key enabler for perception on mobile and edge devices, supporting applications such as augmented reality, robotics, and intelligent video analytics. However, this deployment within federated learning (FL) systems is hindered by severe statistical heterogeneity, high communication costs, and the unreliability of wireless networks. This paper introduces Lyapunov-based Resource Allocation for FL (LyRA-FL), a unified cross-layer scheduling algorithm grounded in control theory and stochastic geometry. At the learning layer, we integrate the SegFormer foundation vision model with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to enable parameter-efficient fine-tuning and reduce the communication and computation burden on clients. At the communication layer, LyRA-FL employs a stochastic geometry-driven Lyapunov scheduler that jointly optimizes communication reliability, a novel Value-of-Participation (VoP) metric, and long-term fairness during client selection. Extensive experiments on the Cityscapes and IDDA benchmarks show that our unified framework achieves over 82% reduction in the number of trainable parameters and converges significantly faster than state-of-the-art baselines, achieving up to 10% and 33% higher final mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU), respectively. Our LyRA-FL scheduler successfully manages issues like wireless uncertainty, Non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) data, and stragglers, enabling our framework to achieve a higher final accuracy under realistic channel conditions than the SiloBN+LAB baseline in an idealized, error-free setting.

items.title: Low-Altitude Hunter: A System for Vision-Language Anti-UAV Task With MLLM
items.abstract: With the rapid expansion of the low-altitude economy (LAE), safety governance in urban airspace has become increasingly important, and physical capture is widely regarded as a promising, safe, and efficient approach to countering non-cooperative uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, physical capture in complex and rapidly changing urban environments remains difficult to achieve: traditional end-to-end control methods suffer from limited generalization, while aerial vision-language action (VLA) paradigms, despite their stronger generalization potential, are still primarily developed for static target-reaching tasks. To bridge this gap, we present the Low-altitude Hunter system for the vision-language anti-UAV (VLAU) task with a multimodal large language model (MLLM). Specifically, we build a high-fidelity simulation platform that integrates diverse urban scenes, multiple UAV models with realistic flight dynamics, and flexible onboard sensor configurations. Building upon the proposed platform, we further construct a large-scale VLAU that covers diverse spatial layouts, motion trajectories, and task difficulty levels. Then, we develop an MLLM-based framework that unifies offline imitation learning (IL), closed-loop dataset aggregation (DAgger), and online reinforcement learning (RL) to jointly improve multimodal reasoning, continuous control, and online adaptability under distribution shifts and long-horizon interactions. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework achieves higher success rates, stronger robustness, and better policy adaptability than conventional baselines in VLAU scenarios.

items.title: LevelKV: Hierarchical KV Cache Pruning for Efficient and Reliable LLM Inference
items.abstract: The performance and functionality of large language model (LLM)-based applications heavily depend on their contextual inputs. As applications become more sophisticated, their contexts grow increasingly complex, leading to two critical challenges: (i) excessive computational and memory overhead—particularly from the key-value (KV) cache—and (ii) heightened security risks arising from heterogeneous and unverified context sources. Existing approaches fail to address both issues simultaneously: context compression methods often discard crucial information, undermining instruction fidelity, while security-oriented defenses typically introduce additional computational costs. We present LevelKV, a hierarchical KV cache pruning framework that achieves efficient and reliable LLM inference. LevelKV employs a holistic metric to jointly identify critical activations in both Key and Value caches, and introduces a hierarchy-preserving mechanism that structurally prioritizes high-privilege prompts during pruning to maintain reliability. Evaluations on LongBench and SysBench demonstrate that LevelKV achieves state-of-the-art trade-offs between memory efficiency and instruction compliance. Remarkably, it maintains superior Instruction Hierarchy reliability even when retaining only 1/10 of the KV cache, enabling robust and efficient LLM deployment on memory-constrained devices.

items.title: LazyDM: A Machine Learning-Empowered Hot Data Management to Mitigate Premature Migration in High-Density Hybrid SSDs
items.abstract: Modern high-density flash memory technologies, such as Quad-Level Cell (QLC), commonly employ a hybrid architecture in which a subset of QLC blocks operates in Single-Level Cell (SLC) mode as a cache for the remaining QLC blocks. In this architecture, hot data is initially programmed to the SLC cache and later migrated to the QLC region at block-level granularity. However, limited SLC cache capacity and coarse migration granularity can cause hot data that has not yet cooled to be prematurely migrated to the QLC region, significantly degrading SSD performance and lifespan. This phenomenon is referred to as premature migration. To address this issue, this study proposes LazyDM—a machine learning-based hot data management for SLC cache, designed to optimize both performance and reliability in high-density hybrid SSDs. In particular, we develop a machine learning model to predict the duration over which data remains hot (referred to as hotness duration). We devise a hot data allocation scheme that segregates data in the SLC cache based on their hotness durations, ensuring that hot data within each block exhibit comparable cooling times. We further introduce a cooling-aware data migration scheme that efficiently relocates cooled data from the SLC cache to the QLC region, thereby preventing the performance degradation and endurance reduction caused by premature migration. Experimental results show that, compared with state-of-the-art techniques, our LazyDM reduces the hot data migration ratio, average read response time, average write response time, number of garbage collections (GCs), and number of valid page migrations by an average of 55.14%, 15.82%, 23.19%, 21.97%, and 42.83%, respectively. In addition, LazyDM improves the SLC read hit ratio by an average of 19.34%.

items.title: LEHiD: LLM-Empowered Hierarchical DRL Framework for Path Planning in UAV Networks
items.abstract: In the era of 6G and the massive Internet of Things (IoT), Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are a promising option for autonomous data collection under limited mission budget. The core difficulty is to plan trajectories that collect useful data while preserving safe return in environments with structured obstacles, communication-dependent service quality, and changing mission priorities. Classical planners such as A* provide geometric feasibility, but their objectives must often be redesigned when the mission changes. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL), on the other hand, suffers from sparse rewards and weak sample efficiency in these settings. To address this gap, we propose LEHiD, a hierarchical framework that combines a Large Language Model (LLM) for high-level target sequencing, an A*-based layer for safety validation and planner-facing cost estimation, and a DRL policy for low-level reactive control. The A* layer also provides heuristic state augmentation and A*-guided replay-buffer warm starts that improve low-level learning. We evaluate the framework under static structured routing, where each learned-control hierarchy is trained with its corresponding high-level planner, and under semantic-adaptation settings, where the trained D3QN controller is frozen and only the planner-side interface changes after online priority updates. The results indicate that LEHiD remains competitive with strong non-LLM hierarchical training baselines under static routing, exceeds planner-only route-ordering references on landing-aware collection, improves semantic target redirection in a controlled exact priority-shift experiment, and yields the strongest results among the tested planners in the richer structured regional-priority experiment.

items.title: Intent Entropy: Planning Intent Uncertainty Detection and Entropy-Gated Reflection for Ambiguous Instructions
items.abstract: Embodied agents executing tasks from natural language instructions face the challenge of interpreting ambiguous commands that may lead to inconsistent planning. Conventional uncertainty estimation methods, reliant on token-level probabilities or semantic embeddings, struggle to capture task-level intent divergence, while large language model (LLM) based planning suffers from computational overhead. To address these problems, this paper presents Intent Entropy, an innovative uncertainty quantification method that models planning-level ambiguity through structured task chain clustering. By computing entropy over equivalence-clustered subtask sequences, Intent Entropy directly measures intent uncertainty rather than linguistic variations, exhibiting statistically significant negative correlation with task success, substantially outperforming conventional uncertainty measures. Building upon this metric, we introduce the Entropy-Gated Reflection Mechanism (ECHO), a hierarchical framework that employs lightweight models for initial planning and selectively triggers large-model reflection only under high uncertainty. The proposed methodology is evaluated on the ALFRED benchmark, demonstrating superior performance on both seen and unseen scenarios while significantly reducing computational costs compared to baseline methods. Furthermore, ECHO exhibits robust performance across varying instruction ambiguity levels, showcasing its effectiveness in uncertainty-aware adaptive planning.

items.title: Integration of Static Knowledge and Telemetry Data for an IoT-Based Customer Support AI Agent
items.abstract: The operational effectiveness of artificial intelligence agents in customer support is frequently attributed to the generative sophistication of underlying language models, although answer reliability primarily depends on the structure and quality of the referenced knowledge base. In complex technical domains such as the Internet of Things (IoT), static documentation alone often fails to resolve customer inquiries that involve real-time device states, sensor readings, and connectivity logs. This study investigates how progressive tiers of knowledge integration affect the response quality of an AI agent within an IoT customer support context. Employing a mixed-method pilot design combining literature synthesis, comparative analysis, experimental testing, and conceptual exploration, thirty representative questions were classified into informational, status, and diagnostic categories. These queries were evaluated across four operational scenarios: without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), article-based RAG, article plus device metadata records, and a comprehensive hybrid framework integrating static articles, device records, and telemetry streams. Answer quality was measured using Cosine Similarity, BERTScore (F1), and a randomized blind human evaluation assessing relevance, correctness, and usefulness. The results demonstrate that while curated static documentation adequately addresses procedural informational queries, resolving status and diagnostic issues necessitates real-time operational context. The hybrid integration delivered the highest overall performance, achieving a human-evaluation score of 4.40 compared with 2.53 for article-based RAG (p = 0.0039). These empirical findings confirm that robust IoT support agents require dynamic knowledge governance that bridges versioned documentation, synchronized asset metadata, and live telemetry data within a unified retrieval framework.
items.venue: International Journal Software Engineering and Computer Science (IJSECS)

items.title: HyperInfer: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference via Importance-Informed Prefix-KV Caching and Prefetching
items.abstract: Modern advanced large language model (LLM) applications often prepend long contexts before user queries to improve model output quality. These contexts frequently repeat, either partially or fully, across multiple queries. Existing systems typically store and reuse the keys and values of these contexts (referred to as prefix KVs) to reduce redundant computation and time to first token (TTFT). When prefix KVs need to be stored on disks due to insufficient CPU memory, reusing them does not always reduce TTFT, as disk I/O latency is high. In this paper, we present HyperInfer, an importance-informed multi-tier prefix KV caching and prefetching system designed to reduce TTFT in LLM inference. HyperInfer first employs an I/O-efficient algorithm to identify and load only the most important KVs, thereby minimizing I/O overhead. Then, to further hide loading latency, it leverages the inter-layer similarity of token importance to speculatively prefetch the next layer’s critical KVs during the current layer’s computation. Finally, HyperInfer optimizes prefix-KV storage and cache utilization via importance-informed KV placement, further reducing TTFT in end-to-end inference. Our experimental results show that HyperInfer can reduce TTFT by up to 1.75 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × compared to state-of-the-art systems, while maintaining comparable inference accuracy.

items.title: Full-Chip Thermal Monitoring in Silicon-Photonic Chiplet Systems: Repurposing the Photonic Interposer Network
items.abstract: Integration of Silicon-Photonic (SiPh) interconnects with multi-chiplet systems offers unprecedented bandwidth and energy efficiency for next-generation computing. However, the resulting high power density and complex vertical thermal coupling create severe thermal challenges that threaten both computational integrity and photonic communication reliability. Accurate and efficient full-chip thermal monitoring is a critical prerequisite for dynamic thermal management, yet it remains challenging. The limited number of physical thermal sensors that are often sparsely placed on the compute chiplets fails to capture the intricate 3D thermal landscape, especially within the photonic interposer network (PIN) itself. To this end, we propose TherMoPIN, a novel framework achieving accurate yet cost-effective full-chip thermal monitoring. In addition to the physical thermal sensors that are readily placed on chiplets, it repurposes the existing PIN into a uniformly placed virtual thermal sensor array with negligible cost increases. TherMoPIN comprises two key enablers. First, we propose ArbLink, a precise and cost-efficient thermal sensing mechanism, which transforms the entire PIN into a dense and uniformly-distributed ‘virtual’ sensor array by reusing available photonic routers for thermal sensing, with minimal hardware overhead. Second, we develop HorVer, a lightweight thermal reconstruction technique that fuses sparse, direct readings from horizontal on-chiplet thermal sensors (i.e., physical ones) with the dense, indirect thermal data from the vertical photonic interposer network (i.e., virtual ones), capturing and modeling the critical thermal coupling between the compute chiplets and the photonic interposer. This unique horizontal-vertical data fusion allows HorVer to accurately reconstruct the full-chip thermal map of SiPh-chiplet systems. Experimental results demonstrate that TherMoPIN achieves high thermal monitoring accuracy, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods that rely solely on physical sensors. Furthermore, it accomplishes this with negligible additional hardware cost, as it primarily reuses the already-present photonic infrastructure for sensing.

items.title: From World Foundation Models to Real-world applications: An Introduction
items.abstract: This course introduces the emerging paradigm of world foundation models (WFMs) and their role in enabling real-world physical AI systems. Those WFMs learn structured, multimodal representations of physical environments, supporting perception, prediction, and decision-making from a shared representation that spans vision, language, and action. The course connects foundation model concepts to dynamic visual environments, simulation, synthetic data generation, robotics, and sim-to-real deployment.

items.title: From Fabricated Citations to Unverified Journal Matches: Problems and Solutions in LLM Assisted Manuscript Generation
items.abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) in scholarly writing introduces risks of fabricated references, unsupported claims, and unreliable journal recommendations. Evidence gating addresses these risks by allowing outputs only when verifiable conditions are met and requiring explicit abstention otherwise. This study evaluates evidence gating through a design science research approach, examining scopus-jurnal, an open-source Python multi-agent pipeline that retrieves literature, drafts IMRaD sections, validates citations, reviews manuscripts, and recommends journals. Five evaluation episodes combined traceability audits and white-box experiments covering 46 in-text citations, 122 verification cases, 14 reviewer output formats, and 40 journal-matching probes. Results show that although the pipeline abstained when evidence was absent, weaknesses emerged between LLM outputs and deterministic code. Two of 17 specified phases lacked implementation, restricting the pipeline to drafting framing sections. Citation detection resolved only 31.6% of valid APA citations, while fabricated citations were sometimes accepted. Title matching accepted all 14 fabricated near-miss titles and rejected eight of nine legitimate short titles. Reviewer-score parsing failed on seven of ten plausible formats. A revised verification rule reduced false acceptance from 33.3% to 2.4% and false rejection from 43.1% to 0%. Journal-matching experiments showed that scope evidence without a score threshold enabled safe abstention, whereas introducing a threshold eliminated abstention. These findings emphasize tool-level evaluation and contribute an audit protocol, seven design principles, a reference architecture, eight integrity-preserving solutions, and five future research priorities.

items.title: FlexKV: Resource-Efficient Remote KV Reuse for Low-Latency LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional performance across a variety of online services, which require real-time responses with low time-to-first-token (TTFT). To reduce TTFT, existing works commonly reuse the KV cache for requests sharing identical prefixes and leverage remote KV caches to increase the reuse rate. Existing remote KV-cache reuse policies, which we call resource-insensitive reuse policies, assume the network is stable and ignore real-time resource fluctuations. However, such policies cannot maintain low TTFT, as they neither make dynamic selections among different reuse representations nor leverage hybrid reuse to increase resource utilization, leading to significant waste of compute and transfer resources. We propose that an efficient LLM inference system should adopt a resource-efficient KV-cache reuse policy to reduce TTFT. To do so, we design an LLM inference system, FlexKV, which decreases TTFT while achieving high resource utilization by integrating two novel components: an adaptive Hybrid Adapter that chooses which reuse approaches to utilize, and a layer-wise Pipeline Scheduler that coordinates multiple compute and transfer operations. Evaluation across 14 unique model–workload combinations spanning 6.7B to 65B models, including a multi-node LLaMA-65B-GPTQ deployment, shows that FlexKV achieves up to a 4.90× TTFT speedup over evaluated deployable baselines. Compared with the analytical Optimal reference, FlexKV has a median TTFT gap of 8.10%.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

items.title: Falcon: Efficient and Scalable Acceleration of Packet-Level Network Simulation for LLM Training
items.abstract: Network simulation serves as a crucial tool for evaluating the performance of distributed training systems. Evaluating congestion control, routing, queueing, flow control, and tail-latency behavior in large language model (LLM) training networks requires packet-level simulation (PLS) when transient packet, queue, and protocol-state interactions determine the outcomes. However, fine-grained packet-event processing and network-state maintenance impose substantial runtime and memory overhead at cluster scale. In this paper, we propose Falcon , a network-layer accelerator for efficient and scalable packet-level simulation of LLM-training communication traffic. Specifically, we construct a communication dependency tree to capture the spatiotemporal characteristics of LLM training traffic. Then, we propose a decomposition-level lossless spatiotemporal decomposition strategy that preserves the communication dependency tree and packet-level traffic semantics under the stated partitioning conditions, while decoupling simulation tasks into independent sub-tasks for parallel execution. Each sub-task is executed by the underlying packet-level backend. Finally, we present traffic-aware topology pruning and dynamic task scheduling strategies to ensure simulation efficiency in the large-scale LLM training scenarios. We have implemented a prototype of Falcon on SystemC and NS-3. The experimental results indicate that Falcon delivers a 12.5 $\sim$ ∼ 18.9x simulation-execution speedup over monolithic PLS approaches and a 5.7 $\sim$ ∼ 10.3x speedup over representative parallel packet-level simulation approaches.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems

items.title: Energy Efficient Multi-UAV Trajectory Planning in Multi-Hotspot Scenarios: A Large Language Model Enhanced MARL Approach
items.abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has been widely applied in multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) assisted communication for trajectory planning. However, in multi-hotspot scenarios, existing MARL based algorithms suffer from sparse rewards and inefficient credit assignment, leading to poor learning efficiency in UAV agents and constraining the energy efficiency. Notably, Large Language Models (LLMs), leveraging their vast prior knowledge and powerful reasoning capabilities, have demonstrated great potential for optimizing complex systems. However, it is not trivial to deploy LLMs on UAVs with low computational resources. Therefore, we propose a novel LLM-enhanced Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm (LLM-MAPPO) for multi-UAV trajectory planning. LLM-MAPPO integrates the reasoning advantages of LLMs with the lightweight decision-making capabilities of MAPPO agents, significantly enhancing the global energy efficiency of multi-UAV trajectories while ensuring deployability on UAVs. In LLM-MAPPO, we first design a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompt to guide the LLM in reasoning and generate high-quality expert trajectory policies with superior credit assignment capabilities. Then, we develop a dual-phase update algorithm that enables MAPPO agents to inherit knowledge from LLM expert policies and achieve further surpassing. This algorithm enhances credit assignment effectiveness and addresses the sparse reward problem to improve learning efficiency. Experiments show that LLM-MAPPO accelerates agent training by 67% and outperforms compared algorithms among various metrics, notably improving energy efficiency by 194%.

items.title: Enabling Distributed Cooperative Full-Size LLM Inference With Tensor Parallelism Across Heterogeneous Edge Devices
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly penetrating various fields, enhancing a wide range of tasks and services. Enabling edge devices for LLM inference can benefit real-time applications for end users. However, resource limitations and heterogeneity over edge devices hinder the deployment of the full-size LLM. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM inference system in edge environments, facilitating cooperative inference across low-profile edge devices. The system incorporates tensor parallelism technologies across heterogeneous devices, addressing challenges related to limited resources and asynchronous operations in such scenarios. We formulate the problem as a convex integer optimization problem to determine optimal partition strategies. We propose solutions with theoretical bounds on the optimal value. We conduct extensive experiments with real edge devices and large-scale numerical simulations to assess the performance of the proposed solutions. Results from experiments and simulations demonstrate that our approach achieves efficient model partitioning and up to 0.65 seconds per token for full-size model inference performance in edge environments.

items.title: Dynamic Event Knowledge Graph–Based Fault Diagnosis for Multisensor Electromechanical Systems of Aviation Equipment and Its Application
items.abstract: Aviation equipment, such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) rely on a suite of sensors to support their control and navigation functions. Yet, in challenging operational conditions, these sensors are prone to malfunction, posing risks of serious safety incidents and financial harm. Although neural network–based fault diagnosis techniques have gained traction in mechanical systems, they typically struggle to synthesize data from multiple sources and disregard the value of event-based system insights. The rise of large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models is transforming risk assessment and predictive maintenance in engineering systems. These models excel at processing heterogeneous data including maintenance logs, equipment manuals, time-series sensor data, and visual reports, yet suffer from inherent cognitive uncertainty, model hallucinations, black-box opacity, and poor adaptability to dynamic working environments, which limit their use in safety-critical aviation systems. To address this, this work leverages an event knowledge graph (EKG) for UAV sensor fault diagnosis: the graph’s architecture inherently structures the array of distinct sensors. Concretely, causal logic derived from event progression boosts the graph nodes’ ability to extract meaningful features, and a relationship-focused attention mechanism (built on gated convolution) captures spatial–temporal patterns within sensor data. Additionally, this study incorporates a UAV dynamic model (rooted in an event-triggered framework) into EKG construction to improve diagnostic precision, interpretability, and safety margins. When tested on three custom-built data sets, the approach achieved diagnostic accuracies of 94.93%, 98.71%, and 92.97%, respectively. Relative to standard data-driven methods and pure LLM-based diagnostic schemes, the proposed technique also exhibits stronger feature extraction performance, fewer hallucination risks, full decision traceability, and delivers the top overall diagnostic accuracy.
items.venue: ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems. Part A: Civil Engineering

items.title: Dynamic Current Imbalance Mechanism Analysis of Paralleled SiC MOSFETs Based on a Multibranch Parasitic Network Model Considering Common-Path Inductances
items.abstract: Dynamic current imbalance significantly degrades the electrothermal reliability of multibranch paralleled SiC mosfets, necessitating accurate mechanism analysis. Existing multibranch parasitic network models typically incorporate common-path parasitic inductances into branch parasitic inductances, which obscures the resulting interbranch current coupling and its impact on dynamic current imbalance. To address this issue, this article develops a multibranch parasitic network model in which common-path parasitic inductances are characterized separately from branch parasitic inductances. The proposed model reveals that common-path parasitic inductances govern the dynamic current distribution among branches through an intrinsic negative-feedback current-coupling mechanism. Specifically, in the subthreshold region, the initial dynamic current imbalance is mainly governed by the drive-source common-path parasitic inductance, whereas in the saturation region, the peak dynamic current imbalance is primarily governed by the power-source common-path parasitic inductance. PCB-level experiments validate the proposed model and mechanism analysis. Furthermore, to demonstrate the practical value of the proposed model, a stepwise optimization method based on the sensitivity ranking of parasitic inductances is proposed. Module-level experiments show that the dynamic current imbalance is reduced from 56.1% to 3.5%.

items.title: Deep Learning and Generative AI for Structure-Aware Indoor Panorama Modeling and VR Exploration
items.abstract: Surround-view panoramic imaging provides complete visual coverage from a single viewpoint and is widely used for indoor capture, virtual tours, and immersive visualization. However, a 360° panorama is fundamentally a static, viewpoint-centered representation that lacks explicit 3D geometry, architectural structure, stereopsis, and motion parallax. As a result, it often produces a flattened perception of space, even when presented in HMDs, and offers limited support for navigation and editing. This course presents an up-to-date overview of recent methods and trends that combine architectural and data-driven priors with deep learning to infer geometric, structural, semantic, and visual information from a single panorama, enabling advanced indoor modeling and exploration. After introducing panoramic representations, including equirectangular projection, gravity alignment, indoor capture constraints, and available datasets, we examine the priors used to bridge the gap between incomplete visual observations and structured, explorable scene models. We then review the key tasks involved in transforming a 360° image into an enriched indoor representation, including depth and semantic estimation, room layout reconstruction, multi-room localization and connectivity, novel view synthesis, and immersive exploration. We also highlight recent advances in generative and structure-guided methods for panoramic outpainting and completion, aimed at creating realistic indoor 360° content for VR/XR applications, virtual staging, refurnishing, and immersive scene generation. The course also covers the emergence of both general-purpose and 360° -specific foundation models and their impact on panoramic analysis and synthesis. We finally point out relevant research issues and analyze research trends.

items.title: Decoupling Method for Simultaneous Online Tj and Bond-Wire Aging Monitoring of SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Junction temperature ( T j ) monitoring using thermal sensitive electrical parameters (TSEPs) has been widely investigated. However, most TSEPs are susceptible to aging effects, making the decoupling of T j and aging a critical challenge for the online condition monitoring of power modules. Based on the chip structural characteristics of mosfet s, this letter proposes a novel TSEP to achieve decoupling of T j and bond-wire aging. To this end, a dual-sampling and modulation strategy synchronized with the zero-vector is presented to achieve nonintrusive online measurement. The proposed decoupling method features a clear physical interpretation and an analytical model. Experimental results demonstrate that, for T j monitoring, the proposed method is insensitive to bond-wire aging and achieves higher accuracy over the full operating range. For aging assessment, it enables converter-level online identification of bond-wire aging states.

items.title: DPDA: A Dynamic Partition-Driven Data Allocation Scheme for Boosting Hybrid SSD Performance
items.abstract: QLC NAND flash provides superior storage density and cost-effectiveness at the expense of substantial programming latencies. To improve latency performance, hybrid SSDs incorporate high-speed SLC cache to mitigate the latency overhead of QLC flash. However, the hybrid architecture induces a critical performance bottleneck termed Hot-Write Blocking (HWB): prolonged QLC write operations monopolize flash chips, thereby stalling subsequent hot-data writes to SLC cache. This interference significantly exacerbates queuing latency and severely degrades SLC write performance. To address this issue, we propose a dynamic partition-driven data allocation scheme called DPDA that mitigates the hot-write blocking problem in hybrid architecture SSDs. DPDA partitions the parallel planes of an SSD into hot and cold partitions, and segregates hot and cold requests to the planes of distinct partitions, thereby isolating mutually interfering write streams. Specifically, the scheme implements a data dispatch module to allocate latency-sensitive hot requests to the SLC regions of planes in the hot partition, thereby shielding them from the interference of cold QLC writes. Moreover, to prevent insufficient SLC space in hot partitions, DPDA implements a partition control unit to dynamically swap the planes of hot and cold partitions by space utilization, and then uses the SLC regions of the swapped plane to serve hot requests, thus fully utilizing the SLC resources in hybrid SSDs. We compare DPDA with three state-of-the-art schemes SPA, AMPHIBIAN and RRTS in terms of write waiting time, write latency, and read latency under eight real-world workloads. The experimental results show that compared with the existing schemes, DPDA slashes the hot write waiting time, hot write latency, and average write latency by 52.99%, 51.86%, and 47.55%, respectively.

items.title: DADO: A LLM-Based Distribution-Aligned and Diversity-Optimized Data Generator
items.abstract: A key challenge in data-centric training is the scarcity of high-quality labeled data. While large language models offer synthetic generation capabilities, existing methods face two main issues: distribution misalignment (especially for underrepresented classes) and insufficient diversity. We propose DADO (Distribution-Aligned and Diversity-Optimized LLM-based) Data Generator, which jointly addresses these issues through a coordinated pipeline: a two-agent framework (attribute generator and scorer) ensures distribution alignment without manual feature engineering, while a diversity-optimized multi-layer prompt system with exclusion mechanism and few-shot selection maximizes lexical variation. Experiments across e-commerce, social media, and sentiment analysis domains show DADO achieves superior distributional alignment, up to 1.5× greater lexical diversity, and reduces CE loss by 5.6–35.3% when used for data augmentation, with higher quality confirmed by human evaluation.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: CITE: Communication-Efficient Inference Token Exchange for Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Wireless Edge LLMs
items.abstract: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) at the wireless edge is hampered by the “communication wall”: traditional Federated Learning (FL), an offline training paradigm, necessitates exchanging gigabyte-scale parameters, violating real-time latency constraints over fading channels and exposing gradient-based privacy vulnerabilities. For collaboration among already deployed models, we propose Communication-efficient Inference Token Exchange (CITE), a decentralized inference-time framework. CITE employs a lightweight semantic signaling protocol governed by a dual-sided Sanitization-Decomposition mechanism, which bounds sequence-level leakage of sensitive private attributes under explicit context-leakage assumptions. To mitigate the impact of unreliable peers in non-stationary wireless networks, we design a Synergistic Trust Consensus algorithm incorporating a Temperature-Scaled Weighting scheme and a Threshold-Based Pruning strategy, effectively capturing combinatorial peer synergy while reducing computational complexity. An optional Novelty-Weighted Online Adaptation module with Momentum-based updates enables nodes to internalize collaborative knowledge after interaction while filtering gradient noise derived from fluctuating peer qualities. Theoretical analysis characterizes wireless latency and outage feasibility, amortized communication tradeoffs against PEFT-based FL, sequence-level privacy leakage, and convergence under stated assumptions. Extensive experiments on standard NLU and knowledge-intensive benchmarks demonstrate that CITE reduces communication overhead while outperforming state-of-the-art federated baselines in inference accuracy and privacy resilience.

items.title: Augmenting Expert Elicitation With LLMs for Building Causal Models to Aid Decision Making
items.abstract: Objective: This study examines whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can serve as a supplement to traditional expert input when extracting structured causal knowledge, for the case study of decision support in medical diagnostics. Materials and Methods: We compare LLM-generated causal structures against several benchmark causal graphs created for medical diagnostic datasets. To reduce prompt-based variance and enhance reliability, we introduce a novel multi-prompt strategy where each pairwise variable query is tested using seven distinct causal linking verbs. Final edge inclusion is determined by majority voting across these variants. The resulting graphs are evaluated using standard structural similarity measures, such as Structural Hamming Distance, and Total Edge Recall Error. LLMs are able to reconstruct a substantial portion of the true causal structure, improving performance for aggregated responses from multiple prompt variations. Averaging across several prompts mitigated biases introduced by individual phrasing and reduced dependence on any single causal template, confirming that ensemble prompt strategies improve robustness. Conclusion: LLMs show promise as aids to human experts, particularly in settings where expert input is sparse or delayed. Our majority vote multi prompt technique provides a scalable method to reduce linguistic sensitivity in causal elicitation, validated on a broader LLM augmented framework.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

items.title: Approximate computing circuits for error-tolerant applications with low energy consumption
items.abstract: Energy efficiency is a crucial factor in very large-scale integrated (VLSI) circuit design, and traditional methods offer limited solutions to power intensive circuits. Recently, approximate computing techniques have emerged, enhancing key design parameters like power consumption, propagation delay, and area, albeit with a compromise in accuracy. These techniques are especially suitable for high-performance computing, as they offer reduced energy consumption while compromising some accuracy, making them ideal for use in arithmetic circuits. This paper introduces enhanced versions of approximate adders (AxAs) and subtractors (AxSCs) for fundamental operations. Building upon these designs, approximate multipliers using the Wallace tree multiplier (AxWTM) and approximate dividers (AxDs) have been developed, and their performances have been compared regarding power consumed, spatial requirements, delay time, and error frequency. Many digital image and video processing applications, along with other multimedia tools, can function effectively even with slight inaccuracies in their output results. The existing and proposed designs were applied to image squaring, image multiplication, image subtraction, and image division applications, and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) was obtained. It is found that the suggested approximate designs achieved a better PSNR for all image applications, and the results were superior to those of their counterparts.
items.venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)

items.title: Analysis of the impact of natural language selection in large language models on energy consumption
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference is computationally intensive, yet the extent to which the interaction language affects energy consumption remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether inference energy consumption varies across six European languages: Polish, English, German, French, Spanish, and Russian. Three open-weight models, Llama3.1-8b, Gemma-3-12b, and Qwen2.5-14b, were evaluated using ten semantically equivalent prompts, each translated into the six languages and repeated three times. Experiments were conducted on a workstation-class server equipped with an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT GPU and the Ollama inference framework. Whole-system power consumption was measured using a calibrated HIOKI PW3337 power meter, and energy efficiency was expressed as energy per generated token (EPT). Mean EPT varied substantially among models: Llama3.1-8b consumed 6.43 J/token, Qwen2.5-14b 10.23 J/token, and Gemma-3-12b 10.87 J/token. Kruskal–Wallis tests identified statistically significant between-language differences only for Llama3.1-8b; no sig - nificant differences were found for Qwen2.5-14b or Gemma-3-12b. However, regression analysis for Llama3.1-8b showed that response length was the dominant predictor of EPT, as fixed inference overhead was amortized over longer outputs. The findings indicate that apparent language-dependent differences in inference energy are driven primarily by generated-output length rather than by language itself. Energy efficiency also depends strongly on model architecture, tokenizer behavior, and inference implementation, highlighting the importance of response-length control and whole-system measurement in Green AI benchmarking.
items.venue: Advances in Science and Technology Research Journal

items.title: An Improved Signal Mixing Method Based on Tunnel Magnetoresistance-Rogowski Coil Sensors for SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Wide-band current sensors with DC capability are crucial for characterizing both steady state and high-frequency transients in switched-mode power electronics and digital control. Traditional hybrid sensors often suffer from complex circuitry, need for precise tuning, high component count, and elevated cost. This article presents an improved signal mixing method based on tunneling magnetoresistive (TMR) sensors and Rogowski coil sensors. By directly winding the TMR output leads into a Rogowski coil, which is the distinctive design of this work, the two signals are combined without additional complex circuitry. Using only one hybrid integrator, the proposed method achieves a bandwidth from DC to 54.9 MHz, significantly simplifying design and reducing cost. The sensor exhibits linear deviation within 2% and a resolution of 0.1 A at 5 MHz. Double-pulse tests using SiC mosfets further demonstrate its potential for switch transient testing of high-frequency power semiconductors.

items.title: Active-Clamped Stepwise Modulation for Independent Control of dv/dt and di/dt in Medium-Voltage Voltage Source Converters Based on Series-Connected SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Voltage source converters (VSCs) based on series-connected SiC mosfets provide a compact alternative to modular multilevel converters in medium-voltage applications. However, the fast switching of SiC mosfets produces excessive dv/dt and di/dt, which may cause electromagnetic interference and voltage overshoot. To address these issues, this article proposes an active-clamped stepwise modulation method that exploits the existing voltage-balancing active clamping modules to achieve controllable dv/dt and di/dt. By actively switching the auxiliary switches during the dead-time interval, the arm-voltage transition is first shaped into a stepwise waveform, and the subsequent current commutation is then independently regulated. As a result, the arm-voltage and arm-current transitions do not overlap, which relieves the hard-switching stress of the main power devices and enables independent control of dv/dt and di/dt. The operating principles of the proposed method over a fundamental cycle and the design guidelines for the key parameters are presented. The proposed method is experimentally validated on a 3.6-kV/35-A VSC prototype with six series-connected SiC mosfets in each arm. Experimental results show an 81% reduction in voltage overshoot and a 48% reduction in common-mode current while maintaining robust voltage balancing among the series-connected devices. These improvements are achieved with negligible impact on the overall efficiency.

items.title: ALPS: An Application-Aware, Length-Predictive Scheduler for Efficient LLM Inference at Edge
