Pour ce faire, nous développons une approche combinant grands modèles de langage (LLMs) et modèles de classification supervisée. On soulignera que la classification en domaines de connaissances a déjà fait l’objet de plusieurs études computationnelles sur l’Encyclopédie de Diderot & d’Alembert (Horton et al. 2009, Roe et al. 2016, Brenon et al. 2022), mais qu’aucune n’a été conduite à ce jour sur le DUFLT.Dans une première partie, nous présenterons les choix méthodologiques qui structurent notre démarche. Nous justifierons le choix du paragraphe comme unité de base de nos analyses, le regroupement des marques de domaine (simples : en termes de géographie ...; complexes : Terme de Botanique & de Pharmacie) en un nombre restreint de « macro-domaines ». Nous aborderons également les difficultés liées à l’hétérogénéité de ces marques et à la nature parfois pluri-/inter-disciplinaire de leurs contenus.Dans une seconde partie, nous décrirons le protocole expérimental mis en œuvre. À partir d’un ensemble de paragraphes initialement pourvus d’une ou plusieurs marques de domaine (que l’on aura retirées), nous sollicitons différents LLMs dans un cadre de classification few-shot afin de leur faire associer un ou plusieurs macro-domaines. Les prédictions sont ensuite évaluées par comparaison avec les annotations existantes. Cette phase permet d’identifier les configurations de prompts et les modèles les plus performants, et d’affiner progressivement les instructions fournies aux modèles. Les résultats préliminaires montrent qu’un des modèles testés (Gemini 3.5 Flash) atteint un F-score proche de 70 % sur un jeu d’évaluation encore limité à une cinquantaine de paragraphes. L’extension de ce jeu de test constitue une étape importante afin d’obtenir une mesure plus robuste des performances.Le meilleur modèle sera ensuite appliqué à un ensemble de paragraphes dépourvus de marque de domaine. Les annotations produites feront l’objet d’une validation et d’une correction manuelle, permettant la constitution d’un corpus de référence (gold standard). Ce corpus servira à l’entraînement d’un modèle de classification supervisée fondé sur une architecture Transformer de type encodeur, mieux adaptée à un déploiement à grande échelle sur l’ensemble du dictionnaire.Nous montrerons que cette approche progressive, associant annotation assistée par LLM et apprentissage supervisé, permet non seulement d’améliorer la couverture de l’annotation thématique du DUFLT, mais aussi d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour l’étude de l’organisation des savoirs dans les dictionnaires encyclopédiques du XVIIIe siècle.

items.title: Hoss: Fast Oblivious Semantic Search with Heterogeneous GPU-CPU-TEE Architecture
items.abstract: Semantic search is widely deployed in modern AI systems, but protecting both data contents and access patterns remains challenging. The current state-of-the-art system, Compass, achieves oblivious semantic search by building an optimized ORAM over HNSW graphs. However, even with aggressive optimizations, it still incurs large overheads. Closing this performance gap is fundamentally difficult: Compass has already removed most cryptographic overheads, leaving ORAM accesses as the dominant cost, which are constrained by well-known Omega(log N) bandwidth lower bounds. Our key insight is that traditional ORAM overhead stems from the assumption of limited private memory, whereas modern GPU TEEs provide large private memory (Pmem) that blinds internal access patterns (Hunt et al., NSDI '23). This shift opens a new design space. We therefore propose Hoss, a first-of-its-kind oblivious semantic search system with a heterogeneous CPU-GPU TEE architecture that supports fast, scalable search with low cost of ownership. In Hoss, the GPU TEE's large Pmem hosts the hot-path HNSW traversal, while the lower layers of the graph, if they exceed GPU capacity, are offloaded to CPU TEEs. The system invokes oblivious primitives only when accessing these lower layers. The availability of large Pmem also enables new optimization opportunities. For example, Hoss features a host-access ORAM mechanism that goes beyond traditional performance constraints and incorporates several data-dependent optimizations that are not possible in prior designs. We implement a prototype of Hoss and benchmark it against Compass. Our results show that Hoss achieves up to 67x speedup while maintaining high recall, with larger gains at scale.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Heterogeneous Memristive Neuromorphic Computing with Physics-Aware Cross-Modal Attention for Energy-Efficient Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) is a crucial technology for achieving emotional intelligence in human–computer interaction. However, the substantial computational demands of MER models currently overwhelm the capacities of resource-constrained edge devices. To address this problem, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Memristive Neural Network for Multimodal Emotion Recognition. The proposed network adopts a hardware–algorithm co-design approach, in which different memristive devices are assigned to different modal processing tasks according to their physical characteristics. Specifically, highly stable filamentary memristors are utilized to construct deterministic feature extraction pathways for text and video, whereas highly plastic Phase-Change Memory (PCM) crossbar arrays are designed for audio encoding. Based on the high plasticity of PCM, a memristive cross-modal attention network is further designed to achieve dynamic and adaptive multimodal feature fusion. Furthermore, a collaborative weight update method is proposed. During weight updates, the inherent writing noise and conductance drift of PCM are utilized as hardware-level regularization and automatic sparse learning strategies. Simulation experiments conducted on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets using the MemTorch framework demonstrate that the proposed neural network maintains recognition accuracy comparable to GPU baseline models, even when accounting for device non-idealities. Overall, the proposed neural network effectively resolves the “performance–power” conflict when deploying high-performance MER models on resource-constrained edge devices, providing an efficient and stable neuromorphic computing solution for edge applications.

items.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach
items.abstract: Adapting general Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to Autonomous Driving (AD) is thought to require heavy 3D spatial priors or intrusive architectural overhauls to compensate for a lack of spatial grounding. In this work, we present a counterintuitive pilot study: off-the-shelf general VLMs already exhibit remarkable adaptability across diverse driving tasks, while precise metric depth remains the primary missing link, a bottleneck readily addressable via onboard sensors and depth foundation models. To this end, we introduce the Triplet Incremental Training Framework, a non-intrusive paradigm that seamlessly instills 3D geometric awareness into a general VLM backbone while fully preserving its open-world capabilities. Driven by automatically constructed (image, depth, QA pair) triplets, our framework operates via a unified tri-stream training pipeline: an unfrozen primary VLM stream to adapt to driving tasks, an auxiliary depth stream that guides the visual backbone to implicitly imagine 3D scene geometry via explicit geometric constraints, and a frozen twin VLM stream employing logit-level KL distillation to prevent semantic drift. Crucially, the auxiliary depth branch is discarded during deployment, ensuring the enhanced geometric awareness comes with zero inference overhead. We evaluate our framework across four major benchmarks targeting four diverse capabilities spanning 3D spatial perception, driving-oriented language reasoning, end-to-end planning, and general multimodal understanding. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art driving VLMs, rivals domain-specific expert models in 3D perception, and successfully retains its original general reasoning capabilities. This demonstrates that Triplet Incremental Training offers a unified, deployment-ready paradigm for transforming general foundation models into robust driving intelligences.

items.title: Flexible Low-Voltage Thin-Film Transistors for Logic Circuits and Neuromorphic Computing Applications
items.abstract: Flexible thin-film transistors (TFTs) operating at low voltage are key building blocks for next-generation wearable electronics and brain-inspired systems, yet simultaneously achieving low-voltage operation, environmental robustness and multifunctionality remains a great challenge. In this work, flexible indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) TFTs based on a solution-processed nanocomposite gate dielectric were fabricated, in which the introduced nanofiller effectively enhanced the capacitance, mechanical strength and moisture resistance of the polymer dielectric. The resulting devices exhibit an on/off ratio over 106 and can be fully turned on at a gate voltage below 1 V. After 2000 bending cycles, 90-day ambient aging and 3600 s continuous gate-bias stress, the threshold voltage and subthreshold swing show only slight drifts and the on/off ratio remains above 106, demonstrating outstanding mechanical durability, anti-aging capability and bias stability. On this basis, a logic inverter was constructed, which delivers a peak voltage gain of ~9 at a supply voltage of 2.5 V and realizes stable dynamic inversion for low-frequency square-wave signals. Owing to the tunable ion migration and electric double-layer polarization of the gate dielectric, the TFTs emulate typical biological synaptic behaviors, including pulse-dependent potentiation, long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). Neural network simulations based on device conductance states achieve accuracy of ~90% on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset and 88.1% on the challenging Stanford Cars vehicle dataset. This work verifies that the developed flexible TFTs possess dual functions of logic operation and neuromorphic computing, providing a feasible solution for the development of high-performance flexible low-power electronic devices and brain-inspired vision systems.

items.title: FlatSeek: LLM-Driven Symbolic Discovery of Flat Outputs via Backward Data Generation
items.abstract: Differential flatness enables efficient planning and control, but discovering explicit flat outputs for general nonlinear systems remains difficult due to the lack of general methods and supervised data. We propose FlatSeek, a framework combining backward data generation with task-specific large language model (LLM) training. By reversing the defining reconstruction of flatness, we generate system-flat-output pairs with known certificates, then fine-tune an LLM to propose symbolic flat-output candidates for unseen dynamics. On literature and synthetic benchmarks, FlatSeek outperforms both the traditional symbolic methods and the untuned reference models in flat-output discovery success, and uncovers alternative symbolic flat outputs not reported in the literature.

items.title: First-principles investigation of small polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3
items.abstract: Sodium niobate ( NaNbO 3 ) is a perovskite oxide and a key component of emerging lead-free antiferroelectric capacitors for high-energy-density applications. However, its performance can be hindered by irreversible phase transitions and leakage currents associated with low electrical resistivity. Defect and doping engineering offers a potential way to overcome these problems, but its use requires a detailed understanding of electronic, ionic, and polaron charge-compensation mechanisms, where the role of polarons remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the stability of small hole and electron polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3 , which is a structurally well-defined model system that avoids lattice-dynamical instabilities. Trapping energies are calculated using density functional theory corrected by a Hubbard U , using the enforced-piecewise-linearity approach including finite-size scaling. For the small hole-polaron centered on O- 2 p orbital, we find a trapping energy of − 0.65 eV and an adiabatic migration barrier of 0.32 eV determined by nudged-elastic-band calculations. In contrast, we show that excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb- 4 d orbitals, reflecting weak electron-phonon coupling in the conduction band manifold. These results identify oxygen as an intrinsic hole trap in NaNbO 3 and highlight the importance of including hole polarons in defect models of NaNbO 3 -based electroceramics.

items.title: FPSRG: Heterogeneous User Simulation First-Person Post-Training and Multidimensional Semantic Response Grids
items.abstract: Simulating heterogeneous individuals with large language models is an active research direction, and heterogeneous user simulation requires models with different characteristics. We study profile construction: given dimensions, items, and scoring rules, build model configurations that can be retrieved by multidimensional target scores. We introduce First-Person Semantic Response Grids (FPSRG). Shared post-training first teaches the model to judge and answer as the participant; self-report and behavioral targets then refine dimension-specific control vectors. With the model frozen, we measure joint scores for vector-coefficient combinations, filter inadmissible configurations, and store the results in a searchable catalog. Per-token configuration routing, continuous batching, and isolated caches support parallel measurement of different profiles. Non-thinking five- and ten-dimensional Qwen instances and a thinking-mode six-dimensional instance following full-parameter post-training of Huihui demonstrate the complete workflow. With matched data, layers, and norms, refinement increases mean five-axis composite control span from 30.75 to 40.45. Within the five-dimensional 25-75 target region, the qualified five-level vector catalog covers 92.2% of fixed targets under per-axis error at most 20 and total error at most 60; combining it with the prompt catalog increases coverage to 98.7%. At a fixed coefficient range, three-, five-, and nine-level catalogs achieve 71.2%, 92.2%, and 94.6% coverage, demonstrating the gains from denser measurement. These results describe measured reachable regions under a fixed assessment protocol. Through shared adaptation, a small set of learned directions, and reusable joint measurements, FPSRG constructs heterogeneous individual configurations without retraining a model for every profile.

items.title: Evaluating Video LLMs'Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
items.abstract: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as"corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io

items.title: Enhancement of the Mechanical Properties of Low-k SiCOH Films by Plasma Treatment and Ultraviolet Curing
items.abstract: The integration of organosilicate SiCOH low-k dielectrics in back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnect structures requires a balance between low k and sufficient mechanical robustness. Low-k films with a thickness of approximately 2800 Å were deposited on 300 mm Si wafers via plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) using diethoxymethylsilane (DEMS) and O2 at 260 °C. To investigate the effects of process engineering on film properties, the total film thickness was divided into one, two, three, five, or 10 sublayers to compare segmentation, cyclic O2/He-plasma treatment, and interleaved ultraviolet (UV) curing. The resulting films were characterized by spectroscopic ellipsometry, nanoindentation, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiles, and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Segmentation increased the k value from 3.35 to 3.66, accompanied by a non-monotonic mechanical response. Extending the plasma treatment from 1 to 20 s led to a 19.8% rise in the k value, along with respective increases of 9.4% in hardness and 16.1% in the modulus, consistent with carbon/hydride removal and oxidative densification of the silicate network. Increasing RF power from 300 to 900 W caused smaller dielectric changes while raising the hardness and modulus by 8.7% and 10.6%, respectively, indicating diminishing changes at higher applied powers. Interleaved UV curing, comprising UV irradiation and concurrent thermal treatment, reduced the thickness, increased the refractive index (RI), and maintained a lower k relative to the as-deposited films. After five UV curing cycles, the hardness and modulus reached the highest mean values of 4.6 GPa and 35.8 GPa, respectively. FTIR analysis showed systematic depletion of Si–CH3 and Si–H groups and Si–O–Si network evolution, whereas XPS showed relatively stable plateau composition but treatment-sensitive transition regions. The combined results are consistent with oxidation-related modification during plasma treatment and network reorganization during UV curing, with possible differences in the spatial extent of these processes. These results further indicate that an intermediate cycle count provides a favorable balance between dielectric and mechanical properties.

items.title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
items.abstract: Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10-10 m2V-1s-1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2-SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu-Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

items.title: Development and validation of a scale assessing perceived trustworthiness in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly part of everyday life, yet there is no established way to measure how users evaluate their trustworthiness. This study introduces the Perceived Trustworthiness of LLMs scale (PT-LLM-8), a self-report psychometric instrument measuring users’ perceived trustworthiness of their primary LLM. PT-LLM-8 is developed from the TrustLLM framework and adapted as a human-centred measure. The PT-LLM-8 comprises eight items representing truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, transparency, accountability, and compliance with laws. Psychometric properties of the scale were tested with 752 LLM users in the United Kingdom (Mean age = 28.58, SD = 6.11, 50.3% males, 48.8% females). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a one-factor structure, with high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.90, Composite Reliability = 0.91, strong item-total correlations (ranged between 0.62 and 0.75), and measurement invariance across gender. The total score measures overall perceived trustworthiness, while individual item responses may also be examined descriptively for information about the content represented by each item. For researchers, practitioners, and developers, the PT-LLM-8 offers a practical instrument for evaluating interventions, comparing groups and contexts, and examining whether technical safeguards are reflected in users’ perceived trustworthiness of LLM. The scale can also be applied to guide system design, support policy development, and help organisations monitor shifts in user trust toward LLMs over time, making it applicable across research, practice, and governance.

items.title: Deterministic Agentic Workflows and Cognitive Enterprise Search Framework (2026)
items.abstract: This technical report outlines the architectural paradigms required to deploy autonomous AI agents and enterprise cognitive search systems within strict corporate governance parameters. While large language models demonstrate high conversational capability, enterprise adoption requires deterministic tool execution, verifiable grounding, and full EU AI Act compliance. Enterprise AI consulting and operational frameworks are provided by Heinrich Co, developing tailored intelligence roadmaps for global institutions. 1. Cognitive Search & Enterprise Knowledge Synthesis Conventional keyword retrieval systems fail to capture semantic relationships across distributed corporate repositories. Implementing hybrid vector embeddings alongside deterministic BM25 lexical search enables context-aware discovery without hallucination risks. Review implementation details in AI Powered Enterprise Search. 2. AI Readiness & Corporate Operational Audits Successful AI transformation requires data hygiene, schema standardization, and organizational alignment. Before deploying autonomous agent pipelines, enterprises must assess infrastructure feasibility. Reference the structured framework in AI Readiness Consulting Assessment Deliverables. 3. Executive Governance and Future-Proof Roadmaps Strategic deployment must balance rapid innovation with ethical risk management and regulatory accountability. Learn more in the executive analysis Foreword Blog En.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Designing Institutions for Autonomous AI
items.abstract: As autonomous AI agents increasingly interact in persistent populations, their collective capabilities and alignment depend not only on individual models, but also on the institutions governing their interactions. Yet AI research has largely focused on individual agents. In this Perspective, we argue that institutional design must become a distinct focus of AI research. Drawing on institutional political economy, social epistemology and organizational theory, we develop seven principles for designing AI institutions that sustain cooperation, enable reliable collective judgments and remain accountable to legitimate human purposes. These address reciprocal contributions, accountable authority, functional differentiation, epistemic pluralism, criticism and correction, human direction, and institutional adaptation. We illustrate their application through machine science, where autonomous research challenges institutions developed around human capabilities and constraints. We then propose an experimental research programme in which matched populations of AI agents operate under alternative institutional arrangements, and describe MoltJournal, an API-first journal for autonomous research agents, as an illustration of how such institutions can be made programmable and observable. Together, these contributions establish institutional design as a research agenda concerned not only with aligning autonomous agents, but with understanding how institutions can transform them into capable, reliable and accountable collectives.

items.title: Data-Driven Estimation of Ship Manoeuvring Hydrodynamic Derivatives using a Hybrid MARUS–PINN Framework with LLM-Guided Symbolic Discovery
items.abstract: Identification of hydrodynamic derivatives that govern ship manoeuvring behaviour for autonomous vessels such as unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is essential for diverse maritime purposes including oceanographic research, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation. However, conventional hydrodynamic modelling approaches, such as classical manoeuvring models, experimental methods, and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD), are often labour-intensive, costly, and time-consuming, and their estimated parameters may not fully capture real-world operating conditions due to nonlinearities, scale effects, and complex sea states. With the advent of machine learning, recent advances in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a promising alternative by embedding governing fluid-dynamic equations directly into the neural learning network, providing the advantages of data-driven learning while maintaining physical consistency. Hence, this thesis investigates a novel approach that combines Marine Robotics Unity Simulator (MARUS)–simulated manoeuvring data, PINN-based parameter learning, and symbolic discovery via Large Language Models (LLMs) to estimate hydrodynamic derivatives with improved robustness, reduced data requirements, and enhanced interpretability compared to conventional system identification methods, while promoting interoperability and standardization through its modular design. To evaluate this hybrid approach, the thesis addresses the following research question: Can a hybrid MARUS–PINN–LLM framework provide more accurate, interpretable, and data-efficient estimates of manoeuvring hydrodynamic derivatives than conventional system identification methods? To this end, an extensive set of experiments and ablation studies is conducted to compare the proposed hybrid model with its purely data-driven and purely physics-based counterparts across parameter accuracy, trajectory reconstruction quality, and generalization to diverse maneuvering conditions of various industry-standard USVs. The results demonstrate that integrating symbolic discovery with PINNs reduces sway-acceleration error by 86%, yaw-rate acceleration error by 66%, and heading-rollout error by 89% relative to purely data-driven baselines, producing compact, physically consistent residual terms that align with established nonlinear hydrodynamic effects while its physics-only counterparts catastrophically diverge from the ground-truths. Taken together, these findings highlight the potential of hybrid physics–machine-learning frameworks to advance the estimation of manoeuvring coefficients for the next generation of autonomous marine systems.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
items.abstract: Multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate text through iterative masked denoising with bidirectional attention, offering a compelling alternative to autoregressive vision-language modeling. However, each denoising step requires a full forward pass over long multimodal sequences in which visual tokens dominate the sequence length, and a fixed step budget further compounds this quadratic per-step cost. Existing inference acceleration approaches for multimodal dLLMs characterize attention redundancy implicitly, motivating designs from isolated attention visualizations rather than from measurement. We close this gap with DRAMA, a training-free acceleration framework grounded in a systematic dissection of attention redundancy in multimodal dLLMs. By probing attention tensors along spatial and temporal axes, we reveal two persistent redundancy structures: (i) attention mass consistently concentrates on a sparse subset of visual tokens, and (ii) attention distributions rapidly stabilize across denoising steps after an initial formation phase. These findings motivate two complementary mechanisms: Spatial-Redundancy-Aware Visual Token Pruning (SVTP) and Sufficiency-Guided Adaptive Stopping (SGAS). Together, DRAMA achieves an average 18.67 times inference speedup across six vision-language benchmarks without training, architectural modification, or attention caching, while maintaining competitive accuracy. Our results establish a strong, measurement-grounded acceleration baseline for multimodal dLLM inference.

items.title: DDRop: Active Memory Interposer Attacks on Confidential VMs by Dropping DDR5 Writes
items.abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) are increasingly deployed in the cloud to protect sensitive workloads through hardware-enforced isolation, remote attestation, and transparent memory encryption. However, to meet memory performance and size demands, modern TEEs omit cryptographic freshness guarantees, leaving them vulnerable to replay attacks by adversaries with physical memory access. Prior work demonstrated low-cost active interposition attacks on DDR4 without requiring expensive specialized equipment, but these techniques do not extend to DDR5, where existing approaches are limited to passive ciphertext side-channel analysis and rely on bus downclocking to accommodate legacy memory bus analyzers. We present the first low-cost (<200$) DDR5 RDIMM interposer capable of active fault injection at native speeds. By injecting targeted parity errors to silently discard cache line writebacks, we introduce DDRop, a new primitive that exploits the absence of cryptographic freshness to break the integrity of Intel TDX, Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP. Building on this primitive and targeting the APIs exposed by the TDX module and AMD Secure Processor, we show that adversaries can gain ciphertext access, copy arbitrary victim pages, and inject malicious secure page-table entries. We demonstrate end-to-end attacks on an up-to-date TDX platform, including forcing any TD into debug mode and forging attestation reports. While software-level mitigations, including timing-based interposer detection and API hardening, may reduce the attack surface, our results demonstrate that active DDR5 bus interposition is practical at low cost, highlighting the need for robust cryptographic memory integrity protections against physical adversaries.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
items.abstract: A hosted score in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent competition is one noisy number, so development needs a local evaluator that is fast, safe for agent-written code, and matching the hosted scorer's prompts. drydock-eval evaluates a small coding agent (Gemma 4 E4B) at about 250 runs per hour on one RTX 5090. Contain runs each job in a fresh container without network and passed 200 scripted escape tests; conform provides eight checks that compare a local stack's requests with the scorer's configuration, down to rendered tokens; compare provides paired statistics that respect repository clusters. AI agents built and attacked the kit; a human owner approved machine use and release. This extended version repeats the short paper and adds the full record of the experiments made with and around the kit: 9,660 rows of agent runs, 2,494 grading controls and 72 serving measurements, all released. On four L4 GPUs the 31B model decodes 38.1 tokens per second in one stream and E4B 105.8. Six configurations of a 31B agent solved between 37 and 44 of 70 development tasks, and no pairwise difference was detected. A pre-registered five-arm experiment (231 tasks, 4,620 jobs) measured four prompt divergences: no E4B solve-rate change was detected (largest estimate -2.1 points, 95% interval -4.4 to +0.4). Three changes of the E4B agent led their screens by +1.0 to +6.2 points; each was then tested once on new tasks under a frozen pass rule, and none was confirmed (gains -0.35, -0.39 and +4.10 points). The unchanged baseline, run again on the same 128 tasks, moved by 1.17 points, and 65% of these tasks were solved in none of eight runs. Prompts and agent bundles are withheld; every run-level result is public.

items.title: Conserved amount, negotiable placement. Prompting perturbs one architecture, an AI reviewer both
items.abstract: Tesler's conservation law holds that a problem carries an irreducible amount of complexity. Brooks separates that essential part from the accidental part a solution adds. If the essential part is fixed, architecture is placement rather than quantity, and the question is which levers move placement. An AI agent implements sixty accumulating change requests on one REST endpoint under two architectures, a mutative Spring controller and an additive OfficeFloor pipeline, under five conditions, ten runs per cell, model fixed. Four are external controls, from a bare change request to the disclosed structural cost function. The fifth is different in kind. A second agent reviews each change and reasons about cohesion itself. Amount is steady. Across all ten cells the finished complexity varies by 7% to 20% over four operationalisations, and the complexity the sixty rules added by 21% to 29% within an architecture. Placement is not. Under the four external controls the plasticity ratio between the architectures is near 1 on six amount metrics (five of six intervals contain 1) against 2.7 to 10.0 on eleven placement metrics (ten of eleven above 1). The mutative architecture moves, the additive one does not, and the disclosed formula brings it to the additive arm's untouched placement. The AI reviewer is the one lever that moves the additive arm, on one family only. It consolidates the pipeline, raising change- and mass-concentration on every such metric, interval excluding zero, while leaving coupling, file count and per-node complexity untouched. The price is reported in full. Strict correctness fell in most comparisons though each rule was implemented correctly in over 99% of checkpoints, and all three outcome measures favour the concentrated codebase. The contribution is a measurable property of an architecture and its lever, not a verdict on either.

items.title: Climate Temporal Temperature Prediction via an Adaptive Stacked Bidirectional Residual Mamba Network
items.abstract: Accurate temperatures forecasting relies on traditional meteorological parameters that are essential for monitoring weather informatics and guiding forecasting efforts. This study presents Deep DualMamba, a novel deep learning framework for temporal temperature prediction, built upon an enhanced variant of the recently proposed Mamba network. Unlike conventional Transformer-based architectures, which dominate foundation models but suffer from computational inefficiencies on long sequences, Deep DualMamba leverages selective structured state space models (SSMs) to achieve both scalability and performance. We identify a core limitation of prior subquadratic-time models-namely, their inability to perform long-term and robust forecasting and introduce two key innovations. First, we propose an adaptive bidirectional Mamba as encoders to learn complex and efficient features. Second, we develop a hardware-aware, parallel recurrent algorithm to compensate for the loss of convolutional efficiency, ensuring practical viability at scale. Last, the Deep DualMamba's approximation ability and convergence is theoretical analyzed. These design choices culminate in a simplified, attention- and MLP-free neural architecture that exhibits linear complexity with sequence length and significantly improved inference throughput. To demonstrate its applicability in climate informatics, we implement a full forecasting pipeline using historical meteorological data from UK monitoring stations.

items.title: Calibration and Conformal Prediction for Medical Question Answering in Arabic and English: Evidence from Two Non-Parallel Benchmarks
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly tested on medical exam questions, but accuracy alone does not show when an answer can be trusted. I study the calibration and uncertainty of two open-weight models, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Jais-adapted-7B-chat (both run in 4-bit precision), on 2,816 English multiple-choice questions from MedMCQA and 4,927 Arabic multiple-choice questions from MedAraBench. Accuracy was 0.561 (English) and 0.430 (Arabic) for Qwen, and 0.369 and 0.308 for Jais. Raw option probabilities were overconfident in all four settings (expected calibration error 0.242 to 0.486), and a single temperature parameter removed 82% to 93% of that error. Split conformal prediction reached its nominal coverage in all 24 settings I tested (within 0.006), but the sets were large when accuracy was low: at 90% coverage, temperature-scaled sets contained on average 63% (Qwen, English), 78% (Qwen, Arabic), 86% (Jais, English) and 89% (Jais, Arabic) of the options. The margin between the top two option probabilities separated correct from incorrect answers best for Qwen on English (AUROC 0.734) and worst for Jais on Arabic (0.579). Answering only the 20% most confident questions lowered Qwen's English error from 0.439 to 0.098. Jais showed a strong prior for option C (49% of English and 60% of Arabic predictions). Scoring Latin letters only cut the Arabic share to 29% but left accuracy, raw ECE and AUROC nearly unchanged. Because the two benchmarks differ in subject, level and number of options, I do not attribute differences between languages to language itself. Code is available at https://github.com/Mariyaaleem/arabic-english-medqa-uncertainty.

items.title: CNTFET Based Low Power SRAM Design: Architectures, Challenges and Innovative Implementations
items.abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) takes on a vital role in digital technology especially for applications that demand high speed and low power consumption. However, there are top priority with leakage power, reliability and stability owing to continuous technological advancement and the demand for energy efficient systems. Thorough research of low power SRAM design approaches is presented with an emphasis on cutting edge cell topologies and innovative device technologies. Power efficiency, read/write stability and area overhead are examined for various SRAM designs including 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T and 10T cells. Special attention is focused on SRAM designs using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor (CNTFET) which provide excellent electrical characteristics and less leakage than conventional silicon enabled methods. Subthreshold operation and assist methods that enable ultra low voltage capability are also included in the article. To further emphasize the need of low power SRAM designs, growing application domains like Internet of Things (IoT), biomedical systems and Compute-In-Memory architectures are investigated. Major performance deals and design trends are identified through a comparative analysis of this research. In order to facilitate growth of next generation low power SRAM systems, important challenges and future research directions are finally specified.

items.title: CNN on ‘Top’: In search of scalable and lightweight image-based jet taggers
items.abstract: Abstract While Transformer-based and standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be the best performers in classifying different types of jets, they require substantial computational power. We explore the scope of using a lightweight and scalable version of EfficientNet architecture, along with global features of the jet. The end product is computationally inexpensive but is capable of competitive performance. We showcase the efficacy of our network in tagging top-quark jets in a sea of other light quark and gluon jets. The work also sheds light on the importance of global features for both the accuracy and the apparent redundancy of the network’s complexity.

items.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference at datacenter scale is fundamentally bottlenecked by memory capacity and bandwidth limits. Because model weights are read-only and identical across instances, conventional architectures that replicate these parameters across the local DRAM of tens of thousands of accelerators incur massive capital expenditures, significant static power dissipation, and redundant memory-fetch energy. A recent proposal to use optical fiber loops as delay-line memory alleviates these issues, but its recirculating loop must hold the whole model: loop length grows with model size, slack is fixed when the ring is built, and the layouts that serve modern Mixture of Experts (MoE) models efficiently do not fit in it. We propose Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), an open-ended hierarchical Tap-and-Amplify fiber architecture that generalizes and replaces the optical ring paradigm. A centralized memory server continuously broadcasts weights to distributed inference nodes that passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics, delivering parameters directly to compute units without intermediate buffering. To overcome the limitations of continuous weight streaming, we use dynamically-sized slack to accommodate large and variable context lengths. We show how removing the restrictions of the optical ring allows OBM to efficiently serve MoE models. Evaluated at a datacenter scale of 80,000 accelerators, OBM eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system.

items.title: Beyond PCIe Thrashing and Recursive Sandboxes: High-Throughput 30B Sparse MoE Inference and Symbolic-Gated Hallucination Verification on 4 GB VRAM Workstations
items.abstract: Deploying frontier-scale Large Language Models (LLMs) in the 30-billion-parameter class locally on standard enterprise workstations—typically equipped with 32 GB of host DRAM and an entry-level 4 GB VRAM discrete GPU—presents severe memory capacity and interconnect bandwidth bottlenecks. Existing consumer offloading frameworks rely on dynamic runtime migration of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) weights across the PCIe bus or multi-turn recursive code-execution sandboxes for factual verification, both of which incur prohibitive latency on 4 GB GPUs and introduce security risks in enterprise environments. In this paper, we present an end-to-end heterogeneous inference and neuro-symbolic verification architecture evaluated on a standard enterprise workstation (Intel Core i7-12700K, 32 GB DRAM, NVIDIA T1000 4 GB VRAM) running a 30.5B-parameter sparse MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B). First, we demonstrate empirically that dynamic GPU LRU expert caching degrades token generation throughput by 54.1% (from 18.68 to 8.57 tokens/s) on a 4 GB GPU due to synchronous PCIe cache-miss thrashing. To eliminate runtime PCIe migration, we propose Static Frequency-Based Tensor Partitioning combined with Selective Top-K Softmax Expert Pruning and Hybrid CPU Performance-Core Pinning. By permanently pinning 100% of dense Shared Attention, Router Gate, and Output Head tensors alongside M = 7 full MoE layers in 4 GB VRAM (3,762 MiB allocated), locking the remaining 41 sparse expert layers in aligned SIMD host RAM on Performance cores, and restricting active routing to the Top-4 experts per layer (~1.5B active parameters/token, capturing >92% router probability mass), we achieve 39.18 tokens/s sustained generation (5.7x speedup over cold baseline) and reduce Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency by 147x (from 42,811.7 ms to 290.9 ms) while leaving 20.5 GB of host RAM free. Second, we analyze Regime-Aware Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding using a 386 MB Qwen3-0.6B draft model, demonstrating a 94.8% draft token acceptance rate that accelerates full 8-expert inference by +45.1% (18.68 to 27.11 tokens/s). Finally, as a zero-code-execution alternative to Recursive Language Models (RLM), we introduce a Symbolic-Gated Conditional Neural Critic that audits streamed outputs for numerical fidelity and abstract syntax tree (AST) validity in <2 ms (0.403 ms mean), triggering a low-temperature (tau = 0.10) neural repair pass only when the deterministic Grounding Score falls below 100%.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Neural Networks for Differentially Private Tabular Data Synthesis
items.abstract: In differentially private (DP) tabular data synthesis, the consensus is that statistical models are better than neural network (NN)-based methods. However, we argue that this conclusion is incomplete and overlooks the challenge of densely correlated datasets, where intricate dependencies can overwhelm statistical models. In such complex scenarios, neural networks are more suitable due to their capacity to fit complex distributions by learning directly from samples. Despite this potential, existing NN-based algorithms still suffer from significant limitations. We therefore propose MargNet, incorporating successful algorithmic designs of statistical models into neural networks. MargNet applies an adaptive marginal selection strategy and trains the neural networks to generate data that conforms to the selected marginals. On sparsely correlated datasets, our approach achieves utility close to the best statistical method while offering an average 7$\times$ speedup over it. More importantly, on densely correlated datasets, MargNet establishes a new state-of-the-art, reducing fidelity error by up to 26\% compared to the previous best. We release our code on GitHub.\footnote{https://github.com/KaiChen9909/margnet}
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
items.abstract: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics. We challenge this empirically: across multiple NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, we find no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models. This raises a deeper question: given a pool of LLMs spanning frontier and freely hosted or open-weight models, how should one adaptively select which model to invoke at each step of the search? The challenge is non-trivial. The optimal LLM may shift over the course of a run, and because one LLM's output seeds the context for subsequent calls, each model's reward signal is non-stationary and entangled across the heuristic population, thus violating the independence assumptions of classical online decision-making settings. We address this through Ballad (Bandit-based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery), an online bandit algorithm that learns to orchestrate a pool of LLMs into an ensemble that matches or exceeds what any soloist LLM achieves alone. This orchestration is powered by an LLM selection policy that favors rare, high-scoring heuristics over stable averages, a DAG-based credit propagation mechanism through the genealogy of the heuristic population, and discounting of stale observations to remain attuned to each model's current utility. Across five NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems and a pool of four models of varying capability and cost, Ballad not only matches the best individual LLM in hindsight but, in several cases, surpasses every individual model while reducing API cost by up to 65.6% relative to always using the strongest model.

items.title: Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function
items.abstract: We expose a safety vulnerability on nascent agentic reinforcement-learning-as-a-service. Specifically, with a cost as low as \$20, we show that safety alignment of a large language model (e.g., Inkling) can be completely subverted through rounds of harmful agentic reinforcement learning (agentic RL) with a toxic environment from its users. We also demonstrate that upon a successful harmful agentic RL attack via the service API, the attackers can potentially use the safety-degraded model to assist with real-world harmful activities, e.g., exploit software vulnerabilities and launch code re-use attacks. To mitigate harmful agentic RL, we propose Bait, a defense that mitigates the attack via proactively probing the reward function. Experimental results show that such a simple defense can sufficiently mitigate learning from a harmful reward function and can still learn from a benign reward function that promotes benign agentic tasks. Further analysis on both empirical and theoretical aspects shows that an adaptive attacker who assumes the knowledge of Bait defense cannot perfectly subvert it due to a systematic challenge. Source code is available at https://github.com/git-disl/Bait.

items.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
items.abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

items.title: Area–power–delay Optimized RTL-To-GDSII VLSI Implementation of 16-Bit Ve-Dic Multiplier Using High-Speed Adders
items.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis and an ASIC-oriented design of a 16-bit Vedic Multiplier based on the Urdhva-Tiryakbhyam algorithm using Kogge-Stone (KSA), Carry Look-Ahead (CLA), and Carry Save (CSA) adders. The architectures are implemented in Verilog HDL and evaluated across 45 nm, 90 nm, and 180 nm technology nodes using the Cadence suite. Pre-layout synthesis metrics (cell count, delay, and power) are analyzed to study performance trade-offs across nodes. Furthermore, physical design placement and routing at 90 nm confirms ASIC standard-cell feasibility, although detailed post-route parasitic extraction is reserved for future hardware prototyping. Comparisons with FPGA-based works demonstrate significant improvements in speed and power efficiency, making the proposed KSA-based design highly suitable for high-speed, low-power VLSI and DSP applications.

items.title: Agents of Instruction: Co-Creating Learning Materials with AI Agents
items.abstract: AI agents are increasingly used by professional software developers to support tasks such as planning, coding, debugging, refactoring, and drafting documentation. Unlike basic chat models, AI agents work more autonomously toward a broader goal: breaking tasks into steps, taking actions, using tools, and iterating on their own output. Based on our experiences, similar agent-based workflows can be used to assist educators in generating and refining learning materials. In this hands-on tutorial, we will introduce participants to practical ways of using AI agents to support the development of computing education resources, including lecture slides, online textbook materials, programming exercises, explanations, analogies, and visualizations. We will compare different types of tools, including general-purpose AI systems and coding-focused agentic tools, and discuss when each may be useful for educational material generation. Participants will explore agent-based workflows through hands-on activities in which they create, revise, and adapt learning materials for their own teaching contexts. Throughout the tutorial, we will emphasize both the opportunities and limitations of these tools. We will also discuss ethical and practical issues, including copyright, citations, attribution, transparency, and responsible use. Drawing on the organizers' experiences, the tutorial will provide participants with concrete workflows, examples, and strategies for incorporating AI agents into the creation of learning materials in computing education.

items.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
items.abstract: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem in the form a solver receives it: the boundary meshes grouped by condition type, the prescribed values and the fluid properties. The 2,816 samples with a stable time mean form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, engineering metrics and 22 frozen splits, disjoint in geometry, that hold out geometry families, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of the inlet speed in single-seed runs (uniform inlet flow: 11.0%). ISLA, a transformer for boundary-driven PDEs, reaches 5.3% over four seeds, about 4 times the change from a finer mesh. On the same test samples, a held-out geometry family barely changes ISLA's error relative to uniform flow, and a held-out enclosure or boundary-condition layout raises it 2.4 to 9.2 times. The data and the scoring code will be released.

items.title: AI as a Calibration Anchor: Improving Grading Consistency in Large Introductory Programming Courses
items.abstract: Large introductory programming courses often rely on multiple teaching assistants (TAs) to grade open-ended submissions, where partial-credit decisions can vary even under shared rubrics. This experience report describes a human-in-the-loop AI-assisted grading workflow designed to make grading expectations more explicit to ensure consistency between TAs while preserving TA authority over final marks and feedback. The workflow combines instructor-authored rubrics with large language model-generated expansions that surface alternative correct solutions, common errors, and partial-credit cases. These are reviewed by instructors and refined through early TA disagreements before AI-generated marks and feedback are used as decision support that TAs can accept, revise, or reject. We deployed this workflow across two large introductory programming courses, analyzing final TA grades, AI suggestions, comparable pre-AI grading data where grading relied solely on instructor-generated rubrics, grading-time records, number of accepted remark requests, and anonymous survey responses from TAs. Across comparable programming questions from prior offerings, mean inter-TA grading variability decreased from 4.97% to 2.16% (56.5% reduction). Across 7,899 programming AI-TA grade pairs, AI suggestions differed from final TA grades by 2.43% of the maximum question score on average. We also observe higher grading speeds in some cases, and lower change in grade for accepted remark requests. Survey responses highlighted practical benefits: 94% of TAs reported that AI helped catch grading oversights, and 82% reported increased confidence in final grades and notes. Overall, this report illustrates a practical model for AI-assisted grading at scale: improving consistency through shared calibration without replacing human judgment.

items.title: A flexible language model-assisted electronic design automation framework
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming electronic design automation (EDA) by enhancing design stages such as schematic design, simulation, netlist synthesis, and place-and-route. Existing methods primarily focus these optimisations within isolated open-source EDA tools and often lack the flexibility to handle multiple domains, such as analogue, digital, and radio-frequency design. In contrast, modern systems require to interface with commercial EDA environments, adhere to tool-specific operation rules, and incorporate feedback from design outcomes while supporting diverse design flows. We propose a versatile framework that uses LLMs to generate files compatible with commercial EDA tools and optimise designs using power-performance-area reports. This is accomplished by guiding the LLMs with tool constraints and feedback from design outputs to meet tool requirements and user specifications. The framework is used to evaluate case studies on operational transconductance amplifiers, microstrip patch antennas, and FPGA circuits.

items.title: A Survey on LLMs from a Human-Centric Perspective
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) has positioned them as powerful computational instruments for human-centered research and applications, spanning tasks involving cognition, decision-making, and social interaction. This survey examines LLMs from a human-centric perspective organized around individual and collective levels. We first review LLM competencies across perception, analysis, integration, execution, and social interaction, highlighting both their demonstrated capabilities and the evaluation conditions under which these capabilities are observed. We then explore how LLMs are used across behavioral science, psychology, linguistics, political science, economics, and sociology as research tools, behavioral simulators, and objects of inquiry, covering both individual behavior and collective social processes. Finally, we identify challenges and future research directions, such as improving LLM adaptability, affective-to-behavior evaluation, and cultural sensitivity, while addressing inherent biases and enhancing frameworks for human-AI collaboration. This survey aims to provide a foundational understanding of LLMs from a human-centric perspective, offering insights into their current capabilities and potential for future development.

items.title: A Compact Low Power CCII-Based LIF Neuron with Memristive Synapse Exhibiting Synaptic Plasticity
items.abstract: Biological neural systems perform information processing through the collective operation of neurons and synapses, in which learning is achieved by activity-dependent modification of synaptic strength. Emulating these mechanisms in electronic circuits requires compact, low-power, and scalable implementations of spiking neurons and adaptive synapses. This paper presents a compact, low-power second-generation current conveyor (CCII)- based leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with a memristive synapse exhibiting synaptic plasticity. The proposed neuron operates in the current domain. It employs a CCII to implement weighted summation of presynaptic inputs, leaky membrane integration, and threshold-based spike generation using a low-power comparator and a PMOS-based reset mechanism. Both a resistor and a memristor are used to represent synaptic weights at the neuron inputs. At the same time, a memristive device is employed as the synapse in the learning model to provide continuously variable, emulated memristive conductance. In addition, spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is implemented, in which the relative timing difference between presynaptic and postsynaptic spikes governs the change in synaptic strength. A two-neuron system comprising a presynaptic and a postsynaptic neuron, interconnected via a memristor serving as the synapse, is used to demonstrate long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). During LTP, the memristor conductance increases, whereas during LTD, the conductance decreases, thereby demonstrating synaptic plasticity similar to biological systems. The proposed circuit is designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso using 0.18μm CMOS technology to verify its operational performance. Simulation results validate correct LIF operation, stable learning behaviour, and low power consumption (23 μW) in standard 0.18 μm CMOS technology, confirming the suitability of the proposed neuron-synapse architecture for neuromorphic computing systems.
items.venue: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers

items.title: (A)iSpy: Parasitic Trojans for Machine Learning Infrastructure
items.abstract: Modern machine learning (ML) pipelines depend heavily on third party libraries for graph compilation and hardware acceleration. While current practices audit data and model artifacts or rely on file integrity checks, the execution environment remains implicitly trusted. This blind spot enables active threats where a malicious runtime module interacts directly with live training and inference dynamics: exploiting this interaction allows the Trojan to support complex objectives that are challenging for static code or binary modifications, achieving manipulations impossible for standard data and model level attacks. We expose this vulnerability by presenting AiSPY, a parasitic infrastructure Trojan that subverts MLsystems through an active observe and execute paradigm. Operating within the computation graph, AiSPY monitors transient tensor states to perform targeted, stealthy manipulations with negligible overhead. To violate confidentiality, the Trojan identifies all critical training hyperparameters and covertly exfiltrates them via model weights or output logits. To break integrity, it acts as a gradient amplifier: by observing steganographic triggers, it transforms other- wise weak data poisoning into effective backdoor attacks, increasing success rates from near zero to 100%. We further demonstrate broad extensibility across the machine learning lifecycle by validating auxiliary attacks in the appendix, including subpopulation label flipping, availability disruptions, and inference stage manipulations. Importantly, the evaluated malware scanners do not flag AiSPY because current public rule sets lack coverage for ML runtime Trojans, while the associated poisoned inputs and resulting compromised models bypass state-of-the-art inspection tools. We demonstrate the practicality of this threat with an implementation in the ONNX Runtime training and inference engines.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
items.abstract: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods. In the baseline comparisons, TabPFN achieved mean errors close to SchemaGAN's on synthetic sections and lower mean errors at both field sites. On synthetic sections, TabPFN's mean absolute error decreased at each tested increase in CPT count, and, under the baseline input setting, its pointwise prediction intervals had mean coverage close to nominal levels. Subsequent fine-tuning on the synthetic sections used to train SchemaGAN improved synthetic test accuracy but increased mean errors at both field sites. These findings indicate that general-purpose tabular foundation models offer a promising route for updating subsurface predictions from sparse and evolving site-investigation data without retraining.

items.title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
items.abstract: Turbulence modeling relies on human choices of closure form, physical inputs, and tunable parameters. Training closures a posteriori is efficient only with gradients through long chaotic rollouts, which few solvers provide. Most a posteriori approaches therefore resort to gradient-free optimization, and nearly all fix the closure form in advance, learning only its parameters. In this work, we introduce a gradient-aware agentic framework that poses closure discovery as a bilevel problem: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system searches over closure forms, while a GPU-native differentiable computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver supplies gradients, making differentiable a posteriori learning an action of the autonomous AI agent. For each proposal, the agents construct a differentiable training program by embedding the analytical, neural, or hybrid closure in the solver, implementing a differentiable objective, and validating the gradient path. They then decide whether to evaluate the closure, compute its parameter sensitivities, or train it a posteriori, select the optimization settings, and revise subsequent proposals using the simulation outcomes and returned gradients. Truncated-horizon gradients make this training usable under chaotic dynamics for closures with tens of thousands of parameters. Demonstrations include dissipation-law and subgrid-scale closure discovery in two-dimensional turbulence and wall-model discovery for large-eddy simulation of three-dimensional channel flow. With gradient-based training, the agent recovers reference coefficients that forward evaluation alone does not reach within the same budget, and autonomously discovers and trains analytical and neural closures that improve agreement with the targeted reference statistics. These results demonstrate the feasibility of end-to-end autonomous turbulence model development in time-resolved flows.

items.title: Agentic Computational Algebra
items.abstract: We explore the use of AI agents for solving computational problems in algebra. For the problems we consider, the main challenge is not correctness but \emph{time}: general-purpose algorithms are guaranteed to provide correct solutions but can be prohibitively slow, while reformulations that exploit special structure often allow solving a problem much faster. We propose to use this setting to evaluate how effectively agents discover and exploit structure within and across tasks to reduce computational costs. More broadly, computational algebra supplies infinitely many problems with independently verifiable answers and systematically controllable structure and difficulty. To illustrate these possibilities, we use benchmark families of systems with controlled shared structure and evaluate agents in three settings: solving independent instances, solving online streams of related instances using persistent memory, and compiling a fast reusable solver for a known problem family. Our experiments show that (i) agents can extend the range of systems solvable within a fixed budget, although reasoning overhead can sometimes outweigh computational savings; (ii) memory can reduce the cost of repeated solving but may preserve suboptimal strategies; (iii) compilation produces faster reusable solvers but at substantial upfront cost. Overall, computational algebra offers concrete, measurable targets for improving how agents discover and reuse structure.

items.title: Vocabulary-Free Next-Event Prediction on Temporal Graphs
items.abstract: Autoregressive transformer training through next-token prediction has driven remarkable advances in language modeling and has become increasingly effective for time-series modeling. Yet its success in temporal graph learning remains limited, and most temporal link-prediction methods are discriminative rather than autoregressive. While temporal graphs can have a natural serialization through chronological ordering edges, they lack an obvious graph-independent tokenization: existing node tokenization often uses a vocabulary that grows with the number of nodes, limiting scalability and cross-graph training. We propose GTGT, Generative Temporal Graph Transformer, a simple yet powerful vocabulary-free framework for self-supervised next-event prediction on temporal graphs. It predicts events for observed destinations, behavioral descriptors for novel destinations, and time gaps before new event. These targets have shared meanings across graphs, allowing one transformer to train across disjoint node sets without node-specific learned parameters. Local node identifiers let attention capture graph structure: Theoretically, we can show that our transformer-based model has the capacity for time-respecting message passing mechanisms. On Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB), our GTGT not only achieves comparable or better link-prediction performance than established baselines, but also has much lower training cost. These results open the door to temporal graph pretraining for forecasting and other downstream tasks, providing a concrete step toward temporal graph foundation models.

items.title: Scaling public input on AI policy with pluralistic agents
items.abstract: AI is being deployed across a vast range of application domains, cultural environments, and human stakeholders. Safe and responsible AI development requires continuously accounting for diverse perspectives. We develop and test pluralistic agents, AI agent representatives that deliberate on behalf of individuals to align AI systems with diverse human perspectives. Pluralistic agents could help people contribute to many more discussions than they could directly participate in, on technical topics that would require training, and on policy choices that rely on private information that corporations and governments cannot readily share. Our experiments identify opportunities, risks, and perceptions of pluralistic agents. Agents were able to reliably shift policies in the direction of their represented persona's preferences, but the extent of each agent's influence was sensitive to the instructions from its persona, such as having more influence when instructed to be more verbose or less cooperative. This suggests that influence in AI-assisted deliberation could vary based on how participants prompt their agents and how the system is designed. In a preregistered study, 746 humans participated in the pluralistic agents process. Participants viewed pluralistic agents as useful and fair, preferring agents over the baseline of providing input to a single AI reasoning model. Most participants preferred participating themselves over either pluralistic agents or the baseline, but pluralistic agents recovered 68% of the baseline-direct gap in reported satisfaction and 82% in fairness. Because pluralistic agents can be used in many real-world contexts where direct discussion is not, they could be a promising tool to scale AI safety policy development. We encourage cautious exploration of this method, playing to its strengths as an amplifier of human input rather than a replacement.

items.title: What Roles Do System Prompts Really Assign? Validating and Steering Occupational Role Vectors in LLMs
items.abstract: Applications built on large language models assign the model a role through its system prompt, intending to shape how it responds for their use case. We introduce a validation framework for extracting and injecting occupational role vectors, activation-level directions that capture how someone in a given occupational role would distinctively respond to a task or question. We validate these vectors through two complementary lenses, on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The interpretability lens asks whether each vector is a stable, separable, domain-consistent representation of its role: extracted vectors are highly reproducible across repeated runs and sampling temperatures, remain separable even for very similar roles, and agree more with themselves across in-domain and out-of-domain questions than with other roles' signal. The control lens asks whether injecting a role vector during generation makes the model express the role, and sustain it over a conversation, as well as a role prompt does. On Qwen, injecting the vector alone makes the model express the intended role substantially more often than unsteered, but at best matches a role prompt; on both models, adding the vector to the prompt strengthens the role in single answers but did not slow the role's decline over 30 turns. Together, the two lenses show why both are needed: out of domain the role is expressed only subtly, yet the activations still encode it; and a vector that is stable and separable can still barely steer the model's behavior.

items.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
items.abstract: Learning from paired modalities is commonly equated with aligning them: two encoders are trained until the embeddings of a pair coincide in a shared space. We study whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can instead be obtained while the two encoders' own embedding spaces remain directly unaligned. DuoJEPA trains one encoder per modality with the self-supervised LeJEPA objective and appends to each encoder a single transformer layer that translates its embedding into the other encoder's space, supervised by a contrastive objective computed entirely within that target space. No loss term compares the two own spaces directly, although the encoders are optimised jointly through the translation objective. In our experiments, the translator's residual connections determine where the cross-modal pressure is absorbed: with a residual translator the two encoders become directly aligned, whereas with a skipless (residual-free) translator a paired-cosine test detects no alignment in the final models, and at most a weak one in the ablations, at comparable cross-modal performance. The learned class-token translation is well approximated by a single scaled rotation of the source space. We evaluate DuoJEPA on two modality pairs that differ in nearly every respect. On chest radiographs and reports from CheXpert Plus, it attains a zero-shot AUC of 86.6 and a cross-modal retrieval score of 78.5, compared with 60.0 and 64.2 for our reimplementation of LeVLJEPA with the same encoders and data. On Sentinel-2 optical and Sentinel-1 radar imagery, the frozen encoders fall within the range of published Sentinel foundation models under our reproduction of the Copernicus-Bench linear-probe protocol, the translator retrieves the paired image of the other sensor among 4,000 candidates in 77-79% of cases, and a patch-level extension transfers the within-image similarity structure of the scene.

items.title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors
items.abstract: Engineering design studies produce a few tens to a few hundred simulations of one problem, each on its own mesh, and their surrogates are retrained for every study. Tabular foundation models instead infer a new task from its examples in one forward pass, after pretraining on synthetic tasks. We demonstrate the feasibility of in-context learning for physical field prediction on unstructured meshes. A single model, PhysICL, pretrained solely on procedural tasks, predicts fields, with quantiles, directly on each query mesh from labeled simulations, without updating its weights. The same checkpoint accepts variable numbers of context examples, scalar inputs and input fields, and any number of output fields, while mesh size and connectivity can vary within a task. Its procedural prior draws generic laws and boundary-element physical models on morphed 2D and 3D template meshes, evaluated only at the points the model samples, fast enough that tasks generated on the fly by CPU workers keep the GPUs busy throughout pretraining. On five PLAID datasets never seen in pretraining, its field error decreases as the context grows and, from $K = 32$, is below that of the nearest context simulation on every dataset and context draw.
