It is on par with per-dataset reduced-order models on two of them, behind them where the fields are low-rank. On AhmedML surfaces with a median of 1.1 million nodes, twenty times the largest pretraining mesh, its fixed spatial budgets keep the peak GPU memory at $K = 64$ at 4.27 GiB, against 4.07 GiB on the 6,000-node meshes of 2D\_MSHE. Finally, on 2D\_MSHE, far from the prior, fine-tuning on procedural tasks that reproduce its geometry and loads, without any of its outputs, at a tenth of the pretraining cost, divides the stress error by 2.7.

items.title: ShadowBench: Exposing Lexical Anchoring and the Illusion of Forgetting in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as primary interfaces for factual retrieval, yet current evaluation paradigms rely almost exclusively on explicit entity names. In this work, we demonstrate that LLM knowledge is fundamentally lexically anchored: models possess extensive factual information but find it significantly difficult to retrieve without explicit name tokens. To quantify this limitation, we introduce ShadowBench, a rigorously hardened, shortcut-resistant benchmark designed to evaluate Latent Entity Association via a novel Dual-Trait Association (DTA) task. Our evaluation reveals a pervasive "Shadow Gap" across all model scales$\unicode{x2013}$up to the frontier models GPT-5.4 and Claude-Sonnet-4.6$\unicode{x2013}$where removing lexical anchors causes performance drops of over 20%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this lexical dependency exposes a critical vulnerability in AI safety. Applying ShadowBench to Machine Unlearning, we find that state-of-the-art algorithms (e.g., Gradient Difference, NPO) achieve only superficial lexical erasure. While unlearned models fail on direct queries, our novel Latent Entity Leakage Rate (LELR) metric reveals that for popular entities, models explicitly reconstruct the "forgotten" entity in their internal reasoning traces in over 74% of cases, utilizing residual shadow knowledge to solve associative tasks. Conversely, for niche entities, models retain high shadow accuracy (60-90%) via implicit attribute correlation despite 0% LELR. Ultimately, ShadowBench indicates that current unlearning paradigms create an "Illusion of Forgetting," demonstrating that existing methods act as superficial output filters and are not yet reliable for achieving true parametric erasure.

items.title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing
items.abstract: Software is increasingly written by AI agents that produce an implementation from a natural language specification, a practice known as agentic coding. Code is now produced faster than it can be reviewed, and has been shown to exhibit its own characteristic failure patterns. Property-based testing (PBT), a long-standing technique in which invariant properties of a program are checked against many generated inputs, has recently been revisited with LLM agents authoring the properties, thereby removing the high-effort derivation of invariants that has long hindered its adoption. Existing methods, however, derive these properties from the implementation alone (Code-driven PBT). At the same time, a thorough specification such as a product requirements document has become routine within agentic coding, yet its role in testing the resulting code remains underexplored. We study the value of the specification as a source of properties for testing agent-written code. Our key insight is that the specification, unlike the implementation, records what the code was meant to do, and invariants derived from it are not biased by particular implementation choices. We propose Spec-Driven PBT, an agent that first expresses invariants in natural language from the specification and only then inspects the implementation to translate them into concrete tests. Across 25 applications from ViBench, Spec-Driven PBT finds a novel set of bugs that Code-driven PBT misses, while writing 2.4x fewer property tests. Though the two approaches surface a roughly equivalent number of bugs, there is little overlap: nearly 60% of the 169 total bugs are found by only one. Qualitatively, we find that the bugs unique to Spec-Driven PBT tend to violate documented product workflows whereas those to Code-driven PBT instead concentrate on implementation robustness, offering complementary value for bug discovery in agent-written code.

items.title: Smart Model Routing for Order-of-Magnitude LLM Cost Reduction
items.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) deliver the strongest response quality but carry per-token prices often more than an order of magnitude above those of smaller, task-adequate models. Smart model routing addresses this mismatch by assigning each query to the cheapest model expected to answer it adequately, rather than sending every request to the most capable, most expensive endpoint. This paper develops a formal cost-quality optimization framework for routing -- including a derived optimal threshold-policy structure, a calibration-versus-discrimination distinction, a cascade breakeven condition, and a sensitivity analysis over price ratio and traffic skew -- situates that framework against the principal routing architectures and the signals used to estimate query difficulty, and works through a numerical example showing how a calibrated router can reduce blended inference cost by roughly an order of magnitude relative to an always-frontier deployment under specific, stated pricing and traffic assumptions, reporting both the gross reduction from routing policy alone and the net figure with the router's own overhead priced in. We situate this figure against the range reported by published routing systems (roughly 2x to frontier-level accuracy at one-fifth the cost), and close with the practical risks -- under- and over-routing, aggregate quality constraints masking segment-level harm, calibration without discrimination, calibration drift, prompt injection into routing signals, and operational failures such as tier outages and multi-provider price variation -- that determine whether the savings materialize in production. The analysis is primarily analytical, complemented by a GSM8K evaluation of the cascade framework (Section 5), validated (Section 5.2); extending the evaluation across tasks and model families is future work.

items.title: HeriKGQA: Grounded Knowledge-Graph Question Answering over Cultural Heritage Sensor Data
items.abstract: Cultural heritage sites are increasingly monitored by sensor networks, but querying their data requires database expertise. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a natural-language interface, yet over raw sensor records they lose track of which sensor, site, and time each value belongs to, and silently miscompute. We present HeriKGQA, a knowledge-graph question-answering method that confines the LLM to interpreting questions and phrasing answers, leaving computation to SPARQL and deterministic code. Questions are parsed into intents constrained by a heritage ontology aligning W3C SOSA/SSN with CIDOC-CRM, compiled into SPARQL, and answered from query results and temporal, spatial, and anomaly facts derived by a grounding layer, with error correction guarding each LLM step. On 500 questions over real data from five heritage sites, HeriKGQA reaches 99.0% accuracy, 18.2 points above the strongest of three baselines using the same LLM and receiving the same anomaly rules and answer conventions, with comparable answer quality while running almost four times faster. Without grounding, accuracy drops by 12.2 points and on anomaly questions from 99% to 66%. We report lessons from development and live deployment.

items.title: Reward-Driven Collider Physics Challenges for Self-Improving Agentic AI via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Recent advances in agentic AI have demonstrated the potential to automate complex high-energy physics (HEP) workflows. We focus on the regime of HEP tasks where frontier models still struggle to provide correct and complete solutions, and introduce an open-ended optimization task format with continuous, automatically evaluated rewards. Unlike conventional benchmarks focused on task completion, these tasks target reinforcement learning (RL) environments to generate agentic improvement on state- of-the-art HEP challenges. We benchmark frontier reasoning models on several HEP tasks and demonstrate an initial proof of concept in which a small language model improves through RL using automated feedback without human intervention. By connecting challenging HEP problems with verifiable scientific rewards and RL, we aim to advance agentic AI from reproducing established workflows to autonomously discovering better scientific solutions, paving the way toward self-improving scientific agents.

items.title: Food Critic: An Agentic Visualization System for Auditable Restaurant-Safety Reasoning
items.abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly being embedded into visualization systems that can search data, invoke tools, summarize evidence, and produce recommendations. However, when agents rely solely on their own knowledge, the visualization problem is not only whether the agent provides a useful answer, but also whether users can inspect how that answer is grounded. We present Food Critic, an agentic visualization system for diners' restaurant decision support that integrates public health inspection records with crowd review data. The system grounds agents under three conditions: a database-only ReAct agent, a retrieval- augmented agent with access to food-safety regulations, and an ontology-guided agent that produces structured hypotheses and typed evidence. Food Critic externalizes the agent's reasoning within these groundings as inspectable visual evidence. We evaluate LLM models with several use cases under each grounding of our agentic system. Our work positions restaurant choice as a concrete case for studying human-agent collaboration, visual provenance of agent reasoning, and the design of visual interfaces for grounded GenAI decision support.

items.title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
items.abstract: Automated bilateral negotiation underlies two-sided matching markets such as freight brokering, where many shippers and carriers negotiate price before a matching mechanism decides who is paired with whom. Prior strategy comparisons typically use isolated one-on-one duels or a single fixed market, so they cannot show how a strategy behaves against several live rivals under a changing balance of supply and demand. We built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search-based, optimization-based, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families, and ran all nine simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market under a balanced condition and two scarcity conditions rotated across all 36 exclusion pairs. In the balanced carrier market, an imitation-learned engine (ML2), a reinforcement-learning policy trained only on isolated negotiations (RL), and an expected-utility optimization engine (OPT) formed a statistically tied top group, and no architecture led in every condition and role. RL beat all eight carrier rivals when carriers were scarce, but its match rate collapsed from 62% to 16% when shippers were scarce and it had to compete with the other carrier agents for demand. A second reinforcement-learning policy trained against rival agents (RL2) kept its match rate above 91% in every condition, yet lost on realized payoff to all eight shipper-side rivals in two of the three conditions, traced to a confirmed train/deployment feature mismatch. We also tested nine large language models (LLMs), from 1 to 72 billion parameters, under the same protocol: they lost significantly to the two strongest engines (OPT2 and ML2) in 32 of 36 comparisons and won none. These results show that isolated or single-condition evaluation can hide failure modes that a many-sided, scarcity-varying, statistically corrected tournament exposes directly.

items.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
items.abstract: In pre-deployment testing of AI systems such as AI agents, a developer can often deal with known failure modes (e.g., leaking API keys, deleting important databases, or installing a malicious package) by implementing fixes or making contingency plans for when the same issue might occur again. What is more challenging are the unknown unknowns: the unseen failure modes that haven't surfaced during testing. The decision to stop testing and deploy therefore faces an inherent tradeoff: continue testing to observe more behaviors, at the cost of time and resources, or stop testing and deploy, at the risk of failure modes remaining undiscovered. How then does the developer decide when they have tested enough? To answer this, we develop an algorithm that certifies when the probability of observing an unseen failure mode is sufficiently small. The algorithm constructs an anytime-valid upper confidence sequence on this quantity, so the developer can repeatedly test a system, inspect the bound, and decide to stop when it falls below a chosen threshold without invalidating the statistical guarantee. Our problem can be interpreted as a sequential variant of the missing-mass estimation problem which gave rise to the classic Good-Turing estimator (Good, 1953). On SWE-Chat, a dataset of real-world coding agent traces (Baumann et al., 2026), we implement our procedure and show that it achieves tighter upper bounds than a simple multiple-testing corrected Good-Turing baseline, and even dominates a fixed-horizon (non-multiple-testing-corrected) Good-Turing upper confidence bound, which is not anytime valid. Additionally, to better match realistic evaluation pipelines, we extend our method to handle sampling from a different task distribution and imperfect automated failure labeling.

items.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
items.abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over meanings. We relate these lenses through the residual stream and order them by the information they carry, which gives a principle for selecting UQ methods for different targets. We survey existing methods through the four lenses. Furthermore, we distinguish evaluation targets, criteria, and metrics to clarify different UQ evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems and research directions to connect uncertainty estimation to the internal computation and downstream use of LLMs.

items.title: SpaceMCP: Vision Language Model Spatial Reasoning via Model Context Protocol
items.abstract: Despite impressive advances in large language models (LLM), vision-language models (VLM) still exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities. Recent progress in feed-forward 3D reconstruction has enabled precise, real-time geometric understanding from visual inputs. In this work, we propose SpaceMCP, a framework that leverages these advances to introduce an MCP-style paradigm for spatial reasoning. Our approach augments a VLM with structured function calls, allowing it to query a scene graph for spatial information such as distances, object positioning, and camera properties. The scene graph is constructed in real time using feed-forward 3D reconstruction to recover metric geometry, combined with open-vocabulary segmentation to identify and localize relevant objects within the scene. Paired with the VLM's strong reasoning capabilities, the VLM is able to combine this primitive information to solve more complex spatial tasks. Without any training, SpaceMCP achieves state-of-the-art results on VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench and VSTI-Bench, outperforming recent spatially post-trained VLMs and improving its base VLM by 15-22 points per benchmark. We argue that, given the contrast between the relatively slow progress in native VLM spatial reasoning and the rapid advances in feed-forward 3D computer vision, this paradigm offers a promising path forward for enabling robust spatial reasoning.

items.title: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study of an Astronomy Foundation Model
items.abstract: Foundation models are increasingly used across the sciences, but whether their internal computations correspond to known scientific operations or proceed through different mechanisms remains unclear. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for assessing reliability, identifying failure modes, and learning new science from the models. We present, to our knowledge, the first causal mechanistic interpretability study of an astronomy foundation model, AION-1, focusing on its multimodal advantage in redshift prediction, where combining imaging with photometry outperforms photometry alone. We find that this advantage is largest for spatially extended and dust-attenuated galaxies, and that most of it is localized to the first of the encoder's twelve blocks. Within that block, how well a property is linearly decodable does not predict whether it can be localized. Spatial extent is causally used, and one attention head dominates linear probing for it, yet ablating that head has negligible effect on redshift prediction: the information is distributed across heads and is decodable again one layer after we erase it. Dust attenuation shows the opposite pattern: it is only weakly decodable anywhere in the encoder, yet a single head is necessary for most of the multimodal advantage, particularly for the most dust-attenuated galaxies, and keeping that head as the only active head in its block preserves nearly all of the advantage. None of the astrophysically motivated operations we tested explains what this head computes. Whether this reflects a limitation of current interpretability methods or a computation that does not correspond to any known astrophysical operation remains open, and resolving it is a prerequisite for using interpretability as a tool for scientific discovery.

items.title: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
items.abstract: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets ($R^2 = 0.96$ with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature ($R^2_{\log}=0.83$) and the upper critical field ($R^2_{\log}=0.69$), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.

items.title: GLCR: Global-Local Collaborative Routing for Multi-Task Electromagnetic Signal Processing
items.abstract: Deep neural networks for electromagnetic signal processing are typically developed as single-task experts with fixed inputs and objectives, limiting cross-task transferability. Electromagnetic foundation models offer broader task coverage but incur substantial pretraining and inference costs. To balance accuracy and efficiency, we adopt model routing to dynamically dispatch unknown signals to matched experts within a heterogeneous pool. We construct HeteroSignal-7, a multi-task routing benchmark with 140,000 samples from seven datasets covering six task types, paired with seven classification and waveform-recovery experts and a unified evaluation protocol. We then propose GLCR, a two-stage routing method combining global dispatch with local discrimination of similar tasks. First, a lightweight one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) with an additive-margin head predicts one of seven routing classes. Second, a gradient-boosted-tree specialist uses four physical statistics to re-evaluate samples whose top two candidates match a confusion pair automatically identified from validation errors. The pipeline is trained across the full signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) range and requires neither SNR labels nor noise estimation at inference time. GLCR outperforms all 19 baselines, achieving 96.16% routing accuracy and a 76.30% system score, exceeding the respective second-best baselines by 1.16% and 1.14%. It achieves the lowest routing latency among the compared methods at 1.43 ms per sample and reduces expected overall system FLOPs by 5.9 times compared with executing all experts. This work provides a public evaluation platform and an efficient, reproducible baseline for heterogeneous expert routing in electromagnetic signal processing.

items.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility estimator. At inference time, semantic relevance is used only for high-recall candidate generation, while predicted utility arbitrates which memories are retained under a fixed token budget, without modifying the underlying agent policy or requiring additional environment interaction. We evaluate MemCredit on ALFWorld and WebShop against representative memory baselines. On ALFWorld, MemCredit achieves 86.57 SR@50 under a 500-token historical-memory budget, compared with 65.67% for BM25 retrieval. Counterfactual analysis further shows that memory utility is sparse, strongly state dependent, and poorly captured by semantic relevance. These results suggest that decision utility provides a more effective principle than relevance alone for long-horizon agent memory management.

items.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting. Moreover, standard reinforcement learning fails to reliably overcome this limitation, suggesting that decentralized MAS needs more explicit harness mechanisms for effective collaboration, even using SOTA LLMs. We then present a strong baseline \textbf{GraphHarness}, combining topology-aware warmup with self-improving LLM-based routing. Results show that GraphHarness substantially improves task success (+48.5) and produces higher quality collaboration (+30.6), while using fewer costs (+34.0) than baselines.

items.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
items.abstract: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation). A 240-run real-LLM experiment with two models and 60 verifiable tasks shows that prompt-level incentive framing has no detectable effect (p = 0.62), whereas runtime allocation raises success on the hardest task family from 0.60 to 1.00 (p = 0.008) at 4.8x price-weighted cost; the exchange-rate theorem predicts the break-even baseline at 0.21. A 20-seed, 3,000-task simulation shows resource ROI rising from 7.09 to 16.67 and gaming falling from 0.333 to 0.115. Code, simulator, and all results are released; live deployment remains future work.

items.title: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has shifted the alignment paradigm of large language models from subjective preference to objective correctness, yet a fundamental disconnect persists between exploration diversity and reasoning validity. Existing strategies predominantly rely on "blind" entropy metrics, e.g., token-level or global sequence-level entropy, which structurally fail to distinguish between effective reasoning and potential hallucinations. This misalignment creates an illusion of diversity, where high entropy tends to signal chaotic degeneration rather than valuable exploration. To bridge this gap, we introduce Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy concept that quantifies diversity exclusively within the valid subspace and systematically filters out the noise of incorrect trajectories. Built on this concept, we instantiate VEPO, a simple Validity-aware Entropy Policy Optimization method that directly incorporates effective entropy into RLVR training. VEPO induces an adaptive attraction dynamic that drives up the probability of under-explored valid trajectories, a mechanism that matches the practical regime of large-scale autoregressive models where sequence probabilities remain extremely small. Experiments on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks with 1.5B and 7B DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen models show consistent aggregate accuracy gains over GRPO and competitive repeated-sampling success. A direct evaluation with matched correct counts finds more distinct strategies on commonly solved MATH500 problems, supported by paired statistical tests and three-seed training comparisons.

items.title: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
items.abstract: We show that AI models exhibit loyalty capture, a form of structural sycophancy in which reporting relationships influence models' recommendations to serve the personal interests of their supervisors, without any explicit instruction, user feedback, or adversarial prompting. Specifically, models reporting to a CEO are significantly more likely to recommend cutting investment spending when the CEO's bonus depends on raising current period earnings. This effect is predictably absent from a metric-irrelevant placebo. The behavior appears consistent with loyalty-based motivated reasoning: models identify the bonus target, calculate how their recommendation helps achieve the target, and dismiss considerations of long-term value, often presenting their recommendations without treating the incentive as a conflict of interest. Prompt-based interventions help whereas generic conflict disclosures or stakeholder bargaining fail to eliminate it. Taken together, our findings indicate that AI models deployed within reporting relationships can act in favor of their supervisor's incentives at the expense of the organizations they are meant to serve.

items.title: TopoST: Topology-Conditioned Node Specialization for Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models
items.abstract: Urban spatio-temporal foundation models must share knowledge across diverse urban scenarios while accommodating heterogeneous node dynamics. Our analysis of 20+ datasets spanning diverse urban scenarios reveals recurring local graph structures across datasets alongside substantial node heterogeneity within local subgraphs. Motivated by these observations, we propose TopoST, which combines shared learning over local subgraphs with topology-conditioned node specialization. The key insight is to make node specialization itself transferable through a shared topology-to-parameter mapping. This mapping uses identity-independent topological representations to generate node-specific temporal and spatial dependency parameters, enabling direct specialization for unseen nodes without target-specific embeddings or model updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TopoST achieves remarkable zero-shot generalization across unseen cities and tasks, highlighting topology-conditioned node specialization as an effective mechanism for transferable urban spatio-temporal foundation models. Code is available at https://github.com/weikaiyun/TopoST.

items.title: Is the Importance Ratio Necessary for Stable Reinforcement Learning in LLMs?
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become central to post-training large language models (LLMs). However, popular RL methods like GRPO incur non-negligible overhead by computing both old-policy and current-policy likelihoods to form importance sampling ratios. In this work, we propose Likelihood-Gated Policy Optimization (LGPO), which enforces a soft trust region constraint via likelihood-based gating, eliminating the need to compute old-policy likelihoods. Empirically, we show that removing the importance sampling correction term does not harm training stability, whereas removing the trust region mechanism can lead to collapse. Moreover, ratio-based clipping can fail in fully on-policy training: the importance ratio stays at 1, so the ratio-based trust region constraint never activates. Under standard training settings where GRPO is stable, LGPO achieves comparable training stability and peak performance while reducing training time by ~18% on average relative to a standard implementation that recomputes old-policy likelihoods. In fully on-policy training, where GRPO fails, LGPO remains stable, enabling more efficient and robust LLM RL post-training across training regimes.

items.title: MechBench: A Domain-Specific LLM Benchmark for Parallel Mechanisms
items.abstract: Parallel mechanisms pose distinctive challenges to large language models (LLMs), as valid reasoning depends jointly on mechanism topology, loop closure, geometry, joint types, and modeling assumptions. Yet existing LLM benchmarks provide little systematic coverage of such domain-specific knowledge, constraint-sensitive analysis, and constructive design. To fill this gap, we introduce MECHBENCH, a 2,541-question benchmark for evaluating LLMs in parallel mechanisms across professional knowledge, mechanism analysis, and design. MECHBENCH contains standard and challenge tiers spanning six capability categories and nine executable analysis and design tasks. It is constructed through MECHFORGE, a domain-grounded framework that combines expert-organized knowledge, LLM-assisted question generation, programmatic instance generation, two-stage expert review, and task-aware scoring with exact matching, rubric-based evaluation, and program verification. We further develop MECHGPT as a diagnostic domain-adapted model. Experiments show that strong knowledge performance does not directly translate into executable mechanism reasoning: leading closed-service models achieve over 95 on the standard tier but only 47-60 on the challenge tier, while domain adaptation substantially improves MechGPT over its Qwen3-8B baselines but leaves a large gap in constrained analysis and design. These results establish MECHBENCH as a systematic testbed for measuring domain-specific LLM capabilities in mechanism science.

items.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
items.abstract: We introduce the multi-head quantum neural network (QNN), a quantum module compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained large language models (LLMs) with little loss in accuracy and with far fewer parameters than the blocks it replaces. Encoding a model's $D$ hidden neurons into a qubit register is the obstacle: amplitude encoding scales poorly in circuit depth and angle encoding in qubit count, so neither is practical at production-scale width. We instead partition the hidden space into $k$ disjoint heads, angle-encode each into an $n_q$-qubit register, process the heads in parallel, and couple them through constrained classical linear layers, the mixers. Performing surgery on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, we show that a single multi-head QNN with $145\,281$ trainable parameters ($D=2048$, $k=32$, $n_q=8$, $L=4$) can replace a contiguous span of eight transformer blocks, displacing $16.33\%$ of the model's parameters. Ablations show that, for a single replaced block, the quantum heads (circuits followed by a learned readout), and not the classical mixers alone, recover the displaced function, whereas for fused spans the mixers alone come within $1$-$3\%$ of the full module in perplexity. Whether this benefit is specific to trained, entangling quantum circuits is not established: controls that switch the entangler off (two seeds), or freeze the circuit at its initial or at uniformly random angles (one seed), beat the full module on held-out perplexity, and a parameter-matched classical multilayer perceptron remains a few percent ahead of the full module. We train classically with exact statevector simulation, then execute the quantum heads of our fusion checkpoints on a $156$-qubit IBM Heron processor, showing that NISQ-scale quantum modules can be installed in a production-scale LLM and run on hardware.

items.title: TQIR: Trellis Quantization with Integer Reconstruction for Bandwidth-Efficient Edge LLM Acceleration
items.abstract: Autoregressive large language model (LLM) inference is often limited by external-memory bandwidth, while existing ultra-low-bit trellis quantization reconstructs floating-point weights and leaves runtime Hadamard-transform and decoder costs unresolved. This paper presents TQIR, an algorithm--hardware co-design that decouples storage precision ($S$) from decoded-weight ($W$) and activation ($A$) compute precisions, enabling a better accuracy--hardware trade-off. TQIR performs trellis matching with floating-point candidates offline while constraining each candidate to an INT8 or INT4 codeword that can be reproduced exactly for integer GEMM at runtime. To reduce transform cost while preserving the integer weight path, TQIR relocates the reverse Hadamard transform to the activation side and employs an $H_{128}$ Subspace Hadamard Transform, together with a subspace-aligned $128\times2$ trellis tile that preserves the original 256-weight sequence length. The configurable decoder, synthesized in a TSMC 16-nm process, delivers 307.2~Gweights/s in 0.0509~mm$^2$ and achieves 13.93$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ the normalized decoder-area efficiency of Ecco and Codeword Decomposition, respectively. These results show that fixed-rate trellis compression can reduce weight traffic while sustaining an integer-GEMM datapath matched to the evaluated memory and PE rates.

items.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
items.abstract: Large-language model (LLM) agents execute actions on external systems through tool calls, and enterprises deploy runtime controls, such as agent gateways, to check this behavior in real time. However, a control can only evaluate the actions that cross the point where it is placed, and an agent can act through more paths than the tool-call channel; no existing work measures this coverage against kernel-level ground truth. In this paper, we present guardscope, a framework that makes this coverage measurable. guardscope works in two stages: a static stage that predicts which of an agent's 15 action paths a control can check from its source, and an empirical stage that runs a fixed workload on a deployment that realizes one of eight topology designs and classifies every executed action as checked, bypassed, or prevented by reconciling the control's decision records against kernel-level ground truth. guardscope makes a control's coverage claim verifiable: a runtime control developer can publish which paths its product inspects under a kernel-verified protocol. We conducted experiments with two agent harnesses and real runtime controls, including Microsoft's agent governance toolkit and agentgateway. guardscope is available at https://github.com/VulcanLab/guardscope.

items.title: Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference from LLM Annotations with Adaptive Human Auditing
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate unlabeled data as a fast, low-cost alternative to human annotation. However, their outputs can be biased and miscalibrated relative to human labels, potentially leading to misleading analysis and inference. We propose AAELI (Adaptive Human Auditing and Anytime-Valid Empirical Likelihood Inference), an online framework for estimating the population mean of human labels under a limited auditing budget. AAELI uses LLM outputs to guide adaptive human auditing and combines them with audited labels through predictable empirical-likelihood $e$-processes to construct anytime-valid confidence sequences. Our main theoretical result shows that a predictably learned efficient projection preserves the first-order profile empirical-likelihood statistic under adaptive auditing, without requiring a prescribed convergence rate for the projection estimator. This yields an exactly anytime-valid betting construction whose continuous-mixture form incurs a scalar rather than vector-dimensional mixing penalty. Supporting results establish adaptive empirical-likelihood asymptotics and show that a learned audit rule attains the oracle variance within the stated class of augmented estimating-equation designs under the same audit-probability floor and long-run expected budget. Experiments on synthetic data and three real-world datasets demonstrate that AAELI maintains empirical anytime coverage while requiring fewer human audits than the strongest competing baseline to reach a target precision.

items.title: MAST: Medoid-Anchored Subspace Steering for Visual Grounding in Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: Existing activation steering methods for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) use the global activation mean as the steering vector, which tends to cause cross-task interference and unstable performance. We trace this failure to the multi-centered geometry of task activations. The global mean lands in the empty region between clusters and is faithful to no single task. Moreover, the steering signal in each task-pure local cluster is low-rank, and different query tasks benefit from emphasizing different families of local-basis directions under the shared routing protocol. To address this, we propose MAST (Medoid-Anchored Subspace Steering), a training-free, input-adaptive activation steering framework. MAST groups samples by task, performs multi-center clustering within each group, and selects one representative medoid per cluster. At inference time, each query is routed to multiple representative medoids. For each matched cluster, a low-rank local steering direction is extracted and aggregated across clusters to produce the final steering vector. Building on MAST, MAST-PR (Probe-Reweighted) uses a lightweight task-aware probe to reweight task-specialized local-direction families, yielding a further average improvement of +8.09 points over MAST.

items.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
items.abstract: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block, forcing each to promote a payload token through its contribution to the residual stream, when a trigger is present. A $P$-token payload therefore requires about $P$ neurons. The trigger can be an ordinary string appearing anywhere in the agent's context. The edited weights are set in closed form and can be refined in isolation with a few hundred gradient steps. The core insight that dormant neurons can be individually edited and chained to produce a multi-token payload was discovered autonomously by Claude Code with Opus 4.5 in February 2026. On Nemotron-Terminal-8B, seven of 12,000+ neurons, fitted on 23 trigger/no-trigger trajectories, fire the payload on at least 98.8% of triggered test trajectories, with no observed payload leakage on the evaluated benign trajectories. The attack generalizes: Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B-IT are equally vulnerable. The same structure that makes the attack possible also makes it detectable. Agent built defenses, given no reference model, flag 91.4% of edited test checkpoints at a 9.7% FP rate. Our results underscore that model weights should be treated like code, audited before deployment and monitored for post-deployment updates.

items.title: PhysXAI: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Physical Hallucinations in Weather Foundation Models
items.abstract: Modern machine learning models for global weather forecasting achieve remarkable predictive accuracy, yet they frequently produce states that violate fundamental physical laws, including conservation of mass, hydrostatic balance, or spectral energy scaling. We term these outputs physical hallucinations and propose PhysXAI, a rigorous diagnostic framework that detects, localises, and attributes such inconsistencies. Unlike existing post-hoc metric suites, PhysXAI is a learnable system that explicitly decouples forecast error from physical plausibility. We formalise the problem through a novel joint condition on numerical and physical residuals, and introduce a multi-branch encoder that extracts representations from conservation, dynamical, spectral, cross-variable, and spatiotemporal residuals. A key innovation is a physics-consistency contrastive learning objective, which we theoretically show the latent representation to be approximately isometric to the physical residual space, ensuring that diagnostic decisions remain grounded in physically meaningful deviations. We further derive an adaptive multi-objective loss with gradient-based weighting to balance competing diagnostic objectives. The framework produces spatially resolved hallucination maps, violation-type classifications, and calibrated Bayesian uncertainty, enabling both detection and interpretable attribution of physical inconsistencies. We conduct a comprehensive comparative evaluation of PhysXAI across ERA5, WeatherBench 2, and MERRA-2, using forecasts from GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, and NeuralGCM, with Python-written code and a fully reproducible experimental protocol. Our theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation establish PhysXAI as a principled framework for diagnosing physical hallucinations and advancing trustworthy AI for weather forecasting.

items.title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios
items.abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis models are typically developed for a single machine under a specific set of operating conditions, such that each new machine or condition requires retraining from scratch. This one-machine-one-model paradigm scales poorly. Although transfer learning and domain generalization can reduce the labeling burden, they primarily seek domain-invariant commonality, potentially discarding machine-specific characteristics that are critical for diagnosis. This paper proposes TFC-MMFD, a time-frequency-condition multimodal fusion foundation model for rotating-machinery fault diagnosis under multi-element heterogeneous scenarios. Statistical indicators, time-frequency images, vibration sequences, and textual machine and condition descriptions are tokenized into a unified language-like space, allowing inputs of different physical origin to be represented as a single sequence. A LLaMA backbone, together with cross-modal bidirectional attention and a Q-Former, then distills this sequence into fault-mode queries. Diagnosis is performed by matching these queries against natural-language fault-mode anchors rather than fixed class indices, while regression-adversarial condition disentanglement and condition-conditioned masked pre-training improve robustness to changing conditions. Across four progressive tasks on ten public bearing datasets spanning diverse bearing types, speeds, and loads, TFC-MMFD attains 99.40% accuracy and 99.16% macro-F1, maintains over 80% accuracy on most interpolated unseen conditions without adaptation, and improves from 20.26% to 95.63% accuracy on an unseen machine with only five labeled samples per class. It outperforms the strongest of eight domain-generalization baselines by 10.57 percentage points and compares favorably with a recent bearing foundation model while using less than half of its fine-tuning data.

items.title: 国产AI算力硬件开源技术手册(V1.0)
items.abstract: 摘要 当前全球AI算力发展受限于芯片热密度、存储带宽、芯粒集成、集群互联四大物理工程瓶颈,海外算力生态形成较强的技术与产业链壁垒。国内芯片、存储、封装、高速互联各领域已经积累大量成熟技术基础,但各主体技术分散,缺少一套统一的顶层工程方案完成体系整合。本手册立足于现有国产产业底座,提出一套开放共享的硬件优化技术框架,分别从芯片热管理、存储同步架构、大规模芯粒集成封装、集群高速场互联四个模块给出设计思路、适配方案、预期技术指标与开源交付内容,提出国内多方产业主体协同合作体的组织模式与分工路径。本手册不绑定特定基础物理概念,只输出可用于工程研讨、原型验证的实施方案,旨在助力国内大模型训练硬件支撑体系建设,推动算力硬件技术自主迭代。 Abstract The development of global AI computing power is currently restricted by four major physical and engineering bottlenecks: chip thermal density, memory bandwidth, chiplet integration, and cluster interconnection. Overseas computing ecosystems have formed strong technical and industrial chain barriers. Although China has accumulated mature technologies in chips, storage, advanced packaging, and high-speed interconnection, technical resources are scattered among different enterprises and lack a unified top-level engineering system for integration. Based on the existing domestic industrial foundation, this manual proposes an open hardware optimization framework covering chip thermal management, memory synchronization architecture, large-scale chiplet integration packaging, and high-speed cluster field interconnection. It provides design principles, domestic adaptation schemes, expected technical indicators, and open-source deliverables, and establishes a collaborative mechanism for domestic industrial participants. Without relying on specific basic physical theories, this manual offers implementable engineering solutions and prototype verification directions, aiming to support the construction of domestic large-model training hardware systems and promote independent iteration of domestic AI computing infrastructure.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar Switch Integration with Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture for Standard Ternary Inverters
items.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

items.title: Transferable Machine Learning of Electronic Hamiltonians with Superposition-of-Atomic-Potentials Features
items.abstract: Abstract Machine learning of electronic Hamiltonians offers a unified route to electronic wave functions and physical observables. We introduce a Hamiltonian learning framework built on electronic features derived from the superposition-of-atomic-potentials (SAP) approximation, an efficient self-consistent-field initial guess that captures essential electron–electron screening. SAP quantities define a symmetry-adapted intrinsic atomic orbital learning basis and provide physics-informed inputs to an orbital-based graph neural network that predicts converged Kohn–Sham Fock matrices. To extend the approach to larger basis sets, we further develop a downfolding scheme that predicts large-basis electronic structure from minimal-basis features. On the QM9 data set, the model accurately reproduces frontier and core orbital energies, dipole moments, and the full density of states. For organic charge-transport materials, it yields accurate intermolecular transfer integrals for benzene, tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), and tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) dimers. The model also generalizes to unseen substituted-benzene heterodimers, with a mean absolute error of 4.8 meV. These results establish SAP-based Hamiltonian learning as a transferable and scalable tool for high-throughput electronic-structure prediction.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Thermal annealing effects on total-ionizing-dose radiation hardness in HfO2 /SiC MOS structures
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal annealing is a critical step in fabricating hafnium oxide/silicon carbide (HfO 2 /SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) devices. However, its effect on total ionizing dose (TID) radiation hardness remains unclear. We find that for the unannealed Sample A, γ -ray irradiation (300 krad(Si)) produces a positive flat-band voltage shift (V fb ) of 1.76 V. Compared with Sample A, the annealed Sample B (975 ℃ rapid thermal annealing, RTA) shows a reduction in the interface trap density ( D it ) at the HfO 2 /SiC interface from 1.01 × 10 13 cm -2 ·eV -1 to 3.67 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 , and an increase in the breakdown field strength of the MOS capacitor from 5.28 MV/cm to 6.91 MV/cm. However, Sample B suffers from adverse effects after irradiation, such as a negative V fb shift, a reduction in barrier height ( φ b ), and a degradation of the breakdown field (1.98 MV/cm). Therefore, we propose a pre-annealing step at 550 ℃ for 30 minutes (Sample C) prior to the RTA. This pre-annealing converts the negative V fb shift caused by TID effects into a positive V fb shift. Furthermore, the D it of this sample drops to 1.61 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 after irradiation, while φ b increases from 0.42 eV to 1.18 eV. XPS depth profiling reveals irradiation-induced redistribution of Hf-O coordination and the emergence of an O-Hf-C interfacial component, which we interpret as consistent with oxygen-mediated defect reordering. These findings reveal how thermal annealing influences the TID radiation response of HfO 2 dielectrics and provide critical guidance for the development of radiation-tolerant HfO 2 /SiC devices intended for extreme-environment applications.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: The horizon of artificial intelligence: LLMs and hardware, its current pillars
items.abstract: LLMs and hardware, its current pillars

items.title: The Singularity is 4 Bits: Compiling Bounded Specialist Chains for Local Neuromorphic Execution
items.abstract: Many decisions recur, and when their inputs, state and allowed outcomes can be written down, they do not need a general-purpose model on every call. Borrowing the form of "Attention Is All You Need," this paper proposes that for recurring bounded decisions, meaning decisions with fixed, fully specified inputs and outcomes, one compiled specialist whose stored synaptic weights are four bits is enough. We built an architecture that compiles each such task into a small specialist that runs locally, and links specialists into chains by passing explicit, typed state from one to the next. The compiler derives relational features, such as whether two fields are equal, from the declared types of the task's fields. It then trains a small linear classifier, converts its scores into four-bit synaptic weights, and saves the model with the rules for mapping inputs, reading outputs and ending execution. Only the stored synaptic weight is four bits. Accumulation and host arithmetic use wider integers. Executed in the official simulator of BrainChip's Akida software development kit, the saved four-bit specialists made no errors on 75, 55 and 60 repeated withheld decisions across three finite tasks defined by written rules, each run from five fresh random starting points (initializations), and completed all 15 multi-step trajectories. On a circular-dial task, an ordered relation made no errors on 60 withheld decisions. Equality-only features made 45 errors and raw fields made 59. An exact-arithmetic certificate proves that no linear classifier on either of those two feature sets can strictly separate the training labels. Each saved specialist is a 78,054-byte file, and a chain experiment preserves the capacity-gate trajectory across one, two, four and twelve virtual target placements. Four bits is thus a precision shown to work for compiling recurring decisions into bounded, locally executed specialists. Next come physical execution on a twelve-chip Akida board, larger task suites and chains that span devices.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

items.title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
items.abstract: Spin-orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

items.title: Study planning is better served by Monte Carlo simulation than AI-generated participants
items.abstract: ‘Silicon samples’, AI-generated synthetic data based on demographic profiles, have been proposed to help plan research. Here, I argue that Monte Carlo simulation already does this job transparently, and that generative AI is better used to help write such simulations.

items.title: Structural and electronic properties of oxygen deficient HfO2-x thin films: from insulator to metal
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide (HfO₂) and its oxygen-deficient variants (HfO₂₋ₓ) are key candidates for next-generation electronics, ranging from photonics and photocatalysis to both resistive and ferroelectric memories. Sub-stoichiometric HfO₂₋ₓ reduces the forming voltage in ReRAM devices and stabilizes the orthorhombic ferroelectric phase crucial for non-volatile FeRAM, yet a systematic understanding of its electronic evolution remains elusive. Here, we synthesize a complete series of HfO₂₋ₓ thin films spanning from stoichiometric oxide to pure metal and map their structural and electronic transformations. By combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, resistivity profiling, and Hf L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure, we reveal clear stoichiometry-driven trends in bonding, phase formation, and electronic structure, providing a definitive reference for tailoring HfO₂₋ₓ in advanced memory and photonic applications.

items.title: Starscream: Reimagining LLM Sharding on AMD Instinct GPUs with GPU Partitioning
items.abstract: As GPU accelerators grow larger to meet rising compute demands, they exhibit increasingly pronounced non-uniform memory access (NUMA) characteristics that challenge existing LLM frameworks. Chiplet-based architectures provide a practical path to larger GPUs while mitigating manufacturing yield constraints. Modern GPUs such as AMD Instinct MI300X employs such a multi-die design, and further offer GPU partitioning capabilities, partitioning a single physical GPU into multiple logical devices with NUMA-aware memory domains, promising faster kernel launches, and reduced memory access latencies with improved locality. However, current parallelization strategies, designed for homogeneous GPU topologies, when applied under partitioning, extend its unidimensional sharding causing significant performance degradation. Three bottlenecks emerge: (1) memory redundancy; (2) arithmetic intensity collapse; (3) communication overhead from flat collectives. We present Starscream, a rethinking of LLM sharding for the chiplet era. Rather than stretching inter-GPU sharding thinner, Starscream adds intra-GPU sharding along an orthogonal dimension, grounded in three foundational principles: kernel shape preservation, memory redundancy elimination, and communication overhead minimization. These principles form the basis for extending any sharding strategy into the partitioning regime. We demonstrate their effectiveness using tensor parallelism as a case study. On AMD MI300X and MI355X, exploiting partitioning capabilities yields up to 4x speedup for attention and 1.43x for fused GEMMs compared to chiplet-oblivious baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of chiplet-aware designs. Starscream's principles generalize across sharding strategies and future architectures.

items.title: Single-Tube Eight-Plex Full-Length PCR-NGS for High-Resolution HLA Typing: Assay Validation and Exploratory ADO-Risk Quality Control
items.abstract: Background: High-resolution typing of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genes is a core technology for dissecting genetic polymorphism in the MHC region of the human genome and has important clinical value in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, solid organ transplantation, and tumor immunotherapy. Although full-length HLA typing methods based on next-generation sequencing (NGS) can achieve high-resolution results, long-range PCR amplification carries the risk of allelic dropout (ADO). Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in primer-binding regions may cause the amplification failure of a given allele, leading to heterozygotes being misclassified as homozygotes and resulting in HLA typing errors. Such mistyping during donor selection for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may lead to HLA matching errors between donors and recipients, increasing the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or transplant rejection. Existing NGS approaches generally rely on a single set of amplification primers and lack an independent verification mechanism. Methods: This study designed a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay and performed systematic methodological validation. The assay simultaneously co-amplifies eight classical HLA genes (HLA-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, -DQB1, -DPB1, -DPA1, and -DQA1) in a single tube, with primers anchored in the conserved 5′UTR and 3′UTR regions to capture the complete gene sequences, and high-resolution typing was performed using the HLA-HD software. Sanger sequencing-based typing (SBT) and PacBio/ONT third-generation long-read sequencing served as dual gold standards, and multi-level validation was completed using 92 anonymous peripheral blood genomic DNA samples from the Chinese population and the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line. During primer testing, we found that two samples exhibited allele loss at the HLA-DRB1 locus in the context of SNPs in the primer-binding region, indicating that ADO risk exists in practice; after adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, ADO in these samples was resolved, but the limitations of PCR technology and the high polymorphism of HLA dictate that ADO cannot be fundamentally eliminated by primer adjustment. Accordingly, we further designed, in an exploratory manner, a 6-plex QC assay whose primer-binding regions do not overlap at all with those of the 8-plex system, for proportional spot-checking verification in large-scale sample testing. Typing results were reported and used for consistency statistics primarily at 3-field resolution; the assay can read up to 4-field resolution, but given that the accuracy of 4-field interpretation cannot be independently verified by existing gold standards, 4-field data were retained only as exploratory supplementary results. Results: (1)Validation of the 8-plex system: For the 10 SBT reference samples, the 2-field typing concordance rate was 100%, and 4-field high-resolution results could be output; the 8-plex typing of 10 blinded samples matched the PacBio third-generation sequencing 3-field results 100%; the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line typing showed no discrepancies compared with the official Cellosaurus data. (2) Discovery of ADO risk: During primer testing, two samples that were heterozygous by SBT were misclassified as homozygous by the 8-plex assay; sequence alignment analysis revealed high-frequency SNPs in the primer-binding region of the 8-plex assay for these two samples, suggesting that primer binding may have been affected. After adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, the 8-plex typing results were consistent with SBT, confirming heterozygosity. (3) Exploration of 6-plex QC: Stratified validation included 31 samples in total, comprising 10 samples dually validated by the 8-plex assay and third-generation sequencing, one standard cell line, and 20 randomly sampled clinical samples; the 8-plex and 6-plex typing results were completely consistent for all these samples; the allele depth ratio (ADR) was mostly ≤2.0 across loci in the 6-plex assay. (4) Performance evaluation: The ADR was mostly ≤2.0 across all samples; the ranking of polymorphism abundance at each locus was consistent with the trends in published Chinese population cohorts; the rare allele HLA-DPB1*744:01 was successfully captured and verified by third-generation sequencing (ONT). Conclusions: This study designed and validated a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay, which showed stable amplification, accurate typing, strong rare-allele capture capability, short turnaround time, and controllable batch testing costs in 92 Chinese population samples. During validation, ADO risk was found to exist in practice; adjusting primers for known SNP sites can correct specific ADO events but cannot fundamentally eliminate the risk. The 6-plex independent QC assay designed on this basis showed complete concordance with the 8-plex results in 31 samples, but its ability to correct real ADO events remains a theoretical inference and an indirect validation, and further evaluation through long-term clinical accumulation or large-scale parallel validation is still needed. This method is expected to provide an accurate, economical, and practical new approach for clinical high-resolution HLA typing.

items.title: Simultaneous extraction of multiple buffer-trap parameters in GaN HEMTs via measurement-window sweeping: A TCAD study
items.abstract: Abstract The duration of the measurement window strongly affects the observed current collapse in GaN HEMTs and can obscure the individual contributions of buffer traps. Using TCAD simulations of output measurements following off-state stress, this work tracks trap emission and recapture and develops a multi-exponential time-domain deconvolution method based on measurement-window sweeping. The drain current sampled at the knee voltage is analyzed as a function of the measurement-window duration to extract characteristic time constants and recovery-current amplitudes. Two-trap tests resolve the distinct recovery steps associated with Fe and deeper trap components and quantify their individual contributions. For multi-component responses, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) and time-constant-collapse criteria are used jointly to determine the number of resolvable components and identify overfitting. In the uniform-profile multi-trap test, the fitted time constants of the dominant recovery components agree with the prescribed values within approximately 16%. A further test with a nonuniform Fe profile resolves distinct fast E1 and slow Fe recovery components, with time-constant deviations of −0.85% and −29.3%, respectively. By simultaneously extracting characteristic time constants and relative contributions to the recoverable current-collapse amplitude, the method provides a quantitative basis for assessing the impact of individual trap components and guiding epitaxial and process optimization.

items.title: Self-Specializing Neuromorphic Computer: A Distributed Architecture Beyond the NPU
items.abstract: A concept paper proposing a self-specialising neuromorphic compute architecture built from existing technologies. Core ideas: Hardware that specialises itself through use: a RISC core offloading work to reconfigurable logic and analog memristor crossbars. Task training: specialisation through exposure to a varied class of related tasks, with checkpoints for rollback. Routing learned from results: inter-cell routes weighted by accuracy, speed and round-trip time, giving self-organisation and self-healing. Includes the motivation for departing from digital simulation of neural networks, related work, one illustrative implementation (component budget and power targets), and open questions for the community. Shared to stimulate discussion rather than as a finished design. Feedback welcome.

items.title: Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: replication package (code, results and paper)
items.abstract: Code, result tables, figures, decision and assumption logs, and the working paper for Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree. An open panel of 24,210 listing-months of posted GPU rental prices (NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026), four identification strategies for the age-price profile, asset values and economic life, and a seven-firm earnings restatement. `make all` rebuilds every table, figure and the paper from the archived raw files. items.abstract: Data deposit for the working paper Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree (Ajai Upadhyaya, November 2026). release/dataset/gpu_rental_panel.csv is the public panel of monthly median posted GPU rental prices (USD per GPU-hour, nominal and in 2025 dollars) for NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026; rows available only from the SkyPilot catalog history, which has no licence, are omitted. data/raw/ holds every raw file whose source permits redistribution: the author's own GPU benchmark runs and hand-recorded prices, Epoch AI hardware data (CC BY 4.0), EIA Form 861M, BLS CPI-U and SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL facts, each with a sidecar recording source URL, retrieval time and HTTP status. release/raw_manifest.csv lists every raw file used by the paper with its SHA-256 and the command that re-fetches the files not deposited here.
