items.title: Charge‐Trapping Multilayer Electrets for Partial Discharge Mitigated AlN Substrates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High electric fields within power devices can trigger partial discharge (PD), which can gradually degrade insulation materials, such as ceramic substrates and encapsulation compounds. This work counters and reduces electric fields using multilayer thin‐film electret structures incorporating , , , and AlN to mitigate PD in WBG power electronic packages. The proposed thin film structures can be conductively charged, allowing charges to be injected and trapped within the thin film stack. The stored charges generate electric fields and reduce intensified local fields that cause PD. The proposed electret design allows in‐situ conductive charging, unlike previous electrets that required pre‐charging through an external charging system. To evaluate the electric field suppression capabilities, PD measurements were performed under steep (high‐dV/dt), high‐voltage pulse excitations. The results show a decrease in PD activity, indicating a successful electric field reduction. Finite‐element simulation of the measured structure shows that the retained charge reduces the field at the triple point by about 32, and the measured apparent charge decreases in almost all conditions above the inception voltage. Overall, the proposed approach provides a promising way to improve insulation performance in high‐voltage WBG power modules.

items.title: Biologically inspired neuromorphic algorithms for low power learning
items.abstract: While neuromorphic computing offers a potential low power alternative to current resource-hungry AI, it requires fresh algorithmic approaches. The field needs a new generation of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that have not evolved with conventional hardware but instead align with characteristics of nascent neuromorphic platforms. With this goal in mind, we research biologically inspired networks that expand by incorporating fresh neurons to facilitate continual learning. This architectural plasticity is largely overlooked as a technique in conventional machine learning and is inspired by biological adult neurogenesis. To underpin our research, we provide a unifying definition and mathematical formulation for a group of associative memory networks that expand during learning. Our formulation enables theoretical network optimisation which demonstrates greater than 10,000 times improvement in memory capacity compared to previous work. We then direct our focus on the learning step itself and propose several new neurogenesis learning strategies that increase in memory recall accuracy from 69% to 96%, while retaining a fixed resource budget. Furthermore, through application of our findings to the more complex task of Class Incremental Learning (CIL), we are able demonstrate that dedicating separate resources to the independent learning of each class can help to regulate learning. Our consolidated findings include: methods to increase accuracy by reducing bias towards specific memories during learning; methods to reduce the computational cost of architectural plasticity during learning; and empirical demonstration that a modular network topology can be exploited to optimise neurogenesis. In summary, we extend existing neuromorphic research through the formal articulation, assessment, and advancement of learning strategies that incorporate architectural plasticity. The research responds directly to calls from the neuromorphic research community for original approaches to progress neuromorphic algorithm development.

items.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research Trends on Simulation Studies of AlGaN/GaN High-Electron-Mobility Transistors Using the Scopus Database
items.abstract: Abstract As the design space of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) grows increasingly complex, simulation has become an indispensable tool for understanding device physics and optimizing performance before fabrication. However, few studies have measured and analyzed the scientific publications on AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation from a global perspective. In this bibliometric study, our aim was to evaluate the global research trends in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation areas based on publication outputs, co-authorships among countries, and co-occurrences of author keywords. Using the Scopus database, a total of 4,492 journal articles and conference papers published between 1997 and 2026 were retrieved and analyzed using VOSviewer. Results have shown that since 2001, the number of publications has increased steadily, with the highest annual output recorded in 2025 (490 articles), resulting in a steady increase in the cumulative total publications. China (1,284 articles) and India (961 articles) are the leading contributors, followed by the USA (695 articles); however, Belgium, the UAE, and Singapore exhibit the highest rates of international collaboration. A keyword co-occurrence analysis of 61 keywords revealed six distinct thematic clusters, dominated by power/thermal management, device/HEMT core, modeling/RF, TCAD/gate, electric field, and machine learning. The most recently active keywords include TCAD simulation, gate leakage current, power amplifier, and S-parameter, suggesting a growing emphasis on simulation-driven design and RF performance in recent years. In conclusion, recent progress in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation research includes the following (but not limited to): (i) integration of advanced TCAD and physics-based models for trap dynamics and self-heating; (ii) AI-driven and machine learning approaches for device modeling; and (iii) continued exploration of p-GaN gate and enhancement-mode structures for high-power and high-frequency applications.

items.title: BF-IMNA: A Bit Fluid In-Memory Neural Architecture for Neural Network Acceleration
items.abstract: Mixed-precision quantization, which assigns precisions per-layer, per-network, per-channel, or per-parameter, is gaining traction for efficient Neural Network (NN) realization with higher throughput and lower energy. Unlike conventional fixed-precision accelerators, BF-IMNA advances the mixed-precision design space through an AP-based in-memory implementation. We present BF-IMNA, a bit fluid IMC accelerator for end-to-end Convolutional NN inference supporting static and dynamic mixed-precision without run-time reconfiguration overhead. At its heart are Associative Processors (APs), bit-serial word-parallel SIMD-like engines. We evaluate ImageNet inference with AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 across SRAM and ReRAM CAM cells, mixed-precision configurations, and supply voltages. To demonstrate bit fluidity, we apply HAWQ-V3's published ResNet18 schedules to the BF-IMNA cost model and pair them with HAWQ-V3's published accuracies and model sizes. The results reveal an accuracy–Energy-Delay Product trade-off. The high-latency point is \(1.16\) points below INT8 accuracy with \(1.13\times\) better EDP, while the low-latency point has \(1.91\times\) better EDP and a \(45.5\%\) smaller model at a \(3.00\) -point accuracy reduction. At 500-MHz, true-batch-one comparison, BitFusion provides lower absolute energy and latency, while BF-IMNA provides lower average power at all five operating points, \(2106\times\) greater on-chip weight capacity ( \(32.8\times\) per unit modeled area), and larger relative energy reductions at aggressive INT4 and low-latency HAWQ points.
items.venue: ACM Journal on Emerging Technologies in Computing Systems

items.title: BCAT: A Block Causal Transformer for PDE Foundation Models for Fluid Dynamics
items.abstract: Background: Foundation models have demonstrated remarkable generalization in vision and language, but their accurate use for scientific computing remains challenging. For two-dimensional fluid-dynamics prediction, current transformer-based models are often hindered by limited context and rigid causality information, as they typically map fixed windows to the next step. Objectives: We aim to develop a unified architecture for heterogeneous fluid-dynamics families. The goal is to better capture the complex spatio-temporal dependencies inherent in nonlinear fluid dynamics. Methods: We introduce BCAT, a block-causal transformer for autoregressive prediction of two-dimensional fluid-dynamics solutions. Our approach adapts block-causal attention to next-frame prediction, leveraging previous frames as contextual priors. The model is trained on 69K trajectory sequences from PDEBench, PDEArena, and CFDBench using the Muon optimizer. Results: BCAT achieved an average relative 𝐿 2 error of 1.18% across the six evaluated fluid families, reducing error by 45% relative to a 3.4-times-larger baseline. In ablations, next-frame prediction was 3.5x more accurate than the corresponding nexttoken variant. A five-seed analysis, noisy-input stress test, long-rollout analysis, and physics diagnostics further characterize the model. Conclusions: The block-causal framework captures spatial interactions within frames while enforcing temporal causality across frames. BCAT provides an accurate and computationally efficient model for the two-dimensional fluid-dynamics benchmarks considered here.

items.title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry with Emulated Double-Precision Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
items.abstract: The evaluation of exact exchange and the treatment of electron correlation remain major computational challenges in electronic-structure theory. Over the past decade, GPU computing has substantially accelerated these calculations, extending the scale and complexity of electronic-structure problems that can be addressed computationally. More recently, GPU architectures developed to meet the demands of artificial intelligence have introduced new opportunities for acceleration, with Tensor Cores providing reduced-precision arithmetic throughput far exceeding that of native double-precision (FP64) operations. Exploiting this performance advantage while preserving the numerical accuracy required in quantum chemistry remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate the Ozaki-I and Ozaki-II floating-point emulation schemes in the RI-HF, RI-MP2, and RI-CCSD implementations of EXESS on NVIDIA GB200 GPUs. We demonstrate that Ozaki-II at 52-bit precision achieves numerical accuracy comparable to native FP64, delivering complete calculation speedups of up to 1.26× (cc-pVDZ) and 1.50× (cc-pVTZ) for RI-HF, 2.55× and 3.01× for RI-MP2, and 3.11× and 2.15× for RI-CCSD. The energy to solution improves by 1.22× and 2.21× for the representative RI-HF and RI-MP2 cc- pVTZ calculations and by 2.37× for the RI- CCSD cc-pVDZ calculation. Reducing the precision to 47 bits provides further acceleration while maintaining total energy deviations below 0.1 kcal mol -1 across all systems examined.

items.title: AI-Assistant Thermal Hotspot Prediction and Chip Placement Optimization for Semiconductor Packages
items.abstract: Semiconductor packages are becoming more complex due to the increasing integration of multiple chips and chiplets within a single package. This can lead to higher heat generation and uneven temperature distribution, resulting in the formation of thermal hotspots. Excessive temperature can affect the performance and reliability of semiconductor devices. Conventional thermal analysis methods generally require repeated simulations to evaluate different chip placement arrangements, which can increase the time and computational effort. This project proposes an AI-based thermal hotspot prediction and chip placement optimization system for semiconductor packages. The proposed approach uses HotSpot thermal simulation to generate temperature data for different chip placement configurations. The generated dataset is processed using Python or MATLAB and used to train a Machine Learning model. The trained model predicts the maximum temperature and identifies possible thermal hotspot regions for different placement arrangements. Based on the predicted temperature, suitable chip placement configurations are selected and validated using HotSpot simulation. The proposed system aims to reduce the effort required for evaluating multiple placement configurations and support improved thermal-aware chip placement
authors: Prathiksha P, Shamini Genisia D, Dhecika M
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.title: AI ethics by design: implementing customizable guardrails for responsible AI development
items.abstract: This paper explores the development of an ethical guardrail framework for AI systems, emphasizing the importance of customizable guardrails that align with diverse user values and underlying ethics. We address the challenges of AI ethics by proposing a structure that integrates rules, policies, and AI assistants to ensure responsible AI behavior, while comparing the proposed framework to the existing state-of-the-art guardrails. By focusing on practical mechanisms for implementing ethical standards, we aim to enhance transparency, user autonomy, and continuous improvement in AI systems. Our approach accommodates ethical pluralism, offering a flexible and adaptable solution for the evolving landscape of AI governance. The paper concludes with strategies for resolving conflicts between ethical directives, underscoring the present and future need for robust, nuanced and context-aware AI systems.

items.title: ADAPTATION AND EVALUATION OF THE MEMBRAIN SYSTEM FOR PROFILE-GUIDED DATA PLACEMENT ON INTEL XEON MAX PROCESSORS
items.abstract: We investigate the efficient utilization of tiered HBM and DDR memory on Intel Xeon Max processors under constrained high-bandwidth memory capacity. Unlike conventional capacity-expansion architectures (DRAM + CXL/NVM), tiered memory management with an integrated HBM tier remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we adapt the MemBrain automated profile-guided data placement framework for Intel Xeon Max servers: implementing interprocedural allocation-site function cloning in the LLVM compiler, hardware monitoring of last-level cache misses via PEBS, and guided user-space memory placement via the Intel UMF library. We study data placement optimization strategies based on an exact combinatorial optimization model (knapsack problem) and heuristic selection algorithms. Experimental evaluation on the LULESH 2.0 and Graph500-BFS benchmarks demonstrates that profile-guided data placement achieves up to 98.4%–99.9% of pure HBM performance while utilizing only a fraction of its physical capacity.

items.title: A Scalable 5 kW Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) Source for Next-Generation EUV Lithography: Design, Thermal Management, and Spectral Purity Analysis
items.abstract: The semiconductor industry's reliance on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is currently bottlenecked by the Laser-Produced Plasma (LPP) source, which suffers from low conversion efficiency (CE~5%), tin debris, and massive power consumption (>1 MW). In this paper, we propose a scaled-up Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) source as a possible alternative. By scaling a laboratory microwave-discharge approach to a 5 kW microwave input, we outline a design that delivers between about 5 W and 110 W of in-band EUV power, depending on a conversion efficiency (0.5% to 10%) that is not yet verified for xenon. We address the main engineering bottlenecks of MDPP through three solutions: (1) a water-cooled aluminium nitride (AlN) capillary, transparent to microwaves, to manage a 4,500 W thermal load, (2) magnetic confinement and a magnetic nozzle to shrink the emitting column and reach a geometric etendue of about 1.0 mm²·sr, and (3) a Zr filter and two Mo/Si mirrors that reach a spectral purity above 99.99% under stated assumptions. A source-to-machine analysis shows that, for a 20 W target at the intermediate focus, a 5 kW source needs a conversion efficiency of at least about 3.6% with hemispherical collection, and about 81% with the closed end-on capillary, so the source geometry must be chosen from the optics requirement. Our calculations also expose open problems: the plasma density needed for efficient 13.5 nm emission is far above what a 100 mTorr, 2.45 GHz discharge is known to reach, and the Zr filter and the collection geometry limit the usable power. The design is therefore a concept for further modeling and experiment, not a demonstrated source.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A 1.25‐GS/s SAR ADC With Scalable Input and 3–6‐Bit Reconfigurable Resolution for Operation Unit‐Based RRAM–CIM Architectures
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The operation unit (OU)‐based architecture is widely adopted in resistive random access memory‐based compute‐in‐memory (RRAM–CIM) macros. As the OU size may vary across different designs and under different workloads, the resolution‐reconfigurable analog‐to‐digital converters (ADCs) are required for better energy efficiency. To this end, this paper presents a 3–6‐bits reconfigurable asynchronous successive approximation register (SAR) ADC with an input‐scalable architecture. The proposed design supports resolution reconfiguration by scaling the bitline current that charges the sampling capacity dynamically according to the required computing resolution. Moreover, we utilize the upper‐plate sampling method to reduce settling time during the most significant bit phase and introduce an asynchronous control scheme combined with a high‐speed dynamic comparator to enable a short decision period. The proposed single‐channel SAR ADC is designed with a 28‐nm process, achieving 1.25‐GS/s sampling rate at 1‐V supply with only 0.85‐mW power consumption. Compared to the fixed‐resolution ADC, the proposed design achieves 13%–43% power savings by reducing comparison cycles and enabling early termination.
items.venue: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.abstract: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.abstract: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

items.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
items.abstract: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. In particular, for all three properties, TabPFN applied to Chemprop's own embedding is more accurate than Chemprop's predictions. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying "both are bad" rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model's share of decisive votes is flat. The rise holds within the same voter and on the same pair, and across arrival cohorts from their first recorded vote. It holds with prompt controls, in every major language, for dated vendor snapshots, open-weight models and models with stable answer length, and between interface changes. The drift is shared across models: month effects estimated from other models' pairs remove it from each model's own pairs. Platform-wide, the average model would be expected to score 78% against the 2023 average, yet the share of "both are bad" votes ended near where it began. The pattern fits a standard that follows the category's progress, so a product that stands still is judged as declining. Absolute verdicts on AI drifted while relative comparisons held steady, an evaluation drift that matters for LLM leaderboards and for the human feedback used to train models.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.abstract: Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale. Performance simulation offers a lower cost alternative, yet controlled comparisons among existing simulators remain difficult because they differ in the training stages they model and the workloads on which they are evaluated. We introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators. The framework decomposes simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule level aggregation, connecting execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets. Following this framework, we profile 23 model settings from 10 dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM families on an Ascend Neural Processing Unit (NPU) cluster. The resulting dataset contains 348 feasible configurations that jointly vary five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation, with six views spanning configuration, rank, operator, event, and kernel granularity. Evaluations of representative training simulators demonstrate how LM-SimBench supports comparisons of prediction accuracy, assessment of configuration selection, and diagnosis of prediction errors. Matched GPU-NPU experiments validate the cross-platform applicability of the collection and evaluation protocol and demonstrate NPU-guided GPU configuration selection.

items.title: Chain of Physics: Supporting Fault Diagnosis with Engineering-Inspired Large Language Model Reasoning
items.abstract: Fault diagnosis in complex systems requires linking observed changes in physical quantities to the failure mechanisms that produce them. Experienced engineers perform this task by combining sensor information with knowledge of system behavior and fault propagation. Large Language Models (LLMs) can support this process, but their diagnostic reasoning depends on the availability of asset-specific engineering knowledge and on how this knowledge is represented and used during inference. This work introduces Chain of Physics (CoP), an LLM-based fault-diagnosis framework built around a Constrained Knowledge Graph (CKG) generated automatically from asset-specific reference documentation. CoP addresses failure-sensor association from textual engineering knowledge. The CKG stores diagnostic chains connecting failure modes, changes in physical quantities, and monitoring sensors. During inference, semantically similar graph paths are retrieved for each question and used as both information and in-context examples for the reasoning process. Candidate failure modes are extracted from the question and analysed independently through dedicated LLM calls, which generate plausible failure-to-observation chains. A final decision module compares these chains with the available answer choices. CoP is evaluated on the FailureSensorIQ benchmark across four industrial asset classes and three LLMs. Compared with direct prompting and conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), CoP improves diagnostic accuracy across all evaluated models, with gains ranging from 7.8 to 19.6 percentage points and from 11.7 to 18.2 percentage points, respectively. The results show that structured engineering knowledge can improve LLM-based diagnostic reasoning when graph retrieval is combined with in-context examples of fault propagation.

items.title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
items.abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a reserved Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value declaring agent traffic, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration to a class served after best-effort traffic, and a rate-limited priority queue. VATC was compared with static Differentiated Services (DiffServ), a dedicated class that trusts the marking, and fq_codel, a per-flow fair-queuing scheduler, in two simulators and on a real Linux kernel. VATC matched DiffServ under steady load. In a constructed burst it cut mean agent queuing delay by 98% relative to DiffServ in simulation (assuming an immediate verdict), at a 12% increase in human delay; most of the gain came from the separate class. Under a spoofed flood in the kernel, the rate limit held human latency 11 times below DiffServ's. Without verification, DiffServ and a tightly configured fq_codel gave legitimate agents lower latency than VATC; a live four-feature classifier then demoted all 20 bulk-shaped spoofers and gave agents 0.30 ms, but missed six spoofers that copied the agent pattern. With emulated network delay, a timing feature of the classifier stopped separating agent from human flows. In real agent harnesses on a congested link, router queueing took 13% to 63% of task time, depending on harness and assumed model latency. The traffic was synthetic or sandbox-scale.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.abstract: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropout ($Δ= -12.4$ percentage points [pp], exact McNemar $p = 5.5 \times 10^{-6}$), while LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct drops from $84.0\%$ to $76.8\%$ ($Δ= -7.2$ pp, $p = 0.0198$). Conversely, dispersing the identical cumulative budget uniformly across generation steps via stratified quintile matching yields substantially milder degradation (retaining $91.2\%$ in Qwen and $84.0\%$ in LLaMA). In an exploratory factorial dissociation ($N=100$), single-step dropout density is associated with an acute drop in a single schedule draw ($-10.0$ pp on Qwen, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.0425$), while multi-token continuity exhibits an inconclusive compounding trend ($-7.0$ pp, $p_{\text{holm}} = 0.1892$). Error analysis reveals that Qwen failures reflect derivation errors within formatted responses (conditional accuracy drop of $-11.4$ pp), whereas in LLaMA $22.2\%$ of discordant losses lack a final answer format line (conditional gap narrows to $-5.0$ pp). These findings demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are particularly vulnerable to concentrated structural disruptions, providing empirical benchmarks for fault tolerance in transformer architectures.

items.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model
items.abstract: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. HaiRuo pairs two components with a clear division of labour: (1) HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global satellite-altimetry observations, which supplies the 15-day physical fields and masks (+0.14 field skill and +1.1 mIoU points under the same decoder) and further lowers 15-day centre error by 1.2 km frozen (1.35 km over training from scratch); and (2) XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that samples the evolving forecast in each eddy's co-moving polar frame and refines the 15-day path across three look-ahead rounds, removing 2.5 km on HaiRuo-1B (2.9 km with joint fine-tuning) and 2.5-3.3 km via its object attention across six published backbones. Under one pre-registered global evaluation over the whole ocean, HaiRuo improves on fourteen methods on every endpoint (25.2 vs. 30.6 km 15-day centre error, -18%), holding its margin outside the labelled regions and through both phases of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), while reproducing westward drift, 50-60 deg S eastward reversal and poleward cyclone-anticyclone deflection. Over ten days through one fixed tracker, HaiRuo's forecast field cuts the eddy-centre error of WenHai and XiHe by 37-43% (-2.8 km vs. day 0 while they degrade +4.3-8.7 km), and its object trajectories cut pipeline error by 77-78% globally. Open-weight checkpoints, code and project page: https://github.com/xkqin/HaiRuo

items.title: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
items.abstract: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. Sable fixes an integer function F_O with no floating-point step, in which every rounding, normalization, softmax and sampling decision is determined by its inputs, and proves it with a constraint system whose relations provably never wrap modulo the 31-bit KoalaBear prime. The proof batches zerochecks and LogUp-GKR lookups into one sumcheck per domain, and commits to every witness tensor and weight in one multilinear commitment built from Reed-Solomon codes, BLAKE3 Merkle trees and a mixed-length BaseFold opening. The prover streams the model layer by layer on one GPU. On one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, Sable proves all 64 layers of Qwen2.5-32B in 92.5 s for 4,096 tokens and 398 s for 16,384 tokens, and covers Qwen3-32B and the mixture-of-experts Qwen3-30B-A3B (4,096 tokens in 121.8 and 84.7 s). A proof costs 41 to 50 times the serving time, or 6.4 cents per 4,096-token request at public GPU prices, and 40 to 64 times less time per parameter and token than zkLLM. On WikiText-2, F_O's greedy token matches the BF16 model's at 86.3% of positions; on Qwen3, F_O is within 1.6 points of BF16 on MMLU and 1.7 points on GSM8K. A verifier with a compiled core checks a proof on one CPU core in 19 to 56 s. In the random-oracle model, the interactive proof has round-by-round soundness error 2^-103. The proof is not zero-knowledge, so the system targets open-weight models. Code: https://github.com/moonmath-ai/Sable

items.title: From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models
items.abstract: Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to''. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails. We argue that positionality -- the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said -- is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? Against the vendors' answer of nowhere and the seductive possibility of everywhere, we argue that when a model is taken as-if speaking, it speaks from somewhere, and this means positionality can describe models, and the way they are believed beyond their warrant, even though they are not accountable speakers. A model's positionality is laminar -- laid down across corpus, tuning, system prompt, application and the live conversation. We separate three sets of factors: the positionality of a model's creators, the behaviour they intend for it, and the behaviour it enacts, and situate current work within this matrix. This lets us highlight what each stratum inherits from the one below, with ruptures and collapses where that inheritance is disavowed. We then return to where models speak from, and discuss the implications for how models are made, read and held accountable.

items.title: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents
items.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous builders of biomedical models, but existing benchmarks are small, near saturation or open to leaked information. We present BioXArena-Pro, 64 research-level modelling tasks from eight biomedical domains, each rebuilt from a published study; most hold out whole biological units such as species or cohorts. Across 22 agent configurations, the best scores 55.1 of 100, and the scaffold matters almost as much as the model. We re-ran a published method for every task: where the published recipe applies unchanged, the best agent and the methods tie; on rebuilt tasks the methods trail by 8.2 points, suggesting that agents gain by adapting to new data. Pretrained models (including biological foundation models) matter where the strongest agent uses them: forbidding them decreases its score on those tasks by 9 points. Every task was audited in several AI-assisted rounds and a final human review.

items.title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
items.abstract: Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

items.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
items.abstract: Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reasoning on later segments. To address these limitations, we propose TreeAgent, a structure-aware agent that uses the input hierarchy to guide both segment-wise context processing and access to past information. Specifically, TreeAgent constructs segments from complete subtrees and groups of adjacent sibling subtrees to preserve local structural relationships. We provide theoretical guarantees on segment counts to guide token budget selection toward matching the segment count of fixed-length segmentation. We further attach structural paths to the segments for the agent to identify their ancestors and hierarchical positions. We also introduce residual memory links from the segments of low-level children to the segments of high-level parents, enabling direct information flows beyond successive memory updates. We evaluate TreeAgent with four representative memory agents on eight retrieval and aggregation tasks. The inputs are derived from real-world application data in JSON, HTML, YAML, and JavaScript and range from 8K to 1M tokens. TreeAgent improves the average score across the four datasets for all four agents, with 3.61% performance gain on average.

items.title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
items.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.

items.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
items.abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

items.title: Uncovering the Memory Hierarchy of Modern NVIDIA GPUs for Accurate Simulation
items.abstract: Emerging artificial intelligence workloads, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), place unprecedented demands on GPU memory systems. Consequently, architectural innovations increasingly target the memory system to alleviate these bottlenecks. However, existing works still rely on outdated memory hierarchy models that fail to capture the complexities of modern hardware. This fidelity gap leads to inaccurate characterization and could misguide optimization strategies. To bridge this gap, we present GemAtlas, the first systematic reverse engineering of the memory hierarchy in modern NVIDIA GPUs. By developing fine-grained SASS-level benchmarking, we expose critical, previously undocumented micro-architectural details across different cache levels, including cache set associativity, slice-routing and set-indexing hash functions, replacement policies, coherence behavior, and interconnect topologies. We integrate these discovered micro-architecture details into the state-of-the-art GPU simulation framework. The final results demonstrate that GemAtlas reduces the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 31.69% to 22.24% on average across four GPUs. Specifically, GemAtlas reduces the MAPE from 34.04% to 23.98% for real-world LLM operators.

items.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
items.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

items.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% area reduction over commercial synthesis. (3) Design-specific synthesis optimization. We explore agent-driven synthesis script tuning and the discovery of executable synthesis algorithms across intermediate representations, technology-independent optimization, and technology mapping. Finally, we envision AI-native design automation that jointly explores architectural, RTL, and EDA algorithm design spaces, guided by verification constraints and implementation feedback.

items.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
items.abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. AutoManifold conditions every stage of its design on user-specified structural preservation preferences, and iteratively refines the algorithm configuration through an LLM-guided, metric-grounded iterative loop. We compare the generated algorithms against the three strongest and most frequently used SOTA methods (t-SNE, UMAP, and PaCMAP) on real-world datasets spanning different difficulty regimes under identical evaluation infrastructure. The results demonstrate that LLM-driven, priority-conditioned algorithm synthesis can move beyond hyperparameter tuning, producing genuinely new algorithms that outperform traditional hand-designed methods in their ability to steer towards user-specified properties without compromising the intrinsic structure in the original data. The code of AutoManifold is available at https://github.com/buraksusam/AutoManifold_NeurIPS2026.

items.title: FedVP: Federated Learning across Heterogeneous Models by Pooling Locally Trained Verifiers
items.abstract: Conventional federated learning relies on the shared model backbone to aggregate client updates, limiting collaboration among institutions that deploy large language models (LLMs) from different families and at different scales. We propose Federated Verifier Pool (FEDVP), a new federated learning paradigm that enables heterogeneous clients to collaborate through shared verification rather than parameter aggregation. Each client trains a verifier using local data and responses generated by its chosen LLM backbone. The server pools these independently trained verifiers and combines their judgments to select answers without merging model parameters. This allows both LLM backbones and verifiers to differ in architecture and size, while keeping the LLM backbones frozen and deriving collaborative gains from improved answer selection. We evaluate FEDVP across five public medical question-answering datasets treated as federated clients, using Qwen and LLaMA backbones ranging from 3B to 14B parameters. FEDVP consistently improves performance across all five clients and outperforms the strongest conventional federated baselines by 1.46-5.79 percentage points in mean accuracy.

items.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
items.abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating and optimizing hardware circuits, ensuring the correctness of AI-generated designs becomes more important. Meanwhile, advances in AI lower the barriers to developing and applying formal methods, creating new opportunities to automate and improve hardware verification. This invited paper presents an overview of the methodologies and applications of hardware formal methods in the AI era. First, we examine how agentic AI advances hardware formal methods across three levels: specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines. Second, we discuss how formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization. We review representative research alongside our recent contributions, highlighting key technical advances and insights from experimental results. Finally, we discuss future research opportunities toward proof-native hardware development, where formal reasoning could become an integral part of autonomous hardware design.

items.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
items.abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poisoning attacks may be developed. In this paper we focus on semantic memory, we discuss its attack, and mitigation strategies. We introduce private knowledge retrieval and private inference. We propose a signature system in the knowledge base to prevent from undesired manipulation. This should avoid memory poisoning attacks by introducing security by design in the construction of the semantic memory. In our architecture, an agent contains a local Prolog-like inference system (i.e., using Horn clauses to represent knowledge) which accesses an external knowledge base to get the required knowledge. This externally signed knowledge base is accessed privately. We provide different implementations in Python using different privacy levels including k-anonymity and information-theoretical privacy (IT-PIR).

items.title: ZEBRA‐Prop: A Zero‐Shot Embedding‐Based Rapid and Accessible Regression Model for Materials Properties
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit substantial potential across diverse scientific disciplines, including materials science. A property prediction framework, ZEBRA‐Prop (Zero‐Shot Embedding‐Based Rapid and Accessible Regression Model for Materials Properties), is presented here as an extension of LLM‐Prop. In contrast to LLM‐Prop, which requires task‐specific fine‐tuning of the LLM, ZEBRA‐Prop keeps the text encoder frozen and eliminates task‐specific fine‐tuning of the LLM, thereby reducing computational cost and enabling rapid model training. The framework employs MatBERT, a language model pretrained on materials science literature, to enhance predictive capability. Multiple textual embeddings are incorporated through a learnable weighting mechanism, which alleviates the context‐length constraints inherent in LLM‐Prop and facilitates effective integration of diverse textual representations. Evaluation is conducted using two datasets: the TextEdge dataset (~140,000 entries) and an in‐house dataset (~2000 entries) derived from the Materials Project database, with physical properties obtained from first‐principles calculations. The predictive performance of ZEBRA‐Prop is close to that of LLM‐Prop, while the training time is reduced by approximately 95%. The performance improvements are attributable to three principal factors: domain‐specific LLM utilization, diversified textual descriptions, and systematic text preprocessing. ZEBRA‐Prop is a scalable, computationally efficient framework that supports accelerated materials discovery, particularly under limited computational resources.

items.title: Where Correction Stops Paying: Error-Correction Energy for Memory at Fleet Scale
items.abstract: Error-correcting code (ECC) memory costs energy three ways: extra stored bits, patrol scrubbing, and correction logic on every access. This paper prices those costs at fleet scale from published inputs (DRAM soft-error rates from the large-fleet studies of Schroeder et al. 2009, Sridharan et al. 2013/2015 and Meza et al. 2015, which span orders of magnitude; ECC overhead fractions for SECDED (64+8) and a stronger device-correcting code (128+32); DRAM access energy from Horowitz 2014) and prices what correction buys under a plainly stated energy valuation of a prevented crash (1.2e6 J: a 500 W server restarting for 600 s plus re-executing half of a 1 h checkpoint interval, with one uncorrected error in 1e4 taken to cause a crash; silent corruption is assigned no energy value). For a reference fleet of 100,000 servers with 512 GiB each (54.98 PB), SECDED draws a continuous 707759.3 W (6.204 GWh per year), 97.09% of it the background power of the extra stored bits; scrubbing draws 114.53 W and logic 450.0 W. At a representative 25000 FIT per Mbit the fleet corrects 4.2290e-3 errors per joule of ECC energy (236.46 J per correction, against 2.8836e-9 J for the correction act itself) and the avoided crash energy is 0.5075 times the energy spent. SECDED breaks even in energy at 49263.0 FIT per Mbit, at the top of the published range; the stronger code breaks even against SECDED only at 2539132.7 FIT per Mbit, far above any published fleet rate. Conclusion: ECC is not an energy-saving measure at any published error rate; it is a continuous capacity cost paid for correctness. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF and markdown, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).

items.title: Wafer-to-Wafer Bonding-induced Fingerprints and Their Interaction with Optimal Choice of Field Layout for Backside Lithography
items.abstract: Wafer-to-wafer bonding schemes requiring backside lithography absorb bonding-induced distortions into the target wafer, directly affecting the achievable on-product overlay after thinning. While scanner correction models can compensate a large fraction of this distortion content, the influence of litho-graphic field layout on correction efficiency remains insufficiently understood. In this work, experimentally measured (backside-) distortion maps from hydrophilic fusion-bonded wafers with densely distributed alignment markers are used as inputs to large-scale correction-per-exposure (CPE) simulations. More than 6600 virtual field layouts are evaluated using a common six-parameter intra-field correction model. The results show that residual overlay varies by more than a factor of two across the investigated field-layout space despite identical input distortion fields and identical correction methodology. Several geometric descriptors are introduced to quantify the interaction between exposure fields and a localized annular bonding-induced fingerprint. The study demonstrates that field-layout selection constitutes a significant optimization variable for backside lithography. The proposed descriptor framework provides physical insight into the interaction between lithographic exposure fields and bonding-induced distortion fingerprints, and underlines the need for practical guidelines for minimizing residual overlay when low-order field-wise correction models are employed.

items.title: Understanding Advances in Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Over the Past Ten Years: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience (CCN) is an interdisciplinary field that uses computational models to understand how the brain gives rise to cognition. Although the field has grown substantially over the past ten years, no review has systematically mapped the major advances achieved during this period. This review therefore aims to map advances in CCN over the past ten years by analyzing the most frequently used computational models, the cognitive domains investigated, and the computational tools employed, and by determining the predominant emphasis of the studies, whether theoretical, translational, or integrated. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the methodology proposed by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) and reported following PRISMA-ScR. Searches were performed in PubMed, Embase and IEEE Xplore between 24 and 28 April 2025, and were complemented by a supplementary relevance-ranked Scopus search and by expert-informed identification of additional records. A total of 104 studies were included. Recent progress in CCN was found to be predominantly theoretical, with research focused on memory, learning, language and communication, and decision-making. Recurrent neural networks and Bayesian models emerged as the most widely adopted frameworks. Although CCN has advanced rapidly over the past ten years, the field continues to face critical challenges, notably concerning neurobiological plausibility, model integration, limited external generalizability, and a pressing need for more translational research. Beyond the reviewed corpus, the review discusses emerging AI paradigms, transformers, foundation models, large language models, and neuromorphic computing, as prospective directions informed by complementary literature.

items.title: Two-dimensional indium selenide (InSe): fundamentals, synthesis strategies, and next- generation optoelectronic device architecture
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) layered semiconductors have garnered significant interest as promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic applications, owing to their tunable electronic band structures, high surface-to-volume ratios, and pronounced light-matter interactions. Among this growing family of materials, van der Waals indium selenide (InSe) has emerged as a particularly attractive candidate for future high-mobility optoelectronic devices, such as high-performance photodetectors, polarisation-sensitive devices, and chemical sensors. This is primarily due to its thickness-dependent bandgap, high intrinsic carrier mobility, and strong optical absorption. Compared with other extensively investigated 2D materials, InSe combines a comparatively high electron mobility with a layer-tunable band gap and spectral response extending from the visible to near-infrared region, whereas graphene lacks a band gap and MoS 2 shows weak near-infrared absorption. Its practical advantage, however, depends on encapsulation, contact quality, and phase control. This review provides a comprehensive and critical assessment of recent advances in InSe-based photodetectors, with particular emphasis on their crystal structure, electronic properties, synthesis methodologies, and device engineering strategies. Various fabrication techniques, including mechanical exfoliation, liquid-phase exfoliation, chemical vapor deposition, and physical vapor deposition routes (physical vapor transport, pulsed laser deposition, molecular beam epitaxy, and thermal evaporation) are systematically discussed in relation to their impact on material quality and device performance, together with the transfer and device fabrication steps that link the material to the photodetector. Furthermore, the fundamental photodetection mechanisms, including photoconductive, photovoltaic, and photogating effects, are analyzed in detail to elucidate charge generation and transport processes. Recent developments in device architectures, particularly heterostructure-based photodetectors, are also highlighted to demonstrate performance-enhancement strategies. Moreover, key challenges, such as environmental instability and the need for scalable synthesis approaches, are critically examined. Future research directions aimed at achieving high-performance, stable, and commercially viable InSe-based optoelectronic devices are also outlined.

items.title: Tri-Stack-PIM: A Heterogeneous Multi-Die 3D-Integrated Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Efficient LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference during autoregressive decoding is fundamentally memory-bandwidth-bound. Existing three-dimensional (3D) stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures alleviate the off-chip bandwidth wall, yet remain constrained by several limitations: physical layer (PHY), controllers, and direct memory access (DMA) engines compete with arithmetic units for advanced-node base-die area; hybrid-bonding keep-out zones fragment the base-die floorplan and impede physical design; compute tiles built in a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) process are restricted to low logic density, capping achievable throughput; and nonlinear operations offloaded to the host reintroduce a communication bottleneck. We present Tri-Stack-PIM, a heterogeneous three-die architecture that resolves these tensions by dedicating a top DRAM die to storage, a middle buffer die on a mature process node to PHYs, DMA engines, and near-memory compute units, and a bottom base die on an advanced node exclusively to single-instruction-multiple-data (SIMD) multiply-accumulate (MAC) arrays. We further introduce a Unified Buffer-Aware Ready-based (UBAR) hardware out-of-order micro-operation scheduler that enforces cross-die dependency correctness at runtime while maximizing issue-slot utilization through a multi-term priority function, recovering up to 90% of the cycles that an in-order policy would forfeit. A joint architecture-dataflow co-exploration identifies Pareto-optimal configurations that reduce the energy-delay product (EDP) by 33-66x over naive parameter selection. Evaluated across multi-head, grouped-query, and multi-query attention (MHA, GQA, MQA) mechanisms with batch sizes 1-32, Tri-Stack-PIM achieves geometric-mean speedups of 4.95x, 2.57x, and 1.68x across all three attention mechanisms and batch sizes over a graphics processing unit (GPU) baseline, AttAcc, and H2-LLM, respectively.

items.title: Time Series Analysis in Frequency Domain: A Survey of Open Challenges, Opportunities and Benchmarks
items.abstract: Frequency-domain analysis has emerged as a powerful paradigm for time series analysis, offering unique advantages over traditional time-domain approaches while introducing new theoretical and practical challenges. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of spectral methods from classical Fourier analysis to modern neural operators, systematically summarizing three open challenges in current research: (1) causal structure preservation during spectral transformations, (2) uncertainty quantification in learned frequency representations, and (3) topology-aware analysis for non-Euclidean data structures. Through rigorous reviewing of over 100 studies, we develop a unified taxonomy that bridges conventional spectral techniques with cutting-edge machine learning approaches, while establishing standardized benchmarks for performance evaluation. Our work identifies key knowledge gaps in the field, particularly in geometric deep learning and quantum-enhanced spectral analysis. The survey offers practitioners a systematic framework for method selection and implementation, while charting promising directions for future research in this rapidly evolving domain.

items.title: Thermodynamic and Infrastructural Implications of Spatial State Computation for Synthetic Intelligence
items.abstract: Thermodynamic and Infrastructural Implications of Spatial State Computation for Synthetic IntelligenceAuthor: David P. Reichwein (Asymmetric Intelligence & Innovation, November 2026) Executive Summary & Core Premise The Energy Wall: Contemporary AI inference relying on dense matrix multiplication (GEMM) over continuous weight tensors faces severe infrastructural limits, driven by high-bandwidth memory (HBM) traffic, long planar interconnects, and facility-scale power demands reaching hundreds of megawatts. Software guardrails add an additional 20% to 100% tax in latency and power without altering the dominant energy terms. The Spatial Substrate Alternative: This paper examines an alternative architecture defined in the AI² corpus: a finite three-dimensional lattice where computation is a field configuration rather than a token string. Architectural Specifications (S₁) The object is defined as S₁ := ⟨ Q_64³, L_codex, Π_PCR, T ⟩, comprising: The Body (Q_64³): A face-centered-cubic parity sublattice consisting of 131,072 sites with a 12-neighbor stencil (||δ||₂ = √2) and a graph diameter of 94 hops. Dual-Bus Registers: Every site carries two distinct registers: a cognitive symbol C(v) typed in Codex-1, and an authorization state E(v) ∈ {⊥, IDLE, COND, ⊤}. The authorization field is monotone non-increasing between exogenous grants, meaning changes in C cannot produce an ascent in E. Language & Clock (L_codex & Π_PCR): Codex-1 is a total, bounded language where every rewrite declares a domain, budget, and effective bound (T_eff). The Permission Control Runtime (Π_PCR) operates with states of DENY, PAUSE, and RUN (where Deny dominates), serving as the sole clock on which any configuration can become an external effect. Thermodynamic Shifts & Structural Implications Primitive Transformation: Replacing dense GEMM with local neighborhood operators under a total language eliminates long-distance data movement in favor of short stencil communication (√2 lattice units). Energy Scale Reduction: Elementary local CMOS transitions on short interconnects dissipate on the order of 10 aJ to 100 fJ, compared to 0.5 pJ to tens of pJ per FLOP for FP16 tensor-core operations with memory traffic. Control Without a Tax: Because authorization lives on the same geometry via a disjoint bus and is evaluated as a meet (unsigned minimum) over a declared domain, supervision does not require a second model inference pass. What is Proved vs. Open (Track E) Proved (Structural Safety): Structural safety results (such as finite body bounds, deny-dominance, non-autonomous recovery, and the separation of cognitive and authorization registers) hold independently on ordinary binary CMOS using a two-bit encoding per site; a native quaternary device (Quadzistor™) is an optional implementation rather than a prerequisite. Open Measurement Obligations (Track E): The paper explicitly notes that no numerical equivalence between one lattice sweep and one transformer token has been established yet. Order-of-magnitude performance claims or representation capacities remain open measurement obligations until empirical mapping of Codex-1 terms to field regions is completed. Pattern > Noise Hardware > Hope Fail-safe is not a feature. It is our duty.

items.title: Thermal annealing-induced charge storage enhancement in WO3/β-Ga2O3 nanowire heterostructures for MOS capacitive memory
items.abstract: This paper examines non-volatile metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) capacitive memory based on WO3/β-Ga2O3 heterostructure nanowire arrays. The WO3/β-Ga2O3 vertical oriented axial heterostructure nanowires (VAHNWs) were synthesized using glancing angle deposition (GLAD) technique installed in an RF sputtering system. The fabricated VAHNWs were also subjected to air annealing at 600 ˚C for 1 hour. The interface trap density (D_it) decreased from 1.7×10^10 〖eV〗^(-1) 〖cm〗^(-2) (as-deposited) to 1×10^10 〖eV〗^(-1) 〖cm〗^(-2)(annealed) which is consistent with a reduction in electrically active interface states. The MOS capacitor exhibited a significant memory window of approximately 5.35 V at ± 8 V and stable endurance over 2000 programming/erasing cycles. Moreover, a charge retention duration as long as 3.5×10^(4 ) s was observed after annealing. These enhanced parameters can be ascribed to the annealing-induced modification of electrically active defects together with improved interface quality. The results demonstrated the thermally annealed WO3/β-Ga2O3 VAHNWs as a promising candidate for future non-volatile memory technologies..

items.title: Thermal Budgets of AI Accelerators from First Principles: The Thermodynamic Floor, Present Practice, and the Cost of Moving Data
items.abstract: A first-principles thermal budget for AI accelerators. The Landauer erasure floor at 300 K is compared with the energy per operation of a current flagship accelerator at vendor peak throughput and thermal design power (a gap of about eight orders of magnitude), totalled over a published frontier training run of 3.8e25 operations with its heat-rejection requirement, and decomposed with published per-access energies showing that data movement, not arithmetic, dominates. All numbers are produced by the deposited computation script from published constants and specifications. Model calculations: simulated, not measured.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Thermodynamics of Copying Information: Accuracy, Not Erasure, Sets the Price
items.abstract: Copying a bit, unlike erasing it, has no Landauer floor: copying a known bit onto a blank target is logically reversible, and the minimum copy energy is set by accuracy. In an antipodal discrimination model against Gaussian thermal noise the minimum is 1.31e-19 J per bit at an error probability of 1e-15 at 300 K. DNA replication copies at 8.30e-20 J per bit with a final error rate of 1e-10 per base (2.00004 ATP equivalents per base, including proofreading and mismatch-repair costs), within a factor of 1.92 of the accuracy floor per copied symbol. Silicon copying costs 4.50e-11 J per bit (DRAM to DRAM with SECDED error correction), 2.17e-10 J per bit (solid-state drive to drive) and 8.52e-9 J per bit (hard disk to hard disk), that is 3.45e8 to 7.03e10 times the floor, because a silicon bit is a macroscopic object. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its output (results.json).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Iwakuni Base Resilience Protocol: Engineering Physical, Neural, and Economic Buffers for 300-Year Autonomous Civilizational Units (邦題:岩国ベース・レジリエンス・プロトコル:300年を見据えた「余白」の設計論 — 不揮発知能・熱力学的自律性・自動経済防衛の統合実装)
items.abstract: Abstract (English): Modern lean-efficiency engineering lacks structural buffers against non-linear climatic extremes—spanning both severe thermal waves exceeding 40°C and sudden sub-zero cold snaps. Triggered by empirical motor burnout failures in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi, Japan, this monograph establishes the Iwakuni Base Resilience Protocol (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24094981), a comprehensive blueprint for a 300-year autonomous civilizational unit maintained at a net operational expenditure (OpEx) under 2,000 JPY/month. The architecture integrates four foundational pillars: (1) Non-Volatile Edge Intelligence, deploying Renesas RA8D1 (Cortex-M85) MCUs with embedded STT-MRAM Processing-in-Memory (PIM) and Everspin xSPI MRAM black-box loggers executing 10 kHz TinyML anomaly prediction (Motor-Guard) immune to thermal charge leakage up to 125°C and power-loss volatility; (2) Thermodynamic Autonomy (Tri-Generation), cascading a 700 W Solid Oxide Fuel Cell (SOFC, 55% LHV electrical efficiency) with a compact LiBr-water absorption chiller (Yazaki Aroace, 5 USRT), a 1,000 L 2.0G-seismic GRP thermal/water buffer tank (~58 kWh thermal capacity), and IntelliThaw freeze-protection tracing to achieve 85–90% total exergy efficiency; (3) Automated Economic Shielding (Resilience as a Service, RaaS), combining objective index-triggered parametric catastrophe insurance with low-friction P2P mutual aid pools (Frich) backed by cryptographic/MRAM waveform evidence; and (4) A 300-Year Material Shell utilizing deeply carbonized Yakisugi (Shou Sugi Ban) cladding for zero-repainting salt-air and biological durability. 要旨(日本語): 短期的な効率最大化を目的としリソースを極限まで削ぎ落とす現代の設計思想は、40℃超の酷暑と突発的な氷点下の寒波(小氷期リスク)が共存する非線形な気候変動に対して構造的な脆弱性を抱えている。本論文(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24094981) は、山口県岩国市におけるモーター焼損事象を工学的教訓とし、実質月額維持コスト(OpEx)2,000円以下で300年間自律機能する文明の最小単位「岩国ベース・レジリエンス・プロトコル」の包括的実装仕様を提示する。本システムは以下の4層で構成される。(1) 不揮発な神経系(MRAM PIM):125℃の高温下でも電荷リークを起こさず瞬時起動(インスタント・オン)を実現するRenesas RA8D1(内蔵MRAM)およびEverspin xSPI MRAMを採用し、10kHzサンプリングのTinyML予兆検知アルゴリズム「Motor-Guard」をエッジ実装する。(2) 熱力学的自律性(Tri-Gen+物理タンク):発電効率55%のSOFC(エネファーム type S)の高温排熱を小型吸収式冷凍機(矢崎総業 Aroace)で冷熱変換し、水平震度2.0G対応の1,000L GRP製断熱パネルタンク(熱容量約58kWh)とIntelliThaw凍結防止機構を連成させることで総合エクセルギー効率85〜90%を達成する。(3) 経済的セーフティネットの自動化(RaaS):気象・地震指標連動のパラメトリック保険(テールリスク移転)とMRAM波形ログを証跡とするP2P互助(Frich:小口設備損害補填)のリスク・サンドイッチ構造を構築する。(4) 300年外殻:塩害・腐朽菌・紫外線に耐える本焼き「焼杉」外壁によりライフサイクルコストを極小化する。
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Four Sovereignty Invariants: Quantifying Single-Point Chokepoints Across the Global AI Compute Supply Chain
items.abstract: Executive Abstract: Between 2024 and 2026, nation-states and Fortune 500 enterprises committed over $1.4 trillion to 'Sovereign AI' initiatives under the assumption that purchasing domestic GPU clusters or training national foundation models confers strategic autonomy. This working paper demonstrates why that assumption is structurally false. By mapping 12 physical and jurisdictional layers of the global AI compute stack, we show that single-vendor or single-region concentration exceeds 70% to 100% at six non-substitutable bottlenecks—including 100% of High-NA EUV lithography (ASML), 92% of CoWoS advanced wafer packaging (TSMC), 90% of ultra-high-purity crucible quartz (Spruce Pine, USA), and extraterritorial cloud IAM kill-switches. We formalize the Four Sovereignty Invariants from The Sovereign Illusion to provide policymakers and CTOs with a quantitative framework for auditing supply-chain resilience. Companion Volume & Open Dataset: Book (Amazon Kindle / Print): https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HMS4JJ1R (ASIN: B0HMS4JJ1R / Paperback: B0HMX59GSQ / Hardcover: B0HMZRG96T) Open Chokepoint Dataset & Interactive Simulator: https://github.com/digbijoylabs/the-sovereign-illusion Publisher Portal: https://digbijoylabs.com
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Technical Note TN-2026-HBN-02: Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Fabrication and Open-Surface ALD Protocol for h-BN Protective Linings in Ultra-High-Gradient PWFA Capillaries
