items.abstract: This technical note details the Longitudinal Split-Wafer (Clamshell) Architecture and Open-Surface Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) protocol for depositing 50.0 nm hexagonal Boron Nitride (h-BN) protective linings inside high-gradient Plasma Wakefield Accelerator (PWFA) capillary channels. To overcome precursor gas diffusion limits (Knudsen transport bottleneck) in ultra-high aspect ratio micro-channels (up to 2,000,000:1), matching semi-circular micro-grooves are precision-machined onto planar synthetic sapphire blocks. This leaves the surface completely open during deposition, guaranteeing zero precursor depletion and uniform 50.0 nm h-BN atomic layer growth across the entire 1.0-meter channel length prior to optical contact fusion. Key Specifications & Results: - Substrate: High-purity synthetic sapphire (0001 c-plane planar slabs) - Capillary Baseline Length: 1000.0 mm (1.0 meter) - Groove Radius / Post-Bonding Inner Bore: r = 250.0 nm, width w = 500.0 nm (ϕ_ad = 500.0 nm) - Surface Roughness: R_a < 0.5 nm (CMP polished optical standard) - Protective Liner Thickness: t_hbn = 50.0 nm ± 1.2 nm - Assembly Method: Direct solid-state thermal fusion at 1100°C in UHV after cleanroom optical contact alignment Includes full fabrication process steps, metrology requirements, and prototype non-recurring engineering (NRE) cost estimates.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Structural and electronic properties of (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ phases from first principles
items.abstract: (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ material system is promising for ferroelectric devices, owing to their compatibility with the existing electronics manufacturing processes. Technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations can be used for the device design and optimization, but the predictive power of TCAD device simulations depends on the quality of the material parameters. These are still surprisingly poorly understood, also for the metastable ferroelectric phase, largely owing to the difficulties in synthesizing phase-pure samples. Here, we carry out high-quality first-principles calculations to extract reliable lattice parameters, dielectric constants, and band gaps for six of the most common phases of HfO$_2$, Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$, and ZrO$_2$. We compare results from GGA, meta-GGA, and hybrid functionals to shed light on the sensitivity of the results on the level of theory and to connect the results to earlier literature. In the case of band structures, we also consider $GW$ corrections as well as the effects of temperature-induced band gap renormalization and excitonic effects. Finally, we use these results in TCAD simulations for (Hf,Zr)O$_2$ FeCAP to demonstrate the effect that non-ferroelectric interlayers could have on the hysteresis curves and band diagrams.

items.title: Structural Analysis of Sparse Model Architectures: Hidden Gaps, Recurring Patterns, and Five Open Paradigm Candidates for Next-Generation LLMs
items.abstract: Version 5.1 corrects: the omission of prior work on adaptive computation (Adaptive Computation Time, Universal Transformers, Mixture-of-Depths, Mixture-of-Recursions, early exit), dynamic and zero-computation expert routing, adaptively sparse attention, neural architecture search, learned addressing for N-gram memory (Lngram), and writable or editable conditional memory (Memorizing Transformers, User as Engram, Writability and the Pathway, EngramEdit). A related-work section is added. Per-token skipping, adaptive depth, learned numbers of active experts and learned or searched architecture are established, and writes into hash-addressed Engram rows have been demonstrated when the fact and its trigger are supplied from outside, mainly by gradient optimization and with precomputed overrides applied per request at serving time; gradient-free variants have been tried with limited success. The gap and novelty statements of Gaps 1, 2, 4 and 5, Candidates 1–5 and the corresponding open questions are narrowed accordingly to what remains open: writes into hash-addressed tables that the model itself triggers from its hidden state during generation, with collision handling in a shared table, and an effective gradient-free write; a per-token choice between memory lookup and computation; an allocation search that includes the conditional-memory axis; and learned memory-specific structural decisions. “Open” in the title refers to this restricted sense. One table entry that attributed shared experts to the original Mixture-of-Experts layer, and two author lists in the bibliography, are corrected. The previous version is 10.5281/zenodo.19312203; this version supersedes it. We present a structural analysis of sparse model architectures, identifying five gaps in the current paradigm, documenting recurring meta-patterns across major AI breakthroughs, and proposing five candidate architectures for the next paradigm shift. This version integrates discussion of Titans and UMoE as related work. This paper presents no experimental results; it presents a structural argument for where to look next. Files. structural_analysis_v5.1.pdf (paper), structural_analysis_v5.1.tex (LaTeX source).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: SlipStream: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference demands ever more memory capacity for larger models and batch sizes. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) replaces the DRAM dies of HBM with NAND flash and provides up to 16x the capacity at comparable read bandwidth. However, HBF can incur a read latency of nearly 20$\mu$s, 20x that of HBM, so on-demand HBF accesses slow inference by up to 12.8x. Conventional cache-line prefetchers require 20x more in-flight tracking state to cover this latency. Tensor-streaming designs, such as H3, follow virtual-address order as opposed to kernel-demand order, and therefore need hundreds of megabytes of buffering. We propose SlipStream, a software-hardware co-designed prefetcher that turns prefetching into a demand-paced producer-consumer pipeline. In software, SlipStream profiles the repeatable weight-page demand order of data-independent LLM kernels and inserts a staging warp that replays this order with non-blocking STAGE instructions. In hardware, the staging warp acts as the producer and the work warps as consumers. Our key insight is to retire each STAGE tracking entry only when demand first accesses the page, as opposed to when the page returns from HBF. Demand thus paces staging and bounds how far staging leads consumption. SlipStream tracks 4 KB pages instead of cache lines and allocates buffer slots only when pages return, which decouples the buffer size from outstanding traffic. Across seven dense models spanning 16-800 GB, SlipStream with a 40 MB staging buffer achieves 92.4% of the performance of an ideal HBF with HBM-like latency. H3 achieves only 43.1%, even with a 320 MB buffer. The buffer sizing of SlipStream is independent of HBF latency and workload. SlipStream with 16 MB buffer, 20x smaller than that of H3, performs within 4% of SlipStream-40MB. SlipStream also supports Mixture-of-Experts models and reaches 91.2% of ideal performance (40 MB buffer).

items.title: Situating virtue ethics and consequentialism in European AI guidelines for journalism
items.abstract: The rapid development of AI in journalism, particularly following the emergence of generative AI, has intensified the need for ethical guidance, prompting news organisations and self-regulatory bodies to produce a growing body of guidelines and recommendations.Drawing on a moral pluralist perspective, this paper investigates how virtue ethics and consequentialist reasoning interact with duty-based approaches across a corpus of 65 texts published by European newsrooms, professional organisations and self-regulatory actors.The analysis examines how virtues such as prudence, authenticity and vigilance, alongside outcome-oriented considerations such as harm prevention, public trust and societal impact, are operationalised in practice.The findings show that ethical reasoning in AImediated journalism is frequently hybrid and context-dependent: duties establish normative boundaries, while virtues and consequences guide contextualised judgement and decision-making.These results suggest that the ethical challenges posed by AI cannot be adequately addressed without a pluralist approach integrating rules, consequences and professional judgement, highlighting how guidelines transform ethical journalism into an interpretive structure in which these elements become operational mechanisms.

items.title: Secure AI Agent Infrastructure
items.abstract: Reproducible research prototypes addressing one question: can an autonomous agent be trusted with a security decision, and would you know if it could not? Contains an agent verification harness that scores whether each claim in an LLM's output is supported by the documents it retrieved, a per-class smart-contract vulnerability benchmark with audited negative controls, and an LLM audit agent. Results files record measured runs against SHA-256-pinned sources; metrics that the evidence does not support are withheld with a machine-readable reason rather than reported.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Secondary switching ratio: an electrical probe of polarization switching evolution in HZO/ZrO2 hybrid bilayers
items.abstract: The ferroelectric-to-antiferroelectric (FE–AFE) crossover in HfO 2 -based capacitors produces multi-step switching responses that cannot be fully described by conventional hysteresis parameters. Here, we introduce the secondary switching ratio, R sec , extracted from transient switching currents, to electrically probe the FE–AFE switching character and its evolution in HZO/ZrO 2 hybrid bilayer capacitors, in which a ferroelectric HZO layer and an antiferroelectric ZrO 2 layer are combined with systematically varied composition and thickness ratios. Importantly, R sec is not interpreted as an absolute orthorhombic/tetragonal phase fraction, but as a functional measure of the relative secondary-switching contribution associated with antiferroelectric-like recovery under a defined pulse protocol. Across the hybrid stack series, R sec evolves systematically from the FE-dominant to the AFE-dominant limit, is qualitatively corroborated by GIXRD signatures, and captures hold-time-, temperature-, cycling-, bias-, and bilayer thickness-ratio-dependent changes in the switching response. Hold-time and delay-time measurements from 83 K to 353 K reveal history-dependent secondary-switching relaxation with a finite low-temperature component, supporting a field-driven contribution with additional thermal assistance at higher temperatures. Temperature-dependent measurements and XPS depth profiling indicate that the wake-up evolution is mainly associated with field-driven switching-state reconfiguration, while oxygen-vacancy redistribution acts as a secondary contributor in the present hybrid bilayer system. This framework establishes R sec as a practical electrical probe for tracking FE–AFE switching evolution in hafnia-based hybrid bilayer capacitors.

items.title: Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Logic Circuits Driven by Ion‐Mediated Organic Electrochemical Diodes
items.abstract: The rapid growth of data‐intensive computing has exposed the physical limitations of conventional hardware architectures. While accumulative multistate memory devices offer low‐power alternatives, incorporating multistate reconfigurability into switching devices enables fully integrated, multifunctional neuromorphic operations across both logic and memory. Herein, we report programmable multistate logic circuits based on organic neuromorphic devices. By leveraging the intrinsic learning capability of organic electrochemical diodes (OECDs), multiple logic functions are realized within a single diode‐resistor configuration. The channel conductance of each OECD is dynamically modulated by the polarity and frequency of the input voltage, enabling seamless reconfiguration to execute custom logic operations (e.g., AND/OR and XOR/unknown). Furthermore, we demonstrate a functional half‐adder by cascading two multistate logic circuits as a proof‐of‐concept neuromorphic computing architecture. These results establish a promising pathway toward on‐chip, learning‐based digital circuitry with potential relevance to future neuromorphic computing applications.

items.title: Q-Planner: A Harness System for Quantum Chemistry Agents
items.abstract: Abstract LLM-based agents for computational chemistry commonly place the model inside an accumulating execution loop, causing context growth proportional to workflow length, unpredictable token costs, and degraded plan reliability at scale. We present a chemistry computation harness that confines LLM invocations to three semantically bounded stages─compound identification, planning, and reporting─while delegating all tool dispatch, parallel scheduling, arithmetic derivation, and artifact routing to a deterministic LangGraph executor that consumes zero LLM tokens during execution; a library of domain skill modules injects specialist quantum chemistry protocols into the planner context at planning time without enlarging the execution context. Across five representative quantum chemistry workflows, the planning, calculator, and reporting calls averaged 9700–25,300 tokens per run, with zero execution-stage tokens in every case─more than 93% fewer tokens (before caching) than loop-based multiagent systems─and, on a high-throughput single-point-energy scaling benchmark, a full-scheme plan representation sustained 100% plan-structural correctness across all 30 runs from N = 10 to 100 compounds of one workflow type, generating a 200-node graph of 100 independent single-point jobs from a single planning call. On the workloads tested, harness design made quantum chemistry automation more robust and its cost more predictable; the model ablation shows that model capability still matters.

items.title: Power Optimized High Speed Sense Amplifier for 6T SRAM
items.abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) is used in a wide range of applications in modern VLSI like processors, microcontrollers, embedded systems and SoC due to its High Speed data access and reliable operation. A standard 6T SRAM cell is composed by 6 MOS transistors, two cross coupled inverters and two access transistors. While reading data there is a small voltage difference between complementary Bit Lines (BL and BL̅) which needs to be correctly sensed using a Sense Amplifier. Problems faced by traditional sense amplifiers can include increased levels of power consumption, slower sensing speeds and reduced reliabilities especially during low voltages. This project proposes a Power Optimized High Speed Sense Amplifier for 6T SRAM. The system uses a 6T SRAM Cell, Bit Line Precharging Circuit and Optimised Sense Amplifier. LTspice was used to create the design. The circuit was analysed by using transient waveforms of voltage and currents. Key parameters were looked at such as power consumption, speed and Read Delay. This should give us a fast data sensing circuit with reduced power consumption and reliable reading. The design would be useful for Low Power VLSI memory applications.
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines
items.abstract: DeepSeek-V4.1's 203 GB of Engram n-gram tables sit in host DRAM today, taking 190 of the 223 GiB a 4-GPU serving process uses. Row indices depend only on input tokens, so reads can start with each step and overlap earlier layers. V4.1's two Engram layers have windows that differ by 30x (0.3 vs. 9.3 ms). We show that this deadline, together with session reuse and contention on a shared device, decides which tier each table can use and which layers need cache, and we give a model that predicts the resulting slowdown from measured read times. Agent and chat traffic reuse rows within sessions, and static hot sets transfer poorly. We build SlackTier, a table tier for SGLang that issues all lookups at step start. It reads the short-window layer first and splits a small GPU row cache across layers. The path runs inside the decode CUDA graph and is bit-exact with the original gather. Layer 14's table can go to NVMe uncached with no measurable decode cost. With both tables on four NVMe disks, mean time per output token on agent and chat replays rises at most 1.4% over unmodified SGLang, and host memory falls from 212 to 34 GiB. Both tables need no cache when read over RDMA (remote direct memory access) from another node's memory; one copy serves two instances. On a KV-constrained agent workload, using the freed memory as host KV cache at the same memory budget raises median throughput by 36% and cuts median p90 time to first token from 38 to 24 s.

items.title: Pico-X: a 24.9 nanowatt microcontroller for long-duration autonomous operation in flexible landing-pad sensor networks
items.abstract: Flexible landing-pad sensor networks require local intelligence that can remain dormant for long periods yet respond rapidly to sparse mechanical events. General-purpose microcontrollers incur substantial retained-state and control overhead under such workloads, whereas hardwired controllers sacrifice programmability. Here we present Pico-X, a state-minimized eight-bit programmable processor designed for patch-level wake-up, sensing, event classification and reporting. A compact multi-cycle architecture, unified retentive memory and workload-constrained instruction framework reduce retained state and standby leakage. Fabricated in a 28-nanometre fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process, Pico-X consumes 728.2 nanowatts during active operation at 25 kilohertz and 24.9 nanowatts in state-retentive deep sleep without body bias, while preserving deterministic state recovery after wake-up. We further integrate Pico-X into a 4 × 4 flexible landing-pad demonstrator that records 12,842 events and achieves class-wise detection rates (recall) of 96.3% for occupancy, 92.1% for load imbalance, and 94.6% for deformation. Mean event-to-report latency is 38 milliseconds, packet delivery reaches 99.12%, and operation remains stable for more than 72 hours. These results establish a low-overhead programmable architecture for distributed, long-duration sensing. Researchers present Pico-X, a programmable microcontroller designed for sparse event-driven sensing. Operating at nanowatt power levels, it enables long-duration autonomous monitoring and reliable event detection in distributed flexible sensor networks.

items.title: Physics-Aware Co-training to Overcome Device Non-idealities in Canted SOT-MTJ Arrays for In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: Abstract The physical non-idealities inherent in emerging spintronic devices, such as device-to-device variations, stochastic switching, and nonlinear conductance responses, pose fundamental challenges for their deployment in in-memory computing architectures. Here, we investigate the integration of canted spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs) for deep learning applications and propose a hardware-aware deep learning framework that embeds into the training process experimentally extracted device characteristics, which are faithfully resolved via a dedicated three-terminal SOT testing scheme that effectively suppresses spin-transfer torque, halves the switching threshold voltage, and eliminates parasitic drifts to minimize measurement-induced fluctuations and reveal intrinsic 1010-cycle endurance, thereby directly facilitating robust hardware–software co-optimization. By tuning a normalized conductance factor gnorm, we achieve a median classification accuracy of 88.9% on the Wine dataset using a 13 × 13 SOT-MTJ array, surpassing baseline software-to-hardware weight mapping. Incorporating hardware-aware co-training further elevates the median accuracy to 94.4%, demonstrating substantial robustness against device imperfections. Overall, our results highlight that explicitly modeling device variability at both the physics and algorithm levels can enable spintronic hardware based on SOT-MTJ arrays to function as compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic platforms, allowing device stochasticity to be incorporated as a learnable constraint, ultimately recovering hardware inference accuracy to within a few percentage points of the ideal software baseline.

items.title: Performance Prediction Techniques for Deep Learning Systems: A Survey
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning models has led to their widespread application across various domains; however, this has resulted in a significant increase in both hardware and software costs, necessitating optimizations for resource efficiency. To address this issue, performance prediction techniques evaluate the performance impact of corresponding optimizations on deep learning systems to maximize performance gains. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of performance prediction techniques for deep learning systems, categorizing them into allocation, cluster, and accelerator levels based on the system level at which their corresponding optimizations are situated, ranging from high to low. Allocation-level techniques primarily construct the relationships between resource configurations and their performance, cluster-level techniques model the optimizations within deep learning frameworks at given configurations, while accelerator-level techniques assess the efficiency of specific hardware. We point out that prediction techniques at different levels exhibit a hierarchical relationship rather than operating in isolation. High-level prediction techniques can incorporate the results from low-level techniques into their performance models to accommodate more low-level optimizations and improve their prediction accuracy. However, this will slow down the construction and execution speed of performance models, requiring trade-offs for specific use cases. Finally, we discuss future challenges and research directions in performance prediction techniques for deep learning systems.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization

items.title: PILLARS OF SILICON: FROM SAND PHYSICS TO ALGORITHMIC CONSCIOUSNESS A Comprehensive Journey Through Semiconductor Physics, Computer Architecture, Computational Theory, Artificial Intelligence, and the Future of Computing
items.abstract: PILLARS OF SILICON: FROM SAND PHYSICS TO ALGORITHMIC CONSCIOUSNESS Summary This comprehensive work traces humanity's greatest material transformation: how inert silicon sand becomes the foundation of algorithmic consciousness. Spanning eighteen chapters across six major parts, the book constructs a unified narrative connecting quantum mechanical properties of silicon atoms to the emergence of artificial intelligence and post-silicon computing paradigms. Part One explores semiconductor physics, from silicon crystal lattices and band theory to MOSFET transistors and EUV lithography manufacturing. Part Two examines computational structures, progressing from Boolean algebra through computer architecture to parallelism and hardware optimization. Part Three ascends to computational theory, covering Turing machines, algorithmic complexity, and the P versus NP problem. Part Four delves into artificial intelligence, from machine learning foundations through transformer architectures and reinforcement learning. Part Five surveys future paradigms including quantum computing, neuromorphic systems, and brain-computer interfaces. Part Six explores post-silicon frontiers and ultimate boundaries. The revised edition introduces critical additions: the hard problem of consciousness and Integrated Information Theory, hardware security vulnerabilities (Spectre, Meltdown), the thermodynamic footprint of modern computing, and explicit connecting threads maintaining narrative unity throughout. Licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0 for academic use with commercial licensing reserved, this work provides foundational understanding for navigating computing's past, present, and future.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Non‐Invasive Optical Inspection of Thermally Driven Interface State Evolution at Buried Metal–MoS 2 Contacts
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Van der Waals (vdW) metal contacts to two‐dimensional semiconductors promise efficient carrier extraction alongside long photocarrier lifetimes, yet how the buried interface evolves under back‐end‐of‐line thermal budgets remains difficult to track. Here, annealing‐dependent transient reflection spectroscopy is established as a device‐free optical readout of interface state evolution for transferred vdW Au, graphene‐buffered Au, and deposited semimetal Sb contacts on multilayer MoS 2 up to 400°C, correlated with cross‐sectional electron microscopy, photoelectron spectroscopy, and first‐principles calculations. As the Au–S separation contracts from 3.47 Å to 2.16 Å (into the bonding range) two distinct optical signatures emerge: reduction of the early‐time excitonic response from the first annealing step, consistent with strengthening extraction, and a picosecond capture channel that appears at 200°C, following thermally activated chemisorption whose hybridization‐induced gap states straddle the pinned Fermi level. At matched separation, the Sb interface forms comparable gap states that lie occupied below its Fermi level, explaining its nearly invariant response, whereas graphene delays the transformation by holding the metal away from the semiconductor. These results frame contact selection as a navigable trade‐off between carrier extraction and photocarrier lifetime and identify interlayer engineering and semimetal contacts as complementary routes to thermally robust 2D interfaces.

items.title: No Request Left Behind: Tackling Heterogeneity in Long-Context LLM Inference with Medha
items.abstract: Deploying million-token Large Language Models (LLMs) is challenging because production workloads are highly heterogeneous, mixing short queries and long documents. This heterogeneity, combined with the quadratic complexity of attention, creates severe convoy effects where long-running requests stall short, interactive ones, degrading system responsiveness. We present Medha, a serving system that eliminates these convoys by introducing fine-grained, preemptive scheduling to LLM inference. Medha makes preemption practical with a co-designed set of mechanisms – including Adaptive Chunking and Stream Pipeline Parallelism – that overcome the perceived inefficiencies and scaling challenges of chunking. Additionally, we present a new parallelism strategy KV-Cache Parallelism to reduce the decode latency and afford interactivity despite very long context. These mechanisms are orchestrated by a Length-Aware Relative Slack (LARS) scheduler, a deadline- and heterogeneity-aware scheduling policy that prevents both the convoy effect and the starvation that plagues simpler policies. Under a heterogeneous workload, Medha improves throughput by 5.7 × while reducing median and 90th-percentile latency by 30 × and 174 ×, respectively, compared to state-of-the-art non-preemptive systems.

items.title: Neuromorphic Chips
items.abstract: Neuromorphic Chips by Claude
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: MosaicKV: SLO-Aware KV-Cache Virtualization for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving in the Cloud
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving has become a first-class cloud workload. The dominant cost driver is no longer compute alone. The key-value (KV) cache consumes tens of gigabytes per replica. It forces providers to either over-provision GPU memory or reject long-context requests. Existing high-throughput engines largely optimize within a single server. They assume KV stays resident in GPU HBM. Under multi-tenancy, HBM is routinely oversubscribed. Naive offloading (e.g., CUDA Unified Memory paging) then creates severe p99 TTFT spikes. These spikes break service-level objectives (SLOs). This paper presents MosaicKV, a KV-cache virtualization layer for multi-tenant LLM inference on shared GPU servers. MosaicKV exposes KV as a schedulable and migratable resource. It jointly optimizes GPU-memory partitioning across tenants. It decides which KV pages stay on HBM versus spill to host DRAM. It also times prefetch and micro-batching to hide PCIe DMA transfer latency. The key insight is that decoding has a predictable layer-by-layer access pattern. By co-designing page layout with a slack-aware scheduler, MosaicKV turns KV offload from reactive paging into a planned pipeline. On an 8-GPU server (8 × H100 SXM 80 GB) serving Llama-3.1-70B, Qwen2.5-32B, and Mixtral-8x7B under a 64-tenant mixed workload, MosaicKV improves goodput-under-SLO by 1.93–2.31 × under the same SLO contract (p99 TTFT ≤ 400 ms for interactive tenants; p99 completion ≤ 2 s for best-effort tenants) while reducing peak HBM KV footprint by 38%. Under flash-crowd bursts, MosaicKV keeps interactive-tenant p99 TTFT at 378–386 ms (within SLO). Unified Memory spikes to 1,055 ms (∼ 2.6 × SLO). MosaicKV achieves these gains without model changes. Runtime overhead remains modest (2.9–6.2%). This enables operators to safely run long-context and bursty tenants on shared GPU fleets.

items.title: Memory as a Temporal Resource: Lifetime Contracts for Multi-Retention Systems
items.abstract: Computers move and rewrite data whose useful lifetimes range from inner-loop iterations to years, yet memory systems usually hide retention as a fixed physical property. We argue that required lifetime should become a first-class resource across algorithms, programming systems, controllers, and devices. Building on prior lifetime-aware placement, we propose an event-based validity contract that links application completion events to retention-class selection and renewal of protection. Applications would be enabled to express semantic contracts such as ``until this tile completes'' and the system will map data to homogeneous arrays engineered for ephemeral, epoch, or durable retention and preserve correctness through margins, ECC, refresh, migration, or recomputation. We present a trace-based simulator and FPGA prototype that exercises class migration.

items.title: Memory Materials on One Budget: The Physics of Retention Media Compared
items.abstract: Six retention media (DRAM, NAND flash, magnetic disk and tape, phase-change memory, FeRAM, and MRAM) are compared on a single physical budget: retention mechanism, physical failure channel, characteristic energy barrier from the literature, retention time at 300 K computed by anchored Arrhenius scaling, and holding energy per bit-year computed from published device figures. DRAM is the only medium with second-scale retention and a large continuous holding cost (1.38e-4 J per bit-year); every nonvolatile medium retains unpowered at zero holding energy, with computed 300 K retention from 1.52 years (end-of-life NAND flash) to 9.88e7 years (phase-change memory). Magnetic tape on a shelf is cheapest per bit-year at scale; phase-change memory is most stable per joule. Model calculations are simulated, not measured. Computations and drafting were performed with Dave, an AI research system.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Measurement Is Not Free: The Energy Ledger of a Measure-Record-Erase Cycle at the Thermodynamic Floor and in Practice
items.abstract: The standard Szilard-Bennett accounting holds that measurement can in principle be free and that the unavoidable cost of an information cycle sits in erasing the record, at the Landauer floor k_B T ln 2 per bit. This paper tests that accounting for a stated measurement chain. The minimum energy to acquire one bit at error probability p_e against thermal noise is derived for a thermal-noise-limited sampler as E = 2 k_B T [Q^-1(p_e)]^2; at p_e = 1e-6 and 300 K this is 1.87e-19 J per bit, 65.20 times the Landauer floor, and acquisition exceeds erasure at the floor for every error probability below 0.2780. A Texas Instruments ADS1115 converter (16-bit, 860 SPS, 150 microA, datasheet SBAS444E) spends 3.60e-8 J per measured bit in practice. With published DRAM and NAND per-bit energies, the full measure-record-erase cycle costs 1.90e-19 J at the floor (98.49% acquisition) and 3.60e-8 J in practice with a volatile record (99.89% acquisition). The standard claim fails in the stated regime, at the floor and in practice. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Location-Controlled Ge Grain Growth via Nanoscale Cooling-Hole-Assi-sted Laser Crystallization for Low-Thermal-Budget Monolithic 3D Integration
items.abstract: Abstract Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) integration requires high-performance channel materials processed under strict thermal budgets (<400 °C). While germanium (Ge) is a promising candidate, the stochastic nature of grain boundaries (GBs) in conventionally crystallized films severely degrades carrier transport and device uniformity. In this work, we demonstrate a deterministic location-controlled grain (LCG) growth technique for Ge thin films utilizing a nanoscale “cooling hole” architecture combined with green nanosecond laser crystallization (GNSLC). Transient thermal simulations and microstructural analyses reveal that the nanoscale cooling holes act as localized thermal sinks, inducing lateral crystallization while maintaining the underlying substrate temperature below 240 °C. Furthermore, the incorporation of a silicon nitride (SiNx) capping layer modulates thermal dissipation and exerts stress-mediated growth, yielding highly ordered, single-crystal-like Ge domains up to 1.2 μm with GBs precisely confined between the nanoscale cooling holes. Back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible FinFETs fabricated within these deterministic grains exhibit superior electrical characteristics and significantly tightened performance distributions. Notably, the standard deviation of the subthreshold swing (SS) is reduced by more than 50% compared to conventional polycrystalline devices. By effectively eliminating random GB scattering from the active channel, this LCG platform significantly suppresses device-to-device variability. Ultimately, it provides a robust nanoscale material engineering solution for advanced heterogeneous M3D integration.

items.title: LLM Analysis of 150+ Years of German Parliamentary Debates on Migration Reveals a Shift from Post-War Solidarity to Anti-Solidarity in the Last Decade
items.abstract: Abstract Migration has been a core topic in German political debate, from postwar expellee displacement to labor migration and recent refugee movements. Large-scale analysis of such political discourse has traditionally required extensive manual annotation, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable alternative. Using a theory-driven annotation scheme, we examine how well LLMs annotate subtypes of solidarity and anti-solidarity in German parliamentary debates and whether the resulting labels support valid downstream inference. We first evaluate multiple LLMs across model size, prompting strategies, fine-tuning, historical versus contemporary data, and systematic errors. The strongest models, especially GPT-5 and gpt-oss-120B, achieve macro-F1 scores comparable to human agreement, although their systematic errors can bias downstream results. We therefore combine soft-label model outputs with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL) to reduce bias in long-term trend estimates. Beyond the methodological evaluation, we interpret the resulting annotations from a social-scientific perspective across the Reichstag (1867–1933), West German Bundestag (1949–1990) and Re-Unified German Bundestag (1990–2025) corpus to trace trends in solidarity and anti-solidarity toward migrants, with detailed analysis of postwar Germany (1949–1957) and contemporary Germany (2009–2025). We find relatively high levels of solidarity in the postwar period, especially in group-based and compassionate forms, and a marked rise in anti-solidarity since 2015. We argue that LLMs can support large-scale social-scientific text analysis, but their outputs require rigorous validation and, where systematic errors are present, statistical correction.

items.title: LHEMO: LLM-based heuristic evolution for multi-objective sensor-weapon-target assignment
items.abstract: The multi-objective sensor–weapon–target assignment (SWTA) problem requires the coordinated allocation of heterogeneous sensing and action resources under conflicting objectives such as mission effectiveness, resource consumption, and response time. Existing SWTA solvers, including classical multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and recent large language model (LLM)-based automated heuristic design (AHD) methods, either rely heavily on hand-crafted search components or transfer poorly to SWTA because of its heterogeneous entities, strict feasibility requirements, and Pareto-oriented feedback. To address these challenges, we propose LHEMO, an LLM-based heuristic evolution framework for multi-objective SWTA. LHEMO adopts a bi-level architecture: an outer level evolves executable heuristic programs through LLM-guided operators, and an inner multi-objective solver evaluates each candidate. Two reconstruction operators expand exploration through line- and module-level code regeneration, a validation-and-repair mechanism recovers invalid candidates, a cross-generation reflection mechanism reuses evolutionary experience, and a seeded initialization anchors early-stage search. A Pareto-oriented fitness built on per-instance normalized hypervolume and a feasibility penalty guides the evolution toward high-quality trade-off solutions. Experiments on a benchmark ranging from 8 to 320 targets show that LHEMO attains the best hypervolume among nine compared methods on every instance with at least 64 targets and improves upon the strongest hand-crafted baseline by up to 178.9%. Heuristics evolved on a single 12-target training instance retain about 85% of this performance on instances up to 26.7 times larger. These results establish LLM-driven heuristic evolution as a practical paradigm for constraint-intensive multi-objective resource allocation.

items.title: Inter-Site Fluctuation Mechanics in the ADC Single-Trap Random Telegraph Signal (RTS) Regime: Closed-Form Characteristic Functions and Non-Gaussian Quantization Dynamics
items.abstract: In our foundational treatment of direct-sampling Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) and software-defined radio (SDR) front-ends, we established the macroscopic Gaussian ensemble limit where large populations of interfacial traps validate the Central Limit Theorem and Hooge-like resistance flicker. However, in cryogenic quantum-readout ADCs operating at millikelvin temperatures and deeply scaled nanoscale FinFET/GAAFET sampling switches, defect freeze-out and constrained active gate areas frequently reduce the active trap population to the few-trap or single-trap limit. In this work, we abandon the Law of Large Numbers (LLN) and formulate a rigorous first-principles theoretical framework for the Single-Trap Random Telegraph Signal (RTS) regime. Modeling the individual interfacial trap as a continuous-time two-state Markov jump process, we derive exact closed-form marginal and two-time joint characteristic functions. We prove that macroscopic Gaussian exponential damping is replaced by exact trigonometric interference, leading to periodic spur nulling, asymmetric phase rotation, and discrete Lorentzian harmonic sideband skirts. Finally, we establish the composite master characteristic function bridging ensemble Gaussian flicker with discrete non-Gaussian RTS dynamics.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Impact of a Process-Induced Interfacial Layer on Ferroelectric Switching and Reliability in AlScN/β-Ga₂O₃ MFS Capacitors
items.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate AlScN-based metal-ferroelectric-semiconductor capacitors directly integrated on a heteroepitaxial β-Ga2O3. Structural analysis reveals the presence of a process-induced amorphous intermixed layer at the AlScN/β-Ga2O3 interface. The fabricated devices exhibit ferroelectric switching behavior, characterized by counterclockwise hysteretic current-voltage loops with an on/off current ratio of >102, which is limited by the intermixed interfacial layer. Piezo-response force microscopy measurements confirm the intrinsic polarization switching capability through phase reversal and butterfly-shaped amplitude loops. Furthermore, positive-up-negative-down measurements indicate polarization switching while revealing a switching current asymmetry. We identify that this asymmetry originates from the internal electric field and charge trapping associated with the interfacial defect layer. This interfacial instability primarily affects the device performance observed during retention (103 s) and endurance (5×103 cycles) tests, suggesting significance of interface engineering for stable ferroelectric operation in AlScN/β-Ga2O3 devices.

items.title: Hyperdimensional Photonic AI Computing
items.abstract: We discuss our work on hyperdimensional photonic AI accelerators, that leverage time-space- and wavelength-division multiplexing towards enhancing compute power and energy efficiency. We benchmark their performance against state-of-the-art GPUs, demonstrating superior throughput and low-energy operation
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Holding a Qubit: The Retention Price of Quantum Memory
items.abstract: Classical retention costs almost nothing: a bit in DRAM costs 1.57e-8 J per bit-hour in self-refresh, a bit in flash at most 5.70e-14 J per bit-hour as an amortised rewrite bound, and a bit on tape on a shelf costs nothing. This paper prices the quantum analogue: holding one logical qubit, with no computation performed on it, below a cumulative failure probability of 1% for one hour, one day, and one year. Because bare qubits survive only microseconds (superconducting) to minutes (trapped ion), retention requires continuous surface-code error correction at a 100% refresh duty cycle, with code distance growing as the interval lengthens. Holding one logical qubit takes 15,741 W, 17,569 W, and 20,784 W continuously on the superconducting platform (physical error rate 1e-3, 1 microsecond cycles, distances 27/31/37, 10 kW fixed cryostat plant included) and 2,721 W, 3,057 W, and 3,681 W on the trapped-ion platform (1 ms cycles, distances 19/23/29). The energy per logical-qubit-hour exceeds the classical DRAM bit-hour by a factor of 6.23e14 to 4.76e15, the flash bit-hour by about 1e21, and is unbounded against tape on a shelf at zero holding cost. Quantum memory with present architectures is not a storage medium but a continuous power commitment. Model calculations are labelled SIMULATED, NOT MEASURED. The deposit includes the paper PDF and markdown, the computation script (compute.py) that produces every number in the paper, and its outputs (results.json, results.txt).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Highly Reliable Sub-2-nm Hafnia Ferroelectric Tunnel Junction via All-Atomic Layer Deposition Growth
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.

items.title: HARDWARE INTEGRATION OF NFNS AND SBNS NUMERAL SYSTEMS IN A FAULT-TOLERANT NEUROMORPHIC PROCESSOR ARCHITECTURE
items.abstract: This paper investigates the microarchitectural principles and technological prospects of designing a fundamentally new class of computing devices – a hybrid fault-tolerant neuromorphic processor. The feasibility of deep hardware integration of the New Fibonacci Numeral System (NFNS) and the Scaled Bergman Numeral System (SBNS) on a single semiconductor die is substantiated. It is demonstrated that due to the identical nature of their underlying mathematical principles (representation of weights via fractions, Fibonacci confluent/convoluted rules), both systems can share up to 85–90% of the physical area of the arithmetic logic unit (ALU) and utilize a unified hardware parity filter. A mechanism for dynamic on-the-fly switching of the computational basis within a single clock cycle via a configuration register depending on the specific application task is described. A technological forecast is formulated, according to which the integer NFNS mode ensures noise immunity and error control (bit-flips) in critical discrete environments (aerospace, cryptography), while the SBNS mode, leveraging the Truncation Symmetry Theorem, eliminates the accumulation of rounding errors and optimizes the bit-width of the significant register mantissa, serving as an ideal foundation for neuromorphic AI accelerators.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Graphene/Si Heterojunction Platform with a Multifunctional Atomic Bridging Layer for Photoelectrochemical CO2 Reduction
items.abstract: Abstract The facile integration and stability of Si-based photoelectrode architectures are the remaining challenges in the photoelectrochemical (PEC) conversion of CO2 to fuels. In this work, the single-atomic-layer graphene is used as a functional bridging layer to integrate both Si photocathodes and photoanodes, which enable the direct electrodeposition of metal-based electrocatalysts (Cu, Ag, and In–Sn alloys) and a semiconductor-based catalyst Ni–Fe layered double hydroxide (Ni–Fe LDH) on graphene/Si heterojunction electrodes for PEC CO2 reduction and O2 evolution reactions, respectively. We demonstrate a PEC device with a full-cell configuration consisting of an In–Sn/graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and a Ni–Fe LDH/graphene/Si heterojunction photoanode, exhibiting a reduced photovoltage of ∼1080 mV compared to the electrochemical counterparts. A self-powered PEC CO2 reduction with a solar-to-fuel conversion efficiency of 3.2% can be obtained by integrating the graphene/Si heterojunction photocathode and photoanode with a Si photovoltaic. In addition, in situ PEC X-ray absorption spectroscopy analyses show that the electrodeposited catalysts on the graphene layer lead to the transport of photogenerated electrons and preserve durability throughout the reaction. Utilizing graphene as a chemically inert atomic bridging layer enables the seamless integration of Si photoelectrodes with various catalysts, providing a platform for the PEC CO2 reduction reaction.

items.title: Fabrication and characterization of high-quality Nb/Al-AlO x /Nb cross-type Josephson tunnel junctions utilising CMP-based planarisation techniques
items.abstract: Abstract Josephson tunnel junctions (JJs) are the fundamental building blocks of today's most advanced superconducting electronic components, such as qubits and superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs). Given the ongoing demand for scalability of these devices on the wafer-scale, it is crucial to control the fabrication process as precisely as possible to ensure uniform quality and reproducibility. Today, window-type JJs are often used in the production of DC SQUIDs and while they are reliable and reproducible, they suffer from alignment inaccuracies caused by photolithography and unavoidable parasitic capacitances, thus limiting the energy sensitivity of DC SQUIDs. These problems can be circumvented by producing JJs with cross-type geometry, which allows for smaller junction areas and eliminates parasitic capacitances. Here we discuss the fabrication of Nb/Al-AlO x /Nb-based cross-type JJs, where the trilayer is embedded in sputter-deposited SiO 2 to allow for planarisation of structures and to ensure reliable insulation of the sidewalls of the bottom electrode. Instead of lift-off processes that can require processing times of several hours and potentially produce residual dielectric features along the structure edges that might compromise subsequent layers, we use chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) for the removal of excess SiO 2 . This reduces the duration of the planarization step from hours to minutes and yields smooth, uniform surfaces with a within-wafer non-uniformity of below 5%. The resulting process achieves a junction yield above 90% across 3 inch wafers. In addition, we discuss the influence of fabrication details on the quality and electrical properties of our JJs with different junction areas down to 1 µm × 1 µm distributed across the wafer and extract the junction specific quality parameters from their IV -characteristics. Across the junctions, the spreads are approximately 1% for gap voltage, below 3% for critical current, below 4% for the subgap-to-normal resistance ratio, and below 1% for characteristic voltage.

items.title: Emerging Perovskite Quantum Dots for Optoelectronic Sensing–Memory–Computing Neuromorphic Systems
items.abstract: With the explosive development of artificial intelligence (AI), unprecedented demands have been imposed on modern computing hardware. Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from inherent data throughput and energy efficiency bottlenecks due to physical isolation between computation and memory units. In this context, brain-inspired neuromorphic computing system enabled by emerging optoelectronic synaptic devices (OSDs) has emerged as a highly promising and transformative alternative, offering a viable pathway toward next-generation intelligent computing systems featuring parallelism, low power consumption, and high efficiency comparable to biological neural networks. Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) exhibit exceptional optoelectronic properties, making PQDs-based OSDs (PQDs-OSDs) a research hotspot. This review summarizes recent advances in PQDs-OSDs including the material characteristics and synthesis methods of PQDs, as well as the device structures, working mechanisms, and applications of PQDs-OSDs. We systematically introduce the applications of PQDs-OSDs in brain-inspired computing and artificial vision. Furthermore, the critical challenges of stability and scalability are comprehensively discussed, providing fundamental insights for advancing the application of PQDs-OSDs in optoelectronic sensing-memory-computing neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Efficiency Enhancement of Inductive Power Transfer Systems through Adaptive Compensation Topologies and Advanced Power Converter Design
items.abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) provides a promising solution for autonomous and implantable electronic devices. However, maintaining high efficiency under varying loads, coil distances, and misalignments remains challenging, particularly in low-power applications. This dissertation develops a high-efficiency, self-adaptive, and communication-free IPT system. First, an enhanced Class B amplifier is introduced as a compact transmitter, exploiting controlled crossover distortion to achieve zero-voltage switching (ZVS) and approximately 98% efficiency. Second, a generalized analytical framework is developed to evaluate basic and hybrid compensation topologies, enabling systematic selection according to output characteristics, efficiency, and misalignment tolerance. Third, a novel three-switch receiver converter is proposed to improve regulation efficiency through an inherent bypass mode, reduce duty-cycle sensitivity, and enable autonomous maximum-efficiency tracking using locally measurable variables without transmitter–receiver communication. Experimental results demonstrate receiver efficiency above 95%, with resonance, soft switching, and load adaptation maintained under variations in coil distance, misalignment, and load. The proposed solutions provide a compact and reliable approach to efficient wireless power delivery for low-power electronic applications.:Chapter 1. Introduction Chapter 2. Inductive Power Transfer Theoretical Background Chapter 3. Efficiency Improvement Methods in Low-Power IPT Chapter 4. Modeling of Generalized Compensation Topology and Transmitter–Receiver Resonant Converter Design with Maximum Efficiency Tracking Chapter 5. Experimental Investigations Chapter 6. Performance Evaluation and Design Implications of IPT Systems Chapter 7. Conclusion and Outlook
items.venue: Qucosa (Saxon State and University Library Dresden)

items.title: Dynamic Reprogramming Voltage Design and Optimization for 3D TLC NAND Flash Memory in Physical-Layer Storage Systems
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) TLC NAND flash memory serves as a core physical-layer storage component in high-performance data storage and transmission systems. Although reprogramming techniques effectively boost storage density and memory endurance, long-term data retention degradation and persistent cell loss severely impair the physical-layer reliability and channel stability. To alleviate these impairments during reprogramming operations, this paper proposes a dynamic write voltage design and optimization scheme for 3D TLC NAND flash memory in physical-layer storage systems. The proposed method extracts physical-layer channel parameters from real flash chips and integrates them into the threshold voltage distribution model to realize adaptive reprogramming voltage adjustment. Based on the measured channel characteristics, a dynamic reprogramming voltage strategy from MLC mode to TLC mode is constructed for reliable data refresh in SSD controllers.

items.title: Design and implementation of a high-speed reversible arithmetic logic unit for power-efficient computing
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents the design, simulation, and hardware validation of a high-speed, power-efficient reversible Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) architecture, implemented in Verilog HDL. The ALU consists of three modular blocks—Arithmetic, Logical, and Control Units—and employs reversible logic gates to minimize power consumption and information loss. The proposed design achieves a Total Reversible Logic Instruction Count (TRLIC) of 53, reflecting a 62.67% improvement over prior works. Functional verification was carried out through simulation in Xilinx Vivado and ISE 14.7, followed by FPGA prototyping on the NEXYS A7 (Artix-7) board, confirming accurate operation. Beyond FPGA validation, the design was synthesized and implemented as an ASIC using Cadence Genus and Innovus with the 90-nm CMOS technology, completing the RTL-to-GDSII physical-design flow. The ASIC implementation achieved a critical-path delay of 1.195 ns, with a reported switching power of 1.72 µW.

items.title: Decoupling Metal Deposition from Contact Formation Enables Polarity Transformation in WSe2 Transistors
items.abstract: Polarity control in two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor field-effect transistors (FETs) is essential for their integration into complementary logic circuits. However, existing polarity-engineering approaches often fail to preserve high-quality contact interfaces because atomically thin 2D semiconductors are highly sensitive to fabrication processes. Here, we introduce an effective buffer-layer removal process that enables polarity transformation while preserving a high-quality contact interface. A thin semimetal layer (Bi or Sb) is deposited prior to high-work-function metal evaporation and subsequently removed by a wet chemical treatment that preserves a high-quality metal/semiconductor interface. Minimizing the contact angle of the rinsing solution suppresses wrinkle and bubble formations and reduces Fermi-level pinning. The same WSe2 transistors transform from semimetal-dominated n-type transport before treatment to high-work-function-metal-dominated p-type transport afterward. Monolayer devices exhibit a maximum two-terminal hole field-effect mobility of 313 cm2 V-1 s-1 after treatment, while also supporting a maximum electron mobility of 41 cm2 V-1 s-1 before treatment. These results demonstrate n-to-p polarity transformation in WSe2 transistors enabled by a removable semimetal layer, providing a potential doping-free route toward complementary 2D electronics.

items.title: Comparative Study on the Translation Quality of "Three-Character Classic" by Large Language Models and Multimodal Large Models
items.abstract: With the widespread application of large language models (LLM) and multimodal large models (MLLM) in the field of machine translation, how to evaluate the translation quality of different models for ancient Chinese classics has become an urgent issue to be explored. This study takes the children's educational classic "Three Character Classic" as the research object, selects eight representative original sentences, and translates them into English using both LLM and MLLM. The translated texts are then quantitatively compared using the BLEU automatic evaluation tool. The aim of this study is to determine which type of model performs better in the English translation of classical Chinese texts and which model is more suitable for the translation tasks of Chinese classical literature. The study found that, here, fill in the actual experimental data: the BLEU and METEOR scores show which type of model performs better. This study provides empirical reference for AI-assisted English translation of Chinese ancient classics and also offers an empirical basis for the applicability of automatic translation quality assessment tools in the context of classical Chinese translation.

items.title: Cold-source field-effect transistor with type-III band-aligned HfS 2 /WTe 2 heterostructure
items.abstract: The cold source field-effect transistor (CSFET) is promising for reducing power dissipation in integrated circuits by engineering the density of states at the injecting source. Existing CSFET designs utilizing Dirac-source metals or p-Metal-n stacks are challenged by Schottky barriers at the metal-semiconductor interface. In this work, a 2D WTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ heterojunction with type-III band alignment is proposed to be an excellent design of cold source and CSFET. The architecture has a high band-to-band transport mechanism by removing the detrimental Schottky barrier issues. Importantly, the proposed CSFET has the same channel barrier modulation principle as conventional MOSFET to enable a high on-state current. Using first-principles-based quantum transport modeling, we predict a very high $I_{\rm on}$/$I_{\rm off}$ ratio at $\sim$ 10$^{10}$, a low subthreshold swing below the thermal limit for a wide range of gate voltages, reaching as small as 41.3 mV/dec, at low source-drain bias $V_{DS}=0.3$ $\rm V$. These findings establish a design principles for next-generation low-power nanoelectronic switches leveraging 2D van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Code and data for: Electrode-area precision and odd-state quantization failure in neuromorphic memristive synapses
items.abstract: Simulation code and stored results for the Letter 'Electrode-area precision and odd-state quantization failure in neuromorphic memristive synapses'. Includes the interface-type memristor compact model, the precision-area law, the closed-form dead-weight fraction and SQNR, post-mapping of a trained network onto N conductance levels, hardware-aware training with a straight-through estimator (7 seeds), the clipping-threshold scan and device-to-device variability sweeps, with a numpy-only script that verifies the central numbers.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Chip‐Level Voltage Controlled Magnetic p‐Bits Array with Variation Compensation for Stochastic Neural Network Computation
items.abstract: The increasing computational and energy-efficiency demands of artificial intelligence are driving the development of new computing paradigms based on emerging memory devices. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) based on magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs), benefiting from energy efficiency, CMOS compatibility, and fast sampling, show broad potential in stochastic neural networks. However, unavoidable device-to-device variations in MTJ switching probabilities hinder the realization of scalable p-bit chips. Here, we integrate a high-density array of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy MTJs (VCMA-MTJs) and employ a tail truncation strategy to compensate for their variations in probabilistic switching ranges, enabling chip-level p-bit functionality. Our VCMA-MTJ chip (VM-chip) successfully implements restricted Boltzmann machines (RBM) and deep belief networks (DBN) for image recognition, anomaly detection, image completion, and image generation, demonstrating the practical utility of this chip in stochastic neural networks. Furthermore, we propose a dual-control strategy that tunes both the amplitude and duration of the voltage pulse, significantly enhancing network performance and performing comparably to conventional software-generated pseudo-random numbers. Our work enhances the tolerance of probabilistic computing to variations in MTJ switching probabilities, offering flexibility in device selection and array integration. This approach may provide a promising pathway toward scalable p-bit hardware and cost-effective manufacturing in future probabilistic computing systems.

items.title: BinauralLM: spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation with large language model
items.abstract: Abstract Binaural audio is a practical spatial audio format for headphone playback and is widely used in immersive media such as games, VR/AR, and interactive multimedia. Currently, binaural audio is still largely obtained either by specialized recordings or by spatializing pre-recorded monaural signals, which limits flexibility for controllable content creation. While recent text-to-audio models can generate the required audio, most of them target monaural output or unconstrained stereo. They provide limited control over spatial attributes such as direction and motion. To address these challenges, we propose BinauralLM, a spatial prompted text-to-binaural audio generation framework with large language model (LLM). BinauralLM adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, we use a Qwen2.5 LLM to autoregressively generate coarse binaural token sequences conditioned on text and spatial prompts. To effectively couple semantic content with spatial cues, we introduce a spatial prompt encoder and an attention fusion module to produce a unified conditioning representation for binaural token generation. Second, we employ a flow matching model that takes the coarse binaural tokens as conditions and reconstructs high-quality binaural waveforms in the continuous domain. Experimental results on the BEWO-1M dataset demonstrate that BinauralLM achieves superior performance on standard text-to-audio metrics and binaural spatial metrics, and achieves higher MOS scores in perceptual evaluation, especially on spatialization quality. These results indicate that our proposed method offers an effective route to controllable and high-quality text-to-binaural audio generation.
items.venue: EURASIP Journal on Audio Speech and Music Processing

items.title: Biased Error Attribution in Multi-Agent Human–AI Systems Under Delayed Feedback
items.abstract: Human decision-making is often influenced by cognitive biases, especially under uncertainty and risk. Prior works have studied biases in single-step decision environments with immediate outcomes or in interaction with a single AI agent. However, less attention has been given to (1) cascaded settings with delayed outcomes, where decision at one step influences future system states and (2) to interaction with multiple AI agents. To study this, we designed a naval battle strategy game where participants interact with two AI advisors. We find asymmetric responses to positive and negative outcomes, with significant changes after negative outcomes. Participants failed to identify the actions responsible for failures and misattributed responsibility across AI agents, leading them to modify decisions steps weakly related to the true cause of poor performance. We refer to this behavior as bias in error attribution. Our findings show how cognitive biases can emerge in human-multi AI teams in cascaded settings.
items.venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting

items.title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing
items.abstract: Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

items.title: An AI-powered trisomy 21 Research Assistant
items.abstract: Down syndrome, caused by trisomy 21, increases the risk of diverse co-occurring conditions. With more than 34,000 related publications indexed in PubMed as of early 2026, keeping pace with this expanding literature is challenging. While general-purpose large language models are widely used for information retrieval, they often rely on broad training data rather than specific evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves rigor and reliability of responses by linking model outputs to source texts. In research, source texts are peer-reviewed articles. Standard implementations treat all manuscript sections equally, allowing background text to rank as highly as experimental results. To focus model outputs on experimentally supported responses, we developed the T21 Research Assistant, a section-aware RAG system that prioritizes Results sections to ground responses in primary experimental evidence. The system draws exclusively from 1,789 open-access Down syndrome publications from PubMed Central, including 327 NIH INCLUDE-funded studies, and uses a multistage pipeline for query validation, retrieval, reranking, synthesis, and citation verification. Built on NVIDIA Nemotron models, it generates structured, cited responses. Evaluation using expert-curated questions demonstrated strong performance, achieving a BERTScore F1 of 0.712 and recall of 0.758, comparable to or exceeding leading proprietary and open-source models. T21 Research Assistant is available at: https://bioinformatics.cuanschutz.edu/t21-res-assi/.

items.title: Aligning heterogeneous DFT datasets: a graph neural network approach to cross-functional formation energies
items.abstract: Heterogeneous density functional theory (DFT) calculations, particularly plane-wave implementations, introduce systematic formation energy errors ranging from tens to hundreds of meV/atom, depending on the selection of exchange-correlation functionals, kinetic energy cutoffs, pseudopotentials, and dispersion corrections. As demonstrated by the MatPES dataset, identical structures can exhibit an average energy discrepancy of 107 meV/atom between PBE and r 2 SCAN calculations. Such method-dependent discrepancies hinder the integration of multi-source DFT data, greatly limiting the scale and quality of datasets for training robust materials AI models. Here, we resolve this fundamental data silo barrier via graph-based transfer learning. Leveraging 380,190 structurally paired PBE–r 2 SCAN entries from the MatPES database, we train a structure-aware graph neural network to predict cross-functional energy residuals and align inconsistent DFT energy scales. By adopting GPTFF model architecture, the model converts conventional PBE energies to r 2 SCAN-level accuracy with a mean absolute error of 14.3 meV/atom, compared with 18.2 meV/atom achieved by CHGNet. This versatile approach effectively upgrades massive legacy PBE datasets to high-precision r 2 SCAN standards. It enables reliable predictions of phase stability, battery voltage profiles, and reaction thermodynamics, while allowing the integration of multi-source DFT data to advance the development of high-performance materials foundation models.

items.title: ATIC: a closed-loop, migration-aware tiering controller for cloud and edge NVMe storage
items.abstract: Tiered cloud and edge storage pairs a small, fast tier with a larger capacity tier, but traditional storage replacement policies can allow for the admission of large or sequentially accessed objects whose migration cost is greater than the object’s reuse value. This paper introduces an online admission and eviction controller, ATIC, that combines interpretable benefits per byte of decayed frequency, compactness based on reuse-gap (rather than reuse-size), sequentially, read propensity, object size, device service-time savings, and promotion cost. A quantile gate dynamically tunes the admission selectivity every 750 requests, based on the ratio of promoted bytes to requested bytes. ATIC is benchmarked in a disclosed object-level queueing simulator with five business-intelligence and five artificial-intelligence workload families, 30,000 requests per workload and 20 paired seeds. Relative to GDSF, ATIC saves 41.3%–80.3% of promoted bytes and 2.9%–10.5% of modeled active-I/O energy at 10% capacity for all workloads (one-sided paired Wilcoxon p < 10⁻⁴). With the best latency baseline, ATIC reduces the latency for AI training by 0.5%, and checkpoint traffic by 2.6%, outperforming effectively tied for ETL, and 10.5% and 3.6% slower for locality-dominant BI and mixed analytics, respectively. Ablations reveal that size normalization keeps latency failure from becoming widespread, while the adaptive gate mostly restricts migration. ATIC thus offers a clear migration-energy-latency trade-off, instead of a general latency improvement. Before deploying, hardware and production-trace validation is still required.

items.title: A monoelemental ferroelectric semiconductor
items.abstract: Abstract The emergence of single‑element ferroelectricity beyond traditional compound ferroelectrics broadens the ranges of ferroelectric materials and enriches polarization mechanisms. However, all prior elemental ferroelectrics (e.g., Bismuth and Tellurium) are metals or semimetals with narrow bandgaps, causing large leakage current, low breakdown voltage, and poor device reliability, severely limiting their practical applications in low‑power electronics and neuromorphic computing. Here, we report the first discovery of robust room-temperature ferroelectricity in a monoelemental ferroelectric semiconductor, two‑dimensional selenium (Se) nanosheets. Unexpectedly, a strong dipole-interlocking coupling between in-plane and out-of-plane polarizations enables simultaneous switching of both components. This coupling is rarely observed outside α-In₂Se₃. Our findings not only overcome the long-standing limitations of metallic/semimetallic elemental ferroelectrics by introducing a semiconducting elemental ferroelectric (Se), but also establish Se as a highly promising material platform for future low-power, multi-terminal, and multimodal neuromorphic computing hardware.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Thermal–Electrical–Mechanical Trade-offs and Design Rules for Through-Silicon Vias in 3D Chiplet Integration
items.abstract: A PRISMA 2020 systematic review of numerical, analytical and experimental studies that vary through-silicon via (TSV) geometry or layout in 3D ICs, 2.5D interposers and chiplet packages. It quantifies how diameter, height/aspect ratio, liner thickness, pitch and arrangement affect heat transfer, electrical parasitics and thermo-mechanical stress, audits the rigour of the numerical models, and derives evidence-graded design rules.

items.title: A Reconfigurable Ferroelectric Acoustic Computational Primitive for Analog In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: Abstract The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence (AI) have renewed interest in emerging nonvolatile memory (eNVM) crossbar array technologies for in-memory computing to reduce the energy cost of moving data between processors and memory. Here we report a computational primitive that merges ferroelectric memory and acoustic resonators in a single platform: Ferroelectric memory Embedded in Nanoscale Acoustic resonators (FENA). We experimentally demonstrate over 100 nonvolatile analog admittance states arising from partial ferroelectric polarization switching in lithium niobate resonators. The devices exhibit highly symmetric potentiation and depression characteristics, which directly impact computation accuracy, favorable dynamic range and linearity, and low projected read and write energies after scaling. We further propose a radio frequency (RF) peripheral readout architecture that extracts frequency- and phase-sensitive effective conductance states to offer an expanded state space and hardware-level reconfigurability. System-level evaluation using the NeuroSim multi-layer perceptron (MLP) simulator demonstrates the suitability of FENA for both online and offline neural-network training, with scaled devices achieving competitive 84% and 92% classification accuracies, respectively.

items.title: A Novel STT-MRAM-Based Massive Parallelism Strong PUF with High Throughput and Low BER for IoT Security
items.abstract: The lightweight design and reliability of physical unclonable functions (PUFs) are critical for IoT security. In this work, we propose a strong PUF based on spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory (STT-MRAM). For the first time, we adopt a logic-in-memory (LIM) structure known as Computational Random Access Memory (CRAM) in order to promote massive parallelism and low area overhead. In our simulations of the results, the proposed PUF macro occupies 2960.4 μm2 in total, 5.77 μm2 per cell, and presents a high bit rate of 1.42 Gb/s. In addition, we introduce the TRIM circuit and algorithm into the response generation process and develop two TRIM algorithms to optimize its reliability. The proposed PUF presents an excellent average intra-chip Hamming distance of 0.288% under the temperature range from −10 °C to 150 °C. The PUF also achieves an inter-chip Hamming distance of 50.003% and generates 22N/3 challenge–response pairs (CRPs), which surpass other state-of-the-art MRAM strong PUFs. More importantly, the proposed PUF shows excellent machine-learning resistance. This work provides a new strong PUF solution for resource-limited system-on-chip (SoC) chips for edge applications.

items.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
items.abstract: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to Sn(OH)$_3$-Me and its hydrates, minimal models of organotin photoresists for extreme-ultraviolet lithography, from 32 to 70 qubits. After one round of hardware sampling, followed by classical ranking and recovery of the cached counts with the molecular Hamiltonian and no further QPU calls, 27 of 28 runs at 46-70 qubits are within 15 mHa of the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) reference (median 4.5 mHa), and in all eight runs with an untrained control the trained policy is more accurate. At 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use 34-72 times fewer two-qubit gates than the local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuit transpiled for the same device. These results demonstrate that circuit generators can be trained with quantum hardware at 70 qubits.

items.title: A Comparative Study of Investment Environments in Japan and South Korea amid US Supply Chain Restructuring: The Role of Political Systems and Governance Models (2021-2026)
items.abstract: Amid US-led supply chain reconfiguration and rising geopolitical and economic uncertainty, Japan and South Korea are both seeking to strengthen industrial and investment resilience.
