We further analyze 90 DW and find that frustrated phonon modes emerge at the wall center, where the coexistence and competition of condensed modes promote local reconfiguration of the lattice distortions, contributing to the elevated DW energies. Importantly, experimental observations with STEM imaging provide direct evidence of atomic mode distortions in stable 90 DW, consistent with the theoretically identified low-energy DW. These findings provide the fundamental structural mechanism underlying 90 switching dynamics, competing domain-wall physics, and macroscopic ferroelectric behavior.

items.title: Mitigating Sequence-of-Returns Risk with Regime-Switching Asset Allocation: A Comparison of Econometric and Deep Learning Models in Portfolio Decumulation
items.abstract: Abstract Retirement portfolios under regular withdrawals face sequence-of-returns risk: early losses can exhaust capital even when average returns are adequate. We examine whether regime-switching dynamic asset allocation mitigates this risk for a 60/40 stock-bond portfolio, and whether deep learning identifies regimes better than classical econometrics. Five models (a Markov-switching model, a multivariate and a univariate Gaussian hidden Markov model, an LSTM, and an encoder-only Transformer) are compared under identical data, tuning, and walk-forward validation. Their signals, net of transaction costs, feed 10{,}000 stationary-bootstrap retirement paths in three withdrawal scenarios. At 4.0% the MSM, the univariate HMM, and the LSTM cut the depletion rate from 3.30% to 0.57%, 0.60%, and 0.60% with disjoint Wilson intervals; at 6.0% only the LSTM reduces it (17.01% against 33.04%), the univariate filters raising it to about 49% as their return sacrifice becomes the dominant ruin cause, and the multivariate HMM raising it in every scenario. Only the econometric models turn defensive in all five crisis windows; neither network identifies regimes more accurately, and the LSTM holds the highest median terminal capital by staying invested rather than by timing regimes. Classification quality and search diagnostics do not predict decumulation value. Regime-switching allocation in decumulation is a state-contingent tail hedge: model choice determines the protected risk profile, and above a critical withdrawal rate the premium exceeds the payout.

items.title: Microelectronics Assembly and Packaging: Materials and Technologies, 2nd Edition
items.abstract: This Reprint collected 10 outstanding peer-reviewed articles, which focused on the materials and technologies of microelectronics assembly and packaging. The content of these articles was within the scope of the Special Issue. For example, the assessment of crack formation at a hybrid bonding interface was reported; interposer-based ESD protection was found to be a potential solution for μ-packaging reliability of 3D chips; interconnects’ resonance and signal/power integrity degradation in glass packages were measured and analyzed; the impact of bonding pressure on reactive bonding was explored; post-wire-bonding corrosion prevention strategies were proposed to mitigate Chloride- and Bromide-induced corrosion failures in Cu- and PCC-based wire-bonded packages; etc. Any readers whose interests are within the aforementioned areas, we welcome you to read this Reprint.

items.title: Machine-Learning Dynamics of Redox-Active Materials: Polaron Diffusion on the TiO2(110) Surface
items.abstract: Abstract In redox-active materials, atoms dynamically change their oxidation states in response to excess charge and electronic transport, with the potential for novel technologies spanning electronics, catalysis, and energy storage and conversion. Despite the remarkable progress of modern artificial intelligence methods in accelerating atomistic simulations, capturing the quantum-mechanical nature of charge transport and dynamically varying oxidation states remains a fundamental challenge, limiting scientific and technological progress. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning-based molecular dynamics framework capable of explicitly tracking the oxidation state dynamics arising from small-polaron hopping (excess charges trapped on single lattice sites that diffuse upon thermal activation). Our model uses descriptors augmented with charge localization information at each time step and is trained on density functional theory data to capture signatures of polaronic diffusion. We apply our method to the rutile TiO2(110) surface, which is a prototypical reducible oxide. Our simulations reveal that charge-carrier diffusion is highly sensitive to the local surface environment: polarons preferentially localize near oxygen vacancies, whereas their interaction with hydroxyl groups is weaker. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of experimental observations, highlight strategies to tune charge-carrier mobility through surface engineering, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach to investigating charge transport in complex materials.

items.title: Learning to remember: advances in memory mechanisms for large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations, or model weights; and memory for agent evolution, where stored experiences support reinforcement learning, continual learning, procedural reuse, context engineering, and agent harness design. Evaluation is treated as a separate cross-cutting component rather than as a memory mechanism. Unlike surveys that focus primarily on retrieval-augmented generation or long-context modeling, this paper emphasizes the full memory life cycle: construction, maintenance, retrieval, consolidation, forgetting, governance, and evaluation. By aligning conceptual motivations, computational memory mechanisms, benchmarks, and deployment concerns, the survey provides a structured roadmap for designing memory-augmented LLM agents that are persistent, adaptive, auditable, and safe to update over time.

items.title: Large Language Models in Museum Communication: Opportunities, Risks, and Implementation Requirements
items.abstract: The transition of museum institutions into the era of generative artificial intelligence is characterized by systemic transformation, from the representation of digitized collections to dynamic interaction within a synthetic digital environment. Under these conditions, the challenge of adapting traditional standards of museum authenticity to the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) becomes particularly pressing. This study aims to develop a conceptual understanding of the transformation of museum communication, identify the epistemological challenges posed by the algorithmic generation of context and meaning, and describe mechanisms for preserving institutional authority as neural network–based tools are integrated into the public sphere. The study draws on a synthesis of institutional and communication approaches, which makes it possible to consider the museum not only as a custodian of material heritage but also as an active mediator amid increasing information noise. The empirical basis of the study consists of an analysis of the practical and educational agenda of the Hermitage School of Communication, held in Petrozavodsk in September 2025. The methodology involved identifying the professional competencies required to work in a hybrid media environment and evaluating practical applications of media analytics carried out by museum professionals using readily available AI tools designed for end users. The findings indicate that the adoption of LLMs inevitably shifts the focus of museum work away from routine content creation toward critical verification, strategic planning, and the management of meaning-making narratives. The stochastic nature of these models was found to give rise to risks of semantic uncertainty, including the loss of historical context, the reproduction of latent biases, and the substitution of factual information with probabilistic constructs. At the same time, the study illustrates the high effectiveness of algorithms in media analytics tasks, such as clustering audience inquiries and identifying latent patterns in unstructured feedback data. A key determinant of success is not only the model's technological capabilities but also the quality of research design established by the specialist when formulating the prompt. The findings point to the need to reconsider assumptions about the extent to which intellectual work in the cultural sector can be automated. An approach is proposed in which AI operates within bounded environments of verified museum data. The need for museums to adapt their infrastructure is also highlighted, including the creation of secure digital corpora, the implementation of transparent protocols for labeling synthetic content, and the development of ethical principles. The study emphasizes that, in the era of synthetic communication, the critical thinking and in-depth expertise of museum professionals remain particularly valuable resources.

items.title: La Vattiata, Federico; Kenyon, Tony; Lombardo, Antonio; Wallis, Kate; (2026) Regulating Neuromorphic Computing in the UK: An application-led framework for brain-inspired Technologies
items.abstract: Emerging technologies are difficult to regulate because their capabilities, uses and even basic boundaries can change quickly, and develop faster than regulators' understanding and existing regulatory frameworks.This creates a difficult policy challenge: regulators must protect the public from potential harms without unnecessarily constraining innovation.Where regulation fails to keep pace, significant harms may fall through regulatory gaps.At the same time, where regulation is introduced without a clear understanding of the technology or its risks, it may impose unnecessary burdens on beneficial innovation.Neuromorphic computing (NC) illustrates this challenge particularly well because its technical boundaries remain fluid and its applications can create very different risks.Neuromorphic systems may combine hardware-dependent processing, edge deployment, real-time operation, and adaptation after deployment.These characteristics challenge assumptions underlying existing approaches to regulating emerging technology, including how countries currently approach artificial intelligence (AI) governance.1,2,3,4 What is neuromorphic computing?Neuromorphic computing is a family of braininspired technologies.The term encompasses different combinations of hardware, software, sensors and braininspired computing methods, and the field remains at an early stage of development.These systems aim to make computing more energy-efficient, responsive, and capable of processing information closer to where it is generated.Potential applications include autonomous vehicles, medical devices, industrial systems and defence.However, NC is not a single, clearly bounded technology.

items.title: Ion–Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
items.abstract: A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single-channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion-electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual-channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic-light-guided closed-loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This "single device enabled, distinguishable dual-channel readouts" principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

items.title: Interface‐Mediated Self‐Rectifying CsCuCl 3 Memristors With Tunable Thresholds for Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We demonstrate a simple 1R self‐rectifying halide perovskite memristor with dynamically tunable thresholds for selector‐free crossbar arrays and programmable T‐ReLU mapping. The memristors achieve an ON/OFF ratio > 10 5 and rectification ratio > 10 4 . The switching mechanism involves two synergistic processes: bulk ion migration within CsCuCl 3 provides and sustains the low‐resistance state essential for a high ON/OFF ratio, while the Ag‐Cl‐containing oxidized interfacial layer introduces a Schottky barrier and trap filling/release mechanism that governs the HRS to LRS switching. Systematic simulations using CNN architectures reveal a dataset‐dependent threshold sensitivity: MNIST accuracy remains robust (> 98%) regardless of threshold variations, whereas CIFAR‐10 accuracy drops sharply as positive thresholds increase. Based on this complexity‐dependent trend, we exploited the bi‐directional tunability for dual‐mode applications: (i) Negative threshold operation in CNNs maintains 91.0% accuracy for low‐light image recognition (comparable to the ReLU baseline); (ii) Positive threshold modulation in a customized SparseResNet‐18 architecture is explored for sparsity‐aware edge computing, where thresholds τ ∈ [0, 0.3] are adjusted according to simulated battery levels to control the sparsity‐accuracy trade‐off. Under low‐battery conditions (τ = 0.3), the simulated network achieves 76.3% activation sparsity while maintaining 90.1% accuracy without retraining. This work highlights the potential of tunable activation thresholds for reconfigurable neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Influence of epitaxial strain on structural relaxation in crystalline membranes of fluorite oxides
items.abstract: Using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we investigated how epitaxial strain influences structural relaxation in freestanding crystalline membranes of fluorite oxides. When epitaxial films of yttrium-doped hafnium oxide Hf0.93Y0.07O2(HYO) with the metastable orthorhombic phase under compressive strain were exfoliated from La0.7Sr0.3MnO3(LSMO)-buffered (110) SrTiO3 substrates, the strain was partially relaxed, while the metastable phase was preserved in the membrane form. In contrast, the metastable orthorhombic phase of zirconium dioxide (ZrO2) films grown on (110) LSMO/STO substrates and under negligibly small strain underwent structural relaxation into the thermodynamically stable monoclinic phase upon exfoliation from the substrate. These results indicate that the energy barrier between the metastable orthorhombic phase and the monoclinic one is less for ZO than for HYO, highlighting that the stability of the metastable phase, which is modulated by the strain, influences the structural relaxation in fluorite oxide membranes.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: Impact of a process-induced interfacial layer on ferroelectric switching and reliability in AlScN/ β -Ga2O3 MFS capacitors
items.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate AlScN-based metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor capacitors directly integrated on a heteroepitaxial β-Ga2O3. Structural analysis reveals the presence of a process-induced amorphous intermixed layer at the AlScN/β-Ga2O3 interface. The fabricated devices exhibit ferroelectric switching behavior, characterized by counterclockwise hysteretic current–voltage loops with an on/off current ratio of >102, which is limited by the intermixed interfacial layer. Piezo-response force microscopy measurements confirm the intrinsic polarization switching capability through phase reversal and butterfly-shaped amplitude loops. Furthermore, positive-up-negative-down measurements indicate polarization switching while revealing a switching current asymmetry. We identify that this asymmetry originates from the internal electric field and charge trapping associated with the interfacial defect layer. This interfacial instability primarily affects the device performance observed during retention (103 s) and endurance (5 × 103 cycles) tests, suggesting significance of the interface toward stable ferroelectric operation in AlScN/β-Ga2O3 devices.

items.title: HyperMesh-512: Hyper-Parallel Inference Acceleration Architecture for Massive Language Models Based on a 2D Mesh NoC and a Decentralized 32-Channel LPDDR4X/DDR4 Bus
items.abstract: HyperMesh-512 is a hyper-parallel PCIe inference accelerator architecture engineered to overcome the Memory Wall bottleneck during autoregressive decoding of massive language models (such as Llama 3.1 70B/405B and DeepSeek-R1/V3 671B MoE). Featuring 512 GB of commodity LPDDR4X/DDR4 memory distributed across 32 independent physical 64-bit point-to-point channels coupled to 16 ASIC micro-chiplets in a 2D Mesh NoC (X-Y DOR routing), the board delivers 819.2 GB/s to 1,092.1 GB/s of sustained memory bandwidth. To address ultra-long context windows (≥ 128k tokens), each chiplet integrates a dedicated single-cycle affine INT4 to INT16 hardware decompressor, reducing 128k KV-cache footprint from 41.94 GB down to 10.49 GB and raising effective context read bandwidth to 3,276.8 GB/s equivalent. Audited Industrial BOM: US$ 1,680.00. Target MSRP: US$ 4,999.00 delivering 102.42 GB/k$ (a 48x capital-efficiency advantage over corporate HGX H100 clusters), with a 98.33% CapEx reduction and 96.57% electrical OpEx reduction for on-premise, air-gapped private generative AI workloads. Declaração de Natureza Teórica: Artigo teórico / preprint técnico contendo modelagem arquitetural, RTL sintetizável e projeções tecno-econômicas. Propriedade Intelectual e Licenciamento (Royalties): Titularidade de Tiago Barbosa Dias Maciel (CPF 060.184.906-09, tiago@brmg.com.br). Qualquer exploração comercial sujeita a licenciamento e royalty de US$ 50,00 por placa ou US$ 3,00 por chiplet integrado.

items.title: Hardware reconfigurable secure data acquisition system of a shared ADC in heterogenous multi-channel inputs with automatic sampling frequency configurations
items.abstract: Abstract Multi-channel Data Acquisition (DAQ) Systems can use a single multiplexed analog to digital converter (ADC) to reduce system cost. But this ADC must be configured to proper sampling rate for each channel. In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed to automatically generate ADC configuration, and improve the ADC’s utilization and utility, reduce the number of redundant bits, and reduce cost. This proposed algorithm is mathematically formulated, and numerical examples are given. The research methodology involves using FPGA board with analog to digital and digital to analog conversion card, and synthetic wave form is generated and captured for verification. In this phase, a single channel is investigated, as the investigation of multi-channel DAQ requires the integration and scheduling of the ADC with an external analog multiplexer. In prior work, a custom computer board is designed to implement the HTMS algorithm for 32 analog channels. To effectively demonstrate the previously proposed HTMS superiority against other approaches, new performance metrics were defined, namely the ADC’s utilization, utility and efficiency using two different heuristic analog input sets. These metrics show that the HTMS-based DAQ outperforms relevant systems as it reaches 100% of ADC’s utilization and utility, while other systems have 75% utilization, and 6.25% utility. By devising a unified figure of merit for multiple DAQ systems, it is shown that the proposed system is higher by 218% compared to the baseline multi-channel DAQ system. Furthermore, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) has been extensively investigated for cryptographic applications. A given pipelined 54-cycle AES-256-bit key core is considered for enhancement. With a single cycle design approach, the given core is successfully implemented in FPGA device using only 14-cycles / round, and generating a maximum encryption throughput of 12.8 Gb/s, with an FPGA utilization of only 9% Cyclone V SX SoC 5CSXFC6D6F31C6N, with speed up factor of 7 times is reported, compared to recent results, operating at a maximum clock frequency of 100 MHz. The proposed system will have a broader impact, particularly in medical diagnosis and prognosis, where multiple sensors of heterogenous types are used simultaneously, and the collected data must be secured to protect subjects’ privacy.

items.title: Hacking Back the AI Hacker: Prompt Injection as a Defense Against LLM-driven Cyberattacks
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are making multi-step cyberattacks cheaper to run and easier to automate. We present Mantis, a mechanism that leverages prompt injection for defensive purposes, turning it against the attacking LLM-agent itself. Once Mantis detects an attacking agent, it injects defender-crafted content into system responses and steers the agent toward one of two outcomes: a tarpit that wastes time and resources, or a controlled hack-back action that helps collect attribution information. Mantis combines decoy services with dynamic prompt injections and uses the attacker’s own interaction loop to deliver the defense. In our evaluation, Mantis achieves the sabotage objective in 95.4% of runs and keeps attacker success below 3%. We release Mantis as open source.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: Guarding Delegated Authority: Professional certification and operational safeguards for AI agents
items.abstract: AI agents can perform consequential actions through tools, credentials and delegated permissions. The governance problem is not only whether a threat can be recognised, but whether authorised limits remain enforceable while evidence is incomplete and intervention is time-sensitive. This discussion paper proposes two specialist qualifications within one professional scheme: an AI Red-Team Assessor, responsible for authorised adversarial evaluation, and an AI Security Operator, responsible for operational monitoring, containment and recovery. The proposal extends the author's Clean Engagement, Reflection Skills, Verification and Provenance and Certified Remote Operator frameworks. It distinguishes individual competence from service capability and deployment assurance, and argues that decisive restrictions must be enforced outside the model. A staged pilot is proposed for enterprise agents using documents, email and cloud business tools, with independent assessment and measures of containment, false intervention, evidence quality, recovery and delivery cost. The paper is a conceptual design proposal, not an empirical evaluation. It establishes neither accreditation, effectiveness, market demand nor commercial returns. Its contribution is a testable connection between professional qualification, delegated authority and operational evidence. Final discussion paper, version 1.0. Conceptual proposal, not an empirical evaluation. Not peer reviewed. No accreditation, endorsement, measured effectiveness, market demand or commercial returns are claimed. The sole author, B. Fischer, leads the GCTI/Emboa initiatives discussed and has a commercial interest in their development. AI assistance was used in drafting, editing, source checking and document preparation; it is not independent assurance.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Giving AI a Language of Its Own
items.abstract: Giving AI a Language of Its Own explores whether AI agents could benefit from a computational language designed around learned operations, compact expressions and reusable functionality. AIN (AI Native Language) is the reference concept for this proposed language and native compilation architecture. Short references represent known capabilities: for example, !501(config) could invoke an approved database connection method. A compiler would resolve these references into native implementations. AICC (AI Computational Commons) complements this approach through shared, approved and versioned capabilities that agents can discover, bind and reuse. The paper presents examples across C#, Python, C++, Ruby and Java, alongside processing experiments, bounded native compilation tests, small model adaptation studies and comparisons of alternative code representations. It distinguishes measured results from conditional calculations and proposed future work. Current text-token comparisons favor compact Python; idealized workflow calculations show potential savings under explicit assumptions, with equivalent ideal Python and intermediate representations matching AIN. The complete language and compiler remain conceptual. The contribution is a research approach supported by bounded prototypes, documented evidence and a plan for further evaluation. A reproducible test package accompanies the article, including protocols, scripts, recorded results and instructions for independent review by researchers and AI agents. This working paper is released to invite criticism, replication and collaboration.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Generative AI and the architecture of knowledge work: Expertise bypass, exchange governability, and shifting bottlenecks
items.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Research on GenAI and work has largely focused on tasks. We ask when task‐level effects alter knowledge‐work industry architecture: the allocation of activities across firm boundaries. Using a three‐stage abductive design—an executive roundtable, a panel of 626 firm websites (2017–2025), and 33 interviews plus two further roundtables with C‐level executives and corporate directors—we document divergent repositioning: professional services firms foreground relational value, while interface‐oriented technology firms emphasize scalable interfaces. We find that activity reallocation is shaped by two independently varying dimensions: expertise bypass and exchange governability. Their intersection yields four configurations: contestable reallocation, persistent bundles with selective insourcing, federated expert provision, and integrated expert provision. We extend industry architecture theory by explaining change when production and exchange conditions shift separately. Managerial Summary GenAI is not simply making knowledge work more efficient—it may be changing which organizations perform which work. We document that professional services firms are emphasizing relationship‐driven, judgment‐intensive work, while interface‐oriented technology firms are extending scalable delivery. Our framework explains why task exposure alone does not determine where work moves. We distinguish between expertise bypass—whether GenAI can produce an output without the expertise previously required—and exchange governability—whether that activity can be specified, verified, priced, and warranted across firm boundaries. Where both are present, work becomes contestable and may be reallocated. Where they diverge, highly exposed activities may remain bundled, while less exposed, human‐intensive work may move through federated specialist models. These conditions shape which organizational forms become viable.

items.title: Gender Bias Beyond Stereotypes: Towards Linguistically Gender-Fair Conversational LLMs
items.abstract: Gender bias in NLP has mostly been studied through the lens of stereotypes, i.e. associations between gender and occupations or personality traits. In this position paper, we argue that the rise of conversational large language models (LLMs) and open-ended generation stressed another important problem that remains largely unaddressed: masculine generics bias. In many languages, including German, French or Spanish, masculine forms are used to refer to mixed-gender groups or to people whose gender is unknown or non-binary (masculine generics, or MG for short). Decades of psycholinguistic research show that these forms are not interpreted as truly generic and instead lead people to have more male-centric mental representations. As LLMs are adopted by an ever-growing number of users worldwide for a wide range of tasks, this bias can now be perpetuated in everyday interactions, all the more since preliminary studies already show that LLMs lean heavily on MG and are reluctant to use gender-fair language spontaneously. We review the evidence for why it matters, explain why existing mitigation approaches are not enough for conversational LLMs, show that GFL in German, French and Spanish is lacking in LLM pre-training corpora, and outline 6 research directions towards building multilingual, linguistically gender-fair conversational LLMs.

items.title: Gateless 1T-DRAM for cryogenic memory applications
items.abstract: Cryogenic memory has emerged as a key technology for quantum-computing systems. In this Letter, a gateless one-transistor DRAM (1T-DRAM) operation is demonstrated at cryogenic temperatures. As the temperature decreases, the latch window expands from 0.26 V at 300 K to 2.26 V at 4 K, resulting in stable memory operation with a large sensing margin of 414 μA at 4 K. Suppressed Shockley–Read–Hall recombination at cryogenic temperatures improves static retention exceeding 500 s at 77 and 4 K, with dynamic retention exceeding 1000 s. These results demonstrate the potential of gateless 1T-DRAM for high-density cryogenic memory applications.

items.title: From EGOFET to OECT: Operational Control Engineered via the Electrolyte
items.abstract: Electrolyte-gated transistors (EGTs) are promising platforms for chemical/biological sensing and neuromorphic computing. A key research challenge lies in the selection of appropriate semiconductor and electrolyte materials to achieve efficient, stable, and reproducible devices. This work uses honey, a natural, antimicrobial, and non-volatile material, as the versatile electrolyte in EGTs that was anchored to a paper matrix for easier handling, reducing the reservoir construction step. We fabricated honey-gated transistors (HGTs) using a P3HT (poly(3-hexylthiophene-2,5diyl)) semiconductor and tested two electrolyte configurations: pristine honey and honey mixed with lithium perchlorate (LiClO4). These configurations led to distinct EGT operating modes. With pristine honey, the device operated as an electrolyte-gated organic field-effect transistor (EGOFET), governed by a field-effect mechanism. The addition of LiClO4 shifts the device’s operation mode to that of an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), where ionic doping modulates the channel conductivity. Key electrical parameters such as threshold voltage, transconductance, and on/off current ratio reflected this transition. Transient response measurements confirmed faster operation in EGOFET mode. Electrochemically, pristine honey exhibited excellent stability, with a wide electrochemical window (∼ 4V) in cyclic voltammetry. Impedance spectroscopy measurements show that incorporating LiClO4 to honey doubles the gate capacitance compared to the pristine honey device. These results demonstrate honey’s versatility as an electrolyte, enabling tunable EGT operation with a single semiconductor and highlighting a key design strategy for electrolyte engineering. This approach holds significant potential for sensing and neuromorphic applications.
authors: H. J. N. P. D. Mello

items.title: First-principles carrier mobility and optical absorption of strained ZnO with self-consistent Hubbard interactions
items.abstract: Carrier mobility and optical absorption are key performance parameters of oxide semiconductors in transparent and flexible displays. We use a newly developed density-functional perturbation theory with a self-consistent Hubbard correction (DFPT+U) to study phonon-limited electron transport and phonon-assisted optical absorption in strained zinc oxide (ZnO). This parameter-free approach accounts for electron-phonon interactions and on-site correlation effects simultaneously. Electronic structures and phonon dispersions are computed under three distinct uniaxial strain directions. Uniaxial tensile strain up to 4.8% along [\bar110] is found to increase the room-temperature electron mobility by 19% while leaving visible-range optical absorption essentially unchanged. These results demonstrate that moderate strain can selectively enhance carrier transport without degrading optical transparency, and establish DFPT+U as an effective framework for predicting strain-dependent transport and optical properties in wide-band-gap oxides with implications for strain-engineered display and optoelectronic applications.

items.title: FermiLink: An Agent Harness for Multidomain Scientific Simulations
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) agent harnesses have been developed for autonomous scientific simulations, but most current agent harnesses are tested on a single or a small set of software packages. Herein, FermiLink, an extensible open-source agent harness, is introduced for multidomain scientific simulations. Its key design principle is the separation of package knowledge bases from simulation workflows, so that simulation workflows in FermiLink, from figure-level simulations to full-paper-level research on high-performance computing clusters, operate uniformly among supported packages via a four-layer progressive disclosure mechanism. This agent harness is specifically optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling multiday, multistep scientific simulations in the absence of human intervention. Using OpenAI Codex as the agent provider, the capabilities of FermiLink are demonstrated across approximately 50 scientific software packages spanning nine research domains from chemistry to engineering. Systematic benchmarks on 132 real-world figure-level reproduction tasks with 44 packages show that FermiLink reproduces 74 (56.1%) of published figures with simulations, among which 30 (22.7%) achieve high-fidelity agreement and 35 reach qualitative agreement with the target figures. A smaller set of human expert-guided reproduction benchmarks with 10 packages in physics and chemistry further highlights the importance of expert insights for improving the simulation fidelity. Beyond reproduction, a single-blinded study demonstrates that FermiLink can produce research-grade results on unpublished polariton physics problems when provided with sufficiently detailed research objectives. Overall, FermiLink provides a scalable research infrastructure that may accelerate the path from scientific questions to computational results across diverse domains.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Experimental Verification of a ±10% Accurate 1‒Dimensional Output Resistance Model for Long Channel Silicon and SiC MOSFETs in Saturation Suitable for Hand Analysis in CMOS IC’s
items.abstract: Accurate (±5%) quantitative predictions for the output resistance of MOSFETs operating in their saturation region have long been associated with 2-dimensional (2D) modeling of electric fields near the drain junction. The complexities of such analytical and numerical models tend not only to hinder intuitive appreciation of the dominant effects determining the behavior of the output resistance, but to render them unsuitable for hand analysis, and even for efficient computer-aided design, as well. On the other hand, extant simplified 1-dimensional (1D) models approximating channel shortening by the length of the drain’s depletion region, (a) typically underestimate the output resistance by 50%, (b) fail to account for non-negligible dynamic range degradation, and (c) predict substrate voltage effects qualitatively opposite to observations. These shortcomings are suggestive of underlying conceptual wants. We elaborate a 1D model of the pinchoff region whose extent is determined by (i) an “internal” saturation voltage VDSAT corresponding to the limit of laminar flow, the objective criterion which obtains as the surface potential transitions from strong to weak inversion and, in view of current continuity, (ii) the inversion charge Qi injected into the pinchoff region. This concept, underpinned by physical considerations and guided by observations, yields a continuous drain-source conductance through the triode, transition, and pinchoff regions. We develop a simple expression for the saturation region’s incremental conductance whose dominant underlying effects conforming to the EKV model are explicit, and which is suitable for hand analysis and design of well-tempered contemporary circuits down to the limit of planar CMOS (about 20nm). Its accuracy, which is close to modern PSP-based models’, is within experimental and typical process parameter uncertainty (±10%) for silicon and silicon carbide MOSFETs, to whose characteristics we compare it critically.

items.title: Evaluating LLMs on Italian through multi-prompt: the Evalita-LLM benchmark
items.abstract: Abstract We present Evalita-LLM, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on Italian tasks. The key innovation of Evalita-LLM is the use of multiple prompts for each task, which mitigates the model’s sensitivity to specific prompt formulations and ensures a robust and objective performance assessment. We propose an iterative methodology for selecting and validating multiple prompts, and metrics that capture both high performance and stability of a prompt given a set of LLMs. The resulting Evalita-LLM multi-prompt benchmark is based on ten native Italian tasks, eliminating translation issues and potential cultural biases. It includes a mix of multiple-choice and generative tasks, enabling more natural interactions with LLMs. We report experimental results from the benchmark’s development phase, along with performance statistics for several state-of-the-art LLMs. Evalita-LLM is publicly available with a leaderboard hosted on Hugging Face to support transparent evaluation and comparison of LLMs.

items.title: Evaluating AI Alignment in LLMs: Output Analysis of Value Priorities Across 75 Models with Human Benchmarking
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in human-AI interaction research and practice, yet existing capability and safety benchmarks reveal little about the value priorities these systems express or how those priorities correspond to human judgements. Across three studies, we introduce an output-based approach to evaluating one facet of AI alignment by treating LLM-generated text as behavioural data and comparing expressed value-priority profiles with a human reference. Study 1 used inductive qualitative analysis to derive six themes of optimal AI functioning, namely Performance, Adaptive Capacity, Social Good, Ethics and Responsibility, Relational Integration, and Agency. Study 2 showed that LLM outputs were highly stable within models and converged on a common value-priority structure across models, indicating reliable and comparable value profiles. Study 3 benchmarked 75 contemporary LLMs against 376 human respondents using a profile-fidelity metric capturing both the relative ordering of priorities and the calibration of between-priority differences. Although most models reproduced the human ordering of values, some systematically exaggerated the differences between them, showing that models can appear aligned on conventional benchmarks while still diverging from human value calibration. Profile fidelity varied substantially across models and did not consistently scale with size, recency, or capability tier. Both LLMs and humans converged on a deprioritisation of Agency, raising important questions about the development of increasingly agentic AI systems. For research and applied use, the six themes and profile-based metric provide a scalable method for auditing LLM value profiles before deployment in contexts where alignment with human priorities is critical.

items.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. Over 10 years of continuous operation under the NEMA Power Index mission profile for variable-load centrifugal systems (pumps, fans), the CSC's higher part-load efficiency translates into a clearly lower life-cycle carbon footprint of around 900 kgCO2eq compared to the VSC's 1130 kgCO2eq when operating with a carbon-intense electricity mix (440 gCO2eq/kWh). However, this difference almost vanishes when considering a future renewable electricity mix (25 gCO2eq/kWh).

items.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
items.abstract: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1\% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

items.title: Empirical UVM 1.2 & Bare-Metal FPGA Verification Telemetry for the Q1.30 Sobolev Hardware Memory Engine (omega\_mollifier\_core)

We present a fixed-point SystemVerilog co-processor that computes analytical derivatives in one forward pass via discrete Sobolev-space Friedrichs mollification, achieving 264.0 ns FPGA latency, 91.25% memory compression, and 18.4 mW power. items.title: Editorial: Big data mining and artificial intelligence in earth science
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) for geoscience uses intelligent algorithms to extract concealed patterns from big Earth data, enabling more accurate predictions and decisions in scientific discoveries and applications, such as Earth's evolution, geological modeling, environmental monitoring, hazard mitigation, and resource exploration (Zhou et al., 2018(Zhou et al., , 2026)). Its evolution has followed a clear paradigm transition-from early expert systems through data-driven machine learning, to the current physics-informed, knowledge-data dual-driven approaches (Zhou et al., 2018;Zuo et al., 2023;Cheng et al., 2025). This progression is not merely incremental; it is fundamentally reshaping geoscience by integrating big data analytics with machine learning algorithms, and in doing so, redefining the practices of many researchers and engineers in their daily work (Zuo et al., 2023;Zhou et al., 2026). This is the reason why this special topic issue comes to exist here. It is devoted to showcase recent advances in the research and application of AI across many geoscience disciplines. It highlights innovative methodologies in data science, machine learning, and 2 / 14 generative AI technologies that address the integration and interpretation of multidisciplinary geoscientific data.The special issue is also initiated to commemorates the 10th anniversary of the Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences, established under the Chinese Society for Mineralogy, Petrology and Geochemistry in 2016, with Professor Zhou Yongzhang, then the awardee of the IAMG Felix Chayes Prize, as its inaugural Chair (Zhou et al., 2026). This marked the first organized effort in China to promote AI and big data research in mineralogy, petrology and geochemistry, and was among the earliest such professional bodies worldwide. In 2018, the committee published the textbook Big Data Mining and Machine Learning for Earth Science (Zhou et al., 2018). In April 2026, the 10th China Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Big Data for Geosciences was held at Hefei, drawing over 1,200 participants-a clear indicator of the rapidly growing interest in intelligent geoscience.Featuring 18 original contributions, this special issue focuses on three transformative areas: intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits, intelligent sedimentary and reservoir evaluation, and intelligent prediction of Earth processes and geological systems. The methods span from conventional machine learning to deep learning, knowledge graphs, large language models (LLMs), and beyond, reflecting both the breadth and depth of current AI-driven geoscience research.The intelligent prospecting of solid metal deposits is revolutionizing mineral exploration through the integration of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and advanced remote sensing. These technologies synthesize extensive geological, geophysical, and geochemical datasets to identify concealed mineralization patterns with exceptional precision. Predictive algorithms refine target selection, thereby reducing drilling costs and minimizing environmental footprint. Real-time fusion of drone and satellite imagery enables dynamic 3D modeling of subsurface structures. This intelligent approach not only accelerates discovery rates but also mitigates risks in structurally complex terrains. Ultimately, such systems empower geologists to make data-driven decisions, transforming traditional exploration into a sustainable, efficient, and scientifically rigorous pursuit for securing critical metal resources. This collection showcases recent advances in intelligent prospecting for solid metal deposits, underscoring a paradigm shift toward data-driven, multi-method integration. Wang et al. (2026) improve the interpretability of convolutional neural networks by applying SHAP and partial dependence plots, revealing apparent resistivity as the primary controlling factor in iron ore mapping. Their case study focuses on the Yemaquan iron ore concentration area in Qinghai Province, northwestern China, and successfully delineates several high-potential targets within the region. Zhao et al. (2026) employ LLMs to rapidly construct knowledge graphs for tungsten deposits, thereby enhancing reasoning capabilities and facilitating the extraction of prospecting indicators. Their study centres on methodological innovations for efficient knowledge graph construction in the mineral resource domain, proposing an LLM-driven framework guided by domain-specific geological knowledge. The framework is applied to a case study at the Dajishan Tungsten Mine in China. The results demonstrate that the LLM-integrated knowledge graph not only substantially accelerates the speed and scale of information integration but also enables deeper extraction of prospecting insights, highlighting its strong application potential. Zeng et al. (2026) apply co-simulation (Plurigaussian + turning bands) to jointly model grade and lithology, capturing spatial uncertainty in gold deposits. The method explicitly captures both auto-correlations and cross-correlations between variables, enabling realistic spatial reproduction of orebody geometry and internal heterogeneity. Results show that the outputting three-dimensional stochastic models effectively represent the spatial anisotropy and variability of mineralization, accurately delineating orebody continuity and its lithological controls. Shan et al. (2026) combine FLAC3D numerical simulation with machine learning, integrating chemical reactions and strain to predict gold targets. The study selects the Sanshandao-Haiyu gold belt as a case study to investigate the integrated application of these two approaches for deep mineral exploration, which remains poorly understood. First, chemical reactions are incorporated into FLAC3D via a custom-developed program to calculate the mineralization rate. Subsequently, the authors employ machine learning techniques to integrate simulation outcomes (i.e., volumetric strain and mineralization rate) with fault morphology in different combinations, constructing four predictive models for comparative validation. Based on the predictions, two prospective targets are delineated. Gao et al. (2026) propose a CPA attention mechanism for cross-regional knowledge graphs, achieving high F1-scores in complex entity extraction. This study proposes a novel knowledge graph construction and application framework centered on a Content-Position Attention (CPA) mechanism. The resulting knowledge graph system enables intelligent information retrieval, multi-dimensional correlation analysis, and mineralization potential prediction, demonstrating its practical effectiveness in supporting cross-regional resource management and intelligent decision-making. It offers a replicable technical pathway for knowledge management and decision analysis in the mineral resource domain.Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent systems-ranging from explainable deep learning and LLM-driven knowledge engineering to stochastic simulation and physics-informed machine learning-are making exploration more accurate, interpretable, and efficient, while addressing data heterogeneity and uncertainty in three-dimensional and cross-regional contexts.The intelligent evaluation of sedimentary reservoirs is revolutionizing hydrocarbon exploration through the integration of machine learning, deep learning, and automated seismic interpretation. These technologies synthesize multi-scale datasets-including well logs, core photographs, seismic attributes, and depositional analogs-to predict porosity, permeability, Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent approaches-encompassing unsupervised deep learning, hybrid inversion, semantic-guided simulation, and augmented experimental data-substantially enhance predictive accuracy, geological interpretability, and uncertainty quantification. They enable rapid, automated, and reproducible workflows that minimize subjective bias and computational overhead, while offering robust frameworks for reservoir characterization, dynamic management, and exploration in complex, data-scarce settings.Intelligent prediction of Earth systems and geological processes is revolutionizing geoscience by integrating multi-source data, physics-informed modeling, and advanced machine learning. Satellite remote sensing, ground-based geophysical surveys, and real-time sensor networks generate vast spatiotemporal datasets that, when processed by convolutional and recurrent neural networks, enable increasingly accurate forecasting of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, landslides, and surface deformation. Hybrid approaches that embed physical conservation laws into deep learning frameworks enhance generalization beyond purely statistical correlations, while uncertainty quantification through ensemble methods and Bayesian inference delivers robust risk assessments. For long-term geological evolution, generative models and digital twin simulations reconstruct paleoenvironments and project future changes in hydrology, erosion, and sediment transport under climate forcing. Automated pattern recognition in seismic waveforms, ground-penetrating radar, and borehole logs accelerates hazard mapping and resource characterization. These intelligent systems reduce subjective interpretation, enable near-real-time early warnings, and support sustainable land-use planning. By bridging observations, theory, and computation, they transform traditional qualitative geology into a quantitative, predictive, and adaptive science for mitigating natural risks and managing Earth's resources.In this collection, the intelligent prediction of Earth sciences and geological processes encompasses diverse applications-from groundwater and atmospheric CO₂ to reservoir characterization and rock mechanics-all unified by data-driven, hybrid, and interpretable methodologies. Li et al. (2026) Collectively, these studies demonstrate that intelligent prediction-via foundation models, bidirectional recurrent networks, physics-informed deep learning, ensemble algorithms, and optimized machine learning-strengthens accuracy, interpretability, and generalization under varied data constraints and across scales. They turn raw observations into actionable forecasts for resource management, carbon neutrality, geotechnical engineering, and hydrocarbon exploration, while prioritizing uncertainty quantification and feature importance analysis to build confidence and ensure practical relevance.Revealing prominent research frontiers and distinctive textures in AI for Geoscience, this special issue can serve as a valuable reference and the catalyst practitioners of data-intensive geoscience research. Nevertheless, we are aware that the papers do not comprehensively cover the entire field of AI in geoscience. Stepping back from a future vantage point, it is clear that many unresolved challenges remain, calling for persistent scientific investigation and innovation. Among them are included: Data heterogeneity and scarcity: Geoscientific data come from diverse sources (seismic, well logs, satellite, laboratory) with varying formats, resolutions, and quality. Many critical regions lack sufficient labeled samples, limiting the training of robust deep learning models and causing overfitting.Interpretability and trust: Deep learning models often act as "black boxes," making it difficult for geologists to validate predictions against physical principles. This hinders adoption in high-stakes decisions like drilling or hazard warning, where explainability is as important as accuracy (Zuo et al., 2023).Generalization across space and time: A model trained on one mineral deposit, basin, or geological setting frequently fails when applied to another due to differing tectonic histories, lithologies, or fluid properties. Transfer learning and domain adaptation remain open problems in geosciences.Computational and operational costs: Processing large-scale 3D/4D datasets (e.g., full-waveform inversion, climate simulations) demands massive computing resources.Real-time deployment in field operations is often impractical, and energy consumption raises sustainability concerns.As we look ahead, greater scientific attention should be directed toward the following issues, all of which are essential to advancing AI for geoscience (Zuo et al., 2023;Cheng et al., 2025;Zhou et al., 2026).Physics-informed and hybrid modeling: Embedding physical conservation laws (mass, momentum, energy) into neural networks will produce predictions that are both data-driven and physically consistent, reducing data dependence and improving extrapolation capabilities.Foundation models for Earth systems: Large pre-trained models based on multi-modal Earth data (imagery, time series, text) can be fine-tuned for diverse downstream tasks-from mineral mapping to earthquake forecasting-to offer a unified intelligence backbone for geoscience.Real-time digital twins: Integrating AI with continuous sensor streams and high-performance computing will enable dynamic digital replicas of subsurface reservoirs, volcanic systems, or coastal zones, supporting near-real-time hazard response and adaptive resource management.Human-AI collaboration and democratization: Future systems will prioritize interactive visual analytics and natural language interfaces, allowing geologists to query, question, and refine AI outputs. Open-source platforms and cloud-based toolkits will lower barriers, fostering global collaboration and equitable access to intelligent geoscience.

items.title: Echoes of Intelligence: What AI Could Learn From Bats
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid progress of deep learning has been driven in part by general principles of biological information processing, yet current AI systems still fall short of biological intelligence in critical ways such as integration of the computational and physical domains, i.e., embodied AI, and achieving autonomy in complex environments. This perspective argues that bat biosonar offers a particularly valuable model system for advancing embodied AI and autonomy in complex environments beyond the currently dominating vision‐centered and data‐intensive paradigms. Bats navigate dense and dynamic environments based on sparse trains of clutter echoes with random waveforms. These capabilities suggest alternative computational principles for perception and action: exploiting statistical rather than deterministic signal structure, extracting task‐relevant information from low‐bandwidth streams, and integrating morphology, actuation, and neural processing into closed‐loop embodied intelligence. This perspective reviews how bat biosonar differs from engineered sonar, identifies desirable capabilities that could inspire next‐generation autonomous systems, and outlines future research directions for deciphering and reproducing bat‐like intelligence through multimodal biological data, machine learning, neuromorphic processing, and biomimetic robotic platforms. By framing bat biosonar as a model for dynamic embodied intelligence, this perspective highlights a path toward AI systems that are more robust, parsimonious, and highly capable in real‐world environments.

items.title: Design of an ultra low voltage VDBA using bulk driven quasi floating gate techniques for high order biosignal processing
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a high-performance ultra-low-voltage (ULV) voltage differencing buffered amplifier (VDBA) operating from a 0.5-V supply. Consisting of an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) followed by a voltage follower (VF), the proposed VDBA combines bulk-driven (BD) and bulk-driven quasi-floating-gate (BD-QFG) MOS techniques to overcome threshold-voltage limitations and enhance the performance of subthreshold circuits. Designed in the Cadence Virtuoso environment using the TSMC 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed VDBA consumes only 370 nW and occupies 0.022 mm 2 area. Its applicability is demonstrated through a fifth-order Butterworth low-pass filter for ECG signals, achieving an electronically tunable cutoff frequency from 73.65 to 557.8 Hz, 1.1% THD for a $$\:100{\text{}\text{mV}}_{\text{p-p}}$$ input signal, and a 44 dB dynamic range. Monte Carlo and PVT analyses confirm the robustness of the proposed design, while experimental implementation using the commercially available LM13700 further validates the proposed filtering approach.

items.title: Design of an X-Band 50-W, 12-Way GaN HEMT Power Amplifier Using an Integrated FET Process
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and measurement of a 50W-class GaN HEMT power amplifier for X-band radar and satellite communication systems. To overcome single-device output limitations and achieve high integration, a 12-way parallel combining structure based on an Integrated FET process was proposed. The amplifier features integrated 4-way and 12-way divider/combiner stages within the chip to minimize loss. Phase and amplitude imbalances were resolved, achieving <0.4 dB amplitude error and <1° phase error. Alumina and Taconic RF-35 substrates were used for the RF and bias circuits, respectively, to ensure stable DC supply and high isolation. Evaluated at 10 GHz with a 25 us pulse width and 10% duty cycle, the fabricated amplifier demonstrated 47.78 dBm (approx. 60 W) output power, 44.11% PAE, 16.72 dB small-signal gain, and 12.76 dB large-signal gain, satisfying all design goals. This topology is applicable to next-generation high-power RF systems.
items.venue: The Transactions of The Korean Institute of Electrical Engineers

items.title: Design and Performance Analysis of Novel Single-Fin Core Shell Junctionless FinFET (CS-JL-FinFET)
items.abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling of conventional field-effect transistors intensifies short-channel effects, leakage current, degraded electrostatic control and mobility-related limitations, motivating the development of alternative device architectures with improved carrier transport and gate controllability. In this work, a single-fin core-shell junctionless FinFET (CS-JL-FinFET) is proposed using three-dimensional technology computer-aided design simulations. The proposed device employs core-shell doping to modify the internal electrostatic potential, carrier distribution and gate-to-channel coupling while retaining the junctionless operating principle. A conventional single-fin JL-FinFET with identical fundamental dimensions, material system, gate work function, bias conditions and simulation methodology is employed. The electrostatic and transport characteristics are evaluated through transfer and output characteristics, potential and electric-field distributions, transconductance, output conductance, capacitance, temperature-dependent behavior, intrinsic gain, Early voltage and circuit-level inverter operation. At the nominal operating condition, the proposed CS-JL-FinFET achieves an ON-state current of \(\:{10}^{-5}\)A/µm and an OFF-state current of \(\:{10}^{-16}\)A/µm, resulting in an \(\:{I}_{on}/{I}_{off}\:\)ratio of \(\:{10}^{11}\), compared with \(\:{10}^{10}\)for the conventional JL-FinFET. The proposed device also shows a subthreshold slope of 64 mV/dec, compared with 82.7 mV/dec for conventional JL-FinFET while the peak transconductance is reported to improve by 60-67%. The enhanced current modulation by increased output conductance, resulting in lower output resistance, intrinsic gain and Early voltage than the conventional device. Resistive-load inverter shows successful voltage inversion with a 0-0.5 V input swing. These results establish core-shell doping engineering as a promising approach for enhancing the current-driving and switching characteristics of nanoscale junctionless FinFET.

items.title: Crack–Defect Landscapes Enable Multimodal Memristive Switching in WS 2 Mono‐Bilayers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT While nano or micro cracks are often unavoidable during the scalable growth of 2D materials, their role and interactions with vacancies in facilitating variable memristive switching are generally overlooked in device applications. Addressing device‐to‐device and cyclic variability in 2D memristor demands a mechanistic understanding of vacancy dynamics and their conduction pathways. We unveil how point defects and intergranular cracks modulate dynamic memristor behavior in mono‐bilayer WS 2 lateral devices associated with varied sulfur vacancy concentrations, ranging from nearly pristine to ∼10 14 cm −2 , as confirmed by aberration‐corrected electron microscopic and spectroscopic investigations. The crack boundaries act as preferential sites for vacancy migration and charged species, facilitating resistive switching in polycrystalline like WS 2 mono‐bilayers. The observed conductance switching originate from Schottky barrier modulation at the WS 2 metal interface and the redistribution of vacancies within the channel. To enhance the device performance, controlled thermal annealing in distinct environments has been performed. The devices exhibited distinguishable switching for 800 cycles with consistent resistance ratios followed by onset of toggling state and later collapsing to trap state. These findings establish a direct correlation between atomic‐scale defects and memristive performance, providing fundamental insights into vacancy–crack interactions that govern charge transport and stability in 2D materials.

items.title: Compact convolutional neural networks for AI-based drone detection system
items.abstract: The increasing use of first-person-view drones in modern conflicts has created a demand for compact and reliable detection systems capable of operating in complex electromagnetic environments. These drones continuously transmit video signals through onboard video transmitters, generating radio-frequency emissions that can be exploited for early detection. This study investigates the use of lightweight convolutional neural networks for automated detection of drone signals captured by a software-defined radio-based electronic warfare framework. Samples are converted into rasterized time-domain images, providing a computationally efficient input representation suitable for embedded systems. Several custom model architectures were designed and benchmarked in terms of accuracy, model size, and inference performance using a dataset containing approximately 40,000 labeled images. In addition to offline testing, the models were integrated into a GNU Radio signal processing chain for real-time evaluation. Under the evaluated conditions, the compact models achieved high detection accuracy while maintaining small model size and low inference latency, supporting the feasibility of embedded radio-frequency monitoring.

items.title: Comment on “Self-organizing neuromorphic nanowire networks as stochastic dynamical systems"
items.abstract: Self-assembled networks of nano-objects have attracted growing interest as physical substrates for brain-inspired computation. The work of Milano et al. 1 is a valuable study of the dynamics of memristive networks of nanowires. The experimental data presented by the authors are comprehensive and of high quality, providing extensive material for validating stochastic conductance models in such systems. The compact Markovian model proposed in ref. 1 , formulated as a stochastic differential equation of the Itô type that combines deterministic return to equilibrium with random components (Gaussian noise and jumps), allows for the description of certain aspects of the dynamics and an assessment of the impact of stochasticity on computational capabilities within the reservoir computing paradigm. However, closer examination of the data from ref. 1 reveals that each key aspect of the conductance dynamics (deterministic relaxation, jump process, and Gaussian fluctuations) exhibits non-Markovian properties, which calls into question the original stochastic model and suggests a need for its fundamental revision.

items.title: Beyond the Syntax: Do Security Experts Trust LLMs for NIDS Rule Engineering?
items.abstract: As network threats evolve, manual Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) rule engineering has become a critical operational bottleneck. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for automating this process, their ability to produce production-ready rules remains unvalidated. This paper presents a human-centered investigation into LLM-based NIDS rule engineering, formalizing a context-aware generation framework and evaluating it through an exploratory user study with 10 domain experts. Our evaluation reveals a syntax-semantics paradox: although LLMs generate syntactically correct rules, experts find them only partially practically useful due to low specificity and logic hallucinations in 12% of cases. While the system received a favorable SUS score of 67, practitioners remain skeptical of its autonomous capabilities, viewing LLMs as support tools for drafting and verification rather than independent generators. Finally, our statistical analysis indicates that while large-scale models (≥ 70B) consistently produce syntactically valid rules, small models (≤ 4B) are largely ineffective for IDS rule generation.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: Balancing Performance and Energy Efficiency: A Comparative Review of Near-Data Processing, Heterogeneous Cores, Persistent Memory Controllers, and Chiplet-Based Disaggregated Memory
items.abstract: Computers keep getting faster, but moving data between memory and the processor can now cost more time and energy than the computation itself. This paper presents a comparative review of four architectural directions that try to deal with this problem: near-data processing (NDP), heterogeneous core integration, persistent memory controllers, and chiplet-based disaggregated memory. NDP moves part of the work to where the data already sits, so fewer transfers are needed. Heterogeneous processors mix fast cores with frugal ones and give each task to whichever suits it better. Persistent memory controllers manage memory that keeps its contents without power, so they have to balance durability, write endurance, and latency. Chiplet and disaggregated designs break a system into smaller pieces that can be scaled separately, but they bring interconnect delays, coherence problems, and harder software management. Recent survey literature was reviewed and compared in terms of performance, energy efficiency, scalability, reliability, programmability, and cost. The review finds that no single approach wins on every workload. NDP fits data-heavy tasks built from simple operations, heterogeneous cores fit mixed workloads, persistent memory fits applications that need durable state, and chiplets fit systems that have to grow in flexible ways. The most promising path is to combine them through coordinated hardware and software design and to measure energy at the whole-system level. Gaps remain in shared benchmarks, workload-aware scheduling, and cross-layer evaluation.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Atomistic understanding of hybrid bonding in Cu interfaces using multiscale microscopy
items.abstract: Achieving wafer-scale reliability in Cu–Cu hybrid bonding remains challenging due to process-induced non-uniformities and the limited understanding of buried interfacial contamination. Here, we employ a correlative multiscale microscopy framework combining scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom probe tomography (APT) to investigate bond degradation from the wafer center to the edge. We observe progressive bond deterioration characterized by interfacial delamination, reduced Cu grain size, and the formation of a nanometer-scale amorphous interlayer. While such interlayers have been widely observed in hybrid bonding, their chemical nature has remained largely unresolved. APT directly reveals that the interlayer consists of Si-, C-, and N-bearing species consistent with contributions from the adjacent SiCN dielectric, together with Cu oxide and organic-related contaminants. By correlating interlayer chemistry and thickness with microstructural evolution, we establish a direct link between interfacial contamination, suppressed cross-interface grain growth, and bond degradation. Furthermore, we observe a progressive thickness-dependent degradation, where interfacial thickening from ∼1 to 2 nm at the center to ∼2 to 3 nm in the donut region is accompanied by deterioration in mechanical bond integrity and localized delamination. These findings provide atomistic insight into the chemistry governing hybrid bond reliability and establish quantitative guidelines for process optimization toward wafer-scale integration.

items.title: Applications of Directed Self-Assembly Lithography in Advanced Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: As semiconductor devices continue to scale down, conventional lithography technologies face increasingly severe challenges in resolution, stochastic defect control, and manufacturing cost. Block copolymer (BCP) directed self-assembly (DSA), which offers molecular-scale control over pattern formation and compatibility with existing lithographic processes, has emerged as a promising complementary nanopatterning technology for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. This review summarizes the microphase-separation mechanisms of DSA, major guiding strategies including graphoepitaxy and chemoepitaxy, and pattern-transfer techniques such as dry and wet etching and sequential infiltration synthesis (SIS). In terms of device applications, particular emphasis is placed on recent progress in DSA for Fin Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) fin patterning, silicon nanostructures, high-density contact holes, memory devices, two-dimensional semiconductors, and Complementary Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor (CMOS) optoelectronic devices. Key challenges, including defect control, process-window optimization, pattern transfer, and wafer-scale manufacturing, are further discussed, together with future directions involving the integration of DSA with extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, advanced etching, and data-driven process optimization. This review aims to outline the technological evolution of DSA from nanoscale self-assembly toward integration into advanced semiconductor manufacturing and to provide a reference for high-resolution patterning at advanced technology nodes.

items.title: A thermodynamic and phase-field framework for domain nucleation and polarization switching in Al1− x Sc x N
items.abstract: Uniaxial wurtzite ferroelectrics have emerged as promising candidates for non-volatile memory applications; however, their large coercive fields remain a major challenge for device operation. Reducing the coercive field requires a fundamental understanding of the role of domain nucleation during polarization reversal, where polarization discontinuities at the domain walls are expected to strongly modify the nucleation energy barrier. Here, we develop a thermodynamic framework for inversion domain nucleation and polarization switching by combining classical nucleation theory with phase-field simulations. Using Al0.7Sc0.3N as a representative system, we demonstrate that the polarization discontinuity associated with inclined domain walls produces large local electrostatic potentials and electric fields, leading to high energy barriers for nucleation and highly anisotropic nucleation morphology. By explicitly incorporating electrostatic interactions among ionized dopants, electronic carriers, and bound charges arising from polarization discontinuities at domain walls, we find that the availability of free electronic carriers reduces the energy barrier for nucleation and brings the predicted coercive field closer to experimentally observed values and below dielectric breakdown limits. By explicitly incorporating the nucleation process, phase-field simulations capture the electric-field-driven evolution of domain nucleation and growth, enabling quantitative investigation of switching kinetics, providing a powerful approach for understanding and predicting polarization-switching behavior and long-term reliability in ferroelectric memory devices.

items.title: A plane bipartite graph whose only Fries structure is not a Clar structure
items.abstract: A plane bipartite graph whose only Fries structure is not a Clar structure. A perfect matching of a plane bipartite graph makes a bounded face alternating when the face's boundary edges alternate between matched and unmatched; the Fries number is the most alternating faces in one perfect matching, and the Clar number the most pairwise vertex-disjoint alternating faces in one perfect matching. Bérczi-Kovács and Frank (Discrete Mathematics, 2024) write that the conjecture that a plane graph has a largest Clar set extending to a largest Fries set is still open for general perfectly matchable bipartite plane graphs. This record gives a counterexample: an 11-square polyomino (two vertical bars of four squares joined by a horizontal bar of five) with 116 perfect matchings, Fries number 8 reached by exactly one perfect matching whose alternating squares contain at most 4 pairwise disjoint ones, and Clar number 5. check_fries_clar.py verifies this by listing every perfect matching. Claude (Anthropic), a large language model, assisted this work under my direction: it wrote and ran the search and checking code, checked the results and the literature, and assisted with the writing throughout; the text is my own and I take full responsibility for it.
