items.title: A data-efficient PINN-Bayesian optimization framework for state variable active filter design
items.abstract: Designing an analog active filter is rarely a single-target exercise: cutoff frequency, quality factor, gain, power draw, total harmonic distortion (THD), and sensitivity to component spread all have to be pulled into line at once. In practice, this still means loop after loop of SPICE runs and manual tweaking, which eats up design time and computing budget alike. This paper instead builds a Bayesian Optimization loop around a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate to automate the synthesis of State Variable Filters (SVFs). Adaptive sampling of the design space, LTspice-based circuit simulation, PINN surrogate modeling, and Bayesian Optimization are brought together so that optimal component values can be located with far fewer costly simulation runs. By incorporating the governing circuit relationships, analytical transfer function, frequency–response characteristics, and stability constraints into PINN training, the proposed surrogate captures the nonlinear relationship between component values and filter performance while maintaining physical consistency. That trained surrogate then drives the Bayesian search, quickly narrowing in on Pareto-optimal filter configurations across cutoff frequency accuracy, passband gain, quality factor, power consumption, THD, and sensitivity. The resulting design reached a cutoff frequency of 10.01 kHz, a gain of 0.998, a quality factor of 0.709, an estimated active-filter power of 12.4 mW, THD of 0.32%, and a sensitivity index of 0.048, with Bayesian Optimization converging in 37 iterations and an average run time of 42.8 s. Benchmarked against Random Search, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Differential Evolution, the proposed framework consistently reached lower objective values than any of them. A TL084-based hardware prototype backed up the simulation results as well: measured cutoff frequency, gain, and phase response tracked the LTspice predictions closely, and the absolute THD deviation came in at just 0.04%. Taken together, these results point to a PINN-assisted Bayesian Optimization framework that is efficient, scalable, and well suited to next-generation computer-aided design of analog and mixed-signal circuits.

items.title: A Study on the Design and Control of a 6.6-kW Three-Phase Interleaved Totem-Pole PFC for OBC Applications
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, control, and experimental verification of a 6.6-kW three-phase interleaved Totem-Pole power factor correction (PFC) converter for on-board charger (OBC) applications. Three parallel PFC phases are operated with PWM carrier phase shifts of 0°, 120°, and 240° to distribute the input current and reduce the synthesized input-current ripple. SiC MOSFETs are employed for high-frequency switching operation. A digital control system consisting of output-voltage and input-current control loops, a Second-Order Generalized Integrator Phase-Locked Loop (SOGI-PLL), a notch filter, and duty feed-forward was implemented for stable DC-link voltage regulation and input-current control. A 6.6-kW prototype operating with a 220-Vrms input and a 400 V DC-link voltage was developed. Compared with the two-phase interleaved configuration under the same Boost inductance and switching frequency conditions, the three-phase interleaved configuration reduced the maximum input-current ripple from 3.4 A to 2.28 A, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 32.9%, while increasing the ripple frequency from 140 kHz to 210 kHz. The threephase interleaved configuration exhibited an input-current THD up to 3.871 percentage points lower than that of the two-phase configuration while maintaining a comparable power factor. At rated load, the developed converter achieved an input-current THD of 5.438%, a power factor of 0.996, and an efficiency of 97.978%.

items.title: A Non‐Volatile Heterogeneous Quantum Dot III‐V/Si DFB Laser With Optical Memristive Behavior
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, we introduce a non‐volatile heterogeneous quantum dot (QD) III‐V/Al 2 O 3 /Si distributed feedback (DFB) laser exhibiting optical memristive behavior. The device operates in the O‐band (∼1300 nm) with a threshold current density of 234 A/cm 2 and a side‐mode suppression ratio exceeding 48 dB. Co‐integrated Al 2 O 3 ‐based memristors produce bipolar resistive switching, yielding non‐volatile wavelength shifts of ∼46 pm and ∼ 17 dB peak power contrast with zero static holding power. The III‐V/Al 2 O 3 /Si heterojunction memristor I – V hysteresis is also modeled. This new device enables simultaneous coherent light generation and persistent optical state storage, establishing a new class of active photonic memory for neuromorphic and reconfigurable wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) applications.

items.title: A Flexible Complementary Memristive Synapse for Convolutional Neural Network Applications
items.abstract: Abstract The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.

items.title: A Deep Digital Multilayer Processor Architecture with Projection-Enforced Manifold Admissibility
items.abstract: Fully Digital Implementation: The architecture shifts from analog memristive crossbars to standard-cell digital CMOS logic, eliminating analog thermal drift, write-endurance wear, and process-voltage-temperature variations while ensuring strict bit-level determinism. Low-Rank Factorized Projection: By projecting input vectors onto the ten-dimensional physical symmetry manifold using a two-stage matrix decomposition, the processor slashes multiplier logic by over forty times compared to full dense evaluation while maintaining single-cycle execution. Synchronous Digital Shunt-on-Error: A parallel subtraction tree continuously calculates the geometric distance between the current state and the admissible manifold, instantly clearing the pipeline and suppressing invalid data if noise or corruption exceeds the safety threshold. Exact Integer Arithmetic Unit: Floating-point units are completely replaced by dual-integer datapaths operating over an algebraic integer ring, using hardwired shift-and-add logic to execute exact complex algebra with zero mantissa rounding, no denormal stalls, and zero numerical drift over arbitrary run lengths. Multilayer Associative Memory: High-speed on-chip spline lookup tables combined with a high-order polynomial associative memory engine trap computational states into discrete topological basins, storing hundreds of millions of distinct patterns without crosstalk or hallucination. Bufferless Direct Interconnect: Processing nodes communicate across an eight-hundred-sixty-one lane direct static mesh with eighty dedicated connections per node, achieving an aggregate throughput exceeding twenty-seven terabits per second with zero packet collision, no arbitration logic, and identical median and tail latencies. Symmetrical Phase Clocking: Die-wide timing is locked across seventy-two discrete sectors via a circulating shift-register ring and balanced distribution tree, suppressing phase jitter and eliminating clock skew across large silicon areas. Silicon Profile: Designed for modern four-nanometer fabrication, a monolithic core integrates roughly forty million standard gates onto an area of approximately eleven square millimeters, operating at eighteen watts under standard cooling solutions.

items.title: simantalahkar/lammpskit: LAMMPSKit v1.2.1
items.abstract: LAMMPSKit v1.2.1 LAMMPSKit is a Python toolkit for post-processing and analysing molecular-dynamics simulations run with LAMMPS. It was built for simulations of HfTaO-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) devices. It tracks how conductive filaments form and evolve, analyses atomic, charge and displacement distributions, and produces publication-ready plots. This release is an archived snapshot of the code as of 29 July 2025, tagged v1.2.1. It is the version that matches the published PyPI package and Docker image below. What the package does Filament analysis: OVITO-based cluster analysis that tracks filament connectivity, gap, size and height over time (lammpskit.ecellmodel.filament_layer_analysis). Distributions: atomic, charge and displacement distributions by element and position (lammpskit.ecellmodel.data_processing). Trajectory input: readers for LAMMPS trajectory and displacement files (lammpskit.io), with input validation and descriptive error messages (lammpskit.config). Designed for large trajectories (more than 1M atoms, more than 10K frames). Plotting: publication-ready time-series and comparison plots with central control of fonts and styles (lammpskit.plotting). Example workflow: usage/ecellmodel/run_analysis.py runs four analyses: filament evolution, displacement by species, charge distribution and atomic distribution under different voltages. Changes in v1.2.1 (since v1.2.0) Improved the reliability of the GitHub Actions status and coverage badges, and added automated coverage-badge generation to the CI pipeline. Added a fail-safe Codecov upload that runs on Python 3.12 only, to avoid duplicate uploads. Fixed the tests badge so it points to the docker-ci.yml workflow. Updated version references across the documentation and configuration files. No change to the analysis, I/O or plotting code is recorded for this release; see CHANGELOG.md for the full history, including 1.0.0 (modular restructuring, timeseries plotting module, configuration system, extended test suite with visual regression tests). Install and run PyPI: pip install lammpskit==1.2.1 (requires Python 3.12 or later; NumPy, Matplotlib and OVITO 3.12.4 or later) Docker: docker pull simantalahkar/lammpskit:1.2.1 Documentation: https://lammpskit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ Citation If you use LAMMPSKit in your research, please cite the paper that describes the simulations it was built for: S. Lahkar et al., Decoupling Electric Field and Temperature-Driven Atomistic Forming Mechanisms in TaOx/HfO2-Based ReRAMs using Reactive Molecular Dynamics Simulations, arXiv:2505.24468 (2025), https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2505.24468 To cite this exact software version, use the DOI that Zenodo assigns to this release. Related software The simulations analysed with LAMMPSKit were run with the integrated CTIP–EChemDID package for LAMMPS: https://github.com/simantalahkar/LAMMPS-CTIP-EChemDID Licence GPL-3.0-or-later. Author: Simanta Lahkar.

items.title: Xenosophy: preregistrations of the next phase
items.abstract: Preregistration of the test of generation announced in "Xenosophy: Asking About Contact When No Common Frame Is Guaranteed" (version 0.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23816129). The test asks whether the approach's procedures of variation, applied to its distinctions, lead an AI analyst to hypotheses about a published study's object that AI judges rate as testable and absent from the field more often than hypotheses given under a plain instruction to be bold, or under a generic list of heuristics. A further arm tests the practice of the author's laboratory as a whole, reported as a black box, against the plain instruction. The cases are drawn from listed pools by euro reference rates published after this record is made public. The document fixes the design, the rules of scoring and what counts against the approach before any case is drawn; it may add conditions to those of the announcement, never weaken them. Use of AI. The design and every decision in it are the author's. The document was drafted under the author's decisions by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), which also compiled the pools, compiles one of the lists of the field record and takes part in the tally; it is not independent of the test. The test uses AI systems as analysts (ChatGPT; Claude Opus 5.5), judges (GLM, Qwen; Gemini in reserve), the source of a control and a parallel tallier (DeepSeek), a compiler of the field record (Perplexity), and a tallier used only if the tallies diverge (Kimi). No AI system is an author or contributor.

items.title: When Is High-Bandwidth Flash Cost-Effective for LLM Inference?
items.abstract: Can high-bandwidth flash (HBF) make LLM inference cheaper than adding GPUs? By storing weights closer to the GPU than SSD, HBF may reduce the number of GPUs needed for model capacity. However, this integration is only justified if it meets service targets and its cost is recovered. We simulate this integration using public component data across nine dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, five workloads, two GPU platforms, and 1--100 GPUs. At fixed demand, HBF reduces the minimum GPU count to meet a service target in 98 of 468 comparisons; majority of them are paused and short sessions, 63 remain cost-effective at half a GPU price per HBF stack. For single short-chat users, HBF enables large MoEs, e.g. DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2, to meet a relaxed service target on one RTX~4090 GPU, where conventional serving fails. At fixed GPU count, HBF improves throughput in 48\% of matched comparisons below 16 GPUs and 13\% at larger counts. Even at 100 RTX~4090-scale GPUs, cascaded HBF raises offline throughput by 16.4--26.5$\times$ for three large MoEs. We found savings and throughput gains arise in different scenarios.

items.title: Vertical GaN Trench MOSFET‐Based Devices for Multifunctional Optoelectronic Logic Gates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of optoelectronic technology has highlighted the potential of optoelectronic hybrid logic circuits in low‐power logic circuits. While two‐dimensional (2D) materials are commonly used in traditional optoelectronics, challenges remain in device stability, mass production, and integration efficiency with existing semiconductor technologies. To meet the demand for high‐performance materials in optoelectronic logic gates (OELGs), this study develops GaN‐based OELGs with high responsivity and low power consumption, aiming to overcome limitations of conventional devices and address future optoelectronic integrated system requirements. Through optimization strategies including trench etching, damage repair and vertical structural design, the developed GaN MOSFETs demonstrate exceptional performance: a responsivity ( R ) of 2.1 × 10 4 A/W, a photo‐to‐dark current ratio (PDCR) exceeding 10 7 , and rapid response speeds ( τ rise / τ fall of 2.0 ms/1.1 ms). The optical communication module validates their feasibility in communication transmission, providing crucial experimental evidence for optoelectronic logic gate research. The successfully developed OELGs operate stably under basic logic states, confirming their viability in next‐generation photonic logic computing circuits. This work demonstrates a proof‐of‐concept GaN trench MOSFET platform for optoelectronic logic operations. It exhibits photogain with millisecond‐scale response and a clear gain–speed trade‐off, showing promising potential for photonic logic circuits and ultraviolet optical signal processing.

items.title: Verify Before You Fetch: Reliable KV Cache Compression for LLM Inference
items.abstract: Long-context applications, long-lived agents, and multi-agent systems require large language models (LLMs) to process and retain extensive information. In these settings, the KV cache can exceed GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity, necessitating offloading to host memory, where CPU-to-GPU transfers can dominate inference latency. While KV cache compression can reduce data movement, query-agnostic compression that guarantees accurate attention for arbitrary queries is extremely challenging, if not impossible. We introduce VerKV, a hybrid approach that provides $(ε, δ)$ guarantees for approximating attention on any given query. VerKV maintains a compact set of query-agnostic pivotal tokens on the GPU, together with a token-level sketch of the full KV cache, while retaining the complete cache in CPU memory. We introduce a novel stochastic sampling procedure, PoissonComp, to select the pivotal tokens. At inference time, our proposed KVFetch algorithm uses the pivotal tokens and the sketch to estimate the relative error of the resulting attention computation. If the estimate satisfies a user-specified $(ε, δ)$ tolerance, inference proceeds without accessing host memory. Otherwise, VerKV performs query-aware retrieval to fetch additional tokens from the CPU, refining the attention computation to meet the required tolerance. Thus, VerKV enables attention with bounded approximation error while minimizing CPU-to-GPU transfers. We show that PoissonComp outperforms state-of-the-art approaches to KV cache compression. Combined with KVFetch, it achieves near-dense performance (90-100% of dense quality at 32K context length, averaged over RULER and LOFT), using Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B and Ministral-3-8B, while reducing the GPU memory footprint by 8-32x and keeping CPU-to-GPU memory fetches within 2-23% of the cache per generated token, depending on the model.

items.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization
items.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces large language model (LLM) deployment costs, but preserving quality requires accounting for uneven weight sensitivity. Uniform PTQ uses one weight bit-width, importance-aware PTQ adjusts scales or reconstructs weights within that width, and column-wise mixed precision retains selected columns at higher precision. However, sensitivity varies within columns, so whole-column retention also protects less sensitive weights, while runtime outlier detection adds decoding overhead. We therefore introduce TileQuant, a training-free framework that assigns precision to hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles. Offline calibration provides input-activation-aware scoring from forward statistics for lower calibration cost and gradient-informed scoring from loss sensitivity for stronger quality preservation. Within each projection's retention budget, the highest-scoring tiles remain at 16-bit and the rest use 8-bit. The resulting map guides reconstruction into compact weight buffers, which the kernel reuses for native integer and 16-bit computation with local accumulation to reduce memory traffic. Experiments show that TileQuant reaches 2.66x the original model's generation throughput. Across language modeling, reasoning, long-context retrieval, and question answering, it preserves quality and surpasses quantized and original models on multiple tasks. These results support selecting precision units that capture local sensitivity while enabling efficient hardware execution. The implementation is: https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileQuant

items.title: Three tiers of indeterminacy: the exact hull at small places and the container of Step (v) of IUT IV
items.abstract: In Step (v) of the proof of inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT) IV, Theorem 1.10, the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of the Θ-pilot object is bounded by a container that contains the region pλ·(RI)∼; the indeterminacies (Ind1) and (Ind2) are accounted for by the arbitrary automorphisms φ of IUT IV, Proposition 1.2, and (Ind3) by taking upper bounds. At places that are small in the sense of Proposition 1.2(iii) (p odd and every ramification index at most p − 2), this note compares the container with the hulls reached by four classes of maps: unit scalars and field automorphisms; the maps induced factor by factor by the actual (Ind1) and (Ind2); all factorwise automorphisms of the log-shells; and all automorphisms φ of Proposition 1.2. For the last two classes the hull is exactly p⌈λ⌉−𝔡I·(RI)∼, where 𝔡I is the sum of the orders of the differents, whereas the container of Step (v) has hull p⌊λ⌋−𝔡I·(RI)∼. So when λ is not an integer, which is always the case at bad places, the container is larger than anything these automorphisms reach by exactly a factor p (log p in log-volume). The difference comes from the proof of Proposition 1.2(ii), which uses Proposition 1.1 with the different of every factor; Proposition 1.1 applied to the factor that carries pλ removes it. Unit scalars and field automorphisms do not enlarge the hull; the actual (Ind1), (Ind2) reach the exact value when λ is an integer, provided that automorphisms of the local Galois groups carry a unit to the boundary of the log-shell, which at small places reduces to one condition on the transvections of Hoshi–Nishio and Kondo. The difference is a term of conductor type and does not change the shape of the inequality of IUT IV. An example at a bad place of an explicit initial Θ-datum is computed. The note credits the earlier statements it builds on: IUT IV, Proposition 1.1, is stated with a free choice of the factor that does not pay its different; Dupuy and Hilado choose the factor that makes the inclusion tightest (arXiv:2004.13108); the public repository lana-agents/iut of Project LANA states that for λ = 0 the hull is exactly the container of IUT IV; Mochizuki states that automorphisms of the log-shells give only bounded discrepancies. It is the local, numerical counterpart of the author's note Where Theorem 3.11 sits, whose Theorem 22 uses only an upper bound for the same quantity. No claim is made about the truth of Corollary 3.12 of IUT III or of the abc conjecture. The proofs are on paper and the computations are exact; versions of the statements about the actual indeterminacies were also checked in Lean 4 in a development of the author that is not part of this deposit, and the proofs do not rely on it. The comparison studied here arose in the author's discussions with generative AI tools, and the author decided to make it the subject of this note. The proofs were found with generative AI tools (large language models) under the author's direction, and these tools were also used for the computations, the formalization, the literature search and the writing. The author's own reading of the proofs is still in progress. The author takes full responsibility for the note. The deposit contains the note and an archive of the folder three-tiers/ (LaTeX source, Python scripts and their outputs), made from tag v0.25.0 of github.com/turahigashi/iut-explicit-initial-theta.

items.title: Silane coupling agent for semiconductor manufacturing
items.abstract: Silane coupling agents (SCAs) have evolved from conventional adhesion promoters into multifunctional interfacial materials essential for semiconductor packaging reliability. As device miniaturization, heterogeneous integration, and advanced packaging technologies intensify interfacial challenges, SCAs increasingly contribute to moisture resistance, stress mitigation, electrical performance, and thermal stability. This review examines six decades of SCA development, from composite reinforcement to applications in 2.5D/3D integration, fan‐out packaging, and high‐frequency electronics. Interfacial bonding mechanisms, deposition methods, characterization techniques, and reliability considerations are systematically discussed within front‐end‐of‐line (FEOL) and back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL) processes. Conventional organosilanes, including APTES and GLYMO, are compared with emerging alternatives such as dipodal silanes, cyclic azasilanes, phosphonic acids, imidazole‐based primers, and self‐healing and bio‐derived silanes. Key scientific debates concerning interphase architecture, molecular chain length, hydrolytic stability, and amine orientation are critically evaluated. Advances in vapor‐phase deposition, molecular layer deposition, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning are highlighted, particularly emerging relationships between amine protonation states and highly accelerated stress test (HAST) reliability. Remaining challenges include high‐frequency dielectric compatibility and discrepancies between laboratory measurements and actual packaging conditions. Future advances will require precise molecular‐level engineering of interfacial architectures rather than developing generic coupling agents to satisfy increasingly demanding semiconductor reliability requirements.

items.title: SILICON VERSUS CARBON The Great Computational Confrontation Between Artificial Intelligence and the Human Brain A Comprehensive Scientific Treatise on the Architecture, Efficiency, and Future of Intelligence
items.abstract: "SILICON VERSUS CARBON" dissects the computational confrontation between artificial intelligence and the human brain, revealing a fundamental efficiency chasm. While AI systems consume megawatts across sprawling data centers, the brain operates on merely 20 watts. The true miracle lies at the operational level: biological synapses cost approximately one femtojoule (10^-15 J) per operation, while modern GPUs consume roughly one nanojoule (10^-9 J)—a million-fold efficiency gap that no amount of Moore's Law scaling can bridge. The treatise dismantles the "brute force" paradigm through three critical arguments. First, it exposes the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture as a crude digital approximation of biological sparsity, lacking the analog, asynchronous efficiency of ion-channel activation. Second, it invokes Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and the Phi (Φ) measure to demonstrate that current von Neumann architectures exhibit near-zero integrated information due to their modular, feed-forward design, suggesting true consciousness requires the dense, recurrent connectivity unique to carbon-based brains. Third, it positions neuromorphic computing—merging memory and processing on unified chips—as the only viable path toward twenty-watt efficiency. The verdict is absolute: silicon simulates intelligence through astronomical energy consumption; carbon embodies it through thermodynamic elegance. The future of computing lies not in scaling brute force, but in bio-inspired architectures that honor the physics of biological computation.

items.title: Project Proteus: One Nitride, Three Forms, Three Puzzles
items.abstract: Project Proteus follows the Angelica series onto the nitrides. Near lattice match to GaN, one wurtzite ScₓAl₁₋ₓN layer can be a transistor barrier, a ferroelectric switch and a piezoelectric resonator, and each form hides a disagreement in the literature. On the Angelica GaN-on-Si foundation, the paper computes everything that can be computed before a wafer is needed, and ends with five test vehicles for what computation cannot settle. Every result is tagged IMPLEMENTABLE, TESTABLE or CONCEPT. Puzzle 1, the matched composition: laboratories report 0.09, 0.11 and 0.14; 0.18 is the theoretical value. No common match with composition-scale errors of 7–10 % reconciles the three measurements (χ² = 13.8, 2 degrees of freedom).Puzzle 2, the missing mobility: with Angelica's calibrated scattering model, two laboratories' ScAlN HEMTs need an extra scattering channel of about 641–658 cm²/Vs. ScAlN buys current (5.7–8.1 A/mm, 2.5–3.5× AlGaN), not speed.Puzzle 3, two ferroelectrics: sputtered films switch at 4–5.5 MV/cm, epitaxial films near match at 0.65–1.2 MV/cm. In a HEMT gate stack, 2DEG screening and interlayer breakdown let only about 27–45 % (epitaxial) and 2.5 % (sputtered) of the polarization switch, enough for the reported 1–2 V windows.Form 3: a 39 GHz (n260) resonator needs x ≥ 0.175 under an optimistic bandwidth rule and x ≈ 0.30 under a conservative one, so the matched barrier composition is at best marginal for it.On silicon, heat, not current, caps power (4.0 vs 8.8 W/mm on SiC for +175 K); the RF loss of the stack depends on whether a parasitic layer forms at the silicon surface, not on the oxide thickness. Formal paper in English (authoritative), Traditional Chinese and Japanese; primers for middle-school readers in the same three languages; full code and sources. Not peer-reviewed. Defensive publication. Text CC BY 4.0, code Apache 2.0.

items.title: PRISM: Preference-based Reward and Uncertainty-Integrated Synthesis Minimization for RTL PPA Optimization
items.abstract: This paper introduces a budget-aware, multi-objective framework (called PRISM) for RTL optimization that improves power, performance, and area (PPA) while sharply limiting expensive commercial synthesis tool calls. Starting from a synthesizable baseline and functional testbench, the method iterates through LLM-driven rewrite generation, fast compile/simulation equivalence filtering, low-cost proxy feature extraction, and selective commercial synthesis tool (Synopsys Design Compiler (DC)) evaluation. To prioritize which candidates deserve high-quality synthesis, we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes, and combine ensemble uncertainty with a diversity-aware acquisition rule to avoid early bias and redundant evaluations. A key advantage is that PRISM maintains a best-tradeoff set G of non-dominated designs throughout the run: G preserves the best solutions found so far, is fed back into generation and refinement, and enables consistent, cumulative improvements rather than repeatedly restarting from the baseline. Across RTLLM v2.0 modules, the approach consistently yields post-synthesis gains under fixed commercial synthesis tool call budgets, and ablations confirm that reward-guided selection and candidate dropping are central to sample-efficient progress. PRISM efficacy is evaluated across multiple technology nodes (7 nm, 15 nm, and 45 nm) using identical pipelines without retraining.

items.title: Multi-agent generative AI ecosystems for cyber-physical systems in Industry 5.0
items.abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are increasingly being implemented in critical industrial infrastructure, where complexity and interdependence are rising, posing significant cyber and operational risks. Traditional anomaly detection algorithms can be ineffective in capturing temporal dynamics, relational dependencies, and interpretable response requirements. The present paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI system to detect CPS anomalies and provide decision support by combining temporal feature encoding, relational modeling as graphs, supervised learning, and reasoning with an LLM. The architecture consists of detection, diagnosis, planning, governance, and human-in-the-loop validation agents. The framework is tested on the SWaT benchmark data. Findings indicate that the Autoencoder, LSTM, and 1D-CNN are more effective in terms of raw detection metrics, whereas the Random Forest provides more interpretable and agent-readable evidence to support the post-detection decision. Analysis of features and sensor family suggests the relevance of relational dependencies in characterizing anomalies. The multi-agent layer converts selected anomaly predictions into context-dependent explanations and governance-filtered recommendations to aid operator review, response planning, and process resilience. Overall, the framework supports transparent and human-supervised CPS anomaly management aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

items.title: Medical AI Technology Gaps and Investment Priorities: Non-Contrast CT "Virtual Contrast" Synthesis, 3D Swin-UNETR ASIC Acceleration, and Clinical ROI Asymmetry (医療AI技術ギャップと投資優先順位:単純CT仮想造影「Virtual Contrast」・Swin-UNETR ASIC・ROI非対称性)
items.abstract: This monograph establishes a rigorous technical, thermodynamic, and capital-allocation framework evaluating the technology gaps and investment priorities in clinical medical AI, centering on three structural axes: (1) Non-Contrast CT to Contrast-Enhanced CT "Virtual Contrast" synthesis, (2) dedicated 3D Swin-UNETR ASIC hardware acceleration, and (3) structural Return on Investment (ROI) asymmetry across hospital reimbursement and liability regimes. While 3D shifted-window transformer architectures (Swin-UNETR) demonstrate high structural fidelity in volumetric feature extraction from routine non-contrast CT (NCCT) scans, executing high-resolution 3D window self-attention on general-purpose GPUs incurs severe memory-bandwidth bottlenecks and latency penalties in acute triage workflows. We formulate a deterministic custom ASIC dataflow architecture tailored for 3D Swin-UNETR volumetric patch partitioning, on-chip SRAM cyclic window shifting, and cryptographic zero-knowledge state verification (QFS-zkVM over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) to eliminate stochastic hallucination risks in synthetic vascular enhancement. Furthermore, we quantify the clinical and economic ROI asymmetry between capital-intensive foundational model training and deterministic edge-ASIC deployment—accounting for contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) mitigation, iodinated contrast supply-chain volatility, radiology throughput gains, and statutory Human-in-Command (HIC) fiduciary liability boundaries. items.title: IF:CARGO: LLM-Based Semantic Compilation for Al-Native Rule Programming Games
items.abstract: This case study presents IF: CARGO, an experimental puzzle game that uses a large language model as a semantic compiler rather than an autonomous game-playing agent. Players author IF/THEN rules in natural language, which the model translates into a constrained command schema for deterministic validation and execution by the game engine. This architecture creates a playable loop of expression, execution, observation, and revision, framing AI interaction as semantic debugging. A mixed-methods playtest with 24 participants across eight levels examined player attempts, thinking time, perceived controllability, adjustability, and interpretations of the AI’s role. Results suggest that players generally understood the model as a translation intermediary and could revise their strategies through feedback, while periodic commands, multi-robot coordination, and rule-priority mechanics created greater cognitive and diagnostic demands. The study proposes a practical pattern for AI-native gameplay: constrain natural-language input, preserve player authorship, and ensure deterministic execution.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial EDA flows. The experiments evaluate 22 configurations spanning seven models on 21 public and 19 private tasks. Mean layout scores range from 4.22 to 80.26 on public tasks and from 1.43 to 67.01 on private tasks, on a 100-point scale. Higher reasoning effort does not consistently improve mean scores, and configurations with comparable scores can incur substantially different model costs.

items.title: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: AI Agents for Bomb Busters
items.abstract: Bomb Busters is a cooperative board game where players work together to defuse a bomb represented by 48 wires of 12 ranks. Wires are dealt to each player secretly, and are held in ascending order. Using only these constraints, and almost without any explicit communicative actions, players must deduce the ranks of wires held by other players. We present AI agents for the four player base version of the game that use a possible worlds model to represent other players' hands which is narrowed by observations made during game play to play the game near optimally, winning 9915 out of 10000 games. We also discuss the impact of different design decisions on the score of the game.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: High‐mobility p‐type Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin‐film transistors with self‐passivating contacts
items.abstract: Abstract Tellurium (Te) has emerged as a significant semiconductor material due to its intriguing physicochemical properties and great potential in next‐generation electronics and optoelectronics. The Se alloying method has been proved to be effective in improving the static control ability of Te semiconductor film. However, the traditional metal/semiconductor contact severely limits the mobility and on‐state current density of Te 0.65 Se 0.35 films due to the existence of interfacial Schottky barrier and insufficient charge injection efficiency. Here, we propose a TeO x self‐passivating assisted metal/semiconductor contact method to reduce the contact resistance, enabling ultrahigh mobility and on‐state current in the p‐type Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin film transistors. The TeO x passivation layer with a higher work function reduces contact resistance and weakens the Schottky barrier by passivating possible defects on the Te 0.65 Se 0.35 surface and inhibiting elements diffusion in the materials. The TeO x self‐passivating assisted Te 0.65 Se 0.35 thin film field effect transistor has a contact resistance as low as 1.2 kΩ μm and a contact interface with a near‐zero Schottky barrier. Compared with the original device, the on‐state current is increased by about 5 times to 250 μA, the hole mobility is increased by about 4 times which is up to 88.8 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , and the on–off ratio is about 2 × 10 4 . The comprehensive performance has reached the leading level and achieved the highest hole mobility among the evaporated p‐type films. This method fills the gap in the large‐scale preparation and optimization of p‐type semiconductors, providing the possibility for industrial wafer‐level preparation. image

items.title: Governed Memory for AI Agents: a shared spine with a human merge gate, in production across four deployments
items.abstract: AI collapsed the cost of executing project work and, in doing so, moved the bottleneck to continuity of understanding: the one thing an agent cannot supply for itself, because every session begins amnesiac. Memory stores for agents now appear weekly. Few of them answer the question an organisation has to answer before it lets agents write into its memory: who is allowed to change what we believe, and how is a wrong change undone? We report on Architect, a system in daily production use since April 2026 that answers that question structurally rather than by policy. Its contributions, in order: (1) a lifecycle-gated write contract, in which agents may deposit freely into an append-only spine but may only propose changes of state, one human merges on one surface, and authority is recomputed at the moment of application rather than at the moment of grant; (2) a set of spine invariants that make governance operative instead of descriptive: supersede-not-delete with lineage, structural refusal of malformed or unauthorised writes, human-tethered recording authority for agent personas, and provenance stamped on every unit; (3) the matter-scoped memory substrate those invariants run on, where scope attaches before any prompt, the reachability boundary doubles as the data-sovereignty boundary, a reconciler round-trips records between markdown files and a database, and a third-party AI can connect over a standard protocol and complete the full loop. We present four deployments (a multi-matter central instance, a user-bound matter, a pooled multi-tenant box and a single-tenant box) as measured on 20 August 2026: a corpus of 9,784 units, of which 6,520 are lived rather than imported, and the system's audit of its own lineage, which found 62 supersessions predating a fix, 38 of them in the wrong direction, and reversed 11 by a judge under a confidence floor while holding the other 27 for a human. We close with the frontier (automatic contradiction surfacing, as-of-t query, unit-level promotion) and show, with numbers, why the merge gate itself is the scaling bottleneck and why the answer is graduated autonomy rather than faster human review.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Extreme temperatures characterization of Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMT
items.abstract: In this work, we fabricate and characterize ultra-wide bandgap Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs with Pt/Au gate under a wide temperature range of 20 K to 650 K. The devices retained robust modulation capability throughout the measurement, with excellent on/off ratio of 9.7 * 107 and 6.4 * 107 under 20 K and 650 K. The DC output IV measurement was performed, with Id,max of a device with Lsd = 9 μm measured to be 240 mA/mm and 120 mA/mm under 20 K and 650 K. In addition, low drain and leakage were observed in multiple devices, and the device robustness was evaluated under room temperature after the extreme temperature measurement with minimal degradation observed in Id,max and Rsheet. Moreover, transfer I-V characteristics of the Al0.6Ga0.4N channel HEMTs have also been studied, where a relatively small Vth shift was observed. TLM measurement and transconductance analysis both indicate the presence of weak temperature dependent scattering mechanisms in the device channel. The subthreshold swing (SS) was calculated and observed to increase parallelly to SSideal under investigated temperature, indicates a robust gate structure. Finally, the on/off ratio and Ig of the 9 μm Lsd device were benchmarked and compared favorably against other reported results. While the results offer insight into the extreme temperature performance of AlGaN channel HEMT with Al composition higher than 50%, it also establishes AlGaN channel HEMT as a promising candidate for extreme temperature electronic applications.

items.title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
items.abstract: We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with -CF2- dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer-perovskite composite design.

items.title: Enforcing Narrative Reliability and Epistemic Pacing in LLM-Driven Detective Games via Structured Knowledge Trees
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable open-ended dialogue in interactive games, but their non-deterministic outputs make it difficult to preserve authorial control, factual consistency, and the intended sequence of information disclosure. These challenges are particularly significant in detective games, where premature revelation or fabricated details can undermine the logic of player progression. We present a Structured Knowledge Tree architecture coupled with a tri-agent LLM pipeline for controlling dialogue in an open-ended interrogation game. The system separates knowledge retrieval, dialogue generation, and response verification to ensure that the virtual suspect reveals only information permitted by the current narrative state. We evaluate the approach through The Interrogation of Adrian Gale, a playable detective-game testbed, and a formal user study examining hallucination reduction, adherence to authored disclosure sequences, and perceived logical progression. Our results demonstrate that the structured architecture reduces critical hallucinations by 64.78% and entirely prevents premature narrative disclosure. While the strict mechanical constraints introduced usability trade-offs regarding forced conversational reveals, the system successfully enforces rigorous epistemic pacing and provides players with a clear, subjective sense of progression toward solving the case.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: Design and ASIC Implementation of an Edge-AI SoC Subsystem for Detecting Driver Unresponsiveness and Requesting a Minimum Risk Manoeuvre
items.abstract: Driver drowsiness and loss of responsiveness are major causes of road accidents, and a warning buzzer alone cannot protect a vehicle whose driver has stopped responding. This paper presents a digital hardware subsystem for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) that takes precomputed class scores (logits) from an upstream Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), judges their reliability, cross-checks them with an independent fatigue indicator, and escalates from a warning to a Minimum Risk Manoeuvre (MRM) request if the driver does not respond. The design contains a CNN confidence unit, a PERCLOS-inspired fatigue unit using a 32-frame sliding window, a safety arbiter and a risk-adaptive finite state machine (FSM) whose response timeout shortens as obstacle and lane-drift risk rises. The Verilog RTL was verified with a 12-scenario testbench in Synopsys VCS and Verdi. Synthesis with Synopsys Design Compiler on the SAED32 library at a 4 ns clock (250 MHz) gave 582 cells, a total cell area of 1726.40 units, 195.69 µW dynamic power and a setup slack of 0.00 ns. A Synopsys IC Compiler II analysis reported 667 cells and 79.38% core utilization. These are pre-layout and placement-stage estimates, and their limitations are stated explicitly.

items.title: CU-3D: A Scalable Legality-Aware RTL-to-GDS Flow for 3D-IC Physical Design
items.abstract: Face-to-face (F2F) hybrid bonds shorten interdie connections, but data, clock, and power-grid (PG) connections must be realized together. CU-3D is a RTL-to-GDS physical design flow based on commercial EDA tools. It derives role-compatible hybrid-bond (HB) sites from a 17-metal ASAP7-based technology model, complete HB footprints, and constructed PG geometry. To coordinate partitioning with placement flexibility, Scaled refines an inherited 2D placement, whereas Fresh places the receiving die first and uses its pin locations and clock loads to guide placement of the other die. Data and clock HB assignments are jointly optimized while retaining alternative data sites and reserving capacity for subsequent PG assignment. The selected HB sites and stacks are preserved during 3D clock-tree synthesis, supply-aware cell insertion, and routing. Across eleven designs, including a 133-macro processor, the flow achieves zero backend DRC violations and passes signal-connectivity checks. Nine paired designs admit lower-footprint, lower-power implementations; four improve setup WNS. On JPEG, early joint planning gains 87 ps and mobility-aware partitioning gains 346 ps. Path analysis explains why cell-delay savings can outweigh net-delay increases.

items.title: Bias‐Tunable Dual‐Interface Phototransistors for Polarization‐Sensitive Photodetection and Neuromorphic Vision
items.abstract: Optoelectronic devices that concurrently perform photodetection and synaptic computation are central to neuromorphic vision, yet they face an intrinsic trade‐off in which high‐speed detection demands rapid carrier transport while durable memory depends on slow charge trapping. Here, a bias‑tunable dual‑interface Ta 2 NiSe 5 /ReS 2 /Au van der Waals phototransistor is presented, in which two physically distinct interfaces are switched between two operational modes. At zero bias, the built‑in electric field at the Ta 2 NiSe 5 /ReS 2 heterojunction drives self‐powered, broadband (375–850 nm) polarization‐sensitive photodetection with a responsivity of 30 mA W −1 , detectivity of 7.7 × 10 9 Jones, and 66 µs response speed, further demonstrating polarization imaging and in‐sensor image processing. At positive bias, the elevated ReS 2 /Au Schottky barrier confines photogenerated carriers within intrinsic defect states, yielding a retention time exceeding 5000 s and thereby emulating short‑term to long‑term plasticity, paired‑pulse facilitation, and learning‑forgetting‑relearning behaviors. The device exhibits multi‐wavelength polarization‑sensitive static visual memory and serves as a physical front‐end that improves neural‐network recognition under low‐contrast degraded imaging. Leveraging its intrinsic temporal dynamics, the system enables with a motion direction classification accuracy of 96.67%. The dual‑interface strategy reconciles fast photodetection with long retention, offering a route to low‐power multifunctional neuromorphic vision hardware.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Software Testing: A Systematic Survey of Test Generation, Mutation Testing, and Flaky Test Management
items.abstract: Software testing consumes a large share of development effort, and its most labor-intensive tasks — writing test cases, judging whether outputs are correct, and keeping test suites reliable — are precisely the tasks where artificial intelligence has recently made the largest advances. This paper presents a systematic survey of artificial intelligence in software testing. It traces the field from classical and search-based test generation, through symbolic execution and fuzzing, to the present generation of large language model methods; it reviews how AI is used for automated test generation, assertion and oracle construction, mutation testing, flaky-test detection and management, and test prioritization and fault prediction; it examines the evidence for each family of techniques, including where empirical results are strong, where they are mixed, and where they rest on narrow benchmarks; and it analyzes the central challenges of the field — the oracle problem, evaluation validity, non-determinism, cost, and the risk of over-trusting generated tests. The survey concludes that AI has moved testing from a largely manual craft toward a semi-automated discipline, but that generated tests still require human review, measured adequacy criteria, and disciplined suite maintenance, and that the field's most valuable direction is the combination of learned models with classical, coverage-guided, and mutation-based methods rather than the replacement of one by the other.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: An AI-Enabled Software Development Lifecycle with Governed Agent Execution
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to engineering, delivered behaviour and delegated execution. This paper proposes a software development lifecycle (SDLC) integrating people, AI agents and conventional automation. Three independent applicability questions—Assist, Embed and Operate (A/E/O)—distinguish participation from autonomy and maturity. Seven recurring activities connect tasks, verification and handoffs to accountable decisions. Three operational measures cover accepted-change elapsed time, review effort and delivery cost per accepted change alongside quality and safety guardrails. A purposive synthesis of 58 external source records informs fourteen core requirements, reproduced with verification notes in Appendices A–B. A SupportFlow sandbox demonstration exercises selected application controls using sample records and supplied AI-output fixtures; Appendix C identifies the evidence boundaries. Packaged-software adoption remains illustrative. Internal consistency checks and a prospective comparison with existing DevSecOps address different evaluation questions; comparative effectiveness remains untested. Conceptual research preprint, version 4.0. Not a peer-reviewed journal publication or an empirically validated standard. The paper includes Appendices A–C. Supporting materials provide the current criteria, source records and reproducible internal consistency checks. CC BY 4.0 applies to the paper; supporting-file rights are specified in LICENSES.md.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: AKANE Architecture E2: Finding an LLM's mistakes from how its answers connect
items.abstract: Code, data, and results for small experiments in which a small language model (Gemma-2 2B) answers many true/false statements and writes its own consistency rules, some of them wrong. A network checks the model's answers against those rules while also doubting each rule, using belief propagation, and the signals are compared with the model's confidence and with counting rule violations.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
items.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built on Refinitiv and MSCI ratings, and pass VaR backtests at 95% coverage. The results support text-based ESG modeling as an alternative to vendor-rating-based approaches, particularly where downside risk management and traceable explanation are jointly required.

items.title: A Gold-Standard Study of What Makes a Lightweight Game-Playing Agent Strong
items.abstract: A reinforcement learning agent is only as strong as the opponents it trains against, and it is also hard to grade. It beats a random opponent over 99 percent of the time, and it only ties copies of itself. So we build a strong, fixed, rule-based expert for Gin Rummy and never train against it: no expert games, no demonstrations, no gradients. It does pick the shipped checkpoint, and we say where that matters. The expert beats every agent we trained 66 to 99 percent of the time. Across more than a hundred runs we ask what makes a small agent stronger, and five things help. They are trust-region updates, a well-aimed reward, a curriculum of tougher opponents, warm starting, and keeping the best checkpoint. Stacking them lifts a self-play champion from about 30 to about 34 percent against the expert. Several other ideas did not pay off. Reward shaping at two horizons, learned state embeddings, and DAgger imitation were each unhelpful, and a live large language model opponent was far too slow. Extra capacity does little to break the ceiling, across MLP, convolutional, set-based, attention and recurrent encoders. Handing the learner the opponent's hidden hand does not move it either. We add two standard baselines: neural fictitious self-play and information-set Monte Carlo search. We also reproduce the grading protocol on Leduc Hold'em, whose optimum is computable. The result is a small, fast recipe that never trains on the expert, plus a grading protocol that carries over to any game with a fixed reference. We report bootstrap intervals on the multi-seed comparisons and release the code.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: A Controlled Benchmark of Edge AI Accelerators for Traffic Object Detection: scripts and results
items.abstract: Scripts, raw result files and deployed models for an MSc thesis benchmarking one EfficientDet-Lite2 detector on the Coral Dev Board Mini, Khadas VIM3 and AMD Kria KV260, with a Jetson Nano reference.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: • Technical Specification of the Lotus Core-V3 Ultra: An Optimized 360-Qubit Superconducting QPU Utilizing Zero-Skew Multi-Die Interconnect Topology
items.abstract: This technical specification details the architectural parameters and hardware-level optimizations of the Lotus Core-V3 Ultra, a scalable superconducting quantum processing unit integrating 6 clusters of 12 physical transmon qubits each, yielding a total of 360 physical channels. Moving beyond the NISQ baseline, this multi-die chiplet network achieves permanent geometric zero-skew symmetry (theta = 0.00°), completely neutralizing signal propagation timing errors directly on the hardware plane and eliminating compiler-level software latency overhead. Inter-die capacitive and inductive crosstalk is suppressed to <= -68.5 dB via an atomic layer deposited (ALD) 25 nm Al2O3 insulation matrix paired with a 10 µm grounded shield net. Systematic mitigation of parasitic bus line capacitances drosselt the aggregate thermal dissipation under multi-channel full computational load by 43%, limiting the total cryogenic thermal load to 8.18 nW at a 10 mK stage to preserve maximum quantum coherence.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: • Technical Specification of the Lotus Core-V3 Hexa: A Scalable 288-Qubit Superconducting QPU Network Utilizing Multi-Die Concentric Ring-Bus Topology
items.abstract: This technical specification details the hardware architecture and multi-die orchestration framework of the Lotus Core-V3 Hexa, an aggregated virtual Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) comprising 6 interconnected 48-qubit superconducting dies, yielding a total of 288 physical Transmon processing cells. Moving away from monolithic, low-yield high-qubit grids, this framework links independent symmetrical dies via a centralized 5.50 GHz superconducting coplanar waveguide (CPW) ring-bus interconnect. Vertical signal routing is handled by back-side 3D Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) to eliminate 2D line-crossing constraints. Embedded lambda/4 stub filters and a 10 um ground isolation matrix suppress capacitive inter-die crosstalk to <= -55 dB. Systematic mid-circuit phase errors (theta = 8.39°) induced by routing timing skews are dynamically compensated via a compiler-driven, runtime-free Virtual-Z gate protocol, optimizing the system for complex biomedical Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) operations. ---
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization charge-induced modification of Schottky barrier width strongly affects the hole transport and memory properties of MoS2-HZO FeFETs. We further demonstrate several advantages and unique features of the FeFETs such as nondestructive data readout, non-volatile data retention under zero gate bias, low operation voltage, high write endurance and ultra-fast switching speed. These 1T memory cells can simplify the dense 3D integrated array architecture and offer additional practical functionalities, such as fast programming and erasing of large data arrays that are absent for many conventional memories. The demonstrated MoS2 and HZO-based FeFET shows great potential for on-chip complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible circuits for multifunctional devices, especially for 3D monolithically integrated architectures for AI workload.

items.title: Ultra‐Robust All‐Weather Perovskite Memristor Protected by Conformal Parylene Nanoscale Coating
items.abstract: Halide perovskites are promising memristive materials for neuromorphic computing, yet their practical deployment in hardware is severely hindered by instability against moisture, oxygen, and reactive metallic ions. Here, we develop an ultra‐robust perovskite memristor with all‐weather adaptability protected by a ∼100 nm conformal polymeric nanoscale coating. Deposited by low‐temperature, solvent‐free chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technique, the polymeric Parylene serves as an encapsulation, interfacial passivation, and homogeneous dielectric layer. The memristor exhibits excellent bipolar resistive switching under ambient conditions with high uniformity, an endurance of 1.5 × 10 4 cycles (over 12.5‐fold improvement), and a low set voltage of ∼0.27 V. It maintains stable operation under 100% relative humidity, thermal treatment at 348 K, 6‐month ambient storage, and 300 bending cycles at 90°, and even passes the stringent IPX7 waterproof standard. A hardware‐mapped convolutional neural network leveraging the synaptic properties of these memristors achieves a highly reliable MNIST recognition accuracy of 90%±0.4% across 10 independent test cycles. This work demonstrates that conformal Parylene encapsulation offers a comprehensive solution to the perovskite instability, paving the way for flexible and low‐power neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Thermodynamic Supremacy and Structural Victory: A Rigorous Comparative Monograph on Millikelvin Surface Code Quantum Error Correction vs. Ambient Spintronic MRAM-PIM and SOFC Cogeneration Architectures under Deterministic QFS-zkVM Governance
items.abstract: 概要/要約: このモノグラフは、回転表面コード($T \approx 15\text{ mK}$ の $d$ 距離安定化格子)を利用する極低温超伝導量子コンピューティングアーキテクチャと、固体酸化物燃料電池(SOFC)トリジェネレーションインフラストラクチャと結合した常温スピントロニクス磁気抵抗ランダムアクセスメモリ処理インメモリ(MRAM-PIM)との間の厳密な熱力学的、トポロジー的、および制度的比較分析を確立します。錦川(岩国市錦帯峡)の極低温水圧下で形成された生物学的回復時間目標(RTO P2.0)恒常性生存閾値を基に、超伝導表面符号は致命的なカルノー熱力学的ペナルティ($\text{COP}_{\text{Carnot}} \approx 5 \times 10^{-5}$)と、非決定論的な遅延違反を引き起こす$\mathcal{O}(d^3)$最小重み完全マッチング(MWPM)症候群復号ボトルネックに悩まされていることを示します。一方、SOT-MRAM PIMと確率ビット($p$ビット)イジングマシンは、室温の熱ゆらぎ($T = 300\text{ K}$で$E_b > 60 k_B T$)とキルヒホッフの法則に基づくメモリ内蓄積を利用して、極低温オーバーヘッドなしでフェムトジュール規模の決定論的計算を実現します。さらに、200 kWのSOFCコジェネレーションユニットと二重/三重効果吸収式チラー(COP ≥ 1.2、冷却能力216 kW / 暖房能力180 kW)を統合した自律的な物理インフラストラクチャモデルを正式に構築し、厳密な24.0℃±0.5℃の人間による運用環境を確保します。最後に、すべての組み合わせ最適化軌道と熱テレメトリは、PHOENIX_BRIDGEとPHOENIX_ROUTERを介して、64ビットのGoldilocks素数体($\mathbb{F}_p、p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1$)上のQuantum Financial System Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machine(QFS-zkVM)内に暗号的に固定され、SEC規則15c3-5の取引前リスク管理とデラウェア州のCaremark受託者監督基準に完全に準拠します。 items.title: Thermally Conductive and Electrically Insulating Thermal Interface Materials for Advanced Packaging: From Filler and Interface Engineering to Thermal Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal interface materials (TIMs) that combine efficient heat transport with electrical insulation are increasingly important for three‐dimensional integration and high‐power electronic packaging. Existing reviews commonly organize the field by filler type or treat surface modification, filler alignment, and network construction as separate strategies, obscuring their coupling across length scales. Here, we present a hierarchical design framework linking physical fundamentals, filler/interface engineering, and thermal‐network engineering. We first examine phonon transport, electrical‐failure mechanisms, area‐normalized thermal resistance, and effective‐medium models to define the constraints governing filler selection. We then compare oxide and nitride ceramics, carbon‐based materials, and emerging high‐thermal‐conductivity candidates, with emphasis on anisotropy, defect chemistry, processability, and electrical compatibility. Filler functionalization, spheroidization, and core–shell design are subsequently analyzed together with orientational alignment, multicomponent hybridization, and three‐dimensional network construction. Particular attention is given to the coupled effects of composite thermal conductivity, interfacial thermal resistance, bond‐line thickness, electrical insulation, processability, and long‐term reliability. Finally, we discuss six research directions spanning unconventional fillers, adaptive interfaces, multiscale computation, advanced manufacturing, chemical interphase design, and sustainable package co‐design. This framework shifts TIM development from isolated property maximization toward package‐relevant thermal–electrical–mechanical co‐optimization.

items.title: The 2026 Global Liquidation of Fraud Hypothesis: Sovereign Seizure of Shadow Bitcoin Reserves, Thermodynamic Collapse of AI Scaling Hype, and Deterministic Settlement via QFS-zkVM
items.abstract: This monograph formalizes the "2026 Global Liquidation of Fraud" (世界規模の不正清算) hypothesis proposed by Yoko Hasebe, demonstrating the structural isomorphism between two seemingly disparate macro-events in early 2026: (1) the kinetic seizure of the Maduro regime's estimated 600,000 BTC "Shadow Reserve" following Operation Absolute Resolve and its prospective absorption into the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (SBR) under Executive Order 14233, and (2) the institutional authority contraction within frontier AI laboratories (exemplified by Google DeepMind) driven by physical high-bandwidth memory (HBM) bottlenecks, grid power deficits, data exhaustion, and negative return-on-investment (ROI) scaling walls. We construct a unified thermodynamic and algebraic model under RTO P2.0 and QFS-zkVM over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field ($\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64}-2^{32}+1$) that distinguishes unbacked paper claims and illicit shadow liquidity from verifiable Proof-of-Work and physical infrastructure assets. Furthermore, we integrate Q-SAFA cryptographic sovereign asset forfeiture auditing, PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER liquidity isolation gates, Human-in-Command (HIC) fiduciary interlocks, SEC Rule 15c3-5 pre-trade market access controls, and Delaware Caremark board oversight duties to establish a rigorous institutional framework for surviving systemic asset impairment and sovereign supply shocks. items.title: Supplementary reproducibility package for "Independent Gate-Control and Source-Service Partitioning in Multi-Output GAA Logic"
items.abstract: Selected derived evidence supporting the research article "Independent Gate-Control and Source-Service Partitioning in Multi-Output GAA Logic", submitted to IET Circuits, Devices & Systems. The package contains the matched-resource physical acceptance records, extraction configuration, contact-resistivity sensitivity sweep, isolated/crossed source-network impedance matrices, paired compact-model circuit comparisons, fixed-network membership results, arc-characterization grids, workload and contact extensions, receiver-margin constants, deterministic-seed OpenROAD metrics, mesh comparisons, fixed-layout timing-replay records, the two-branch analytical rule, the figure-generation scripts, and an origin-path/SHA-256 manifest binding every copied artifact to its source in the project record. This is a selected evidence package, not a self-contained experiment archive. Raw transient waveforms, routed databases, simulator decks, and full run configurations are not included. GT3 (BSIM-CMG 111.2.1 in ngspice 47), PKP3, and OpenROAD-flow-scripts are public and are cited in the article. Results are predictive comparisons from research compact models and do not claim fabricated silicon, foundry signoff, or statistical yield. Integrity: SHA256SUMS inside the archive lists every file; the manuscript's PACKAGE_VERIFICATION.json records the SHA-256 of this ZIP.
