items.title: DEQ-Det: Dual Evidence Queries for Few-Shot Analog IC Device Detection
items.abstract: Detecting analog integrated circuit (IC) devices in layout images supports circuit analysis and inspection. With only a few annotated examples, variation in device geometry and visual similarity to dummy or routing structures make reliable detection difficult. Foreground similarity alone can highlight plausible targets without distinguishing them from competing layout patterns. We propose Dual Evidence Queries for Detection (DEQ-Det), which constructs complementary foreground and background references from the same support images without additional annotations. Foreground references capture target morphology, while selected background references characterize surrounding layout patterns. Both sources guide query selection and region verification, combining target appearance with layout context. Across five held-out device categories and three random seeds, DEQ-Det achieves macro AP50 of 39.41 and 53.03 at 10 and 30 shots, exceeding the strongest listed baselines by 3.97 and 9.71 points, respectively. A matched 30-shot ablation further shows that RoI background evidence reduces pooled false positives at comparable recall, supporting its role in interference suppression.

items.title: Cu–Cu Grain Intermixing Quantification for Hybrid Bonding Applications
items.abstract: Cu–Cu hybrid bonding at reduced thermal budgets depends critically on reliable grain intermixing across the bonding interface. Yet interfacial evolution is still predominantly assessed qualitatively, precluding objective comparison across copper microstructures and process conditions. Here, we introduce Bond IQ, an automated image-based metrology framework that converts registered cross-sectional FIB-SEM datasets into physically interpretable descriptors using classical computer-vision methods. We apply the framework to five blanket chip-level pairings spanning three engineered copper microstructures: coarse-grain (CG), fine-grain locked (FG-L), and fine-grain thermally dynamic (FG-TD) Cu, thermocompression bonded at 210 °C for 2 h. Three coupled but distinct metrics are extracted: Bridged Interface Fraction (BIF), Interface Void Loading (IVL), and normalized Grain Penetration Depth (GPD). The symmetric CG/CG interface exhibited the weakest evolution, combining high IVL (5.4 nm) with low BIF (6.1%) and low GPD (0.20). By contrast, CG/FG-TD achieved the highest BIF (54.5%) at low IVL (0.6 nm), signifying broad but comparatively shallow bridging, whereas CG/FG-L reached the highest GPD (0.89) at moderate BIF (32.7%), indicating localized yet deeper directional grain advancement. Among symmetric fine-grained interfaces, FG-L/FG-L displayed the lowest IVL (0.5 nm), underscoring the role of fine-grain stability in void suppression. Collectively, these results demonstrate that interface bridging, void elimination, and penetration depth are governed by distinct but interrelated contributions of grain-size contrast and microstructural stability. By reducing subjective interfacial assessment to quantitative, mechanistically interpretable descriptors, Bond IQ offers a scalable route to screen copper microstructures and bonding conditions, and it can be extended to other metal–metal interfaces where microstructural evolution governs low-temperature bonding reliability.

items.title: Conveyor-mode electron shuttling through a T-junction in Si/SiGe
items.abstract: Abstract Conveyor-mode shuttling in gated Si/SiGe devices enables adiabatic transfer of single electrons, electron patterns and spin qubits confined in quantum dots across several microns with a scalable number of signal lines. To realize their full potential, linear shuttle lanes must connect into a two-dimensional grid with controllable routing. We introduce a T-junction device linking two independently driven shuttle lanes. Electron routing across the junction requires no extra control lines beyond the four channels per conveyor belt. We measure an inter-lane charge transfer fidelity of $$F={100.0000000}_{-9\times 1{0}^{-7}}^{+0}\,\%$$ F = 100.0000000 − 9 × 1 0 − 7 + 0 % at an instantaneous electron velocity of 270 mm s −1 . The filling of 54 quantum dots is controlled by simple atomic pulses, allowing us to swap electron patterns, laying the groundwork for a native spin-qubit SWAP gate. This T-junction establishes a path towards scalable, two-dimensional quantum computing architectures with flexible spin qubit routing for quantum error correction.

items.title: Considerations for Bond Strength Metrology and Standards
items.abstract: Chevron based bond strength structures provide significant advantages over the double cantilever beam method commonly in use. We introduce new bond strength test structure designs with the goal of simplifying the implementation of the chevron test and improving the availability of bond strength metrology. We describe designs based on chip-to-chip bonding which could be expanded to chip to wafer. There are both asymmetric bond structures based on separate designs for the top and bottom chips and symmetric designs in which the same chip design serves as both top and bottom. We describe a fabrication process which is compatible with both blanket dielectric and metal bonding surfaces as well as patterned surfaces including hybrid bonding type materials. We also describe a testing apparatus and the potential to adapt commercial die shear testers for this measurement. Finally, we describe a plan to realize research grade test materials based on these test structures.

items.title: Comparative Analysis and Genetic Algorithm Optimization of Multi-Transistor FinFET SRAM Topologies for SNM, Leakage, and Delay Improvement at 18nm
items.abstract: With continuous technology scaling, Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) faces significant challenges including increased leakage power, reduced stability, and higher delay. FinFET technology has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional CMOS technology due to its superior electrostatic control and reduced short-channel effects. This paper presents a multi-objective Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization framework for 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T, and 10T SRAM architectures using 18nm FinFET technology. The proposed optimization methodology focuses on minimizing leakage power, dynamic power, read delay, and write delay while maximizing Static Noise Margin (SNM). Cadence Virtuoso and the Spectre simulator were used for transient, DC, and power analysis. Genetic Algorithm optimization was implemented using transistor sizing and fin-count optimization techniques. The optimized SRAM architectures demonstrated significant reductions in leakage and dynamic power at a reduced supply voltage (1 V versus 1.5 V), with lower noise margins and a mixed effect on propagation delay. Simulation results show that optimized 10T SRAM achieved the lowest leakage power while 9T SRAM exhibited the highest read stability.

items.title: Collapsing Silicon Hegemony: Backend RISC-V Erosion, SoftBank LTV Margin Contagion, and Deterministic QFS-zkVM Interlocks for Post-Arm AI Infrastructure
items.abstract: Modern computational infrastructure has historically rested on the surface tension of a single proprietary Instruction Set Architecture (ISA): the Arm licensing ecosystem. However, as of 2026, two irreversible structural fractures have invalidated this hegemony: (1) Qualcomm's decisive final judgment victory over Arm in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware (September 30, 2025), which neutralized intellectual property intimidation over Architectural License Agreements (ALAs); and (2) Arm's predatory pivot into selling finished 136-core 3nm silicon ("Arm AGI CPU"), creating an irreconcilable conflict of interest with hyperscale licensees (AWS Graviton, Google Axion, Microsoft Cobalt). Concurrently, compiler-level hardware abstraction via OpenAI Triton, JAX/XLA, and PolyBlocks, combined with system-level Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures such as Microsoft's 1-trillion-parameter MAI-Thinking-1, has rendered proprietary frontend ISAs economically obsolete. Hyperscalers and sovereign-scale initiatives—most notably the $500 billion, 10-gigawatt Stargate Project—now face an existential mandate to eliminate multi-billion-dollar Arm royalty deadweight losses by transitioning backend compute to open RISC-V Vector Extension (RVV) chiplets and constant-stride EARTH memory architectures. This monograph formalizes the four-phase financial and physical contagion triggered by the collapse of Arm's growth terminal value: (Phase I) Valuation contraction of Arm shares; (Phase II) Breach of the 25% Loan-to-Value (LTV) threshold across SoftBank Group's (SBG) $18.5 billion Arm-backed margin loans alongside its $40 billion unsecured bridge debt (CDS spread at 355 bps); (Phase III) Forced liquidation of AI equity portfolios; and (Phase IV) Stranded-asset collapse across crypto-mining facilities that pivoted $65 billion into non-interruptible AI High-Performance Computing (HPC) data centers, culminating in forced Bitcoin treasury liquidations. To insulate sovereign AI and energy grids from this cascading failure, we introduce a deterministic hardware-cryptographic governance architecture integrating Real-Time Optimization (RTO P2.0), the Quantum Financial System Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machine (QFS-zkVM) over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ ($p = 2^{64}-2^{32}+1$), Q-SAFA cryptographic attestation, PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER autonomous load-shedding, and Human-in-Command (HIC) statutory interlocks enforcing SEC Rule 15c3-5 and Delaware Caremark fiduciary oversight. items.title: Co-optimization of spin coherence and valley splitting in Si/SiGe heterostructures
items.abstract: Single electron spins can be used to encode and process information in semiconductor quantum devices. Progress has been hindered by materials challenges, such as the small energy splitting between low-lying valley states and hyperfine coupling to nuclear spins. Here we use density functional theory to optimize the valley splitting and spin dephasing time in realistic Si/SiGe heterostructures. Reductions in the Si quantum well width generally increase the valley splitting. However, in narrow quantum wells, a larger fraction of the electronic wavefunction resides in the SiGe buffer layers, which increases the hyperfine coupling with spinful $^{73}$Ge. Our work shows that Si/SiGe heterostructures with 3~--~4~nm wide quantum wells and $^{73}$Ge and $^{29}$Si concentrations of 50 ppm should support average valley splittings $E_{v}$~$>$~500~$μ$eV and spin dephasing times $T_2^*$ exceeding 15~$μ$s assuming an effective quantum dot area of 700 nm$^2$. In addition, sharper Si/SiGe interfaces in general result in larger valley splittings and longer spin dephasing times.

items.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur severe memory-access overheads due to the cost of loading large weight matrices and key-value (KV) caches. Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) is an emerging solution that enables computation directly on static weights stored in memory, substantially reducing energy and latency. 3D-IMC further stacks memory arrays into vertical tiers, increasing capacity but revealing a new challenge: how weights are placed in memory determines which matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) can execute concurrently, affecting latency and throughput. The concurrency aspect of 3D-IMC weight-mapping remains underexplored in the literature, leading to sub-optimal utilization of compute resources on 3D-IMC chips. In this context we propose CAMP (Context-Aware Mapping and Placement), an inference-context-aware weight mapping algorithm for 3D-IMC-based LLM accelerators. CAMP captures the potential resource contention resulting from the architecture, targeted network, and runtime context in a conflict matrix, enabling throughput-optimized weight mapping. This mapping is refined through a profiling-driven feedback loop that efficiently prunes the search space and returns optimized mappings within practical runtimes. CAMP is an offline, software-based solution requiring no hardware changes and improving 3D-IMC compute utilization from 42.4% to 60.3%, delivering up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms.

items.title: Balancing DOF margin and stochastic failure in high-NA EUV process
items.abstract: BackgroundHigh-numerical aperture (NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography delivers superior resolution, but it severely restricts the depth of focus (DOF) window. To expand this margin, the detrimental impact of stray photons leaking into unexposed areas must be mitigated. Crucially, we confirmed that increasing the photo contrast to decrease stochastic failure conversely increases sensitivity to this leakage light, thereby degrading the DOF margin.AimWe aim to maximize the functional DOF window in the High-NA EUV process by understanding the effects of the photoresist material configurations and post-exposure bake (PEB) process conditions.ApproachBased on lithographic simulations, we employed a low-contrast resist environment that exhibits low sensitivity to optical leakage in defocused condition.ResultThe DOF window was expanded by elevating the PEB temperature, reducing the polymer molecular weight, decreasing the protecting group (PG) ratio, or applying a PG with high activation energy (Ea) for deprotection. These adjustments reduced profile degradation and pattern collapse by systematically lowering the photosensitivity of the resist matrix against optical leakage in High-NA process.ConclusionThese findings expose a fundamental problem of High-NA process. Widening the DOF margin requires an insensitive resist environment, which can inherently degrade pattern uniformity. Therefore, achieving a manufacturing window demands a multidimensional approach that precisely balances process margin with stochastic problem.

items.title: Analytical mean-field model for electrochemical metallization memristors with a nanoporous matrix: application to Ag/anodic alumina/Al
items.abstract: Memristors based on electrochemical metallization with many filaments are usually modeled by microscopic simulations with many parameters or by phenomenological laws whose parameters are hard to relate to physical quantities. We present an analytical mean-field model for a population of Ag filaments confined in the pores of a nanoporous matrix, built on Ohm's law, Faraday's law and a power-based rupture criterion. The filaments have a truncated normal distribution of cross-sections and rupture leaving lognormally distributed gaps whose median grows with the dissipated power. Gap closing shifts the distribution of squared gaps rigidly, and the model therefore admits closed-form expressions for the switching voltage, the read current, the rupture branch and the high-voltage current. We apply it to Ag/nanoporous anodic alumina/Al structures fabricated from industrial-grade aluminum, with a 2.4$μ$m alumina layer, and measured under ambient conditions. The parameters were fitted to the bipolar sweeps, with the gap dispersion taken from the temporal shape of the read after a pulse. They reproduce the bipolar response, including voltage-controlled negative differential resistance, and predict without refitting the unipolar sweeps and the amplitude of the pulse response, where state memory appears. A second sample, with a larger contact deposited chemically, is described by the same model. In vacuum the devices neither switch nor show negative differential resistance, as expected if adsorbed water supplies the counter reaction; the residual high-voltage current follows ionic hopping conduction.

items.title: Analog‐Tunable Nonvolatile Memristors with Self‐Compliance Behavior via a MoS x ‐Interlayer Strategy for Neuromorphic Recognition and Zero‐Trust Image Encryption
items.abstract: The von Neumann memory wall severely restricts the performance of traditional computing systems, and memristors have emerged as premier candidates for neuromorphic computing by virtue of their ability to integrate storage and computation functions. However, conventional HfO x memristors suffer from abrupt resistive switching and lack of intrinsic self‐protection, limiting their synaptic emulation performance. Herein, a novel nonvolatile HfO x /MoS x /HfO x trilayer heterostructure memristor with intrinsic self‐compliance and analog conductance modulation was constructed. The optimized device exhibits stable cycling endurance, multilevel retention stability and fast response speed, and achieves linear and symmetric conductance potentiation and depression. Furthermore, the proposed memristor successfully emulates diverse biological synaptic plasticities, including EPSC, IPSC, PPF, and PPD. A constructed neural network based on this device achieves a high handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 93.84% on the MNIST dataset, with excellent noise immunity and device variation robustness. Furthermore, the memristor acts as an irreplaceable physical entropy source for zero‐trust XOR‐based image encryption, generating ciphertext images with near‐optimal information entropy reaching 7.978 bits. This work presents a feasible MoS x interlayer modification strategy to optimize high‐performance artificial synapses on oxide memristors, enabling co‐integration of neuromorphic computing and hardware security.

items.title: An on-glass a-IGZO TFT operational amplifier for local voltage regulation in display driving systems
items.abstract: This work presents an on-glass amorphous indium-gallium-zinc oxide thin-film transistor (a-IGZO TFT) operational amplifier to achieve an integrated local voltage-regulation for reference-voltage stabilization in display driving systems. The fabricated op-amp adopts compact n-type-only two-stage architecture to reduce circuit complexity and internal high-impedance nodes for closed-loop operation. Under ± 15 V supply voltages, the measured op-amp exhibits a voltage gain of 35.5 dB, a cut-off frequency of 5.8 kHz, and a unit-gain frequency of 39 kHz. To examine closed-loop controllability, the op-amp was combined with external pass/load components in a prototype regulation setup. The measured output voltages were 1.82 V, 3.79 V, and 5.55 V for reference voltages of 2 V, 4 V, and 6 V, respectively. Circuit-level simulations were further used to analyze line-ripple suppression and load-transient recovery. The results indicate that a-IGZO TFT op-amps can be useful analog building blocks for low-current local voltage regulation in system-on-glass display platforms.

items.title: A superhard and ultra-wide bandgap tetragonal C3N2 featuring a deep-ultraviolet isotropic point
items.abstract: The pursuit of materials that simultaneously exhibit superhard mechanical behavior and ultra‑wide bandgap semiconductor characteristics remains a critical challenge for next‑generation precision deep-ultraviolet (DUV) optics and extreme-condition applications. Here, we report P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 , a novel tetragonal carbon nitride phase predicted and validated by first‑principles calculations. This structure features a three‑dimensional covalent network with four‑coordinated carbon and three‑coordinated nitrogen atoms. Formation enthalpy calculations show that P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 becomes thermodynamically stable against decomposition into graphite and N 2 above 28 GPa, indicating its feasibility for high‑pressure high‑temperature synthesis. The material exhibits an indirect ultra-wide bandgap of 4.27 eV and a macroscopic Vicker’s hardness of 47.7 GPa, placing it in the superhard regime. Notably, P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 possesses highly anisotropic mechanical and optical properties. Its hole effective mass along the [001] direction is only 0.545 m 0 , significantly smaller than those of GaN and ZnO and comparable to hexagonal boron nitride, suggesting a potential advantage for p‑type doping. Furthermore, the calculated optical response reveals an isotropic point at ~5.2 eV (238 nm) with zero birefringence near the transparency threshold, offering a unique mechanism for narrow-band isotropic filtering and distortion-free deep-ultraviolet optics. These characteristics make P4 2 /nmc -C 3 N 2 a promising multifunctional material bridging superhardness and tailored anisotropic optical functionality.

items.title: A High‐Speed Dielectric Approach to Track Domain Structure Evolution in Operating Ferroelectric Devices
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric switching is a fundamental process underpinning the functionality of modern electronic devices, yet the dynamic evolution of ferroelectric domain structures, especially in thin films, remains poorly understood. While established techniques such as piezoresponse force microscopy and transmission electron microscopy successfully image ferroelectric domains, they fail to capture global transient domain dynamics due to resolution limits and slow acquisition. In addition, performing in operando measurements on functional devices is highly impractical with these methods. This gap has hindered progress in understanding and controlling ferroelectric switching in thin films, which is critical for applications from nonvolatile memories to sensors. Here, we introduce a novel approach using amplitude‐modulated dielectric signals in the frequency domain to drastically reduce acquisition times to microseconds, instead of seconds. This method allows real‐time, nondestructive, and in operando tracking of domain wall density and mobility in ferroelectric devices, overcoming the limitations of existing techniques. By applying this approach to (Ba,Ca)TiO 3 thin films, we directly probe transient states in response to electric pulses, revealing previously inaccessible dynamics. This breakthrough opens new avenues for studying dynamic domain switching in thin films and promises to advance the design of ferroelectric materials for next‐generation electronic devices.

items.title: 2D Memory Transistors for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: The boom in artificial intelligence has driven in-memory computing for high speed and power efficiency. Motivated by the need, neuromorphic computing (NC)—mimicking biological spike neural networks—ies a promising alternative that requires artificial neurons and synapses to construct NC circuits. 2D memory transistors have received intensive interest in recent research for NC applications as both artificial neurons and synapses with additional advantages for high device density and energy efficiency. This review intends to highlight recent progress made in the exploration of 2D memory transistors and their implementation into electrical and optoelectronic NC circuits. Discussions of remaining challenges and future perspectives are also provided.

items.title: 忆阻器与忆阻网络的SM建模:档位判据、事件级联与统一结构域
items.abstract: 摘要 忆阻器最深刻的现象——量子化电导台阶、随机电报噪声、雪崩开关——携带离散结构的信息,是连续与统计工具箱未问也未答的问题。本文以SM立体矩阵理论(元=独立耦合量,阶=每耦合量的分辨率档位数;3元3阶即3个耦合元素各3个分辨状态)建模忆阻器个体与网络,给出四组判据:档位归约判据|G−nG0|≤Δ/2、跨档概率统一公式P=erfc(Δ/(2√2σ))、设计裕度Δ≥6σ(误判率≤0.27%)、事件级联幂律τ=f(K,p)。预言A(判读成功率S=erf(Δ/(2√2σ)))改以held-out检验消除循环验证:档1-2拟合σ=0.304G0,档3预测命中(误差<1pp),档4预测偏差+10pp、与σ漂移至0.390G0精确一致——档位依赖噪声由此获得定量证据。雪崩指数(隧穿涨落驱动下τ≈−2.08,单点拟合)落入纳米线网络文献区间(1.8~2.9)。结论:忆阻器的离散性不是缺陷而是结构本体,SM给出统一的重构入口与可验证预言。 Abstract The sharpest phenomena of memristors, quantised conductance steps, random telegraph noise and avalanche switching, carry information about discrete structure that continuous and statistical toolboxes neither ask for nor answer. This paper models individual memristors and memristive networks within Stereo Matrix Theory, where an element is an independent coupling quantity and an order is the number of resolution levels per coupling; three elements at three orders means three coupling quantities each with three resolution states. Four groups of criteria are obtained: the level-reduction criterion on the deviation of conductance from n times the quantum, a unified inter-level transition probability in erfc form, the design margin of six sigma (misjudgement rate at most 0.27 per cent), and an event-cascade power law. Prediction A, the read-out success rate, is reformulated as a held-out test to remove circular verification: fitting on levels one and two gives a noise of 0.304 in units of the quantum, level three is predicted correctly within one percentage point, and level four deviates by +10 percentage points, exactly consistent with a drift of the noise to 0.390. Level-dependent noise thus acquires quantitative evidence. The avalanche exponent obtained under tunnelling-fluctuation driving, about -2.08 from a single-point fit, falls inside the literature range of 1.8 to 2.9 for nanowire networks. The conclusion is that the discreteness of memristors is not a defect but the structure itself, and that SM provides a unified entry point for reconstruction together with testable predictions. 本记录当前为中文版(Chinese version);英文版将作为新版本追加(English version to follow as a new version)。
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: vExpert: Virtualizing Expert Storage for Adaptive Load Balancing in Distributed MoE Inference
items.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become prevailing, yet their distributed deployment suffers from severe dynamic load imbalance due to the conflict between static expert placement and inherent routing dynamism. While host DRAM offers capacity to avoid static device storage for load balancing, we identify existing offloading works fundamentally fail in distributed inference due to two overlooked challenges: (1) coupled performance impacts of runtime Host-to-Device transfers due to load dynamism and shared PCIe topology; (2) system-level memory overhead incurred by DRAM usage at scale. In this paper, we propose vExpert that shifts DRAM offloading paradigm from partial residency to full redundancy through virtualized expert storage. We pioneer the first systematic performance model that jointly captures H2D latency, PCIe contention, and load imbalance, building a lightweight allocator to dynamically map physical experts to virtual slots runtime. A novel disaggregated manager is designed to reduce memory overhead in multi-process environments. Evaluated on DeepSeek-V3.1 within an 8-node H100 cluster, vExpert improves load balance ratio by up to 55% and achieves 1.2$\times$ end-to-end speedup.

items.title: eBPF-Driven Adaptive Lifetime-Aware Data Placement for Shared FDP SSDs
items.abstract: NVMe Flexible Data Placement (FDP) reduces SSD write amplification by separating data with different lifetimes to minimize garbage collection (GC) copying. However, on shared servers, multiple tenants generate more lifetime classes than the available placement handles. Existing approaches rely on static mappings or application-specific knowledge, failing to capture runtime lifetimes and adapt to changing workloads. The challenge is to identify which data die together and determine which classes should be separated to maximize GC savings under a limited handle budget. We present eFDP, an eBPF-based system that automatically learns data lifetimes and manages FDP placement for unmodified applications on a stock Linux kernel. By tracking writes and invalidations, eFDP identifies lifetime classes and estimates the GC copying saved by separating them. It first assigns each tenant a handle, then allocates the remaining handles to the separations offering the greatest savings. It also re-plans placement when active tenants change. With four database tenants on an emulated FDP SSD, eFDP eliminates twice as much excess write amplification as tenant-level isolation and improves every writing tenant's throughput by 19-23%. On an enterprise FDP SSD, given RocksDB's levels, it matches a manually optimized placement using three handles instead of five. After a tenant switch, eFDP re-plans within seven minutes and maintains 25% lower write amplification than the original layout even after an hour.

items.title: UniCompress: From Multi-LoRA Experts to One Compact Model for Edge Intelligence
items.abstract: Embodied and edge systems increasingly rely on vision-language models (VLMs) to support heterogeneous skills, yet deploying a separate task adapter for each skill while retaining a high-precision backbone creates substantial memory and management costs. We present UniCompress, a deployment-oriented framework that converts multi-task expertise into one compact, adapter-free model. Starting from a consolidated BF16 Qwen3-VL-4B teacher, UniCompress constructs an asymmetric INT2 student using GPTQ initialization and teacher-guided quantization recovery. The approach jointly quantizes and recovers the projection weights in the vision encoder and language backbone, enabling aggressive compression of the complete vision-language model while preserving its multi-task behavior. We evaluate UniCompress on four heterogeneous embodied tasks: posture recognition, household-safety understanding, multimodal dialogue routing, and mobile-GUI action prediction. UniCompress reduces the approximate weight storage from 8.9 GB in BF16 to 2.1 GB in INT2, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 76%. It improves the INT2 macro task score by 34.3 percentage points over GPTQ-INT2 while remaining within 0.9 points of the consolidated BF16 teacher. These results demonstrate the potential of teacher-guided joint vision-language INT2 recovery for deploying a single multi-skill VLM on resource-constrained embodied platforms.

items.title: Thermal 3D Magnetic Imaging of Advanced Packages
items.abstract: Advanced packages provide a flexible design platform for high-performance computing, at the cost of increased complexity. Thermal reliability is a critical metric in the design of new 2.5D and 3D microelectronics packages, but the current state-of-the-art requires testing to failure or full thermal test chip fabrication, which generally makes advanced packaging development more expensive and less US-friendly. We have developed magnetic nanoparticle technology that can remotely image temperature through millimeters of material. Recently, we have made significant advances toward applying this technology to accurately image temperature and heat-flow in commercial packaging materials and in proxy advanced packages, without the need for de-processing, which will provide the semiconductor industry with thermal data to aid in failure analysis and comparison against simulations.

items.title: The Ideal Switch®: Glass-based Device With Demonstrated Reliability
items.abstract: Menlo Microsystems Inc. (Menlo Micro) has introduced a MEMS switch that utilizes both a glass substrate and a glass cap with through glass via (TGV) technology to provide an all-glass packaging solution. The MEMS switch technology combined with an all- glass packaging solution, has resulted in the Ideal Switch®. It is the world’s smallest, most reliable, and efficient micro-mechanical switch that can be used for numerous RF and power applications. The Ideal Switch® gains superior performance as well as mechanical, electrical and thermal reliability from several aspects of the MEMS and glass packaging design including robust electrical contacts, low electrical loss of glass, and hermetic TGVs which provide a well-controlled environment. This controlled environment is crucial for attaining reliable performance over billions of cycles. In addition to long lifetimes, parasitics are reduced by >75% vs. Si based RF devices enabling the devices to have a wide operational bandwidth from DC to > 50 GHz and high signal integrity. To enable the volume manufacture of this device, Menlo Micro has driven advancements in the glass supply chain over the past several years, leveraging mostly standard semiconductor manufacturing processes, on glass substrates (with and without TGV). In addition to hermetic TGV, the device contains multi-layer plated and deposited structures, hermetic wafer level glass to glass bonding, post-bond die singulation and device packaging in multiple formats. These devices pass standard JEDEC reliability testing and have operational lifetime in excess of 3 billion cycles. In this presentation we will discuss a number of advanced packaging processes employed by Menlo Micro in the manufacturing process in a volume manufacturing environment as well as key performance metrics of the Ideal Switch®. We will also discuss some early failure modes seen from this glass-based device in both device and packaged form, and how Menlo Micro has established solutions and demonstrated reliable performance relative to JEDEC standards.

items.title: Takeaway & Assignment of Packaging Technology for Heterogenous + Large Body Packages
items.abstract: For decades, Moore’s Law has driven semiconductor scaling by improving transistor density, performance, and cost efficiency. However, as technology approaches sub-1 nm nodes, physical and economic limitations—including rising design complexity, mask cost, and yield challenges—have slowed this trend, making large monolithic SoCs increasingly unsustainable. Consequently, advanced packaging has emerged as a key driver of system-level scaling, with heterogeneous integration extending Moore’s Law in a “More than Moore” paradigm. This shift enables chiplet-based architectures that integrate logic, memory, and specialized functions within a single package, but also drives rapid increases in package size and complexity. AI and HPC applications demand extreme bandwidth, power, and compute density, relying on technologies such as HBM, 2.5D interposers, and 3D stacking. These advancements introduce significant challenges, including interconnect scaling, thermal management, power delivery, mechanical stress and warpage, yield management, and supply chain constraints. Addressing these issues requires close co-design across silicon, package, and system domains. This work presents an overview of heterogeneous integration and large-body packaging and outlines key technical and economic challenges as future “homework” for enabling scalable solutions in the post-Moore era.

items.title: Separating Motion Artifacts from Biomarker Signals in Flexible MoS2 FET Cortisol Sensors: A Coupled Multiphysics Model and Finite-Element Analysis of Strain-Binding Cross-Talk and Mitigation Strategies
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors can monitor cortisol in sweat, but their atomically thin channel is strongly piezoresistive, so body movement produces current changes that resemble hormone signals. We present a six-stage multiphysics model that links wrist and elbow flexion and walking to a strain-equivalent false cortisol concentration. Channel strain is computed by plane-strain finite-element analysis in the open-source solver Elmer, verified against laminate beam theory, and drives compact models of piezoresistance, Schottky-barrier lowering, strain-binding cross-talk, aptamer kinetics and Debye screening. For a 25 µm polyimide patch the model predicts wrist flexion produces a current artifact of 44% of the full-scale cortisol response and walking 5 to 11 ng/mL of false cortisol, with about 70% of the artifact arising at the Schottky contacts. Low-pass filtering leaves the non-zero mean of unipolar flexion (22% of full scale). Twin-sensor subtraction is limited by gauge mismatch and by a cross-talk floor proportional to aptamer occupancy, 1.0 to 2.8% of full scale across the physiological range at the wrist. With a 2.5 µm substrate and matched twin channels the residual falls to 0.9 to 1.3 ng/mL, not consistently below a 1 ng/mL target at the wrist for the assumed affinity. A rigid island under the channel retains 18 to 109% of the baseline strain under end-moment loading and about 300% when the skin imposes the curvature, so it fails to isolate the channel in bending. The predicted magnitudes scale with the assumed threshold shift; design guidelines by body location are given.

items.title: Scalable Four-Layer Redistribution Layers via Fully Additive Build-Up: Demonstration of Defect-Free Multilayer Integration
items.abstract: The increasing complexity of heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based electronic systems is driving demand for multilayer redistribution layer (RDL) architectures with reliable lateral routing and vertical interconnection capability. However, increasing the number of RDL layers remains challenging due to cumulative surface topography, interfacial instability, layer-by-layer alignment complexity, and microvia integration challenges. In this work, we report the first four-layer RDL architecture fabricated using the fully additive Sequential Build-Up Covalent Bonded Metallization (SBU-CBM) process. The structure was fabricated on an FR-4 substrate and comprised four lateral copper redistribution layers interconnected by three staggered copper microvias embedded within five polyurethane dielectric layers. X-ray computed tomography (XCT) confirmed the successful formation of the four-layer architecture and the spatially distributed staggered microvia configuration. Optical and topographical analyses revealed progressive surface-topography accumulation with increasing RDL layer number, while the fabricated stack remained structurally stable with no visible delamination, edge separation, or large-scale deformation. This work represents the highest multilayer integration level achieved to date using the SBU-CBM process and establishes an important milestone toward fully additive multilayer RDL manufacturing for next-generation heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based electronic systems.

items.title: SL²OT: Scaling LLM Locality on Tile with Distributed 3D-DRAM as Unified Memory
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly limited by memory bandwidth and latency rather than compute throughput. Our modeled 3D-DRAM system offers 4× the raw bandwidth of the HBM reference. However, high remote-access latency (~3× local latency) and redundant NoC traffic reduce its effective bandwidth below that of HBM. We present SL2OT, a hardware--software memory system that harnesses the raw bandwidth of distributed 3D-DRAM to improve LLM performance, guided by four principles---Scalability, Locality, Orchestration, and Temporality. Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) localizes remote accesses through asynchronous prefetching while preserving a unified address space. Asynchronous Request Coalescing (ARC) merges asynchronously arriving requests to the same address across tiles, reducing redundant transfers. Kernel Memory Migration (KMM) prefetches data for upcoming kernels, overlapping host-to-device transfers with computation. Accel-Sim evaluations using A100-80GB SASS traces show 1.22--3.03× speedup over HBM across operators and transformer blocks, and 3.51× speedup over naive distributed 3D-DRAM on GEMM. A matched FlashAttention study reduces mean global-read latency by 73.4% relative to Mesh. SL^2 OT reaches 72.2% effective bandwidth utilization, versus 15.1% without SL2OT.
items.venue: International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS)

items.title: Reverse Laser Thermo-Compression Bonding (R-LTC) for Simultaneous Thermal Uniformity and Thermomechanical Stress Mitigation in Heterogeneous Chiplet Integration
items.abstract: Chiplet‑based heterogeneous integration has become a key packaging approach for high‑performance artificial intelligence systems; however, assembly‑induced warpage, stand‑off height (SOH) non‑uniformity, and accelerated intermetallic compound (IMC) growth remain major challenges in large‑area modules. These issues are primarily driven by a mismatch in the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and non‑uniform heat distribution during solder bonding. This study introduces a Reverse Laser Thermo-Compression bonding (R-LTC) scheme based on thermal inversion, in which heat is delivered from the substrate side rather than the chiplet side. This approach fundamentally modifies the heat flow path in heterogeneous structures, mitigating thermal gradients induced by mismatches in thermal conductivity. A systematic comparison of reflow, Top Laser-Assisted Bonding (T-LAB), Reverse Laser-Assisted Bonding (R-LAB), Thermo-Compression Bonding (TCB), and R-LTC was conducted under conditions where the edge Cu-pillar bump temperature reached 245 ± 5 °C. The results demonstrated that conventional approaches have difficulty simultaneously achieving thermal uniformity and minimizing thermomechanical stress in heterogeneous structures, highlighting a critical limitation in current bonding technologies. Under the same conditions, R-LTC demonstrated a significant reduction in temperature non-uniformity (ΔT reduced from 52 °C to 4 °C) and suppressed IMC thickness by ~26% compared to TCB, while maintaining comparable SOH control and warpage behavior. This substrate-driven heat flux homogenization, together with reduced thermal exposure time, minimizes diffusion-driven interfacial reactions and is expected to reduce thermomechanical stress, as supported by simulation results showing decreased von Mises stress. This study demonstrates that thermal inversion is a promising design approach for bonding processes, enabling scalable and reliable heterogeneous integration for next-generation 2.5D/3D packaging.

items.title: ReconLLM: Execution-Internal Interconnect Specialization for MoE Serving on Chiplet Systems
items.abstract: Chiplet technology and active interposers enable dynamic reconfiguration of physical routing topologies. However, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving introduces pronounced phase heterogeneity in communication demands, creating a structural mismatch with fixed interconnects. We propose ReconLLM, a hardware/software co-designed framework for execution-internal interconnect specialization in MoE serving on chiplet-based active interposers. ReconLLM shifts interconnect adaptation to offline compilation: for deterministic phases (prefill and decode), it analytically extracts phase-specific communication requirements from model structure and execution order; for input-dependent MoE routing phases, it pre-generates a bounded family of routing templates based on serving parameters such as batch size and expert-load skew, with lightweight binding performed at runtime. The framework then synthesizes an offline library of phase-optimal topologies and triggers one-shot synchronous switching at runtime-visible phase/window boundaries. To support this model, we design ARIC, a lightweight reconfigurable active interposer that enables asynchronous preloading, double-buffered configuration state, one-shot synchronous commit, and direction-safe switching. Fabricated in 28 nm technology, ARIC operates at 500 MHz, delivers 400 GB/s bandwidth, and supports sub-microsecond one-shot reconfiguration. Evaluations on ASTRA-Sim 2.0 using a normalized 4×4 chiplet platform show that ReconLLM reduces communication cycles by 45.4%--52.2% compared with the fixed sparse interposer baseline (ARIC-fixed) and achieves up to 3.05× communication speedup over fixed mesh-class interposers. On the same workloads, ReconLLM improves serving metrics by reducing time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 1.4%--9.1%, time-per-output-token (TPOT) by 27.4%--44.2%, and end-to-end critical-path wall cycles by 23.9%--39.5%, while increasing steady-state throughput by 37.8%--79.3%. These results demonstrate that phase-level interconnect specialization is a powerful optimization dimension for MoE systems on physically constrained chiplet substrates.
items.venue: International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS)

items.title: Packaging Technologies for Modern High-Reliability Electronics for Harsh Environment
items.abstract: Modern high reliability systems require electronic packaging that can withstand extreme thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses while meeting the demand for increased functional density and a miniaturized design to realize SWAP gains. This paper explores critical design and process considerations for high-reliability applications, focusing on the strategic design and assembly of Ceramic Leadless Chip Carriers (CLCC), ceramic J-Lead and ceramic Area Array (Ball Grid Arrays (CBGA), Ceramic Column Grid array (CCGA) packages. While plastic packages are heavily favored in commercial consumer electronics due to their low cost and lightweight nature, ceramic structures remain indispensable for mission-critical, high-power, and aerospace systems. Several generic ceramic COTS package sizes were tested with different board materials and reliability gains were assessed. Size and material tradeoff studies showed the effect of these factors on reliability. This paper will highlight some of the observations that will guide designers to consider for high reliability.

items.title: PIMROP: A Feasibility Study of Return-Oriented Programming on Commercial Processing-in-Memory Architectures
items.abstract: Processing-in-Memory places small programmable cores on the memory device, where they execute beside the DRAM banks and beyond the control-flow defenses that protect host programs. The security of this in-memory code is an attack surface that remains largely unstudied. We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA. We show that return-oriented programming is feasible on a real, commercially shipped PIM instruction set, the UPMEM DPU, whose DRAM Processing Units run C compiled by a dedicated LLVM toolchain. We build Galileo-for-DPU, a gadget scanner adapted to the DPU's fixed-width, 8-byte-aligned RISC encoding, and run it entirely on the UPMEM functional simulator in a reproducible Docker and VM environment. We find the runtime library that every kernel links already yields 517 non-trivial gadgets covering all five canonical ROP primitive classes, and all 13 PrIM benchmarks we scanned carry gadgets as well. We then demonstrate two verified end-to-end attacks, each reproducible on 10 of 10 runs. In the first, a stack buffer overflow in a DPU kernel overwrites the saved return address and diverts control into a routine that copies a secret into host-readable memory. In the second, we leak the same secret using a chain of reused gadgets alone, without diverting control into any such routine. We further show that two standard defenses--stack canaries and _FORTIFY_SOURCE-style bounds-check fortification--fail on the DPU in ways specific to the platform (misplaced canary, silently inactive wrapper), and we verify a bounds-checked DMA that stops the attack on 10 of 10 runs with no effect on benign requests. To enable further research on PIM security, we open-source Galileo-for-DPU and our testing harness at https://github.com/wtegge2/ROP-in-PIM.

items.title: Ohutkalvojen kemiallinen kaasufaasietsaus ja atomikerrosetsaus niobiumpentakloridilla
items.abstract: The need for faster, more powerful, and energy-efficient computing drives the development of smaller and more complex semiconductor devices. Making these devices requires new approaches in deposition and etching of materials. Of the latter, gas phase etching (GPE) and its variant atomic layer etching (ALE) have gained popularity as they offer selective, isotropic, and uniform etching also in non-line-of-sight areas. The literature part of this thesis reviews the current state of thermal GPE and ALE processes. Principles and mechanisms of GPE and ALE are introduced, with specific focus on the mechanisms of thermal ALE. Selected GPE processes are discussed in detail, and a thorough account of the published ALE processes is given. The review of ALE processes reveals how different chemistries are used in the ALE of different classes of materials such as oxides, metals, and nitrides. The goal of the experimental work was to develop new thermal GPE and ALE processes for the semiconductor industry. A secondary objective was to avoid fluorine-containing etchants as they can be harmful for the etching equipment and its operators. They can also leave difficult to remove fluoride contamination which may affect device performance. NbCl5 as an etchant for metal oxides was taken as the starting point, as it has previously been observed to etch Nb2O5. NbCl5 was found to etch Ta2O5, TiO2, ZrO2 and HfO2 selectively to Al2O3, SiO2 and TiN. The NbCl5 etchant was further applied to ALE of metallic tantalum and molybdenum via oxidation and selective removal of the oxidized layer with NbCl5. ALE of metal nitrides TiN and TaN was done with O3 as the oxidizer. The properties of the thin films were studied before and after partial etching using methods such as x-ray diffraction, x-ray reflectivity, scanning electron microscopy, energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), atomic force microscopy, and resistivity measurements. Mechanisms of the etching processes were elucidated using thermodynamic analysis, in situ quadrupole mass spectrometry and in vacuo XPS and low energy ion scattering. Properties of the metal oxide and molybdenum films were largely unaffected by the etching. The structure of the TiN films was likewise unchanged. For tantalum and TaN, oxidation of the films beyond the surface layer was observed and required careful control of the process parameters to avoid. Residues from the etching were observed to be minimal, with only small amounts of chlorine seen on the oxide films and metallic tantalum. On the nitride films, small niobium residues were also detected with XPS. NbCl5 turns out to be a versatile etchant. It etches metal oxides by itself and metals and metal nitrides in ALE with different oxidizers. By adjusting the etching temperature and varying the oxidizer, selectivity between these different materials can be achieved.

items.title: NN-Based FeFET Compact Modeling for SPICE Simulation
items.abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. This work presents a derivative-free NN training framework employing spectral normalization to naturally smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise. Using drain current measurements from a fabricated 28 nm ferroelectric device, we design an NN-based compact model that captures the full spectrum of polarization amplitudes and supports dynamic polarization switching in transient simulations. To demonstrate its capability, we deploy the model in a commercial SPICE software to simulate write and read operations for large-scale memory arrays with up to 512x512 size, including parasitic effects. Our approach bridges raw measurements with NN-based SPICE-compatible transistor modeling, significantly reducing model development time and enabling rapid circuit-level prototyping for emerging devices.

items.title: Model-Based Quantized Edge Vision Inference: Component Detection System for the STM32N6 Circuit Diagram
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of the rapid development of Edge AI, deploying object detection models on resource-constrained microcontrollers (MCUs) presents simultaneous challenges in terms of computing power, memory, and accuracy. This paper proposes an improved algorithm for detecting components in circuit diagrams and deploys it on an STM32N6 edge device. At the algorithmic level, using YOLOv8n as the baseline model, the study addresses the characteristics of circuit diagram components—which are extremely small and often arranged horizontally or vertically—by introducing an NWD-SIoU joint loss function to replace the default CIoU loss, thereby providing stable gradient signals and directional alignment for tiny objects.Additionally, Dropout regularization is incorporated into the detection head structure of YOLOv8n to address overfitting in circuit diagram training scenarios. Compared to the original algorithm, the improved algorithm achieves a 0.036 increase in F1-score, with precision and recall improving by 0.017 and 0.031, respectively. At the deployment level, post-training quantization from FP32 to INT8 was completed, reducing the weight size from 12 MB to 3.23 MB. To address the limited SRAM capacity of the STM32N6, a heterogeneous storage hierarchy allocation scheme was designed: static weights are stored in external Flash, while runtime activation tensors are locked in the NPU’s dedicated RAM. This approach frees up SRAM capacity while accelerating model execution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a balance of size, accuracy, and speed on the STM32N6 platform. It validates the feasibility of running complex vision models on edge devices and provides a reusable technical path for the implementation of edge AI in the field of industrial vision inspection.
items.venue: International Journal of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering

items.title: Metrology challenges and trends for through-glass vias in advanced semiconductor packaging
items.abstract: Abstract Through-glass vias (TGVs) are emerging as a key technology for three-dimensional heterogeneous integration and advanced semiconductor packaging because of their low electrical loss, tailorable thermal expansion, and compatibility with large-format panel-level processing. However, the optical transparency, refractive properties, and brittleness of glass create significant inspection challenges, making reliable high-throughput metrology a major barrier to TGV manufacturing. This review presents a requirements-driven framework for TGV metrology that links fabrication processes and defect mechanisms to quantitative measurement needs. Key defects associated with laser ablation, laser-induced deep etching, and metallization including microcracks, nanovoids, sidewall roughness, via taper, copper protrusion, and thermomechanical cracking are examined. Representative metrology requirements include detection of sub-1-µm microcracks and sub-2-µm voids, characterization of sidewall roughness below 50 nm, taper-angle uncertainty below 0.1°, and panel-scale inspection at thousands of vias per second. Established and emerging techniques, including shadowgraphy, optical coherence tomography (OCT), spectral reflectometry, digital holographic microscopy (DHM), and two-photon fluorescence, are compared in terms of measurement capability, uncertainty, calibration, traceability, and throughput. No single technique currently meets the combined requirements for resolution, field of view, defect sensitivity, and high-volume throughput. Multimodal inspection, AI-assisted defect classification, physics-informed reconstruction, virtual metrology, and TGV-specific reference artefacts and standards are therefore identified as key directions toward robust, traceable, and scalable TGV metrology.

items.title: Mechanistic Origins of Atomic-Scale Control in Plasma-Thermal Atomic-Layer Etching of Nickel
items.abstract: Abstract We present a mechanistic density functional theory (DFT) investigation of atomic-layer etching of nickel previously modified by surface nitride formation. Etching is performed via gas-phase formic acid, and we focus on the influence of nitrogen coverage on reaction energetics and mechanisms. Using two models for the etching process, removing a partial or full surface Ni atomic layer, we examine formic acid adsorption and reaction by dehydrogenation and hydrogen transfer to nitrogen. We show that the mechanism for Ni etching initiates with the formation of metastable nickel-formate surface complexes, partially decoordinated from other Ni on the surface, and their desorption with accompanying ammonia release. Product stability calculations reveal that polynuclear nickel-formate-ammonia complexes are thermodynamically favored over mononuclear species, with meta-generalized gradient approximation (GGA) functionals (SCAN, R2SCAN, R2SCAN-rVV10) providing consistently lower (more favorable) reaction energies than Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) and better in line with experimental observations. Mechanistic pathways on the stepped Ni(843) surface demonstrate a strong dependence on nitrogen coverage: low coverage preserves surface crystallinity but limits the thermodynamic driving force for product desorption, whereas high coverage populates terrace and subsurface sites, weakens Ni–Ni bonds, and facilitates surface rearrangements, forming nickel-formate surface complexes that render early desorption steps accessible. These findings underscore the critical role of nitrogen content in enabling controlled and efficient etching and provide atomistic insight into surface complex formation, hydrogen stabilization, and nickel removal. This work establishes a computational framework to optimize atomic-layer etching of nickel nitride surfaces.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C

items.title: Materials-Architecture Co-Design of 3D Integrated Circuits: Resolving the Dielectric Thermal Choke and Eliminating TSV Shear via Atomically Ordered B₅C₆N₅ Superlattices and Uncompromised PG(3, q) Routing
items.abstract: ## Abstract Three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D-ICs) for high-density AI tensor acceleration face a fundamental physical bottleneck: conventional inter-die bonding oxides ($\mathrm{SiO}_2$, $k_{\mathrm{ox}} = 1.40\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$) and carbon-doped silicon nitrides ($\mathrm{SiCN}$, $k = 2.20\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$) act as planar thermal blankets between stacked active tiers. In prior projective geometric 3D-IC architectures (*S3P17*), overcoming this dielectric thermal choke required drilling continuous, macro-scale copper Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs, $k_{\mathrm{Cu}} = 385\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$) across active silicon substrates and sacrificing $k - \lambda$ channels per node of the finite projective geometry $PG(3, q)$ to serve as vertical thermal chimneys. However, macro-TSVs induce $305.59\,\mathrm{MPa}$ of Lamé thermoelastic shear stress upon cool-down from back-end-of-line (BEOL) bonding ($523.15\,\mathrm{K} \to 300.0\,\mathrm{K}$), enforcing $8.28\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ transistor Keep-Out Zones (KOZs) that forfeit $215.41\,\mu\mathrm{m}^2$ of active CMOS area per via. Here we introduce a closed-loop **Materials-Architecture Co-Design** framework structured across a two-horizon foundry roadmap: (1) **Horizon 1 (Industrial Bridge)**, pairing atomic-layer-deposited $\mathrm{AlN}$ lateral heat spreaders with low-$\kappa$ $\mathrm{SiOC}$ signal-pad collars ($k_\parallel = 162.00\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}} = 3.20$); and (2) **Horizon 2 (First-Principles Target)**, synthesizing an **atomically ordered zincblende-derived $\mathrm{B_5 C_6 N_5}$ superlattice** ($(\mathrm{BN})_{0.625}(\mathrm{C}_2)_{0.375}$, $98.74\%\,sp^3$ hybridization with $1.26\%$ compliant insulating $sp^2\text{-BN}$ grain boundaries). By preserving translational crystal symmetry ($\eta_{\mathrm{order}} = 0.9992$), the ordered supercell suppresses Klemens $\omega^4$ point-defect phonon scattering, achieving $k_\parallel = 186.38\text{--}210.57\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ ($23.78\times\text{--}26.18\times$ above disordered IBAD $\mathrm{BCN}$ alloys) and a Kapitza-coupled cross-plane effective conductivity of $k_{\perp,\mathrm{eff}} = 116.97\,\mathrm{W/(m\cdot K)}$ across a $1.0\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ isolation stack ($84.60\times$ above $\mathrm{SiO}_2$). Simultaneously, matching the integrated thermal strain of silicon across the entire BEOL bonding envelope ($\int_{300\,\mathrm{K}}^{523.15\,\mathrm{K}} [\alpha_{\mathrm{BCN}}(T) - \alpha_{\mathrm{Si}}(T)]\,dT = 0.00\,\mathrm{ppm}$) collapses residual film stress to $\le 2.00\,\mathrm{MPa}$ under $\pm 0.05\%$ stoichiometric fab tolerances ($99.34\%$ reduction vs. $\mathrm{Cu}$ TSVs). Coupled with pulsed ALD/PECVD growth, chemical-mechanical planarization ($R_a = 0.10\,\mathrm{nm}$), and $\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}$ plasma $\mathrm{B\text{-}OH}$ hydrophilic activation, macro-TSVs are eliminated entirely in favor of BEOL-confined sub-micron direct $\mathrm{Cu\text{-}Cu}$ hybrid bond pads ($0.00\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ active silicon KOZ). In 24,000-cell anisotropic 3D Finite-Volume simulations at $225\,\mathrm{W/cm^2}$, peak die temperature drops from $104.68^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (clustered baseline) and $82.32^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (*S3P17*) to **$61.19^\circ\mathrm{C}$**, with vertical inter-tier thermal differentials collapsing from $23.78^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to **$1.34^\circ\mathrm{C}$**—liberating $100\%$ of $PG(3, q)$ projective lines for non-blocking AllReduce tensor communication ($2.333\times$ to $8.111\times$ bandwidth gain).

items.title: Iteration-Free Candidate Pruning and an Index-Domain VLSI Architecture for Sort-Free MIMO Box Decoding up to 1024-QAM
items.abstract: Wi-Fi~7 and 5G NR use constellations up to $4096$-QAM and $1024$-QAM at multi-gigabit peak rates. The MIMO detector must sustain these rates at a low cost. Linear MMSE detection meets these rates at low cost but loses several dB in SNR. $K$-Best detection recovers this loss, but its per-layer sorting grows with the modulation order and needs large sorting networks or deep pipelines at these rates. Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search detector whose complexity does not depend on the QAM order, and its deterministic pruning keeps the cost fixed as the MIMO size grows. Single-step candidate pruning (SCP) is fully parallel but less accurate, while iterative candidate pruning (ICP) is more accurate, but its selection loop costs either throughput or area. This paper proposes Max-Min-Exchange Candidate Pruning (MMECP), which replaces the selection loop of ICP with a single max-min exchange without a feedback path and keeps \mbox{near-$K$-Best} performance. The paper also presents a VLSI architecture that represents each candidate by its integer constellation index, so that candidates and their distances are obtained by bit selection instead of operations on symbol values. A $4\times4$ detector synthesized in TSMC $16$\,nm detects one vector per cycle at $1$\,GHz for $64$- to $1024$-QAM and produces up to $40$\,Gb/s, while its gate count grows by $63\%$ over this range. Its normalized hardware efficiency is $2.3\times$, $12\times$ and $14\times$ that of the best compared hard-output detector at $64$-, $256$- and $1024$-QAM.

items.title: Interchannel Coupling in Two-Channel THz Detectors]{Interchannel Coupling in Two-Channel AlGaN/GaN Plasmonic Terahertz Detectors
items.abstract: Abstract A second two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) forms in AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) capped with AlN. The strong response of measured double-channel terahertz (THz) detectors has been attributed to the coupling between the channels, but a measured responsivity also contains the antenna coupling and the bias, so whether the coupling itself helps is not known. We isolate the coupling by modelling plasma-wave rectification in this detector and in uncapped and GaN-capped single-channel references. A semi-analytical theory, to our knowledge the first for rectification in asymmetric coupled channels, joins analytic coupled eigenmodes of the gated region to transmission-line access regions and splits the photovoltage exactly into modal terms. A full-device perturbation model adds Schr\"odinger--Poisson and two-dimensional electrostatics, a floating drain and hot electrons. A nonlinear time-domain solver verifies its implementation within 3.0\% over 375 cases, the model reproduces the Dyakonov--Shur limit within 0.4\%, and a Boltzmann (Mermin) estimate keeps kinetic corrections below 0.3\% at zero bias. We find that in these AlN-capped devices the coupling does not help. For matched, conjugate or direct antenna coupling and a floating drain, the single-channel devices respond best (0.22--0.28\,V/W at 1\,THz, against 0.10\,V/W). A design map over upper-channel mobility and barrier thickness shows that a better upper channel makes the detector worse: it shunts the access regions and lowers the device impedance, while the rectification itself changes little. Toward threshold the small-signal noise-equivalent power falls to about 20--23\,pW/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ in the hydrodynamic model. Both models apply to other stacks of capacitively coupled channels.

items.title: High-resolution 3D Inspection of Bonding Defects in HBM using Optically-coupled X-ray Computed Laminography
items.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and high-performance computing has accelerated demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), in which dozens of DRAM dies are vertically stacked and interconnected through through-silicon vias (TSVs) and micro-bumps. Bonding defects such as bump voids, non-wets, and misalignment in these interconnects critically affect device yield and reliability, making nondestructive three-dimensional (3D) inspection essential. Conventional X-ray imaging systems rely on geometric magnification, which forces the use of low-power nano- or micro-focus sources and results in scan times exceeding 30 minutes per HBM module. In this work, we present an optically-coupled X-ray computed laminography (CL) system that decouples spatial resolution from the X-ray focal spot size by placing a scintillator in direct contact with the object and acquiring images through an optical magnification stage. This configuration allows the use of a high-power X-ray tube with a large focal spot without sacrificing resolution. A sub-micrometer spatial resolution was achieved using a 11-μm-thick CsI:Tl scintillator and a 10× optical lens, and 3D reconstruction of an HBM module from 1600 projections clearly resolved DRAM-to-DRAM and DRAM-to-logic micro-bumps along with bump voids. The proposed system establishes a practical route toward high-throughput, high-resolution in-line inspection of advanced 2.5D/3D semiconductor packages.

items.title: Fluorine surface engineering for Vt control and memory window boost in HZO FeFET toward high-performance, energy-efficient in-memory computing
items.abstract: Threshold-voltage (V t ) control without sacrificing the memory window remains a key challenge for energy-efficient ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based in-memory computing. Here, we introduce a novel fluorine surface treatment (FST)-based V t tuning strategy that selectively engineers the interfacial layer of Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 based Si FeFETs. Fluorine-induced electrostatic modulation and interfacial defect passivation jointly contribute to a positive shift of the entire transfer hysteresis and memory-window enhancement without noticeably altering the ferroelectric switching characteristics of the HZO layer. The optimized FST achieves an approximately 0.5 V positive V t shift, an approximately 0.5 V memory window enhancement, and a 40× reduction in leakage current at 0 V, enabling normally-off operation of the low-V t state. The resulting devices exhibit robust reliability, consistent device-to-device characteristics, and favorable analog synaptic behavior. Furthermore, simulation using the experimentally measured device characteristics improves CIFAR-10 classification accuracy from approximately 78% to 83%. These results establish interfacial-layer-selective fluorine engineering as a compelling route toward low-leakage, reliable, and energy-efficient FeFET-based analog in-memory computing.

items.title: File-Semantic SSD for I/O-centric Architectures with NFS-over-NVMe Protocol
items.abstract: Emerging I/O-centric architectures empower peripheral devices to access storage directly while bypassing the host CPU and kernel. However, SSDs expose only a block interface and rely on the host filesystem for file metadata and access control, making file-level access for applications and peripheral devices inherently difficult in I/O-centric architectures. This tight coupling between the host filesystem and storage device introduces unavoidable software overhead and limits the potential of fully hostless I/O paths. In this paper, we present File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD), a new SSD architecture that provides a native file abstraction within SSDs, enabling direct file access by peripheral and remote devices without host intervention. FS-SSD adopts the lightweight, stateless NFS interface and introduces NFS-over-NVMe, a protocol extension that embeds NFS operations into the standard NVMe command structure. This allows FS-SSD to support local and remote file I/O through existing PCIe and NVMe-oF transports. Our evaluation shows that FS-SSD provides on-device file abstraction while fully utilizing raw-device bandwidth in I/O-centric architectures.

items.title: Direct-Access-Enabled GPU Memory Offloading with Optimal Efficiency for LLM Inference
items.abstract: LLM inference is constrained by GPU memory capacity and bandwidth. Tiered memory architectures mitigate this by allowing the GPU to offload memory to the remote tier. However, existing memory offloading frameworks rely on prefetching data into local GPU HBM. This approach underutilizes system resources by introducing HBM contention, squandering memory capacity, and creating pipeline bubbles. We show that enabling direct GPU access to remote memory significantly outperforms prefetching, achieving optimal aggregate system bandwidth. We propose SplitKernel, an end-to-end direct-access memory offloading framework that uses the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) to asynchronously fetch offloaded weights and KV caches directly from remote memory into GPU shared memory (SMEM). To maximize remote access performance, SplitKernel introduces a greedy algorithm to determine optimal per-operation offloading ratios, alongside active congestion control and TMA multicast to eliminate interconnect bottlenecks and read amplification. Evaluations across diverse architectures show that SplitKernel achieves near-optimal bandwidth aggregation, with up to 7.7× performance gains on NVLink-C2C and 2.3× on PCIe systems compared to state-of-the-art memory offloading baselines.
items.venue: International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS)

items.title: Copper Pillar Patterning Using Digital Exposure Technology with Dry Film Resists for 2.5D PLP
items.abstract: Fan-out panel-level packaging (FO-PLP) is a growing segment in heterogeneous integration, gaining importance as a cost-efficient solution for advanced packaging. Panel formats of 310×310 mm² demonstrate technical advantages over wafer substrates while avoiding the process complexities associated with larger panel sizes. In this work, a novel dry film resist (DFR) was patterned using digital exposure lithography for high aspect ratio (high A.R.) Copper pillar (Cu pillar) application. CD uniformity confirmed a deviation within ±4.00%. Patterning of both, round and square via geometries proving straight side wall profiles with a VIA and L/S resolution of 30 μm was demonstrated in 120 μm-thick DFR. Subsequent electroplating and resist stripping enabled the successful fabrication of Cu pillars with A.R. of 1:3 and 1:4, respectively. In addition, newly developed equipment software features effectively addressed the challenges associated with 2.5D and 3D integration, supporting the requirements of next-gen AI and HPC devices.

items.title: Composition-Dependent Atomic Layer Etching of Multicomponent Oxide Semiconductors with Preserved Electrical Performance
items.abstract: Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for next-generation memory device scaling, owing to their low off-state current, low-temperature processability, and excellent compatibility with back-end-of-line manufacturing. Here, we report the composition-dependent atomic layer etching (ALE) behavior of the multicomponent oxide semiconductor InGaZnOx (IGZO), enabled by a hydrogen-based surface modification chemistry. The constituent cations of IGZO exhibit markedly different reactivities toward hydrogen, allowing the overall etch rate to be systematically tuned through elemental composition. Because this reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, ALE minimizes damage to the underlying front-channel region, achieving atomic-scale material removal with minimal degradation of electrical performance, in contrast to conventional dry-etching approaches that often degrade transistor characteristics. Leveraging this low-damage, self-limiting characteristic, we further demonstrate that ALE enables post-deposition trimming of nonuniform IGZO films conformally deposited within three-dimensional trench structures, improving step coverage to nearly 100%. These results establish hydrogen-based ALE as a versatile, composition-aware process for the atomic-scale control of multicomponent oxide semiconductor channels, offering a low-damage route toward scalable three-dimensional memory device architectures.

items.title: Beyond the European Chips Act: Mobilizing Public Banks to Solve Europe’s Semiconductor Supply Chain Paradox
items.abstract: The European semiconductor supply chain is characterized by a “missing middle.” While the continent hosts global leaders in equipment manufacturing (such as ASML) and advanced research (IMEC, CEA-Leti), its situation in the production of power and automotive semiconductors (STMicroelectronics, Infineon, NXP) has deteriorated, and it is almost entirely absent from the leading edge of logic chip production (with the exception of Intel in Ireland, which produces for the USA). At the same time, Europe is a vast downstream consumer of semiconductors, embedded not only in its automobile, aerospace, and industrial sectors but also in final consumer demand for smartphones, computers, and digital devices. This paradox – strength upstream and downstream, but weakness in the middle of the supply chain – renders the continent acutely vulnerable to economic disruptions and geopolitical shocks. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed these vulnerabilities, as shortages forced months-long shutdowns in European automobile production, while the concentration of advanced-node capacity in Taiwan and South Korea continues to heighten systemic risks. The EU Chips Act (2023) seeks to address this imbalance by doubling Europe’s global market share to 20 percent by 2030. Yet compared with the U.S. CHIPS and Science Act, the initiative remains underfunded and fragmented, with only €3.3 billion in direct EU funding and uneven national subsidies. Intel’s withdrawal from the Magdeburg project has further undermined Europe’s sub-7 nm ambitions. This article argues that Europe requires a more ambitious approach. While direct EU subsidies are off the table due to European institutional constraints, the EU could resort to strategic, highly leveraged, public-private partnerships, where leading players such as TSMC would engage in technology transfer against higher-than-usual profitability. In effect, manufacturers would invest 20% of the total capex needed while public and private banks would provide the remainder. Public promotional banks, such as the EIB, KfW, Bpifrance, CDP, and ICO would be key actors of this plan, because these institutions operate outside the Maastricht definition of public debt, and they could collectively mobilize up to €170 billion between 2026 and 2033.

items.title: ApproxHDC: Approximation Tuning for Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: As Moore's law reaches its physical and economic limits, domain-specific approaches are increasingly employed to accelerate machine learning workloads. Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) represents one such emerging paradigm, offering an alternative to conventional deep learning techniques. Rooted in cognitive models of computation, HDC is designed bottom-up with hardware efficiency as a first-class objective. Consequently, HDC workloads map naturally to heterogeneous hardware platforms, including CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, as well as emerging in-memory computing technologies such as Resistive RAM (ReRAM) and Phase-Change Memory (PCM). The intrinsic tolerance of HDC algorithms to noise and approximation enables substantial performance gains with minimal loss in inference quality. In this work, we introduce ApproxHDC, a framework for automated identification and application of domain-specific approximations in HDC workloads. ApproxHDC extends the HPVM-HDC compiler infrastructure to enable retargetable compilation across diverse hardware backends, including CPUs, GPUs, and simulated ReRAM and PCM-based accelerators. The space of possible software and hardware approximations in HDC is exponentially large, making exhaustive exploration intractable; ApproxHDC employs efficient search and analysis techniques to navigate this space and identify high-impact approximations. We further integrate hardware-level approximation mechanisms within the HDC accelerator to demonstrate ApproxHDC's ability to exploit both software and hardware approximations. Experimental evaluation shows that ApproxHDC achieves up to 17.25x speedup on CPUs, 14.97x on GPUs, and 4.69x on SpecPCM while staying within user-specified quality-of-service constraints, outperforming the state-of-the-art MicroHD framework by 3.49x. HDC-specific search space pruning reduces the design space by 71 to 491 orders of magnitude automatically and up to 89 more with developer guidance, enabling discovery of high-quality configurations within minutes.
items.venue: International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS)

items.title: The Unreported Variable:Collector Selectivity in Data Placement Evaluation
items.abstract: A solid-state drive cannot overwrite data in place, so it cleans full blocks by copying out still-valid data, costing speed and lifetime. Interfaces such as NVMe Flexible Data Placement (FDP) let the host label data by expected lifetime so data dying together is stored together, and published schemes report cutting these copies by 20--75%. Those studies rarely state which blocks the drive chooses to clean. Varying only this choice in simulation, we show it decides how much a label is worth: label value peaks when the drive searches moderately for blocks holding little valid data, falls when it always takes the block with the least, and turns negative when it ignores how much valid data blocks hold. This holds in 47 of 48 synthetic configurations, and one real mail-server trace shows the same shape at about half the magnitude. Priced as spare capacity, a two-class label is worth 65% more spare when each scheme runs at its best setting, but becomes a net loss at 20% label error, typical of learned classifiers. Labels stating which data die together keep most of their value at 16 FDP handles and gain as cleaning improves. Evaluations must report the drive's cleaning policy.

items.title: Temperature-controlled synthesis and characterization of boron nanoparticles with semiconducting properties via dual-pulsed laser ablation
