items.title: SNAP-FPCIM: A 28-nm Embedded-Serial-Alignment and Non-2's-Complement-MAC Floating-Point Compute-in-Memory Macro With Adjustable Computation Precision
items.abstract: Digital compute-in-memory (DCIM), particularly floating-point CIM (FPCIM) has emerged as a promising technique to enhance energy efficiency with higher accuracy for artificial intelligence (AI) applications. However, previous works incurred substantial hardware overhead for FP multiplication and accumulation (MAC) and failed to leverage the bit-level sparsity across data formats. This work presents SNAP-FPCIM, an embedded-serial-alignment, non-2’s-complement-MAC and adjustable computation precision FPCIM based on 6T static random-access memory (SRAM). The contributions of this work include: 1) a broadcast input and embedded light-convertor structure to enable BF16/INT8 MAC operations with improved input reusability; 2) an embedded area-efficient serial-alignment scheme with dual-bit-serial MAC; 3) a format-mixed N2CMAC flow to reduce circuit dynamic activity and signed computation overhead; 4) a mode-reconfigurable design to accommodate diverse computational precision requirements. A fabricated 28nm 64Kb SNAP-FPCIM macro supports FP-MAC operations of BF16 and INT8, achieving an energy efficiency of 62.84TFLOPS/W in BF16 mode and 90.15TOPS/W in INT8 mode.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: SMART-AIMC: Sensitivity-Aware Mixed ADC Resolution with Fine-Grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: Analog In-Memory Computing (IMC) is a promising paradigm for accelerating GEMM-based AI workloads by executing computations directly within the memory array in the analog domain. While IMC delivers substantial energy and throughput improvements, it can suffer from significant task accuracy degradation due to analog-to-digital converter (ADC) quantization noise, which occurs at the GEMM output and is thus different from weight/activation quantization, which occurs at the GEMM input. Mixed ADC resolution allows IMC modules to choose between high- and low-resolution ADC modes with different energy costs, offering a compelling accuracy-energy trade-off. However, selecting ADC resolutions across IMC units while respecting hardware granularity constraints remains challenging. In this paper, we propose SMART-AIMC, a Sensitivity-aware Mixed ADC Resolution framework with fine-grained Tunability for Analog In-Memory Computing. SMART-AIMC correlates the algorithmic task loss to hardware ADC quantization noise in the form of an ADC Channel Sensitivity (ACS) metric. Using this metric, SMART-AIMC systematically, and in a disciplined manner, allocates ADC resources to critical computations. Furthermore, we introduce a sensitivity-based channel reordering scheme that overcomes the hardware granularity constraints with no runtime overhead and approaches the optimal ADC quantization possible for the model. Evaluated across diverse workloads, SMART-AIMC unlocks a superior accuracy-energy Pareto frontier, providing (1) higher task accuracy at matched energy budgets and (2) fine-grained tuning across efficiency targets, from aggressive energy savings to near-digital inference accuracy. At the latter operating point, SMART-AIMC achieves $6.99\times$ higher modeled system-level energy efficiency for linear projections than the INT8 digital baseline with negligible accuracy degradation.

items.title: Roll-to-Roll fabrication Cu-Carbon Nanotube composites for advanced electrical conductors
items.abstract: We report on the development of high-volume, continuous-feed, roll-to-roll (R2R) batch-processing capability for the scalable fabrication (>1 m length) of high-performance composite conductors that incorporate carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into the Cu matrix, ultra-conductive metal composites (UCC). Long-length UCCs are formed by uniformly coating Cu tapes with CNT-infused polymer nanofibers via an electrospinning unit followed by R2R thermal treatment and R2R deposition of Cu thin films using a magnetron sputter system. All R2R assembled UCCs exhibited electrical and mechanical properties comparable to those of stationary-processed counterparts, including similar electrical conductivity, ∼10 % higher current-carrying capacity, and ∼20 % greater tensile strength than those obtained on pure Cu tapes. The technology being developed and scaled here introduces vast application opportunities and immense technological/economic impact in all energy sectors ranging from on- and off-board components in electric drive vehicles to power grid systems, as well as interconnects to electronic devices and data centers.

items.title: Role and calculation of the thermal resistance for the compact modelling of TiN/Ti/HfO2/W memristors
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the compact modeling of TiN/Ti/HfO 2 /W memristors across a wide range of time scales, spanning approximately seven decades. The time required for the reset process to occur (under constant applied voltages and starting from different conductance states) is experimentally measured and modelled. First, a simple analytical formulation is developed to fit the experimental Time-to-Reset across a wide voltage range. Then, a new methodology, based on analyzing the overlap of Time-to-Reset versus temperature plots for different initial device states, is proposed as a parameter extraction procedure to experimentally obtain the thermal resistance values for the corresponding conductive filament states, which are subsequently used for compact modelling purposes. This state-dependent thermal resistance is dynamically incorporated into a SPICE simulation model, which successfully replicates the transient current drops during pulsed reset operations. In addition, the overlap of the considered Time-to-Reset versus temperature plots for different filament states can be interpreted as a fingerprint of a common, thermally activated mechanism.

items.title: Rigorous Foundations of the Deterministic Spectral Manifold on a Chip
items.abstract: The Deterministic Spectral Manifold architecture establishes an 861-node network derived from the pair intersections of 42 base elements. The network partitions into three identical 273-node compute blocks coupled through a central 42-node communication kernel. Grounding a single reference boundary node removes network singularities, guaranteeing stable and unique signal routing across the entire fabric. Power delivery uses a 72-phase resonant clock that recycles charge between complementary logic rails, cutting energy dissipation toward fundamental thermodynamic limits. Dynamic current ripple caused by transistor capacitance cancels out across the symmetric phases and shifts to high frequencies where chip packaging naturally attenuates it. Compute dies connect to the boundary core across a silicon interposer with vertical through-silicon vias and planar inductors tuned to cancel micro-bump parasitics, ensuring low-loss signaling. Fault isolation clamps failing nodes directly to virtual ground rather than severing physical interconnects. This clamping acts as an exact mathematical shortcut, allowing the system to update routing matrices in real time within a fixed clock pipeline without software interrupts or iterative reconfiguration.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Revealing and Enhancing Channel-Coupled Polarization Reversal in Oxide-Semiconductor FeFETs Through Post-Channel Ferroelectric Crystallization Annealing
items.abstract: Oxide semiconductor FeFETs (OS-FeFETs) suffer from inefficient erase operation due to limited positive-charge supply from the OS channel. Here, a length-scaling polarization extraction (LSPE) method is proposed to separate switchable-polarization contributions from the floating-body MFIS region and MFISM gate-to-source/drain (S/D) overlap regions. Devices annealed before channel deposition show an unstable memory window (MW) and suppressed ${P}_{\text {MFIS}}$ , indicating inefficient polarization reversal in the OS-channel-coupled region. Crystallization annealing after channel deposition enhances both components and stabilizes the MW. O $1{s}$ XPS results show an increased oxygen-vacancy-related component, suggesting enhanced donor-state-assisted positive-charge supply. These findings provide a viable pathway to improve erase efficiency and MW stability in OS-FeFETs for nonvolatile memory applications.

items.title: Re-deposition and etching characteristics of plasma-exposed ceramics for semiconductor etching equipment
items.abstract: Ceramics are widely used as plasma-exposed components in semiconductor etching equipment owing to their high plasma resistance; however, exposure to reactive species and energetic ion bombardment during plasma etching can generate etch-derived byproducts that accumulate locally and cause contamination. Nevertheless, studies on plasma-resistant ceramics have mainly focused on material erosion, such as etch depth and surface morphology, while the generation and re-deposition of etch-derived species remain less explored. Here, re-deposition characteristics of Al 2 O 3 , Y 2 O 3 , YAG, and SiC were investigated in an RF-biased inductively coupled Ar/O 2 /CF 4 plasma. A masking geometry with adjacent masked and plasma-exposed regions was used to investigate local re-deposition near geometrical boundaries relevant to confined regions in plasma-processing equipment. Re-deposition was characterized in terms of morphology, depth profile, and elemental composition, while its dependence on plasma conditions was examined through measurements of plasma density, electron temperature, V dc , and optical emission. Re-deposition depended on both ceramic material and ion-bombardment conditions. Higher increased both etch depth and re-deposition height, whereas increasing ICP power enhanced etching but reduced re-deposition at 1900 W, suggesting that net local re-deposition reflects a balance among material-dependent plasma–surface interactions, the supply of etch-derived species, and their ion-induced removal near the mask boundary.

items.title: RRAM-Based Computing-in-Memory FPGA Architecture for Low-Power Applications
items.abstract: Circuit design often faces a fundamental trade-off: ASICs offer peak efficiency at the cost of high design complexity and inflexibility, whereas FPGAs provide fast adaptability but suffer from high power consumption. In this work, we propose an RRAM-based FPGA architecture with a Reconfigurable Computing-in-Memory Logic Unit (RCLU), thereby achieving both flexibility, low cost, and low power consumption. By proposing a 2T2R structure that prevents RESET/SET operations in RRAM during logic computation, the proposed RCLU achieves significant improvements in delay and energy efficiency. In experimental benchmarks against conventional SRAM-FPGA and state-of-the-art RRAM-FPGA design, our architecture achieves power-delay product (PDP) improvements of up to 76.89% and 57.09%, respectively. Furthermore, to validate the low-power advantage of the proposed architecture, we implement ASCON, a representative lightweight IoT encryption algorithm. Simulation results show that our design achieves significantly lower energy per bit than conventional FPGAs and approaches ASIC-level efficiency, demonstrating strong potential as an energy-efficient IoT hardware solution.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: QUARC: A Compact and Energy-Efficient Quad-Mode Reconfigurable Analog--Digital Hybrid eDRAM CIM for Ternary-LLM Acceleration
items.abstract: This paper presents QUARC, a highly energy-efficient analog–digital hybrid computing-in-memory (CIM) processor for ternary large language model (LLM) acceleration. QUARC leverages a high-density 3T1C embedded DRAM bitcell and introduces a quad-mode reconfigurable macro with causal-mask-adaptive operation to improve both macro- and system-level energy efficiency. The proposed architecture incorporates four key features. First, a sign-embedded ternary encoding scheme supports both ternary projection and multi-bit attention, enabling area-efficient analog MAC operations. Second, an in-column signed-magnitude SAR ADC reduces ADC area overhead by up to 87.5% and lowers ADC energy consumption by up to 82% through comparison skipping. Third, in-column partial-sum accumulation exploits in-memory digital computation to process only effective bits, reducing accumulation area and energy by 90.5% and 91%, respectively. Fourth, causal-mask-adaptive pipelining dynamically scales with the linearly increasing attention workload and eliminates redundant KV re-computations that can incur up to a $30\times $ overhead. Implemented in a 28 nm CMOS process, the proposed CIM processor achieves a macro cell density of 1.91 Mb/mm2 and peak macro energy efficiencies of 390 TOPS/W and 48.2 TOPS/W for ternary projection and multi-bit attention, respectively. It also achieves system energy efficiency of 101.4 TOPS/W while maintaining a perplexity of 11.9 on WikiText-2 with 1.3B ternary-LLM.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: Proton‐Transfer Ferroelectrics With High Switching Endurance
items.abstract: Reliable organic ferroelectrics for memory applications require high endurance under repeated electrical switching. Here we demonstrate robust fatigue resistance in highly crystalline 2‐methylbenzimidazole (MBI) films grown by low‐temperature deposition followed by restrained crystallization (LDRC) on interdigital electrodes. Switching kinetics analyzed using the Kolmogorov–Avrami–Ishibashi (KAI) model reveals characteristic millisecond switching times and quasi‐one‐dimensional domain growth associated with proton transfer along hydrogen‐bond chains. Guided by these kinetics, we examined the switching endurance under a stringent protocol that ensures complete polarization reversal. After ~10 8 continuous cycles (~2 weeks), the remanent polarization shows a small initial wake‐up behavior (~10% increase within the first 10 4 cycles), followed by stabilization at values close to the initial polarization, indicating robust ferroelectric endurance under prolonged electrical cycling. The combination of LDRC‐enabled high crystallinity and localized proton‐transfer switching, which introduces minimal structural perturbation during polarization reversal, may have enabled this fatigue tolerance and highlight MBI as a simple, fluorine‐free platform for durable organic ferroelectric devices.

items.title: Process-Controlled Polarity Reversal of Flat-Band Voltage Modulation via Finite TiN Oxidation in La-Dipole-Last Processed TiN/HfO2/SiO2 Gate Stacks
items.abstract: Lanthanum (La) dipole-last integration provides an attractive near-zero-volume approach for threshold-voltage tuning in advanced high- $\kappa $ /metal-gate stacks, yet the origin of the induced flat-band voltage ( ${V}_{\text {fb}}$ ) shift remains unclear. In this work, TiN thickness and wet-clean chemistry were investigated as two key process variables in La-dipole-last TiN/HfO 2 /SiO 2 gate stacks. The La-treated MOS capacitors show a nonmonotonic TiN-thickness dependence of $\Delta {V}_{\text {fb}}$ , with positive shifts of 60 and 160 mV for 8 and 25 TiN, respectively, and a slight negative shift of −10 mV for 38 TiN. Electron energy-loss spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses reveal that the nonmonotonic ${V}_{\text {fb}}$ shift is associated with the formation of finite oxidized TiN regions induced by residual La, which is strongly dependent on the wet-clean chemistry. First-principles calculations show that interfacial La reduces the oxygen migration barrier from 2.49 to 2.01 eV and 1.34 eV when La substitutes for Hf and Ti, respectively, thereby facilitating oxygen transport and TiN oxidation within a finite region. These results clarify the process-dependent origin of polarity reversal in La-dipole-last integration and provide guidance for multi- $V_{\text {th}}$ engineering in advanced gate-stack architectures.

items.title: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition and Substrate Engineering of Low-Resistivity Ultrathin MoCx Films for Advanced Interconnect Applications
items.abstract: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistance because of their relatively high resistivity. Therefore, a key challenge is to develop ultrathin liner/barrier materials that can maintain low resistivity while providing effective Cu diffusion-barrier performance. In this work, we demonstrate MoC x as a liner-free barrier material using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). For this PEALD-grown film, cycloheptatriene molybdenum tricarbonyl, (η 6 -C 7 H 8 )Mo(CO) 3 , was first introduced as a precursor to synthesize ultrathin molybdenum carbide (MoC x ) films. The effects of plasma reactants, plasma power, deposition temperature, film thickness, and substrate types were systematically evaluated to clarify how PEALD process conditions and substrate chemistry influence the electrical performance of ultrathin MoC x films. We observed nucleation differences during the growth based on the substrate; MoC x films deposited on Al 2 O 3 consistently exhibited lower resistivity than those grown on SiO 2 . Using the optimized deposition process, amorphous MoC x films thinner than 5 nm showed resistivities as low as ~230 μΩ·cm without any post-deposition annealing. For reference, current Ta/TaN liner/barrier layers typically exceed 500 μΩ·cm resistivity in the sub-5 nm thickness regime. Sub-5 nm MoC x film also showed good Cu adhesion and effective Cu diffusion-barrier behavior after thermal annealing of up to 500 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of ultrathin amorphous MoC x as a low-resistivity liner-free barrier material for advanced Cu interconnects.

items.title: Plasma information–based characterization of wedge-shaped bowed etching profile driven by ion dynamics with the tailored voltage waveform bias
items.abstract: Wedge-shaped bowing during high-aspect-ratio Si trench etching under tailored voltage waveform (TVW)-driven dual-frequency capacitively coupled plasma conditions is analyzed from a plasma physics perspective. TVW operation modifies RF sheath dynamics, producing a bi-modal ion energy distribution with an enhanced high-energy component. When reflected from tapered SiO2 mask sidewalls, these ions induce localized energy-flux focusing near the upper trench region, resulting in sharp wedge-shaped profile deformation. Combining in situ diagnostics with feature-scale transport modeling, a plasma-information index, PIBow, is introduced by normalizing the ratio of reflected high-energy ion energy flux to transported O radical flux to a characteristic profile-transition reference scale. This dimensionless index quantifies the competition between ion-driven etching and radical-mediated passivation, and wedge-forming and non-wedge-forming conditions are systematically organized around the normalized reference state PIBow≈1 for the analyzed system. Furthermore, a plasma information–based virtual metrology framework then transforms optical emission spectroscopy and voltage-current sensor measurements into physics-informed plasma variables for wedge geometry prediction. The model reproduces the measured wedge length with a high coefficient of determination (adj. R2 = 0.981) and yields an interpretable process-control window governed by the balance between energetic-ion delivery and O-radical-mediated passivation. An angle-dependent etch rate model is also proposed to describe wedge angle formation, reproducing the measured dependence on the operating conditions. Wedge-shaped bowing thus represents a distinct regime of profile evolution governed by coupled ion dynamics and transport-limited radical supply under TVW conditions, and the methodology presented here offers a scalable framework for understanding, predicting, and engineering plasma–surface interactions in plasma-assisted manufacturing.

items.title: Physical Analysis of Stress-Induced Multilevel and Fast Random Telegraph Noise in BCAT DRAM Devices
items.abstract: The buried channel array transistor (BCAT) is widely used in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM); however, a detailed analysis of the degradation mechanisms within the buried channel remains limited. In this study, stress-induced charge trapping in the BCAT is systematically investigated using drain-current random telegraph noise (RTN) under a gate stress of 2 V. Under prolonged gate stress, the investigated BCAT cell exhibited an evolution from two-level to multilevel RTN, together with the emergence of a fast RTN component near 200 s. Fast RTN components are first isolated and removed using a pulsewidth- and amplitude-based filtering scheme, and the remaining multilevel signal is decomposed using a factorial hidden Markov model (FHMM) model. Depth analysis reveals an initial shallow trap near the channel, followed by the emergence of additional border or oxide traps after 10 and 500 s of stress. Oxide-trap and interface-trap densities are extracted and used to interpret the observed RTN behavior. Finally, the long-term reliability implications are estimated based on the evolution of interface traps and fast RTN behavior. The RTN amplitude increases with stress, leading to long-term dispersion in current uniformity. These observations provide quantitative signatures of trap evolution relevant to reliability assessment in scaled BCAT DRAM transistors.

items.title: PALIKV: PM-Resident Learned Index-Based Key-Value Store for the DRAM-PM-SSD Hierarchy
items.abstract: Persistent memory (PM) bridges the latency and cost gap between DRAM and SSDs. Within the DRAM–PM–SSD hierarchy, deploying key-value-separated key-value stores (KV-separated stores) is imperative for optimizing system longevity and performance. This architecture mitigates SSD write amplification and preserves PM endurance by minimizing writes. Existing KV-separated stores in the DRAM-SSD architecture, however, fail to fully exploit this three-tier hierarchy due to three issues. First, LSM-tree indexes incur high read amplification on PM. While learned indexes offer faster reads, they suffer from severe write-read asymmetry that can undermine overall efficiency in write-intensive workloads. Second, the lack of real-time obsolete data identification delays space reclamation. Third, contemporary KV stores treat PM as a passive write buffer, underutilizing its low read latency under skewed workloads. To address the above issues, we propose PALIKV – a PM-resident learned index-based KV store for the DRAM-PM-SSD hierarchy. We first design an adaptive two-level index that combines a PM learned index with a dynamic DRAM B+-tree buffer. This structure balances lookup efficiency with high write throughput while filtering redundant updates and extending PM lifespan. Second, the learned index enables real-time obsolete data identification. This facilitates an expedited garbage collection with device-specific reclamation granularity, thereby significantly reducing space amplification. Third, a hotness-aware data placement proactively migrates warm data from SSD to PM, allowing PM to serve skewed reads and eliminating the latency-constrained SSD from the critical read path. The experimental results unveil that PALIKV significantly outperforms SOTA KV-separated stores and DRAM-PM-SSD KV stores in terms of throughput and latency.

items.title: Overcoming the Drive Current--Threshold Voltage Tradeoff in BEOL-Compatible ALD-In2O3 Transistors via Oxygen Plasma Passivation
items.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate the overcoming of the conventional drive current–threshold voltage (I ON –V ${}_{\text {TH}}\text {)}$ tradeoff in back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible atomic layer deposition indium oxide thin-film (In 2 O ${}_{{3}}\text {)}$ transistors using oxygen plasma passivation. A 100-nm-channel optimized device exhibits a positive threshold voltage (V ${}_{\text {TH}}\text {)}$ shift of 0.63 V while simultaneously enhancing drive current (I ${}_{\text {ON}}\text {)}$ by 211% to $105~\mu $ A/ $\mu $ m at an overdrive voltage of 1 V. It also shows excellent gate control and bias stability with a subthreshold swing (SS) of 78.8 mV/dec, drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) of 21.1 mV/V and a $\Delta $ V TH of −5 mV under positive bias stress. This improvement originates from polarity-selective defect modulation by oxygen plasma: passivation of donor-like traps reduces the carrier concentration and induces a positive V TH shift, whereas stronger suppression of acceptor-like traps mitigates trap-limited conduction (TLC) and enhances carrier transport efficiency. This work establishes a correlation between oxygen plasma treatment, defect polarity evolution, and carrier transport. It provides a simple and BEOL-compatible defect-engineering strategy for high-performance and stability-enhanced In 2 O 3 logic devices.

items.title: Optimizing High-Level Synthesis Sparse Matrix--Vector Kernel for Alveo FPGAs
items.abstract: Sparse matrix–vector multiplication (SpMV) is a critical kernel in scientific computing and high-performance applications, yet it remains challenging to optimize due to irregular memory access patterns and low computational intensity. This work targets the AMD Vitis SpMV kernel on high-bandwidth memory (HBM)-equipped Alveo field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and introduces hardware-aware optimizations that significantly improve performance, especially in reduced precision scenarios. Building on prior evaluations of the Vitis kernel, we propose two key enhancements: coefficient grouping and index packet coalescing. These reduce padding overhead and improve memory bandwidth efficiency without requiring a complete redesign of the vendor-supplied kernel. Experimental results over 33 matrices from the SuiteSparse collection show up to $4\times $ speedup and an average improvement of $1.6\times $ compared to the original Vitis kernel. Our method demonstrates how practical architectural adaptations can yield substantial performance gains, supporting the growing trend toward lower-precision and energy-efficient computing in FPGA-based accelerators.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Online Junction Temperature Monitoring Method for Paralleled SiC MOSFETs With the Discrete Gate Drive Control
items.abstract: To meet higher power demands, multiple SiC mosfet chips are often connected in parallel. However, nonuniform junction temperature distribution among these paralleled devices has emerged as a critical challenge, significantly impacting system reliability and lifetime. Despite various thermal management efforts, existing techniques lack an accurate, real-time method to monitor individual chip junction temperatures in paralleled configurations. In this article, a junction temperature monitoring method for paralleled SiC mosfets with discrete gate drive (DGD) control is proposed. A PCB Rogowski coil is settled on the confluence of paralleled branches to capture dynamic current characteristics. By actively adjusting the turn-on delay among SiC mosfets, the junction temperature can be extracted by leveraging the temperature dependence of quasi-threshold voltage (Vth-qua) during a gate delay interval without intrusive sensing. Comprehensive analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of device temperature imbalance and varying operating conditions on measurement accuracy. The proposed method is finally applied and verified online in a buck experiment platform to sensing junction temperature of paralleled SiC mosfets. Under three distinct uneven cooling scenarios, the maximum monitoring error is limited to just 2.9 °C, confirming the method's high accuracy and robustness. This article offers a practical and scalable approach for junction temperature monitoring in paralleled SiC mosfets, paving the way for more reliable thermal design and intelligent health monitoring in high-power, safety-critical applications.

items.title: Numerically Stable Small‐Signal Modeling of Highly Linear Composition‐Engineered AlGaN/GaN Fin‐HEMTs Using a Stabilized Berroth‐Based Extraction Methodology
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This work presents a comprehensive TCAD‐to‐RF modeling framework for composition‐engineered multifin AlGaN/GaN HEMTs incorporating fin‐dependent aluminum composition. The proposed device employs asymmetric barrier engineering (AlGaN with across three fins) to simultaneously tailor the threshold voltage and improve linearity while maintaining adequate RF performance. To accurately extract the intrinsic small‐signal parameters, a numerically stable Berroth–Bosch‐based extraction methodology is developed by integrating LOESS‐assisted smoothing, robust mid‐band slope estimation, and physically constrained parameter estimation within the de‐embedding procedure. Unlike conventional extraction techniques, which are susceptible to numerical oscillations and nonphysical parameter values, the proposed methodology consistently yields stable intrinsic parameters enabling reliable evaluation of the RF figures of merit and . Furthermore, robustness against realistic measurement uncertainty is demonstrated through standard‐deviation Gaussian perturbation of the TCAD‐generated S ‐parameters, where the proposed methodology maintains physically meaningful parameter extraction while conventional methods exhibit significant numerical instability. The extracted parameter set represents an equivalent compact small‐signal model of the complete multifin device without increasing circuit complexity as the number of fins increases. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and numerically robust foundation for compact modeling and RF characterization of composition‐engineered multifin GaN HEMTs for high‐frequency integrated circuit applications.
items.venue: International Journal of Numerical Modelling Electronic Networks Devices and Fields

items.title: Negative Activation Energy Under Dynamic Stress of 650 V E-mode GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: We demonstrate for the first time that the process responsible for dynamic R ON degradation in GaN HEMTs operated under application-close SALT hard-switching (HS) conditions exhibits a negative activation energy. This behavior has been attributed to the mitigation of hot-electron-induced degradation at higher temperatures, resulting from the reduced electron mean free path. In addition, a novel real-time in-situ technique to monitor the threshold voltage (V TH ) variation during HS operation is presented. Negligible V TH variation was observed during the tests, along with a significant increase in on-resistance: this result supports the conclusion that hot-electron trapping in the access region is the dominant mechanism responsible for the observed degradation.

items.title: Near-Vacuum UV Imaging for Energy-Efficient Artificial Synaptic Activity in ZnGa2O4 Super-BandGap Response
items.abstract: Neuromorphic computing using new devices has the potential to surmount the von Neumann bottleneck, which is the limitation imposed by the necessity of transferring data between memory and processing units, hence facilitating energy-efficient data processing. Demand for ultrasensitive near-vacuum ultraviolet (NVUV) sensors and energy-efficient neuromorphic devices has propelled wide bandgap oxide semiconductor research. We present a ZnGa2O4-based dual-mode photodetector that uses its super-bandgap transition for severe UV detection and artificial synaptic activity used for tactile memory. Under NVUV (near about 200 nm) illumination, the device with a single-crystalline MOCVD-grown ZnGa2O4 on sapphire substrate using has responsivity of 30 mA/W. Ultrawide bandgap of ZnGa2O4 and intense interaction with short-wavelength photons result in higher responsivity than traditional semiconductor-based NVUV sensors. Besides photodetection, the technology mimics neuromorphic processes with synaptic functionality. The heterostructure’s conductance states are modulated by photogenerated carriers, causing excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), and paired-pulse facilitation (PPF) corresponds to biological plasticity. A super-bandgap transition causes synaptic weight modulation enabling quick, energy-efficient synaptic processes. Its femtojoule (fJ) energy consumption per synaptic event makes it a good choice for ultralow-power artificial synapses. Extreme ultraviolet sensing with artificial synaptic learning on a single crystalline platform could enable next-generation optoelectronic and neuromorphic applications.

items.title: Multipath Interference Mitigation Framework for Indirect Time-of-Flight Imaging Based on Compact Model and Hybrid Optimization
items.abstract: Three-dimensional spatial sensing is increasingly required in robotics, industrial automation, spatial metrology, and shape reconstruction, where both accuracy and robustness are critical. Indirect time-of-flight (iToF) is widely used because of its high spatial resolution, but its ranging reliability is degraded by scene-induced multipath interference (MPI) and system-induced wiggling error. Existing MPI mitigation methods often require either a wide modulation-frequency range or high computational cost. In addition, reliable MPI mitigation also requires correction of wiggling error, but existing wiggling correction methods are difficult to combine effectively with MPI mitigation. This study proposes an iToF error mitigation framework that combines a compact parametric model based on harmonic signal analysis with hybrid optimization-based MPI mitigation. A pixelwise parametric model is first constructed to describe wiggling error caused by nonideal modulation signals in iToF systems, and computationally efficient single-frame correction is conducted using Newton’s method. The corrected multifrequency complex signals are then processed by a hybrid optimization method, in which orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) provides an initial estimate of the dominant path, and Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) refines it. This enables stable MPI mitigation within a relatively narrow modulation-frequency range. Experiments show that the proposed wiggling correction reduces the residual distance error to 0.76 cm at 14 MHz and 0.52 cm at 28 MHz. For MPI mitigation, the mean absolute error (MAE) is reduced from 178.54 to 13.85 mm in one scene and from 248.12 to 32.51 mm in another. In addition, the proposed method maintains accuracy comparable to existing optimization-based methods while reducing computation time by factors of 7.96 and 6.72 relative to our previous method in the two scenes. It also provides additional speed improvement over a previously reported optimization-based method. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves computational efficiency and implementation feasibility while maintaining correction accuracy in the evaluated measurement scenarios.

items.title: Multi-regime trap dynamics in Si/SiGe/Si MOSFET current transients at cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: We investigate transient charge-trapping dynamics in Si/SiGe quantum-well MOSFETs at cryogenic temperatures between 𝑇 = 4 K and 𝑇 = 8 0 K . Transient current behavior is analyzed using stress-relaxation measurements inspired by the extended measure–stress–measure (eMSM) technique. The recorded current transients were analyzed by using phenomenological models and extracting corresponding mean relaxation times. A comparison with CV and IV characteristics links these regimes to the activation of different conduction channels in the SiQW/SiCap layers. These results provide new insight into cryogenic trap kinetics relevant for CMOS based Si/SiGe/Si quantum devices.

items.title: Multi-probe transport measurements of few layer molybdenum disulfide
items.abstract: The deterioration of transistor performance due to carrier scattering when the thickness of silicon is reduced below a few nanometers is one of the major concerns in silicon-based electronics. Atomically thin two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) do not suffer from this problem and are thus appealing candidates for next generation transistors. To speed up the development of TMDCs for device applications, a fast, noninvasive, and reliable technique to measure the electrical properties on the micrometer scale is paramount. Here, we use multi-probe cantilevers with micrometer pitches to non-invasively probe the electronic properties of mono-, bi-, and trilayer molybdenum disulfide samples. We extract field-effect mobilities in the range from 2.7 to 16.3 cm2 V−1 s−1. Furthermore, atomic force microscopy images taken after the transport measurements reveal that landing damage from the multi-probe cantilever to the sample can be avoided, provided that the landing of the probe is gentle and the drain–source currents are limited.

items.title: Monolithic 3-D Integration of Memristive Bayesian Neural Network With Intrinsic Stochastic Gaussian Weight Generation
items.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) enable robust uncertainty quantification for safety-critical tasks via probabilistic weight sampling, outperforming overconfident deep neural networks (DNNs) in scenarios like autonomous driving. However, BNN hardware implementation faces two fundamental bottlenecks: the excessive area and power overhead of Gaussian random number generation (GRNG) circuits, and the severe von Neumann bottleneck in conventional 2-D architectures. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic 3-D integrated memristive BNN (M3D-BNN) that addresses these bottlenecks by harnessing the intrinsic stochasticity of resistive random access memory (RRAM) and vanadium dioxide ( ${\text {VO}}_{{2}}$ ) devices. The proposed M3D-BNN monolithically integrates memristive standard Gaussian distribution (SGD) generators, memristive ReLU activation (MRA) units, and a 40-nm 1-Mb RRAM-based in-memory computing (IMC) core into a three-layer 3-D stack. When validated on an intelligent motion planning task, the M3D-BNN achieves software-equivalent inference accuracy and delivers a ${2}.{47} \times $ improvement in predictive uncertainty quantification over conventional DNNs. Compared with its 2-D counterpart, our design realizes a ${{2}.{1}} \times $ boost in processing speed and a ${19}.{9} \times $ reduction in energy consumption, paving the way for energy-efficient hardware acceleration of efficient intelligent decision-making at the edge.

items.title: Modality-Dependent Memory Mechanisms in Cross-Modal Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Memory-augmented spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a pathway toward energy-efficient, multi-sensory artificial intelligence, yet their generalization across sensory modalities remains largely unexplored. We present the first comprehensive cross-modal ablation study of SNN memory mechanisms across visual and auditory neuromorphic data sets.

items.title: Medusa: A Scalable Quantum-Inspired k-SAT Solver With Make and Break Feedback
items.abstract: Boolean satisfiability (SAT or $k$ -SAT, $k \ge 3$ ) is a binary combinatorial optimization problem (COP) that is challenging for traditional classical computing to address in polynomial time. Quantum and quantum-inspired systems have been touted to tackle these and similar nondeterministic polynomial-time (NP) problems. This work describes Medusa, a quantum-inspired $k$ -SAT solver capable of addressing problems of up to 200 variables and 1016 clauses. Implemented using analog and mixed-signal circuits, the solver benefits heavily from massive parallelism, continuous-time operation, and excellent energy efficiency, and advances the field of quantum-inspired, analog computing with best-in-class performance and energy efficiency. This performance is achieved with the introduction of three key architectural advancements: dual Make and Break feedback, a distributed logic feedback network, and multi-macro operation. The dual feedback mechanism improves the mean time to solution (TTS) for 50-variable 3-SAT problems by $30\times $ when compared with a single feedback mechanism. The distributed logic in the feedback network implements all-to-all spin connectivity with arbitrary order interactions, enabling $k$ -SAT operation and supporting the scalability of the solver, which is further enhanced by multi-macro operation. Medusa, implemented in a 28 nm process, achieves a $4.92~\mu $ s TTS for the popular SATLIB uf50-218 benchmark with a mean energy to solution (ETS) of 19.1 nJ. For the uf200-860 benchmark the solver achieves a 30.9 ms mean TTS, outperforming quantum annealing for problems of the same size.

items.title: Measurement and Quantitative Analysis of Oxide Trap Evolution in Power SiC Devices
items.abstract: This work proposes a nondestructive framework to track the time- and depth-resolved evolution of oxide traps in 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) structures during time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) stress. The approach combines time-resolved gate admittance measurements with a distributed oxide admittance model and frequency–temperature depth mapping to reconstruct the measured dispersion at flatband voltage and recover nonuniform oxide trap profiles without imposing an a priori spatial distribution. Applied to long duration negative-bias TDDB, the extracted profiles reveal a strongly depth-nonuniform and field-accelerated defect build-up: higher stress not only increases the trap population, but also broadens the active defect region deeper into the oxide as breakdown is approached. By tracking the average trap density and the centroid of oxide trapped charge in the probed oxide region, we quantify the spatial evolution and relate it to the concurrent transients in gate leakage current, flatband voltage shift, and increment of interface trap density, without relying on destructive techniques, such as transmission electron microscopy, thus preserving the device for continuous evaluation. The same methodology is further demonstrated on stressed silicon carbide (SiC) power mosfets, supporting device-level relevance and providing a workflow for depth-resolved characterisation of SiC gate oxide degradation under negative stress.

items.title: Low-Temperature Nanoscale Additive Manufacturing of High Performance Gate-All-Around Field Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Stacked nanosheets/nanowires (NWs) in gate-all-around (GAA) configuration are the leading channel geometry for sub-2 nm logic nodes. However, achieving electrostatic control comparable to that of the GAA process under the low thermal budget ( $\le$ $ 400~^{\circ }$ C) required for back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes and monolithic 3-D sequential integration remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate multichannel silicon nanowire (SiNW) GAA field-effect transistors (GAAFETs) fabricated by an epitaxy-free, transfer-free additive manufacturing route: dense crystalline SiNW arrays are grown at only $300~^{\circ }$ C via the in-plane solid–liquid–solid (IPSLS) mechanism and vertically aligned over four stacked guiding terraces, yielding four-level stacked NW channels with a diameter of 22.3 nm and a spacing of 60.6 nm. At a proof-of-concept gate length of 180 nm, the Schottky-contacted p-channel GAAFETs deliver an on / off current ratio of up to $2\times 10^{{7}}$ and a best subthreshold swing (SS) of 64 mV/dec, approaching the thermal limit. Temperature-dependent transport analysis further yields an apparent ballistic efficiency of ~0.26 at room temperature, extracted within the Lundström scattering framework. These results establish catalytic IPSLS growth as a nanoscale additive manufacturing route to GAA-grade electrostatic integrity within a BEOL-compatible thermal budget, offering a scalable pathway toward sequentially stacked 3-D integration.

items.title: Leak-CIM: A PVT-Robust and Energy-Efficient SRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro Exploiting Transistor Leakage
items.abstract: The binarized neural networks (BNNs) significantly reduce arithmetic and storage costs for edge inference, but repeated bitwise accumulation and memory access still limit system energy efficiency. This article presents leak-computing-in-memory (CIM), a $256\times 64$ static random access memory (SRAM)-based voltage-mode CIM macro that exploits the subthreshold leakage of off -state transistors as ultrahigh-impedance pseudo-resistors for low-energy analog accumulation. Unlike charge-sharing CIMs, the proposed scheme maintains a wide read-bitline (RBL) dynamic range while strongly suppressing the shoot-through current that typically limits voltage-mode operation. To compensate for the process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity of leakage-based pull-up and pull-down paths, the leak-CIM employs a postfabrication N-well bias calibration scheme that restores their resistance balance. The postlayout simulations show that the calibrated macro maintains a normalized mean-squared error below $1.12\times 10^{-2}$ across 40 global PVT conditions. Fabricated in a 22-nm bulk-CMOS process, the macro achieves up to 1799 TOPS/W and 31.67 TOPS/mm 2 across measured operating points. When the measured ADC characteristics are incorporated into a BNN inference model, leak-CIM attains 98.15% accuracy on MNIST and 86.04% on CIFAR-10.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: Layer-Constrained Bottleneck Channel Routing for Area Minimization in VLSI Designs
items.abstract: It is known that the number constraint of the used layers becomes more important for cost reduction of chip designs. Based on the insertion of necessary vias onto the routing nets on the constrained layers inside a bottleneck channel, an efficient routing algorithm, including layer-constrained global routing for area minimization and layer-constrained detailed routing for area minimization, has been proposed for layer-constrained bottleneck channel routing (BCR). Based on the reassignment of the routing segments in the Manhattan routing model, our proposed routing algorithm is the first algorithm for the layer-constrained BCR problem. In layer-constrained global routing, based on the assignment of the represented intervals with covering compatibility, the represented intervals on the extra tracks can be first reassigned onto the constrained tracks by using two separation-and-reassignment operations. Furthermore, the represented intervals can be mapped onto the global wires of the routing nets on the constrained layers for the minimization of estimated area. In layer-constrained detailed routing, the boundary-oriented paths of the routing nets or sub-nets can be first assigned on the constrained layers for area minimization. Furthermore, the physical paths of the routing nets or sub-nets on the constrained layers can be modified to reduce the number of the used bends or vias of the routing nets. Compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s two-layer routing algorithm and sequential conflict reassignment (SCR) for the 2BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 54.7% of CPU time to further reduce 2.6% of the routing area and 1.7% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average. On the other hand, compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s three-layer routing algorithm and SCR for the 3BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 19.3% of CPU time to further reduce 3.0% of the routing area and 1.0% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: LOW-POWER SECURE UART DESIGN USING DATA SCRAMBLING AND ERROR DETECTION
items.abstract: Serial links in embedded and IoT systems face two problems: channel noise can silently flip bits, and plain-text transmission can be read by anyone monitoring the line. This paper presents a low-power secure Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART) architecture, built as a transmitter chain and a receiver chain joined by a single serial channel, that recovers the original data and provides reliable data transfer. In the transmitter chain, 8-bit parallel data is first passed to a CRC generator, which appends the check bits. The result is scrambled by an XOR scrambler driven by an LFSR keystream loaded with a TX seed, and the UART transmitter then adds the start, parity and stop bits and sends the frame serially. In the receiver chain, the UART receiver detects the start bit, samples the frame and rebuilds the parallel word. A descrambler with an LFSR loaded with the matching RX seed recovers the original data, and a CRC checker recomputes the CRC and compares it with the received value to ensure reliable data transfer. The data output block delivers the 8-bit word together with an error flag, which is raised on any mismatch caused by channel noise or a seed error. The design uses only shift registers, XOR gates and finite-state logic, which gives low area and low power, and clock gating of the CRC, LFSR and UART blocks cuts dynamic power when the link is idle. It is suited to FPGA and ASIC implementation in sensor networks, IoT nodes and industrial control. LFSR scrambling provides lightweight obfuscation, not strong encryption.
items.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT

items.title: KWS-CIM: A Charge-Domain eDRAM-Based Compute-in-Memory Macro for Ternary DFSMN Keyword Spotting
items.abstract: This paper presents a 3T2C embedded DRAM (eDRAM)-based charge-domain compute-in-memory (CIM) macro for ternary deep feedforward sequential memory network (DFSMN)-based keyword spotting (KWS) with ternary activations and binary weights. The proposed architecture integrates a charge-domain ternary multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) bitcell, a selectable dual-mode sensing scheme, and an in-array offset calibration technique using fixed calibration rows. The dual-mode sensing scheme supports an energy-prioritized conventional sense amplifier (SA) mode for always-on monitoring and an accuracy-prioritized two-step sense amplifier (TSSA) mode for robust inference under reduced sensing margins. The proposed TSSA mitigates decision-timing-induced kickback disturbance, while the calibration rows suppress systematic column-wise sensing offsets. A sense amplifier-based 1-bit readout is employed to minimize area overhead. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed macro operates up to 250 MHz and achieves 930–1335 TOPS/W in the conventional SA mode and 82–336 TOPS/W in the TSSA mode, with an area efficiency of 18.45 TOPS/mm2. For DFSMN-based KWS, the measured accuracies with the calibrated TSSA mode reach 91.66%, 89.87%, and 87.30% for the 12-, 20-, and 35-class KWS settings (CLS12, CLS20, and CLS35), respectively. Additional evaluations achieve 98.02% on MNIST and 87.32% on CIFAR-10 with ResNet18, demonstrating the general applicability of the proposed eDRAM CIM macro.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: Ising-type ferroelectric switching and piezoelectric response in wurtzite KMgP: First-principles study
items.abstract: The present paper employs first-principles calculations based on density functional theory to investigate the structural, electronic, ferroelectric, and piezoelectric properties of KMgP in the wurtzite LiGaGe-type phase. The thermodynamical, mechanical and dynamical stability of the compound are confirmed through the formation energy, elastic coefficients and phonon spectrum, respectively. Our results reveal that wurtzite KMgP is a semiconductor with a direct band gap of 1.25 eV within the local-density approximation. We use the Berry-phase approach to evaluate the polarization properties inherent to the polar structure of KMgP, yielding a spontaneous polarization of 0.385 C/m2 and Born effective charges near their nominal ionic values. The ferroelectric nature of the material is demonstrated by the characteristic double-well potential associated with Ising-type polarization reversal. With a high Curie temperature (385.32 K) and low switching energy barrier (0.0568 eV) and coercive electric field (2.78 MV/cm), we predict that wurtzite KMgP possesses highly reversible polarization, making it a promising candidate for novel ferroelectric applications. Moreover, we find that KMgP is an anomalous piezoelectric compound with a negative longitudinal piezoelectric coefficient (modulus) of −0.75 C/m2 (−52.66 pC/N).

items.title: Influence of Space Weather on Single Event Effects in Aviation When Employing Modern Commercial Sub‐100 nm Electronic Devices
items.abstract: During November 2025 thousands of commercial aircraft (Airbus A320s) had to be grounded due to the risk of ionizing radiation effects on the avionics system. Safety‐critical systems continue to use modern commercial devices, and therefore an understanding of their responses within enhanced radiation environments is crucial to ensure reliable operations. Complex Single Event Effect (SEE) behaviors are often overlooked during Single Event Upset (SEU) testing but they can impact both the magnitude of the upset rate and increase the supply currents (from possible micro‐latches). This paper presents SEU Cross‐Sections for several modern Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) types and summarizes complex upset behaviors that were repeatedly observed in one SRAM type. The expected SEU rates, and other SEE metrics, for two SRAM types during extreme radiation events are compared with older SRAM technologies with larger feature sizes. Global upset rates are presented for one SRAM type indicating a very high upset rate over polar regions at altitudes where future supersonic aircraft are expected to operate at. Exemplars of how the micro‐latches may effect the long term reliability, by considering the thermal impact, are presented for two possible transport applications.

items.title: Influence of Packaging Technologies on Pulsed Power Capability of SiC MOSFETs Across Different Timescales
items.abstract: The pulsed power capability of SiC mosfets under extreme operating conditions (e.g., short circuits, surge currents) is critical to the robustness of power conversion systems. Packaging influences the transient thermal impedance and chip temperature rise, thereby impacting the device’s pulsed power capability. Therefore, this article investigates the influence of packaging technologies on device pulsed power capability across different timescales. It is found that packaging technologies have little impact on the devices’ short-circuit capability but can affect their surge-current capability. Different package layers influence the devices’ surge current capability across different timescales. For pulsewidths (tp) on the order of hundreds of microseconds, adopting a die top system (DTS) or a copper-clip (Clip) structure on the top surface of the chip can improve the pulsed power capability. The Clip further outperforms the DTS at millisecond timescales due to its larger thermal capacitance. Regarding the bottom die-attach interface, using silver sintering to increase the thermal conductivity enhances the device’s pulsed power capability only as tp approaches 1 ms. Modifying the thermal capacitance or thermal resistance of the direct bonded copper (DBC) affects the chip temperature rise only as tp approaches 10 ms. Moreover, since the DBC is located relatively far from the chip, the resulting reduction in temperature rise is insufficient to improve the pulsed power capability. These findings provide guidelines for package design to improve the pulsed power robustness of SiC devices.

items.title: Influence of Growing Parameters on Optical Band Gap of Gallium Nitride Deposited on Sapphire by Reactive Magnetron Sputtering
items.abstract: The presented work discusses the preparation of gallium nitride by reactive magnetron sputtering technology and the study of its optical properties. In particular, the dependence of the optical band gap of gallium nitride on technological parameters, such as temperature, UV irradiation and impurity diffusion. The optical band gap was calculated from the emission spectra using the Tauce Plot method. The emission spectra were measured on a UV/VIS/NIR Spectrophotometer Analyzer. The temperature dependence showed an improvement in the band gap with increasing temperature and amounted to 3.37 eV, which is close to the known band gap of gallium nitride of 3.4 eV. The influence of UV irradiation was also studied, which showed a slight improvement in the band gap. In general, UV irradiation improves the structural properties of gallium nitride and, accordingly, was expected to have a positive effect on the optical properties. During magnetron sputtering, silicon as a dopant was mixed, doped. The result showed that doping gallium nitride with silicon reduces the optical band gap by 0.06 eV.

items.title: InGaZnO Optoelectronic Synapses With Temporal Processing and Nonvolatile Memory for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: A multifunctional InGaZnO (IGZO) optoelectronic synaptic transistor fabricated via laser direct-writing lithography is proposed for neuromorphic visual computing. Benefiting from the persistent photoconductivity of the IGZO channel, oxygen vacancy ionization and recombination under optical stimulation provide the physical basis for synaptic plasticity. The device successfully emulates key synaptic functions, including excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), and short-term to long-term plasticity (LTP) transition. Leveraging its transient dynamics and multilevel nonvolatile conductance states, system-level simulations are conducted in two representative neuromorphic computing frameworks. In reservoir computing, short-term memory dynamics enable temporal feature extraction, achieving 92.5% motion recognition accuracy. In a fully connected neural network, stable multilevel conductance states are employed for synaptic weight storage, yielding 88.9% accuracy on the Fashion-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistor for integrated temporal information processing and nonvolatile memory in multifunctional neuromorphic visual systems.

items.title: Improved Reliability of Hafnia-Based AFE Capacitors Through BEOL-Compatible Furnace Annealing
items.abstract: Here, we investigate the enhanced endurance and reliability of Hf ${}_{{0}.{2}}$ Zr ${}_{{0}.{8}}$ O 2 (HZO) antiferroelectric (AFE) capacitors after an initial $550~^{\circ }$ C/30 s rapid thermal annealing (RTA) crystallization and subsequent 150– $400~^{\circ }$ C BEOL-compatible furnace annealing. The HZO capacitors retain AFE switching through $10^{{8}}$ cycles and show no hard electrical breakdown up to $10^{{9}}$ cycles, despite evolution toward a ferroelectric (FE)-like loop. Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) measurements and Weibull analysis show lifetime improvements of $8.9\times$ to $11.9\times $ , with the projected B 10 ten-year voltage increased from 1.58 V to 1.90 V. These results indicate a wide post-crystallization thermal-reliability window for HZO AFE capacitors.

items.title: Improved AC PBTI in Si FinFETs With HfO2/ZrO2/HfO2 Nanolaminate Gate Stack
items.abstract: This work demonstrates significantly improved AC positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) reliability in Si FinFETs utilizing an ultra-thin 20-Å HfO 2 /ZrO 2 /HfO 2 (HZH) nanolaminate gate stack compared with conventional HfO 2 . Unlike static DC stress, dynamic AC operation involves concurrent trapping and detrapping processes, making both degradation and recovery kinetics essential for realistic lifetime assessment. Under AC stress, the HZH stack substantially suppresses threshold-voltage shift ( $\Delta {V}_{\textit {th}}$ ) accumulation while accelerating recovery kinetics. This reliability advantage persists at elevated temperatures, where mitigated degradation and rapid recovery synergistically minimize $\Delta {V}_{\textit {th}}$ . Systematic analysis using ultra-fast on-the-fly (OTF) measurements and physics-based modeling reveals that the superior AC PBTI performance stems from a modified defect landscape within the HZH stack. Defect time-constant extraction indicates slower trapping during stress and accelerated detrapping during relaxation, consistent with a reduced density of traps featuring long emission time constants. These findings establish HZH nanolaminate engineering as an effective strategy for robust high- $k$ metal-gate (HKMG) integration in next-generation high-speed logic technologies.

items.title: Impact of Spatially Correlated Ionic Disorder and Interface Morphology on Forming Variability in Oxide RRAM
items.abstract: A physics-based fully coupled technology computer aided design (TCAD) framework for oxide-based resistive random access memory (RRAM) is developed to investigate the statistical variability of the forming process, with a 2-D axisymmetric configuration employed for the statistical simulations. The model self-consistently solves the Poisson equation, electron drift-diffusion (DD) equation, Fourier heat conduction equation, and oxygen-vacancy transport equation using a Newton-based nonlinear coupling scheme. The proposed framework successfully reproduces experimentally observed forming, reset, and set characteristics, while the forming process under different compliance-current conditions is accurately captured using a unified parameter set. A spatially correlated Gaussian random field is introduced to emulate initial disordered oxygen-vacancy distributions with tunable fluctuation amplitude and correlation length. Statistical results show that increasing fluctuation amplitude significantly increases forming-voltage variability and conductive filament (CF) location randomness, while correlation length mainly affects filament continuity and growth stability. Interface morphology effects are also studied using conical and truncated-cone electrode protrusions. Results indicate that interface nonuniformity induced local electric-field enhancement strongly localizes filament nucleation, reduces forming voltage, and suppresses device-to-device variability.

items.title: Impact of Geometrical Modification at the Electrode/Channel Interface on a-IGZO Transistors
items.abstract: This study showed the structural effects of current crowding at the hole corners of the electrode/channel interface on the electrical contact properties of amorphous In-Ga-Zn-O (a-IGZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs). Hole-patterned a-IGZO TFTs incorporating an Al 2 O 3 -doped ZnO (AZO) interlayer (IL) exhibited a width-normalized external parasitic resistance ( ${R}_{\text {ext}}{W}\text {)}$ of $0.08~\Omega \cdot $ cm, substantially lower than $2.0~\Omega \cdot $ cm for the control device. The significant improvement in parasitic resistance properties could be attributed to the combined effects of electric field amplification at the hole corners and the AZO IL functioning as an n + layer. This reduction in ${R}_{\text {ext}}{W}$ led to an enhancement in field-effect mobility from $38.7~\pm ~0.38$ to $47.9~\pm ~0.39$ cm 2 /Vs.

items.title: Hybrid Physics–Machine Learning Modeling of HZO-Based Ferroelectric FETs: From TCAD Acceleration to Compact Models and DTCO Challenges
items.abstract: Machine-learning-enhanced TCAD and compact modeling have become essential for accelerating the design and optimization of HZO-based ferroelectric FETs (FeFETs). ML surrogates trained on TCAD, phase-field, compact-model sweeps, and experimental data deliver 10³–10⁵ times speed-up while preserving compact-model-level accuracy for I D –V G , V TH , memory window, and variability. This review organizes data representations, feature/label mappings, and architecture roles across FNN/MLP, CNN/GNN, RNN/GRU/LSTM, GP/MDN/BNN, and PINN models, and performance targets for SPICE-grade deployment, including log-RMSE <0.05 dec, memory-window error <50 mV, and sub-ms inference. Key challenges persist in physical consistency, extrapolation, uncertainty quantification, and process transfer. We highlight hybrid physics–ML approaches as the most scalable path toward robust, technology-portable FeFET design and array-level computing applications.

items.title: Hierarchical spectral control of porous silicon microcavities at 1.55µm via dielectric inclusion engineering and graphene tuning
items.abstract: We theoretically investigate hierarchical spectral control of a porous-silicon defect microcavity near 1.55 µm by combining dielectric inclusion engineering with graphene tuning. A transfer-matrix model incorporating effective-medium descriptions and Kubo-based graphene conductivity is used. Dielectric inclusions provide coarse spectral positioning, while a single graphene monolayer at the defect center enables fine electrical adjustment. The baseline cavity exhibits a resonance near 1.55 µm, a peak transmission of 0.994, and a quality factor of about 20. SiO 2 , Al 2 O 3 , and TiO 2 inclusions produce substantial resonance shifts, while varying the graphene Fermi energy from 0.30 eV to 1.50 eV yields a tuning range of approximately 4.45 nm. This exceeds the calculated temperature-induced shift of 2.60 nm over 293 K to 373 K, highlighting graphene’s potential for post-fabrication spectral calibration and possible future temperature-drift adjustment. The results establish a hierarchical design strategy combining passive spectral positioning with active electrical trimming.

items.title: HEIRS-PS: Hybrid 3-D RRAM- and SRAM-CIM for Pipelined Sparse Multitask Transformer Acceleration
items.abstract: Multitask transformers have garnered widespread attention for fast task adaptation at edge. However, in addition to matrix–vector multiplication (MVM) with static and dynamic weights in the data-intensive transformer, task adaptation introduces new challenge of weight updating. Besides, while sparsity can help mitigate the rapid growth in parameter size and computational demand, it requires great hardware flexibility. Compute-in-memory (CIM) is widely explored to overcome the memory bottleneck in neural network acceleration, mainly with single type of memory devices, but struggles to balance the storage density with computing flexibility across multiple tasks. Meanwhile, the conventional pipeline parallel dataflow for high throughput suffers from the underutilization with bubbles caused by variable input sequence length and model sparsity. In this article, HEIRS-PS, a hybrid three-dimension RRAM- and SRAM-CIM architecture, is proposed for the pipelined multitask transformer acceleration with sparsity. With the 3-D integrated RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM arrays, a novel hybrid-CIM paradigm is proposed with the collaborative addition to achieve both high storage density and computing flexibility for multitask inference. Moreover, by fully leveraging the hybrid-CIM structure in HEIRS-PS, a new dynamic workload scheduling method is proposed with a layer regrouping method to balance the computing latency across pipeline stages. By eliminating the bubbles, the model inference latency is reduced with higher throughput. Experiment shows that the proposed HEIRS-PS architecture improves the energy efficiency by up to $13.3\times $ and $8.68\times $ , compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM works on Llama-1.3B. Moreover, HEIRS-PS also reduces the computing latency by up to 29.5% with the balanced latency across pipeline stages.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Gate Stack Engineering in FeVNAND for Multi-Level Operation: Balancing E-Field Distribution and Grain-Induced Current Margin Variation
items.abstract: This work investigates channel insulator engineering in MIFIS-structured FeVNAND using TCAD simulation. Optimized channel insulators improve electric field distribution and gate coupling, enhancing charge trapping and expanding the memory window from 3.9V to 7–9V. Analysis of process induced poly-Si grain characteristics also improves transient channel conduction, reducing read verify time from $10\mu $ s to $0.3\mu $ s and lowering sensing delay. These results demonstrate the potential of channel insulator engineering for high speed, reliable, low voltage FeVNAND.

items.title: Fast Unified Short-Circuit Protection for SiC MOSFET via Kelvin-Source Charge Integration
items.abstract: SiC mosfets require ultrafast short-circuit (SC) protection because of their limited SC withstand time. However, most existing indirect SC detection methods rely on instantaneous electrical quantities and are therefore vulnerable to switching noise. This letter proposes a unified SC protection method based on Kelvin-source disturbance charge integration. By rectifying and integrating the disturbance current coupled into the Kelvin-source path, the proposed method suppresses short switching spikes while preserving sensitivity to sustained SC disturbances. Thus, both hard-switching fault and fault under load can be identified using the same detection variable and the same threshold-based criterion. Experimental results demonstrate detection times of 90–96 ns and total protection times of 400–407 ns, without additional power-loop sensors and with strong potential for compact gate-driver integration.

items.title: FWA BLOCK SYSTEM: EVERYTHING IS A BLOCK

items.title: FANS: A Fairness-Aware and QoS-Enhanced Scheduler for ZNS SSDs in Shared Environments
items.abstract: Zoned Namespace (ZNS) solid state drives (SSDs) are increasingly adopted in data centers, leveraging fixed-size zones with coarse-grained mapping and sequential write constraints to mitigate over-provisioning and write amplification. When a zone is exclusively used by a workload, sending sequential read/write transactions together to the backend can leverage plane-level parallelism within the zone. However, when multiple workloads share the same ZNS SSD—even accessing distinct zones—they still compete for backend physical resources, which we refer to as zone interaction. We observe that current transaction scheduling strategies for ZNS SSDs do not fully consider the impact of zone interaction between workloads, which leads to reduced fairness and quality of service (QoS) degradation. First, chip-level queues are scheduled independently, considering only intraqueue zone interactions. This can cause transaction adjustment to expand global unfairness across workloads. Second, fairness-oriented scheduling methods interleave transactions from different workloads (zones), which prevents ZNS sequential write requests that could exploit plane-level parallelism from being issued to the backend storage (BS) simultaneously. To address these challenges, we propose FANS, a fairness scheduler for shared ZNS SSDs. FANS globally perceives the impact of zone interactions across different workloads and achieves global fairness through a two-phase transaction adjustment strategy. Within each workqueue, FANS employs zone-aware scheduling to ensure that plane-level parallelism can be fully utilized. Evaluations with mixed workloads show FANS achieves 22% higher fairness and 62% greater throughput compared to state-of-the-art frameworks.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: EnFault: Enhanced Fault-Tolerant Physical Design of FPVA Biochips Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of microfluidic technology toward large-scale integration, a new generation of microfluidic systems, known as fully programmable valve array (FPVA) biochips, has emerged. These biochips offer superior programmability and flexibility, making them ideal for a wide range of biochemical experiments. However, the shrinking size of chip features presents a substantial challenge in automating the physical design process. Furthermore, the occurrence of physical faults in these chips can lead to inaccurate bioassay results, further complicating the design process. The deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm has proven effective in managing the high-dimensional state space inherent in physical design tasks, enabling the identification of viable solutions even in large-scale faulty circuits. In this article, we propose EnFault, an enhanced fault-tolerant physical design framework for FPVA biochips that addresses both placement and routing challenges in the presence of physical faults. Based on the DRL algorithm, we develop fault-tolerant placement and routing decision-making models, named DRL-FTPlacer and DRL-FTRouter, to optimize the solution quality of physical design while ensuring fault tolerance. The framework optimizes the design process by dynamically adjusting placement and routing decisions, thereby enhancing solution quality and chip reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing algorithms in terms of completion time of bioassay and total path length of fluid transportation for both small-/medium-scale and large-scale circuits. Especially in large-scale circuits, the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in solution quality, fault-tolerance performance, and execution efficiency.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Effect of Channel Thickness on Amorphous In─Ga─Zn─O‐Thin‐Film Transistors
items.abstract: Thin‐film transistors based on amorphous oxide semiconductors demand thinner channels for next‐generation display and memory applications. However, channel‐thickness scaling causes a positive threshold‐voltage shift and degrades field‐effect mobility. Here, we report film densification in sputter‐deposited, hydrogen‐free amorphous indium–gallium–zinc oxide as the channel thickness decreases, with the film density exceeding that of single‐crystal InGaZnO 4 . Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal a change in polyhedral connectivity from corner‐sharing to edge‐sharing. Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy and chemical etch‐rate measurements support this structural change, showing a shift of the M─O vibrational band peak to lower wavenumber and an increased etch rate. We propose that the resulting reduction in the M─O─M bond angle induces strain. In the proposed model, this strained local structure can enhance the formation of interstitial oxygen and lead to the formation of an oxygen Frenkel defect pair. This defect pair deepens the donor level and broadens the tail states below the conduction‐band minimum, thereby degrading thin‐film transistor performance. The degradation is suppressed in the In‐rich composition. This result may be understood in terms of the stabilization of interstitial oxygen as an electrically inactive peroxide species identified by the experimental results.

items.title: Dual Thermal Pathways in 3D Ultrasonically Exfoliated BNNS/CF Skeleton for Thermally Conductive Epoxy Composites
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid miniaturization and high‑power density of modern electronic devices pose rigorous demands on high‑efficiency thermal management materials. Boron nitride nanosheets (BNNSs), with high thermal conductivity and superior dielectric insulation, are promising thermally conductive fillers. Herein, BNNSs were exfoliated by 1200 W high‑power ultrasonication. A carbon fiber/boron nitride nanosheet (CF/BNNS) thermal‑conductive skeleton was fabricated via ultrasonic dispersion and vacuum filtration. Carbon fibers and laminated BNNS construct a dual thermal conduction pathway for multidirectional heat transport. Multi‑gradient carbon fiber/phenolic resin/boron nitride nanosheet/epoxy (CF/PF/BNNS/Epoxy) composites were prepared by vacuum infusion and hot‑pressing curing. The optimized CF/PF/BNNS/Epoxy‑1.5 composite achieves an in‑plane thermal conductivity of 76.47 W/(m K) and through‑plane value of 5.09 W/(m K). COMSOL simulations and practical tests on light emitting diode (LED) and mini serial advanced technology attachment (mSATA) solid‑state drives (SSD) confirm its outstanding heat‑dissipation capacity with a maximum cooling of 27.9°C, offering a reliable strategy for electronic thermal‑dissipation composites.
items.venue: Journal of the American Ceramic Society

items.title: Design-Technology Co-Optimization: Analysis of Source/Drain Fence for Performance Improvement and Cell Size Scaling in Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistor-Based Circuits
items.abstract: As transistor dimensions continue to scale down aggressively, the lateral overgrowth of source/drain (S/D) epitaxy has emerged as a critical limitation. When the spacing between transistors becomes narrow, uncontrolled lateral overgrowth can cause the merging of S/D regions in adjacent transistors, leading to fatal errors such as electrical shorts. The introduction of a fence structure effectively suppresses this overgrowth, thereby enabling cell size reduction and improved integration density. However, it also introduces complex changes in device characteristics, including increased contact and S/D resistance, as well as reduced parasitic capacitance. In this work, we systematically analyzed the impact of the fence structure from a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) perspective. The DC performance of transistors was evaluated based on the linear mode on -state current ( $I_{DS,LIN}$ ), effective drive current ( $I_{EFF}$ ), and saturation mode on -state current ( $I_{DS,SAT}$ ). For transient response characterization, we investigated the propagation delay (high-to-low propagation delay, $t_{pHL}$ ; low-to-high propagation delay, $t_{pLH}$ ) of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) inverters under two configurations—Fan-Out 0 (FO0) and Fan-Out 3 (FO3)—to assess both intrinsic device characteristics and circuit-level behavior. The results demonstrate that optimized fence implementation can achieve performance gains while simultaneously enhancing integration density, thereby providing significant design advantages in advanced semiconductor technologies.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Design of a Digital MRAM-Based Processing-in-Memory Architecture for In Situ Arithmetic and Convolution Operations
items.abstract: Digital processing-in-memory (PIM) has emerged as a highly promising architecture that significantly enhances computational efficiency by embedding logic operations directly within memory. In particular, the spin-orbit torque magnetic random access memory (SOT-MRAM)-based PIM approach is regarded as a high-throughput and energy-efficient solution for data-intensive applications, effectively mitigating the inherent memory bottleneck issues in conventional computing systems. In this work, we develop low-cycle arithmetic operations using a 3T2M cell structure composed of two magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) that exploit both SOT and voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effects, integrated with three transistors to form a compact computational unit capable of full Boolean logic evaluation.
