The bitwise convolutional (CONV) operation implemented for CONV neural network (CNN) computational tasks exhibits higher parallelism and improved memory cell utilization, achieving a throughput approximately 29 times greater than that of low-cycle arithmetic operations. Furthermore, a novel comparison operation based on the 3T2M cell has been proposed and integrated into the computational module of the pooling layer within a digital MRAM-based PIM digital MRAM-PIM (DMPIM) architecture. A CNN implementation leveraging the proposed operations achieves an energy efficiency of 4.9 TOPS/W on the CIFAR-10 dataset using 16-bit precision for both inputs and weights.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Design and Optimization of E-Mode AlN FETs Featuring p-NiOx Gate Stack and Junction Termination Extension
items.abstract: This work demonstrates a novel enhancement-mode (E-mode) AlN-channel FET utilizing a recessed p-NiO x gate stack and an optimized junction termination extension (JTE). The electrons beneath the gate electrode are effectively depleted by the recessed p-NiO x gate. TCAD simulations reveal that the synergistic optimization of gate-recess geometry and JTE parameters enables a record-high breakdown voltage ( ${V}_{\text {BR}}\text {)}$ of 6210 V and a remarkable power figure of merit (PFOM) of 5.51 GW/cm 2 . These results significantly surpass reported $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 and GaN-channel devices. Furthermore, the high thermal conductivity of AlN ensures superior thermal management, with a minimal lattice temperature rise of only 10 K at peak power. This study provides a critical design framework for next-generation kilovolt-class ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) power electronics.

items.title: DIONet3D: Dual-Input Dual-Output Deep Neural Network With 3-D-Enhanced PDN Feature for IR Drop Prediction in 3-D ICs
items.abstract: Accurate IR drop analysis in 3-D integrated circuits (3-D ICs) is critical for ensuring power integrity and physical design convergence. However, conventional IR drop simulation flows suffer from extensive runtime and complicated flows, making them difficult for early-stage design evaluation and large-scale design iterations. To address this challenge, we propose DIONet3D, a novel dual-input dual-output neural network tailored for IR drop prediction in 3-D ICs. DIONet3D takes feature maps from both top and bottom dies as input, incorporates a shared backbone with U-Net structure, and outputs IR drop maps for both dies simultaneously. To enhance the modeling of 3-D power-delivery effects, we introduce a physics-guided 3-D-enhanced power delivery network (PDN) representation, in which planar PDN stripes are converted into spatially continuous features through Gaussian kernel-based smoothing, while vertical hybrid bonding (HB)/through-silicon via (TSV) connections are encoded to capture cross-die power delivery. This hybrid representation enables the network to capture both interdie and intradie features effectively while balancing the computation efficiency and feature representation efficiency. Furthermore, a compound loss function is proposed, combining multiple loss functions with dynamic weighting to balance multitask convergence and improve structural consistency. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art convolutional neural network (CNN) methods and achieves good generalization performance. Compared to commercial EDA simulation tools, DIONet3D achieves high structural and spatial similarity, with up to $309\times $ runtime speedup and $89\times $ memory reduction under CPU inference. Our results demonstrate that DIONet3D offers an accurate and lightweight surrogate solution for 3-D IC IR drop evaluation.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: DIMWIT: Directly Invoking Models Without Intensive Tuning
items.abstract: Resource managers typically encode what to do in a task-specific policy---a heuristic, an optimization procedure, or a model trained for the task---that must be developed before use and may need revision as the workload or system changes. We propose bypassing policy development and instead asking pretrained models to make resource-management decisions directly, given the current system state, desired outcome, and available choices. We evaluate this approach on microservice autoscaling, DRAM sizing, and video encoding, using a frontier LLM and two small decision models. On two microservice applications, a small decision model meets latency targets while using within 10% of the replicas allocated by policy-based autoscalers and within 13% of the frontier LLM. In DRAM sizing, a small decision model reduces DRAM usage by up to 27.5% relative to static provisioning while maintaining at least 95% of baseline performance. In video encoding, it completes encodes up to 4.3$\times$ faster than the frontier LLM, with an imperceptible 1.1-point decrease in Video Multi-Method Assessment Fusion (VMAF), a metric of perceptual video quality. Making individual resource-management decisions may be considerably simpler than developing a general strategy for making them.

items.title: Customized Diffusion Model Empowered by Heterogeneous Graph Network for Effective Floorplanning
items.abstract: Floorplanning is a critical phase in the very-large-scale integration (VLSI) physical design, focusing on determining block positions while optimizing the wirelength under specified area constraints. However, classical analytical-based floorplanners are highly sensitive to the quality of initial solutions, and existing learning-based methods often suffer from high-computational inefficiency and complexity. In this article, we propose a customized diffusion model to directly generate high-quality initial floorplans. By leveraging a classical analytical-based floorplanner on top of this initial floorplan, the final floorplanning results are significantly improved. To enhance the feature extraction, a heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) is developed to explicitly incorporate block-to-block (b2b) and pin-to-block (p2b) relationships from the netlist during the diffusion process. We further propose a classifier-free conditional diffusion method based on adaptive maximum-mean discrepancy (Ada-MMD) to guide the generation process without relying on external classifiers. The Ada-MMD mechanism adaptively captures structural correlations in the latent space, improving conditional consistency and enabling more controllable and accurate initial floorplan generation. In addition, a novel guidance sampling function is introduced to optimize both wirelength and overlap, effectively reducing the required sampling steps while maintaining competitive initial solutions. Experimental results demonstrate that integrating our proposed diffusion model with an advanced analytical-based floorplanner achieves at least 10.8% reduction in runtime and 3.8% reduction in HPWL compared with the original state-of-the-art floorplanner and other diffusion-based methods.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Corrections to "Unified Analysis of Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown to Extend Reliability Margins"
items.abstract: In the above article [1], the correct notation of (7) is presented as follows: \begin{align*} F_{\mathrm {hbd}}\left ({ t }\right)& = 1-\exp \left \{{ -\left ({ \frac {\eta _{\mathrm {wo}}}{\eta _{\mathrm {sbd}}} }\right)^{\beta _{\mathrm {sbd}}} }\right. \\ & \quad \times \left.{ \int _{0}^{\left ({ t/\eta _{\mathrm {wo}} }\right) ^{\beta _{\mathrm {wo}}}} \left ({ \frac {t}{\eta _{\mathrm {wo}}}-u^{\frac {1}{\beta _{\mathrm {wo}}}} }\right)^{\beta _{\mathrm {sbd}}} e^{-u}du }\right \}.\end{align*}

items.title: Comparison of the Roles of Iron and Carbon Doping in Achieving Semi‐Insulating GaN Buffer Layers
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Semi‐insulating GaN buffer layers are essential for suppressing leakage currents and enhancing the performance of AlGaN/GaN high‐electron‐mobility transistors. Here, we present a first‐principles density functional theory investigation of the thermodynamic stability and diffusion mechanisms of iron (Fe) and carbon (C) dopants in GaN. We calculate formation energies, charge transition levels, and migration barriers for Fe‐ and C‐related point defects and complexes. Our results show that Fe substituting Ga () and C substituting N () act as amphoteric defects, enabling compensation of n‐type conductivity. However, Fe exhibits significantly lower migration barriers compared to C, leading to higher diffusivity, particularly along the a ‐axis. The presence of nitrogen vacancies increases migration barriers, whereas Si defects enhance C mobility, highlighting the importance of growth conditions in controlling dopant distribution. We further demonstrate that Fe–C co‐doping forms a highly stable complex with deep electronic levels, also offering an effective strategy for achieving semi‐insulating buffer layers. These insights provide design guidelines for optimizing GaN buffer growth and improving the reliability of next‐generation high‐power electronic devices.

items.title: Comparative Investigation on Device-Level Failure of Three Typical SiC MOSFETs Under Single Surge Current Stress
items.abstract: Surge current pulse critically challenges the reliability of SiC metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (mosfets). A dedicated investigation on degradation behaviors in diverse devices with typical device architectures subjected to extreme single surge current (SSC) is very significant. Following electrical parameters comparation and physical failure analyses for devices with asymmetrical trench (AT), double trench (DT), and planar gate (PG) under SSC pulse, three distinct degradation modes and failure mechanisms have been identified. For the AT devices, SSC stimulates the gate oxide degradation with increase in near-interface traps, leading to negative Vth shift and gate turn-off failure. The body diode of the DT devices is damaged in terminal fields due to the concentration effect of current density caused by the source metal peripheral wiring even under low SSC. The PG devices suffer thermal burnout withstand relatively high SSC due to excessive heat. The results confirm that the SSC-induced failure is strongly correlated with device architectures, the reliability of the gate oxide and the design of the source metal wiring are worthy of attention. It is of valuable reference for the optimization of surge reliability and practical application of SiC mosfets.

items.title: Cognitive Optoelectronic Memristor Based on TeOx/SrTiO3 Heterojunction for In-Memory Computing Applications
items.abstract: Cognitive optoelectronic memristors (COMs) that can perceive, memorize, and preprocess visible light signals hold great promise for integration into artificial visual systems. In this work, we propose a first tellurium oxide (TeO x )/strontium titanate (SrTiO 3 ) heterojunction-based transparent COM, enabling dual-mode electrical/optical neural functionalities. The proposed COM exhibits pulse endurance and retention characteristics for $10^{{6}}$ cycles, and $10^{{4}}$ s, respectively. On the basis of reversibly tuned current states, a 97% high accuracy is achieved through the software simulation of a Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture-based neural network model for the fingerprint image classification task. Pulse-width, pulse-rate, and pulse-number-dependent plasticity behaviors, along with short- to long-term memory transition and image memory function, are emulated through the optically induced excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) response of TeO x /STO heterostructure memristive synapse. Regulated by optical pulses with different wavelengths, it imitates logic functions and associative learning. Furthermore, its potential application is also demonstrated in the processing of optical information. This work provides an effective strategy for the development of simple and efficient COMs for future neuromorphic vision system applications.

items.title: Cavity-Enhanced Multilevel Nonvolatile Photonic Memory With Phase-Change Nanobeam Cavities for In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: Nonvolatile photonic devices are central to enabling energy-efficient and scalable in-memory photonic computing. However, achieving multilevel programmability within ultra-compact footprints remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a cavity-enhanced photonic memory cell that integrates Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST) with a photonic crystal nanobeam cavity (PCNC), enabling electrically programmable, multilevel optical modulation with zero static power consumption. Distinct from conventional resonator-based platforms, the strong light-matter interaction and subwavelength mode confinement of the PCNC substantially enhance the effective refractive index modulation of GST, allowing high-density integration with improved modulation efficiency. The device achieves 28 programmable transmission levels with a minimum spacing of 0.2 dB and an extinction ratio of up to 13 dB by exploiting the large optical contrast between crystalline, amorphous, and intermediate phase states of GST. Reversible phase switching is experimentally demonstrated. As a proof of concept, a 4 × 4 photonic convolution kernel is implemented in a wavelength-division multiplexed photonic neural network, achieving a classification accuracy of 98.91% on the MNIST dataset with 4-bit quantization. These results establish PCNC/phase-change material integration as an effective strategy for realizing compact, low-power, and high-density multilevel photonic memory, providing a scalable pathway toward energy-efficient in-memory photonic computing systems.

items.title: Calibration and Enhancement of Analytical IR-Drop Model for Resistive Crossbar Arrays
items.abstract: Resistive in-memory computing (IMC) architectures emerged as a promising solution for efficiently accelerating neural network (NN) workloads on-chip, particularly in edge artificial intelligence (AI) applications where energy and area constraints are critical. Among the various challenges limiting IMC adoption, voltage drops caused by parasitic resistances significantly degrade the computational accuracy. While high-fidelity nodal analyses can model these effects accurately, their computational cost makes them unsuitable for system-level AI accelerator design. Analytical models offer a compelling alternative thanks to their speed and simplicity. However, the absence of a systematic method to fit them to different resistive memory devices and crossbar configurations might limit their applicability. In this work, we overcome this limitation by introducing a calibration procedure across a variety of input patterns and weight matrices. Furthermore, we evaluate the models under nonlinear $I$ – $V$ characteristics of resistive random access memory (RRAM) devices fabricated at IHP Microelectronics. Finally, we propose an enhanced analytical model for the better estimation of the voltage drops across the memory cells. Our modeling strategy is benchmarked against state-of-the-art approaches, achieving best-in-class performance among the analytical models in terms of accuracy and runtime. With more than two orders of magnitude improvement in simulation speed and a 5.9% median misalignment in the output currents approximation compared to SPICE-based nodal analysis, the presented solution is a compelling approach for evaluating large-scale IMC systems.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: CTH-CAM: A Cryogenic eDRAM-Based CAM With 1--26 Tunable Hamming Distance
items.abstract: Cryogenic approximate content-addressable memory (ACAM) offers an appealing solution that allows mismatches between the query and the stored data, measured by the Hamming distance (HD). However, in ACAM designs, increasing the word length shrinks the matchline (ML) voltage spacing between adjacent HD tolerance levels, thereby limiting the tunable-HD tolerance range and degrading discrimination. To address this issue, we propose a cryogenic eDRAM-based tunable-HD CAM (CTH-CAM) for reliable approximate search with a small ML voltage spacing. First, we present a cryogenic 4T1C single-finger embedded dynamic random access memory (eDRAM) gain cell with two complementary and decoupled comparison ports, which enables a wide HD tolerance range in approximate search with a small ML voltage spacing. Second, we introduce an adaptive reference voltage generation (ARG) scheme that replicates mismatch-driven ML voltages, enabling fine-grained discrimination with a small ML voltage spacing. Third, the CTH-CAM supports various operations, including memory, approximate BCAM/TCAM search, logic-in-memory (LIM), and matrix transposition operations, enabled by a cryogenic full-swing sense amplifier (FSSA). Measurement results of our test chip in a 28-nm CMOS process show that, compared to a state-of-the-art design (1–8 tunable-HD tolerance range for 64-bit word lengths), CTH-CAM achieves an improved tunable-HD tolerance range of 1–26 for 128-bit word lengths at 77 K, while maintaining a voltage spacing of $\geq 13$ mV throughout the tunable range. Moreover, it also achieves an energy consumption of 1.37 fJ/bit at 0.9 V and 77 K.

items.title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
items.abstract: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.

items.title: Antiferroelectric-Boost Charge Trapping Flash Enabled by Antiferroelectric/N-Rich-SiON Co-Optimization With 100-ns Operating Speed
items.abstract: In this work, we utilize ZrO2 antiferroelectric (AFE) to replace the blocking oxide layer (BL) of traditional oxide/nitride/oxide (ONO) charge trapping flash (CTF). Meanwhile, the tunneling oxide layer (TL) is nitrided to optimize the bandgap, trap energy levels, and the density of the traps. The novel AFE-boost charge trapping flash (AFE-Boost CTF) achieves a maximum memory window (MW) of 6.62 V with the program/erase (PGM/ERS) voltage less than 15 V. Besides, the ERS speed can reach 100 ns, which is much faster than that of traditional ONO flash. In addition, the device can achieve an endurance of more than 6000 cycles and exhibits a relatively stable retention. This work provides an alternative approach to the current scaling challenges faced by 3-D nand.

items.title: Analysis of Degradation Behaviors During Repetitive Operation Switching in Schottky GaN HEMT
items.abstract: In this study, the degradation trend between hard-switching and soft-switching stress under Schottky GaN high-electron mobility transistor (HEMT) is analyzed. The degradation in drain current becomes more severe as the switching waveform transitions from soft switching to hard switching. However, there is an unusual trend in the positive threshold voltage shift, characterized by an initial rise followed by a decline. The deterioration of soft switching is dominated by the off-state leakage. In the case of hard switching, the degradation is dominated by hot electrons and the trap-assisted thermionic field emission (TA-TFE) mechanism and is verified by pulse stress under different periods, but there are issues observed in the off-state as well. The steady-state conditions during the on- and off-states, along with temperature-dependent analyses, are employed to explain this unusual trend. This degradation results from the chain reaction of the rapid switching between the off-state and the on-state, making it challenging to be observed under the steady-state conditions.

items.title: An SAC-Based Auto Optimization Model for Dynamic Current Balancing of Multichip Paralleled SiC Power Module
items.abstract: The dynamic current imbalance between the paralleled SiC mosfets in multichip power modules, which is commonly attributed to the asymmetric module layout, severely limits their current capacity and thermal reliability. Adjusting the connection points of bonding wires is an effective method to mitigate imbalanced dynamic current. However, manual trial-and-error is currently the most common method for optimizing connection points, which is both deficient and inefficient. Existing automated solutions usually rely on a prefitting process based on large datasets, which is time-consuming and impractical for high-dimensional parameter applications. Thus, this article proposes an optimization model to mitigate dynamic current imbalance, which can automatically adjust the connection points of bonding wires without any manual intervention. The reinforcement learning (RL) soft actor-critic algorithm was applied to the power module optimization, eliminating the need for prefitting and enabling high-dimensional parameter optimization. After optimization, nearly complete dynamic current balancing in both high-side and low-side switches in a multichip-paralleled half-bridge power module is achieved, as verified by simulations and experiments. This model achieves true dynamic current balancing automation for the first time, providing an important reference for the application of RL to the automated optimization of multichip power modules.

items.title: An NRZ/PAM-4 Dual-Mode Transmitter Using Tx-Interleaving Technique for Low-Power DRAM Interfaces
items.abstract: This article proposes a nonreturn-to-zero (NRZ)/PAM-4 dual-mode transmitter for low-power double data rate (LPDDR) memory interfaces that employs a transmitter-interleaving (TI) technique to enhance power efficiency while maintaining high-speed signaling capability. Instead of separate data and clock paths in the conventional dual-mode transmitters, the proposed architecture inserts clock-controlled NMOS switches into the low-voltage swing-terminated logic (LVSTL) output driver structure, thereby merging the serialization path with the driver stage. This structural integration eliminates the need for a dedicated high-speed serializer and reduces switching activity in the driver block. A prior TI driver-based transmitter requires a clock bootstrapping circuit and typically does not support ZQ calibration, resulting in impedance mismatch. In contrast, this work removes the bootstrapping circuit and adopts a dual-mode ZQ calibration scheme that maintains constant output impedance across both NRZ and PAM-4 modes. A prototype chip is fabricated in a 1-poly 10-metal (1P10LM) 28-nm CMOS process. Measured results demonstrate that the proposed transmitter consumes 10.82 mW while transmitting 11-Gb/s PAM-4 data, achieving an energy efficiency of 0.98-pJ/b, confirming that the proposed structure is highly suitable for LPDDR.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: Adaptive Management With Learning-Based Page-Level FTL for Flash-Based SSDs
items.abstract: We present LearnedFTL+, a demand-based, page-level flash translation layer (FTL) that integrates learned-index-based translation with adaptive DRAM co-management to improve address translation efficiency in flash-based SSDs. LearnedFTL+ combines two complementary components under a fixed DRAM budget: A cached mapping table (CMT) for locality-rich accesses and a learned-index region for accesses where the CMT becomes ineffective. To make learned indexing practical for SSD address translation, we introduce three key techniques. First, an in-place-update linear model with a bitmap filter ensures that only trustworthy predictions are used for direct translation. Second, a virtual PPN (VPPN) representation constructs contiguous LPN-to-VPPN mappings without restricting physical placement. Third, group-based allocation, together with training assisted by sequential writes and GC, reduces model-training overhead. In addition, LearnedFTL+ supports eviction-driven model initialization and unified eviction across CMT entries and model segments, enabling adaptive DRAM co-management according to runtime access behavior. Experiments on a FEMU-based SSD prototype show that LearnedFTL+ improves throughput by up to 71.6% and reduces I/O latency by 11.9% on average, compared to state-of-the-art page-level FTLs.

items.title: Achieving Large Memory Window and Area-Efficient FeFETs via Vertically Stacked Ferroelectric Gates
items.abstract: Large-memory-window (MW) ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with high area efficiency and high reliability are experimentally demonstrated using a vertical stacked-ferroelectric-gate (SFG) architecture. The TiN-separated FE gates enable enhanced voltage fraction across the FE stack and effective polarization switching, without increasing the lateral footprint. Based on this design, the proposed SFG-FeFETs exhibit $16\times $ higher operation-voltage-normalized MW and $14\times $ higher FE-thickness-normalized MW than metal-ferroelectric-metal-insulator-semiconductor (MFMIS) FeFETs at area ratio of 1. The results confirm that the MW enhancement originates from the SFG architecture rather than increased operation voltage or FE thickness. Benefiting from robust and uniform FE sublayers, the SFG-FeFETs exhibit projected 10-year retention, endurance beyond $10^{{10}}$ cycles, and write-disturb immunity exceeding $10^{{7}}$ cycles. The design of SFG architecture provides a promising route toward FE memories with large MW, minimal area overhead, and high reliability.

items.title: AI-assisted performance prediction and optimization of CMOS and GDI logic circuits at 45 nm
items.abstract: An artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted optimization framework is presented for low-power digital circuit design using gate diffusion input (GDI) logic in 45 nm complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology. Core combinational and sequential building blocks, including logic gates, adders, multiplexers, and flip-flops, are implemented at the transistor level using Cadence Virtuoso and compared against conventional CMOS realizations. To accelerate design-space exploration, a random forest regression (RFR) model is trained using transistor-level simulation data to predict power consumption and propagation delay based on supply voltage, transistor sizing, and load capacitance. The proposed model achieves prediction accuracy exceeding 95%, reducing repeated SPICE simulation effort by approximately 45%. Simulation results demonstrate that GDI-based designs achieve up to 55% reduction in power consumption, 45% reduction in silicon area, and nearly 50% improvement in power delay product (PDP) compared to CMOS implementations, while maintaining delay variation within acceptable limits. A cross-technology comparison with 90 nm designs further confirms the scalability and energy efficiency of the proposed approach. The integrated AI–GDI method provides an effective solution for energy-efficient very large scale integration (VLSI) and embedded system applications.
items.venue: International Journal of Reconfigurable and Embedded Systems (IJRES)

items.title: A zero-power biasing approach for Mach–Zehnder modulators using phase-change materials
items.abstract: High-performance and energy-efficient optical modulators are indispensable for the development of next-generation high-speed optical interconnects. Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) has emerged as a leading platform owing to its large Pockels coefficient and broad optical transparency. Despite the outstanding performance of lithium niobate electro-optic (EO) modulators, a bias method is typically required to set the Mach–Zehnder modulators (MZMs) to the operating point. Conventional bias schemes, whether based on EO or thermo-optic (TO) approaches, consume static power to sustain the bias. In this work, we integrate the low-loss phase-change material (PCM) Sb2Se3 into the phase-shifting section of a TFLN MZM, enabling precise nonvolatile phase calibration and zero-power biasing. Laser-induced crystallization is employed to program the PCM phase state for bias adjustment, and replacing the TO heaters further simplifies chip layout. In addition, the high-speed performance of the PCM-biased modulator has been verified, with 120 Gbps on–off keying and 160 Gbps four-level pulse amplitude modulation successfully demonstrated. The proposed PCM-biased strategy shows great potential and offers a scalable and energy-efficient solution for bias establishment in advanced TFLN modulators.

items.title: A nonlinear mathematical model for the transient heat equation in resistive memories
items.abstract: Resistive random access memories (RRAMs) operate, in general, by means of the reversible formation (set process) and rupture (reset process) of nanometric conductive filaments (CF). Capturing correctly their reset dynamics requires, under certain conditions, a mathematical treatment that goes beyond the linear Fourier description of heat conduction to describe experimental data. In this work, we formulate a nonlinear constitutive law for heat transport, consistent with Landauer’s approach to address physical systems in the nanoscale regime, and couple it with electrostatics and filament kinetics to describe the temperature dependence of CF rupture. The resulting multiphysics system is implemented in weak form using the COMSOL Physics Builder , which enables the creation of a new physics module not available in standard libraries. This custom module simultaneously solves the electrical potential, non-linear heat flux, and CF evolution, while a workflow updates both the CF geometry and the simulator mesh along different time steps to balance numerical accuracy and computational performance. Simulations demonstrate that non-linear heat transport could contribute to explain RRAM operation. From a mathematical viewpoint, the study emphasizes the role of discretization strategies, adaptive meshing, and reduced-order formulations in capturing strongly localized, transient phenomena. The proposed framework is thus both physically consistent and computationally rigorous, offering a reproducible methodology for the analysis of nonlinear multiphysics systems at the nanoscale.

items.title: A Valuewise Hybrid-Domain Compute-In-Memory Macro for Energy-Efficient Edge-AI Devices
items.abstract: This article presents a valuewise hybrid (VWH) compute-in-memory (CIM) macro that improves hybrid efficiency by $1.75\times $ while simultaneously reducing computation error by $2.02\times $ compared to prior bitwise hybrid schemes. The VWH approach performs accurate computations digitally for the most significant values (MSVs) in a small proportion, while the vast majority of the values are processed by lossy analog CIM (ACIM) macros to achieve high energy efficiency. To minimize latency and enhance the energy efficiency of the ACIM macros, a heterogeneous memory fabric (HMF) is introduced, which combines the benefits of static random access memory (SRAM)-CIM and dynamic random access memory (DRAM)-CIM. In addition, an asynchronous sparsity manager (ASM) enables adaptive throughput and power consumption based on sparsity. Fabricated using a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype VWH-CIM macro achieves energy efficiencies of 470.5 TOPS/W in four-bit mode, 109.8 TOPS/W in eight-bit mode, and 48.5 TOPS/W in 12-bit mode.

items.title: A Two-Stage Turn-On Crosstalk Model for SiC MOSFETs in Half-Bridge Circuits
items.abstract: SiC mosfet s suffer from serious crosstalk issues due to their fast-switching speed and low threshold voltage, which threatens the device's reliability. It is commonly believed that the crosstalk voltage is caused by the rapid change in the drain-source voltage during the Miller plateau stage coupled with the gate-drain capacitance ( C gd ). However, this article reveals that the crosstalk voltage can also be induced by the small variation in the body diode voltage drop during the current commutation stage, which is commonly overlooked. This phenomenon is attributed to the pronounced increase in C gd as the drain-gate voltage ( V dg ) approaches zero and becomes negative. The underlying physical mechanism of the nonlinearity of C gd over the entire V dg range is elucidated. Based on these findings, a two-stage dv/dt -dependent crosstalk model incorporating both the current commutation stage and the Miller plateau stage is proposed. The proposed model is experimentally verified using SiC mosfet s with Kelvin-source connection in a half-bridge configuration. The findings of this article provide new insights into the root cause of crosstalk behavior and contribute to the design of crosstalk mitigation strategies.

items.title: A Two-Phase 140-A/1-MHz GaN–Silicon Hybrid Voltage Regulator Module for Vertical Power Delivery
items.abstract: This article presents a vertical power delivery (VPD) module that integrates hybrid devices within a compact 3-D structure. The proposed module addresses the limitations of individual device technologies by leveraging the fast switching capability of gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) and the high current handling capacity of Silicon mosfet s. The VPD scheme minimizes power distribution network parasitics, enabling efficient high-frequency operation. Furthermore, an alloy powder inductor is optimized to achieve high peak current capability. Experimental results demonstrate that the two-phase prototype achieves a peak efficiency of 91.4% (1 V / 50 A) and full-load efficiency of 83.6% (1 V / 140 A) at 12 V input with a switching frequency of 1 MHz. The prototype current density reaches 0.79 A/mm $^{2}$ and an inductor current density of 2.75 A/mm $^{2}$ .

items.title: A Third-Quadrant Transient Voltage Method for Hole Trapping and Threshold Voltage Shift Characteristics in SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Gate oxide defects in silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs have emerged as a primary cause of threshold voltage $\boldsymbol {\textbf {(}} {V}_{\mathbf {\text {TH}}} \boldsymbol {\textbf {)}}$ shift, significantly impacting device reliability. In this work, we have developed a gate-bias-free third-quadrant transient voltage method based on the body effect to effectively extract hole traps associated with the ${V}_{\text {TH}}$ shift in SiC MOSFETs. By measuring the transient voltage of the body diode, the pure detrapping behaviors can be directly extracted without applying an additional gate voltage. The time constants and activation energies of two distinct hole traps in the gate oxide layer are accurately extracted. Tp1 with an energy level of ${E}_{\text {V}}{\,}{\,}+{\,}{\,}{0}.{34} ~\text {eV}$ is attributed to interface traps at the $\text {SiO}_{\textbf {{2}}}$ /SiC interface following NO annealing. Tp2 exhibits a higher energy level of ${E}_{\text {v}}{\,}{\,}+{\,}{\,}{0}.{79} ~\text {eV}$ and a much longer time constant (>150 s). It is identified as a near-interface oxide trap, which becomes active under medium electric field stress and facilitates the Poole–Frenkel (PF) tunneling. This method provides an effective approach for profiling gate oxide reliability, which offers critical insights into the physical origins of ${V}_{\text {TH}}$ instability in SiC power devices.

items.title: A Surrogate-Assisted TCAD Modeling Framework for 4H-SiC/SiO2 Interface in 4H-SiC MOSFET
items.abstract: A surrogate-assisted TCAD modeling framework is proposed for the physics-based extraction of microscopic SiC/SiO2 interface properties in 4H-SiC MOSFETs. The framework incorporates interface charges, defect-state distributions, and carrier-scattering mechanisms, while a neural-network surrogate and an improved genetic algorithm enable efficient extraction of coupled interface parameters from device electrical characteristics. Compared with the conventional genetic algorithm and full TCAD-based genetic-algorithm optimization, the proposed framework achieves a $16.6\times $ speedup in parameter extraction while enabling quantitative identification of process-dependent microscopic interface properties. The extracted parameters reproduce the measured characteristics of devices with different gate oxidation processes, enabling quantitative comparison of process-dependent interface properties and linking gate-oxide processes to microscopic interface characteristics and device behavior.

items.title: A Surrogate Model for Variation-Aware Clock-Mesh Analysis and Design-Space Exploration using Graph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Clock meshes are widely used in high-performance VLSI systems to minimize skew and tolerate On-Chip Variation (OCV) in nanometer technologies. However, analyzing meshes is difficult because reconvergent paths and multi-source drivers prevent static timing analysis (STA) tools from handling mesh loops, making SPICE the industrial standard. SPICE simulations are accurate but slow, so clock-mesh synthesis relies on approximate models that overlook critical effects such as non-linear buffer driving caused by input slew and input skew. We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture that predicts power while also improving the delay and slew predictions at the sinks and capturing the skew histogram under OCV. Trained on SPICE data and tested on unseen real designs, our model achieves average errors of $3.40$~ps in delay, $4.14$~ps in slew and $4.46$~ps in skew, compared with $6.28$~ps, $12.35$~ps, and $11.62$~ps for our prior model, and $74.37$~ps delay and $27.51$~ps skew for the approximate method used in current state-of-the-art works. Our model predicts power within $3.4\%$ of SPICE on average, while delivering $18\times$-$1706\times$ speed-ups over the approximate method under OCV modeling, enabling faster and more accurate clock-mesh design-space exploration. A case study on a real design further shows that our surrogate model finds buffering candidates that, at a balanced tradeoff, improves $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile skew by $49.1\%$, reduces power by $25.7\%$, and reduces area by $37.3\%$ at the cost of a $6.8\%$ increase in $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile maximum slew as compared to the state-of-the-art work.

items.title: A Stacked Top Select Gate Architecture for High-Density 3-D nand Flash
items.abstract: In the pursuit of higher density 3D nand flash memory arrays, the “sacrificial holes” necessitated by traditional top select gate (TSG) for solid isolation present an enduring challenge to scaling. To overcome this barrier, this study proposes a novel TSG architecture featuring an independent stack design, which can reduce the channel to dielectric spacing to satisfy isolation requirements while eliminating “sacrificial holes” and significantly increasing storage density. Furthermore, the proposed architecture follows standard design with a solid polysilicon channel structure, relieving complex process demands.

items.title: A Simple Method to Extract the Field Effect Mobility of Free Carriers in SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: The observed low mobility in SiC MOSFETs is thought to be due to a high density of defects at or above the conduction band edge. Charge trapping in these defects greatly complicates conventional electrical analyses. In this work, we detail a simple analysis to quantify the charge trapping as modification to the threshold voltage. Accounting for this charge trapping allows for an extraction of field effect mobility of free carriers in the channel.

items.title: A Preload Compression Using Test Vector Segmentation for High-Speed Memory Testing
items.abstract: The algorithmic pattern generator (ALPG) is widely adopted to address massive test vector volumes in memory testing. However, the test rate is limited by the complex arithmetic operations required for real-time vector generation, making it difficult to match the high operating speeds of modern memory. While this test rate bottleneck is mitigated by adopting code-based compression schemes with simple decoding hardware, insufficient compression ratios are obtained for memory test vectors. Therefore, a new preload compression (PLC) is proposed to achieve high compression ratios and high-speed memory testing simultaneously. High compression efficiency is achieved by segmenting the test vector based on DRAM properties and preloading valid care bit fields into the don’t care (X) bit fields generated during mandatory stabilization cycles. Furthermore, high-speed memory testing is enabled by the PLC decoder through a simple mechanism that shifts preloaded care-bit data out or holds it to align with the original vector timing. In experimental results, test rates at least 62.58% higher than conventional ALPGs are achieved by the proposed PLC. Moreover, an average compression ratio 25.56% higher than conventional compression methods is achieved for test vectors generated by diverse test patterns and memory specifications.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A Physics-Based Reconstruction Framework for fmax in RF GaN HEMTs: From Technology Scaling to Power-Gain Formation
items.abstract: A physics-based reconstruction framework for the maximum oscillation frequency ( ${f}_{\textit {ma}{x}}\text {)}$ is established by revisiting Mason’s unilateral gain ( ${U}_{g}\text {)}$ . Its numerator is reinterpreted using the delay-decomposition framework for the current-gain cutoff frequency ( ${f}_{T}\text {)}$ , while its denominator is decomposed into output-conductance and gate-feedback charging penalties. The intrinsic and extrinsic parameters governing these penalties are predicted using physics-based gate-length ( ${L}_{g}\text {)}$ scaling relationships and complementary DC/RF characterization techniques. This formulation expresses ${f}_{\textit {ma}{x}}$ in the delay domain as the combined outcome of current-gain formation and parasitic-limited power-gain multiplication. The proposed framework establishes a direct hierarchical link from technology scaling and HEMT physics to current-gain formation, power-gain formation and ultimately ${f}_{\textit {ma}{x}}$ , thereby revealing the dominant ${L}_{g}$ -dependent power-gain limiting mechanisms. Validation over the investigated ${L}_{g}$ and bias ranges shows excellent agreement between the predicted and experimentally extracted values of ${M}_{p}$ and ${f}_{\textit {ma}{x}}$ , verifying the proposed physics-based reconstruction framework.

items.title: A Novel Polar Zinc‐Based Hybrid Material: Structure, Properties, and Memristive Performance
items.abstract: Memristors are promising components for neuromorphic computing because of their resistive switching and synaptic functionalities, enabling more energy‐efficient computing architectures. Lead halide perovskites are attractive memristive materials due to their coupled ionic‐electronic conductivity, but lead toxicity limits their practical use. Herein, we report a new lead‐free hybrid zinc halide, (CHA) 2 [ZnI 4 ] (CHA = cyclohexylammonium), synthesized through a simple, scalable, and environmentally friendly route. Single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction shows that the compound crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure composed of isolated (ZnI 4 ) 2− tetrahedra separated by CHA cations, resembling Ruddlesden–Popper phases despite its zero‐dimensional nature. Although the material is polar, no ferroelectric behavior is observed due to dominant electrical losses, likely related to its 3.9 eV bandgap. Memristors based on (CHA) 2 [ZnI 4 ] exhibit stable and reproducible electroforming‐free resistive switching at low voltages, together with short‐ and long‐term synaptic plasticity under pulsed bias. These results establish (CHA) 2 [ZnI 4 ] as a promising sustainable material for memory and neuromorphic applications and demonstrate the potential of Zn‐based hybrid halides for advanced electronic devices.

items.title: A Novel Grid-Based, Reconfigurable Strong PUF Architecture Integrated With MRAM, Resilient to Learning-Based Inference
items.abstract: This article presents a reconfigurable physical unclonable function (PUF) architecture integrated into a novel magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM) structure to mitigate read disturbance. Designed using 7-nm FinFET technology, the design employs an advanced write scheme that improves area and delay efficiency relative to conventional memory. A resilient writing circuit enables dynamic reconfigurability by altering magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) states. A novel level converter reduces the transistor count from 14 to 8 without using thick-oxide devices, thereby maintaining gate voltages within V DD limits. Postlayout simulations validate the design’s efficiency for both memory write operations and PUF operations. The PUF array occupies $34.7\mu $ m 2 and achieves ultralow energy consumption of 7.78 fJ per bit, making it suitable for IoT applications. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations confirm robust performance, with a worst case average bit error rate (BER) of 1.89%, an intra-Hamming distance (intra-HD) mean of 0.0077 and a standard deviation ( $\sigma $ ) of 0.0027, and excellent uniqueness with an inter-HD mean of 0.5000 and a $\sigma $ of 0.016. The PUF exhibits high diffuseness (mean: 0.499 and $\sigma $ : 0.015), passes all National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) randomness tests, and shows strong resistance against learning-based attacks, including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), multilayer perceptron (MLP), Larq, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), deep neural networks (DNNs), and reinforcement learning (RL), achieving almost 50% prediction accuracy after training on one million challenge–response pairs (CRPs). The architecture provides a larger CRP space than the median CRP space of benchmarked designs. Evaluated under process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations and process corners, the design demonstrates strong reliability, security, and efficiency, featuring a complete system-level architecture for secure authentication, reconfiguration, and enrollment suitable for IoT and edge-security applications.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A Novel Adaptive Crosstalk Detection and Selective Encoding Scheme Without Redundant Bits
items.abstract: Crosstalk in vertical interconnects of 2.5D and 3D integrated circuits has become a critical issue as interconnect density rapidly increases. With the scaling of through-silicon vias (TSVs) and micro-bumps, capacitive and inductive coupling intensifies, leading to signal degradation, timing errors, and increased power consumption in multi-layer architectures. This work presents a novel architecture for crosstalk detection and selective encoding and decoding to mitigate crosstalk effects. The primary objective of this work is to first detect both inductive and capacitive crosstalk patterns in the bitstream and then apply encoding and decoding selectively, ensuring minimal overhead and complexity. This detection and selective encoding approach significantly reduces computations compared to traditional crosstalk avoidance code (CAC), as on average, around 50% of the data does not require encoding for groups of 3-8 TSVs. However, the proposed architecture is designed using Python and Verilog, implemented on an Altera Cyclone V FPGA using Quartus, and analyzed at the RLC circuit level using Cadence Virtuoso. We achieve 100% accuracy in detecting opposite- and three-or-more same-side switching patterns, as well as in eliminating harmful switching through encoding, with minimal resource utilization on the FPGA. The design is synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler (SDC) at multiple process nodes, achieving a peak frequency of 2.128 GHz, with a critical path delay of 0.37 ns, an area of $163.7856~\mu m^{2}$ , and a power consumption of 0.1970 mW at the 45nm. Moreover, the proposed scheme does not require look-up tables, codeword books, or redundant bits for encoding. Together, this hardware-friendly approach demonstrates strong potential for deployment in future 2.5D and 3D integration technologies.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A Hybrid-Package 3-D GaN Power Module With Optimal Thermal Performance and High-Density Integration
items.abstract: Gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs), based on its superior characteristics, enable power electronic converters to evolve toward higher frequencies and greater power density. However, the high thermal flux density within the GaN HEMTs and the parasitic inductance introduced by the package limit the full realization of GaN's advantages. This article presents a 3-D integrated hybrid package using phase change vapor chamber, flexible printed circuit, direct plating copper, and diamond. This package improves vertical space utilization and reduces profile height. The design considerations, thermal and electrical properties are analyzed and the fabrication process is introduced. Finally, a 23×31×4.7 mm double-sided cooling half-bridge power module with integrated gate drivers is fabricated. Compared with double-sided ceramic module, the junction temperature can be reduced by 30% at a power loss of 60 W. The inductance of the power loop is reduced to 0.75 nH. This article optimizes the overall performance of GaN power module, balancing integration level with electrical and thermal performance.

items.title: A Hybrid Inner--Outer-Product SRAM Compute-in-Memory GEMM Engine With Precision-Adaptive Systolic Dataflow
items.abstract: This article presents an efficient SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macro design for general matrix multiplication (GEMM). A hybrid inner–outer product (HIOP) architecture is designed to enable long-time weight reusing and short-time input reusing, reducing 1.57– $2.69\times $ overall SRAM access. A data-precision-adaptive dataflow is developed to scale the CIM macros with balanced bandwidth (BW) across varying data precisions. Our CIM-friendly dataflow obtains 19%–38.5% reduction in operation cycles with the CIM capability of concurrent read/write and computing. Fabricated in 22-nm technology, the CIM macro achieves energy efficiency (EE) of 56.2 TOPS/W for GEMM and 71.65 TOPS/W for multiply–accumulate operation (MAC) in 8-bit inputs and weights. The macro and system area efficiency (AE) are 3.18 and 1.89 TOPS/mm 2 , respectively, which is $1.42\times $ and $1.12\times $ compared with prior state-of-the-art (SOTA) designs.

items.title: A Geometry-Scalable DC I–V Calibration Methodology for a Commercial Bulk CMOS Process Design Kit for Cryogenic ICs Operating Near 1 K
items.abstract: This article presents a systematic methodology for calibrating a commercial process design kit (PDK) for cryogenic CMOS (cryo-CMOS) integrated circuit (IC) design. Built on the PSP compact model adopted in the baseline PDK, the proposed approach calibrates cryogenic DC $I$ – $V$ characteristics across multiple device geometries through a structured geometry-aware parameter-tuning flow based on cryogenic DC measurements. By leveraging geometry-dependent parameterization supported by the PSP compact model, the methodology preserves compatibility with standard electronic design automation (EDA) toolchains. Using this methodology, a prototype cryo-CMOS PDK (cryo-PDK) is developed by calibrating a commercial 28-nm bulk CMOS PDK with a selected set of tuning-point (TP) devices. Its prediction accuracy at 1.58 K is then evaluated across both the TP devices and additional cross-point (CP) devices, which use an intermediate width and/or length within the TP boundary dimensions and are excluded from tuning. Compared with the baseline PDK predictions at 1.58 K, the proposed cryo-PDK reduces the mean drain-current error, normalized to the measured drain current, by up to 67.8 percentage points for nMOS TP devices, 66.3 percentage points for nMOS CP devices, 40.6 percentage points for pMOS TP devices, and 45.5 percentage points for pMOS CP devices. These results demonstrate substantial error reduction in cryogenic DC $I$ – $V$ prediction and the geometry scalability of the proposed calibration methodology.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A Dynamic Compact Model for Phase-Change Memory With Coupled Thermal--Electrical--Phase Dynamics
items.abstract: A dynamic thermal–electrical–phase (TEP) compact model for phase-change memory (PCM) is presented and implemented in Verilog-A for device-to-subarray simulation. The model establishes a closed-loop coupling mechanism in which terminal electrical power induces self-heating, temperature governs phase dynamics, and the resulting phase configuration in turn modulates electrical conduction and threshold-switching behavior. Effective latent heat, quench-dependent solidification, and distinct threshold and holding conditions are formulated using continuous and bounded state equations. Calibrated against measurements from a 40-nm 64-Mb prototype chip, the model accurately reproduces the I–V characteristics, bidirectional programming, and multilevel programming capability. Monte Carlo simulations with parameter variations further capture device-to-device variability. Array-level validation demonstrates complete SET–read-- RESET–read operation in 1024 explicitly instantiated cells, while transient simulations of up to 32 768 cells complete without convergence failure. Overall, the model provides a physically consistent, numerically robust, and computationally efficient framework for PCM memory and in-memory-computing circuit design.

items.title: A Dual-Channel GaN HEMT Nanosecond Pulse Generator With Enhanced Rising Edge and Frequency-Doubling Operation
items.abstract: Nanosecond pulse generators with fast voltage transitions and high repetition rates are required in advanced pulsed-power applications such as electron gun grid control, plasma generation, and high-speed pulsed driving systems. However, achieving subnanosecond rising edges at elevated repetition frequencies remains challenging due to switching limitations and parasitic effects in compact power loops. This article proposes a dual-channel nanosecond pulse generator based on independently driven GaN HEMTs. The proposed generator operates in two modes. In the synchronous mode, two parallel switches are turned on simultaneously to enhance the transient current capability and accelerate the pulse rising edge. In the delayed-trigger mode, the two channels are triggered sequentially to achieve frequency doubling without increasing the switching frequency of each device. To support fast switching, a floating half-bridge gate driver with adjustable positive and negative gate voltages is employed, and a compact symmetric PCB layout is adopted to suppress loop parasitic inductance. A 200-V prototype is built to validate the proposed design. Experimental results show that the 10%–90% rise time of the load pulse is reduced from 920 ps in single-device operation to 710 ps under synchronous dual-device operation. In addition, nanosecond-range pulsewidth tuning and stable 20-MHz output operation within a 10- $\mu $ s macropulse are experimentally demonstrated. The results verify the feasibility of the proposed generator for high-speed nanosecond pulse generation requiring fast rising edges and high effective repetition rates.

items.title: A Crosstalk Suppression Scheme Utilizing the Dynamic Shielding and Bit-Stuffing Code for Hexagonal TSV Arrays
items.abstract: The through-silicon via (TSV) arrays play the role of vertical electrical interconnections in the chiplet-based integrated circuits. The hexagonal array achieves a higher TSV density than the rectangular array, but it suffers from more severe inter-TSV crosstalk, which increases the interconnection delay and deteriorates the signal integrity. Researchers have proposed many crosstalk suppression schemes based on the shielding and crosstalk avoidance code (CAC) techniques, but most of them are applicable only to rectangular arrays. This article proposes a crosstalk suppression scheme utilizing the dynamic shielding and bit-stuffing code techniques for hexagonal TSV arrays. First, a novel dynamic shielding scheme is proposed to reduce the maximum crosstalk of the signal TSVs in hexagonal arrays. Then, the bit-stuffing CAC (BS-CAC) is proposed to eliminate the data patterns that cause the high-level crosstalk when these patterns are transmitted through TSVs. The analysis and simulation show that the proposed scheme is able to reduce the inter-TSV crosstalk in hexagonal arrays by 4C-level with the bit overhead of less than 51.5%, and the hardware overhead is less than the existing FTF/FPF-CAC methods.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A 9.75-Gb/s Matrix-Assisted Anchor-Decoding TPC Decoder for NAND Flash Memories
items.abstract: With the increasing storage demand driven by artificial intelligence and other data-intensive applications, nand flash memories require error-correction code (ECC) solutions that provide sufficient correction capability while maintaining low power consumption. Although low-density parity-check (LDPC) decoders are widely used in modern nand flash controllers, their soft-decision decoding process usually introduces high implementation complexity and power overhead. Turbo product codes (TPCs), which rely on iterative hard-decision decoding (iHDD), offer a low-complexity alternative. In this work, a matrix-assisted anchor-decoding (MA-AD) TPC decoder architecture is proposed. The proposed design employs an error matrix, conflict registers, and a rollback handling unit to realize conflict detection and rollback operations. By reorganizing the dynamic and irregular anchor-decoding procedure into a static matrix-assisted decoding flow, the proposed architecture becomes more suitable for hardware implementation. Compared with the conventional extended Bose–Chaudhuri–Hocquenghem (eBCH)-based TPC decoder, the proposed MA-AD TPC decoder improves the correction capability in the waterfall region by 0.25 dB with a limited reduction in throughput. Implementation results show that the proposed decoder achieves an area of 0.49 mm2, a throughput of 9.75 Gb/s, and an energy efficiency of 6.5 pJ/bit.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: A 3-bit Digitally-Reconfigurable Driving-Capability nW-Powered Three-Stage Fully-Synthesizable Inverter-Based OTA for Multi-Load/Applications
items.abstract: This paper presents a fully synthesizable three-stage inverter-based operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) featuring a 3-bit digitally reconfigurable output stage for robust operation across a wide range of capacitive loads in ultra-low-voltage (ULV) and ultra-low-power (ULP) environments. Implemented entirely with standard-cell inverters and inverting-tristate (ITS) buffers, the proposed architecture operates from a 0.3-V supply while consuming less than 2.7 nW. The digital tuning mechanism enables near-constant gain-bandwidth product ( $GBW$ ) and average slew rate ( ${SR}_{av}$ ) across a 10-110 pF load range, making the OTA suitable for both on-chip and off-chip applications in battery-less and energy-harvested systems. Fabricated in 180-nm CMOS, the OTA achieves > 65-dB DC gain, 3.5-kHz $GBW$ , 0.16-V/ms ${SR}_{av}$ , and 94% rail-to-rail output swing, while demonstrating strong resilience to PVT variations. Measurements confirm > 2.1X improvement in small-signal efficiency establishing a new state-of-the-art for < 0.5-V digital-based OTAs.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 3-MHz All-NMOS Adaptive Active Gate Driver With Dual-Buffer Architecture and Detection-Free CSIV Spike Suppression for SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: This paper presents the on-chip all-NMOS adaptive active gate driver (ANA-AGD) for high-speed, high-voltage SiC MOSFET applications. A dual-floating dual-buffer architecture enables inherent suppression of Common Source Inductance Voltage (CSIV)-induced oscillations without auxiliary sensing circuits. By forming two floating source-buffer paths with distinct frequency responses, the architecture generates a transient voltage difference in response to high-frequency CSIV components, enabling implicit spike discrimination without explicit sensing circuits. An active float bridge (AFB) is introduced to ensure reliable signal transmission across floating domains, preventing signal distortion and device overstress under high-voltage operation. In addition, an adaptive drive strength (ADS) structure dynamically regulates the gate-driving current through a frequency-dependent mechanism, limiting excessive current during fast transients while enhancing drive capability during the Miller plateau region. The proposed driver is fabricated using TSMC $0.18~\mu $ m CMOS HV BCD (T18HVG2) process. Measurements validate operation from 1 kHz to 3 MHz while driving a 1.2-kV SiC MOSFET. The proposed driver achieves a rise time below 25 ns at 500 kHz and an average power consumption of 58 mW. Compared to a widely-used commercial gate driver, the overshoot rate is significantly reduced from 47.3% to 1.4%, confirming effective suppression of CSIV-induced oscillations. These results demonstrate that the proposed ANA-AGD provides a compact, power-efficient, and high-speed solution for robust SiC MOSFET gate driving without requiring explicit sensing circuitry.
authors: L. S. S. P. K. Chodisetti
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 28-nm Sign-Bit-Embedded Bit-Parallel SRAM Compute-in-Memory Macro With Stage-Wise-Enabled Transition-Counting-Lines and Accumulators for Edge-AI Devices
items.abstract: Computing-in-memory (CIM) architectures are promising for edge-AI devices, as they mitigate the von Neumann bottleneck and reduce data movement. Bit-parallel CIM macros with direct memory mapping and low toggle rate are well-suited for computing systems. However, severe routing congestion, inefficient signed computation, and unnecessary toggling of intermediate signals in local multiply-accumulate (MAC) circuits remain unsolved. This article presents a 28-nm bit-parallel SRAM CIM macro for efficient INT8 and BF16 MAC operations, featuring three techniques: 1) a transition-counting-line (TCL) that performs sparsity-adaptive, lossless bit-column compression by recording full-swing transitions derived from partial products, thereby mitigating routing congestion while preserving full precision; 2) a bus-based TCL that reuses sign-bit multiply-multiplex units (MMUs) to realize embedded sign extension with only 3% area overhead and no additional cycles; and 3) a shared ten-phase generator that enables TCLs and accumulations in a stage-wise manner to suppress spurious toggling, improving energy efficiency by 42%. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the 32-kb macro occupies 0.072 mm2 and supports 64 input channels. The macro achieves a 4.1-ns access time at 0.9 V, with peak energy efficiencies of 106.85 TOPS/W in INT8 mode and 77.68 TFLOPS/W in BF16 mode, and peak area efficiencies of 1.73 TOPS/mm2 and 1.24 TFLOPS/mm2, respectively.

items.title: A 28-nm Floating-Point SRAM-CIM Macro With In-Array Shifting for Exponent Normalization and Mantissa Alignment Based on Exponent Midrange
items.abstract: Floating-point computing-in-memory (FP-CIM) macros typically suffer from prohibitive area and power overheads due to the complexity of alignment logic. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel FP-CIM macro that integrates two key in-memory operations: shifting-in-memory exponent normalization (SIMENP) and shifting-in-memory mantissa alignment (SIMMAP). SIMENP enables in-array exponent shifting using the proposed 9T bitcell, thereby eliminating redundant processing latency. For mantissa alignment, a midrange-based subtraction-shifting scheme is implemented using the proposed 10T bitcell, which obviates the need for dedicated shift registers while halving the clock cycles required for data shifting. The proposed macro is designed and simulated in a 28-nm CMOS process with a 36-kB capacity. Simulation results demonstrate an energy efficiency of 11.63 TFLOPS/W at 150 MHz under a 0.55 V supply. Compared to state-of-the-art subtractor-based FP-CIM architectures and D flip-flop (DFF) combined schemes, the proposed design reduces the shifting-logic area by 45.7%, while also reducing the number of cycles required for mantissa alignment by 50%.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: A 28-nm 64-kb Bit-Rotated Hybrid Domain Computing-in-Memory Macro for High-Performance Computing
items.abstract: The development of computing-in-memory (CIM) has gone through the era of analog domain CIM, which pursued extreme energy efficiency and area efficiency, and the era of digital domain CIM, which pursued extreme computational precision. Currently, research is exploring hybrid domain CIM designs that combine the advantages of both analog and digital approaches. In order to find a better balance point between computational precision and hardware efficiency, this work proposes a bit-rotated hybrid domain CIM design which primarily employs: 1) a bit-rotated feature-in hybrid structure to achieve the optimal boundary segmentation (better computational precision) with lower hardware overhead; 2) an embedded sign-bit-processing SRAM array, enabling sign-bit extension with low hardware overhead; 3) an multi-bit-fusion scheme for low-power multi-bit quantization; and 4) a dual-granularity cooperative quantizer based on the charge domain, supporting low-power multi-cycle quantization. A 64 kb bit-rotated hybrid-domain CIM chip was fabricated with TSMC 28 nm. It supports efficient hybrid multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations and achieves 21.04–67.8 TOPS/W in energy efficiency and 0.41–1.57 TOPS/mm2 in area efficiency, which can be used to accelerate various CNN and Transformer based inference tasks.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 28-nm 2.25-Mb CO-DCIM RRAM Macro With 1.25-ns/bit Read Speed, 0.12-pJ/bit, and 12.85-Mb/mm2 Storage Density for Autoregressive Transformer
items.abstract: Edge AI urgently demand computing hardware with large on-chip storage capacity, low memory access overhead. Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based digital computing-in-memory (DCIM) suits such scenarios by achieving a optimized performance balance in calculation precision, storage density and access overhead. However, traditional RRAM-DCIM scheme suffers from two issues: 1) RRAM multi-bit storage boosts density but introduces significant errors, while conventional ECC scheme requires massive redundant bits that offset density gains; 2) Wiring RC parasitism in large-scale arrays leads to slow and energy-intensive random access. To resolve these issues, the proposed computation-oriented DCIM (CO-DCIM) paradigm integrates two core solutions: a hierarchical multi-bit storage coding scheme and a charge-domain continuous access scheme. The designed CO-DCIM macro is fabricated in a 28nm CMOS technology. Measurement results show a single RRAM read latency of 2.5 ns, normalized read energy of 0.12 pJ/bit, and a storage density of 12.85 Mb/mm2. The macro is further evaluated on public SimpleAR-0.5B-RL and SimpleAR-1.5B-RL workloads, showing a 29.2x reduction in mapped-weight access energy relative to LPDDR5X DRAM at $256\times 256$ resolution.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 100--140-GHz Differential LNA Using Stacked-Transistor Neutralized Cascode Topology
items.abstract: This letter presents a 100–140-GHz low-noise amplifier (LNA) implemented in a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology using a neutralization technique based on stacked transistors. High gain, low noise, and wide bandwidth (BW) are achieved by applying the proposed neutralization technique, which consists of stacked transistors to precisely attain the low capacitance required at F-band. The fabricated two-stage LNA is based on differential cascode topology and achieves a peak gain of 28.7 dB with a 3-dB BW ranging from 100 to 140 GHz while consuming 30.7 mW from a 1.8-V supply. The measured noise figure (NF) is 3.3 dB at 132 GHz, while the fit NF curve reaches 4.5 dB. An input 1-dB compression point ( $\textbf {IP}_{\textbf {1 dB}}$ ) of $\mathrm {-19.8~dBm}$ and an input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of $\mathrm {-14.1~dBm}$ are measured. The LNA is evaluated under modulated signals using a 128-QAM scheme at a symbol rate of $\mathrm {2~\text {G}baud}$ , resulting in an error vector magnitude (EVM) of −30.46 dB at −26-dBm peak input power. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this work achieves the lowest measured NF and the highest reported figure of merit (FoM) among silicon-based F- and D-band LNAs.
items.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters

items.title: 3-D NMC-HBM: Design of 3-D Near Memory Computing Architecture in High Bandwidth Memory Considering Signal/Power Integrity and Computing Performance
items.abstract: In this article, we propose a design framework for a 3-D near-memory computing architecture in high bandwidth memory (3-D NMC-HBM) considering signal/power integrity (SI/PI) and computing performance. The design framework enables the physical codesign of the 3-D interconnect and power distribution network (PDN) based on an electrical performance evaluation, while integrating the extracted interconnect-level parameters into a cycle-accurate simulator for a system-level performance evaluation. Each component of the 3-D NMC-HBM architecture including the NMC processor die, interconnect channels, and a hierarchical 3-D PDN is modeled considering the physical dimensions of the conventional graphics processing unit (GPU)-HBM module. The electrical performance of the 3-D NMC-HBM architecture is analyzed using a detailed methodology considering SI for providing the extended bandwidth, and PI to ensure stable power delivery for high performance operation of the NMC processing units. Furthermore, the efficacy of the proposed framework is verified through a system-level evaluation. Integrated with a cycle-accurate GPU simulator, the computing performance and power consumption of the 3-D NMC-HBM architecture is evaluated, considering the effects of reduced interconnect length, bandwidth extension, and higher core utilization. The results show that the 3-D NMC-HBM architecture achieves higher computing performance and lower power consumption when computing memory-bound workloads, compared to the GPU-HBM.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: 28-nm High-Consistency SRAM-CIM Macro With Cascode Current Mirror for Convolutional Neural Networks
items.abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), neural network applications demand increasingly efficient data processing. The traditional von Neumann architecture faces a growing “memory wall” bottleneck, making computing-in-memory (CIM) a highly promising solution. This brief presents a 4-Kb 10T static random access memory (SRAM)-CIM macro designed for convolutional neural networks (CNNs), featuring a charge–discharge consistency circuit based on a cascode current mirror that provides stable bias voltages for current-domain computation. The proposed architecture significantly improves the consistency and linearity of bitline charging and discharging, thereby enhancing computational accuracy. Furthermore, only four tail transistors in the 10T SRAM bit cell are used to perform computation, greatly improving throughput. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the SRAM-CIM macroachieves an energy efficiency of 26.43–68.78 TOPS/W and a throughput of 1016 GOPS. With four-bit signed input and four-bit unsigned weight precision, the circuit achieves estimated inference accuracies of 93.4% on the MNIST dataset and 81.6% on the CIFAR-10 dataset.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: 1.6-GW/cm2 Baliga’s Figure-of-Merit Au-Free p-GaN Gate HEMTs on 6-in Si Enabled by Regrown Ohmic Contacts
items.abstract: High-performance p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) on 6-inch Si were demonstrated using a CMOS-compatible, Au-free ohmic scheme. Selective MOCVD regrowth of heavily Si-doped n + -InGaN yielded an excellent low wafer-level average contact resistance (R ${}_{\text {c}}\text {)}$ of $0.14~\Omega \cdot $ mm. The integration of regrown ohmic contacts with a dual field-plate architecture, comprising lateral and vertical components, effectively redistributed the electric field and enhanced breakdown performance. For devices with a $15~\mu $ m gate–drain spacing, a threshold voltage of 1 V, a saturation drain current of 465 mA/mm, and an on-resistance (R ${}_{\text {on}}\text {)}$ of $7.2~\Omega \cdot $ mm were achieved, along with an off-state breakdown voltage of 1620 V. These metrics correspond to a Baliga’s figure of merit of 1.6 GW/cm 2 , indicating competitive performance among GaN-on-Si p-GaN HEMTs. Across the 6-inch wafer, both contact resistance and channel sheet resistance exhibited tight distributions, underscoring the manufacturability and process uniformity of the Au-free approach within Si CMOS production lines. This scalable, contamination-free process provides a practical pathway toward high-volume production of GaN power devices with robust electrical performance and CMOS fab compatibility.

items.title: te-comp: A Complete MLIR Compiler Generating Self-Contained C Inference Engines for MCUs
items.abstract: Deploying deep learning on microcontrollers (MCUs) requires fitting both the model weights and runtime activations within tens to hundreds of kilobytes of SRAM and Flash. Existing approaches either use an interpreter with a pre-written kernel library or combine a Python code generator with hand-written C kernels. This incurs dispatch overhead and requires framework dependencies. None produces self-contained, dependency-free C code specialized to a given model. In this paper, we present te-comp, the first complete MLIR-based compiler that takes a standard model in .tflite or .safetensors format and emits all C source files needed for deployment: the inference engine (kernels, weight arrays, memory layout) and the RTOS integration layer with zero runtime dependencies. On 10 MCUNet CNN benchmarks, te-comp outperforms MCUNet TinyEngine by using 38% less SRAM (up to 5.9$\times$) and 15% less Flash, while generating complete C code rather than linking a pre-written kernel library. To demonstrate, we use te-comp to compile an 8.3M-parameter GPT-Neo transformer (TinyStories-v2) and deploy it on a single-core Cortex-M7 at 160MHz. The full firmware uses 249KB of 512KB SRAM and 3.62MB of 4MB Flash and achieves approximately 1 token/s interactive text generation via Q4_0 weight quantization, a stateful int4 KV cache, and vocabulary pruning -- a capability no existing MCU inference framework supports.

items.title: Themis: improving fairness and performance in multi-stream NVMe SSDs
items.abstract: NAND flash-based SSDs are widely adopted for their performance, with the NVMe interface further enhancing I/O throughput by providing multi-stream support. However, streams with high intensity and/or strong locality can monopolize shared resources, degrading fairness and performance of concurrent streams. Existing fairness efforts rely on a slowdown-based metric, which suffers from practical measurement challenges and limited accuracy, while neglecting request-level dynamics. Consequently, they optimize inter-stream fairness but overlook intra-stream variations. This paper introduces the Request IneQuality (RIQ) score, a requestlevel fairness metric based on the Lorenz curve computed from perrequest Normalized Completion Round (NCR) scores. Subsequently, we design a flash I/O scheduling mechanism called Themis, which monitors the NCRs of in-flight requests and applies a two-step scheduling strategy to improve both inter-stream and intra-stream fairness, thereby enhancing overall I/O service quality. Trace-driven simulation experiments using a variety of production multi-stream mixes show that Themis significantly improves request-level fairness, stream-level fairness, average I/O response time, as well as tail latency compared to state-of-the-art I/O schedulers.

items.title: Temperature-dependent operating margins of proton-irradiated integrated 4H-SiC CMOS current mirrors
items.abstract: Integrated 4H-SiC CMOS current mirrors and co-fabricated MOSFETs were characterized at temperatures up to 180 °C and after 15 MeV proton irradiation. The SiC mirrors retain highly linear current transfer over the measured current ranges, with coefficients of determination of 0.99943–0.999996 across the reported conditions. Heating reduces the threshold-voltage magnitude of both NMOS and PMOS devices, whereas irradiation predominantly increases the PMOS threshold-voltage magnitude and the supply voltage required for stable mirroring. Using a common target current ratio of 2.47, the minimum measured supply voltage of the type 2 mirror increases from 7.5 V before irradiation to 10.5 V after a fluence of 5 × 10¹³ cm⁻² at room temperature, and decreases to 9.5 V when the irradiated circuit is measured at 180 °C. Devices annealed in hydrogen before irradiation require higher supply voltages: 12.0 V at room temperature and 10.5 V at 180 °C.
