These results demonstrate partial, temperature-dependent improvement of the circuit operating margin after irradiation. They do not establish thermal removal of radiation-induced defects. The device and circuit measurements identify threshold-voltage shifts and processing history as relevant considerations for the operating margins of this SiC CMOS platform.

items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. GRAPE integrates a stable global predictor based on interpretable representations with two lightweight streaming adapters that correct feature-level and environment-level shifts through online updates. Experiments on two real-world semiconductor manufacturing datasets, including chronologically held-out blind-test streams, show that GRAPE improves robustness and generalization under real temporal drift compared with both conventional batch-learning methods and existing online learning baselines.

items.title: Single-Ended 7T SRAM Cell Design Using 18 nm FinFET Technology for Low-Power and High-Stability Nanoscale VLSI Applications
items.abstract: This study presents the design and performance evaluation of a single-ended seven-transistor (7T) static random-access memory (SRAM) cell in 18 nm fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) technology for low-power, high-stability nanoscale very-large-scale integration (VLSI) applications. The cell combines separate read and write bitline paths, a transmission-gate (TG) read port that removes read-bitline precharging and substantially reduces read disturb, and a virtual-ground (VGND) power-gating scheme that suppresses subthreshold leakage through the body effect. The cell is benchmarked against nine existing topologies (6T, 7T, two 8T, 9T, 10T, and three Schmitt-trigger cells), all re-simulated at the same 18 nm FinFET node to remove cross-technology bias. The evaluation covers hold, read, and write static noise margins (SNM), write-trip voltage, access time, dynamic and leakage power, and energy-delay product (EDP), together with five-corner process-voltage-temperature (PVT) analysis and Monte Carlo simulation with 1000 samples. The proposed cell reduces leakage power by 75.6% relative to a conventional 6T cell, achieves the highest write-trip voltage (615.2 mV) of all compared cells, and ranks fourth-lowest in normalized EDP, at an estimated area of 1.18 times that of the 6T cell. The combined Monte Carlo functional yield is 96.9% to 97.8%. The VGND-float write assist that maximizes the write-trip voltage also weakens the hold-mode pull-down strength, so the cell has the lowest static voltage noise margin of the compared topologies. All results are obtained from schematic-level (pre-layout) simulation. Within these limits, the cell is a suitable candidate for last-level cache and embedded memory in area- and power-constrained mobile system-on-chip applications.
items.venue: Journal of Computers Mechanical and Management

items.title: R-E-M: Reset-Retain-Make - A Method to Skip Redundant Writes in Non-Volatile Memory
items.abstract: Memristor / RRAM is non-volatile memory that remembers data without power. Normal systems waste energy by rewriting same data. This paper proposes R-E-M: Reset-Retain-Make. If stored==wanted, E=RETAIN skips write with zero energy. Demonstrated with Arduino + 3 LEDs.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Organic Thin Film Transistors (OTFTs) Compact Model in Verilog-A (Gen1 Low-k and Gen2 High-k): Physics-Based Models for SPICE Simulation, Devices Fabricated at CEA-LITEN, Grenoble
items.abstract: Two Verilog-A compact models for Organic Thin-Film Transistors (OTFTs) for SPICE-compatible circuit simulation: one for low-k dielectric devices (Gen1) and one for high-k dielectric devices (Gen2), both at L = 20 µm, W = 1000 µm. Both models share a common physics-based core (Poisson equation with exponential DOS and variable-range hopping transport). Version 2.0 fixes transient convergence issues, adds clamping voltages for numerical stability, and (for Gen2) updates the series resistance and subthreshold slope equations. The README provides full equations, parameters, device/fabrication details, measurement conditions, and measurement data. See README for references and contact information for Gen2 raw data.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Neutron Conversion Layers for Semiconductor Neutron Detectors: A Review of Materials, Thin-Film Deposition Technologies, and Performance Optimization
items.abstract: Semiconductor neutron detectors are compact, low-voltage alternatives to 3He-based detectors, and their detection performance hinges on the conversion layer that transforms neutrons into charged particles. Previous reviews have treated this layer as an auxiliary component rather than as a thin-film engineering problem. Here, four representative conversion materials (6LiF, 10B4C, BN, and Gd) are evaluated against five deposition technologies (magnetron sputtering, vacuum evaporation, solution-based deposition, chemical vapor deposition, and atomic layer deposition) within a four-dimensional framework of areal density, density/uniformity, conformality, and adhesion/interface quality. The comparison shows that performance differences among deposition technologies trace to their deposition mechanisms: PVD processes enable large-area planar films but lack three-dimensional conformality; CVD and ALD coat conformally, but the isotope areal densities they deliver are rarely reported and therefore remain unquantified; solution-based methods scale cheaply but lose efficiency to binder dilution and porosity. Three-dimensional microstructured architectures relax the planar self-absorption constraint, with intrinsic efficiencies well above the ~4–5% ceiling of the single-sided single-layer planar configuration, although device-level validation of conformal deposition rests on only a few reports, principally LPCVD 10B trench filling, with reported intrinsic efficiencies of 16.3 ± 1.6% and 26.1 ± 0.3%, and interfacial dead layers and radiation damage remain key reliability concerns. Magnetron-sputtered 10B4C is currently the most mature option; further progress requires cross-process thin-film benchmarking, device-level testing of conformal coating on 3D microstructures, and semiconductor-grade material quality in emerging functional-integration candidates such as h-BN.

items.title: Mitigating the effect of traps in p-GaN HEMTs through field plate and doping optimization
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents a complete analysis of normally-off p-GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) with field plate using TCAD simulations in conjunction with physics-based analytical model. The study focuses on maximizing the breakdown voltage ( $$V_{BR}$$ ) through the integrated optimization of field plate (FP) length and Magnesium (Mg) doping concentration in the p-GaN cap layer under the influence of thermally assisted traps. The analyses were performed taking the reported experimental values of Mg and TAT (Trap Assisted Tunneling) concentrations. Implementation of the field plates successfully suppresses the crowding of electric field and enhance the channel breakdown voltage. The numerical length of the field plate is optimized for the highest breakdown voltage which was achieved at 978V when the field plate length (LFP) was 1.5 $$\mu $$ m in combination with high Mg doping.TCAD results also reveal that, Mg concentration significantly modulates the device’s threshold voltage ( $$V_{TH}$$ ), power density and leakage current. Explicitly, increasing the parametric value of Mg active concentration to $$1\times 10^{18}$$ $$cm^{-3}$$ increases the DC peak output current from 12 mA/mm to a saturation value of 67 mA/mm for V $$_{GS}$$ = 10V, while shifting the threshold voltage $$V_{TH}$$ from 4.91V to 1.6V. Furthermore, the TCAD results are compared with a physics-based analytical models specially developed for p-GaN HEMTs. These comparisons demonstrate strong agreement between the TCAD and the theoretical results in terms of DC characteristics for the proposed device. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the combined optimization of field-plate length and Mg doping under trap-assisted tunneling conditions has not been previously investigated in detail. With the analytical cross-validation against experimentally-calibrated TCAD simulation, this approach also offers various performance parameter configurations, helping designers select the ideal combination for reliable high-power applications.

items.title: Mechanical Control of Polar State in Antiferroelectric Order
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Antiferroelectric thin films can stabilize electrically written metastable polar states, but deterministic reset of these states after electrical writing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that localized mechanical force can deterministically erase an electrically written metastable polar state in epitaxial PbHfO 3 thin films, driving the system back toward the antipolar antiferroelectric ground state. Electrical bias stabilizes a persistent metastable polar state, whereas once the polar state is established, tip‐applied mechanical force progressively suppresses both piezoresponse and surface‐potential contrast, consistent with force‐assisted relaxation of the polar state toward the antiferroelectric state. Time‐dependent measurements further reveal that the written ferroelectric state is intrinsically metastable and relaxes only slowly without external perturbation. Together, these results demonstrate a deterministic electromechanical write–erase paradigm, in which electric fields encode, and mechanical forces erase ferroic order. This work introduces a new modality for controlling competing ferroic phases and provides a foundation for mechanically reconfigurable nanoelectronic and logic devices based on antiferroelectrics.

items.title: Interfacial Layer Engineering for Memory and Reliability Enhancement in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 FeFETs
items.abstract: The interfacial layer (IL) in the gate stack of Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) strongly affects device performance and reliability. In this work, high-κ IL engineering is investigated using calibrated TCAD simulations and experimental verification to study the role of dielectric constant, physical thickness, and interface traps on the performance enhancement of HZO FeFETs. Typical higher-κ materials, namely, Si3N4, Al2O3, and HfO2, are chosen as ILs. At a fixed physical IL thickness of 2 nm, increasing κ reduces the voltage drop across the IL and redistributes a larger fraction of the applied voltage to the HZO layer, thereby promoting more complete polarization switching. The simulated memory window (MW) consequently increases from 0.77 V for SiO2 to 2.20 V for HfO2. In contrast, at a fixed EOT of 1 nm, the memory performance of the FeFETs remains nearly unchanged among different IL materials, while higher-κ ILs substantially reduce the electric-field stress across the IL, suggesting a potential benefit for gate-stack reliability. Experimental measurements of the no-IL, SiO2-IL, and HfO2-IL devices are further used for model calibration and interface-trap analysis. By incorporating IL-associated interface traps into the calibrated model, the experimentally observed MW differences are discussed in terms of both interface-related effects and IL dielectric properties. These results clarify the condition-dependent benefits of high-κ IL engineering and provide design guidance for improving the memory performance and electric-field management of scaled HZO FeFETs.

items.title: First-Principles Field Theory of Pre-Breakdown Fluctuation Phenomena and Filamentary Percolation in Transition Metal Oxide Memristors (HfOx, TaOx): Topological Scaling, Collective De-Pinning Metrology, and Endurance Control
items.abstract: In non-volatile resistive switching memory (RRAM) and neuromorphic memristive architectures, electrical conduction transitions between High-Resistance States and Low-Resistance States via the field-driven migration of oxygen vacancies that form a nanoscale conductive filament. However, stochastic variability during filament formation and destructive dielectric breakdown severely limit device endurance and multi-bit precision. Traditional models rely on empirical percolation descriptions devoid of an explicit microscopic Hamiltonian. Here, we present a first-principles field theory of pre-breakdown fluctuation phenomena by formulating continuum path optimization and fractal percolation topology across the inter-site electrostatic potential manifold. Convolving the Gaussian Density of States with non-equilibrium quasi-Fermi level gradients reveals that active transport volumes scale fractally under filamentary conditions (with topological volumetric exponent mu_topo approximately equal to 0.414). Furthermore, we prove that the Differential Noise Spectroscopy response resonance peak serves as an exact, non-destructive operando precursor for filament formation, enabling pre-breakdown halting algorithms that extend memristor endurance by over three orders of magnitude. Key Contributions: Derivation of continuum path optimization and active thermodynamic feedback in transition metal oxide memristors (HfOx, TaOx). First-principles unification of microscopic inter-site hopping barrier fluctuations with macroscopic current noise spectral density and the Hooge parameter. Demonstration of fractal volumetric scaling in pre-breakdown insulating oxide gaps. Introduction of Differential Noise Spectroscopy as a non-destructive operando metrology tool to detect critical pre-SET resonance thresholds and prevent permanent dielectric breakdown. Provision of an end-to-end modular MATLAB simulation testbench and validation pipeline for semiconductor characterization environments.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Effects of Deposition Temperature on the Microstructure and Electrical Properties of 50 nm High-k BaTiO3 MIM Capacitors Fabricated by Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of BaTiO3 (BTO) is of interest for next-generation microelectronic devices, including RAM and NAND memory. Herein, we investigate the influence of deposition temperature on the microstructure and electronic properties of 50 nm BTO thin films fabricated by ALD at 200, 220, 240, and 280 °C using bis-(1,2,4 triisopropylcyclopentadienyl)-Ba [Ba(iPr3Cp2)], titanium isopropoxide, and water as precursors, and highlight the significance of void formation in films based on this chemistry. Self-limiting ALD behavior is observed, such that the deposition rate and Ba:Ti ratio are independent of prolonged Ba dose times. XRD shows that films deposited at 220 and 240 °C are significantly more crystalline than films deposited at 280 °C after annealing. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a difference in film microstructure depending on deposition temperature, indicative of different “structural zones”. Cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy reveals that annealed, crystallized BTO films are susceptible to void formation, especially when lower ALD deposition temperatures are used. This void formation appears to result from a combination of the microstructure of the as-deposited film and the easily hydrated barium constituent and is identified as an important structural defect that will need to be avoided to achieve desired dielectric performance. Electrical properties, such as capacitance–voltage (CV), dielectric loss, and DC current–voltage (IV), are closely correlated with microstructure. Fifty-nanometer BTO thin films deposited at 220, 240, and 280 °C have relative permittivity values (εr) of 73, 60, and 33, respectively, at 10 kHz after annealing. Dielectric loss (tanδ) is as low as 0.001. A modest dispersion in capacitance is observed across varying sampling frequencies. Future research to further understand and mitigate void formation while retaining proper stoichiometry for this ALD chemistry is recommended to further improve dielectric performance.

items.title: Effect of Operating Conditions on Switching Variations in Ag/Ti/SiOx/Au RRAM Devices
items.abstract: In this work, Ag/Ti/SiOx/Au RRAM devices were fabricated, and their electrical characteristics were investigated under different operating conditions to understand the stochastic nature. For increasing compliance (250 µA – 1 mA), the devices exhibit coexistence of volatile and non-volatile behaviour from cycle-to-cycle that broadens the overall switching voltages variability. This trend results from stochasticity in filament formation and rupture from volatile and non-volatile switching. Furthermore, the variability enhances through increasing the reset voltage. The increased electric field and Joule heating at a higher reset voltage (– 1.5 V) cause larger filament rupture during the reset operation that varies from cycle-to-cycle than at lower reset voltage biases, thereby increasing variability. The combination of ± 1.5 V sweep bias at 5 mA compliance appears to be the optimal operating parameters for our devices to achieve higher switching-voltage variability. The variability of these devices under different operating electrical parameters can be utilized as a source of entropy for security applications.
items.venue: Transactions on Electrical and Electronic Materials

items.title: EL-RAKHAWI PROTOCOL FOR ALGORITHMIC MORPHABLE SILICON: PROCESSORS THAT AUTONOMOUSLY RECONFIGURE THEIR LOGICAL AND PHYSICAL ARCHITECTURE IN REAL-TIME USING META-AI AND PHASE-CHANGE MATERIALS
items.abstract: "Algorithmic Morphable Silicon" introduces a revolutionary paradigm where hardware physically and logically adapts to software in real-time, erasing the static architecture bottleneck. By integrating nanoscale Phase-Change Materials (PCM) like Ge2Sb2Te5 into 3D silicon BEOL layers, the system creates millions of dynamic "logical bridges" reconfigurable in nanoseconds. Core innovation: Neuro-Topological Evolution Algorithm (NTEA) translates AI computational graphs into optimal physical topologies, governed by on-chip Meta-AI that learns workload patterns and pre-configures hardware, creating "silicon instincts" for instant adaptation. Mathematical framework: Morphological Efficiency Index (MEI), strictly bounded 0.0-1.0 via bounded logistic formulation, quantifies performance gains versus reconfiguration costs and entropy penalties. Hierarchical wear-leveling addresses PCM endurance limits (10^9-10^12 cycles) by throttling bulk reconfigurations to millisecond intervals. Engineering breakthrough: single AMS processor achieves 90% reduction in data movement energy, 10-100x task-specific throughput improvement, microsecond reconfiguration latency. Applications span edge AI, cryptographic acceleration, scientific computing, and eliminating planned obsolescence. Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23831711."
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Dual‐Input Two‐Dimensional Floating‐Gate Memory With Intrinsic Stochasticity for Secure Information Processing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT 2D materials have enabled diverse electronic and optoelectronic devices, yet intrinsic stochastic behaviors are commonly regarded as detrimental to device reliability and controllability. Here, we demonstrate a dual‐input 2D floating‐gate memory that deliberately harnesses intrinsic stochastic optoelectronic responses as a functional degree of freedom for secure information processing. By integrating electrical gating and optical excitation within a Bi 2 O 2 S/h‐BN/graphene heterostructure, the floating‐gate device simultaneously achieves non‐volatility, multilevel programmability, and reconfigurable device‐intrinsic stochastic conductance responses. The memory exhibits a high on/off current ratio (>10 6 ), a wide memory window (83.4%), long retention (10 4 s), and robust endurance (>2000 cycles), enabling stable hardware‐level extraction of physical features. As a representative application, the stochastic optoelectronic features are combined with standard cryptographic primitives to realize reversible text and image encryption with pronounced diffusion and avalanche characteristics, while session‐level freshness is naturally supported to mitigate replay attacks and key reuse. Beyond cryptography, this work establishes a materials‐enabled strategy for transforming intrinsic stochasticity in 2D floating‐gate devices from an undesired effect into a useful functionality, opening new opportunities for multifunctional memory and secure information processing architectures.

items.title: Baseline Uncertainty Limits Mechanistic Interpretation of Power-Law Degradation Exponents in GAA Transistors
items.abstract: Power-law exponents are widely used to describe time-dependent transistor degradation and to extrapolate accelerated measurements toward operating conditions. Their physical interpretation, however, depends on the baseline from which degradation is measured. This study examines baseline sensitivity using published gate-all-around (GAA) transistor degradation data and a zero-curvature baseline reconstruction rule. In a primary dataset of 24 degradation curves, each curve yields one admissible zero-curvature root, shifting the median nominal exponent n = 0.550 to a reconstructed value 1/m = 0.346. Within an established phenomenological framework, this shift changes the inferred correlation parameter from χ = −0.820 to χ = −1.899. The apparent decrease in the local exponent with accumulated degradation appears in 19 of the 24 nominal curves but remains in only 5 curves after baseline reconstruction and is not robust under cross-fitted analysis. Across 26 eligible external nanowire curves (≥5 time points, out of 32 total curves), 19 curves yield a single admissible zero-curvature root. These roots remain numerically stable under single-point deletion (median relative change in m of 2.97% across 15 eligible curves) without systematically improving the secondary log–log fit. Numerical root stability therefore does not establish physical baseline validity. Consequently, the empirical exponent remains a useful kinetic descriptor, but it does not by itself distinguish between HCI- and BTI-like behavior or establish a transition between them.

items.title: A statistical framework for laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Abstract Laser slicing of 4H-SiC enables low-kerf wafer separation, but reproducible subsurface crack formation remains challenging because the modified layer is buried, defect-sensitive, and statistically variable. Here, nanosecond laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in commercial n-type 4H-SiC are described probabilistically rather than through deterministic thresholds. Incident fluence, pulse-to-pulse pitch, and focal depth below the surface were varied systematically, and image-derived outcomes were classified as modification onset, crack onset, or stable crack formation. Weibull analysis was used to describe the probability of each outcome, while binomial confidence intervals and bootstrap resampling were used to quantify uncertainty. Modification formed within a comparatively narrow fluence band across all tested depths and pitches. Pulse pitch emerged as the primary parameter governing the transition from modification to cracking. At smaller pitch, stable cracking became probable within the same fluence interval as modification, whereas at larger pitch a statistically separable fluence range produced modification without subsequent cracking. Cross-sectional SEM supported the corresponding morphological progression from void-like or elliptical modifications to wedge-like, crack-forming inclusions. This combined statistical and morphological analysis captures both systematic parameter trends and excursions among nominally identical conditions, providing a basis for selecting more reproducible crack-forming process windows for 4H-SiC wafer slicing.

items.title: A Near Threshold SRAM Compute-in-Memory Transformer Accelerator with Adaptive Precision Scaling for Sub mW Edge AI Applications
items.abstract: The increasing trend towards the adoption of transformers in edge devices stipulates the need for ultralow power devices that also require high energy efficiency with power budget constraints. This article proposes a near-threshold SRAM compute-in-memory transformer accelerator with adaptive precision scaling for sub-mW edge AI applications. The architecture performs MAC operations directly inside a modified 6T SRAM cell, minimizing data movement between compute and memory. Operating at 0.45 V reduces total power consumption by 58% compared with conventional digital MAC accelerators running at 0.9 V. An adaptive precision precision mechanism has been implemented to switch between the INT4 and INT8 precision dynamically based on the sensitivity of the layer, resulting in an additional 27% savings with less than 1.2% degradation on TinyML transformer benchmarks. The proposed accelerator is implemented in 28 nm CMOS. All reported results (power, energy efficiency, MAC linearity, and noise margins) are obtained from post-layout simulations using TSMC 28 nm LP foundry models and SPEF-extracted parasitics; they are not silicon measurements. The design shows an energy efficiency of 12.4 TOPS/W with a total power of 0.82 mW at 50 MHz.
items.venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

items.title: A Layered Strategy for Placement and Routing in Large-Scale Field-Coupled Nanocomputing Circuits
items.abstract: Field-Coupled Nanocomputing (FCN) devices are emerging nanotechnologies for next-generation logic computing, driven by the physical limitations of CMOS technology. As the scale of circuit design increases, automatic placement and routing (P&R) become crucial for optimizing device performance and ensuring scalable fabrication. Previous algorithms face challenges in solving large-scale placement and routing problems with the current clocking scheme. In this article, a novel approach is proposed to decouple the placement and routing issues in the design of FCN logic circuits. By adopting a layered method, the issues are confined within each layer, and long wires between layers are eliminated while reducing crossovers through node sorting. A* algorithm is employed to solve the routing between logic gates, and an innovative clock allocation mechanism ensures clock synchronization. A standard cell library is used to implement the mapping of an FCN circuit from a gate-level layout to a nanocell-level layout. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared with state-of-the-art approaches such as fiction, Ropper, and genetic algorithms (GA). Specifically, it achieves higher success rates, fewer gates and faster execution times, along with lower delays–while also delivering reduced area overhead, particularly when compared with Ropper and GA. Furthermore, this article achieves automatic placement and routing of FCN circuits with over 1000 nodes, making it more suitable for large-scale FCN circuit design.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems

items.title: (CeO2)1/(HfO2)2 ferroelectric superlattice with low polarization switching energy barrier
items.abstract: HfO 2 ferroelectric materials have received widespread attention due to their compatibility with complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) processes. However, the orthorhombic phase of HfO 2 is thermodynamically metastable, and its high polarization switching energy barrier results in a high coercive field, which severely limits the practical application of HfO 2 as a functional ferroelectric material. Therefore, developing HfO 2 -based ferroelectric materials with excellent ferroelectric phase stability and low polarization switching barriers is crucial for their applications in ferroelectric devices. In this work, the (CeO[Formula: see text]/(HfO[Formula: see text] superlattices were designed, and their ferroelectric phase stabilities and polarization switching properties were studied using density functional theory-based first-principles calculations. The (CeO[Formula: see text]/(HfO[Formula: see text] superlattice is found to exhibit good ferroelectric phase stability with out-of-plane oriented polarization. Its polarization switching energy barrier is reduced to 0.083 eV/u.c., which leads to a more than 40% lower switching electric field, as compared with that of pure HfO 2 . The underlying reason for the energy barrier reduction is the tensile strain induced by the superlattice. Our results indicate that the superlattice strategy with (CeO[Formula: see text]/(HfO[Formula: see text] structure is an effective approach for achieving low-power ferroelectric devices.

items.title: Wafer topography effects on high-NA lithography with metal oxide resists: impact and rectification
items.abstract: High-numerical-aperture (high-NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography enables continued scaling by directly printing increasingly dense 1-D and 2-D features. However, the reduction in depth of focus (DOF) increases sensitivity to wafer surface topography, where local height variations can introduce defocus and degrade imaging performance. Although scanner leveling systems can detect and compensate for certain classes of topographical variations, residual focus errors may remain depending on the size, orientation, and magnitude of the topographic feature. In this study, line/space patterns with pitches ranging from 21 nm to 24 nm were printed using high-NA EUV lithography on substrates containing intentionally engineered topography. The impact of topography on critical dimension (CD), line-edge roughness (LER), and line-width roughness (LWR) was systematically evaluated across multiple illumination conditions, pitch values, and topographic heights. The results quantify the dependence of patterning performance on both wafer topography and scanner correction capability, while identifying conditions under which leveling compensation is effective. To mitigate the impact of topography-induced focus variation, illumination source optimization and rigorous lithography simulations were performed. In addition, the influence of mask absorber materials and multilayer properties, including tantalum boride (TaB)-based mask stacks, were evaluated as potential approaches to improve the manufacturable depth of focus. The combined experimental and simulation results provide insight into process, mask, and illumination strategies required for robust high-NA EUV patterning in the presence of local wafer topography.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: Visible Light Accelerates Ultralow Electric Field‐Induced Switching of Antipolar‐to‐Polar Orders in Photoactive Ferroelectric
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) have emerged as intriguing electroactive materials due to their unique merits arising from electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar phases. For molecular AFEs, however, a high electric field strength is required to switch antipolar dipoles in adjacent sublattices because of complex intermolecular interactions. Herein, we propose visible‐light irradiation as a feasible strategy to accelerate electric field‐induced switching of antipolar‐to‐polar states in a photoactive AFE perovskite, (benzylammonium) 2 (ethylammonium)BiI 6 , with an ultralow coercive field. It is a multiaxial ferroelectric with large spontaneous polarization of 3.5 µC cm −2 . The cooperation of organic cation dynamics and inorganic octahedral distortion induces stepwise symmetry breaking in (benzylammonium) 2 (ethylammonium)BiI 6 , described by the point‐group sequence m ‐2/ m ‐3 m ‐ m . Strikingly, visible light accelerates its electric field‐induced AFE‐to‐ferroelectric switching; it shows near‐room‐temperature AFE behavior in the dark even under a high electric field, whereas visible‐light irradiation enables field‐induced ferroelectricity at an ultralow coercive field ( E c = 0.8 kV cm −1 , merely 1/39 of that in the dark). Nanoscale piezoresponse force microscopy studies further confirm this light‐accelerated polarization modulation, resembling an optical writing/reading memory process. This work provides a new pathway to modulate ferroic orders toward electronic device applications.

items.title: Time-Domain Jitter due to Random Telegraph Noise: An Analysis of the Charge Trapping Impact on the Variability of Oscillators
items.abstract: Abstract Charge trapping and de-trapping phenomena are the core mechanism of Random Telegraph Noise (RTN), causing deviations in drain current amplitude over time due to the constant capture and emission processes of charges from the transistor’s channel. As the timing characteristics of oscillators, such as voltage-controlled oscillators and phase-locked loops, depend on the amplitude of the drain current, RTN impacts the stability of periodic signals by inducing variance in the length of the oscillation period (i.e., jitter). In this work, the time-domain jitter (under the concepts of absolute jitter, period jitter, and cycle-to-cycle jitter) induced by RTN in free-running and closed-loop oscillators is estimated. SPICE-level simulations demonstrate that the jitter of CMOS oscillators evolves differently depending on the arrangement of the oscillating structure and its timing behavior. The analysis is validated by straightforward analytical expressions and supported by experimental data from the literature. The relevance of this work lies in presenting a qualitative analysis of the RTN-induced jitter in CMOS oscillators for the characterization and evaluation of circuit design performance and reliability.

items.title: TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator
items.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) accelerators for edge inference must meet tight energy, latency, and area (EDP) constraints, and their optimal hardware architecture and dataflow configuration is typically identified through design space exploration (DSE). However, on-chip memory technology including cell type, bank organization, and process node, is rarely treated as a first-class citizen in DSE. For example, increasing memory capacity can reduce memory accesses through greater data reuse, but at the cost of higher area and access energy, thereby limiting the compute units budget. Consequently, memory technology can fundamentally shift the optimal accelerator architecture for a given area and EDP budget. Existing machine learning (ML)-based DSE methods require repeating simulation, data generation, and model training for each new memory technology. We present TADA, a memory technology-aware DNN accelerator performance and energy estimator that predicts system latency and energy for a given workload, hardware configuration, and memory technology. TADA is trained on a synthetic dataset that generalizes across memory technologies. The dataset spans current and future technology trends while enforcing physics-based guardrails to preserve realistic area-energy trade-offs. Each memory technology is represented by a technology signature, a vector of read energy, write energy, and storage capacity across a range of areas, provided as input alongside the workload and hardware configuration. Across 21 unseen technology curves spanning SRAM, STTRAM, ReRAM, PCM, FeFET, eDRAM, and CTT, TADA predicts system energy and latency with 1.5-4.4% and 0.7-1.2% mean absolute percentage error, respectively. In three pairwise case studies, it matches the simulator-selected memory technology at 98.7-100% of area budgets, with a mean EDP loss of at most 0.21%, while achieving over 10^4x higher evaluation throughput.

items.title: Surface chemistry as data for level-set simulation of etching and deposition
items.abstract: Level-set simulators of etching and deposition move the surface with a velocity that depends on adsorbate coverages. These coverages are usually computed from balances solved and coded by hand for each chemistry, whereas voxel-based Monte Carlo profile simulators read the reaction mechanism as data. For the open-source level-set simulator ViennaPS, this work presents a surface model whose rate laws, Jacobian and velocity are derived from a reaction file and evaluated with ray-traced fluxes. Steady-state coverages are obtained with Newton's method and transient coverages with a conservative integrator. One compiled model is applied to eight chemistries for chemical vapour deposition, selective epitaxy, plasma etching, sputtering and atomic layer deposition. It reproduces a hand-written silicon etch model to seven significant digits at a single point and within the Monte Carlo noise in a masked trench. In a high-aspect-ratio cavity, alumina conformality is determined by a trimethylaluminium reaction probability within the measured range.

items.title: Strategic approaches to EUV mask materials and structures for DRAM and logic devices
items.abstract: As semiconductor manufacturing moves toward High-NA (HNA, 0.55 NA) EUV for higher-resolution patterning, EUV mask approaches offering patterning advantages for both DRAM and logic devices are receiving growing attention. To comprehensively consider their device-specific requirements and the coexistence of Low-NA (0.33 NA, LNA) and HNA platforms, we analyzed generation-dependent patterning trends for DRAM and logic through optical simulations. Several phase-shift mask (PSM) candidates were designed, spanning a range from low-n to higher-k absorber concepts, with new candidates introduced to achieve a practical balance among performance, productivity, and manufacturability. We evaluated their relative imaging performance to assess their utility and applicability across devices, generations, and use cases. The results indicated that the low-n PSM with high reflectivity remained broadly attractive under LNA conditions, while the other options could provide complementary advantages depending on the pattern type and requirements. The PSM candidates exhibited different characteristics under HNA conditions, reflecting trade-offs between imaging performance and implementation considerations. The feasibility of EUV AIMS as a pre-validation method was also demonstrated through its repeatability and reliability in distinguishing mask-blank-dependent optical responses, while the measured results were consistent with calculations incorporating the actual mask geometry. Overall, we propose strategic approaches to mask-blank development through simulation-based analysis and AIMS-based pre-validation to address practical uncertainties. These approaches are expected to improve decision-making efficiency in evaluating and selecting diverse candidates and in defining subsequent development directions.

items.title: Selection of the most appropriate semiconductor on the DC-DC buck converters by multi-criteria decision making methods
items.abstract: Abstract The selection of suitable semiconductor is one of the most important factors affecting the performance of the power electronics circuits. The general characteristics of the circuit such as voltage, current, and switching frequency limit the switch selection. When choosing semiconductors that meet these constraints, the criteria such as switching speed, losses, cost etc. are be taken into consideration. The importance weights of the criteria may vary depending on the expert’s experience and the application conditions. Therefore, to make the best decision, it is necessary to make a choice based on all criteria. In this paper, the most suitable semiconductor selection for a 36–12 V DC-DC buck converter has been made using the multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods, MOORA and integrated AHP-TOPSIS firstly in the literature. GaN-transistor, IGBT and power MOSFET has been evaluated according to the four criteria. The consistency of the results obtained with both MOORA and the integrated AHP-TOPSIS methods demonstrates that these methods are successful in determining the most suitable semiconductor in power electronics applications where there is more than one option.

items.title: Segmentation-Engineered Ge4Sb6Te7 Switch on SOI Platform for Multilevel Nonvolatile Photonic Neural Inference
items.abstract: Abstract Phase-change materials (PCMs) have emerged as key enablers of nonvolatile, ultracompact photonic switches for energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) applications. In this work, we computationally investigate the recently discovered Ge4Sb6Te7 (GST-467) as a high-contrast optical PCM and demonstrate its suitability for multilevel photonic computing. We experimentally measure the complex refractive indices of amorphous and crystalline GST-467 and use them to numerically propose a segmented silicon-on-insulator photonic switch optimized at 1550 nm. Three-dimensional (3D) finite-difference time-domain simulations show that segmentation significantly enhances the extinction ratio while maintaining low insertion loss, yielding a design figure of merit more than 7-fold higher than that of an unsegmented design. Multiphysics thermo-optical simulations further demonstrate efficient, reversible laser-induced switching with sub-nJ energy requirements for crystallization and amorphization. Compared with established GST, GSST, and GSS compositions, GST-467 provides the largest transmittance contrast and supports up to 48 resolvable optical states. When deployed as multilevel weights in photonic DNN architectures, the GST-467 switch achieves superior classification accuracy on EMNIST and Fashion-MNIST benchmarks. These results position GST-467 as a highly promising PCM for scalable, low-energy photonic computing and neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Quantifying acoustic intermodulation distortion from a dual-frequency (3+5 MHz) megasonic cleaning system
items.abstract: Advanced 193i and EUV megasonic photomask cleaning processes operate within a narrow process window, where the margin between particle removal efficiency (PRE) and pattern damage is minimal. Optimizing drive frequency and transducer output pressure is critical. Single-frequency systems sometimes fail to clear high-aspect-ratio (HAR) features without inducing cavitation-related damage. Advanced dual-frequency systems aim to “tune” the acoustic boundary layer by combining lower frequencies that generate cavitation events to remove larger particles and higher frequencies that create a thinner boundary layer to remove smaller particles. This study investigates the nonlinear acoustic interactions unique to dual-frequency excitation from a 3 + 5 MHz SONOSYS nozzle transducer. When both frequencies are driven concurrently, nonlinear effects from Intermodulation Distortion (IMD) generate additional spectral components at combinations of the two frequencies. Using a wide-bandwidth 25 MHz measurement system, a proprietary decomposition algorithm quantified and isolated the IMD-driven pressure components compared with a single-frequency profile. The characterization demonstrates a significant process benefit: the spectral redistribution of acoustic energy into a higher density of stable cavitation modes. Generating intermediate-frequency bands maintains the benefit of thinning the viscous boundary layer for small-particle removal while suppressing the stochastic, high-amplitude transient cavitation events associated with pattern damage. These findings provide a framework for potentially expanding the available process window, offering a scalable path toward meeting the stringent zero-defect requirements of next-generation lithography.

items.title: Plasma etching profile control of next-generation absorbers for high-NA EUV photomasks
items.abstract: As semiconductor device scaling progresses into the sub nanometer regime, next-generation high-NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography places increasingly stringent demands on photomask materials and patterning processes. Precise sidewall profile control during plasma etching is critical for high-NA EUV photomasks, as it directly affects line-edge roughness (LER), defect formation and pattern-transfer fidelity. Emerging low‑n / high‑k absorber films, that are generally composed of binary alloys are particularly difficult to etch due to their chemical inertness and element-dependent chemical reactivity. Conventional plasma etching faces fundamental challenges, including plasma-induced damage and limited control over sidewall profile. This work addressed these challenges by combining process tuning and hardware-enabled plasma control to balance sidewall protection and byproduct removal for achieving smooth absorber sidewalls. Three representative etch regimes can be identified by (i) insufficient sidewall protection leading to plasma damage, (ii) balanced sidewall protection with effective byproduct removal that achieves a smooth sidewall profile, and (iii) excessive and non-uniform byproduct accumulation that roughens the sidewall. The results suggest proper control of plasma chemistry and ion flux distribution during the etching process to sustain a stable balance between sidewall protection and byproduct removal. This approach enables smooth absorber sidewalls while maintaining selectivity, sidewall angle, critical dimension, and linearity, supporting robust pattern transfer in next‑generation high‑NA EUV photomask manufacturing.

items.title: Monotonic machine learning for etch retargeting: demonstration and validation in an advanced-node EUV process
items.abstract: Etch bias retargeting in optical proximity correction (OPC) is critical for advanced-node manufacturing. Production fabs typically rely on calibrated rule tables derived from after-development inspection (ADI) and after-etch inspection (AEI) metrology to guide etch bias retargeting. While incrementally refinable, these tables struggle with the high-dimensional feature interactions and spatial dependencies present in advanced nodes, which limits their predictive accuracy. Semi-empirical physical models such as variable etch bias (VEB) provide greater flexibility but require recalibration in post-tapeout scenarios, and neural-network etch models capture richer feature representations but offer no monotonicity guarantee and impose significant computational and engineering burden for the iterative updates that are routine in production. Monotonic machine learning (MML) reconciles these competing requirements. The MML framework combines the incremental adaptability of etch tables with the accuracy and feature richness of modern machine learning, while remaining lightweight in both computation and engineering effort. Its applicability spans early-stage development and production refinement: a push-button workflow with rapid turnaround enables efficient model development during initial etch characterization, when the process is not yet stable, while the monotonicity property permits continuous refinement in post-tapeout contexts where OPC models are already qualified for manufacturing. In this work we demonstrate MML for etch-bias prediction in an advanced-node EUV layer. Candidate features are derived from geometric and density-based measurements, and a feature-selection algorithm identifies the most predictive subset for training. We evaluate the framework in both gauge-based and contour-based metrology modalities, holding the training and test partition consistent across all methods to ensure a fair comparison. Within the gauge-based modality we compare MML against a conventional rule table, and within the contour-based modality against a semi-empirical VEB model. On an independent test set of 88 held-out gauges the MML model achieves an RMSE of 0.28 nm versus 0.44 nm for the rule table, a 36% improvement in predictive accuracy, and on the contour dataset it matches a fully recalibrated VEB model without any physical re-parameterization.

items.title: Low‐Frequency Noise Evolution in Thin SiN x ReRAMs After Sequential Constant Voltage Stress
items.abstract: In this work, thin SiN x films in MIS ReRAM cells are stressed with a constant voltage for various sequential durations (25, 45, 65, 110 and 250 s) and the low‐frequency noise signal generated after each stress duration is measured using different sampling rates. This enables the capture of both fast and slow trapping phenomena and the monitoring of defect creation evolution. Random telegraph noise (RTN) signals illustrate the gradual formation of various defects in the material, which deteriorates and ultimately results in catastrophic failure. This progressively causes the slope of the power spectral density (PSD) plot to transition from 1/ f 2 to 1/ f behavior. The analysis of these signals can reveal the properties of these defects.

items.title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement‐mode transistors with sub‐3 nm channels, featuring near‐zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate‐stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high‐performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next‐generation nanoelectronics.

items.title: Impact of curvilinear designs on mask inspection
items.abstract: For High-NA EUV lithography, depth of focus (DoF) has become a key challenge, driving the adoption of freeform sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) to improve process robustness and reduce process variation (PV) band distribution. However, the increased geometric complexity of freeform SRAF designs raises concerns regarding mask manufacturing, including increased OPC and MDP runtime, larger file sizes, mask patterning complexity, and potential impacts on mask inspection performance. In this study, the impact of SRAF complexity on mask inspection performance was evaluated using representative High-NA EUV hole-pattern layouts containing No SRAF, Constant Width SRAF (CW SRAF), Variable Width SRAF (VW SRAF), and Variable Continuous Tone Mask SRAF (VCTM SRAF) configurations. Lithography simulations were used to identify defect sizes corresponding to approximately 10% wafer CD variation, which were defined as wafer-relevant defects and used as inspection targets. Inspection results demonstrated that all wafer-relevant defects were successfully detected for every evaluated SRAF style, including the most complex VCTM SRAF layouts, under optimized inspection conditions. While the detection limits varied depending on defect type, certain defect type exhibited a measurable dependence on SRAF complexity. Analysis of inspection images showed that surrounding SRAF structures modify local inspection-image contrast and influence defect signal magnitude. Although SRAF complexity was found to affect defect detectability, all wafer-relevant defects remained detectable under the evaluated inspection conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of DUV inspection for High-NA EUV curvilinear logic hole-pattern masks and indicate that, for the layouts investigated in this study, the impact of SRAF complexity was not large enough to prevent reliable detection of wafer-relevant defects.

items.title: HippocamPEX: A Hippocampus-Inspired In-Silico Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
items.abstract: The brain's hippocampus enables episodic memory - the ability to encode events within their context, organize them into sequences, and generate predictive representations to guide adaptive behavior. Modern computing architectures, however, are optimized for large-scale arithmetic and struggle with such context-dependent sequential prediction or "cognitive" tasks. To translate these capabilities into a mixed-signal architecture, we first derived a working model from the neuroscience literature distilling key hippocampal computations into engineering-friendly abstractions. We then leveraged converging advances in in-memory computing, neuromorphic computing, asynchronous circuits, and analog computing to design a mixed-signal hardware architecture implementing these computations, called HippocamPEX. Finally, we demonstrated that HippocamPEX reproduces characteristic representational dynamics of hippocampal subregions and performs robust context-specific sequence prediction through detailed activity and circuit simulations. By tightly coupling hardware design with neuroscience knowledge, this work establishes a pathway for artificial systems capable of rapid, adaptive, and context-aware decision-making, addressing a central gap between biological and conventional computing.
