items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. TiN gates deliver drain-current density up to 450 mA/mm at $V_{\mathrm{th}} = -13$ V, whereas Pt gates shift $V_{\mathrm{th}}$ to -2.5 V with a reduced current drive of 220 mA/mm, reflecting the effects of gate work function. TiN-gated devices exhibit lower current degradation under pulsed operation and a higher critical breakdown field ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 3.5$ MV/cm) than Pt-gated devices ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 2.98$ MV/cm), measured without field plating at $L_{\mathrm{GD}} = 2.3$ $μ$m. Collectively, these results establish a low-thermal-budget, fully Au-free, CMOS-compatible metallization platform for high-performance Al-rich AlGaN UWBG power electronics.

items.title: Comparative analysis of gate-dielectric effects on the analog and linearity performance of MoS2-, MoSe2-, and WS2-based FETs
items.abstract: Abstract This work investigates the influence of gate dielectric engineering on the analog, RF, and linearity performance of transition metal dichalcogenide field-effect transistors (TMD-FETs). A self-consistent non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF)-based simulation framework is employed to analyze MoS 2 -, MoSe 2 -, and WS₂-based FETs integrated with different high-k gate dielectrics. The impact of dielectric materials on electrostatic integrity, carrier transport, transistor efficiency ( g m / I D ), quality factor (Q-factor), and RF linearity metrics is systematically examined. Key device parameters including ON current ( I ON ), OFF current ( I OFF ), current ON/OFF ratio ( I ON / I OFF ), subthreshold swing (SS), transconductance ( g m ), second-order transconductance ( g m2 ), and third-order transconductance ( g m3 ) are evaluated. The results demonstrate that high-k dielectrics significantly enhance gate electrostatic control, resulting in improved ON-state current, reduced SS, enhanced g m / I D efficiency, and superior Q-factor characteristics. Furthermore, the use of high-k dielectrics shifts the peaks of g m2 and g m3 toward lower gate voltages, indicating improved low-voltage RF linearity behavior. Among the investigated materials, WS₂-based FETs exhibit superior transconductance and RF performance characteristics, while MoS 2 -based devices provide an excellent trade-off between power efficiency, nonlinear distortion behavior, and analog/RF characteristics. The findings offer essential insights for optimizing dielectric–channel combinations in next-generation low-power, high-linearity, and RF-oriented nanoelectronic devices.

items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Caerus: Prefetching by Thinking Globally and Acting Locally
items.abstract: Modern processors rely heavily on data prefetching to bridge the growing performance gap between computation and memory accesses. In offset prefetching, prefetches are issued at an address delta relative to the most recently observed access, selecting deltas that have exhibited high coverage in the recent access-stream history. The Best-Offset Prefetcher (BOP) exemplifies this approach by selecting a single uniformly-issued global offset that delivers timely prefetches. However, its lack of context-sensitive accuracy tracking results in significantly increased DRAM traffic and sometimes disappointing performance. Conversely, Berti, the state-of-the-art offset prefetcher, achieves impressive prefetching performance and accuracy. However, its Program-Counter (PC)-local approach to extracting offsets limits its ability to capture global memory patterns, meaning there are many scenarios where simpler global offset prefetchers, such as BOP, outperform it. Observing the limitations of contemporary offset prefetchers, we present Caerus: an offset prefetcher that employs PC-local filtering on multiple non-overlapping globally derived offsets. Caerus extracts multiple offsets from the global memory trace and maximizes their combined coverage by training each offset only on accesses not already covered by previously learned offsets. The accuracy of each extracted offset is tracked per-PC based on whether it can cover future accesses for any PC. This allows Caerus to address complex delta patterns while maintaining high accuracy. In SPECspeed 2017, Caerus gains a geomean speedup of 8.3%, outperforming Berti by 2.0% while achieving low hardware and DRAM-traffic overhead.

items.title: CFET RMG Dual Work Function Metal Patterning with Sacrificial Layer for Nanosheets Pinch-Off
items.abstract: We reported the process flow and challenges of dual work function metal patterning between different work function metal thicknesses and gate lengths to monolithic Complementary FET. To resolve the dilemma of spin-on-carbon hard mask fill and nanosheet pinch-off, we propose integrating sacrificial gap-closure layers and isotropic etches to dual work function metal patterning. We prove that the sacrificial layers can be removed with high selectivity to work function metal in wet etch chemistry. We report the controllable wet etch rate of the sacrificial layers by concentrations and temperatures. Finally, we first demonstrate dual work function metal patterning with a sacrificial layer and isotropic etch step by step on a monolithic Complementary FET test vehicle.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Assessment of Stripping Efficiency of Non-TMAH Based Solvents on Photoresist and Temporary Bonding Materials
items.abstract: Effective removal of photoresist (PR) and Temporary Bonding Materials (TBM) is critical in advanced packaging and three-dimensional integration (3Di) processes within semiconductor manufacturing. Traditional wet stripping methods, primarily based on tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH), offer high performance but pose significant environmental and health risks. To address these concerns, this study explores the use of water-based, environmentally benign stripping formulations developed by Intelligent Fluids as sustainable alternatives. These microemulsion-based "green solvents" are engineered to provide efficient cleaning, enhanced surface wettability, and compatibility with sensitive substrates. A series of laboratory-scale stripping tests were conducted on silicon coupons coated with various PR and TBM layers, comparing the performance of four Intelligent Fluids formulations against a conventional TMAH-based solvent. Post-strip surface characterization was performed using contact angle measurements, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Time of Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) to evaluate cleanliness and chemical modifications. Solvent durability was also assessed by monitoring performance over successive stripping cycles. The results demonstrate that the Intelligent Fluids formulations achieve comparable or superior cleaning efficiency while being non-toxic and reducing the energy consumption by decreasing the operating temperature during the process, making them promising candidates for next-generation semiconductor cleaning solutions. Keywords: Photoresist (PR), Temporary Bonding Material (TBM), green solvents, Microemulsion, TMAH alternatives, Advanced packaging, 3D integration, Sustainable semiconductor processes, Wet stripping
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Analysis of Si/SiGe Intermixing Layer Thickness by Inductively Coupled Plasma – Mass Spectrometry
items.abstract: A new method for characterizing the intermixing layer between epitaxially deposited Si and SiGe based on the atomic scale wet etch combined with Inductively Coupled Plasma – Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). The thermally induced Ge and Si interdiffusion is considered as one of the root causes for the poor process control and undesired cavity profile after etch, which, in turn, may significantly impact the device performance. The developed ICP-MS method allows us to analyze the thickness of the Si/SiGe intermixing layer and the Ge concentration profile, which can help to improve the upstream processes.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: APPlace: Co-Optimizing Device Locations and Access Points for Routing-Aware Analog Placement
items.abstract: Analog layout automation remains challenging in Analog/Mixed-Signal circuit design, because parasitics and mismatches introduced during layout strongly affect circuit performance. Placement is especially critical among the layout stages, as it constrains the routing solution space and the achievable post-layout performance. Existing analytical placement methods optimize device coordinates under center-based wirelength proxies and leave access point (AP) selection to routing. In analog circuits, however, a routing pin is an extended piece of terminal metal rather than a fixed point, and the best AP on it depends on where the other connected devices are placed, so a coordinate-only placement optimizes for connection points that the router will not use. We present APPlace, a routing-aware analog placement framework that co-optimizes device locations and AP selections during global placement, followed by a legalization stage that preserves the structure established by global placement. Experimental results on four real-world analog benchmarks show that APPlace achieves better overall post-layout performance than representative baselines at comparable layout area. Ablation studies further show that removing AP co-optimization causes up to a 13 dB CMRR loss among the OTA benchmarks and a 23% increase in comparator delay.

items.title: AIMS AutoAnalysis: the highly utilized standard for automated defect review on aerial images
items.abstract: Defect-free photomasks are critical for achieving high yield in semiconductor lithography. AIMS® aerial image technology has been the industry standard for defect verification for several decades. However, manual evaluation of aerial images is time-consuming and dependent on operator expertise. AIMS® AutoAnalysis is a software-based solution designed to automate the evaluation of aerial images and to enable reliable and reproducible defect disposition. The system leverages a recipe-driven approach allowing flexible configuration of analysis strategies, including critical dimension (CD) evaluation, edge placement analysis, and intensity-based metrics. The integration of AIMS® AutoAnalysis into a server-based environment enables parallel processing of measurement and evaluation, significantly reducing mask turnaround time. Results are automatically generated and reported once a measurement is completed, enabling seamless integration into high-volume manufacturing workflows. Results from multiple customer applications demonstrate high accuracy, improved productivity, and successful deployment across EUV and DUV technologies as well as various pattern types. These findings confirm AIMS® AutoAnalysis as a key enabler for reliable and efficient mask repair verification.

items.title: A federated learning-based collaborative demand forecasting framework for multinational oil companies
items.abstract: This study discusses the difficulties of energy effectiveness, device Variability, and privacy of data in distributed demand forecasting systems for the Industrial Internet of Things enabled by 5G(IIoT). Federated Education (FL)-based collaborative framework is proposed, enhanced with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to optimize client selection, task scheduling, and energy consumption in highly dynamic oilfield environments. The framework uses multi-agent DRL to balance energy efficiency and prediction accuracy, so as to realize real-time decision-making and adaptive orchestration of IIoT devices. Gradient compression techniques are used to minimize communication overhead without affecting model performance. Experimental validation on a synthetic oil production dataset shows that the proposed framework reduces energy consumption by 60% while maintaining prediction accuracy, with a tradeoff rate of only 5% compared to traditional FL methods. The framework improves the convergence speed, and the number of training cycles is reduced by more than 50% compared with baseline models such as FedAvg and FedProx. These findings confirm the effectiveness of DRLdriven optimization in meeting the special needs of Internet of Things (IIoT)-based oilfield operations. This study provides a reliable and scalable method to predict collaborative demand in distributed Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. The potential of the framework in improving operational efficiency and data privacy is significantly demonstrated due to the integration of multi-agent DRL and energy-aware orchestration mechanism, allowing intelligent decision-making in complex oilfield environments.
items.venue: The International Conference on Optical Imaging and Deep Learning

items.title: A VLSI-Like Design and Verification Flow for Quantum Circuits: A Case Study in PI Estimation
items.abstract: This paper proposes a VLSI-like design and verification flow for quantum circuit implementation, covering four levels: behavioral modeling, register-transfer level (RTL), gate level, and full-circuit integration with quantum algorithms. Using quantum Monte Carlo methods for pi estimation as a case study, the proposed flow provides a systematic path from initial specifications to large-scale quantum circuit implementation. The paper highlights two key contributions. First, quantum digital design supports a broad range of applications beyond predefined circuit templates. This capability is particularly important for application-specific operations in algorithms such as Shor's, Grover's, and quantum amplitude estimation (QAE), and can significantly advance fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC). Second, classical simulation shows that replacing random sampling with grid sampling can achieve a quadratic improvement in this pi-estimation case without quantum computation. This suggests that the quadratic speedup may arise from the grid sampling strategy rather than from the QAE circuit itself. By adapting conventional VLSI digital design principles, this four-level flow addresses a key bottleneck in quantum circuit design and enables flexible design initiation from multiple entry points, including specifications, RTL, and gate-level descriptions, paving the way for the practical deployment of quantum computing.

items.title: A Single Volatile VO 2 Memristor Enabling Neuromorphic Perception, Learning, and Computing
items.abstract: Neuromorphic computing requires compact hardware devices capable of supporting multiple brain‐inspired functions. Vanadium dioxide (VO 2 ), with its thermally and electrically driven insulator–metal transition (IMT), offers an attractive materials platform for such applications owing to its intrinsic volatility and fast switching dynamics. Here, we demonstrate a vertical Pt/VO 2 /Pt memristor that integrates multiple neuromorphic functions within a single volatile device platform. VO 2 thin films are deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using the TEMAV precursor, yielding semiconducting insulating and metallic phases with a resistivity contrast of approximately two orders of magnitude. Electrical transport analysis indicates that back‐to‐back Schottky barriers at the Pt/VO 2 interfaces play a dominant role in device conduction and enable reproducible volatile threshold switching. Leveraging the interfacial transport and thermally driven switching dynamics, the same device emulates leakyintegrate‐and‐fire neuronal behavior, Pavlovian‐like associative conditioning, reservoir‐computing‐based temporal signal recognition, and artificial nociceptor responses. In particular, the device‐driven reservoir system is applied to electrocardiogram heartbeat classification, demonstrating its capability for processing real physiological temporal signals. These results establish ALD‐grown vertical VO 2 memristors as compact and multifunctional building blocks for neuromorphic and sensory hardware, highlighting a route toward single‐device platforms that couple perception, learning, and temporal information processing.

items.title: A Novel RMG pWFM Molybdenum Patterning for sub-10nm DRAM Periphery FinFET Platform
items.abstract: We report the wet etch rate difference and device impact between pure metal Molybdenum and metal-nitride complex Molybdenum Nitride and Titanium Nitride. We discuss the wet etch results of acidic and alkaline solutions without oxidant to Molybdenum. We report that Molybdenum can be etched by ozonated water with different concentrations. Finally, we demonstrate p-type work function metal Mo patterning with ozonated water on Ring Oscillator device.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
items.abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

items.title: Substrate orientation-induced device variation in HfO2-based 3D FeFETs
items.abstract: HfO2-based three-dimensional (3D) ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) demonstrate great potential for ultra-high density memory applications. However, the device-to-device variation in threshold voltage (Vth) remains a challenge for their practical implementation. In this work, we systematically investigate the device-to-device variation induced by the variation of ferroelectric properties with the substrate orientation and potential mitigation approaches, an aspect that remains unexplored in HfO2-based 3D FeFETs. First, a device model incorporating randomly distributed nanoscale ferroelectric regions with distinct polarization magnitudes is developed. We reveal that the polarization disparities both among ferroelectric regions and between ferroelectric and non-ferroelectric regions have distinct effects on the device-to-device variation, and that these effects depend critically on the proportion of ferroelectric regions. Building on the inevitable presence of non-ferroelectric regions in the devices, we further explore variation mitigation strategies aimed at alleviating microscopic polarization non-uniformity through adjustments in device structures and operating conditions, such as employing a thicker oxide insulator or lowering the operating voltage. These results provide a theoretical foundation for optimizing the reliability of HfO2-based 3D FeFETs.

items.title: Rosemary: Efficient and Adaptable In-Storage Acceleration for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
items.abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data and is promising for privacy-preserving computing. However, FHE deployment remains constrained due to massive computational, memory, and data-movement overheads. Existing acceleration strategies often overlook the storage I/O bottleneck caused by the enormous size of FHE data in large-scale applications, as most prior works focus on small benchmarks that fit in main memory. Our studies show that state-of-the-art FHE systems spend 71\% to 85\% of their execution time moving data between storage and compute units rather than performing useful computation. To address the I/O bottleneck, we present Rosemary, a heterogeneous FHE acceleration system that incorporates a novel in-storage processing (ISP) architecture with compiler-level and algorithmic optimizations. Our key innovations include 1) an adaptable hardware-aware FHE engine inside a NAND flash-based solid-state drive (SSD) for efficient and cost-effective in-storage FHE processing, 2) a Throughput-Data-Aware Program Allocator (TDAP) that partitions FHE workloads into heterogeneous programs, and 3) a Compiler-Level Ciphertext-Aware Optimizer (CLCAO) that exploits ISP-friendly FHE kernels for low-cost ISP execution. Across a diverse set of FHE workloads, including encrypted deep learning inference and cloud database queries, Rosemary achieves geometric-mean speedups of $185.7\times$ over state-of-the-art CPU/GPU implementations and $3.7\times$ over prior FHE accelerators, while improving energy efficiency by up to $3.9\times$ and Energy-Delay-Area-Product (EDAP) by up to $16.5\times$.

items.title: Oxygen-Assisted Direct Synthesis of Two-Dimensional Ferroelectric Bi2SeO5
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectrics are promising for nonvolatile memory, nanoelectronics, and neuromorphic devices. Among them, bismuth selenite (Bi2SeO5) has recently emerged as a high-performance van der Waals (vdW) ferroelectric oxide. However, its current synthesis mainly relies on the post-oxidation of Bi2O2Se, which complicates the fabrication process and limits its integration potential. Here, we report the oxygen-assisted direct synthesis of 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 nanosheets by regulating the oxygen chemical potential and the resulting relative thermodynamic stability of competing Bi–Se–O phases. The presence of O2 increases the oxygen chemical potential, rendering Bi2SeO5 thermodynamically more stable than Bi2O2Se and enabling its direct growth. The as-grown Bi2SeO5 nanosheets exhibit high crystallinity, uniform composition, well-defined chemical states, and robust in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) ferroelectricity, while temperature-dependent second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements reveal that the non-centrosymmetric phase persists up to approximately 690 K. Lateral and vertical devices further demonstrate stable polarization-controlled resistive switching. This work establishes a direct synthesis route to 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 and provides a foundation for ferroelectric memory and nanoelectronic devices.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing: Hardware for the Next Generation of AI
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has entered a period of unprecedented technological development. The expansion of machine learning, deep learning, generative artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, intelligent sensing and edge computing has created new opportunities across almost every area of modern society. At the same time, this rapid development has created a fundamental challenge: increasingly capable AI systems require increasingly sophisticated computing infrastructure. The demand for computational performance, memory capacity, communication bandwidth and electrical energy continues to grow as AI models become larger, more complex and more deeply integrated into physical and digital environments. For several decades, conventional computing architectures have provided the foundation for artificial intelligence. Central processing units, graphics processing units, tensor processing units, field-programmable gate arrays and application-specific integrated circuits have enabled remarkable advances in machine learning and large-scale AI. These technologies remain essential to contemporary computing. However, the increasing scale and complexity of AI have exposed important limitations associated with energy consumption, data movement, memory access, latency and the deployment of intelligent systems in resource-constrained environments. Neuromorphic computing has emerged as one of the most significant alternative approaches to addressing these challenges. Inspired by selected principles of biological neural systems, neuromorphic computing seeks to reconsider how information is represented, communicated, stored and processed. Rather than relying exclusively on conventional instruction-based computation and repeated movement of data between memory and processing units, neuromorphic architectures emphasise event-driven processing, sparse activity, distributed computation, temporal information, local memory, parallelism and adaptive behaviour. The purpose of this book is to provide a comprehensive examination of neuromorphic computing as a potential hardware foundation for the next generation of artificial intelligence. The book approaches the subject from both technological and conceptual perspectives. It examines not only the architecture and operation of neuromorphic systems but also their relationship with artificial intelligence, edge computing, intelligent sensors, energy-efficient computing, emerging hardware technologies, software ecosystems, industrial applications and future technological development. The book begins by establishing the foundations of artificial intelligence and the evolution of AI hardware. It then introduces the emergence of neuromorphic computing and examines the biological principles that have influenced its development. Particular attention is given to artificial neurons, synapses, spiking neural networks, event-driven computation, synaptic plasticity and the relationship between neuromorphic and conventional computing architectures. The subsequent chapters examine the evolution and architecture of neuromorphic hardware. Different implementation approaches, including analogue, digital and hybrid architectures, are considered alongside memory-centric computing, in-memory approaches, distributed architectures and heterogeneous systems. The book also examines important technological foundations, including CMOS-based circuits, emerging memory technologies, memristive devices, phase-change memory, spintronic devices, ferroelectric technologies, photonic computing, advanced packaging and hardware accelerators for spiking neural networks. A dedicated examination of neuromorphic processors and platforms provides an understanding of how theoretical principles have been translated into practical systems. Important platforms and research directions, including Intel Loihi and Loihi 2, IBM TrueNorth, SpiNNaker and SpiNNaker2, BrainScaleS and SynSense systems, illustrate the diversity of approaches being developed within the field. The book also considers the role of neuromorphic computing in artificial intelligence. Spiking neural networks, neuromorphic deep learning, machine learning, continual learning, online adaptation, unsupervised and self-supervised learning, reinforcement learning and hardware-software co-design are examined as important areas for the development of future intelligent systems. Applications form another central component of the book. Neuromorphic computing has potential relevance to computer vision, speech and audio processing, robotics, autonomous vehicles, healthcare, wearable technologies, cybersecurity, smart manufacturing, the Internet of Things and intelligent edge devices. These applications demonstrate that the significance of neuromorphic computing extends beyond processor design and involves the development of complete intelligent systems capable of interacting with dynamic physical environments. Energy efficiency is given particular attention because it represents one of the strongest motivations for neuromorphic research. The increasing computational demands of AI raise questions concerning the sustainability of large-scale computing infrastructure as well as the practical deployment of intelligence in battery-powered and resource-constrained devices. Event-driven computation, sparse processing, local memory and reduced data movement provide potential mechanisms for improving computational efficiency. However, this book also maintains a critical perspective and recognises that neuromorphic efficiency is dependent on workload characteristics, architecture, implementation and application context. The discussion of software and programming models reflects another important dimension of neuromorphic computing. Hardware innovation alone cannot establish a sustainable technological ecosystem. Programming frameworks, simulation environments, compilers, development platforms, hardware-software interfaces and interoperability mechanisms are necessary for researchers and developers to use neuromorphic systems effectively. The book also provides a critical examination of the limitations of neuromorphic computing. Hardware complexity, scalability, manufacturing constraints, software maturity, training difficulties, data representation, benchmarking, reliability, cost and commercialisation remain important barriers. These limitations are essential to understand because neuromorphic computing should not be presented as a universal replacement for conventional AI hardware. Instead, its greatest potential may emerge through complementary use alongside CPUs, GPUs, TPUs, FPGAs, ASICs and other emerging computational technologies. A major focus is placed on the relationship between neuromorphic computing and edge AI. The movement of intelligence from centralised cloud infrastructure toward devices and environments where data are generated creates new requirements for low-power, low-latency and privacy-preserving computation. Neuromorphic hardware, particularly when combined with event-based sensing, may provide an important foundation for intelligent edge systems. The book subsequently looks toward the future. Neuromorphic generative AI, large AI models, photonic computing, quantum computing, brain-computer interfaces, autonomous and adaptive machines, artificial general intelligence, future communication networks and commercialisation are examined as emerging areas that may influence the direction of the field. Technological development cannot be considered independently from its wider consequences. The book therefore includes a dedicated examination of ethical, social and security considerations. Privacy, data protection, system security, autonomous decision-making, accountability, explainability, socioeconomic implications and responsible development are considered important dimensions of future neuromorphic AI. The final chapters establish the research methodology, discuss the major findings emerging from the literature, and present conclusions and recommendations. The methodological framework provides a structured basis for examining the multidisciplinary evidence surrounding neuromorphic computing, while the discussion evaluates its technological advancement, implications for next-generation AI, energy and computational efficiency, industrial relevance and outstanding research gaps. The conclusion synthesises these findings and identifies priorities for researchers and industry. A central argument developed throughout this book is that neuromorphic computing should not be understood simply as an attempt to reproduce the human brain in hardware. Its broader significance lies in challenging established assumptions concerning the organisation of computation. Biological neural systems demonstrate that intelligence can emerge from distributed, sparse, adaptive and event-driven interactions. Neuromorphic engineering translates selected principles of this organisation into technological architectures designed for particular computational requirements. The future of AI hardware is unlikely to be defined by a single architecture. Conventional processors and specialised accelerators will continue to play critical roles in large-scale numerical computation, model training and general-purpose processing. Neuromorphic systems may instead occupy an increasingly important position within heterogeneous architectures, particularly where real-time processing, low energy consumption, temporal information, continual adaptation and edge intelligence are required. This book is intended for researchers, academics, postgraduate students, engineers, AI practitioners, technology professionals and readers seeking a structured understanding of neuromorphic computing and its relationship with the future of artificial intelligence. items.title: Mathematical Refutation of IP Laundering and Architecting Physical-Layer Silicon Interlocks (Part III): 3nm/2nm ASIC Post-P&R PPA Characterization, UltraScale+ HBM Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Verification, CXL 3.1 / PCIe Gen6 IDE / UCIe Die-to-Die Extensions, and Human-in-Command (HIC) / SEC Rule 15c3-5 / Caremark Forensic Attestation
items.abstract: Following the formal mathematical refutation of syntactic Intellectual Property (IP) laundering in Part I (10.5281/zenodo.23735935) and the synthesizable SystemVerilog Register-Transfer Level (RTL) notarization of the Sovereign Physical-Layer Interlock in Part II (10.5281/zenodo.23737404), hyperscale AI operators and merchant silicon vendors face three final engineering and legal defenses: (1) commercial infeasibility due to silicon Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) overhead; (2) protocol incompatibility across disaggregated CXL 3.1 memory pools, PCIe Gen6 Integrity and Data Encryption (IDE) streams, and UCIe chiplet boundaries; and (3) lack of cycle-accurate Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) timing closure on production High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) accelerators. This Part III monograph (10.5281/zenodo.23741025, revising and extending 10.5281/zenodo.23740271) resolves all three defenses simultaneously. First, we present comprehensive Post-Place-and-Route (Post-P&R) ASIC characterization across commercial 3nm FinFET (N3E) and 2nm Gate-All-Around (GAA / N2) foundry nodes, proving that the complete Sovereign Interlock occupies 0.0315 mm² (31,500 µm²)—representing an infinitesimal 0.0042% area overhead on a standard 750 mm² AI reticle die—while incurring 0.00% effective training throughput degradation via deterministic HBM3e pre-fetch latency hiding. Second, we report Static Timing Analysis (STA) closure and HIL validation on an AMD Virtex UltraScale+ HBM (xcvu37p-fsvh2892-2L-e / Alveo U55C) platform operating at 650 MHz, achieving a positive Worst Negative Slack of WNS = +0.142 ns and sub-cycle (< 1.538 ns) PCIe DMA zeroization upon unlicensed provenance detection. Third, we formalize the CXL 3.1 / PCIe Gen6 512-bit Flit extension (56.5 ns multi-tenant memory pool Sovereign Lock) and UCIe Die-to-Die heartbeat monitoring linked directly to the <= 2.5 mOhm GaN crowbar (PHOENIX_ROUTER). Finally, we specify a hypervisor-bypassing zk-STARK Remote Attestation API reading the 2,048-bit One-Time Programmable (OTP) eFuse (f_otp_latch) to enforce Human-in-Command (HIC) governance and establish incontrovertible Scienter under SEC Rule 15c3-5 and Delaware Caremark fiduciary standards. Complete Vivado XDC physical constraints and cycle-accurate SystemVerilog RTL/testbench modules are provided in Appendices A–C.

items.title: Mathematical Foundations of AI-Assisted VLSI: A Comparative Review of Physical Design, Optimization, Verification and Testing
items.abstract: As Moore's Law slows, advanced-node VLSI design faces increasing computational complexity. Meeting the requirements of 7 nm and smaller technologies involves solving highly complex, often NP-hard, optimization problems. Traditional EDA methods based on deterministic algorithms, such as routing, SAT solving, and sparse matrix computations ($Ax=b$), become increasingly computationally expensive for billion-transistor designs. Consequently, learning-based approaches are gaining attention as complementary solutions. This review examines the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and meta-heuristic optimization techniques for improving placement, optimization, verification, and testing in modern VLSI design. This review examines four key application domains: ($S1$) learning-based methods for physical design optimization, ($S2$) neural-network surrogate models for circuit tuning and performance prediction, ($S3$) AI-assisted logic synthesis and verification on And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs), and ($S4$) machine-learning-guided Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG) to reduce backtracking during testing. Emerging applications in hardware security, including the detection of layout-level Trojans, are also discussed. Additionally, the review highlights the trade-offs associated with AI-based approaches, particularly the balance between computational efficiency and prediction accuracy. Overall, the surveyed literature demonstrates how AI-driven models can accelerate complex optimization tasks and support modern VLSI design workflows.

items.title: Low‐Outgassing Liquid Metal–Silicone Composites for Multifunctional Space Applications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Space‐grade elastomers provide critical sealing, adhesion, and damping functions in spacecraft but require low outgassing to avoid contamination of sensitive optical and electronic components. Silicone elastomers are widely adopted due to their environmental stability, mechanical reliability, and ease of processing. Here, we introduce a multifunctional, low‐outgassing liquid metal elastomer composite with a space‐grade silicone matrix (S‐LMEC) that combines the mechanical reliability of the silicone with enhanced thermal and electrical properties. Dispersed LM microdroplets enable a 2.3 higher breaking strain, an 11 increase in thermal conductivity, and a 9.6 increase in dielectric permittivity without hindering curing. Thermogravimetric analysis demonstrates that the embedded LM does not compromise the underlying thermal stability of the polymer matrix while active electronic testing indicates the S‐LMEC significantly lowers the steady‐state temperatures by promoting rapid heat dissipation. Furthermore, the material can be patterned into complex structures via direct ink write 3D printing. The outgassing evaluation of the S‐LMEC indicates a total mass loss (TML) of 1.00%. To demonstrate practical utility, the S‐LMEC was integrated into a wearable capacitive tactile glove for soft robotic skin applications. This materials platform expands the design space for space‐grade elastomers, enabling advancements in planetary exploration soft robotics and on‐demand electronics manufacturing.

items.title: Influence of ZrO2 Seed and Nb2O5 Capping Layers on the Ferroelectric Characteristics of 4 nm La-Doped Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Capacitors
items.abstract: Abstract While sub-5 nm hafnium zirconium oxide (HZO) films are important for scaled ferroelectric memory devices, stabilizing their ferroelectric characteristics becomes increasingly challenging because the reduced thickness makes phase stabilization highly sensitive to microstructure, stress, and defect chemistry. Here, we evaluate 4 nm La-doped HZO (La:HZO) capacitors using an interfacial engineering strategy combining post-metallization annealing (PMA), ZrO2 seed layer control, and Nb2O5 capping layer. PMA provides a mechanically confined crystallization environment through the presence of the top electrode during annealing. Building upon this confined crystallization environment, the effects of the ZrO2 seed layer deposition temperature and the introduction of the Nb2O5 capping layer on the structural and ferroelectric characteristics of La:HZO were systematically investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD), in-plane XRD, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and positive-up-negative-down (PUND) measurements. Capacitors incorporating only the ZrO2 seed layer exhibit weak ferroelectric switching at 3 MV/cm and early electrical breakdown, indicating that oxygen vacancy-related effects strongly limit polarization switching. Introducing a 2 nm Nb2O5 capping layer decreases the relative intensity of the low-binding-energy shoulders in the Hf 4f and Zr 3d spectra, consistent with a reduced contribution of oxygen-deficient local environments. PUND measurements further reveal a progressive reduction in the leakage current component during the ‘U’ pulse, which is attributed to the oxygen-donating role of the Nb2O5 capping layer, whereas only a weak change is observed during the ‘D’ pulse. This polarity-dependent behavior is consistent with oxygen vacancy compensation near the Nb2O5 capping layer during cycling. Among all investigated device configurations, the capacitor incorporating the 250 °C ZrO2 seed layer and the Nb2O5 capping layer exhibits the highest 2Pr,rel. These results indicate that grain evolution, nonswitching current behavior, and the oxygen-related defect environment are correlated with the ferroelectric response of 4 nm La:HZO capacitors and should be considered together when designing the stack.

items.title: Improvement of AlGaN/GaN HEMT Performance by Using Hybrid Ohmic Source and Drain for Ka-band Applications
items.abstract: Abstract In this study, Γ-gate AlGaN/GaN HEMTs featuring a hybrid ohmic source and drain structure were investigated to meet the requirements for high-power and low-noise performance in Ka-band applications. The proposed hybrid metal devices with extension lengths of 0.25 and 0.35 μm and a conventional ohmic device without an extension were fabricated. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid metal device with a 0.25 μm extension exhibits an improved drain saturation current (IDSS) of 1087 mA/mm and an enhanced peak transconductance (gm) of 408 mS/mm at VDS = 10 V. The device also achieved a cut-off frequency (fT) of 89 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency (fmax) of 171 GHz. At 28 GHz, the device shows an output power (Pout) of 2.82 W/mm with power-added efficiency (PAE) of 22.1% and a minimum noise figure (NFmin) of 1.29 dB. These improvements are associated with improved access-region electrical characteristics and reduced parasitic resistance. In contrast, increasing the extension length to 0.35 μm results in a negative Vth shift and degraded gate control under high drain biases. These results indicate that the hybrid ohmic structure with a proper extension length can enhance device performance for millimeter-wave applications.

items.title: High-Performance Ce-Doped HfO2 Ferroelectric Thin Films by Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract Ce-doped HfO2 (HCO) ferroelectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for next-generation integrated ferroelectric devices owing to their excellent compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology and promising ferroelectric properties. However, previously reported HCO films generally require relatively large thicknesses and high processing temperatures, limiting their application in highly scaled devices. Here, we demonstrate HCO ferroelectric thin films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and systematically investigate the effects of Ce concentration and film thickness on their structural and ferroelectric properties. The HCO film with 5.0% Ce doping exhibits the highest ferroelectric orthorhombic phase fraction, which is attributed to the formation of coupled defects involving Ce-substitution on Hf sites and oxygen vacancies, as revealed by first-principles calculations. Moreover, the HCO films annealed at 700 °C exhibit excellent ferroelectric properties at the thickness ranging from 12 to 24 nm. In particular, the 18 nm-thick HCO film with 5.0% Ce achieves a remanent polarization of 19.4 μC/cm2 and an excellent switching endurance exceeding 1 × 109 cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of ALD-grown HCO as a scalable material platform for highly integrated and multifunctional ferroelectric devices.

items.title: GeoFormer: Non-Equilibrium Metric Manifolds and Quantized Thermodynamic Attractor Convergence for Multi-Hop Transitive Reasoning
items.abstract: GeoFormer is a neuromorphic foundation architecture grounded in Endogenous Propagation Geometry (Q-PG) designed to solve catastrophic forgetting, topological blindness, and compositional collapse in deep neural networks without requiring floating-point matrix multiplications. Abstract Standard Transformer architectures treat latent sequence space as an immutable, flat Euclidean coordinate system. In dot-product attention, dense synaptic weights in ℝD are forced to simultaneously perform semantic feature transformation and topological signal routing, leading to compositional collapse on unseen multi-hop transitive reasoning tasks. GeoFormer structurally decouples frozen 1.58-bit ternary transformation weights (θ ∈ {-1, 0, +1}) from an episodic 4-bit metric conductance lattice W. Relational associations deform this lattice, contracting effective resistances dij = (Wij + ε)-1 → 0 into persistent geodesic highways. Multi-hop transitive deductions are resolved in a single forward pass via continuous Quantized Thermodynamic Attractor Convergence (Q-TAC) graph Laplacian heat diffusion. Core Mathematical & Empirical Highlights Formal Deductive Machine Verification: All 6 governing algebraic invariants (discrete geodesic contraction, Fiedler spectral gap preservation λ2(L) > 0, precision-topology duality, S5 Cayley projection stability, Lyapunov energy monotonicity, and bounded plasticity) are certified UNSAT (counterexample-free) using the Microsoft Z3 SMT solver. Empirical Multi-Hop Generalization: Evaluated across 5 independent random seeds on unseen 2-hop compositions, directed Q-TAC achieves 40.00% ± 7.30% Hits@1 and 89.33% Hits@3, matching non-neural pure graph random walks (45.33%) within 1-to-N candidate branching limits (4.01 ± 2.11 targets/head). Standard Euclidean Transformers collapse to 1.33%. Autonomous Self-Regulation (Irrational Geometry Engine): Integrates golden-ratio quasi-crystalline positional encodings (0.000% collisions, 0 trainable parameters), Diophantine continued-fraction multi-scale relaxation schedules (1.84× latency speedup), and ergodic Weyl rotation drivers for bounded background memory consolidation (zero invariant violations over 1,000 steps). Sub-Nanojoule Memristor Compilation: A first-principles device physics simulation confirms isomorphic mapping to analog 1T1R ReRAM crossbars, dissipating 443.9 picajoules per inference pass (9,462× lower dynamic energy than FP32 GPU baselines) with analog noise absorption up to 20% programming variance. items.title: FlatCake: A Flat KVCache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving
items.abstract: KV cache reuse accelerates LLM serving, but existing systems manage host DRAM and NVMe SSD as a tiered hierarchy where DRAM acts as an intermediate cache. Production LLM workloads break both premises of this hierarchy. First, bimodal reuse defeats DRAM temporal filtering, since workloads are dominated either by one-shot blocks with long reuse distances or by multi-gigabyte agentic sessions that exceed DRAM capacity, putting SSD on the critical read path. Second, DRAM staging and eviction-ordered layout bottleneck SSD restoration. Holding host staging buffers for in-flight prefixes causes contention under load that aborts prefetches, while incremental eviction scatters a session's blocks across the SSD and prevents large sequential reads. We present FlatCake, a flat KV storage architecture that exposes host DRAM and NVMe SSD as peer media in a unified 64-bit address space. Exploiting the fact that KV blocks are write-once, immutable, and reused at session scope, FlatCake places each block directly onto its target medium in session-contiguous, layer-major order at creation time and never migrates it. FlatCake streams coalesced SSD reads directly into a bounded GPU window via GPUDirect Storage and decouples DRAM and SSD request queues to prevent head-of-line blocking. On a production Claude Code trace with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, FlatCake sustains a 94% cache hit rate as load increases (versus 64% for Mooncake), eliminates Mooncake's $6.5\times$--$6.7\times$ SSD read amplification, and reduces peak-load mean TTFT by $1.6\times$ while improving total token throughput by $1.6\times$. Across 8K--128K contexts on Llama-3.1-70B, FlatCake further reduces mean TTFT by up to $2.4\times$ over Mooncake and $1.8\times$ over Mooncake-GDS.

items.title: Exceptionally Matched p-SiNW/n-IGZO Complementary Field-Effect Transistors for Monolithic 3D Logic
items.abstract: Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) provide a route toward a higher logic density by vertically stacking complementary devices within the same footprint. Their realization through heterogeneous integration requires p- and n-channel transistors that are both individually high-performing and electrically matched. Here, we demonstrate high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide M3D CFETs by vertically integrating p-type silicon nanowire (p-SiNW) FETs with n-type indium gallium zinc oxide (n-IGZO) transistors. The site-controlled p-SiNWs are formed through a scalable in-plane solid-liquid-solid (IPSLS) process without postgrowth hydrogen passivation, facilitating subsequent oxide-semiconductor integration. The vertically integrated p- and n-channel devices exhibit closely matched current-driving capabilities, near-zero threshold voltages, and subthreshold swings of 120 and 133 mV dec-1, respectively. This exceptional p/n matching enables sharp and well-balanced switching, yielding a peak voltage gain of 103 V/V at VDD = 5 V, a normalized gain of 20.6 V-1, and large, nearly symmetric noise margins (NML = 0.45 VDD and NMH = 0.44 VDD). The architecture is further extended to NOR, NAND, and OR gates with experimentally verified logic operations. These results establish a high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide integration platform for dense and robust M3D complementary logic.

items.title: Electrically tunable two-dimensional quantum materials for terahertz optoelectronics
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials host electronic and collective excitations whose characteristic energies naturally fall within the terahertz (THz) range. Their reduced dimensionality, strong light–matter interaction, and sensitivity to external fields provide opportunities for electrically reconfigurable THz optoelectronics that are difficult to realize using conventional semiconductors and passive optical materials. In this review, we examine how electrical control of carrier density, dielectric screening, ferroelectric polarization, and correlated electronic states can program the THz response of diverse 2D quantum materials, including topological semimetals, semiconductors with strong excitonic effects, ferroelectrics, as well as their moiré superlattices. We first outline the fundamental THz optoelectronic processes, including generation, detection, and modulation, together with the main limitations of conventional materials and device platforms. We then discuss the distinctive properties of major 2D quantum-material platforms that govern their THz response. Recent progress is subsequently reviewed according to the main electrical tuning mechanisms, including electrostatic doping, displacement-field control, and ferroelectric polarization switching. We introduce how these approaches modify THz properties of 2D quantum materials and how the resulting tunability is used in THz optoelectronics with competitive performance and superior electrical tunability. We conclude by discussing the key challenges and promising future research directions that could advance high-performance, intelligent, and multifunctional THz optoelectronics based on electrically tunable 2D quantum materials.

items.title: Design, Physical Analysis, and Area Scaling Assessment of a 2 nm Single-Fin FinFET with Monolithic Self-Aligned Nanowire Interconnects
items.abstract: This paper presents the design, physical analysis, and area-scaling assessment of a 2 nm single-fin FinFET in which the source/drain regions are extended into monolithic, epitaxially continuous silicon nanowires that double as local interconnects. The nanowire extensions are patterned in the same lithographic and etch step as the fin itself, producing a fully self-aligned, via-less middle-of-line (MOL) integration scheme on an UTB-SOI/SIMOX substrate. Analytical layout comparison against a conventional 2 nm FinFET cell with V0/VD contacts shows a 25–30% reduction in standard-cell area (28% for the reference inverter cell) and a 35–40% reduction in MOL volume, together with an estimated 30% reduction in gate–source/drain overlap capacitance and roughly 34% lower RC gate delay. The tri-gate device concept on which this architecture builds was established in early SOI-based patents on tri-gate devices and fabrication methods (US6858478B2). The results indicate that replacing vertical metal contacts with self-aligned monolithic nanowire extensions is a credible path to cell-area scaling beyond the limits imposed by conventional contact/via modules.

items.title: DRIVE CYCLE-BASED LOSS EVALUATION OF TWO-LEVEL AND THREE-LEVEL INVERTERS IN 400 V AND 800 V ELECTRIC VEHICLE APPLICATIONS
items.abstract: In this paper, the driving cycle model tested by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is utilized to analyze power losses in inverter components, aiming to assess the actual performance and energy consumption of electric vehicle drive systems. The primary losses considered include conduction and switching losses that occur under real-world operating conditions. The analyzed conditions cover urban environments, highways, and challenging terrains involving multiple phases of acceleration and deceleration. Two types of semiconductor devices are evaluated: Silicon Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (Si IGBT) and Silicon Carbide Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (SiC MOSFET), corresponding to battery system voltage levels of 400 V and 800 V, respectively. Three inverter configurations are considered in this study: two-level inverter, T-type three-level inverter, and ANPC three-level inverter. The efficiency and energy losses of each configuration are assessed based on simulation results.
items.venue: Tạp chí Khoa học Đại học Công Thương.

items.title: Beyond Long-Term Protection by Intelligent Poly(lactic acid) Nanofibers: Structuring Multiscale Hierarchies for Passive Sensing
items.abstract: Recent advances in electrospun biodegradable polymer nanofibrous membranes (NFMs) are reshaping the design of functional materials from passive morphological optimization toward programmed charge regulation and function-oriented structural engineering. Extending this concept to biobased poly(lactic acid) (PLA), however, remains challenging because PLA exhibits weak cooperative alignment of ester dipoles, a low dielectric response, and a limited number of highly polar or ionizable groups. These molecular characteristics give rise to shallow charge traps, insufficient interfacial polarization, and rapid charge dissipation across crystalline–amorphous regions. Therefore, the key scientific issue is not only how to fabricate porous PLA membranes but also how to organize their molecular conformations, crystalline domains, filler interfaces, and fibrous networks into a multiscale charge-regulation system. Electrospinning provides an effective route for addressing this issue because electric-field stretching, jet elongation, solvent evaporation, and phase separation can simultaneously regulate PLA chain orientation, crystalline morphology, fiber assembly, and pore architecture without altering the chemical structure of PLA chains. On this basis, research has progressed from single-parameter optimization toward multidimensional structural regulation. First, tuning electrospinning parameters, including voltage, collection distance, solution viscosity, and collector motion, promotes axial chain orientation and cooperative ester-dipole alignment. This oriented conformation enhances crystalline ordering, enriches crystalline–amorphous interfaces, and creates favorable charge-trapping domains, while more ordered fiber assembly narrows pore-size distributions and improves airflow continuity. Second, stereocomplexation between poly(l-lactide) and poly(d-lactide) introduces tightly packed stereocomplex crystallites through stereospecific interchain interactions. These ordered crystallites intensify dipolar polarization, deepen trap energy levels, and improve charge-storage stability, thereby mitigating the poor electret durability of pristine PLA. Third, nanoscale filler interfacial engineering with electroactive porous or dielectric fillers, such as metal–organic frameworks and titanium dioxide, introduces dielectric heterogeneity, defect-rich interfaces, unsaturated coordination sites, and high-surface-area contact domains. These features enrich multilevel charge-trapping sites, promote interfacial polarization, facilitate localized charge regeneration, and impart additional functions, including adsorption, antibacterial activity, humidity tolerance, and photothermal or optical regulation. An increasingly systematic understanding of the processing–structure–electroactivity–function relationship is accelerating the transition of PLA NFMs from mechanistic studies to engineering applications. The coordinated regulation of fiber orientation, stereocomplex crystallization, and nanofiller-mediated heterointerfaces enables coupled charge generation, capture, trap-mediated storage, interfacial migration, and dynamic regeneration. These charge-regulation pathways allow PLA membranes to harvest and retain charges generated during particle filtration, electromechanical deformation, airflow-induced friction, and physiological motion, while suppressing charge decay under humid or dynamically changing conditions. In particulate matter filtration, they couple electrostatic adsorption with optimized porous architectures to achieve efficient particle capture and low airflow resistance. In electromechanical conversion, they enhance triboelectric and piezoelectric responses for biodegradable self-powered systems. In health monitoring, stable charge transduction improves physiological signal acquisition and sensing reliability. In this Account, we critically summarize how electrospinning process regulation, stereocomplexation, and nanofiller interface engineering govern multiscale structures and electroactivity in PLA NFMs. We establish a processing–structure–electroactivity–function framework that involves fiber morphology, crystalline organization, interfacial polarization, charge trapping, and application performance across molecular, interfacial, and membrane scales. It essentially highlights hierarchical structuring as the key to designing intelligent biodegradable nanofibers for efficient filtration, self-powered sensing, wearable health monitoring, and adaptive protective systems.

items.title: A low-power CMOS spiking neuron design with frequency adaptation in 180 nm technology at 300 mV supply
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a low-power spiking neuron design using 180 nm CMOS technology, operating at a 300 mV supply with a frequency adaptation mechanism. The design achieves an energy consumption of 9.3 pJ/spike, a 22.5% improvement over the baseline model (12 pJ/spike), a stable 255 Hz firing frequency, and a 70% increase in spike amplitude through a P-type transistor in the feedback loop. Simulations in ADS confirm the design’s stability, though the lack of hardware validation remains a limitation. Compared to advanced nodes (e.g., 28 nm), it offers a cost-effective solution for IoT and robotics applications, with potential memristor integration enhancing synaptic flexibility. Future work includes hardware validation and scalability improvements.
items.venue: Analog Integrated Circuits and Signal Processing

items.title: A coordination-ligand reorientation mechanism for ferroelectricity in Mn(II) hybrid complex and its utility for memory application
items.abstract: Moving beyond classical models of collective ion reorientation, we present a ligand-tilting design for molecular ferroelectrics. Using the asymmetric isothiocyanate (NCS⁻) ligand as a dynamic “molecular hinge,” we achieve facile polarization switching through geometric distortion and coordination-ligand flipping in the hybrid complex [Ph3PEt]3[Mn(NCS)5]. In this framework, the asymmetric cation stabilizes a polar phase in the triclinic P1 space group and a rare distorted trigonal-bipyramidal Mn(II) center, directed by the tilt of the coordinated NCS⁻ ligand, enabling room-temperature ferroelectricity with saturation polarization (Pₛ) of 1.57 µC·cm−2. Density functional theory (DFT) confirms that ligand-flipping modes are a key switching mechanism with a low barrier to polarization reversal. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) provides visual validation of domain reversals via box-in-box lithography and single-point switching spectroscopy. Incorporation of [Ph3PEt]3[Mn(NCS)5] into ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) yields a memory window (60 V) and an ON/OFF ratio (>104), with electrically controlled transitions between volatile and non-volatile states. The devices emulate synaptic functions, including long-term potentiation/depression (LTP/LTD) and multilevel conductance states (with 64 levels), demonstrating neuromorphic capabilities. Control experiments distinguish polarization-driven switching from charge trapping as the origin of the memtransistor response. Coordinate-ligand dynamics thus emerge as a design principle for molecular ferroelectrics, enabling memory and brain-inspired computing. Addressing the limitations of classical models in molecular ferroelectrics, the authors introduce a ligand-tilting design using asymmetric isothiocyanate ligands. This approach enables room-temperature ferroelectricity and neuromorphic capabilities in devices, with implications for memory and brain-inspired computing, as demonstrated by their integration into ferroelectric field-effect transistors.

items.title: 800 $^\circ$C Air-Ambient Operation of Extreme-Bandgap Al$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N (x>0.6) Digital and Random-Alloy Channel HEMTs
items.abstract: This work demonstrates the high-temperature (room to 800 $^\circ$C) operation of thin Al$_{0.62}$Ga$_{0.38}$N digital alloy (DA) short-period superlattice (SPSL), and random alloy (RA) Al$_{0.64}$Ga$_{0.36}$N channel MOSHEMTs on sapphire. The RA devices employ a doped $n^{+}$-85%-Al barrier and a highly doped $n^{++}$-Al$_{0.86\rightarrow0.20}$Ga$_{0.14\rightarrow0.80}$N reverse-graded layer (RGL) for surface ohmic contact formation, whereas the DA devices employ a binary AlN barrier and selectively regrown $n^{++}$-GaN source/drain contacts. At 800 $^\circ$C, the DA channel devices exhibit better thermal stability: their saturated drain current decreases from 460 to 172 mA/mm (62.6%) compared with 338 to 98 mA/mm (71.0%) for the RA channel, and a lower subthreshold swing (459 for DA versus 550 mV/dec for RA). All tested DA devices also exhibit superior threshold-voltage stability ($ \pm 19\%$ for RA) and maintain an ON/OFF current ratio >$10^4$ at 800 $^\circ$C, compared with ~$10^3$ for RA, thus establishing the DA channel HEMTs as a promising new platform for high-temperature electronics.

items.title: p-DCIM: A 28nm Probabilistic SRAM DCIM based Ising Machine for Near-Memory Context Selection in LLM-RAG Pipeline
items.abstract: We present a fabricated SRAM DCIM Ising machine that performs set-level context selection for large language model (LLM) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In RAG, the evidence-selection stage is increasingly delegated to repeated language-model reranking, which adds substantial energy to the inference pipeline. We reformulate evidence selection as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and solve it on a dual-mode digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro: the same multiply-and-accumulate datapath computes the embedding-similarity scores that populate the QUBO coefficients and evaluates the per-spin Hamiltonian differences that drive the anneal. The annealing temperature is set by a digital plane-count control along with the SRAM pseudo-read random bit flips, giving graded cooling entirely from on-chip digital configuration. The macro is taped-out in a 28 nm process [0.16 mm2, 0.41 mW] and is proposed to be integrated as part of the logic base-die in hybrid high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-bandwidth flash (HBF) stacks in a GPU package, where only the selected passage identifiers return to the host. Replacing the language-model selection pass with the near-memory Ising solver yields a macro normalized selection-energy estimate more than six orders of magnitude lower than the LLM-based baseline and reduces the evaluated total energy per query by 67%, while maintaining comparable token-level F1 on the evaluated examples.

items.title: When Can Nanoimprint Compete? Process-Specific Total Cost, Yield Risk, and the Adoption of Canon Nanoimprint Lithography Relative to ASML Deep-Ultraviolet and Extreme-Ultraviolet Lithography
items.abstract: Nanoimprint lithography (NIL) promises sub-15-nm patterning at a fraction of the capital cost and energy draw of extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, yet the parameters that would tell a cost-rational manufacturer whether to adopt Canon's FPA-1200NZ2C over ASML deep-ultraviolet (DUV) immersion or EUV scanners—defect density, template lifetime, tool price, and qualified yield—go undisclosed. This study bounds those parameters rather than guessing them. It integrates a process-specific total-cost-of-ownership model covering four platforms and five device layers, a Monte Carlo yield-risk simulation (N = 10,000 draws per cell, seed 20261022), and adoption-stage panel econometrics on a firm-platform-year panel (N = 243, G = 9). At central inputs, a single imprint pass costs $54.73, against $37.24 for DUV immersion, $104.22 for Low-NA EUV, and $172.50 for High-NA EUV. Once yield is included, nanoimprint is the low-cost platform in three-dimensional NAND ($312.10 per good wafer vs. $585.50 for DUV immersion and $454.63 for Low-NA EUV, winning in 76.99% of draws), back-end damascene, and photonics; it is marginal in advanced DRAM and uncompetitive in leading-edge logic. Defect density and template life, not tool price, govern the result. Adoption stage tracks accumulated knowledge (logged knowledge-stock β = 1.1306), and no Canon NIL observation reaches qualified high-volume manufacturing (Stages 7–9: 0%). A 97-check audit records 87 PASS, 10 WARN, and 0 FAIL. Cost and simulation findings are conditional scenario mechanics; econometric findings are descriptive associations, not causal effects. Nanoimprint competes where layers are defect-tolerant, not across the board.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Warpage Control Strategies in 3D Advanced Packaging: A Focus on Post-Processing and Material-Level Optimization
items.abstract: As semiconductor architectures vertically scale through high-density 3D advanced packaging, wafer-level warpage introduces severe failure modes that threaten process yield and structural reliability. Driven by the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch between heterogeneous materials, uncontrolled warpage induces critical defects—such as warpage induced cracks and difficulties in post processing—while complicating the package integration. To address these challenges, this study presents a comprehensive, empirical investigation focusing on warpage control; material-level optimization, process impacts, and structural variations, using real-case wafer integration. We systematically evaluate warpage behavior from three engineering perspectives: material CTE/component optimization of epoxy molding compounds (EMCs) under thermal cycling; comparative analysis between capillary underfill (CUF) and molded underfill (MUF) structures; and mechanical configuration tuning using wafer support systems (WSS). Adjusting these critical parameters establishes data-driven process guidelines that enhance manufacturing yield, improve process predictability, and ensure robust compatibility with next-generation 3D integration schemes.

items.title: Verbundprojekt: UniCharge - Universelles, bidirektionales und kostenoptimiertes On-Board-Ladegerät für die Zukunft der Elektromobilität
items.abstract: Das Verbundprojekt UniCharge erforscht ein universelles, bidirektionales On-Board-Ladegerät (OBC) der nächsten Generation zur Förderung der Elektromobilität. Das Gesamtsystem ermöglicht Ladeleistungen von 22 kW am dreiphasigen 400 V Netz sowie 7,4 kW einphasig und deckt Batteriespannungen von 250 V bis 900 V ab. Durch den Einsatz von Galliumnitrid-Leistungshalbleitern (GaN HEMTs), resonanten Topologien und digitalem Condition Monitoring wird daran geforscht Bauvolumen, Gewicht und Kosten signifikant zu reduzieren. Der Teilpartner TU Dortmund war dabei vor allem für die Entwicklung der digitalen Zustandsüberwachung (Condition Monitoring) sowie der optimierten Gate-Ansteuerung der GaN HEMTs zuständig.

items.title: Valley-Dependent Photogating-Controlled Quantum Transport in Monolayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, we develop a theoretical framework to investigate trap-charge-induced photogating as the sole electrostatic control mechanism for quantum transport and different basis for negative differential resistance (NDR) in monolayer \(\:\text{W}\text{S}\text{e}₂\) and \(\:\text{M}\text{o}\text{S}₂\). The valley sensitive optical response, photocarrier generation, carrier trapping, and resulting photogating potential are coupled to quantum transport using the Landauer–Büttiker formalism and an extended transfer-matrix approach. The transport response is systematically examined over photogating voltages \(\:\left({{\Delta\:}\text{V}}_{\text{p}\text{g}}\text{}\right)\:\text{o}\text{f}\:0\:\text{t}\text{o}\:8\:\text{m}\text{V}\). The calculations reveal a strongly nonlinear current response, with photogating-induced currents of the order of \(\:0.2\:{\mu\:}\text{A}\) and maximum peak to valley ratio, mPVR, values of approximately 1.01–1.03. For \(\:\text{M}\text{L}-\text{W}\text{S}\text{e}₂\), the calculated absorption coefficient reaches \(\:17.82\times\:{10}^{5}\:{\text{c}\text{m}}^{-1}\), with a trapped-carrier density of approximately \(\:1.3\times\:{10}^{12}\:{\text{c}\text{m}}^{-2}\). The observed NDR arises from photogating-induced modulation of resonant transmission states in the absence of an externally imposed source–drain driving potential. Our findings establish photogating as a direct means of controlling nonlinear quantum transport and provide a basis for light-controlled low-power switching, signal modulation, sensing, memory, and neuromorphic applications.

items.title: Unlocking Large-Area Two-Dimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: From Epitaxial Growth to Frontier Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Wafer-scale, high-quality, thickness- and stacking configuration-tunable two-dimensional (2D) semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenides (STMDCs) hold great potential to serve as channel materials in complementary field effect transistors (CFETs) at the sub-nanometer technology node, thus further extending the logic technology roadmap. Epitaxial growth of 2D STMDCs on industrial-compatible substrates should be the first step. In this perspective, we present an overview of recent advances in the epitaxial mechanism explorations and wafer-scale growth of monolayer STMDC films or single crystals via substrate surface modulations and growth methodology optimizations. The applications of 2D STMDC wafers in high-performance electronic and optoelectronic devices are reviewed. Challenges and prospects are also highlighted, especially regarding the 12-inch-scale preparations of monolayer STMDC films and functional device integration.

items.title: Towards a Digital Twin for Failure Risk Prediction of Epoxy Mold Compounds and Warpage Modeling in Advanced Packaging
items.abstract: In this work we present a predictive simulation model for epoxy mold compound (EMC), based-on advanced material characterization and inelastic material modelling. Tensile testing at different temperatures and loading rates was conducted to characterize the plasticity, creep and stress relaxation behaviors of the EMC material. Experimentally observed plasticity and creep behaviors are incorporated in the inelastic (viscoplastic) material model. A linear viscoelastic (LVE) material model was fit using the stress-relaxation test data and compared with the widely adopted LVE material model fitted from a frequency-sweep based DMA testing. These models were incorporated into the packaging simulations to account for the realistic behavior of EMC under thermal cycling and wafer warpage. Accumulated permanent strains in EMC were probed for fatigue life predictions. The relaxation testing based LVE model was shown to give more accurate wafer warpage prediction, than the frequency-sweep based LVE models. Furthermore, the merits of the proposed modeling and methodology compared to conventional modeling were discussed. This approach is readily implementable in package simulations using commercial FEA software and expected to add failure predictive capabilities.

items.title: The Effect of Ni Content in Electroless Cu Deposit on the Adhesion Between the Seed Layer and Glass Substrate
items.abstract: In this paper, we discuss a method of improving the adhesion of the seed layer, consisting of a metal oxide deposit and electroless copper film, on the glass substrate. The rapid development of AI technology has dramatically increased the demand for High-Performance Computing (HPC), which requires the processing of massive datasets at extremely high speeds. To achieve high-performance processing for use in HPC, more chiplets should be mounted on a single substrate. As a result, the substrate must satisfy several requirements, such as finer lines and spaces, improved high-frequency performance, larger substrate sizes, and high reliability. However, conventional organic substrates often fall short due to issues such as substrate warpage and high insertion loss at high frequency, caused by their properties. Glass has emerged as a promising alternative to resolve these problems because of its advantageous properties: high stiffness, surface smoothness, low coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) and low dielectric loss (Df). Consequently, there have been numerous efforts to develop new manufacturing processes for glass core substrates. Although the glass is considered a suitable core material, one of the main challenges is achieving good adhesion between the copper film and the glass substrate when using copper for circuit formation. For this reason, in this study, we investigated the process for forming seed layers on glass with enhanced adhesion. In the Semi-Additive process (SAP), which is commonly used in substrate fabrication, plating core materials with electroless copper plating before electrolytic copper plating deposition is common. However, we introduced Metal Oxide Seed Layer (MOSL) with approximately 0.2 μm thickness between the glass and the plating layer in this research. This approach enables the formation of a seed layer with superior adhesion to glass. We evaluated the adhesion by measuring the peel strength. Our results show that increasing Ni concentration in the electroless copper bath improved the deposit’s adhesion to the glass. The best result was achieved with a deposit composed of Glass / MOSL / Cu-Ni alloy (4.6 at% Ni), which exhibited a peel strength of 1000 gf/cm. The value was around two times higher than that of MOSL / Cu-Ni alloy film with 1.4 at% Ni. These results indicate that the increasing amount of co-deposited Ni in the Cu deposit greatly enhances the adhesion. To investigate the mechanism behind this improvement, we performed STEM-EDX analysis to examine the deposit composition. In as-plated samples, no Cu was detected at the interface between the glass and MOSL, regardless of Ni content. However, in post-annealed samples with 1.4 at% Ni, a small amount of Cu was observed at the interface, whereas in the 4.6 at% Ni samples, Cu was barely detectable in that region. These results suggest that high-Ni-content Cu alloy deposits act as a self-formed barrier layer, preventing Cu diffusion through the MOSL layer—a phenomenon well known in sputtering studies. This barrier effect contributes significantly to the improved adhesion between the seed layer and the glass. Our method is expected to enable the formation of high-coverage seed layers inside Through-Glass Vias (TGVs) with high aspect ratios (AR: 10–20), paving the way for advanced glass-based substrates in high-performance applications.

items.title: The Economics of Scarcity and Ecosystem Lock-in: NVIDIA's Premium Pricing, Market Power and Consumer Willingness to Pay in the AI Accelerator Market
