items.abstract: This study analyzes NVIDIA's high pricing model in the AI chip market by combining the concepts of product differentiation, market power, and consumer behavior. It suggests that NVIDIA has established very high switching costs with the CUDA ecosystem, making the price elasticity of demand very low, if not approaching zero, allowing them to charge a price well above the marginal cost. While this approach is based on using excess profits to invest in technological progress, it has also brought about demand-side issues such as distortions in the allocation of resources resulting from the "computing capacity tax" and consumer surplus reductions due to hardware-and-software bundling. At the industry level, it has exacerbated the excessive concentration of the market and created systemic risks. To address this, this study recommends steps to optimize these measures, like setting up interoperable technical standards, moving towards transparent tiered-pricing regulations, and enhancing the resilience of the supply chain. These measures are designed to maintain a balance between the corporate incentives for innovation, market fairness, and efficiency, and to offer a theoretical reference for the healthy development of the AI industry ecosystem and inclusive growth in the global digital economy.
items.venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

items.title: The AtomicLimits Database: Towards Artificial Intelligence as a Research Assistant for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching
items.abstract: Abstract The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.

items.title: Static dielectric constant of thin dielectrics in extremely scaled silicon nanosheet transistors
items.abstract: We argue that the static dielectric constant of small (thin and/or narrow) semiconductor and insulator nanostructures depends strongly on their environment. We do so by considering the electronic response, simply reviewing, briefly but critically, the existing literature. Regarding the ionic response, in addition to reviewing the literature, we use a simple model to account for the confinement of optical phonons in thin films and show that the reduction of their density of states has a negligible effect on the dielectric constant, in contrast to some claims found in the literature. In general, we argue that in realistic structures, such as double-gated Si nanosheets, the use of the bulk dielectric constants for both the channel and the gate insulators is justified.

items.title: Single Bath Copper Electroplating for Seam Free Metallization of Ultra High Aspect Ratio (AR ≤ 34) Through Glass Vias
items.abstract: This work demonstrates a single-bath Cu electroplating process for void-free, seam-free filling of through glass via (TGV) with aspect ratio (AR) up to 34 using direct current (DC) control. Glass substrates of thickness 340 μm and via openings of 10 and 25 μm were studied. A virgin make-up solution with functional additives was developed. Under DC potential control, a suppressor system based on NBT and Tetronic 701 enabled rapid formation of a short H-shaped bridge (~10 μm) at the via center within 40 min, eliminating defect formation. An accelerator promoted bottom-up Cu filling under DC current control. With optimized leveler, suppressor, and accelerator concentrations, TGVs with AR= 34 were filled in a single bath using two-step DC plating, achieving a void- and seam-free filling yield exceeding 95%. Total metallization time was less than 4 hours, with no need for pulse-reverse plating or bath exchange. This process offers a practical approach for Cu metallization of next-generation glass-based advanced packaging.

items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. Gate-level VCD analysis reports 6.0706 μW leakage and 288.2902 μW (post-synthesis) / 322.8850 μW (post-PnR) dynamic power, totaling 328.9556 μW (0.2402% of system power). The EE module dominates dynamic power (58.2%), while WLG dominates area (58.1%). System evaluation on MobileNetV2 (CIFAR-100) shows efficiency scaling from 31.35 TOPS/W (8b/8b, 1.2 V) to 454.91 TOPS/W (2b/8b, 0.8 V), achieving 13.33x improvement without bitcell modification or retraining. The framework targets CNN workloads exploiting sparsity, with Transformer extension as future work.

items.title: Radiation‐Crosslinked Relaxor Ferroelectric Elastomers for Fully Organic Stretchable Capacitive Strain Sensors
items.abstract: The adaptation of capacitors to wearable electronics requires dielectric materials that combine high permittivity with well resilience. Fully organic stretchable capacitive strain sensors are particularly attractive, but their performance is often limited by the lack of suitable elastic high-k dielectrics. Relaxor ferroelectric polymers offer intrinsically high dielectric constants; however, conventional elastification approaches, such as thermal and photo-crosslinking, are constrained by harsh processing conditions and residual chemical species. Here, we present a simple and effective radiation-crosslinking strategy to convert a relaxor ferroelectric polymer into an elastic dielectric without the need for initiators or elevated temperatures. By employing poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene-chlorofluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE-CFE)) in combination with poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) as a crosslinking sensitizer, a stable crosslinked network is formed under mild irradiation conditions. The resulting material exhibits a high dielectric constant (∼37 at 25°C and 1 kHz) together with excellent elastic recovery (∼80%), thereby achieving a desirable balance between dielectric performance and resilience. When integrated with stretchable electrodes, the resulting fully organic capacitive device exhibits reproducible capacitance variation to tensile strain, demonstrating its potential for fully organic stretchable capacitive strain sensing. This work establishes a practical strategy for developing high-permittivity dielectric elastomers and advances the design of stretchable electronic devices.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. On a knowledge graph built from the semiconductor-manufacturing literature, Prospector approaches the strongest off-the-shelf models given the same graph and tools, and it far exceeds off-the-shelf models answering closed-book or from a pre-selected portion of the graph. Although trained only on the semiconductor graph, Prospector transfers to unseen knowledge graphs from three other distinct fields: bio-inspired materials, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and materials properties. Served on a single GPU, Prospector answers faster and at a fraction of the cost of a hosted service, while keeping proprietary data on the owner's hardware. We find that the policy's latent state is indicative of its next move on both seen and unseen graphs, and modulating the latent state can steer the policy from one behavior mode to another. These results suggest a practical LLM + KG paradigm for scientific and engineering reasoning over private data, in which a compact model trained on a graph from published literature transfers its traversal to unseen graphs that stay with their owners.

items.title: Process Window Design Framework for Packaging Materials Using Physics-Informed Property Prediction Models
items.abstract: This study presents a physics-informed encoder-decoder model that directly predicts key material properties influencing warpage in semiconductor package substrates from process conditions. By integrating this model with a data‑driven pattern‑profile prediction model, we develop a process optimization framework that successfully recommends process windows to meet multiple property requirements simultaneously. This reduces development costs for semiconductor packages by replacing extensive trial-and-error experiments.

items.title: Plasma Dicing Innovations on Film Frame Carriers for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and Heterogeneous Integration Devices
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of AI and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is increasing the demands on die thinning, singulation quality, and hybrid bonding readiness. This paper demonstrates an integrated digital lithography and plasma dicing process on film frame carriers (FFCs) for advanced packaging and HBM applications. The flow combines spray-coated photoresist, maskless exposure, oxide and silicon plasma etching, and plasma resist stripping to enable precise 8 μm dicing streets on ultrathin wafers. A negative-tone resist achieved excellent coating uniformity ( 1 μm/min and a silicon etch rate of 10 μm/min. The demonstrated process provides a scalable, plasma-based singulation solution for future HBM, hybrid bonding, and heterogeneous integration architectures.

items.title: Optoelectrical Conditioning in Graphene Quantum Dot‍–‍Vanadium Oxide Artificial Synapse
items.abstract: Neuromorphic computing requires artificial synaptic devices capable of adaptive learning and memory retention. Here, we present a monolithically integrated optoelectronic synaptic device based on a 0D/3D Ag/graphene quantum dot–vanadium oxide (GQD–VO 2 )/Ni heterojunction exhibiting stimulation‐history‐dependent conductance modulation. The device supports synaptic modulation under electrical, optical, and combined optoelectrical stimulation, with enhanced optoelectronic response compared with the bare VO 2 device. Repeated optoelectrical stimulation modifies the retained device state and subsequent potentiation–depression characteristics, a process described here as optoelectrical conditioning. This evolution is evaluated using retained current ( I ), fitted potentiation–depression time constants ( τ ), and nonlinearity coefficients. Wavelength‐dependent optical associative learning with positive and negative reinforcement is further demonstrated under different optical stimuli. Performance evaluation using Fashion‐MNIST and Digit‐MNIST datasets show improved classification accuracy with the progression of optoelectrical conditioning learning cycles, increasing from 81.53% to 84.13% and from 91.71% to 95.58%, respectively. Monte Carlo simulations further indicate improved classification accuracy across multiple runs following repeated learning cycles. Furthermore, this behavior is illustrated through reconstructed Fashion‐MNIST image outputs with the repeated learning cycles. These findings highlight the potential of Ag/GQD–VO 2 /Ni device for neuromorphic applications, advancing AI‐integrated bio‐inspired computing.

items.title: OFDM-Based Neuromorphic Wake-Up Signal
items.abstract: Wake-up radios (WURs) reduce energy consumption by continuously monitoring the channel for a wake-up signal (WUS) while the main receiver remains asleep. Neuromorphic computing offers a promising approach to ultra-low-power WUS detection through sparse, event-driven processing. However, realizing these benefits requires spike-like inputs, which conventional orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms do not naturally provide. To enable neuromorphic WUS detection in OFDM-based systems, we introduce a neuromorphic wake-up signal (nWUS) that can be generated by a standard OFDM transmitter. The proposed design superposes frequency-domain vectors with linear phase progressions across the OFDM subcarriers, producing a time-domain waveform with sparse amplitude peaks at predefined positions. These peaks encode the wake-up signature in a spike-like representation that facilitates neuromorphic processing at the receiver. Building on this structure, we then propose a noncoherent neuromorphic detector that encodes received peaks into spikes and performs sparse correlation only upon spike events. Simulations over a 3GPP urban macro channel show that the proposed approach outperforms on-off keying (OOK) baselines in detection probability while achieving up to 43.5x lower computational cost. During idle periods, event-driven processing further reduces correlation operations by 86% relative to nWUS reception.

items.title: Multifunctional Silicone Hotmelt Materials Integrating Stress Relaxation and Thermal Management for Advanced Electronic
items.abstract: Advanced electronic packaging technologies, including wafer-level packaging (WLP) and panel-level packaging (PLP), increasingly require thinner and larger substrates to support high-throughput manufacturing. At the same time, flexible and foldable electronic devices are rapidly emerging, further increasing the demand for encapsulant and adhesive materials with both high mechanical compliance and effective thermal stress management. Conventional organic-based materials, such as epoxy, acrylic, and urethane resins, are often limited in these applications because their high elastic modulus, typically greater than 1 GPa, tends to generate excessive thermal stress and insufficient flexibility. Silicone materials are attractive candidates because of their inherently low elastic modulus and excellent thermal and chemical stability. However, their relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) has generally limited their use in thin and large-area substrates unless extremely soft gel-type formulations are employed. In this work, a newly developed silicone hotmelt material is presented as a solution to this challenge. Owing to a unique silicone network design, the material provides effective thermal stress dissipation despite a relatively high CTE of approximately 220 ppm/K and an elastic modulus in the range of 10–100 MPa. This silicone hotmelt is available in both film form, referred to as Silicone Hotmelt Film (SHF), and cartridge form, referred to as Silicone Hotmelt Cartridge (SHC), with melt characteristics optimized for film lamination and hot-dispensing processes, respectively. Its rapid thermosetting behavior enables compatibility with high-throughput manufacturing processes for advanced electronic devices. When laminated and cured onto dummy substrates representative of WLP and PLP structures, no measurable warpage was observed, indicating excellent stress relaxation. In addition, reliability testing, including thermal cycling from −40 °C to 150 °C, showed no delamination or cracking in the laminated bodies, demonstrating robust durability under harsh conditions. The material also exhibits adhesion to a broad range of substrates, including cured silicone, fluoropolymers such as ethylene tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE), and precious metals such as gold. This feature enables structural bonding between dissimilar materials with mismatched CTE values. Reliability results obtained from multilayer structures composed of two different substrates and the silicone hotmelt further support its applicability to advanced packaging assemblies. Although silicone materials are generally known for thermal stability over a typical operating range of approximately −50 °C to 200 °C, the newly developed silicone hotmelt exhibited substantially enhanced performance, remaining stable over an extended temperature range from −100 °C to 300 °C. No embrittlement was observed below −50 °C, and strong adhesion was retained even after aging at 300 °C, demonstrating durability beyond that of conventional silicone materials. Furthermore, a thermally conductive version of the silicone hotmelt was developed by integrating thermal management technology into the same material architecture, achieving thermal conductivity of up to 3 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ without substantial loss of mechanical compliance or adhesion. This combination of high thermal stability, stress relaxation, and thermal conductivity makes the material particularly suitable for advanced electronic packaging applications that require both long-term reliability and efficient heat dissipation. Overall, these results indicate that the developed silicone hotmelt materials provide a promising encapsulation and adhesive solution for advanced electronic packaging applications requiring effective thermal stress management, high reliability, and, in some cases, enhanced thermal conductivity, particularly for thin, large-area, and flexible electronic devices.

items.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.abstract: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. We introduce MoI-Bench, a benchmark grounded in mobile user needs, comprising 64 subtasks and 1150 samples. It defines 16 operations, such as removal and replacement, and eight visual target categories covering content such as portraits and text. These form two orthogonal axes whose applicable combinations define specific tasks, such as removing facial makeup. To better guide model improvement, we further propose MoI-Eval, which introduces task-specific criteria covering instruction following, visual quality and detail preservation. We further construct sample-level evaluation questions and aggregate their scores into overall quality and capability profiles along the operation, target and criteria axes. We evaluate representative on-device and server-side models and measure mobile deployment costs. Results show that this decoupled Operation x Target design provides finer-grained guidance for improving compact models. For example, it highlights the need to prioritize specific capability gaps (e.g., text-replacement) over broad application-level goals (e.g., improving text editing). Unlike conventional benchmarks that rank models using a single score, we introduce a two-dimensional Quality-Deployability capability map to assess models for practical mobile use. The map shows that current on-device models can achieve efficient generation or editing but expanding their task coverage deserves greater attention than further improving deployment efficiency. Further progress requires improving editing quality, particularly identity preservation and text rendering, while broadening task coverage.

items.title: Microfluidic Cooling Integrated into Glass Substrates
items.abstract: In this work, 3D Glass Solutions (3DGS) presents an advanced glass-based interposer architecture with embedded single-phase liquid cooling. This combined interposer architecture possesses all the standard building blocks of a typical interposer package, including: top-side flip chip IC, multiple layer electrical redistribution, through glass vias for digital and RF (50Ω) I/Os, and bottom-side BGA for PCB assembly. In addition to these interposer features, the substrate incorporates an in-package integrated microfluidic channel for single-phase liquid cooling. The microfluidic channel structure includes embedded copper pillar structures that enable unique opportunities for thermal transfer enhancement and mechanical channel reinforcement. These channels maintain mechanical stability at an inlet-to-outlet pressure differential of up to 60 psi (414 kPa), supporting volumetric flow rates up to 200 ml/min. This configuration achieves effective heat transfer coefficients ranging from 12.1 to 22 W/ W/cm2⋅K (at 15 and 45 psi, respectively), achieving an approximate device surface temperature of 40 °C under a 300 W/cm2 heat load. Coupled with established 3DGS heterogeneous integration processes, this architecture offers a holistic thermal management solution for advanced packaging systems.

items.title: Material Solutions for AI/HPC Packaging from Wafer Bumping to System Assembly
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a major driving force for advanced semiconductor packaging technologies used in high-performance computing (HPC). Unlike traditional single-chip designs, advanced packaging such as chip on wafer on substrate (CoWoS) allows for heterogeneous integration, combining system on a chip (SoC), graphics processing units (GPUs), and high bandwidth memory (HBM) memory stacks into a single package. However, due to increased package complexity and high-power consumption, AI applications present several challenges from integrated circuit (IC) packaging to system assembly: • Fine-pitch and Micro-bump Packaging: Risks to solder joint integrity and difficulties in residue cleaning for multi-chip configurations. • High Power and Hot Spots: A critical requirement for advanced thermal management. • Large-package Warpage: Significant impact on SMT yield, testing, and system-level thermal interface materials (TIM) application. This work introduces specialized materials designed to overcome these challenges and enable next-generation AI/HPC packaging. Key solutions include high-performance flux materials for micro-bump wafer bumping and chip-on-wafer (CoW) processes. It also highlight mid-temperature solder pastes developed to eliminate head-in-pillow (HiP) and non-wet-open (NWO) defects. Finally, this work present high-performance thermal interface materials designed to significantly enhance the thermal efficiency of HPC chips.

items.title: Low-loss superjunction SiC MOSFET with improved breakdown voltage and reverse-recovery performance
items.abstract: Abstract Conventional silicon carbide (SiC) trench metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) still face challenges such as high body diode forward voltage, and difficulty in balancing static and dynamic performance. To address these issues, a novel split-gate multi-channel superjunction SiC MOSFET with an integrated metal-oxide-semiconductor-channel diode, named as MSM-MOS, is proposed. The electrical characteristics of the proposed device are investigated using technology computer-aided design simulations and compared with those of a conventional trench MOSFET and a superjunction MOSFET with an integrated Schottky barrier diode. The MSM-MOS achieves a breakdown voltage of 2037 V and a specific on-resistance of 0.70 mΩ·cm 2 , showing improved drain-to-source blocking capability in the off-state and on-state conduction performance. In reverse conduction, the MSM-MOS shows a forward voltage of 1.77 V and a low reverse-recovery charge. Consequently, the MSM-MOS achieves the highest Baliga figure of merit of 5.92 GW cm −2 and the lowest dynamic figure of merit of 32.9 mΩ·nC among the three device structures.

items.title: Impact of gate foot height on JFoM and current collapse in double-deck T-gate GaN HEMTs: A simulation study
items.abstract: GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) are key enablers of 5G-advanced and emerging 6G systems, where high power density and high-frequency operation are essential. Double-deck T-gate structures have been proposed to reduce parasitic capacitance and gate resistance; however, the role of individual gate foot heights has not been systematically explored. Previous studies mainly focused on lateral gate dimensions in planar-gate and conventional T-gate structures, while this work extends the analysis to double-deck T-gates by separately investigating the bottom and top gate foot heights. In this study, simulation parameters calibrated from experimental data of fabricated devices are used to investigate the impact of gate foot height on RF performance and device reliability in double-deck T-gate GaN HEMTs. The results demonstrate that the bottom gate foot height (H f1 ) has a more pronounced effect on RF characteristics and electric field distribution than the top gate foot height (H f2 ) because the top gate foot is located closer to the channel than the gate head. Specifically, reducing H f1 redistributes the electric field at the gate edge, leading to an increase in breakdown voltage (V BR ). Consequently, Johnson’s figure of merit (JFoM) is enhanced and current collapse (CC) is mitigated, despite a slight reduction in cutoff frequency. In contrast, RF performance improvements associated with H f2 saturate beyond 250 nm, while maintaining H f2 below this value improves V BR and suppresses CC. The optimized structure (H f1 = 30 nm, H f2 = 100 nm) achieves a 97% increase in JFoM and a 13% reduction in CC relative to the control device (H f1 = 60 nm, H f2 = 250 nm). These results provide practical design guidelines for enhancing the RF performance and reliability of GaN HEMTs and highlight a pathway that complements aggressive lateral scaling.

items.title: High-Temperature Resistant Laser-Release Material for Advanced Packaging Temporary Bonding/Debonding Applications
items.abstract: High‑temperature process steps are becoming increasingly prevalent in advanced packaging as the industry advances toward high‑density 3D architectures. Techniques such as plasma‑enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), hybrid bonding, silver sintering, encapsulant curing, and thermal compression bonding—commonly performed between 250°C and 350°C—introduce significant demands for temporary bonding/debonding (TBDB) materials. These elevated temperatures challenge the thermal stability, mechanical durability, adhesion performance, and cleanability of traditional TBDB materials. To address these challenges, Brewer Science has developed a laser‑release material engineered for high thermal stability and robust process compatibility. The material offers a tunable coating‑thickness range that accommodates diverse topographies and device architectures. Strong adhesion has been demonstrated on silicon, glass, and epoxy‑compound substrates. Its mechanical flexibility effectively minimizes wafer bow and warpage, even in thick‑film applications. When paired with BrewerBOND® C1301-series adhesive materials in a TBDB system, the material maintains structural integrity through processing temperatures up to 350°C without defect formation. The laser-release material provides excellent UV‑laser debond performance at 308 nm, with customizable formulations available for compatibility with 355-nm laser‑debonding tools. In addition, the material serves effectively as a sacrificial layer, enabling straightforward solvent-based cleaning after 350°C thermal treatment and laser‑debond processing. This work will present the material’s design principles, thermal and mechanical properties, debonding and cleaning characteristics, and application-level testing results that simulate high‑temperature manufacturing environments.

items.title: High Density Interconnect Scaling Beyond Organic Substrates Using Glass Cores
items.abstract: The rapidly increasing performance demands of chiplet based AI computing systems require advanced substrate technologies capable of supporting extremely high interconnect densities, low electrical losses, compact form factors, and reliable power delivery. Conventional organic core substrates, while mature and widely used, encounter fundamental geometric, electrical, and dimensional stability limitations when scaled to fine pitch interconnects in the single digit micrometer range. These constraints increasingly hinder their applicability for next generation high bandwidth chiplet architectures. Glass core substrates represent a promising alternative, offering superior dimensional stability, low dielectric loss, and the potential to enable sub micrometer redistribution layers. This work presents key aspects of the process flow for glass core substrate fabrication, including via formation, metallization, and redistribution layer processing. A comparative study is used to identify the threshold at which organic substrates become geometrically and electrically inadequate, necessitating a transition to glass cores for high density designs. In addition, reliability results for copper filled through glass vias (TGVs) are discussed, demonstrating their suitability for high performance packaging applications. To further advance this technology, the recently established Glass Panel Technology Group (GPTG), led by Fraunhofer IZM in collaboration with industrial partners, addresses materials, equipment, and process integration across the entire value chain from glass panel to finished module. First results from this collaborative effort underline the potential of glass core substrates as a key enabler for future chiplet based systems.

items.title: Hardware–Software Co-Design for Reliable and Secure TinyML on Microcontrollers: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Aims: To review how hardware–software co-design can make tiny machine learning (TinyML) on microcontrollers not only efficient but also reliable and secure, to classify existing approaches by design objective and stack layer, and to propose an integrated framework and research agenda for dependable on-device intelligence. Study Design: Narrative (non-systematic) review. Methodology: Peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers, supplemented by a small number of influential preprints, technical reports, standards and one book, were identified from IEEE Xplore, the ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, arXiv and Google Scholar. Studies were included if they addressed machine learning on microcontrollers or reported a reliability or security technique or finding that transfers directly to such devices. The 61 sources retained, published between 1999 and 2026, were classified by design objective (efficiency, reliability, security), layer of the hardware–software stack, platform and type of evidence, and synthesised narratively. Results: Co-design of network architectures, quantisation, kernels, memory scheduling and hardware has made image-, audio- and sensor-based inference feasible within kilobytes of memory and milliwatts of power. However, reliability and security are usually treated as separate afterthoughts. Fault-injection studies show that the impact of soft errors depends strongly on data representation, bit position and layer, and that low-cost measures such as activation range restriction and selective hardening can mitigate many silent data corruptions. However, most of this evidence comes from software fault injection, often on platforms other than microcontrollers. Security studies demonstrate that physical access enables electromagnetic side-channel recovery of model architectures, instruction-skip and bit-flip attacks that alter predictions, and model extraction through query interfaces. Recent laser fault-injection studies on Arm Cortex-M devices have demonstrated practical bit-flip attacks and the extraction of model parameters from flash memory, although under laboratory conditions. Hardware isolation, secure boot, authenticated updates, masking and control-flow protection are available but rarely evaluated together with accuracy, latency and energy. Conclusion: Dependable TinyML requires reliability and security to be treated as first-class design objectives alongside accuracy and efficiency throughout the design, verification, deployment and operation lifecycle. Standardised fault and threat models, benchmarks that report robustness and security costs, and multi-objective co-design tools are the main priorities for future research. Because the evidence is heterogeneous and the review is narrative, these conclusions are indicative and should be confirmed by experimental validation of the proposed framework.
items.venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Reports

items.title: Full Field Dishing Metrology for Hybrid Bonding Process
items.abstract: Hybrid bonding requires tight copper dishing control to ensure both intimate dielectric-to-dielectric contact during bonding and reliable copper-to-copper electrical interconnection after annealing. Existing metrology methods present trade-offs: AFM provides accurate local references but limited throughput and field of view; OCD remains mainly statistical, and classical WLI is affected by transparent layers and material-dependent phase offsets. We introduce FDM™, a machine-learning-assisted optical interferometric method calibrated against AFM, enabling non-contact, full-field copper dishing metrology on heterogeneous hybrid-bonding surfaces for production monitoring.

items.title: Enhancement of switching characteristics in protonic ECRAM through density-controlled ZrO2 electrolyte via low-temperature atomic layer deposition
items.abstract: Proton-based electrochemical random-access memory (H-ECRAM) has attracted attention as a promising emerging memory for neuromorphic computing due to its analog conductance modulation and high energy efficiency. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is attractive due to its excellent conformality and scalability. However, the inherently high density of ALD-grown electrolyte films limits ionic transport, leading to degraded switching performance of H-ECRAM. In this work, we address this issue by engineering the density of ZrO2 electrolytes through low-temperature ALD. By reducing the deposition temperature, the film density is effectively decreased and density-controlled ZrO2 electrolyte exhibits significantly improved ionic mobility. It contributes to a substantial enhancement in switching characteristics, such as larger conductance modulation, an improved on/off ratio, and enhanced weight update linearity. These results show a feasibility that density-controlled ALD electrolyte can offer potential for scalable and high-performance neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Engineering Interfacial Conduction in ALD‐Al 2 O x /STO Bilayer Dielectrics Toward Reliable Gate Dielectric Applications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Combining dielectrics with complementary properties is a widely used strategy for overcoming the trade‐off between achieving a high dielectric response and suppressing leakage current. Freestanding ultrathin SrTiO 3 (FS‐STO), owing to its ultrahigh dielectric constant, is a promising component for bilayer gate stacks when integrated with large‐bandgap Al 2 O x . However, electrically active interfaces can emerge in such heterostructures between nominally insulating dielectric layers, introducing parasitic conduction and electrical instability during transistor operation. In this work, we systematically investigate how the dielectric–dielectric interface‐formation route influences the electrical behavior of Al 2 O x /STO bilayer dielectrics. Heterostructures formed by direct atomic layer deposition (ALD) of Al 2 O x onto STO exhibit a conductive region confined to a finite near‐interfacial depth on the STO side. Closed‐loop electrical measurements further reveal pronounced bias‐history‐dependent conductance, indicating the involvement of a slowly evolving interfacial charge state in addition to any static interfacial carrier contribution. In contrast, mechanically assembled Al 2 O x /FS‐STO stacks strongly suppress this conductive response while retaining the expected dielectric behavior of the bilayer oxide stack, with the Al 2 O x layer providing effective leakage suppression and improved electrical robustness. Monolayer MoS 2 field‐effect transistors (FETs) incorporating a 5 nm Al 2 O x /40 u.c. FS‐STO dielectric exhibit a subthreshold swing as low as 85 mV dec −1 and an effective interfacial trap density of , comparable to devices based on single‐layer dielectrics. These results identify the interface formation route as an important design parameter for multilayer gate dielectrics and demonstrate mechanical assembly as a controlled strategy for suppressing parasitic interfacial conduction.

items.title: Enabling High-Density Power Packaging: Bridge and Fill for Through-Hole Filling in Advanced IC Substrate Core
items.abstract: Through-hole (TH) filling technology has emerged as a pivotal component in high-performance integrated circuit (IC) packaging, effectively addressing the electrical and thermal challenges posed by advanced applications such as artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and data center servers. AI accelerators and HPC modules are driving unprecedented increases in power density, with leading-edge AI devices exceeding 1 kW per package, and server processors routinely dissipating between 400 W and 600 W. These elevated power levels, coupled with increased body sizes reaching 120 x140 mm, emphasize the need for robust vertical interconnects that minimize voltage drop and maintain power integrity under high-current operation in confined spaces. TH fills provide a low-resistance vertical path between the die and substrate, significantly reducing IR drop (voltage drop) – an essential factor as data indicates that even a 10% reduction in voltage drop can yield measurable improvements in computational reliability and energy efficiency. In addition to electrical performance, thermal management remains a critical concern. Next-generation servers are approaching heat fluxes of 150 W/cm², placing immense stress on conventional cooling architectures. TH fills function as efficient thermal conduits, facilitating rapid heat transfer from the die through the substrate and ultimately to the printed circuit board, thereby mitigating hotspots and lowering overall thermal resistance. This capability is vital in AI and HPC deployments, where thermal excursions can limit performance or compromise device lifetime. Furthermore, the compatibility of TH fill with flip-chip assembly and organic substrates supports both the cost and scalability requirements outlined in advanced packaging roadmaps. As packaging technologies evolve toward higher power densities and increased integration, the strategic incorporation of TH filling stands out as an indispensable approach for achieving efficient power delivery and effective heat removal in state-of-the-art electronics. The technical methodology for TH filling involves two sequential stages of acid-copper plating. Initially, a periodic pulse-reverse (PPR) electroplating process establishes a copper bridge near the midpoint of the TH, followed by direct-current (DC) electroplating to complete the fill. This process addresses common challenges such as uneven current distribution. Which, if unmitigated, can result in voids and incomplete fills which are detrimental to HPC and AI reliability. Additive control, electrolyte management, and process optimization, are critical as these factors directly correlate with minimizing surface roughness, dendritic growth, and internal stresses that could otherwise lead to cracking or delamination during thermal cycling in high-power environments. To systematically identify and optimize critical additive parameters affecting void rates and surface copper uniformity, a design of experiment (DOE) will be implemented as part of this study. This investigation evaluates the effectiveness of TH filling through a bridge and fill process applied to panels with challenging thicknesses, representing configurations of advanced server and AI module substrates. The optimized process consistently delivered defect-free THs, with total plated copper thicknesses below 100 μm and surface dimples under 20 μm—metrics aligned with benchmarks for high-reliability interconnects in data center applications. The use of tanks with eductor agitation not only enhances process throughput but also reduces operational complexity and cost, supporting the scale-up requirements for AI and HPC manufacturing. Additionally, the adaptability of this technique to hybrid THs with varying aspect ratios (AR) is examined, demonstrating robust performance and reliability across diverse geometries as demanded by modern server and AI system architectures. In summary, TH fill technology, supported by quantitative literature data, is confirmed as a cornerstone for the power and thermal management challenges inherent to the next generation of high-performance electronic systems.

items.title: Electrostatic shunt RF MEMS switch with a floating electrode for S-band applications: architecture and mathematical modeling
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and modeling of an electrostatically actuated capacitive shunt RF MEMS switch with a floating electrode for S-band operation. The proposed architecture incorporates a mechanically fixed, electrically floating metal electrode positioned above the signal line and separated from it by a high-k TiO2 dielectric layer. This configuration substantially increases the down-state capacitance and improves signal isolation without requiring extremely small interelectrode gaps. The switch is implemented on a coplanar waveguide and uses an aluminum membrane with meander suspensions and perforation to reduce the effective stiffness, actuation voltage, and switching time. The main electromechanical parameters were evaluated analytically and verified by finite element modeling in COMSOL Multiphysics, while the RF performance was analyzed using electromagnetic simulation in ANSYS HFSS. The final design demonstrates a pull-in voltage of 2.7 V, a closing time of 18 μs, a down-state capacitance of 247 pF, and an up-state capacitance of 9.6 fF. In the 2–4 GHz range, the simulated up-state insertion loss is 0.012–0.14 dB, and the down-state isolation is 43.3–89.75 dB. The results show that the floating-electrode architecture provides a high capacitance ratio and significantly enhances the RF performance of the capacitive shunt MEMS switch.

items.title: Domestic Build-Up Film Advancing Fan-Out Wafer-Level Packaging (FOWLP) Through the SHIELD USA Program
items.abstract: Build-up films (BUF) serve as critical dielectric layers in advanced package substrates, where they enable fine pitch interconnects, multilayer redistribution routing, and the high-density integration required for next generation semiconductor devices. These engineered polymeric dielectrics are formulated to achieve a combination of low dielectric constant (Dk) and low dissipation factor (Df), while maintaining excellent thermal, mechanical, and electrical reliability. Key material characteristics such as rheological behavior during lamination, glass transition temperature (Tg), coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE), modulus, and copper adhesion strength must be precisely balanced to ensure robust multilayer stack performance. These properties play essential roles in managing warpage, interfacial integrity, stress distribution, and long-term reliability, particularly as package architectures push toward sub 2 μm line and-space requirements. The properties of Rogers BUF material that is incorporated into the processing of the Fan-Out Wafer-Level Packaging (FOWLP) process led by ASU and Deca through the SHIELD USA (Substrate Heterogeneous Integration Enabling Leadership Demonstration for the USA) program funded under the CHIPS and Science Act will be presented.

items.title: Digital Twin–Ready Underfill Simulation with High-Speed CFD
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of chiplet‑based packaging architectures has significantly increased the number of new package designs reaching production (tape‑out), driving demand for faster, more flexible backend process development. Underfill process optimization, already time‑consuming and costly for single‑die packages, becomes substantially more complex for multi‑die and heterogeneous chiplet designs due to intricate geometries, dense bump patterns, and tight process windows. Traditional trial‑and‑error methods for underfill development are increasingly impractical in high‑mix manufacturing environments. AI-driven automation combined with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) presents a compelling approach to accelerating underfill process development and enabling predictive insight into material behavior. However, conventional CFD tools are often prohibitively slow, expensive, and poorly suited for integration into production workflows. This paper presents a high-speed CFD simulation approach leveraging methods used in porous media flow simulation tailored for underfill processes in advanced chiplet packages, enabling rapid analysis of material flow, void formation risk, and process robustness. The paper introduces key underfill physics and discusses the challenges associated with complex die geometries, nonuniform bump patterns, multi-pass dispense timing, void generation, and external die bridging. A test vehicle is described to validate simulation accuracy. The core of the paper focuses on a high-performance CFD technology (Dive) that significantly reduces simulation runtime while maintaining fidelity, making it practical for both process development and deployment as part of a manufacturing digital twin. Simulation results are correlated with experimental data, demonstrating the technology’s ability to predict critical failure modes and guide process optimization. Finally, the integration of highspeed underfill simulation into production environments is discussed, highlighting its potential to improve time-to-market, reduce development cost, and enhance material and process health monitoring in advanced packaging lines.

items.title: Design optimization of strain distribution and polarization-induced 2DEG formation in III-Nitride/GaN heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) employ polarization-induced two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) formation to achieve high carrier mobility and excellent high-frequency performance. While ferroelectric barriers such as Aluminium Scandium Nitride (AlScN) have demonstrated superior performance compared to conventional AlGaN barriers, limitations including the high cost of scandium, limited availability, structural instability above 30% Sc composition, and challenges associated with metal-organic chemical vapor deposition growth motivate the exploration of alternative materials. In this work, Aluminium Yttrium Nitride (AlYN), Scandium Gallium Nitride (ScGaN), and Gallium Yttrium Nitride (GaYN) are systematically investigated as barrier layers for GaN-based HEMTs. The influence of barrier composition and interlayer engineering on strain, band alignment, and carrier confinement is analyzed. Among the investigated materials, AlYN exhibits the strongest carrier confinement and the highest electron density, reaching approximately 5.93 × 10 13 cm −2 at 14% Y and 5.332 × 10 13 cm −2 at 8% Y composition. The optimum AlYN barrier thickness is found to lie between 8 and 10 nm, and the incorporation of an AlN interlayer increases the electron density from 5.07 × 10 13 cm −2– 5.52 × 10 13 cm −2 . These results identify AlYN as a promising barrier material for next-generation GaN HEMTs, offering high carrier concentration, moderate strain, and enhanced design flexibility compared to existing Sc-based barrier technologies.

items.title: Demonstration of High Output Power (3.75 W/mm) With 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on Sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.
items.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters

items.title: Deep-UV lithographic realization of aperture arrays as etch masks for 3D nanostructures in silicon
items.abstract: Abstract State-of-the-art integrated circuits currently involve multi-layered architectures that rapidly extend towards three-dimensional (3D) semiconductor structures. To overcome out-of-plane alignment issues, we present an original method to employ conventional deep-UV lithography on pre-structured silicon substrates to pattern an etch mask for monolithic 3D nanostructures with N layers using only M = 1 overlay alignment step (instead of M = (N - 1) steps as in layer-by-layer assembly). The target nanostructures studied here consist of arrays of pores that intersect at oblique angles. To this end, we project elliptical apertures on the sidewalls of V-trenches at controllable depths relative to the wafer's top surface. We create V-trenches in Si by hot HF 50% and KOH 25% etching with θ = 54.7° sloping sidewalls. We successfully spin-coat photoresist on the sloping V-trench sidewalls with a thickness between 50 and 800 nm. The photoresist is remarkably homogeneous, better than 4 nm along 2.6μm of the V-trench sidewall. Using a single deep-UV lithography exposure at λ= 193nm (with a 25 mJ/cm 2 dose and a nominal focal plane at 500 nm depth below the Si wafer top-surface) we successfully expose apertures at various depths in the photoresist on sloping sidewall surfaces of the V-trenches. The apertures have diameters between d = 180 nm and 509 nm, to as deep as Z = 1180nm below the wafer surface. We develop an analytical model to successfully describe lithographic exposure on an inclined surface, which allows one to sculpt non-planar aperture arrays on inclined surfaces. In the future, aperture arrays on inclined surfaces may serve as etch masks to create monolithic and controllable 3D nanostructures deep inside silicon with a reduced number of overlay alignment steps, thus increasing the yield and throughput, and reducing costs and use of chemical and material resources.

items.title: Cu intercalation and field-driven filament formation in vertically aligned MoS$_2$ memristors
items.abstract: Vertically-aligned MoS$_2$ films paired with a Cu top electrode have been used as electrochemical metallization cell memristor devices. The memristive switching has been attributed to the formation of conductive filaments, yet their exact structure has remained elusive. Here we carry out a multi-scale computational study of Cu intercalation, clustering, and field-driven dynamics to eventually model the filament formation under operating conditions. We use density-functional theory results to fine-tune a machine learning force field, and the most important physical phenomena are further distilled into multi-particle kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. By exhaustive enumeration of Cu intercalated structures, we find the most stable structure at MoS$_2$Cu$_{0.11}$ composition, with Cu atoms forming a dice lattice between the MoS$_2$ layers. These structures are shown to exhibit metallic character and can thus form conductive filaments under memristor operation. The simulated switching speed and threshold voltage agree well with the available experimental data. Our results give fundamental insights on the device operation mechanism and guidelines for maximizing switching speed and endurance.

items.title: Cost Analysis of 310x310mm Panels for High-Performance Computing Driven by Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Using square or rectangular panels instead of round wafers has been a topic of interest in the microelectronics packaging industry for years. A more recent addition to the discussion is the potential to use panels for advanced packaging applications. This contrasts with earlier panel-level analyses that focused on smaller, basic fan-out packages. Whether evaluating panels for simpler or more complex packages, one primary focus of any panel-level discussion is the potential for cost savings. Previous analysis has been carried out with a focus on traditional fan-out packaging and large panels (600x600mm). At IMAPS Device Packaging this year, the author of this paper also did an analysis of the 310x310mm panel format, with a focus on an advanced fan-out process flow. This abstract proposes a fresh analysis of the 310x310mm formfactor, now with a focus on 300mm round silicon wafers versus square glass panels. Multiple interposer sizes will be evaluated, and yield trade-offs will be included as well. The goal of this paper is to understand the potential cost savings when building complex packages using a 310x310mm glass interposer in place of a 300mm round silicon interposer.

items.title: Computational screening of reconfigurable van der Waals ferroelectric semiconductor heterojunctions for all-in-one optoelectronic devices
items.abstract: Reconfigurable optoelectronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals semiconductor heterojunctions (VSHs) are potential candidates for multifunctional applications in a single device. However, device multifunctionalities highly rely on VSHs with tunable band alignment and band offsets for achieving reconfigurable optoelectronic properties. Herein, we report a new class of 2D VSHs consisting of atomically thin ABP2X6-type ferroelectric (FE) semiconductors for the development of an all-in-one optoelectronic architecture based on high-throughput first-principles calculations and the nonequilibrium Green’s function method. Our results reveal that the polarization coupling of dual FE layers in the VSHs leads to multiple polarization states, allowing a sequential band-alignment evolution. Using CuInP2S6/AuInP2S6 VSHs as a prototype example, we demonstrate the heterojunction with reversible band-alignment transitions and tunable band offsets by modulating the polarization state of dual FE layers. This enables the device to achieve a theoretical tunneling electroresistance ratio (TER) of 106% between the interlayer FE and antiferroelectric (AFE) states at the bias voltage of 1.5 V, as well as positive and negative photoresponses. The FE-polarization-dependent band alignment and photoresponse of the heterojunction device can be used to implement in-sensor broadband convolutional processing for image recognition and reconfigurable optoelectronic logic operations including AND, OR, and XOR. These findings suggest huge potential of 2D FE VSHs for exploiting multifunctional optoelectronic device applications.

items.title: Breaking the Oxide Barrier: Cost-Efficient Plasma De-oxidation of Copper Surfaces for Advanced Hybrid Bonding
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of semiconductor packaging has positioned copper-to-copper (Cu-Cu) hybrid bonding as a critical technology for high-performance interconnects. However, the spontaneous formation of copper oxides (Cu2O and CuO) presents a significant barrier, as these layers inhibit atomic diffusion and degrade electrical performance through interfacial voiding or delamination. This study investigates the efficacy of an Atmospheric-Pressure Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD) plasma process using an H2/N2 gas mixture, characterized by high energy density and uniformity, as a high-throughput deoxidation solution. Utilizing a test vehicle consisting of a 100 nm Ti barrier and a 500 nm Cu film, we demonstrate that plasma-dissociated hydrogen atoms can achieve a maximum reduction depth exceeding 4 nm at a scanning speed of 5 mm/s. Kinetic analysis establishes an inverse relationship between scanning speed and reduction depth, governed by the residence time of hydrogen (H*) radicals and the resulting penetration of the reaction front into the oxide layer. While the process significantly outperforms the industry standard requirement of >2 nm, the study identifies that the rate-limiting factor is not plasma chemistry but the mass transport efficiency of water vapor byproducts. According to Le Chatelier’s Principle, the accumulation of H2O triggers re-oxidation. We conclude that achieving high-volume manufacturing (HVM) stability requires hardware-level optimizations, such as localized exhaust, to lower the partial pressure of H2O and maintain a metallic surface state.

items.title: Bingham Fluid Rheology and a Dimensionless Analysis of Wire Cutting in Fresh Cementitious Filaments
items.abstract: Bingham fluids combine a finite yield stress with an approximately linear post-yield relation between shear stress and shear rate. This compact model is widely used for pastes, slurries, drilling muds, cementitious materials and other viscoplastic media, yet its apparent simplicity conceals the free-boundary problem created by yielded and unyielded regions. This article reviews the constitutive basis of the Bingham model, analytical results for simple flows, and numerical strategies based on regularization, finite elements and the lattice Boltzmann method. The review emphasizes that yield surfaces are stress-defined rather than material interfaces and that regularization parameters must be checked against mesh and time-step sensitivity. A feasible research object is then developed: transverse wire cutting of a freshly extruded cementitious filament. The wire is treated as a translating cylinder in a low-Reynolds-number yield-stress medium. A dimensionless analysis based on the Bingham number separates viscous-dominated, mixed and yield-dominated cutting regimes, while a transparent resistance scale links yield stress, plastic viscosity, wire diameter and cutting speed. The analysis shows why slower cutting does not necessarily minimize resistance when structural rebuilding raises the yield stress. A combined rheometry, force-measurement and regularized-flow simulation protocol is proposed. The Bingham model is suitable as a baseline for process design, but thixotropy, elasticity, wall slip, particle size and fracture must be added when they control the observed cutting response.

items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Adaptive peridynamic neural operators with fracture-aware topology
items.abstract: Predicting fracture in complex engineering systems requires the simultaneous treatment of nonlocal constitutive behaviour, multi-physics loading and multi-scale crack propagation – a combination that no existing framework addresses in a unified, data-driven way. Existing peridynamic neural operators use a fixed horizon that either over-smooths the crack tip or sacrifices the nonlocal bulk response, and none track how a material’s connectivity changes as it fractures. We introduce the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology, which learns bond-level constitutive laws inside a damage-adaptive peridynamic operator, couples a coarse (bulk) and fine (crack-tip) operator through a multi-fidelity mixture and tracks the topology of the fracturing domain through a bond-count invariant, while remaining trainable from simulation or experimental data. Applied to biological soft tissue, ductile metals, polymers, concrete and foams, the adaptive peridynamic neural operator with fracture-aware topology achieves a mean prediction error ≈ 4 . 1 % , against 9 . 0 % for the base peridynamic neural operator and 15 . 8 % for the Fourier neural operator. Five extended physics features (anisotropic horizon, thermomechanical coupling, grain-boundary kernel, learned Paris fatigue law, electro-mechanical coupling) extend the framework to artificial intelligence chip reliability – silicon die cracking, copper pillar fatigue, underfill delamination, through-silicon via (TSV) liner cracking and low-k dielectric fracture – where the full model reaches ≈ 2 . 7 % mean prediction error ( 70 % lower than the base peridynamic neural operator), outperforms the ANSYS cohesive-zone finite element method by 3 . 5 × in accuracy while running 18 × faster and yields three quantitative design rules for bump pitch, low-k material selection and TSV keep-out zones.

items.title: A Study on Performance Comparison and Application Scenarios of PVD, CVD and ALD Thin-Film Deposition Processes
items.abstract: Semiconductor thin films are the core functional structures of microelectronic and optoelectronic devices. The thickness, uniformity, and density of the thin film directly determine the performance, lifespan, and stability of the device. With the continuous miniaturization and three-dimensionalization of semiconductor devices, traditional deposition processes are struggling to meet the high-precision coating requirements of high aspect ratio micro/nano structures. Therefore, precise process selection has become crucial in semiconductor manufacturing. This paper focuses on three mainstream thin film deposition processes: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD), Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD), and Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD). It systematically elucidates the core working principles of these three processes, conducting a horizontal comparison from multiple dimensions, including deposition mechanism, thickness control accuracy, step coverage capability, film quality, and production cost. The paper analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of each process and clarifies the process selection logic in the context of semiconductor device fabrication. Research shows that there is no absolute superiority or inferiority among the three processes, each possesses differentiated application adaptability. PVD is suitable for low-cost planar thin film mass production, CVD balances efficiency and versatility, and ALD dominates the coating of high-end precision micro/nano devices. This paper also summarizes the technical bottlenecks of existing processes and clarifies the industry development trends of low-temperature processing, high-precision low-cost processing, and process integration.

items.title: A Review of Insulation Stress and Partial Dischargein Medium-Frequency Transformers Under Fast Repetitive Voltage Pulses
items.abstract: The use of wide-bandgap power devices in solid-state transformers enables higher switching frequencies and power densities, but it also exposes medium-frequency transformer insulation to fast repetitive voltage pulses. Short rise times, high dv/dt, high repetition frequencies, and harmonic content can produce nonuniform winding voltages, local field enhancement, and partial discharge. This review examines the resulting insulation stress, discharge mechanisms, detection methods, relevant IEC standards, and design approaches. The reviewed studies show that partial discharge inception and insulation lifetime depend on voltage amplitude, rise time, repetition frequency, polarity, temperature, and residual charge. They also show that power-frequency test results cannot be transferred directly to pulse-width modulation service. Reliable insulation assessment therefore requires complete waveform reporting, interference-resistant sensing, and product-specific test procedures. The resulting evidence should then guide an insulation design that combines electric-field control and thermal management while accounting for parasitic parameters and manufacturing tolerances. Future work should establish common test waveforms and relate discharge activity to long-term material damage under representative operating duty.

items.title: A Combined Atmospheric Argon Plasma and In-Situ Formic Acid Vapor Fluxless TCB Process for Advanced Packaging
items.abstract: This work investigates the fundamental interactions of both formic acid (FA) vapor and atmospheric plasma with Sn metal and its oxides (SnO and SnO₂) and compares their performance in fluxless TCB. Plasma-only processing was found to risk void formation and incomplete oxide removal due to its highly directional nature and sensitivity to exposure conditions. Prior work has shown that FA-related contamination strongly depends on initial oxide thickness, with thick SnO₂ layers requiring elevated temperatures or extended exposure times. Building on these insights, we introduce a combined process that applies atmospheric plasma followed by in-situ FA vapor exposure. Plasma pre-treatment effectively thins or disrupts the hard SnO₂ surface layer, enabling efficient reduction of residual oxides by FA while minimizing contamination. This synergistic approach overcomes the limitations of each individual method, improves bond quality, increases yield and throughput, and significantly reduces by-product formation without requiring aggressive over-exposure conditions.

items.title: WorldPager: Zero-Stall Tiered Memory for Long-Horizon World Models on a Single Consumer GPU
items.abstract: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. On a single consumer machine (one RTX 4090, 32 GiB of host memory, one NVMe SSD), long sessions with such memory hit two walls. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes. We show that this memory is capacity-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and that its access set is known before compute, because the camera pose is an input. An analytical model built on these observations predicts spill points to within one chunk and classifies zero versus non-zero stalls correctly on held-out configurations. Guided by it, WorldPager stores int4 KV in a GPU/DRAM/NVMe hierarchy instead of recomputing it, prefetches each chunk's memory from the extrapolated pose, never waits on a miss, and writes back in the background; to our knowledge, it is the first to place the KV memory of an interactive world model on an NVMe tier with zero-stall prefetching. With training-free position handling, it generates 37.5 minutes of video continuously with zero stalls and constant host memory, at about 9.5 frames per second. On a sealed test set, int4 storage shows no measurable quality loss; on long-gap revisits it lowers image quality by about one MUSIQ point.

items.title: The Substrate is the PCB: A Packaging Architecture for Vertical Power Delivery in Multi-Kilowatt AI Processors
items.abstract: For multi-kilowatt AI processors, the package—not the transistor—has become the dominant constraint on power delivery. At 1 kW and a 0.7 V supply, 1,400 A must traverse the full interconnect stack, while electromigration limits each ~100 μm C4 bump to roughly 1 A, forcing 3,500–5,000 bumps onto the power and ground nets and into direct contention with high-density signal escape. As we continue the power trajectory into the multi-kilowatt regime, we argue that the resolution is a directional reorganization of the package: power and heat flow vertically through the stack while high-bandwidth signal flows horizontally to the perimeter, so that the C4 array is dedicated to signal and all high-current regulation is absorbed into the substrate. In this architecture the substrate takes on the traditional role of the printed circuit board. We analyze the packaging consequences: substrate-material selection (organic, glass, SiC, and diamond add-on layers) against four conflicting requirements; hot-spot-driven specification of the embedded inductor and power-delivery network (PDN) (6–10 A/mm²); and the assembly and known-good-die (KGD) reliability of embedding active and passive components. An embedded Package-Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR) reduces PDN droop from ~150 mV to under 40 mV; we identify inductor current density as one of the most challenging technology risks.

items.title: Switching Losses and Their Mitigation in Lateral β -Ga 2 O 3 Power MOSFETs With High-Permittivity Dielectric for Field Management
items.abstract: Ultrawide-bandgap beta-phase gallium oxide ($\beta $-Ga2O${}_{{3}}\text {)}$is promising for high-voltage, low-loss power devices. Field management in$\beta $-Ga2O3transistors using a high-permittivity (high-${k}\text {)}$dielectric can improve the devices’ power figure of merit (PFOM), but the increased drain-to-gate feedback capacitance degrades switching performance. This article reports on a simulation study of the switching losses and their mitigation in a 3.3-kV normally-offlateral$\beta $-Ga2O3MOSFET with high-$k$field management. A source-connected field plate (sFP) is proposed to mitigate the switching losses while maintaining the device’s blocking capability. Under the switching condition of 3.3 kV/20 A, the fall time and rise time are reduced by approximately 61% and 85%, respectively. The associated turn-off and turn-on losses decrease by approximately 63% and 51%, respectively. Meanwhile, the sFP can shield the gate from a high drain bias and improve gate stability. The effect of the sFP in mitigating switching losses is more effective at higher load currents, indicating that the proposed strategy is suitable for high-load switching scenarios. These findings provide guiding principles for the design of lateral$\beta $-Ga2O3MOSFETs to meet switching requirements in power electronics.

items.title: Sustainable Ambient-Air Cu-Cu Wedge Bonding via Cu-Selective Ultrathin Passivation
items.abstract: Despite advances in 2.5D and 3D packaging, wire bonding remains the most widely used interconnection method in the semiconductor industry. Direct copper-to-copper (Cu-Cu) wedge bonding is highly valued in IC packaging due to its excellent electrical and thermal properties and lower material cost compared to gold (Au). However, its industrial use is limited because bare Cu surfaces oxidize rapidly at typical assembly temperatures (198-200 °C), forming a native Cu oxide barrier that causes widespread non-stick-on-lead (NSOL) failures. Traditional solutions involve expensive silver (Ag) finishes or a reducing forming-gas atmosphere (95% N2, 5% H2), both of which increase cost, complexity, and environmental concerns. This study presents a sustainable, precious-metal-free, and forming-gas-free alternative by applying an ultrathin (12-20 nm) Cu-selective passivation layer as a thermal shield during wire bonding. Building on previous passivation studies focused on bimetallic systems such as aluminum (Al) and palladium-coated copper (PCC) wires, this work investigates true monometallic Cu-Cu wedge bonding using 33μm bare Cu wire. The non-passivated Cu leadframe showed 100% failure at lower bonding power [220-230 Ultrasonic Power (US)], with inconsistent adhesion and high pull-strength variability at higher power ranges. In contrast, the passivated leadframe achieved consistent bonding yield across all power levels, with stable pull strength of 3.0-5.0 gf at 220-230 US, 2.0-6.0 gf at 300 US, and 3.0-6.0 gf at 400 US. Post-bonding analysis confirmed the passivation remained chemically stable at 200 °C for 10 minutes, suppressing 60-70% of Cu-oxide growth. Post-pull test failure analysis further confirmed the mechanical integrity of the Cu-Cu interface, with failures primarily occurring as cohesive wire-neck breaks while the second wedge bond remained intact. These results demonstrate a scalable and eco-friendly alternative to traditional Ag-plated leadframes and costly PCC wires, aligning metallurgical reliability with environmental sustainability for next-generation microelectronics packaging.

items.title: SpikePID: Real-Time Neuromorphic Cluster Counting in Future Drift Chambers
items.abstract: Cluster counting ($dN/dx$) measures discrete ionization occurrences along a charged particle track traversing a gaseous medium and is currently being proposed to serve particle identification (PID) in next-generation drift chambers, as it is expected to offer higher separation power than the traditional approach based on the ionization energy loss measurement ($dE/dx$), which has intrinsically larger statistical fluctuations. However, measuring $dN/dx$ in drift chambers proposed for future colliders requires high-resolution waveforms, which result in very large data rates. Running the reconstruction at the edge would drastically reduce the bandwidth required to transmit data off the detector. In this paper, we introduce SpikePID, a neuromorphic computing approach applying spiking neural networks (SNNs) to this task due to their inherently sparse computing and processing nature. We show that an SNN with only 529 parameters improves the kaon-pion separation power by 17% over the traditional derivative-based method and by 4% over an MLP that has $8.6\times$ more parameters. When synthesized to an FPGA, it uses an order of magnitude fewer resources than the MLP, and has an inference latency compatible with the constraints of future collider experiments, making the SNN an excellent algorithmic candidate for real-time data readout in future drift chambers.

items.title: Spatially resolved heavy ion microprobe testing of lateral Ga2O3 MOSFETs
items.abstract: Ultrawide bandgap β-Ga2O3 has been intensively researched for power electronics applications after the first demonstration of high quality MOSFETs and MESFETs in 2012. Testing of β-Ga2O3 transistor structures under heavy ion irradiation is relatively unexplored despite its criticality in developing next-generation radiation-hardened electronics for space applications. Single ion irradiation was performed with 192 MeV Ar and 1182 MeV Au and a lateral spatial resolution of ∼0.5 μm to map the electrical characteristics of β-Ga2O3 MOSFETs as a function of irradiation position and identify the most sensitive regions of the device. This work determines that standard Ga2O3 MOSFETs are not susceptible to single event burnout under in operando irradiation under an applied field of 0.83 MV/cm for Ar irradiation as well as an applied field of 0.07 MV/cm for Au irradiation. Successive irradiations reveal transient increases in drain current associated with threshold voltage shifts attributed to defect generation/ionization in the top atomic layer deposited-Al2O3 dielectric or the semi-insulating Ga2O3 substrate and subsequent thermal relaxation. Fitting in situ transfer curve data reveals that the dominant effect under heavy ion irradiation is the activation of the parasitic channel via the generation of net positive charge at the buffer–substrate interface.

items.title: Research on the Development Status and Patent Competition Situation of Advanced Wafer-level Packaging-Empirical Analysis based on Patents Worldwide
items.abstract: From the perspective of patents, this article analyzes the development trend of wafer-level advanced packaging, points out the direction for technology research and development of innovative subjects, and provides a reference for enterprises to formulate development strategies. This study uses patent information analysis as the core research method to systematically reveal the technological evolution trajectory and competitive situation in this field. The data retrieval in this study adopts the method of "retrieval validation analysis reasons continuation retrieval validation", which is repeated to achieve the retrieval goal, and the retrieval results are manually denoised to obtain the analysis dataset. Research has found that the number of patent applications in the field of wafer-level advanced packaging worldwide has shown a phased increase, and China has become the main technology source country and layout region. From the perspective of technology distribution, packaging structure is the focus of research and development, with bump technology and fan-out packaging process dominating. The main competitors in the industry are enterprises, and Chinese enterprises have significantly enhanced their competitiveness through mergers and acquisitions and international layout. This article provides a review of the development of wafer-level packaging technology from a patent perspective, providing certain support for innovative entities to grasp the technological situation and competition. How to combine patents and papers for analysis in order to draw more valuable conclusions is a question worth exploring. Based on the research results, this article proposes suggestions from the perspectives of core technology research, regional coordinated development, expanding overseas markets, and strengthening industry-university cooperation, providing a reference for policy formulation and corporate strategy.
