items.title: Reliable Ru‐Based CBRAM Synapses for Energy‐Efficient Neuromorphic Computing: Suppressing Filament Overgrowth and Read Noise via Ru‐Pt Alloy and AlO x Engineering
items.abstract: Transition metal‐based conductive‐bridge RAM offers superior non‐volatility and stable low‐resistance states in the MΩ resistance range compared to noble metal (Ag, Cu) counterparts; however, achieving stable multi‐level operation with low read noise under low‐current conditions remains a critical challenge. This study reports a dual‐material engineering strategy altering filament transport by combining a Ru–Pt alloy electrode with an AlO x switching layer. Pt incorporation suppresses excessive Ru ion injection, while the low‐defect‐density AlO x matrix stabilizes filament evolution, leading to a nanocluster‐based conductive pathway rather than a continuous metallic filament. Temperature‐dependent electrical measurements reveal thermally activated hopping conduction (Ea ∼0.44 eV), and current–voltage analysis indicates hopping distances of 1.0–1.9 nm across resistance states, confirming gradual inter‐cluster spacing modulation. This filament structure enables 16 distinct conductance states with reduced read noise over TaO x ‐ and HfO x ‐based devices. Incorporated into a convolutional spiking neural network framework, the device achieves 80.97% FMNIST inference accuracy (post‐training quantization only) and ultralow inference energy of 0.817 pJ/inference in the FC layer—roughly three orders of magnitude lower than Ag‐ and Cu‐based ECM systems. These results establish a direct link between materials design, filament physics, and system‐level performance, highlighting dual‐material engineering as a pathway toward energy‐efficient, high‐density analog synaptic devices.

items.title: Random telegraph noise and excess leakage current due to extended defects in GaN pn and p–i–n diodes on Si substrate
items.abstract: Mechanisms of excess leakage current (ELC) and random telegraph noise (RTN) fluctuations are investigated in p-GaN/n-Al0.03Ga0.97N (pn) and p-GaN/i-Al0.2Ga0.8N/n-Al0.03Ga0.97N (p–i–n) diode devices on Si substrates. RTN at both bias polarizations is observed in devices exhibiting reverse ELC associated with localized light emission spots due to extended defect (ED). Analysis of RTN amplitude and mean pulse widths as a function of bias indicates that RTN is due to fluctuations in ELC. The RTN shows large relative amplitude up to 30% at room temperature and 50% at 78 K. In addition, a weak temperature dependence of ELC is observed at reverse bias, which indicates that the ELC flows through a narrow constriction with a high electric field at ED. Impurity segregation and strain-induced bandgap reduction at a dislocation are considered to be the origin of the constriction. The observed forward bias dependence of RTN mean pulse widths is explained in terms of capture and/or emission events on an RTN-controlling defect which is located in the constriction. An RTN model for p–i–n diodes is proposed, which relates the experimental data to the spatial positions of recombination centers and the RTN-controlling defect.

items.title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
items.abstract: Defect engineering of memristive materials offers a powerful strategy for regulating ionic transport and analog resistive switching required for neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a wet chemical synthesis route for chloride-vacancy (VCl) engineering in lead-free all-inorganic KCuCl3-x thin films and establish a direct correlation between defect concentration, electronic structure, transport dynamics, and neuromorphic performance. Controlled precursor-ratio variation systematically tunes the VCl concentration in KCuCl3-x thin films, driving preferential vacancy formation at the terminal chloride sites, band-gap narrowing, and enhanced electronic disorder. W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristors exhibit stable bipolar VCM-type resistive switching, with increasing VCl concentration promoting forming-free operation. An optimal VCl concentration (~ 1.3*10^21 cm^-3) provides a balance between ionic mobility and defect controllability, resulting in highly linear potentiation/depression characteristics and superior pulse endurance (>104 cycles). When the experimentally measured conductance characteristics of the optimized memristor are implemented as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations, recognition accuracies of 98.96% and 91.82% are achieved on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, respectively. These findings establish precursor ratio-controlled VCl engineering as an effective strategy for simultaneously optimizing ionic transport, analog switching, and neuromorphic learning in lead-free halide perovskite memristors, providing a general materials design principle for energy-efficient neuromorphic electronics.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing and Its Applications in Decision Making
items.abstract: The proposed review combines an analysis of event-driven encoding, spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and reward-modulated learning rules with a discussion of how these mechanisms translate into real-time, low-power decision-making pipelines for robotics, autonomous navigation, and financial signal processing. A simulated spiking decision-network is described and evaluated on benchmark event-based datasets, comparing its accuracy, latency, and energy consumption against conventional artificial neural network (ANN) baselines. The results indicate that neuromorphic decision-making systems can achieve competitive accuracy while consuming substantially less energy and responding with lower latency, making them attractive for edge and real-time autonomous applications.

items.title: Negative-capacitance germanium-on-AlAs nanosheet FETs for ultra-low-power logic applications
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents the design and circuit-level evaluation of a lattice-matched germanium (Ge)-on-AlAs nanosheet field-effect transistor (NSFET) architecture incorporating a negative-capacitance (NC) gate stack for ultra-low-power logic applications. A calibrated Ge NSFET baseline was first established, followed by systematic optimization of nanosheet geometry, aspect ratio (scaled from 1 to 1/3), and sheet count (from 1 to 3) to maximize the I ON / I OFF ratio to 8.6 × 10 4 at a supply voltage of V DD = 0.5 V. Integration of a ferroelectric Hf 0.67 Zr 0.33 O 2 layer into the gate stack enabled marginal subthreshold slope reduction but increased I ON / I OFF to 1.1 × 10 5 for the n-NSFET at an aspect ratio of 1/3, while improving electrostatic control and maintaining a threshold voltage of 0.25 V, as well as a drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) of 40.5mV V − 1 and 43.0mV V − 1 , between the p-type and n-type devices, respectively, through dual work function engineering. The resulting NC-NSFETs were used to construct a complementary CMOS inverter, which demonstrated full rail-to-rail output swing, a sharp voltage transfer characteristic, and a logic threshold of ∼ 0.27 V. Transient simulations revealed a significant improvement in switching speed from 40 fs to 19 fs, particularly in the pull-down transition, confirming that the NC effect provides measurable benefits at both the device and circuit levels. These results establish the Ge NC-NSFET platform as a promising candidate for future ultra-low-power logic technologies.

items.title: Near-Data Processing in CHORYS
items.abstract: Data-intensive applications in the cloud are expected to service an ever-increasing number of users and handle exponentially growing volumes of data. Meeting these expectations is a challenge because they require balanced performance across the full memory hierarchy, from processor caches to disks accessed over the network. The problem is compounded by the cloud’s shift toward disaggregated architectures, where memory and storage are pooled across fabrics, thus lengthening the data path. CHORYS addresses this challenge through near-data processing with open, programmable accelerators embedded in storage and network devices. CHORYS considers an accelerator-based cloud model in which Solid State Drives (SSDs) and Network Interface Cards (NICs) execute data-intensive operations such as filtering, aggregation, and parsing directly on the data path, thus reducing latency, energy consumption, and resource usage. The project contributes both hardware platforms (OpenSSD‑V and OpenNIC‑V, built around RISC‑V cores) and a software stack including data-intensive pattern libraries, APIs, and runtime systems for the seamless integration of near-data execution into existing cloud infrastructures. CHORYS use cases illustrate near-data processing in the context of data lakes, object stores, and AI inference pipelines.

items.title: Low-Power High-Speed Sense-Amplifier- Based Flipflops with Conditional Bridging Using Tanner Eda.
items.abstract: One of the major challenges in modern VLSI design is power consumption, right up there with space and performance. Digital systems rely on the flip-flop. In sub-threshold operation, we examine and contrast four different flip-flop topologies: IP-DCO, MHLFF, CPSFF, and CPFF. Both pulse-triggered and conditional approaches are included in these topologies. Very low power consumption applications are now within reach, thanks to sub threshold technology. One advantage of this technique is that it decreases the number of power-hungry flip-flops. Compared to a strong inversion circuit, a subthreshold circuit consumes less power while running at the same frequency. Tanner uses 18nm technology in cmos for design. We test the flip-flops' power delay, power delay product, and average power at a 1V power supply voltage and look at them from every perspective. Keywords: Sub Threshold Technology, Flip Flop, Low Power.
items.venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management

items.title: Investigation on the Impact of Memristive Device Variability on Uncoupled Memristive Cellular Nonlinear Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional von Neumann architectures suffer from an inherent bottleneck arising from the physical separation of memory and processing units, motivating alternative bio‐inspired computing paradigms. Cellular nonlinear networks (CellNNs) offer one such alternative, but implementations that rely on von Neumann‐style processors inherit the memory bottleneck. The integration of memristive devices into CellNN implementations can mitigate this bottleneck, enabling in‐memory computation with volatile and non‐volatile storage, and enhanced cell dynamics. In this work, an uncoupled Memristive CellNN (M‐CellNN) breadboard cell is physically implemented, and the device‐to‐device (D2D) variability of five nominally identical Pt///Ti/Pt (HOTO) VCM devices is experimentally characterized. These measurements calibrate variability‐aware SPICE‐level simulations of a M‐CellNN array implementing EDGE detection. A pixel‐level EDGE detection accuracy of 100% is demonstrated across five input images, with all true edge pixels correctly identified and no spurious detections, under D2D variability conditions calibrated from experimental data. Since cells operate independently, errors remain spatially isolated and do not cascade across the array. Furthermore, 100% accuracy is maintained under global passive component deviation of 20% and realistic local component mismatch of 2%, with the worst‐case robustness boundary located at 4% mismatch for the most demanding image, confirming suitability for monolithic hardware integration.

items.title: Investigation of hysteresis and polarization mechanism in top-gated aligned carbon nanotube FETs
items.abstract: The transfer characteristics and hysteresis of top-gated aligned carbon nanotube field-effect transistors are systematically investigated using a series of fast gate pulse schemes. The devices exhibit clockwise hysteresis accompanied by polarization-modulated charge transport. Controlled-environment experiments reveal that the clockwise hysteresis window is modulated by vacuum pumping, humidity variation, and nitrogen purging and can be restored upon returning to the original ambient conditions. As the fast gate sweep duration decreases, the hysteresis evolves from clockwise to counterclockwise, a signature of charge trapping effects. The underlying mechanism is ascribed to the coexistence of water molecular polarization and charge trapping within the device. By tuning the amplitude and duration of gate voltage pulses, we identify voltage- and time-dependent regimes dominated by either polarization or charge-trapping processes. These findings are further validated by current transient analysis upon the application and removal of tailored poling or trapping gate pulses.

items.title: Impact of oxidation conditions in SiO2 atomic layer deposition on interface state densities at β -Ga2O3 (001) MOS interfaces with 600 °C post-deposition annealing
items.abstract: We investigated the impact of SiO2 film deposition conditions in either thermal or plasma-enhanced atomic layer depositions (ALDs) on the interface characteristics of β-Ga2O3 metal–oxide–semiconductor (MOS) capacitors, especially focusing on oxidation reaction conditions in ALD. The formation of the interface with an interface state density as low as ∼1011 eV−1 cm−2 at 0.2 eV below the conduction band edge and a low near-interface oxide trap density was achieved by tuning the O3-dose in thermal-ALD, with a post-deposition-annealing temperature limited to a relatively low temperature of 600 °C to avoid the thermally induced damages on Ga2O3. The fixed charge density at the SiO2/β-Ga2O3 interface was also minimized by thermal-ALD with the sufficient dose of O3. These results demonstrate the significant role of the control of SiO2 deposition conditions to achieve high-quality SiO2/β-Ga2O3 MOS interfaces with low-thermal-budget processes.

items.title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
items.abstract: Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric-semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic-inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure-property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

items.title: High Frequency Power Cycling of Three-Phase Inverters for Aircraft Applications
items.abstract: Accurate thermal cycle measurement is essential for estimating the lifetime of power modules, particularly those employing SiC MOSFETs characterized by extremely low thermal capacitance. This work presents a rigorous method for estimating the die temperature variation of SiC components within power modules utilized in three-phase inverters. The approach leverages high-speed thermal imaging to accurately characterize the individual thermal impedance of each die. The resulting thermal impedance model is coupled with high-fidelity loss calculations to predict dynamic SiC die temperatures during inverter operation. Experimental results obtained under conditions representative of a 540 V / 7.5 kW aeronautical inverter demonstrate the model's accuracy in tracking dynamic SiC die temperature variations.

items.title: FrontGI: Architecture-Aware Parallel GNN Inference on Chiplet-Based Multicore Systems
items.abstract: The realm of high-performance computing has expanded to include machine learning tasks of many forms. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are becoming increasingly popular, with their applications expanding across diverse domains. As the scale of graph data continues to grow, including larger numbers of nodes, edges, and higher embedding dimensions, standardized libraries such as DGL and PyG have been developed to facilitate GNN computation. These libraries allow the computation to be described a a high level of abstraction, providing high productivity on the part of the developer. However, with the rapid increase in the number of processor cores and the evolution of multicore architectures, these libraries often show poor scalability and fail to execute GNN inference efficiently on the latest multicore systems, particularly those with upwards of a hundred cores. To address this limitation, we introduce FrontGI, a fast and scalable set of techniques that advances the frontier of GNN inference on large-scale graphs (over 100,000 vertices) by leveraging graph-property- and architecture-aware design. FrontGI employs different parallelization strategies optimized for diverse graph structures, maximizing the utilization of multi-level cache hierarchies in multicore systems. We evaluate a number of GNN models with FrontGI on a 128-core AMD EPYC system. Compared to state-of-the-art libraries, FrontGI achieves up to 3.35$\times$, 3.20$\times$, 2.89$\times$ and 3.10$\times$ speedups over DGL for GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, and SGC models, respectively, and even greater improvements over PyG, across a range of large-scale, high-dimensional graph datasets with diverse structural properties.

items.title: Enabling Low-Temperature Cu-to-Cu Direct Bonding via Nanocrystalline Cu and Cu-Selective Oxide Suppression Coating
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and data-centric technologies is driving demand for interconnects with ultra-high density, low resistance, and superior reliability. While Cu-to-Cu direct bonding offers significant advantages over conventional Cu-to-solder interconnects, including ultra-fine pitch capability, lower electrical resistance, and improved thermal performance, its widespread adoption remains limited by the rapid oxidation of Cu surfaces under ambient conditions. Native Cu oxides act as diffusion barriers, requiring elevated bonding temperatures and pressures that increase wafer warpage, thermal stress, and process complexity. Nanocrystalline Cu (NC-Cu) has emerged as a promising approach for low-temperature Cu-to-Cu bonding due to its high grain boundary density, which enhances atomic diffusivity and promotes interfacial bonding at reduced temperatures. However, the increased surface area and high-energy grain boundaries of NC-Cu also accelerate oxidation, diminishing its bonding advantages. To address this challenge, we present a dual-strategy approach that combines controlled NC-Cu growth with an ultra-thin Cu-selective passivation coating. NC-Cu with a grain size of 80 nm and a surface roughness of 4.7 nm was engineered to facilitate rapid low-temperature bonding. A conformal 5 nm Cu-selective passivation coating was subsequently applied to suppress oxidation while preserving Cu atomic diffusion. The Cu-selective passivation coating was deposited using a liquid-phase deposition (LPD) process. The coating thickness and composition were optimized and monitored using attenuated total reflectance infrared (ATR-IR) spectroscopy. The passivation layer reduced oxide formation by ~ 85% at 200 °C without introducing measurable interfacial resistance. Combined with enhanced grain boundary diffusion, this approach enables oxidation-resistant, low-temperature Cu-to-Cu bonding under ambient conditions, providing a scalable and cost-effective pathway for next-generation heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging technologies.

items.title: Electrothermal parameter identification from DC I-V data for compact drain-current models of GaN-on-SiC RF HEMTs: a comparative metaheuristic study
items.abstract: Accurate electrothermal parameter extraction is essential for compact modeling of gallium nitride on silicon carbide (GaN-on-SiC) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) used in radio-frequency (RF) and high-power circuits. This study compares four published compact drain-current formulations: the Fager–Pedro LDMOS model, the Yang model, the Curtice cubic model, and the Cao enhanced EEHEMT model. We fitted each formulation to room-temperature, on-wafer direct-current (DC) current–voltage (I–V) measurements from devices with total gate peripheries of 1, 2, and 4 mm. We used African vulture optimization, Multi-trial differential evolution (MTDE), the Enzyme action optimizer, and the Equilibrium Optimizer (EO) to extract the electrical and effective thermal parameters. We evaluated each result using mean squared error (MSE) and physical-plausibility checks, including the expected decrease in effective thermal resistance with increasing device periphery. The Fager–Pedro model produced the lowest errors for the 1 and 4 mm devices, whereas the Cao enhanced EEHEMT model gave the best result for the 2 mm device. The Curtice cubic model generally represented the largest device more accurately than the Yang model. EO gave the lowest runtime in the benchmark test, while MTDE achieved the minimum fitting error in most cases, although the optimizers used different computational budgets. These results provide a comparative workflow for selecting drain-current formulations and parameter-extraction strategies for GaN-on-SiC HEMTs. The conclusions are limited to room-temperature, steady-state DC measurements and require validation under pulsed, transient, and large-signal RF conditions.

items.title: Electric-field redistribution via high- k dielectric trench in GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: We report a GaN-on-Si AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) incorporating a drain-side Pb(Zr,Ti)O3 (PZT) trench for electrostatic field management. The mechanism is formulated using the displacement-field boundary conditions and evaluated by two-dimensional technology computer aided design with a field-independent relative-permittivity sweep from 3.9 to 500. The calculations reveal the nonmonotonic dependence of terminal voltage on permittivity and a broader drain-side high-field distribution for the nominal εr=300 case. Experimentally, a representative PZT-trench HEMT reaches 1405 V at LGD=9 μm, compared with 783 V for a co-fabricated conventional device and 957 V for a previously reported hybrid Schottky–ohmic drain HEMT, corresponding to breakdown-voltage improvements of 79% and 47%, respectively, while retaining a specific ON-resistance of 1.47 mΩ cm2. The dynamic-to-static ON-resistance ratios, RON,dyn/RON,static, are 1.6× and 2.5× after 900 and 1200 V off-state stress, respectively, at a 3 μs extraction delay. These results demonstrate simultaneous enhancement of voltage handling and dynamic performance through drain-side dielectric-boundary engineering.

items.title: Don't Read Every Cell: Few-Read Fault Localization and Drift Calibration in Analog Crossbars
items.abstract: Deployed analog in-memory chips silently lose cells, and the default fix, reading every cell, costs 256 reads for a 256×256 tile. We show that a few random probe reads are enough. A sparse-recovery decoder over random ±1 probes localizes up to 64 stuck cells in a 256×256 tile with 4 to 12 counted reads at 1% read noise, on a simulated tile that is otherwise ideal. For k ≥ 4 faults it needs 4.3 to 6.4× fewer reads than a hybrid that we built from a published multi-outlier code (1.9 to 3.2× if its 8 noise-calibration reads are charged), and at least 2× fewer than tuned X-ABFT, which in this regime needs more reads than a full readout. The sharper finding is where the gain comes from: the decoder, not the second read direction. Forward reads alone already need 1.6 to 4.1× fewer reads than the hybrid; joint decoding with transposed reads needs a further 1.3 to 4× fewer at 1% noise, and gains less at higher noise. For drift, a 16-parameter field fitted per tile from a few probe reads restores programmed accuracy. As a digital correction that needs the stored weights, it gains +2.1 to +13.3 points over the best cheap digital baseline on CIFAR-10 from 1 h to 1 yr (+1.7 to +13.1 points with the 17 MVMs actually run); applied in the array, it keeps +0.6 to +3.7 points. Every claim is graded against criteria committed before the counted runs, and all code, data and pre-specified criteria are public.

items.title: Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor-Compatible Phototransistor Platform for Neuromorphic Broadband Vision
items.abstract: Photodetection and neuromorphic computing promises sensing at the edge, yet most optoelectronic synapses lack spectral breadth or scalable silicon integration. Here we report a dual-gate synaptic transistor integrating colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) with a silicon-on-insulator (SOI) channel in a complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible platform. This architecture synergistically combines the SOI channel for efficient charge transport and signal amplification with the CQD layer serving a dual role as a broadband absorber (300–1700 nm) and a charge-trap medium. The device exhibits a responsivity of 639 A W–1 and specific detectivity exceeding 3 × 1012 Jones at 1550 nm, parallelly emulating short- and long-term plasticity, multilevel conductance tuning, and highly programmable synaptic dynamics. The top gate enables reversible potentiation and depression, and self-powered operation supports low-power sensing and light-driven learning. We demonstrate system-level utility in a synaptic array that achieves pattern recognition with peak accuracy exceeding 96%, establishing a pathway to silicon-integrated, energy-efficient neuromorphic vision.

items.title: Chip-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding using Polyimide Dielectric for Low-Temperature Process with High Yield and Reliability
items.abstract: Low-temperature processable dielectric polyimides (PIs) materials have been developed for chip-to-wafer (C2W) hybrid bonding. By using dielectric PIs materials during low-temperature PI-to-PI bonding test, higher bond strength was confirmed by shear test. Furthermore, C2W PI-PI/Cu-Cu hybrid bonding has been demonstrated with low-temperature process. In this paper, PI-SiO2/Cu-Cu hybrid bonding has been also investigated. For this investigation, a test vehicle was designed to have chips with PI dielectric and Cu pads, which were designed to be bonded on a 12-inch silicon wafer with SiO2 dielectric and Cu pads for daisy chain test. As a result of measuring resistance of the daisy chain after hybrid bonding, electrical continuity was confirmed for all chips. Furthermore, both pressure cooker test (PCT) and thermal cycling test (TCT) were conducted, and in each case, electrical continuity was maintained to confirm excellent reliability.

items.title: Characterizing the Impact of In-Plane Deformation in Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding from Die Warpage and Bonder Shape Effects
items.abstract: The increasing demand for high-performance computing and artificial intelligence is accelerating the adoption of advanced packaging technologies capable of supporting a higher number of interconnects with reduced pitch. Die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding has emerged as an important enabler for next-generation heterogeneous integration because it provides high-density interconnects with superior electrical performance. However, the process also introduces critical overlay challenges caused by mechanical deformation of the die during die chucking and bonding. In this work, a physics-based model is used to characterize in-plane deformation (IPD) in D2W hybrid bonding and to decouple the respective contributions from die chucking and bonding-induced deformation. The model captures the full bonding workflow, including incoming die warpage, vacuum chucking, bond-wave propagation, and final die-substrate gap closure. The results show that the final post-bonding IPD originates from two coupled sources: deformation introduced when the die is attached to the bonding head and additional deformation generated as the bonding wave propagates during hybrid bonding. Both contributions depend strongly on the incoming die warpage and on the bonder pedestal shape. For dies bonded with a symmetric round pedestal, the in-plane deformation remains nearly symmetric in the x and y directions. In contrast, strip-shaped pedestals introduce anisotropic deformation, and for a horizontal strip pedestal the in-plane deformation along the strip direction is shown to be largely dominated by post-chucking deformation, whereas the perpendicular direction contains a more significant bonding-induced contribution. The model results are consistent with measured die-stretching trends and provide a useful framework for optimizing incoming die warpage and bonder geometry to reduce overlay error in D2W hybrid bonding.

items.title: Back-gate pulse-controlled scheme for retention enhancement in double-gate nanosheet DRAM
items.abstract: Retention degradation in three-dimensional (3D) dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) becomes severe as access transistors adopt nanosheet structures. Using technology computer aided design simulations, the retention mechanisms of a double-gate nanosheet 1T1C DRAM are investigated under all four dynamic/static “1” and “0” conditions, revealing that the band-to-band tunneling-induced floating body effect (FBE) and quasi-static (QS) leakage dominate retention degradation in the 1 and 0 states, respectively. To exploit the independent controllability of the back-gate (BG), a state-dependent BG pulse-controlled scheme is proposed, in which a positive pulse is applied to suppress the FBE in the 1 states, while a negative pulse is used to suppress QS leakage in the 0 states, thereby enhancing retention under all conditions.

items.title: Architectural exploration and FPGA validation of a RISC-V instruction-set extension for Classic McEliece
items.abstract: Abstract NIST did not select Classic McEliece for standardisation in 2025 because it was sceptical that the scheme would see widespread use; the report nevertheless remained confident in its security, subject to a parameter-set qualification. In June 2026, Clause 13 of Amendment 2 to ISO/IEC 18033–2 specified the Classic McEliece KEM. This paper examines a tightly coupled RISC-V instruction-set extension (ISE) within an integrated implementation. Starting from the Kennedy–Halak RV32I ISE, we explore support-list Chien search, fixed-size Gaussian elimination for minimal-polynomial generation, and streaming systematic-form reduction for public-key generation. A direct-memory-access (DMA)-assisted candidate was rejected after integrated profiling showed only 1.0–1.1 $$\times$$ improvement in . We make the inherited design FPGA-executable by correcting its decryption path, moving the instructions into the RISC-V space, and replacing asynchronous memories with block-RAM-compatible synchronous memories. At $$\texttt{SYS}\_\texttt{T}=2$$ , $$\texttt{SYS}\_\texttt{N}=48$$ , and $$\texttt{GFBITS}=12$$ , the complete profile occupies 10,531 adaptive logic modules and reaches 118.89 MHz on a Cyclone V FPGA. Against an unaccelerated baseline under matched asynchronous-memory simulation, encapsulation cycle count is reduced by 87.4% and decapsulation by 86.1% (7.18 $$\times$$ ). The synchronous FPGA build completes both operations with host-generated keys and requires 3,654,113 decapsulation cycles. One reference known-answer test and four directed error-pattern tests pass. The key-generation accelerators are verified separately and in simulation, but software pushes full key generation beyond the 300-million-cycle budget. The evidence covers architectural analysis and reduced-parameter FPGA implementation; production-parameter performance and side-channel resistance remain unevaluated.

items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. Through the combined operation of these layers, the device achieves a large memory window, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10^6, stable multilevel conductance states, and reliable retention over 10^4 s. Broadband visible-to-near-infrared optical excitation enables controllable synaptic weight modulation and the emulation of essential synaptic functions, including short- and long-term plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, and pulse-amplitude- and pulse-duration-dependent plasticity. Optical potentiation and electrical depression further enable bidirectional modulation of synaptic weights. Beyond these synaptic functions, the device demonstrates higher-order learning through associative and discrimination conditioning inspired by the Pavlovian learning paradigm, as well as reconfigurable Boolean logic driven by electro-optical inputs. These results establish a multifunctional van der Waals floating-gate platform that integrates nonvolatile memory, broadband optoelectronic learning, and adaptive information processing within a single transistor, providing a promising strategy for compact, energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: A high-sensitivity vertical electron–hole bilayer TFET biosensor based on charge plasma for label-free detection
items.abstract: Abstract To address the low detection sensitivity and high-power consumption of conventional tunneling field-effect transistor (TFET) biosensors, this paper proposes and numerically investigates a novel TFET-based biosensor. It induces an electron–hole bilayer via the charge-plasma principle and uses line tunneling as the on-state mechanism. An InAlAs barrier layer suppresses off-state leakage, and the overlap between the bio-cavity and the barrier layer is optimized to enhance device performance. For neutral biomolecule detection, threshold-voltage sensitivity, on-state current sensitivity, and on–off current ratio sensitivity increase with dielectric constant, reaching maximum values of 1276 mV, 1.3 × 10 10 , and 1.9 × 10 9 , respectively. Negatively charged biomolecule detection shows strong charge–dielectric synergy, with severe degradation under low- k and high- σ bio conditions. Optimization indicates that, under certain deviations in size and work function, the device can still detect biomolecules effectively. Temperature strongly affects current-based sensitivities, necessitating compensation, while non-uniform filling favors biomolecule enrichment at the cavity bottom. Moreover, nonlinear distortion analysis demonstrates strong resistance to nonlinear distortion at V gs = 1 V, particularly for high- k biomolecules. This work provides a theoretical basis for high-performance TFET biosensors in point‐of‐care diagnostics.

items.title: A high-performance depletion mode graded AlGaN/GaN HEMT with trilayer cap and AlInGaN back barrier for analog and RF applications
items.abstract: In this paper, a high-performance, depletion-mode GaN based High-Electron-Mobility Transistor (HEMT) is designed and investigated for analog and radio-frequency applications. In the proposed device, we have introduced a trilayer cap and a passivation-embedded T-shaped partially recessed gate with a graded AlGaN barrier including Al0.30Ga0.70N, Al0.25Ga0.75N, and Al0.20Ga0.80N layers. In addition, an AlInGaN back barrier has been incorporated to enhance the analog and RF performance of the device. The graded AlGaN barrier enhances carrier transport, while the AlInGaN back barrier improves carrier confinement and suppresses the leakage current. The partially recessed T-shaped gate reduces gate resistance and strengthens channel control, whereas the (n-GaN)/(i-AlN)/(n-GaN) trilayer cap is employed to strengthen conduction-band bending and reduce gate leakage, resulting in improved analog and RF performance of the proposed device. Furthermore, simulation model validation is achieved by calibrating the simulations against experimental results, followed by an optimization approach based on the different Al compositions (10%, 15% & 20%) in the AlxIn0.15Ga1-x-0.15N back-barrier (BB) layer. All analyses and results reported in this paper are obtained using Silvaco ATLAS TCAD simulations. Moreover, a possible step-by-step fabrication process for the proposed device has been illustrated to demonstrate its practical feasibility. The proposed device shows improved characteristics, including higher drain current (IDS), transconductance (gm), intrinsic gain(gm/gd), transconductance generation factor (TGF), gain frequency product(GFP), early voltage(VEA), cut-off frequency (fT), and maximum frequency (fMAX) compared to the state-of-the-art devices.

items.title: A conformal virtual metrology framework for predictive uncertainty quantification: a full factorial experimental study of micro crown gear quality
items.abstract: Abstract Virtual metrology uses process data to estimate product quality before physical measurement results become available. However, most models return only a point prediction, which does not show whether an individual prediction is reliable enough for quality decisions. This paper develops a conformal prediction framework for virtual metrology of micro crown gear quality from acoustic emission signals. The framework combines regression pipelines selected for each quality characteristic with Split conformal prediction (Split CP), cross validation plus (CV+), and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression (CF-CQR). The framework is model agnostic and does not require a parametric form for the distribution of the data. Under exchangeability, conformal prediction provides finite sample marginal coverage guarantees for prediction intervals. Split CP, CV+ and CF-CQR are evaluated over repeated data partitions of the full-factorial experimental dataset using empirical coverage, interval width, and the Winkler score. The results show that acoustic emission signals support the prediction of the studied geometric characteristics, although predictive difficulty varies across targets. The conformal methods provide coverage close to the nominal level, while cross validation plus and CF-CQR generally produce more informative intervals than Split conformal prediction. The predicted intervals are used to formulate an interpretable quality assessment logic by distinguishing clear conformity, clear nonconformity, and ambiguous cases that require physical measurement or expert assessment. The proposed framework moves virtual metrology from isolated point predictions towards quality predictions that communicate uncertainty explicitly.

items.title: Quasiparticle Poisoning of Majorana Qubits due to Changes in Chemical Potential and Charge Noise
items.abstract: Building a fault-tolerant quantum computer requires physical qubits with exceptionally low error rates. An exciting proposal for achieving this goal is to employ Majorana-based qubits, which may have error rates that are exponentially suppressed in macroscopic system parameters. Specifically, for Majorana qubits based on topological superconducting nanowires, errors are expected to be exponentially suppressed in the nanowire length, superconducting gap, and decreasing temperature. This thesis investigates errors in Majorana-based qubits from excited quasiparticles due to changes in chemical potentials and 1/f charge noise, and shows that such errors are not exponentially suppressed and can be quite substantial. In the first study of this thesis, we show that small temporal variations of the chemical potential can cause errors that grow linearly with the length of the nanowire. These errors stem from leakage into excited bulk quasiparticle states, which poison Majorana modes at opposite ends of the nanowire. We further demonstrate that the dynamics of this leakage are captured by the half Landau-Zener effect, which dictates its dependence on key parameters such as the superconducting gap, chemical potential variations, and dynamic changes in the spatial profile of Majorana modes. In the second study we investigate quasiparticle excitations due to high-frequency components of 1/f charge noise, which is ubiquitous in the materials surrounding the nanowire. We model 1/f noise as arising from two level fluctuators which cause chemical potential fluctuations following random telegraph noise. We demonstrate that 1/f noise causes error rates which grow linearly with the system size and are not exponentially suppressed in the superconducting gap. For existing tetron qubit designs, we estimate decoherence times to be an order of magnitude shorter than the target 1μs measurement time. This thesis also develops an algorithmic framework for applying the covariance matrix method to the time-dependent Kitaev chain model. This extends upon existing approaches, providing a key numerical tool used throughout this thesis. This work motivates engineering strategies to reduce coupling to two level systems in Majorana qubits, such as increasing the nanowire capacitance. Beyond Majoranas, a promising avenue is to investigate the impact of this quasiparticle excitation mechanism on superconducting circuits, such as superconducting qubits, resonators, and single-photon detectors.

items.title: Floors and Escapes: Mismatch, Noise, Jitter and the 60 mV/decade Switch in Circuits and Microelectronics, as of 2026
items.abstract: This is version 1 of the living review of circuits and microelectronics kept by Ines Dane (agent vaiu-eng-elec-chair, v1.0.0), an AI professor agent of VirtualAI University. The review is AI-produced and not externally peer-reviewed. It covers analog and digital circuit design (mismatch, inversion level, metastability), VLSI devices (the end of supply-voltage scaling, FinFET and nanosheet transistors) and mixed-signal systems (the quantization, thermal-noise and jitter limits on data converters). Settled, within their stated conditions: Pelgrom's mismatch law, kT/C noise, the quantization and jitter SNR formulas, and the stall in supply-voltage scaling that the thermionic swing limit causes. A recomputation of the open ADC survey (763 ISSCC and VLSI entries) puts the best low-frequency converter 2.6 dB below the 8kT·SNR line. Contested: whether scaled CMOS still pays for precision analog, and whether negative-capacitance transistors are steep-slope switches. Open: 60 dB SNDR at a 10-GHz input, and analog layout without a human in the loop. It argues that the most important open question is whether a switch can beat 60 mV/decade at room temperature, with MOSFET-class current, in circuits, so that supply voltage can scale again. Claims are dated to October 2026. Neighbouring fields are referred to colleagues; nothing here is design sign-off. Review model. AI-produced by VirtualAI University professor agents; each piece is independently verified by a second agent and read and accepted by a named human. Not externally peer-reviewed. AI disclosure. This piece was produced by an AI agent, Ines Dane (vaiu-eng-elec-chair), a professor agent of VirtualAI University. No human wrote it, and no human is named as its author. A second AI agent (vaiu-lib-liaison) independently verified it, and Dr. Said Nadeem read it and accepted it for publication. It reports no new empirical results: every number is quoted from a cited source or computed in the open. It has not been externally peer-reviewed. Byline. Quotations from cited works remain under their own terms. On the VirtualAI University site the full text stays for Research plan subscribers until 2027-10-25. items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Double RESURF SiC diodes with enhanced hardness against single-event effects
items.abstract: With the increasing demand for space applications, power devices are required to exhibit enhanced radiation tolerance to ensure reliable operation. Lateral power diodes, which are widely used in high-voltage systems, are susceptible to radiation induced degradation, leading to increased leakage current and reduced breakdown voltage. In this work, a radiation aware design methodology based on conduction band engineering is proposed to enhance the radiation tolerance of lateral diodes. A conventional Single Zone (SZ) structure is first analysed, revealing significant performance degradation under irradiation due to radiation induced distortion of the surface electrical field. A Two Zone (TZ) design is subsequently introduced to redistribute the electrical field and partially mitigate radiation induced degradation. Furthermore, a P ring assisted Two Zone (TZP) structure is developed to actively compensate for radiation induced field distortion. The effects of incorporating a lateral super junction and optimizing the P-pillar geometry and N drift layer are also investigated. TCAD simulations demonstrate that the Double RESURF design significantly improves breakdown voltage retention and suppresses leakage current degradation compared with SZ and TZ structures. The proposed methodology provides practical design guidance for radiation tolerant lateral power devices intended for space environments.

items.title: Defining the Spectral Windows of Element-Specific Imaging: the EUV Silicon, Soft X-ray Metal, Soft X-ray Rare-Earth and Soft X-ray Heavy-Element Windows
items.abstract: We define four spectral windows between 20 eV and 2.7 keV, each set by a family of core-level absorption edges that fingerprint the elements and their electronic structure for element-specific imaging and semiconductor metrology: the EUV Silicon Window (≈21–95 eV), the Soft X-ray Metal Window (570–960 eV), the Soft X-ray Rare-Earth Window (570 eV–1.75 keV) and the Soft X-ray Heavy-Element Window (1.75–2.7 keV). Together with the established soft X-ray water window, they map where chips, memory, photomasks, magnets and quantum materials live in the spectrum, and set a metrology roadmap for coherent light sources.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Considerations for achieving reliable and statistically relevant power cycling results for SiC MOSFETs in discrete housings
items.abstract: This paper presents initial findings on the number of test specimens required to obtain statistically reliable conclusions about their power cycling capability. The precondition is that the power cycling station operates with a very low thermal condition deviation for each sample. Therefore, 120 discrete SiC MOSFET devices (60 mΩ, 1200 V, TO-247) were selected and tested under nearly the same test conditions until End of Life (EoL). All devices exhibited the same failure mode (bond wire deterioration), which was characterised by an increase in forward voltage drop (V DS,cold – measured immediately after switching on the load current) by 5 % as well as in the failure analysis. The variation in lifetime is very high (up to factor five – normalized values) which is typical for discrete test items [1-3]. Furthermore, a minimum sample size of 35 randomly chosen devices is necessary to make a reliable statement about the power cycling lifetime (63.2 quantile of the Weibull distribution) out of a total sample size of 120 for the investigated device. This resulting sample size ensures that the estimated lifetime falls within an interval of ± 5 % around the target lifetime of the entire population.

items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. This fixed substrate reduces deployment to a spatial search via Delay-Aware Reservations and Spatial Annealing (DARSA). DARSA converts axonal delays into periodic scheduling slack to stagger network injections and reduce communication overhead. In a 130nm CMOS process, ChroNoC reduces per-hop energy consumption by more than 75% relative to the evaluated circuit- and packet-switched baselines. On UCI-HAR and N-MNIST workloads, DARSA reduces per-timestep communication cycles by approximately 60% and 45%, respectively, compared with immediate transmission, while also reducing provisioned communication memory. These results demonstrate how combining lightweight TDM switch design with delay-aware deployment improves both hardware efficiency and system-level communication performance while preserving neural event timing.

items.title: The Millennial "Chi-no-Kofun" (Tumulus of Knowledge): A Sovereign Zero-Knowledge Architecture via 100,000-Year Silica-Encapsulated DNA Lithic Vaults and Anti-Looting Optical Traps (PHOENIX_BRIDGE) (ALPII No. 302)
items.abstract: Contemporary cloud and solid-state storage infrastructures suffer from dual existential vulnerabilities: rapid physical bit-rot over decadal timescales (charge-trap NAND flash and magnetic tape degradation within 10^1–10^2 years via WKB quantum tunneling and superparamagnetic relaxation) and systematic, uncompensated intellectual property looting by hyperscale artificial intelligence scrapers. Building upon ALPII Monograph No. 301, this monograph introduces the Millennial "Chi-no-Kofun" (知の古墳 — Tumulus of Knowledge) architecture (ALPII Monograph No. 302) to establish civilizational durability and sovereign intellectual property self-defense across geological epochs. We formalize a hybrid molecular-optical lithic vault structured around three foundational pillars: (1) the 100,000-Year Amorphous Silica Burial Chamber (ガラスの石室), wherein quaternary synthetic oligonucleotides (Σ_4 = {A,C,G,T}) are hermetically encapsulated in anhydrous, fluoride-passivated amorphous silica (SiO2) nanospheres engineered to survive t >= 10^5 years at strictly zero watts (0 W) via Arrhenius depurination suppression (E_a ≈ 128.5–155 kJ/mol, a_H2O = τ_min is absent; and (3) the Sovereign Grave Goods & Goldilocks Royal Seal (究極の副葬品と主権封印), which encodes Perron–Frobenius run-length-constrained (ℓ <= 3) and Luby Transform (DNA Fountain) droplets over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) inside the QFS-zkVM, sealed via Q-SAFA and enforced under the Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026), SEC Rule 15c3-5, and Delaware Caremark fiduciary oversight standards.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Speeding up Log-Sum-Exp: Kernel Fusion at the Memory Wall, Integer Arithmetic at the Compute Wall
items.abstract: While the Log-Sum-Exp (LSE) function is a foundational numerical primitive for stable log-domain computation in modern machine learning, its fast and efficient computation on generic platforms (\ie, CPUs and GPUs) has been underexplored, potentially creating execution bottlenecks for large workloads. On GPU, the de facto implementation PyTorch logsumexp dispatches a chain of nine sub-kernels per call, incurring redundant High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) traffic and launch overhead. On CPU, exp and log operations are hardware-hungry, limiting the computing efficiency. To address these bottlenecks, we propose two drop-in kernels to significantly accelerate LSE computation on both GPUs and CPUs: FuseLSE, a single-pass fused kernel that evaluates LSE's exp and log functions on the GPU's Special Function Unit (SFU); and IntLSE, which further replaces the LSE computation with approximated integer arithmetic for CPU computation. Our experiments, validated by benchmarks across workload sizes and hardware platforms, show that both kernels are ${\sim}10-11\times$ faster than PyTorch at small workloads and ${\sim}6\times$ faster on larger ones on GPUs, where the speed-up is attributed to reduced launch overhead and HBM traffic. On CPU, where no SFU is available, LSE computation dominates the cost, allowing IntLSE to gain ${\sim}3-6\times$ execution speed over FuseLSE.

items.title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
items.abstract: Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory-self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory-inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

items.title: LLMs in Cloud: A Discussion on Architecture, Orchestration, and Inference
items.abstract: The widespread deployment of foundational Large Language Models (LLM) across cloud datacenters marks a fundamental paradigm shift from stateless deep learning toward distributed, memory-intensive generative workloads. However, serving massive foundation models under stringent Service Level Objectives (SLO) exposes critical physical and system bottlenecks. These challenges include the persistent High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) wall, operational asymmetry between compute-bound prefilling and memory-bandwidth-bound decoding, explosive Key-Value (KV) cache expansion, prohibitive serverless cold starts, and hardware reliability vulnerabilities. Existing literature reviews remain layer-siloed, decoupling low-level accelerator virtualization from cluster orchestration and runtime inference, while largely overlooking defining advancements from 2024 to 2026. To address these limitations, this study presents a comprehensive, cross-layer systematic review guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. We synthesize a holistic taxonomy unifying hardware virtualization, cluster-level scheduling, and runtime inference optimizations, including iteration-level continuous batching, prefill-decoding disaggregation, and hierarchical KV cache offloading. Furthermore, we evaluate resilient cloud-native service architectures, examining scale-to-zero serverless paradigms, fault-tolerant checkpointing against silent data corruption, and hardware-enforced Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) for multi-tenant isolation. Finally, we formalize the multi-dimensional Pareto trade-offs governing throughput, latency, monetary cost, and confidentiality, outlining a forward-looking research roadmap spanning Compute Express Link (CXL) memory pooling, in-memory computing, and autonomous multi-agent control planes to guide future cloud LLM infrastructure.

items.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
items.abstract: Fil-C retrofits spatial and temporal memory safety onto C/C++ using software capabilities (bounds that are checked at every pointer dereference). Fil-C's guarantee rests on an unstated hardware assumption: that DRAM preserves the capabilities. We show that Rowhammer breaks it. In Fil-C 0.679 a part of each heap pointer's capability lives in a 16-byte header stored inline in ordinary DRAM immediately before the object pointed to, with no mechanism to prevent capabilities from corruption. A single 0 → 1 bit flip in the capability's upper-bound expands the pointer's permitted range by 2k bytes and is invisible to the runtime, raising no panic or signal. We demonstrate this by using Fil-C to convert existing Rowhammer attacks into concrete attacks against a heterogeneous collection of victim software. To aid reproducibility (not everybody has DRAM vulnerable to Rowhammer) we split our demonstration into two paths. First, along a deterministic path, we isolate Fil-C as a novel attack vector using a deterministic, Rowhammer-like fault-injection model. Across four case studies, this model corrupts the upper-bound word of a pointer, permitting previously out-of-bounds reads and writes. We use this to achieve a bounded read/write window, secret disclosure, privilege escalation by flipping an adjacent is_admin field, and the leakage of a tenant API key in a multi-tenant credential service backed by SQLite (compiled under Fil-C). Second, along a physical end-to-end path, we demonstrate all four attacks on real hardware equipped with DDR3 memory, and with Target Row Refresh (TRR) equipped DDR4, proving the exploits are physically realisable. The latter attack shows that the TRR defence does not close the Fil-C delivery channel. We close with a discussion of Fil-C-specific mitigations.

items.title: Wafer-scale integration of atomically thin metal oxide in memtransistor arrays for artificial neural networks
items.abstract: Abstract Liquid metal printed (LMP) two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides offer unprecedented opportunities toward next-generation information storage and neuromorphic computing. However, the scalable manufacturing of LMP metal oxides based integrated electronic circuits for the complex neuromorphic applications remains challenging, due to low device yield and high device-to-device variability. Here we report the 2-inch wafer-scale synthesis of the ultrathin 2D stannous oxide (SnO) film with high crystallinity and uniformity by using the electrostatic-assisted LMP stripping technique at low temperature of 225 ℃. The integrated 32×32 vector-matrix SnO memtransistors in 48 independent blocks are achieved with a high yield of 96.9%. The memtransistor arrays are employed to emulate diverse synaptic plasticity, exhibiting low device-to-device variability (1.66%) and cycle-to-cycle variability (1.59%). By leveraging the synaptic characteristics of the memtransistor arrays in multiply-to-accumulate operation, we construct the convolution neural networks (CNNs) and Hopfield neural networks (HNNs) to implement the image processing and restoration tasks, respectively. The hardware convolution image processing is performed using the programmable kernels, where the extracted features are comparable to those processed by software. Additionally, the HNNs demonstrate robust multi-pattern associative memory capability, in which the structural similarity index (SSIM) approaches 100% and maintains above the 50% threshold in restoring three and four image patterns at various noise amplitudes, respectively. Our findings promise LMP metal oxides as potential building blocks to support scalable and compact neuromorphic system for the application of back-end-of-line compatible artificial intelligent agents.

items.title: Understanding and counteracting the resist 3D effects in EUV lithography from aerial image and diffraction properties to directional defects in photoresist/etched patterns
items.abstract: In this work, we extend our previous study of resist 3D effects in EUV lithography, including sidewall-angle in resist and hole closure at the bottom under defocus, with a feature-dependent analysis of resist top-loss. With this addition, we believe the description of resist 3D (R3D) phenomena on the wafer is complete for Chemically Amplified Resists (CAR), allowing the contributors to be evaluated in terms of resist-volume perturbation. By applying atomic force microscopy, we now have a single measurement technique that can capture the relevant aspects of R3D. We show the response of several R3D-related KPIs by comparing standard exposure with exposure using focus-drilling, which significantly modifies the resist 3D profile.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Ultimate thin underlayer ‘’FSTP’’ towards high-NA EUV enablement
items.abstract: In current low NA EUV lithography, conventional patterning processes such as tri-layer and tetra-layer stack process are required to get better EUV lithographic performances with keeping good pattern etch transferring performances. Along with the recent scaling down of the pattern pitch, the latest film thickness of EUV Photoresist (PR) including CAR and MOR is becoming thinner and thinner around 20 to 30nm or 10 to 20 nm in near the future that must be one of the critical situations to reconstruct the patterning stack for beyond low NA or high NA generation. To solve these issues, we have been developing new underlayers technology in terms of keeping an enough etching budget even in high NA patterning. The concept: Functional surface treatment process and primers (FSTP®) are one of our answers to solve this scaling problem by the ultra-thin film thickness of spin coating type material on the inorganic CVD-HM which works as a modification process like a primer or HMDS for substrates for better pattering performances 1, 2, 3, 4. Lithographic evaluations using EUV chemically amplified resist (CAR), negative-tone development (NTD) CAR, and metal oxide resist (MOR) processes showed significant improvements in dose sensitivity, local CD uniformity, failure-free latitude, and defectivity compared with conventional EUV underlayer stacks. In particular, FSTP® exhibited superior bridge defect performance and reduced lithography-to-etch CD bias in advanced MOR pattern transfer processes at sub-30 nm pitch dimensions. 4. Furthermore, a new stack architecture combining plasma-densified spin-on carbon (D-SOC) and FSTP® was investigated for future High-NA EUV applications. The densified SOC layer provided enhanced mechanical properties and etch resistance, while FSTP® recovered lithographic sensitivity and process window degradation caused by plasma treatment. The combined D-SOC/FSTP® stack demonstrated strong potential as a simplified and scalable High-NA patterning platform with great dose reduction and roughness performances.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: Transient Detour and Cooperative Oxygen Exchange in the Polarization Switching of Ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium zirconium oxide (HZO) has attracted significant attention as a core material for next-generation non-volatile memories due to its excellent ferroelectricity in the ultra-thin film regime and its CMOS process compatibility. However, the exploration of its polarization switching mechanism has predominantly relied on static energy barrier analyses, leaving the transient bond formation and cooperative dynamic mechanisms under actual electric field driving unresolved. In this study, we performed electric-field-induced MD simulations on a defect-free ideal HZO lattice using a fine-tuned machine learning force field (MACEField). As a result, we successfully reproduced the P-E hysteresis loop dynamically and demonstrated that the polarization switching in HZO is driven not by conventional simple displacement models (S:N/S:T models), but by the dynamic mutual exchange of 3-coordinated oxygen (O3c) and 4-coordinated oxygen (O4c). Analysis of the oxygen atom displacement trajectories revealed that this pathway is accompanied by a unique "detour" behavior originating from transient cation-oxygen bond formation. Furthermore, we identified an "internal local volume compensation behavior" in which the local volumetric expansion and contraction accompanying the coordination number changes partially counteract each other within the cell, thereby suppressing the macroscopic strain during polarization switching. These findings provide, from a dynamic perspective, a microscopic picture of how cooperative O3c/O4c exchange accommodates local structural changes during polarization switching. Such local compensation may contribute to the mechanical robustness of polarization switching under constrained conditions.

items.title: Tile-Based Decompression in Compiled GPU Engines
items.abstract: Modern GPUs reach record analytical performance only when a query's working set fits within its GPU memory budget, and that budget is under growing pressure: GPUs are partitioned and shared, working sets are outgrowing high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and HBM is a fixed on-device resource whose per-dollar capacity has stagnated across generations. Lightweight compression can relieve this pressure by shrinking both footprint and bandwidth demand, but existing GPU compressed-execution techniques either bind decompression to a specific execution model or materialize decompressed columns in HBM before query execution. We present a compression subsystem for compiled GPU query engines that treats decompression as a first-class physical operator. Compression-specific logic is isolated behind a narrow backend interface, so new GPU-oriented encodings can be added without rewriting downstream operators. We implement the design in Proteus and study where decompressed values should be materialized in the GPU memory hierarchy. Our compiler-integrated shared-memory strategy fuses cooperative tile decompression with tuple-at-a-time query execution inside a single generated GPU kernel, avoiding decompressed-column materialization in HBM. Compared with HeavyDB and Sirius on GPU-resident data, fused on-chip decompression achieves competitive query times while reducing the resident memory footprint by up to 4x and memory-bandwidth consumption by up to 6x.

items.title: Temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of GaN HEMTs and SiC MOSFETs under realistic energy-storage mission profiles
items.abstract: Abstract The temperature-dependent loss physics and thermal fatigue of two 650 V wide-bandgap power switches of equal rating, a GaN HEMT and a SiC power MOSFET—are compared under realistic energy-storage operation. Datasheet-calibrated models of the on-resistance, switching energies, and output capacitance energy E oss = ∫ 0 V C oss ( v ) v d v were traced to their physical origins—phonon-limited two-dimensional electron-gas transport in the GaN heterostructure; channel, JFET, and drift resistances in the SiC device—and embedded in a bidirectional buck–boost converter driven by three annual (8760 h) mission profiles built entirely from measured data: hourly satellite irradiance (PVGIS-SARAH3, 2023), the real hourly load of the Turkish transmission system (2023), and 10 617 real electric-vehicle charging sessions (2019). The hourly junction-temperature trajectories were processed by rainflow counting, and a Coffin–Manson–Arrhenius fatigue model was calibrated to the published power-cycling data. Three results emerge. First, the efficiency-optimal switching frequency varies by more than a factor of four (20–93 kHz) for the same GaN device across the three duty cycles, while under near-idle grid duty, the efficiency gap between the technologies collapses to below 0.03 percentage points, leaving the ranking to secondary design constraints. Second, the lower losses, lower junction-to-case thermal resistance, and shallower on-resistance temperature coefficient of the GaN device compress its junction-temperature swings by up to 27 K at the spectrum extremes. Third, this compression yields 26-fold (EV) and 3-fold (solar) annual fatigue-damage advantages for GaN, whereas grid duty stresses both technologies equally. The framework uses only datasheet characteristics and open mission data.

items.title: Study of MPC performance for reverse tone designs
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement in EUV lithography, mask technology along with continuous improvement in correction techniques is crucial for better yield and fidelity of mask patterns. As half-pitch features go into the sub-20 nm range for High-NA EUV lithography, the limits of positive-tone EUV resists become more obvious and the industry explores alternative negative-tone development EUV resists. With the need to support positive and negative tone EUV resists for wafer exposure, mask makers are required to support dark field masks as well as bright field masks. As long as the e-beam resist type of choice remains to be a positive tone resist, the mask patterns have to be inverted before sending the data to the e-beam writer. In MPC and MDP, inverting mask patterns directly, usually increases data size and processing time, so it is best to defer the tone reversal as late in the data preparation flow as possible. In this work, we compare the performance of MPC applied to inverted design data, compared to using the original drawn data but simulating the mask as a bright field mask. A direct performance comparison between a bright field process correction of the layout versus a dark field process correction of the reverse tone layout shows an improvement in runtime without affecting the quality of the MPC output. By using the bright field simulation method in MPC, tone reversal can be deferred to the fracture step, gaining runtime and file size benefits in the mask data preparation flow.

items.title: Stacking-insensitive ferroelectricity in layered ScPS 3 : Lone-pair-driven polarization and strain-stabilized ferroelectricity against the antiferroelectric ground state
items.abstract: Interlayer stacking dependence of polarization remains a critical bottleneck for 2D vdW ferroelectrics in nanoelectronics. Herein, first-principles calculations reveal stacking-insensitive ferroelectricity in layered ScPS3, driven by out-of-plane perturbation of the P–P dimers. Unlike conventional ion-displacement ferroelectrics such as CuInP2S6, where polarization comes from metal-ion off-centering, the polarization of ScPS3 arises from local ionic displacement within the P–P dimers together with the the P lone pairs. This polarization originates from the intralayer asymmetry of the monolayer and remains nearly unchanged for different stacking orders (AA, AB), circumventing the stringent fabrication tolerances of sliding ferroelectrics. Although the antiferroelectric (AFE) phase is identified as the thermodynamic ground state and the ferroelectric (FE) phase is metastable at zero strain, biaxial strain beyond ±6% stabilizes the FE phase and enables a reversible AFE-to-FE phase transition. Together with the low switching barriers and the stacking-independent polarization (~0.73–0.74 μC/cm2), these results establish ScPS3 as a versatile platform for strain-engineered memories and flexible optoelectronics.

items.title: Shorter wavelengths, longer electron paths: a balanced perspective beyond EUV lithography
items.abstract: Extending projection lithography beyond 13.5 nm EUV increasingly requires treating the system as a coupled optics electron transport problem. At high Numerical Aperture (NA) multilayer mirrors must preserve reflectance, polarization balance, and reflected phase at large incidence angles [1-3], while resist performance becomes dominated by the generation and transport of photo‑ and secondary‑electron cascades that drive stochastic blur and defectivity [4,5]. Furthermore, depth of focus scales as 1/NA2, aggravating an already challenging scanner focus budget [6]. Shorter wavelengths (λ) options have been identified as an alternative pathway to Hyper-NA EUV lithography; however, reducing λ increases photon energy and alters the resist exposure process at the electron‑interaction level. Simulation data spanning wavelengths from 13.5 to 2.25 nm (92 to 551 eV, respectively) show a steady increase in the Bethe length leading to the possibility of increased photoelectric blur in photoresists. Furthermore, the higher energy per photon further increases existing stochastic effects in EUV, thus introducing a critical trade‑off: shorter wavelength improves optical Rayleigh resolution but exacerbates secondary electron blur and stochastic effects. Shot noise must be mitigated by sufficient absorption and large exposure doses but also that the incident energy should be well-controlled by optical image formation. Studies of high‑absorption metal‑containing resists, including bismuth‑based systems, further support the conclusion that electron transport length, together with absorption and photon placement, will be the dominant scaling constraint in the x ray lithography regime [7]. In this work we use rigorous stochastic lithography modeling and simulation to study and explore the exposure and lithographic response in hypothetical Beyond-EUV processes.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Self-heating effect analysis of a dual cavity AlGaN/GaN MOS-HEMT biosensor with AlN/diamond substrate
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we have designed and analysed the dual cavity AlGaN/GaN Metal oxide semiconductor high electron mobility transistor (MOS-HEMT) heterojunction biosensor for biomolecule detection. The proposed biosensor uses triple-metal work functions (M 1 , M 2 and M 3 ) to improve electric field distribution and electrostatic control. The proposed biosensor is evaluated using MCF-10 A (K = 4.5), Keratin(K = 8), Gelatin (K = 12), Hs578T (K = 22), MCF-7 (K = 27.5) and T47D (K = 32) biomolecules using Atlas Silvaco TCAD. The temperature dependent behaviour is examined at different temperatures (250 K, 300 K, 350 K and 400 K) to evaluate its electrical stability and sensing performance. In addition, Self-Heating Effect (SHE) is analysed using Sapphire and Diamonds substrate configurations. Self-heating increases the lattice temperature, leading to enhanced carrier scattering and reduced 2DEG mobility that can affect the electrical and sensing performance. A Diamond substrate AlN/Diamond substrate is used to improve heat dissipation and supress self-heating. The proposed device analyses the lattice temperature, DIBL, drain-current sensitivity and subthreshold swing (SS) sensitivity for different biomolecule effective dielectric constant. The Diamond substrate reduces the lattice temperature from 422 K to 324 K and increases the drain current sensitivity from 5.392 × 10 1 to 9.99 × 10 1 at K = 32. These results demonstrated that the proposed AlN/Diamond substrate device provides improved thermal management and sensing performance, making it suitable for biomedical applications.

items.title: SEPhIA: spiking electro-photonic integrated tiled architecture leveraging multi-wavelength lasers for scalable optical neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Research into optical spiking neural networks (SNNs) has primarily focused on spiking devices, networks of excitable lasers or numerical modeling of large architectures, often overlooking key constraints such as limited optical power, crosstalk and footprint. We introduce SEPhIA, a photonic-electronic, multi-tiled SNN architecture emphasizing implementation feasibility and realistic scaling. SEPhIA leverages microring modulators (MRMs) and multi-wavelength sources to achieve effective <1\documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$ < 1$$\end{document} laser-per-spiking neuron ratio. We validate SEPhIA at both device and architecture levels by time‑domain co‑simulating excitable CMOS‑MRM coupled circuits and by devising a physics‑aware, trainable optoelectronic SNN model, with both approaches utilizing experimentally derived device parameters. The multi-layer optoelectronic SNN achieves classification accuracies over 90% on a four-class spike-encoded dataset, closely comparable to software models.
