A design space study further quantifies how photonic device parameters impact SNN performance under constrained signal-to-noise conditions. SEPhIA offers a scalable, expressive, physically grounded solution for neuromorphic photonic computing, capable of addressing spike-encoded tasks.

items.title: Reliability evaluation of DG JL and DG IM MOSFETs under oxide trap-induced degradation
items.abstract: Abstract In this paper, a reliability based comparative analysis between conventional double gate inversion mode (DG IM) and junctionless (DG JL) MOSFET has been presented using the Silvaco TCAD. By altering the gate workfunction, the devices are tuned to have the same threshold voltage for fair comparison. Later on, the interface trap charges are included at the oxide/silicon channel interface and the reliability of both devices is assessed by calculating the shift in the threshold voltage brought up by the applied gate voltage stress and sweeping the voltage from 0 to 2 V and then 2 to 0 V. Apart from this, the change in the trans conductance ( g m ), drain conductance ( g d ) and device gain ( g m / g d ) has also been computed by applying the gate and drain voltage stress. According to the computed results, the DG JL MOSFET shows a substantially lesser variation in the calculated V TH after changing the trap density and energy (during forward gate voltage sweep) than the DG IM MOSFET. Additionally, the impact of varying parameters such as temperature, oxide thickness, channel doping, trap density, and its location (energy level) on the shift in the device parameters has been determined. The research also calculates and presents the impact of bias stress on the device breakdown voltage.

items.title: Recent advancement in ferroelectric photovoltaic (FPV) materials for energy conversation and energy storage
items.abstract: Ferroelectric photovoltaic (FPV) materials represent a distinctive category of multifunctional materials that integrate spontaneous electric polarization with photovoltaic functionality. This dual functionality makes them highly promising for next-generation energy technologies, especially in applications involving solar energy conversion and integrated storage. This review provides recent advancements in FPV materials, covering fundamental mechanisms, synthesis methods, material engineering, and device integration. Emphasis is placed on perovskite oxides, organic–inorganic hybrids, lead-free ferroelectrics, and 2D materials, highlighting their photovoltaic performance, dielectric properties, and suitability for self-powered systems. Strategies to optimize FPV efficiency, such as domain engineering, architecture optimization, and heterostructure interfaces, are examined. This review also explores cutting-edge developments in tandem solar cells, hybrid energy systems, and multifunctional devices that bridge the gap between energy harvesting and storage. Critical challenges – including wide bandgaps, low conductivity, instability, and scalability, are analyzed, alongside current challenges and future directions in the field of FPV materials for energy applications. It highlights the need for further research on stability, scalability, and cost-effective solutions through novel materials and device architectures.

items.title: Progress in SADP technology for nanoimprint templates toward sub-10 nm patterning capability
items.abstract: Nanoimprint lithography, NIL, is being revisited as an alternative lithographic pathway for leading-edge semiconductor fabrication. In parallel, EUV lithography, particularly in the high-NA regime, faces increasing challenges related to mask complexity, with assist features approaching nanoimprint-template-level critical dimensions, reduced exposure field size, and heightened sensitivity to stochastic process variability at sub-10 nm dimensions. Under these conditions, the resolution of NIL templates emerges as a key enabler for sub-10 nm patterning, placing template fabrication technology at the center of NIL advancement. As pattern dimensions continue to shrink, further resolution enhancement based solely on incremental improvements in EB writers and EB resists has approached practical limits for reliable template fabrication. This has motivated the development of process-based pitch-splitting technologies, such as self-aligned double patterning (SADP), to extend patterning capability beyond single-exposure limits. In recent work, hp10 nm L/S patterns were fabricated using SADP for NIL templates. This work presents our latest progress in extending the resolution capability of nanoimprint master and replica templates. SADP has demonstrated process capability down to hp9.5nm L/S. A cutting process performed after Qz etching was proposed and demonstrated using hp10nm L/S SADP patterns with a metal-like layout. Template replication by NIL was also applied to SADP-patterned masters, resulting in sub-10nm imprinted line patterns on replica substrates.

items.title: Programmable Organic Light‐Emitting Transistors Enabled by Floating‐Gate Charge Storage
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Display technologies for high‐resolution smartphones, wearable screens and near‐eye VR/AR microdisplays increasingly require compact pixel architectures with high aperture ratios. Organic light‐emitting transistors (OLETs) improve functional integration by combining transistor switching and electroluminescence within a single device. However, conventional OLETs still define emission states through instantaneous electrical bias, leaving state storage separated from light emission. The absence of memory‐emission co‐location limits intrinsic state programmability in OLET‐based pixel devices. Here, we report programmable organic light‐emitting transistors (P‐OLETs) based on a floating‐gate architecture, in which charge storage enables reversible charge trapping and release, producing programmable switching behavior and tunable electroluminescence. The stored charge modulates channel transport and light emission, allowing electrical programming to define persistently retained optical states. Optimized P‐OLETs exhibit a large memory window of 27.07 V, stable luminance retention over 5000 s, and reliable endurance over 100 program/erase cycles. Floating‐gate charge storage shifts OLET operation from bias‐defined emission toward charge‐state defined emission and establishes a memory‐emission integrated device architecture. This work introduces programmable state‐retentive emission as a compact operating concept for programmable optoelectronics and reconfigurable display systems.

items.title: Physics-informed Graph-ResNet for real-time VLSI wirelength prediction with HPC enabled data
items.abstract: In very large scale integration physical design, accurate pre-routing wirelength prediction is a crucial bottleneck. Graph neural networks (GNNs) attain excellent accuracy but have seconds of inference latency, which prevents real-time application inside placement loops, whereas analytical heuristics diverge under congestion. To address these limitations, this paper presents a complete framework based on a proposed Physics-Informed Graph-ResNet. First, we create a dataset of 251 layout variations using two technology nodes (Nangate45 and Sky130) and four open-source benchmark designs using the Parmutkarsh national supercomputer. Our suggested multi-modal differentiable surrogate model combines global physical constraint features with topological graph embeddings from a two-layer residual Graph Convolutional Network. A composite training loss augments mean squared error with an half-perimeter wirelength-derived regularization term ( α=0.1), providing a physically motivated geometric inductive bias to stabilize and accelerate convergence without additional labeled data. Evaluated on held-out RISC-V processor designs (Ibex and TinyRocket), our model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 10.07% on zero-shot cross-design evaluations and an inference latency of only 15 ms per design. This represents a 140× speedup over state-of-the-art GNN baselines while maintaining comparable accuracy, making the proposed model a potential candidate for integration as a differentiable surrogate inside GPU-accelerated analytical placers, although its 55% cross-node error indicates that reliable application currently remains process-node dependent.

items.title: Out-of-band DUV light and standing waves in EUV lithography
items.abstract: Laser-produced plasma (LPP) sources used in extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) emit broadband out-of-band radiation in addition to the 13.5 nm emission used for imaging. Although vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) radiation is strongly attenuated by the scanner optical column and hydrogen environment, a fraction of the deep-ultraviolet (DUV) spectrum can reach the wafer and interact with DUV-sensitive photoresists. We measured the output spectrum of a 250 W LPP EUV source over the 5–400 nm wavelength range using a calibrated transmission-grating spectrometer and estimated the corresponding wafer-level spectrum using wavelength-dependent optical-column and mask reflectivities. Combining the calculated spectrum with representative resist-sensitivity data indicates that wavelengths between approximately 130 and 230 nm may contribute to the effective DUV response. Optical simulations further show that DUV radiation can produce stack- and thickness-dependent standing-wave modulation in thin resist films. Open-field exposures at 248 nm using different underlayer thicknesses demonstrate corresponding changes in dose-to-clear for selected chemically amplified (CAR) and metal-oxide (MOR) resists, supporting the proposed standing-wave mechanism at this wavelength. These results show that effective DUV sensitivity is a property of the complete wafer stack rather than of the resist alone. Quantitative prediction of broadband DUV effects in EUV imaging performance requires wavelength-resolved optical and photochemical characterization of modern photoresist systems.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Optimization of positive-tone metal-oxide resist process for high-NA DRAM applications
items.abstract: A key application of high numerical aperture (High NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is the DRAM storage node layer. The current baseline process for this layer uses a chemically amplified resist (CAR) combined with dark-field imaging. Continued scaling requires pitch reduction to 28 nm and smaller where local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU) becomes increasingly challenging for CAR. Metal-oxide resists (MORs) offer a promising alternative due to their high absorptivity, small granularity and high etch resistance. Conventional MOR operate in negative-tone development (NTD), requiring bright-field imaging to print contact holes. A recent new advancement is positive tone development (PTD) of MORs, which enables contact hole printing using dark-field imaging. In this study, spin-on PTD-MORs are evaluated for pitch 28 nm hexagonal contact holes and benchmarked against NTD-MOR. Process optimization was performed across several key parameters, including post-exposure bake (PEB) conditions, underlayer selection, and pattern-transfer etch.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Optimization of lithography and etch processes to demonstrate the viability of 0.55 NA single patterning for DRAM
items.abstract: High NA (0.55 NA) EUV lithography is a promising technology for future DRAM contact hole (CH) scaling. Continued pitch scaling introduces significant challenges in local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU), defect margin, focus behavior, and pattern transfer quality. In this work, multiple lithography and etch optimization approaches were evaluated on a common High NA P28 CH platform. Advanced resist optimization, resist thickness optimization, Low-n mask technology, assist processing, pupil optimization, and etch optimization were investigated using both After Development Inspection (ADI) and After Etch Inspection (AEI) metrics. Resist optimization and Low-n mask technology improved LCDU and expanded defect margin, while the assist process enabled approximately 10% dose reduction with minimal impact on LCDU and defect margin. Etch optimization further improved transferred pattern quality and achieved the best AEI LCDU performance. Focus behavior was investigated through pupil optimization and resist thickness optimization. A high DoF pupil reduced the impact of focus variation on CD, LCDU, and defect count, whereas 30 nm resist provided a larger focus margin than 50 nm resist. Cross-sectional TEM analysis revealed that thinner resist films undergo less profile deformation during focus shift, resulting in more stable pattern transfer behavior. Together, these results support the viability of CAR based 0.55 NA single patterning processes for future DRAM contact hole scaling.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Negative-voltage-enabled energy efficient nonvolatile memories and in-memory computing based on 2D piezoelectric transistors
items.abstract: Piezoelectric FET (PeFET) is a promising non-volatile-memory (NVM) device that integrates a piezoelectric (PE)/ferroelectric (FE) capacitor with a 2D transistor. It uses the polarization of the FE capacitor for bit-storage and strain-induced bandgap change of the 2D channel during read. Previous PeFET-based NVM designs have shown immense promise in achieving high density and energy-efficiency compared to SRAM. However, a key limitation of these designs is that they must trade-off integration density to enhance energy-efficiency or augment the memory functionality with in-memory computing (IMC). In this work, we show that the unique structure of the PeFET presents an appealing opportunity to counter these limitations, thereby simultaneously achieving high density, high energy-efficiency, and IMC-compatibility. First, we highlight the key reasons for the limited energy-efficiency of the previous PeFET designs. Based on these insights, we propose two flavors of PeFET memories that utilize negative voltage (NeVo) to reduce the major energy-consuming components significantly. Compared to 6T-SRAM (prior PeFET-based NVMs), the proposed designs achieve substantial reductions in energy, lowering read energy to 0.08 × (0.03 × ) and write energy to 0.19 × (0.53 × ), respectively. We then leverage these cells to implement IMC primitives, such as addition, subtraction, and multiply-and-accumulate (MAC), achieving 0.03 × the energy consumption of prior PeFET-based designs.

items.title: Multi‑column e-beam inspection as a production solution for advanced EUV reticle manufacturing
items.abstract: As EUV lithography is broadly deployed across advanced logic, memory, and High-NA technologies, mask inspection requirements increasingly extend beyond sensitivity alone to include application-specific defect characterization and disposition. In this study, we report Samsung's application of a multi-column electron beam inspection (EBMI) system for EUV mask inspection across diverse device technologies and pattern types, demonstrating practical deployment with a balance of resolution and throughput suitable for both development and manufacturing environments. We further demonstrate the capability to detect extremely small defects, on the order of 1× nm, in 2× nm pitch line-and-space patterns, taking advantage of the direct edge-localization characteristics of the electron beam. On Low-NA production masks the system delivered above-specification sensitivity, and on High-NA-relevant P2x line-and-space and P2y contact-and-hole patterns it met the sensitivity target, with defect capture rates of 98% and 96% against specifications of 84% and 79%, respectively. Beyond defect detection, the EBMI system supports high-resolution defect review and printability evaluation through integrated lithography simulation workflows. These include machine-learning-based advanced nuisance control (ANC) and auto defect classification (ADC) for early filtering and labeling of defects using inspection images; lithography printability review for coarse printability assessment at the lithography plane; post-inspection image capture (PIIC) for higher-resolution defect imaging; and aerial image simulation workflows that enable fine printability evaluation. PIIC-based SEM-to-aerial (S2A) analysis correlated with conventional review-SEM-based S2A with R² ≈ 0.97, allowing inspection results to feed directly into disposition without routine SEM review. Finally, an anamorphic pixel matched to the 4×/8× magnification of High-NA masks is introduced as a path to balance sensitivity and throughput. A PDM-to-production matching methodology, in which the recipe qualified on a programmed defect mask (PDM) is applied unchanged to production masks and validated for false and nuisance (F/N) performance and throughput, is used to establish production readiness. This work demonstrates the value of multi-column EBMI for EUV masks across diverse pattern types and device applications and highlights its contribution to mask readiness for advanced logic, memory, and High-NA lithography.

items.title: Multilayer graphene EUV pellicle: plasma CVD synthesis, scalable transfer, and commercialization roadmap
items.abstract: As extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography advances toward high-numerical-aperture (high-NA) nodes, the pellicle remains a critical piece of enabling infrastructure. An EUV pellicle must combine high transmittance at 13.5 nm with mechanical robustness as a full-field free-standing membrane and chemical durability in the hydrogen radical environment of the scanner. We report the development of a multilayer graphene EUV pellicle fabricated using two proprietary core technologies: a high-rate plasma chemical-vapor-deposition (CVD) synthesis process and an automated, scalable transfer process, both implemented in a roll-to-roll configuration. The multilayer graphene membrane exhibits high EUV transmittance at 13.5 nm together with low defect density and high film quality relative to conventional thermal-CVD films, and a clear path toward the theoretical transmittance limit of pristine graphene is identified through continued improvement of film cleanliness. Durability testing under continuous EUV-representative irradiation in a low-pressure hydrogen atmosphere has confirmed stable membrane integrity over extended periods corresponding to tens of thousands of lithographic exposures. We conclude with a commercialization roadmap spanning full-size fabrication, pilot production, and volume manufacturing, positioning multilayer graphene as a viable solution to the EUV pellicle infrastructure gap.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Mask absorber considerations for low-k1 imaging using high-NA EUV lithography
items.abstract: Tantalum has been the workhorse absorber in EUV lithography (EUVL) for more than a decade. However, as high-NA EUV lithography is adopted to support continued device scaling at low k₁, the relatively thick Ta absorber introduces significant mask 3D (M3D) effects that can degrade imaging performance. While high-NA imaging delivers improved resolution, enhanced image contrast, reduced reliance on costly multi-patterning, and tighter control of edge placement error (EPE), line width roughness (LWR), and stochastic defects, its reduced depth-of-focus (DOF) necessitates improved mask performance to maintain adequate process windows. Consequently, the development of alternative absorber materials that satisfy imaging, manufacturability, and high-volume manufacturing requirements has become increasingly important. In this work, the performance of conventional Ta-based absorbers is compared with several alternative absorber solutions, including a high-reflectivity, low-n, low-k absorber and a thickness-optimized low-n, mid-k absorber stack. A systematic co-optimization methodology is presented to determine absorber thickness by balancing mask reflectivity, phase shift, and aerial image contrast at target pitches. To mitigate challenges associated with higher mask reflectivity, a low-reflectivity phase-shifting absorber configuration is also proposed. The imaging performance of this absorber designs is evaluated through both rigorous simulations and experimental exposures using 0.55-NA EUV lithography with metal-oxide resist on silicon wafers. One-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) patterns at 18nm and 21nm pitches are studied. Results demonstrate that the optimized alternative absorber stacks provide improved aerial image contrast, reduced pattern sensitivity, and greater process robustness compared with conventional Ta-based mask absorbers, highlighting their potential for future high-NA EUV lithography applications.

items.title: MBM-4000: latest results and additional benefits enabled by edge dose enhancement
items.abstract: The multi-beam mask writer MBMTM-4000 targets the A14 technology node and beyond, where high-NA EUV lithography is applied. It was launched in Q3 2025, and the first tool is now in use at our customer’s site. The MBM-4000 has the advanced patterning resolution enabled by its 10 nm beams, and it can be further improved by using edge dose enhancement (EDE); inline pixel-level dose correction (PLDC) with dose modeling has reduced critical dimension variability and edge placement error. Having concluded the development of the MBM-4000, we are working on realizing further performance enhancements for future platforms. A new approach of EDE has been developed where offline mask process correction (MPC) defines the EDE, including the patterning information within the chip data, to be applied by the MBM via inline dose modulation during exposure. In this paper, we will give an overview of the MBM-4000 and advanced EDE function along with the latest writing results.

items.title: Low-n/mid-k mask absorber process development for high-NA EUV lithography
items.abstract: High-NA extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) is required to support future semiconductor technology nodes beyond the capabilities of current NA 0.33 systems. Conventional tantalum-based absorbers suffer from mask 3D (M3D) effects that degrade imaging performance, motivating the development of alternative absorber materials. In this study, we evaluate the feasibility of a candidate Low-n/Mid-k absorber material from a mask manufacturability perspective. Particular focus is placed on three critical aspects: patterning performance, defect inspectability, and defect repairability. Pattern profile formation and critical dimension performance were investigated through hard mask and etching process optimization. Defect detection capability was evaluated using programmed defect masks and DUV inspection tools, and repair feasibility was assessed through repair process development. Based on these results, the suitability of the proposed Low-n/Mid-k absorber as a next-generation High-NA EUV mask material is discussed.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: Low-Thermal-Budget High-Mobility In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors Enabled by an In Situ Multifunctional Protection Layer
items.abstract: While atomic layer deposition (ALD)-grown In2O3 thin-film transistors (TFTs) hold great promise for next-generation electronics, the performance and reliability of highly desirable top-gate configurations are often limited by interfacial degradation caused by photolithography chemicals and plasma exposure during device fabrication. Here, a multifunctional protection layer (PL) strategy is demonstrated that simultaneously suppresses chemical and plasma-induced interfacial damage while enabling controlled hydrogen incorporation. The introduction of an in situ plasma-free thermal ALD Al2O3 (T-Al2O3) layer directly onto the In2O3 channel, a robust physical barrier against chemical and plasma damage is established while simultaneously serving as a hydrogen reservoir. Crucially, inserting this T-Al2O3 layer allows for the precise tailoring of hydrogen incorporation by modulating the ALD cycles. The incorporated hydrogen effectively passivates interfacial defects, such as oxygen vacancies (VO) and oxygen interstitials (Oi), while optimizing the carrier concentration. Consequently, the optimized top-gate TFTs deliver an exceptionally high field-effect mobility of 66.7 cm2/V·s, hysteresis-free operation, and outstanding operational stability, with a positive bias temperature stress (PBTS)-induced Von shift of only 0.26 V and excellent resistance to negative-bias illumination stress (NBIS). Notably, these outstanding characteristics are achieved through a completely thermal annealing-free process. These results establish a powerful platform for simultaneous chemical and plasma damage suppression and hydrogen engineering in oxide semiconductor devices, enabling substantial improvements in both electrical performance and operational reliability.

items.title: Looking on the bright side of photomask imaging
items.abstract: Advanced mask metrology tools play a key role in research and development towards future nodes of EUV lithography. Experimental studies are an essential complement to simulation data in photomask technology and lithographic imaging. We are commissioning a mask-imaging demonstrator powered by a high-brightness undulator light source at beamline twelve of the Advanced Light Source at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. The instrument is a zoneplate-based actinic full-field EUV microscope similar to the SHARP microscope, enabling complementary imaging modes, increasing the photon flux at the mask by two orders of magnitude. At frame rates above one hundred hertz, more than a thousand individual pupil channels can be recorded per experiment site, resolving the source-angular spectrum produced by the illuminator. Arbitrary pupil fills can be synthesized from the image data. The data can be used to compute Fourier- Ptychographic reconstructions. Fourier Ptychography (FP) is a computational imaging technique that reconstructs the complex field of the object from a series of intensity images recorded under plane-wave illumination from different illumination angles. FP enables quantitative phase imaging. FP data can be used to emulate wafer-side through-focus behavior in anamorphic image data. We provide an overview of the instrument, discuss data acquisition modes, and present a range of image data, demonstrating short exposure times, FP, and source optimization.

items.title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
items.abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.

items.title: Hyper-NA and shorter wavelength from the perspective of EUV stochasticity
items.abstract: EUV lithography has several extension strategies to pursue the miniaturization of IC chips, such as hyper-NA, shorter wavelength, etc. One of the primary concerns of EUV lithography is resist stochastics. In this paper we study these approaches from the point of view of resist stochastics. Stochastic resist responses to the image qualities and the absolute pattern sizes are investigated by quasi-first principles/discrete dev-etch model simulations to clarify the competing relationship of scalable factors and unscalable factors such as blur, PE scattering, and molecular interactions. Below 10nm patterns, stochastic variability is dominated by unscalable factors. In particular for shorter wavelengths, the behavior of the photoelectron from each single photon absorption becomes clearly visible. The calculation results show that the photoelectron elastic mean free path should be taken into consideration carefully because the results are highly dependent on the photoelectron scattering behaviors.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Hydrogen plasma exposure methodology for accelerated durability evaluation of CNT EUV pellicles
items.abstract: Hydrogen plasma generated inside extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography scanners is considered one of the primary contributors to pellicle degradation, particularly for carbon nanotube (CNT) pellicle membranes. However, reproducing scanner-relevant plasma conditions in laboratory environments remains challenging due to the complex coupling of EUV radiation, thermal loading, and hydrogen radical generation. In this work, we present a hydrogen plasma exposure methodology developed at Samsung Electronics DS Division to emulate key aspects of EUV-induced plasma environments for accelerated pellicle durability evaluation. The system is designed to isolate the effects of hydrogen plasma by intentionally excluding EUV radiation and associated thermal contributions, enabling systematic investigation of plasma-driven degradation mechanisms in CNT pellicles. Over the past three years, hydrogen plasma exposure experiments have been performed on several hundred CNT pellicle coupons under controlled plasma conditions. Based on this dataset, a screening protocol was established to evaluate pellicle robustness as a function of hydrogen plasma exposure time. Both purified CNT pellicles and capped CNT pellicles were investigated to assess the role of surface modification on hydrogen plasma resistance. In addition to EUV transmission measurements, visible transmission at 550 nm was monitored as a complementary optical indicator of pellicle degradation. The evolution of visible transmission showed trends consistent with changes observed in EUV transmission. Furthermore, degradation behavior measured in the hydrogen plasma exposure tests exhibited similar trends to those observed in scanner-based pellicle evaluations. These results demonstrate that hydrogen plasma exposure testing can provide a practical and scalable methodology for accelerated screening of CNT pellicle durability under EUV scanner-relevant conditions.

items.title: High-NA EUV capabilities for volume manufacturing
items.abstract: Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography remains pivotal in enabling cost-effective scaling for advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The transition from 0.33 NA to 0.55 NA offers key customer value drivers and substantial benefits for high-volume manufacturing (HVM), including reduced patterning cost of technology through single exposure per layer, minimized defect density, and relieving multi-patterning design constraints to boost device performance. As the High NA EUV installed base is growing, R&D activities at multiple customer sites and in the imec-ASML High NA Lab are unlocking the imaging capabilities of the High NA platform. Proven performance of the EXE:5000 and EXE:5200B systems and ecosystem developments continue to drive pitch shrink. This presentation outlines the recent progress in platform capability and maturity, including proof data for upcoming Logic and DRAM nodes, and the system availability status. Furthermore, we will present the roadmap for next-generation High NA EUV systems, supporting node requirements for the coming decade while improving patterning cost.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: HIGH-PERFORMANCE IN-MEMORY HALF ADDER AND FULL ADDER ARCHITECTURE BASED ON 8T AND 8+T SRAM CELLS
items.abstract: The increasing volume of data processing has created a growing gap between memory access and computational speed in conventional computing systems.In a conventional von Neumann architecture, operands are repeatedly transferred between memory and processing units, resulting in additional latency and energy consumption.Inmemory computing (IMC) addresses this limitation by performing selected computations within the memory array itself.SRAM is a promising technology for IMC because of its high operating speed, CMOS compatibility, and suitability for dense memory arrays.In particular, 8T SRAM provides an isolated read path that can be exploited for logic computation without directly disturbing the stored data, while 8+T SRAM provides enhanced read capability for more complex operations.Previous research has demonstrated SRAM-based Boolean functions, Half Adders, and Full Adders using computational read paths.However, achieving an appropriate balance between propagation delay, power consumption, transistor count, sensing complexity, and reliable arithmetic operation remains challenging.This work investigates an in-memory Half Adder and Full Adder architecture based on 8T and 8+T SRAM cells.The 8T SRAM structure is employed for Half Adder computation, while the 8+T SRAM structure is used for Full Adder computation.The proposed circuits are intended for transistor-level implementation and simulation in Cadence Virtuoso, followed by evaluation using propagation delay, power consumption, power-delay product (PDP), transistor count, and functional reliability.

items.title: From growth to integration: MOCVD epitaxy of h-BN and heterogeneous integration
items.abstract: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN), as a two-dimensional (2D) material with outstanding structural, electrical, thermal, and optical properties, has attracted widespread attention. This review firstly summarizes the atomic structure and fundamental properties of h-BN, and provides a detailed discussion on its optical, electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties. Particularly, recent spectroscopic breakthroughs are highlighted, confirming the indirect bandgap nature of atomically thin h-BN. Subsequently, this article focuses on the process of synthesizing h-BN using metal-organic chemical vapor deposition, with an in-depth exploration of key parameters such as precursor control, substrate selection, temperature, and V/III ratio, and how these influence the growth process from the gas phase to nucleation. The review also addresses the strategies for thin film quality control, including epitaxial growth model, thermal annealing, and so on. Moreover, doping techniques are also discussed, covering p-type and n-type doping as well as carbon doping, to modulate the electronic properties of h-BN. Finally, the integration of h-BN into 2D and three-dimensional (3D) heterostructures is further explored, particularly its van der Waals integration with other 2D materials such as graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides. Additionally, the potential of h-BN in 3D semiconductor integration is also investigated, showcasing its multifunctionality as a substrate, gate dielectric, encapsulation layer, and tunneling barrier in hybrid systems. These heterostructures can enhance the performance of electronic and optoelectronic devices. Finally, future challenges are addressed, paving the way for the development of next-generation optoelectronic and quantum devices.

items.title: From Monolayer MoS2 FETs to MoS2−MoO2 Nanoheterostructures: Enhanced Self-Powered Visible-Light and NO2 Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Self-powered multifunctional sensors require internal fields that can separate photocarriers and transduce surface adsorption events without continuous external bias. Here, we show that chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth conditions can tune the morphology of nanostructured molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), forming sulfur-deficient quadrilateral flakes with coexisting molybdenum-sulfur (Mo−S) and molybdenum-oxygen (Mo−O) chemical environments, consistent with MoS2−MoO2 (MSMO) phase coexistence. Comprehensive structural, optical, and chemical characterization confirms the distinct growth regimes of monolayer, few-layer, dendritic, and quadrilateral flake and verifies the morphology and composition of the resulting phases. Devices fabricated from pristine MoS2, gate-modulated MoS2, and the MSMO quadrilateral-flake film were compared under visible illumination and NO2 exposure. The monolayer MoS2 FET exhibits n-type gate modulation with an on/off ratio of ∼ 4 − 7, field-effect mobility of ∼0.2−0.7 cm2V−1s−1, threshold voltage of ∼1.5 − 3.1 V, and subthreshold swing of ∼5 − 8 V.dec−1, indicating conventional but weakly gate-controlled CVD MoS2 transistor behavior. The heterostructure device outperforms the monolayer MoS2 FET device, delivering responsivity of 100 A/W, detectivity of 1012 Jones (at 630 nm, 30 mW optical power), response/recovery times of 200 ms, and operation over the visible spectrum at zero bias. The same junction architecture also enables room-temperature NO2 sensing with a sub-ppm (∼0.1 PPM) limit of detection (LOD) at a low bias of 0.5 V, and this decreases further with illumination. The device exhibits a zero-bias sensing response with a few ppm LOD (∼5 ppm), whereas pristine MoS2 control devices require a higher applied bias and exhibit weaker modulation. Thus, internal interface field enables a faster and measurable self-powered photodetection and NO2 sensing than external electrostatic gating.

items.title: Frequency domain analysis of EUV line and space patterns after post-develop treatment for LWR improvement and dose reduction
items.abstract: EUV lithography faces fundamental challenges in simultaneously optimizing resolution, pattern roughness, and exposure dose. This study investigates the impact of post-development beam treatments on the fidelity of EUV line and space patterns. To precisely evaluate the treatment effects, we implement frequency domain analysis, providing a comprehensive characterization of pattern profiles beyond conventional spatial-domain metrics. By evaluating power spectral density (PSD) profiles, we quantify the smoothing effects of directional beam treatment across a broad spectrum of spatial frequencies. Our findings indicate that optimized beam processing significantly suppresses mid-frequency roughness components, leading to a substantial reduction in line width roughness (LWR). The post-processing capability allows for the use of lower exposure doses by mitigating the increased roughness typically associated with low-dose imaging, thereby addressing the intrinsic RLS (resolution, LWR, sensitivity) trade-off. This frequency-based methodology offers a precise framework for optimizing post-lithography treatments, ensuring reliable high-fidelity pattern transfer for advanced technology nodes.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Extendibility of 3D-engineered resist films for 0.55 NA EUV lithography: bright-field hexagonal contact holes and random via patterning
items.abstract: Patterning with 0.55 NA presents significant challenges for conventional photoresists, with achieving a defect-free depth of focus (DoF) emerging as one of the most critical limitations. Dry-deposited and dry-developed 3D engineered resists have previously been shown to offer strong potential for extending the defect-free process window. In this work, we present systematic approaches to optimize the performance of 3D engineered resists and discuss the remaining challenges associated. Test vehicles based on C2C 28 nm Hex CH and P30 random via patterns printed on a 0.55 NA EUV system are discussed. For Hex CH, the impact of 3D dry resist configuration is investigated with respect to depth of focus, dose-to-LCDU trade-off, and defectivity. Optimization of PEB, dry development, and pattern-transfer etch is explored to extend the performance of the 3D engineered dry resist, showing dose-reduction benefits from PEB and DD optimization and revealing merging-cliff modulation at C2C 32 nm with etch optimization, which will be further complemented by STEM studies. In addition, we discuss the evaluation results of the vertical profile modulation capability of 3D engineered resist along with the dose benefit provided by the bright field imaging for random logic via.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Enhanced durability and optical performance of CNT-based EUV pellicles
items.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT)-based pellicles are a promising technology for next-generation extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography because of their high thermal stability and EUV transmittance. A major challenge is to improve durability to hydrogen-radical-induced etching (which can occur inside the EUV scanner) while preserving excellent EUV transmittance. In this study, impact on CNT pellicle durability of three coating structures were investigated utilizing an in-house hydrogen plasma etching test and synchrotron-based EUV exposure at NewSUBARU. Results show an optimal condition (Coating C) exhibiting the smallest changes in both visible-light transmittance after 6000 s of plasma exposure and EUV transmittance after 90 min of high-power EUV irradiation (corresponding to approximately 16,000 wafer exposures in a 600 W-class scanner). It is also noteworthy that the initial EUV transmittance of the optimized coated pellicle is relatively high at 92.5%. This work also describes the successful fabrication and EUV mapping of full-size pristine and coated pellicles at the newly established LINTEC Tsukuba Innovative Creation Center (TICC). These results demonstrate that coating optimization can substantially improve CNT-pellicle durability while retaining EUV transmittance above 92%, and that the technology can be transferred to full-size pilot-line fabrication.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Enabling an accelerated pathway within the U.S. for learning on low-NA EUV and high-NA EUV, and what’s next
items.abstract: Within the NY Creates’ Albany NanoTech Complex, an ecosystem of sophisticated tools and infrastructures is already driving scientific progress. Now, with the addition of High Numerical Aperture (NA) Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) Lithography capabilities, researchers gain access to an elite, collaborative environment equipped for the demands of modern discovery. The impact is unmistakable: rapid screening and prototyping for everything from custom materials to next-generation architecture will become faster, more efficient, and more adaptable than ever before. Barriers to experimentation are removed, enabling bolder ideas to move from concept to reality at unprecedented speed. Here, we will explore not only the technologies and roadmaps, including next-generation light sources, that are propelling this capability forward, but also the unique engagement models to work within this highly collaborative ecosystem.

items.title: Embodied Emissions of 2.5D and 3D Scaling in Chipletized GPUs for Low-Carbon AI
items.abstract: GPU compute resources are scaling to support growing AI workloads, leading to further rises in the climate change impact of hyperscale data centers that rely on high-performance GPUs. To model how packaging decisions impact the carbon footprint we have estimated the embodied emissions (EE) of a chiplet-based GPU that has been scaled in 2.5D and 3D using the imec.netzero modelling platform. We doubled the number of compute units and high bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity in the 2.5D and 3D scaled systems and found that 3D scaling results in an 89% increase in EE, as compared to an increase of 141% for 2.5D scaling, positioning 3D scaling as an attractive solution to limit the embodied emissions due to GPU scaling.

items.title: Diffraction-based metrology and focus correction to overcome DoF loss in high-NA EUV lithography
items.abstract: The transition to high‑NA (NA ≈ 0.55) EUV lithography is essential for continuing the scaling of devices, because it provides the required resolution while reducing reliance on complex multi‑patterning. However, the higher NA reduces the depth‑of‑focus (DoF) by 64% relative to low‑NA tools, making the process highly susceptible to focus‑related CD variation and yield loss. Herein we introduce a focus‑monitoring and correction scheme that exploits optical two scatterometry targets with different pitch and CD. Mask‑3D shadowing shifts each pattern’s optimal focus, producing distinct first‑order intensity peaks allowing to generate a monotonic focus signal from the delta signal (the Cal‑curve). This concept was demonstrated on high-NA (0.55 NA) EUV exposures using line/space patterns with a pitch > 25 nm, a Ta binary mask, and metal‑oxide‑resist (MOR). Here, the Cal-curve was created using 2 patterns having a shift in best focus, generating a monotonic signal over a 50 nm focus range. High‑NA EUV exposure showed a measured focus variation within a wafer of 16.1 nm, of which ≈ 5 nm can be corrected by scanner‑feedback on a single-layer test wafer. Full process on HVM would contain more and worse focus variation for high-NA. Therefore, a new CD-based diffraction-based focus (CDBF) metrology, will play an important role for maintaining and controlling of expected focus variation and difference on high-NA era. This paper demonstrates that integrating diffraction‑based on‑product focus metrology with scanner feedback restores the reduced DoF margin and enables robust, high‑yield manufacturing on 0.55 NA EUV platforms.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography

items.title: Development progress, readiness for HVM, and future perspectives of CNT pellicles
items.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) pellicles are considered among the most promising candidates for next-generation EUV lithography because of their high EUV transmittance and excellent thermal properties. Mitsui Chemicals, Inc. has been actively developing CNT pellicles and launched a high-volume manufacturing (HVM) line in 2026, achieving HVM readiness for commercialization. This paper reports recent progress in CNT pellicle development, including defectivity improvement, lifetime enhancement, and scale-up of capped CNT films. Continuous improvements in the cleanliness of the HVM production line have enabled full-size non-capped CNT pellicle films to achieve zero particle defects larger than 10 μm. Zero reticle adders have also been confirmed in multiple scanner evaluations. To address the lifetime challenge of CNT pellicles, we have developed capped CNT films that suppress hydrogen-plasma-induced CNT etching. By optimizing both the core CNT layer and the capping technology, a near-zero etching rate was achieved in an offline hydrogen-plasma test under conditions equivalent to EUV source powers 600 W or higher, demonstrating a lifetime of more than 100k wafer equivalents. The manufacturability of capped CNT films has also been demonstrated through successful scale-up from coupon samples to full-size pellicles. Full-size capped films exhibited good EUV transmittance uniformity and maintained excellent plasma durability. Based on these achievements, Mitsui Chemicals continues to advance next-generation CNT pellicles toward commercialization and future high-power EUV applications.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Development of CNT-based EUV pellicle for high-power lithography systems
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry advances toward sub-nanometer nodes, extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is transitioning to higher source power levels to enhance throughput. This shift necessitates EUV pellicles capable of withstanding harsh environments characterized by high thermal loads and exposure to hydrogen plasma and radicals while maintaining high EUV transmittance. Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have emerged as a leading candidate for next-generation pellicle films due to their exceptional thermal and mechanical resilience. In this study, we present a high-performance CNT-based EUV pellicle developed for high-power EUV lithography. We implemented a proprietary surface-treatment technology tailored to the unique characteristics of CNT membrane structures. Furthermore, the integration of a specialized capping layer provided a robust chemical barrier, significantly mitigating degradation induced by hydrogen radicals. The resulting CNT-based pellicle achieved an EUV transmittance exceeding 90% and was evaluated up to an irradiation dose corresponding to approximately 30,000 wafer-equivalent exposures under 800 W-class high-power EUV conditions without apparent membrane failure. These results demonstrate that our specialized surface-engineering and capping technologies successfully address the performance and reliability challenges of next-generation EUV lithography, highlighting the potential of the developed CNT-based pellicle for high-power EUV lithography and advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: Density functional theory insights into CsAc for optoelectronic applications
items.abstract: First-principles density functional theory calculations were used to investigate the structural, electronic, mechanical, and optical properties of the proposed hexagonal CsAc intermetallic in the P6₃mc space group. Calculations employed CASTEP with the GGA-PBE functional and spin–orbit coupling. Structural optimization yielded lattice parameters of 3.874 Å along the a-axis and 14.906 Å along the c-axis, corresponding to contractions of 4.81% and 6.87%, respectively, and a unit-cell volume of 193.75 Å³ . The electronic band structure and density of states reveal metallic, gapless behavior, with Ac-6d states contributing prominently near the Fermi level. The bulk modulus of 9.622 GPa indicates a mechanically soft and compressible structure, while the elastic constants reveal anisotropic mechanical behavior. Optical calculations demonstrate orientation-dependent dielectric functions, absorption coefficients, extinction coefficients, and reflectivity, highlighting differences in the interaction of CsAc with electromagnetic radiation. The calculated optical response also exhibits distinct dielectric-loss peaks near 7.19 eV for the (100) orientation and 7.94 eV for the (111) orientation using a 12 × 12 × 12 k-point mesh. The peak intensities remain sensitive to k-point sampling. Overall, these results provide a theoretical understanding of the structural, electronic, mechanical, and anisotropic optical properties of CsAc without establishing specific device performance or experimental realization.

items.title: Deep-Learning-Accelerated Dopant Selection for High-k HfO 2 Dielectrics: A Disorder-Resolved Study of Y, Si, and Al
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide (HfO2) is the cornerstone high-k dielectric in modern silicon technology. Since the constraints of silicon device fabrication rule out replacing the material itself, dopant incorporation is the principal means available to engineer its band gap (Eg) and electronic dielectric constant (ε) within existing process flows. However, dopant selection is still largely empirical due to the coupled interplay among thermodynamic stability, electronic insulation, and dielectric response. Here, we present a high-throughput computational framework integrating special quasi-random structures (SQS), machine-learning potentials (SevenNet), and graph neural networks (ALIGNN) to systematically evaluate doped-HfO2 compositions across three dopants (Al, Si, Y) and two technologically relevant polymorphs (monoclinic and orthorhombic). Our analysis uncovers a fundamental design principle: formation energy, band gap, and dielectric constant are decoupled parameters requiring application-specific prioritization rather than simultaneous optimization. Yttrium achieves the lowest formation energy (−3.763 eV/atom) and favors orthorhombic phase stabilization at process-compatible thermal budgets; silicon preserves near-pristine band gaps (∼5.72 eV) critical for suppressing leakage in gate dielectric applications; and aluminum enables concentration-tunable band gap widening (5.6–5.9 eV) suited for voltage scaling. Validation against experimental literature and density functional theory (DFT) confirms quantitative accuracy (±0.02 eV band gap error for Si-doping, mean absolute error ≤ 0.001 eV/atom formation energy). This framework provides rational, property-decoupled guidance for dopant engineering in HfO2-based dielectrics and related high-k oxide systems.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C

items.title: DESIGN AND EVALUATION OF FINFET-BASED APPROXIMATE MODIFIED BOOTH MULTIPLIER FOR ENERGY-EFFICIENT VLSI SYSTEMS
items.abstract: In the progress of energy-efficient digital multiplication systems, approximate multipliers have been proven to be a good solution to attain high energy efficiency with acceptable computational precision. This paper proposes a 22 nm FinFET-based approximate Modified Radix-8 Booth multiplier which is based on Modified Radix-8 Booth recoding, selective partial-product approximation, controlled truncation, and an optimized reduction and accumulation network to minimize arithmetic complexity and switching activity. This architecture was modeled in VHDL and designed using an ASIC design flow using a 22 nm standard-cell library. Post-layout evaluation showed about 63.4% silicon area reduction, 55.1% propagation delay reduction, and 65.6% power consumption reduction when compared with an exact Booth multiplier with lower Power–Delay Product (PDP) and Area–Power Product (APP). The application-level validation with representative image processing operations resulted in a PSNR of 41.2 dB and SSIM of 0.995, which validated the proposed approximation strategy to maintain high computational quality. The proposed multiplier is well suited for low-power digital signal processing, multimedia processing, and embedded VLSI systems as it gives an effective trade-off between implementation efficiency and arithmetic accuracy.
items.venue: JOURNAL OF MECHANICS OF CONTINUA AND MATHEMATICAL SCIENCES

items.title: Breaking the SS- I on trade-off in 2D TFETs through an isolated conduction band in monolayer AgSe
items.abstract: Abstract Tunneling field-effect transistors (TFETs), operating through the band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) mechanism, are widely regarded as strong contenders for future low-power (LP) electronic applications on account of the potential to achieve subthreshold swings (SS) below 60 mV∙dec −1 . Nevertheless, the inherently limited on-state current ( I on ) has consistently posed a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that a two-dimensional monolayer AgSe TFET can obtain a sub-60 mV∙dec −1 SS and a high on-current at the same time without complex source engineering strategies. The unique isolated conduction band of monolayer AgSe produces a sharp band edge, significantly enhancing the BTBT efficiency and facilitates steep switching characteristics. For a 10 nm p -type AgSe TFET, an SS as low as 31 mV∙dec −1 is obtained, with on-currents reaching 1617 and 716 μ A∙ μ m −1 for high-performance and LP applications, satisfying the requirements defined by the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors. Even if the supply voltage ( V dd ) drops to 0.5 V, the 5 nm device maintains an SS min = 43 mV∙dec −1 , demonstrating excellent voltage scalability. Benchmark comparisons with other widely studied 2D materials further confirm the superior performance of AgSe TFETs. These results identify monolayer AgSe as a highly promising channel material and suggest that isolated-band engineering provides an effective design paradigm for next-generation LP nanoelectronic devices.

items.title: Beyond Passive Reliability: Repeated Electron Wind Force Rejuvenation of GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: Abstract Performance degradation in electronic devices is caused by nucleation and accumulation of electrically active defects and traps. This spotlight on applications introduces a novel paradigm to actively reverse the damage process with electron wind force (EWF). EWF is a nonintrusive and nonequilibrium mechanism for defect migration at near-ambient average temperatures. Enhancement-mode gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) were systematically degraded via high-temperature storage at 310 °C, which induced upto 13% reduction in drain current, 0.2 V negative threshold voltage shift, and 12% reduction in peak transconductance. A brief 1-minute application of EWF achieved full parameter recovery. Crucially, across five consecutive degradation-rejuvenation cycles, the HEMTs maintained excellent resilience, retaining 98.5% of their initial drain current, 97% of peak transconductance, 95% of gate-lag, and 93% of drain-lag responses. These findings indicate that periodic in operando EWF rejuvenation may realize unprecedented reliability of wide-bandgap electronics in mission-critical operations.

items.title: Application of a new mask CD metrology approach to advanced DRAM scaling
items.abstract: As DRAM technology nodes continue to shrink, mask patterns are becoming smaller and more complex due to aggressive optical proximity correction (OPC), the use of assist features and serif structures, and the increasing adoption of irregular or curvilinear geometries. Under these conditions, the reliability of conventional SEM-based critical dimension (CD) metrology, which relies on one-dimensional measurements within limited regions of interest (ROI), is increasingly degraded. Reduced ROI and irregular edge shapes amplify the effects of line edge roughness (LER) and measurement noise, resulting in degraded mask field CD uniformity (FCDU), CD targeting errors, and reduced stability in wafer lithography process control. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an edge placement difference (EPD)-based CD measurement method for advanced DRAM mask patterns. In the proposed approach, pattern contours extracted from SEM images are aligned with target GDS layout contours through correction of translation, scaling, rotation, and distortion. The edge placement difference between the two contours is then calculated along the local normal direction and averaged over the full pattern edge, providing an EPD-based CD metric that is physically compatible with conventional CD. In addition, the ROI definition was optimized for manufacturing applications by incorporating a width tolerance around the measurement point and trimming vertex regions to reduce process-induced patterning errors. The proposed method was first applied in an advanced DRAM technology node and showed approximately 70% reduction in FCDU values compared with conventional CD metrology. This enabled tighter FCDU control while maintaining mask-to-wafer CD correlation. Expanded application to major DRAM mask layers also demonstrated process benefits. In particular, by enabling measurement of regions that were previously difficult to monitor, the method helped reduce exposure dose variation and improve lithography stability in mass production.

items.title: Analysis of pattern-dependent variation transfer in dry and wet metal oxide resist processes for EUV lithography
items.abstract: As memory device patterns continue to scale down in size, extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) faces significant challenges in fabricating ultra-fine features while precisely controlling process-induced variation. These process-induced variations, such as line width roughness (LWR) and local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU) have a substantial impact on yield by causing defects such as bridging and pattern collapse; thus it is essential to analyze and improve the underlying sources of variation. In particular, metal oxide resist (MOR) has competitively emerged as a negative-tone resist for EUVL due to its high EUV absorption and etch selectivity compared to conventional chemically amplified res ists (CAR); however, controlling stochastic variation and achieving high pattern fidelity remain key challenges, particularly for different pattern topologies such as line/space (L/S) and pillar structures. In this work, we performed a comparative analysis of process-induced variation in both MOR1 and MOR2 processes following development and subsequent etch steps for DRAM hexagonal pillar patterns with 3x nm range pitch, and L/S patterns. Further, the transfer of variations was quantified from after development inspection (ADI) to after etch inspection (AEI) using unbiased LWR and power spectral density (PSD), and LCDU for L/S and pillar patterns, respectively. Distinct pattern- and process-dependent behavior was observed. This study has provided valuable insights into pattern formation and process-induced variations in both dry and wet EUVL processes using MOR, enabling a better understanding and potential improvement of process performance.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: Accelerating EUV metal oxide resist development via physicochemical feature-enhanced machine learning
items.abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) metal oxide resist (MOR) development becomes increasingly resource-intensive as multi-precursor formulations expand the experimental design space. Conventional machine-learning approaches based primarily on recipe information can represent precursor identity, composition ratio, and process conditions, but do not explicitly encode the intrinsic physicochemical differences among precursors. This work presents a physicochemical feature-enhanced machine-learning framework that addresses this limitation using actual EUV lithography data. Hundreds of MOR formulations and thousands of lithographic evaluation records were combined with measured and calculated precursor-level physicochemical descriptors. These descriptors were transformed into formulation-level features and used together with conventional recipe information to predict normalized dose-to-size (DtS) and local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU). Models were evaluated using shuffled 5-fold cross-validation. Incorporation of physicochemical features improved prediction beyond recipe-level modeling, while the final models reduced root-mean-square error (RMSE) by more than 60% for DtS and more than 40% for LCDU relative to a mean-prediction baseline. The trained models were further applied to a large, experimentally bounded virtual formulation space for candidate prioritization. These results demonstrate that explicit physicochemical representation can improve data efficiency and enable practical virtual screening for MOR development.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: A new perspective on non-Gaussian CD distributions
items.abstract: Non-Gaussian contact hole critical dimension (CD) distributions are of increasing importance in EUV lithography because distribution tails can contribute to edge placement error (EPE) excursions. Previous studies have explained the emergence of non-Gaussian CD distributions in terms of lithographic stochastics, where photon-induced dose fluctuations are transformed into asymmetric CD distributions through the nonlinear dependence of CD on exposure dose. In this work, a Measure-Etch-Measure (MEM) methodology is used to correlate after-development inspection (ADI) and after-etch inspection (AEI) measurements on the same contact holes. A deeply sampled dataset is analyzed under strongly underexposed conditions. The results show that the non-Gaussian ADI CD distribution can be interpreted as a mixture of populations with distinct transfer behavior: holes that fail after etch contribute to the small-CD tail, whereas successfully transferred holes are generally associated with larger ADI CDs. A substantial overlap exists between printing and failing populations, demonstrating that ADI CD alone cannot perfectly predict etch success. The observations are consistent with a picture in which etch transfer also depends on other characteristics of the developed resist profile, such as residual resist remaining within the contact hole.
items.venue: International Conference on Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography 2026

items.title: A Comparative Study of Parylene, PSPI and ALD TiO2/TiN/Ru/Cu Multilayer as Adhesion Layers on Glass Surface for Glass-Cu Adhesion Enhancement
items.abstract: Glass substrates exhibit great potential in 2.5D/3D advanced packaging, but poor interfacial adhesion with metal layers remains a critical challenge. This work studies three different adhesion layer strategies, namely Parylene-C, photosensitive polyimide (PSPI), and atomic layer deposition (ALD) TiO2/TiN/Ru/Cu multilayer, to improve glass-Cu adhesion. A 30 µm Cu layer was electroplated over glass-Parylene-Ti/Cu, glass-PSPI-Ti/Cu, and glass-TiO2/TiN/Ru/Cu multilayer stacks. The 90° peel test results show that, at the layer thicknesses investigated here, all three strategies increase the glass-Cu peel resistance (approximately 6.5 to 10 times) compared with the conventional glass-PVD Ti/Cu control group (0.62 ± 0.06 N/cm). Parylene-C achieves the highest adhesion strength of 6.25 ± 0.03 N/cm, which is 31.9% higher than the ALD multilayer (4.74 ± 0.28 N/cm) and 55.5% higher than the PSPI (4.02 ± 0.10 N/cm). The adhesion enhancement mechanisms are analyzed, and the comprehensive performance of the three strategies is compared over multiple aspects. Overall, this work provides three practical solutions to improve the glass-Cu adhesion.

items.title: 1/ f Noise model for 4H-SiC MOSFETs incorporating the nonuniform spatial distribution of oxide traps
items.abstract: Conventional noise models exhibit limited capability in characterizing the spatial distribution of oxide traps in 4H-SiC MOSFETs. To overcome this limitation, the present study considers the nonuniform distribution of oxide traps in the direction normal to the channel and employs a Gaussian profile to describe a trap distribution characterized by a localized concentration maximum. Based on this premise, a 1/f noise model that incorporates the nonuniform spatial distribution of oxide traps is developed for 4H-SiC MOSFETs. The proposed model is assessed using Sentaurus TCAD simulations and measured low-frequency noise spectra from practical 4H-SiC MOSFETs. Its applicability is further investigated under various bias conditions through comparisons with exponential- and uniform-distribution models, as well as through measurements on multiple devices. The results indicate that the proposed model effectively reproduces the 1/f noise characteristics of 4H-SiC MOSFETs and facilitates the estimation of model parameters related to the oxide-trap spatial distribution, including peak trap density, peak position, and distribution width, from the low-frequency noise power spectral density. Consequently, the proposed model offers a physics-based approach for characterizing the nonuniform spatial distribution of oxide traps in 4H-SiC MOSFETs.

items.title: SARIA: Persistence-Aware KV Caching with Coordinated DRAM--SSD Reload for LLM Agents
items.abstract: Multi-turn LLM agents usually reuse long context prefixes, making key value (KV) caching crucial for reducing prefill latency. SSDs provide a low-cost extension to limited DRAM capacity but introduce two key challenges. Eagerly persisting all KV cache blocks incurs substantial write traffic and rapidly consumes finite SSD endurance. Meanwhile, the small number of SSDs provisioned in typical GPU servers limits aggregate reload bandwidth, making SSD-resident KV cache much slower to retrieve than that in DRAM and inflating prefill latency. We present \textsc{Saria} (Selective Admission and Reload for Inference Acceleration), a KV caching system that jointly manages DRAM and SSD by exploiting the session-level temporal locality of LLM agents to reduce SSD writes and accelerate cache reload. On the write path, \textsc{Saria} uses eviction and reuse history to selectively persist KV cache blocks that exhibit reuse opportunities beyond their DRAM residency, avoiding unnecessary writes for KV cache already hosted in DRAM. On the read path, \textsc{Saria} promotes selected SSD-hit KV cache blocks from GPU memory into DRAM after prefill, allowing subsequent reuse within the same session to reduce SSD read traffic while limiting DRAM contention. A transfer coordinator paces DRAM reads while SSD transfers are active, allowing both paths to make progress and efficiently share GPU ingress bandwidth. We implement \textsc{Saria} on LMCache MP and evaluate it using workloads from TraceLab and WEKA, covering both full-attention and hybrid-attention models. The results show that \textsc{Saria} reduces SSD writes by 57.1--58.9\% compared with popular full duplicate caching and the mean time to first token (TTFT) by 42.3--79.7\% over DRAM-only caching.

items.title: RobustNCL: Robustifying Neuromorphic Continual Learning under Transient Faults with Lightweight Detect-and-Cure Strategy
items.abstract: In neural networks, continual learning (CL) is a prominent approach for enabling deployed systems to adapt to dynamic operational environments by effectively learning from new unseen data at runtime. Recently, the neuromorphic continual learning (NCL) concept has emerged as an energy-efficient alternative to CL by leveraging sparse event-based operations. However, NCL performance can be undermined by transient faults in the hardware platforms, which may come from high-energy particle strikes at any time. Currently, NCL reliability under transient faults has not been studied, and hence the corresponding fault-tolerance techniques remain unexplored. To address this, we propose a novel RobustNCL framework to improve NCL reliability in the presence of transient faults in the DRAM-based off-chip memory of hardware platforms through a lightweight detect-and-cure strategy. Specifically, it first monitors the presence of faults during weight data access from off-chip memory, and then cures the accessed weights if anomalous signatures are detected. It provides three curing variants: replacement with zero, min/max value, and most-probable value from the original/clean weight distribution. To support this, the weight curing values are stored in the radiation-hardened memory. Experimental results show that, in the presence of high fault rates (e.g., 5x10^{-4} for memory replay), RobustNCL maintains high accuracy close to the accuracy of fault-free models (i.e., within -0.5% accuracy for the best RobustNCL variant) and significantly improves accuracy from the baseline without fault mitigation across different NCL methods and datasets (i.e., Split MNIST, Split Fashion-MNIST, Split CIFAR-10, and Split CIFAR-100), while incurring negligible latency and energy overheads. These results highlight that our RobustNCL framework is a promising approach for enabling reliable and energy-efficient NCL systems.

items.title: Recovery of Hafnium from Mineral and Secondary Resources: Separation Chemistry, Process Intensification, Electrochemical Routes, and Industrial Perspectives (2015–2026)
items.abstract: Hafnium is indispensable to nuclear reactor control systems, high-temperature alloys, advanced electronics, and high-k dielectric technologies, yet it is rarely produced from a stand-alone ore. Its supply is therefore structurally coupled to zirconium production, and its recovery depends on one of the most difficult neighboring-element separations in extractive metallurgy. This critical review synthesizes 108 cited sources (including one 2026 institutional report) from 2015 through September 2026 using a performance-first framework that links feed mineralogy and conditioning to Zr/Hf speciation, separation mechanisms, product purity, reagent regeneration, environmental burden, and industrial readiness. The evidence indicates that the central technical challenge is not simply hafnium dissolution, but deliberately amplifying small differences in hydrolysis, anion coordination, ligand exchange, aggregation, volatility, and redox behavior. Conventional solvent extraction remains the industrial benchmark because of its throughput and flowsheet flexibility, but requirements for acidity control, scrubbing and stripping, solvent management, and coextraction control constrain sustainability. Ion exchange, extraction chromatography, functionalized adsorbents, ion-imprinted membranes, MOF/COF-derived systems, and oxo-cluster precipitation broaden the selectivity toolbox, although most still lack long-term continuous validation with realistic feeds. Thermal-halide and molten-salt routes can integrate purification with metal production but impose more demanding materials-of-construction, energy, and corrosion-control requirements. Secondary streams are strategically important because they can partially decouple hafnium supply from primary zircon throughput. The review therefore proposes a chemistry-to-flowsheet decision framework and identifies the evidence required to translate high laboratory selectivity into industrially robust hafnium recovery.
items.venue: Journal International Review of Research Studies

items.title: Quantized Analog Inference Hardware Enabled by MoS 2– Hf 1‐x Zr x O 2 FeFET Synapses
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Analog in‐memory computing can accelerate edge‐AI inference by executing vector–matrix multiplication directly in memory crossbars, but practical analog deployment is constrained by finite weight resolution and stochastic programming. Here we demonstrate program‐pulse‐engineered MoS 2– Hf 1‐x Zr x O 2 (HZO) ferroelectric field‐effect transistor (FeFET) synapses and a hardware‐consistent quantized machine‐learning workflow for noise‐robust analog inference. The device integrates an atomically thin monolayer MoS 2 channel, representing ultimate body‐thickness scaling in advanced logic roadmaps, with a CMOS‐compatible HZO ferroelectric gate stack. Operating in a near‐coercive regime, trains of identical potentiation/depression pulses yield gradual and reversible multi‐level conductance updates with ∼100 states, enabling array‐realistic programming without per‐device program‐and‐verify. Systematic pulse engineering provides knobs to tune update granularity and dynamic range, and enables offset control of the usable conductance window via asymmetric depression conditions. Crucially, we quantify cycle‐to‐cycle write variability using state‐dependent Δ G statistics and incorporate the measured quantization levels and noise directly into training and evaluation. Using MNIST as a benchmark, noise‐aware quantization‐aware training outperforms post‐training quantization across quantization levels and noise scaling, sustaining up to ∼97% test accuracy under low precision and elevated noise. These results connect measured programming physics to robust quantized analog inference and establish practical device–algorithm co‐design principles for scalable FeFET‐based synaptic hardware.

items.title: Op fysica gebaseerde compacte modellering van degradatiemechanismen van transistoren voor het ontwerp van geïntegreerde schakelingen met het oog op betrouwbaarheid
items.abstract: In order to improve transistor performance from one generation to another, new materials and new device architectures are being continuously introduced (e.g., nano-sheet transistors). But with these innovations, new challenges appear for ensuring their reliability, i.e., limited degradation during operation. As transistors are downscaled toward atomic dimensions, each stochastically behaving defect has potentially a substantial impact on the device operation. Up to now, reliability has been guaranteed at the technology level. Such approach is too restrictive, as it does not take into account the function of each transistor in the circuit. Some transistors are used less than others, while careful and controlled boosting of biases of other transistors beyond their nominal reliability limit could enormously benefit the performance of the entire application. A reliability-aware circuit design, accounting for individual device degradation, is therefore being considered.Thorough, physics-based models are already being developed and improved for the various degradation mechanisms (such as Bias Temperature Instability, Hot Carrier Degradation, etc.) occurring in different regions of the FET {Vgate, Vdrain} operating space. These mechanisms include charging of preexisting defects in the gate dielectrics and simultaneous generation of new defects, e.g. by hot carriers, compounded by significant channel temperature increases due to FET "self-heating". However, to understand the impact of the degradation on circuits, the existing physical insights need to be converted to compact models usable in SPICE-level simulations. The Thesis work therefore encompasses: i) converting the already-developed physical models into such reliability-aware compact models capable of describing the degradation of all major FET parameters, in the entire operating space as a function of an arbitrary stress history, ii) enabling the simulation of FET degradation in various analog and digital circuits and understanding the implications for various circuit parameters, and iii) design, layout, and measurement of test circuits to validate the developed compact models and the simulation methodology.

items.title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
items.abstract: Aluminum nitride-based ferroelectrics combine high remanent polarization, thermal stability, weak size effects, a wide bandgap and back-end process compatibility, making them promising for high density non-volatile memory. However, their high coercive field ($E_\mathrm{c}$) and unclear polarization switching mechanism limit further applications. Theoretical predictions indicate preferential reversed domain growth along the polar axis, whereas experiments show nearly isotropic growth or preferential growth perpendicular to this axis. Here, we combine density functional theory, Deep Potential molecular dynamics and experimental characterization to determine how nitrogen vacancies ($V_\mathrm{N}$) regulate domain growth and $E_\mathrm{c}$. In ideal crystal, strong lattice coupling along the polar axis drives preferential domain growth in this direction. $V_\mathrm{N}$ locally weakens this coupling and promotes polarization nucleation. The spatial distribution of $V_\mathrm{N}$ and the temporal sequence of vacancy induced switching jointly determine the direction and morphology of reversed domain growth. We further show that scandium doping promotes $V_\mathrm{N}$ formation, thereby enhancing defect mediated nucleation and reducing $E_\mathrm{c}$. These findings establish a multiscale mechanism governing thin-film domain-growth kinetics and macroscopic $E_\mathrm{c}$, reconciling experimental observations with ideal crystal simulations and providing defect engineering principles for low-voltage, reliable and scalable ferroelectric devices.
