items.title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization
items.abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a great benchmark for transistor model quality and consistency. To further evaluate model accuracy, we also perform analog- and digital-level simulations for various complex circuits. Our experiments reveal that NN-based models are a valid alternative to existing transistor compact models, capable of producing accurate delay and power estimates with a much higher speed and convergence time compared to the conventional Verilog-A-based industry-standard (BSIM-CMG) transistor compact model. Our NNs achieve sub-0.11% and 0.76% errors for delay and total power evaluation on a wide range of circuits, while taking up to 8 times less time during the standard cell library characterization. Additionally, we provide comprehensive information and guidance on NN accuracy, unveiling the relationship between NN size and its effect on circuit simulation precision.

items.title: Impact of mask absorber geometry on imaging stability in extreme-ultraviolet lithography with high numerical aperture
items.abstract: Extreme-ultraviolet lithography (EUVL) mask absorber patterns inherently form trapezoidal cross-sectional profiles, characterized by a sidewall angle (SWA), because of process limitations. However, this feature has often been considered a fabrication imperfection rather than an optical design parameter. To assess process tolerance, we systematically investigate how the geometric profile and optical constants of mask absorbers influence imaging performance in next-generation high-numerical aperture (NA) EUVL. A tapered sidewall alters the scattering condition at the absorber edge and thereby redistributes the amplitude and phase of the diffracted orders. These changes affect the key imaging metrics, including the normalized image log slope, best focus shift, and horizontal–vertical bias. The sensitivity to SWA variation depends strongly on the absorber material’s optical constants. In particular, a high extinction coefficient and a refractive index approaching unity substantially reduce the impact of SWA variation, thereby improving process tolerance. These findings show that absorber geometry and material properties jointly govern imaging behavior in high-NA EUV systems and provide guidelines for designing next-generation absorber materials with reduced sensitivity to SWA variation.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: High‐Temperature Molecular Ferroelectricity in Organic Cocrystal and Its Application in Tactile Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract For decades, molecular ferroelectrics have been regarded as promising alternatives to inorganic ferroelectrics, owing to their lightweight, flexibility, heavy‐metal‐free composition, and low cost. However, most reported organic compounds met the problem of low Curie point ( T c ). Here, we report a novel ferroelectric donor–acceptor (D–A) cocrystal, namely 7 H ‐benzo[ c ]carbazole–1,2,4,5‐tetracyanobenzene (BCZ–TCNB), which shows significiant polarization at room temperature and its polar structure can be maintained up to a high melting point of 502 K. Owing to the displacive ···D + A − ···D + A − ···D + A − ··· packing along a ‐axis and asymmetric orientation along c ‐axis, bi‐directional polarization behavior is observed in the symmetry breaking binary system. The thermodynamically and dynamically stable polar structure enables a high‐temperature melting state, benefiting from strong charge–transfer interaction and other intermolecular interactions. Considering its good piezoelectric coefficient, organic field‐effect transistors (OFETs) covered with BCZ–TCNB thin‐film exhibits good capability for real‐time monitoring of various signals and expressing spatial information.

items.title: High-Speed Area-Efficient VLSI Architecture of Three Operand Binary Adder Using Verilog
items.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a novel high-speed three-operand binary adder architecture, namely the Han-Carlson adder, which mitigates the inherent limitations of traditional Carry Save Adders (CSAs). The CSA's drawbacks, including slow carry propagation and increased power consumption, are alleviated by the Han-Carlson adder's innovative prefix computation and carry lookahead architecture.The Han-Carlson adder's design exploits the benefits of prefix computation to generate the carry signals in parallel, thereby reducing the critical path delay. Furthermore, the carry lookahead mechanism enables the adder to propagate the carry signals rapidly, resulting in improved speed and reduced power consumption.The proposed Han-Carlson adder is specifically designed for high-performance digital systems, where fast and efficient addition of multiple operands is crucial. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the Han-Carlson adder over traditional CSAs, showcasing its potential as a high-speed and area-efficient solution for digital arithmetic applications. Keywords Han-Carlsonadder,Three-operand binary adder, CarrySave Adder (CSA) ,Prefix computation ,Carry lookahead architecture
items.venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management

items.title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving
items.abstract: KV caching reduces the serving cost of large language models (LLMs), but the growing KV cache footprint is increasingly exceeds GPU and host-memory capacity. Therefore, people use SSD to expand the KV cache storage capacity with high I/O bandwidth. However, in production LLM workload, such as multi-round conversation and LLM agents, the total amount of KV cache writes significantly exceeds SSD capacity, shortening SSD lifetime from years to months. To improve SSD lifetime, a natural solution is to reduce the KV cache writes by gating the KV cache writes via historical access patterns. However, that significantly lowers the KV cache hit rate (and increase the LLM serving cost) since KV caches from different attention types might have identical historical access pattern but different future access patterns. Our insight is that, to reduce KV cache writes without hurting KV cache hit rate, one need to not only consider the access pattern, but also application-level information such as the attention type of KV cache. Leveraging this observation, we propose Gandalf , the first SSD KV cache offloading system with SSD life time awareness. Gandalf prioritize the admission of full-attention KV cache into SSD over the cache generated by other types of attention, which significantly increases SSD lifetime without sacrificing cache hit rate. Our evaluation shows that Gandalf extends the SSD lifetime by 7.3X on average, while having negligible impact on cache hit rate across multiple workload traces and wide range of hardware capacity. Gandalf design can be extended to other flash-based storage, such as High Bandwidth Flash (HBF).

items.title: Effect of the Channel Hole Diameter with Device Variation on 3D NAND Flash Memory
items.abstract: This work investigates the impact of channel hole geometry and fabrication-induced device variations on 3D NAND flash memory using three-dimensional technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations. The channel hole diameter (dhole) is varied over a practical range, tapered and elliptic profiles are introduced to emulate high-aspect-ratio etch distortion, and oxide-nitride-oxide (ONO) thickness fluctuation is applied to reflect deposition non-idealities. The study focuses on the programmed threshold voltage (Vth), subthreshold swing (SS), and bit-line (BL) current (IBL) of each WL and also includes the effect of read temperature in the typical operating range. The results indicate that reducing dhole increases the program efficiency while decreasing IBL. Regarding process variations, both increased ellipticity and ONO thickness were found to degrade the programmed Vth. However, while IBL increases notably with ellipticity, it exhibits a relatively weak dependence on ONO thickness. Furthermore, elevated read temperatures consistently reduce the apparent Vth and IBL, thereby tightening the sensing margin for multi-level operation. These findings elucidate the distinct impacts of geometric scaling on device variability and provide useful design guidelines for high-density memory architectures.
items.venue: JSTS Journal of Semiconductor Technology and Science

items.title: EGGPlacer: Energy-Guided Generative Chip Placement with Diffusion Models
items.abstract: Chip placement strongly affects routed wirelength and thermal behavior, yet these downstream metrics are difficult to evaluate during macro placement. Learning-based macro placers commonly optimize the macro-only half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL), denoted mHPWL, which ignores standard cell connectivity and spatial demand. In contrast, analytical mixed-size placers optimize differentiable full netlist wirelength and density objectives but are typically unaware of thermal effects. We propose EGGPlacer, an energy-guided diffusion framework that incorporates analytical placement feedback and thermal feedback into macro placement generation. An analytical placer acts as an online physical response model, exposing the standard cell distribution and a full netlist wirelength proxy induced by each intermediate macro placement, while a differentiable thermal model provides temperature feedback. These signals are formulated as composable energies and injected throughout reverse diffusion without retraining the underlying generative model. Experiments on public placement benchmarks show that EGGPlacer achieves competitive mixed-size HPWL relative to strong analytical and learning-based macro placers. In the end-to-end evaluation, EGGPlacer also obtains the lowest average routed wirelength and peak temperature among the evaluated methods. Ablation studies further demonstrate that analytical and thermal guidance provide distinct and complementary benefits across wirelength proxies, routed wirelength, and thermal objectives.

items.title: Dual‐Mode Optoelectronic Synapse Based on Ultrathin In x Ti y O Films for In‐Sensor Neuromorphic Computing and Physical Image Encoding
items.abstract: In this work, we propose a dual‐mode optoelectronic synaptic device based on an ultrathin In x Ti y O channel and demonstrate conductance‐state‐based image encoding. The ultrathin In x Ti y O channel was fabricated via ALD super‐cycle engineering, enabling precise control of the channel characteristics for optimized synaptic operation. The device operates through an interfacial charge‐trapping mechanism and exhibits both electrical and optical synaptic behaviors. Notably, nearly linear conductance modulation was achieved through the accumulation of photogenerated carriers under optical stimulation, indicating its suitability for precise synaptic weight control in neuromorphic learning systems. Furthermore, multilevel conductance states were achieved under different electrical stimulation conditions and utilized to encode image information into current maps. Even when multiple patterns overlap, the encoded information can be effectively represented through the linear superposition of current values. These results demonstrate the potential of the device to integrate sensing, memory, and security functions within a single platform. Overall, the proposed In x Ti y O‐based optoelectronic synaptic device provides a promising platform for functionally integrated in‐sensor neuromorphic systems and next‐generation AI hardware.

items.title: Dose- and exposure-controlled stop-flow atomic layer deposition of TiO2 in deep macroporous silicon: Quantifying infiltration by energy-dispersive x-ray line profiling
items.abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) enables conformal coatings on complex three-dimensional substrates, but precursor transport in deep porous systems remains strongly constrained by diffusion and surface consumption. Here, TiO2 ALD is investigated in branched macroporous silicon with pore depths of 15–30 μm and average diameters of 100 nm, corresponding to aspect ratios up to 300. Continuous-flow ALD, single-injection stop-flow ALD, and double-injection stop-flow ALD are compared in order to distinguish the respective roles of precursor dose, exposure time, and injection strategy. Cross-sectional SEM and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDX) line profiling show that continuous-flow ALD yields a Ti signal limited to only a few micrometers, whereas optimized stop-flow conditions extend the Ti-containing distribution down to approximately 22 μm without evidence of pore entrance clogging. Penetration-depth metrics derived from normalized Ti EDX profiles reveal that increasing precursor dose strongly improves infiltration, while increasing exposure time is beneficial only up to an optimum. Excessively long dwell times lead to reduced Ti signal near the pore bottom, consistent with transport limitations within the progressively coated porous network. These results establish macroporous silicon as a stringent benchmark for evaluating ALD infiltration in realistic porous semiconductors and demonstrate that EDX line profiling provides a practical process-qualification route to compare oxide infiltration in complex high-aspect-ratio architectures.
items.venue: Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A

items.title: Design and implementation of a wafer-level verification system targeting 2D-mesh interconnection networks
items.abstract: System on Wafer (SoW), as a key technological path to break through the traditional chip area limitation and achieve a leap in computing power, has become an active research focus in the field of integrated circuits in the post-Moore era. In response to the diverse, dynamic, and high-speed communication requirements in AI and high-performance computing, building a wafer-level reconfigurable switching network has emerged as an effective solution. However, constrained by implementation costs and technical barriers, current research largely remains at the stage of simulation verification using simulators such as gem5 and Garnet, lacking a verification platform that can truly reflect the physical characteristics of wafer-level system integration. To this end, this paper designs and implements a wafer-level verification system for reconfigurable switching networks, which integrates 36 switching chiplets and 288 thermal test chiplets, and provides topology/routing configuration, fault injection, and wafer-level physical parameter testing capabilities at the design level. The initial-prototype tests show that the communication rate between adjacent nodes reaches up to 145.95 Gbps and that each computing node can emulate a thermal load of up to 900 W (eight thermal test chiplets per node, each rated at up to 112.5 W).
items.venue: Journal of King Saud University: Computer and Information Sciences

items.title: Design and Evaluation of InAs/GaAs Quantum Dot Integrated Scintillation Detectors for HEP Applications. Final Technical Report
items.abstract: This Report covers the portion of the project conducted at SUNY Polytechnic Institute before the project was transferred to the University at Albany – SUNY for its third year. The third year of the project was approved and carried out at the University at Albany - SUNY under contract DE-SC0025402 ending 08/31/2026. The joint proposal from the University at Albany and Fermilab aimed to improve the performance and capabilities of a novel detector concept, which seeks to replace the relatively slow charge-drift process in semiconductors with light-collection, thereby achieving exceptional timing performance in thin, low-mass, high channel density charged particle tracking detectors. InAs Quantum Dots (QDs) embedded into GaAs semiconductor waveguide have unique scintillation properties, valuable for nuclear security, medical imaging, and high energy physics. In this work, we developed thick (~25m) epitaxial heterostructres with high luminescence efficiency composed of self-assembled nano-engineered InAs QDs grown by molecular beam epitaxy. In this type of detector, the GaAs matrix acts as a stopping material for charged particles or photons generating electrons captured by the QDs acting as luminescence centers. The QD medium is designed to provide fast capture of electrons into QDs (few ps), high QD luminescence efficiency at room temperature (>50%), and strong red-shift of photoluminescence (PL) from the GaAs absorption edge (>250 nm). Typical devices consist of a 10-25m thick GaAs layer with embedded sheets of modulation p-type doped InAs QDs and an InGaAs photodetector tuned to the QD emission wavelength. Over the duration of this project, the following tasks were completed: (a) Designed the InAs/GaAs QD structures with high light yield (~50%) with an integrated metamorphic p-i-n photodiode spectrally matched to QD luminescence. (b) Simulated light propagation and PD signal formation in the detector and read-out front end electronics and compared the signal to its LGAD counterpart using WEIGHTFIELD2 code. (c) Carried out scanning optical experiments to assess optical losses in the waveguiding scintillator. (d) Re-assessed the read-out front end electronics for the detector for improvement of the signal-to-noise ratio and optimization of the bandwidth. (e) Carried out ionization particle experiments including energetic alpha-particles (Am-241), low-energy gammas (Co-57 and Am-241) and near-MIP betas (Sr-90) with different front-end electronics. (f) Re-Assessed radiation tolerance of different QD media.
items.venue: OSTI OAI (U.S. Department of Energy Office of Scientific and Technical Information)

items.title: Datapath Width Design Space of 32-Bit RISC-V Processors for 2D Semiconductor Logic
items.abstract: The first 32-bit RISC-V processor on a two-dimensional semiconductor, a 5,931-transistor MoS2 chip, is bit-serial to fit a device-count-limited process. This work determines where the optimal datapath width departs from bit-serial execution. A digit-serial RV32I core of 1 to 32 bits is synthesized onto a model of that process, with every mapping and pipelining step formally proved. Serialization saves only about 2.5× in transistors, not 32×, because control and state do not scale with width. At the fabricated 1 kHz clock a 32-bit core thus delivers 13.5× the throughput at 5.2-5.5× lower energy per instruction. The energy ordering reverses when the throughput is fixed and the core cannot be power-gated. At the 2025 device parameters only yield selects bit-serial execution, above about 250 defects per million transistors if the 17-stage depth rule of the process is a delay budget, or 75 if it is a hard constraint. Mapper quality moves these values by up to 2.3×. Under the Poisson statistics every design yields below 1% at the published defect density, and a 10% die yield requires a 3.6-5.4× lower density, less with defect clustering. With an on-die register file, serialization saves only 11-13% of the transistors, and bit-serial execution is never the widest feasible design. Closed-form boundaries locate other technologies on this width map.

items.title: DNA Data Storage and Molecular Computing: Error-Correcting Codecs, Nanopore Basecalling, and In-Vitro Random Access Retrieval
items.abstract: Abstract—Global digital data generation is expanding at an exponential trajectory, projected to exceed 175 zettabytes within the decade. Conventional silicon-based non-volatile memory technologies—including magnetic tape, hard disk drives (HDDs), and solid-state NAND flash—are rapidly encountering insurmountable physical and logistical constraints: finite retention spans (<30 years), severe raw-material scarcity, and massive warehouse-scale electrical power consumption. Synthetic Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) establishes an ultra-dense, durable, and sustainable molecular data storage substrate, theoretically offering 215 petabytes per gram and stable biochemical retention spanning millennia at room temperature. However, translating synthetic oligonucleotides into a functional, enterprise-grade storage tier introduces severe cyber-physical and information-theoretic bottlenecks: high chemical synthesis and sequencing error rates characterized by asymmetric insertion, deletion, and substitution (IDS) channels; homopolymer-induced basecalling drift in Oxford Nanopore sequencers; high read-coverage redundancy overheads; and molecular random-access retrieval complexities in complex oligonucleotide pools. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of DNA data storage architectures. We formalize the molecular insertion-deletion-substitution channel, derive robust two-dimensional error-correcting codecs uniting inner Varshamov-Tenengolts (VT) codes with outer Reed-Solomon (RS) and Luby Transform (LT) Fountain codes, and model polymerase chain reaction (PCR) primer design optimization avoiding secondary hairpin structures. Furthermore, we construct an end-to-end biological and computational testbed encoding, synthesizing, and retrieving 50 megabytes of encrypted multi-tenant data over Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencers. Our empirical findings demonstrate that our composite VT-Fountain codec achieves 100% error-free data reconstruction under a physical sequencing raw error rate of 8.4%, while boosting net information density to 1.78 bits per nucleotide (89% of the theoretical 2.0-bit Shannon channel capacity). Concurrently, orthogonal nested PCR primers execute targeted random-access retrieval in 18.2 minutes with zero non-specific cross-hybridization. Finally, we establish open research directions in enzymatic de novo synthesis, all-molecular in-memory computing, and zero-trust bio-cybersecurity.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Antiferroelectric Phase Transitions Under Electric Fields: A Review of Physics and Applications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Antiferroelectrics, distinguished by reversible field‐driven phase transitions, hold broad promise for energy storage, cooling, and microelectronic devices. Yet the field remains fragmented by enduring debates on transition mechanisms and the absence of a framework that unifies microscopic ordering with macroscopic functionality. Moving beyond isolated progress reports, this review integrates thermodynamic formalisms, phase‐field simulations, and experimental advances to construct a coherent multiscale hierarchy. We critically reconcile phenomenological models with atomistic origins, map regulation strategies onto fundamental free‐energy landscapes, and anchor emerging applications—including negative capacitance, tunneling junctions, and thermal switches—in their underlying phase‐transition physics. We further identify CMOS‐compatible fluorite‐structured antiferroelectrics and machine‐learning‐accelerated multiscale modeling as critical translational frontiers. By bridging long‐standing fundamentals with application‐driven design, this work provides a framework to accelerate both mechanistic discovery and device innovation.

items.title: An AI‐Driven Framework for Directed Self‐Assembly Toward Design‐Technology Co‐Optimization
items.abstract: Directed self-assembly (DSA) provides a promising route for sub-10-nm patterning, but its integration into design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) remains limited by the difficulty of translating self-assembly process constraints into manufacturable layout solutions. Here, an artificial-intelligence-driven closed-loop simulation framework for DSA is presented to convert experimentally constrained DSA process knowledge into a process-constrained design-space map for DSA-aware layout decomposition. The framework integrates a three-dimensional Ohta-Kawasaki model with Bayesian optimization and convolutional neural network screening, enabling automated model calibration using experimental racetrack-template data without manual tuning. It efficiently identifies optimal model parameters, achieving a mean simulation-experiment error below 1.5 nm while maintaining morphological consistency. In addition, four multimodal large language models are further evaluated for DSA morphology screening and are shown to adapt to new image modalities and defect criteria without additional task-specific fine-tuning, relying solely on text-based rules and few-shot examples. The calibrated model enables target-constrained inverse design of experimentally validated template windows, translating DSA constraints into a manufacturable solution-space map for layout decomposition. Its extension to peanut-shaped templates without additional parameter calibration further supports DSA-aware layout decomposition and DTCO. Overall, this work establishes an intelligent closed-loop workflow linking experiment, simulation, and design, providing a practical route toward DTCO.

items.title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
items.abstract: AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next-generation ferroelectric in-memory computing architecture and radio-frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high-quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system-level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy-efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

items.title: A Review of Research Progresses in Through-Glass Via (TGV) Metallization
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs), as key vertical interconnect structures in 2.5-D/3-D advanced packaging, offer low dielectric loss, low parasitic capacitance, and excellent high-frequency transmission performance. However, several challenges remain in TGV metallization, including (1) incontinuity of seed layers in high aspect ratio TGVs; (2) non-uniform distributions of copper-ion concentration and current density, leading to significant differences in copper deposition rates between the via interior and the via opening; (3) voids, seams, and double bridging caused by excessively rapid deposition at the via opening or poor control of the central bridging position; and (4) low filling rate and resulting high cost. This article reviews the research progress in TGV metallization to address the above issues. Several electroless plating studies were reported to improve the seed layer continuity and uniformity. Adjusting the concentrations of copper ions, chloride ions, accelerators, suppressors, and levelers in the plating bath are the keys to regulating the deposition rates at the via opening, via walls, and via center. Electroplating strategies, including pulsed electroplating and multistage electroplating, can optimize the electric-field distribution inside the vias. Ultrasonic agitation enhances forced convection within the vias and thereby improves mass-transport conditions. In summary, this paper reviews the research progress in TGV metallization, with emphasis on these key challenges and corresponding solutions, and discusses their prospects for high-density interconnects in advanced packaging.

items.title: A Multimodal Piezoelectric Vertical Sidewall Architecture for Scalable In‐Plane NEMS Resonators
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The continued scaling of wireless communication systems toward higher operating frequencies and increased data traffic places growing demands on radio‐frequency (RF) resonators in terms of footprint, multiband capability, and power efficiency. While piezoelectric microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) resonators based on aluminum nitride (AlN) represent mature technology, their conventional planar designs rely on thickness‐defined frequency, which limits their chip‐level integration. We report a unified vertical in‐plane piezoelectric platform capable of multimodal lithography‐defined resonant operation using a fully released, symmetric sidewall transducer design. The resonator is first validated at the microscale, demonstrating a clear length‐extensional resonance response. This foundation is used for a further transition into the nanoscale high‐frequency regime via a cavities‐first process flow, with conformal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of AlN to realize piezo‐transducer stacks on high‐aspect‐ratio vertical surfaces. The impact of fabrication‐induced deviations, including silicon sidewall taper, process‐specific patterning approach, and AlN crystal quality, is studied using finite‐element reverse modeling. The resulting structures preserve first‐order width‐extensional operation at X‐band (∼10 GHz), while the current properties of ALD‐AlN primarily limit electromechanical performance. These results establish a scalable nanoscale fabrication and design platform for a new generation of in‐plane piezoelectric NEMS resonators and adaptive RF components.

items.title: A Multi-stationary Computing-in-memory Processor with Scalable-precision ADC for Keyword Spotting from Raw Audio Signal
items.abstract: Keyword spotting (KWS) is an essential technology for realizing always-on voice interfaces in edge devices, demanding extremely low-energy operation. Computing-in-Memory (CIM) architectures are promising for energy-efficient neural network processing by eliminating frequent external memory access. However, previous CIM-based KWS processors still suffer from low utilization in depthwise convolution (DWCONV) and significant energy consumption in analog-to-digital converters (ADCs). This paper presents an eDRAM-based CIM processor that achieves high integration density and ultra-low-energy end-to-end KWS operation through three key innovations. First, a frequency-selective stride convolution (FSSC) algorithm reduces the length of the raw audio input by 99.22%, thereby minimizing memory usage and computational complexity. Second, a multi-stationary CIM architecture maximizes hardware utilization in the DWCONV layer and reduces MAC energy by 95.26% by decreasing wordline driving activity. Third, a scalable-precision ADC optimizes capacitive digital-to-analog converter (CAP-DAC) switching energy according to the output range, achieving up to 75.71% lower conversion energy. As a result, the proposed processor achieves 95.1% accuracy on the 10-keyword Google Speech Commands dataset, with a macro-level energy efficiency of 34.8 TOPS/W and a system-level energy efficiency of 21.6 TOPS/W, consuming 0.62 µJ per decision.
items.venue: JSTS Journal of Semiconductor Technology and Science

items.title: Verified DRAM Address Mapping Reverse Engineering with Threshold Sweep
items.abstract: We propose an end-to-end software pipeline for solving and validating DRAM address mapping functions on embedded LPDDR5 systems, and we instantiate it on embedded platforms. Starting from a large latency dataset of address pairs, the pipeline first builds a latency histogram and then performs a threshold sweep to obtain candidate same-bank address pairs. For each threshold, we apply a Knock-Knock-style linear-constraint solver to recover candidate bank masks. Final bank masks are calculated using GF(2) reduced row echelon form (RREF). To verify correctness, we implement two verification stages, group verification and single function verification, inspired by prior work. Group verification checks whether bank partitions induced by the recovered masks agree with observed timing behavior. Single function verification removes one addressing function at a time and measures the resulting change in verification pass rate. Unlike approaches that return only a single inferred mapping, our workflow systematically records, for each candidate threshold, the solved bank masks and validation metrics. This pipeline supports more robust selection of bank masks on ARM-based embedded devices and provides an efficient method for reverse engineering DRAM address mapping functions and subsequent Rowhammer analysis.
