items.title: Transistörlerin Gelişimi ve Nanoölçeğe Geçiş Süreci
items.abstract: Transistör, yirminci yüzyılın ikinci yarısından itibaren bilgi ve iletişim teknolojilerinin temel yapı taşı hâline gelmiştir. Bu çalışmada, vakum tüplerine dayalı ilk elektronik sistemlerden başlayarak 1947 yılında Bell Laboratuvarları'nda gerçekleştirilen nokta temaslı transistörün icadı, eklem transistörü, tümleşik devre, MOSFET ve CMOS teknolojilerinin ortaya çıkışı kronolojik olarak incelenmiştir. Moore Yasası ve Dennard ölçekleme kuralları çerçevesinde transistör boyutlarının mikrometre düzeyinden birkaç nanometre düzeyine nasıl indirildiği ve bu süreçte karşılaşılan kısa kanal etkileri, kapı oksidi tünelleme akımları ve güç yoğunluğu sorunları tartışılmıştır. Gerilmiş silisyum, yüksek-κ dielektrik/metal kapı, FinFET ve kapı-her-yönden-saran (GAA) nanoyaprak transistörler gibi çözümler değerlendirilmiş; tamamlayıcı FET (CFET), iki boyutlu yarı iletken kanallı transistörler, karbon nanotüp transistörler, tünel FET ve negatif kapasitans FET gibi geleceğe yönelik yaklaşımlar ele alınmıştır. Sonuç olarak, klasik boyut küçültmenin kuantum mekaniksel sınırlara yaklaştığı, gelişimin artık yalnızca boyutla değil; yeni malzemeler, üç boyutlu mimariler ve sistem düzeyinde tümleştirme ile sürdürüleceği vurgulanmıştır.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The quest for the ideal power transistor: are ultra-wide bandgap devices the answer?
items.abstract: Abstract Power devices are undergoing a renaissance, driven by wide bandgap semiconductors such as gallium nitride and silicon carbide, which are rapidly displacing traditional silicon devices in electric vehicles, data centres, consumer electronics, and other key applications. On the horizon, a new class of ultra-wide bandgap materials—including aluminium gallium nitride alloys, diamond, and gallium oxide—is emerging. Thanks to their excellent material properties, these semiconductors could, in theory, enable near-ideal transistor performance with lower conduction and switching losses, as well as smaller chip footprints. In this perspective paper, we examine complexities associated with deep dopants, passivation layer selection, and the electro-thermal response during fast switching such as short-circuit events. We unravel root causes behind performance limitations and outline key innovations required to pave a path to market for devices based on these promising but challenging materials.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: The Deception of Sight: Camouflaging Chips Information Against Optical Probing Attacks By Selective Increase of Local Density
items.abstract: In recent years, a novel non-invasive laser-assisted attack known as Optical Probing (OP) has been demonstrated to effectively probe the internal state of integrated circuits. This attack exploits the relative transparency of the silicon substrate to Near-InfraRed (NIR) light, enabling optical access through the backside of the chip. Consequently, OP poses a significant threat to information processed or stored on the chip and may facilitate Intellectual Property (IP) theft or reverse engineering. Existing mitigation techniques can be broadly classified into three categories: (1) fabrication-level modifications, (2) sensor-based countermeasures, and (3) circuit-level design techniques. Fabrication-based countermeasures are costly and often incompatible with standard industrial manufacturing processes, limiting their practicality for OP-resilient chip design. Sensor-based countermeasures may be circumvented by adaptive attackers, whereas circuit-level techniques typically require modifications to the layout of standard-cell libraries. Such modifications are time-consuming and can introduce considerable PPA overheads relative to conventional standard-cell designs. Therefore, this study investigates whether increasing the local layout density around a target logic cell can enhance resilience against OP attacks without requiring modifications beyond the layout level. In this context, local density refers to the fraction of a predefined region surrounding the target cell that is occupied by neighboring logic cells and associated layout structures. Our methodology employs standard logic cells to protect the chip’s sensitive information from an adversary equipped with OP capabilities. We found that increasing the local density of surrounding logic cells near a target logic cell enhances overall reflection, effectively masking the reflection from the target logic cell. This can significantly improve the concealment of the secure cell’s information from the OP attack since the reflections from the neighboring logic cells overlap with the target logic cells that need to be secured. Hence, an adversary cannot distinguish the exact location of the source of reflection. We demonstrate that this methodology can effectively countermeasure against OP attacks by conducting detailed experiments on the relationship between density and reflection, using NAND, INVERTER, NOR, and Flip-Flop cells. We exhaustively evaluated thousands of placement strategies with varying densities to show the efficacy of our technique against OP attacks. Moreover, we demonstrate the integration of our OP attack mitigation technique into the ASIC flow for designing an AES-128 core. We demonstrate that our technique in the worst-case comes with a 1% increase in power consumption, a 1% increase in area, and no change in the operating frequency compared to the unprotected AES-128 core against OP attack.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems

items.title: Technology readiness of PFAS-free lithography materials: an anonymized survey of resist and ancillary material maturity
items.abstract: BackgroundPer- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are widely used in lithography materials because of their unique chemical and surface properties, but their extreme environmental persistence and toxicity drive increasing regulatory and sustainability pressure to eliminate their use. Substantial efforts are therefore underway to develop PFAS-free alternatives for photoresists and associated lithography materials across deep ultraviolet and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) technologies. However, an industry-wide visibility of the maturity of these PFAS-free solutions has been lacking.AimThis work aims to provide a transparent, technology-neutral snapshot of the maturity of PFAS-free lithography materials, including both photoresists and key ancillary materials, across major lithography platforms.ApproachAn anonymized lithographic materials supplier survey was conducted within a precompetitive framework using a lithography-adapted technology readiness level (TRL) scale ranging from TRL 1 to TRL 9. Participants self-assessed the maturity of their PFAS-free resists and ancillary materials for i-line, KrF, ArF dry, ArF immersion, and EUV lithography. All data were reported exclusively as aggregated TRL ranges to preserve confidentiality and avoid disclosure of proprietary or IP-sensitive information.ResultsPFAS-free resist solutions are reported for all lithography platforms, spanning TRLs 4 to 9. i-line and KrF resists show the highest readiness, including solutions approaching or reaching high-volume manufacturing. ArF dry, ArF immersion, and EUV resists are predominantly at mid-TRL levels, reflecting the ongoing performance optimization and integration work. Ancillary materials exhibit a wider dispersion in maturity, ranging from the topcoat category at TRLs 2 to 3 to PFAS-free developer rinses at TRL 9. The remaining gaps are largely driven by process integration, defectivity control, and manufacturing validation rather than fundamental chemical limitations.ConclusionsThe survey reveals that PFAS-free lithography materials are technically viable across the full lithography landscape. Although some platforms and material categories are close to manufacturing readiness, others, particularly EUV resists and selected ancillary materials, require further development. The anonymized, TRL-based assessment provides a common reference for the lithography community to prioritize R&D efforts toward fully PFAS-free lithographic manufacturing.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials, and Metrology

items.title: Surface Fluorination of ALD Tin Oxide by SF 6 Plasma for Operationally Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
items.abstract: Colloidal tin oxide (c‐SnO x ) is the dominant electron transport layer (ETL) used in efficient n–i–p perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet intrinsic oxygen‐related vacancies undermine operational stability. Here, we report a fluorinated SnO x electron transport layer (ETL) fabricated by SF 6 plasma‐assisted atomic layer deposition (ALD), in which plasma‐generated fluorine species chemisorb preferentially at oxygen vacancy (O v ) sites. Density functional theory calculations show that F and F − bind at a bridging O v with adsorption energies of −5.66 and −4.95 eV, respectively, whereas neutral SF 6 , SF 5, and SF 4 species bind weakly (−0.04 to −0.45 eV). Bader charge analysis confirms electron transfer from the SnO x surface to the adsorbed fluorine. Experimentally, the fluorination induces a surface dipole that shifts the vacuum level and elevates the work function without altering the intrinsic valence band onset of the F‐containing SnO x . This dipole‐induced vacuum level shift influences the interfacial energetics governing directional charge extraction and suppresses interfacial charge accumulation, which enhances device performance and operational stability. PSCs with SF 6 ‐plasma ALD SnO x achieve a power conversion efficiency of 21.0%, retaining 17.29% after 1400 h without encapsulation and sustaining stable power outputs for nearly 7000 min under continuous tracking. These results demonstrate superior performance and operational stability compared to thermal ALD‐grown SnO x without fluorination. The results establish plasma‐enabled interfacial fluorination as a strategy to engineer surface electrostatics and enhance the long‐term stability in perovskite photovoltaics.

items.title: Sub‐nm 2 Ferroelectric Domains via Charged 180° Walls in ZrO 2
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics ( or ) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half‐unit‐cell width (0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in thin films consisting of closely spaced head‐to‐head (HH) and tail‐to‐tail (TT) charged 180 walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk‐like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of 1–2.75 nm, yielding in‐plane domains with sub‐ footprints—among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound‐charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low‐voltage, domain‐wall‐based nanoelectronics.

items.title: Remote Charge Modulation in WSe2 Transistors via Plasma-Induced Charged Defects in hBN
items.abstract: Abstract Noninvasive carrier-density modulation is essential for two-dimensional (2D) electronics, where conventional doping often introduces lattice disorder or charged scattering centers near the transport channel. Remote doping offers a route to suppress charged impurity scattering, but commonly requires an additional charge-supply layer separated from the channel by a passive spacer. Here, we demonstrate oxygen-plasma-engineered hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as both a protective spacer and an electrostatically active remote dopant for tungsten diselenide (WSe2) field-effect transistors (FETs). Oxygen plasma treatment generates donor-like defect states near the hBN surface, enabling n-type modulation of the underlying WSe2 channel while preserving spatial separation between the charged defect states and the transport channel. The plasma-treated hBN exhibits clear electrostatic and optical signatures of defect-state formation, and the WSe2 channel remains structurally intact after treatment. The resulting WSe2 FETs show controllable n-type doping, with the doping density increasing nearly linearly with plasma-treatment time. Moreover, the increased carrier density is accompanied by enhanced mobility without an increase in the charged impurity density, indicating remote charge modulation with suppressed charged impurity scattering. This defect-engineered hBN platform provides a simple and noninvasive strategy for carrier-density engineering in 2D electronic devices.

items.title: Recessing material and process for improving contact hole patterns for high-NA and hyper-NA EUV lithography
items.abstract: In high-NA and hyper-NA EUV lithography, the reduced depth of focus (DOF) necessitates the use of thin resist films. However, increasing the resist thickness is advantageous for improving the local critical dimension uniformity (LCDU) of contact-hole patterns. This creates an inherent trade-off between LCDU improvement during exposure and DOF control in the final resist pattern. To address this challenge, we propose a new material and process scheme in which the resist is maintained at a relatively large thickness during exposure to enhance LCDU, while the effective resist thickness is reduced after development by removing the defocused upper portion of the resist. We evaluated the feasibility of this concept using a chemically amplified resist (CAR) platform. We demonstrated a process using a 70 nm-thick CAR film followed by a 30 nm recess of the top resist region, resulting in an effective final resist thickness of ∼40 nm. The LCDU was approximately 4.41 nm for the conventional process using an initially coated 40 nm-thick resist film. In contrast, the LCDU improved to 3.67 nm when a 70 nm-coated resist was followed by the 30 nm resist-recess process. These results demonstrate the feasibility of controlled resist recessing as a practical approach for extending CAR-based contact hole patterning toward high-NA and hyper-NA EUV lithography.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials, and Metrology

items.title: Realization of “Region Solar Cell” With 70% Theoretical Energy Conversion Efficiency
items.abstract: Considerable progress has been achieved in semiconductor technologies. The development of epitaxially grown, highly doped Si:P (HDSiP) for low‐voltage power metal–oxide–semiconductor field‐effect transistors has provided further clarity on the mechanism of phosphorus behavior during annealing. Furthermore, sub‐10‐nm half‐pitch critical dimension has been realized via extreme‐ultraviolet (EUV) lithography or nanoimprint lithography (NIL). In June 2024, “Region solar cell” was proposed as a potential candidate for next‐generation photovoltaics. Its theoretical energy conversion efficiency can exceed 70% owing to photon absorption and countermeasures for a detailed balance. In a 2024 paper, it was claimed that Regions could be formed using ion implantation. Although the use of ion implantation technology was novel and original, it posed significant engineering challenges. In this study, we discuss new methods for fabricating a Region solar cell using the latest or already realized technologies, namely EUV lithography and NIL, and new insights into solar cell annealing from the development of HDSiP.

items.title: Proba: A High-Performance, Low-Traffic Probabilistic Spatial Memory Streaming Prefetcher
items.abstract: Spatial Memory Streaming (SMS) prefetchers exploit recurring spatial access patterns across memory regions to predict future accesses. Despite their effectiveness, existing SMS-based designs suffer from coarse control over aggressiveness and limited adaptability to dynamic program behavior and historical patterns. In this work, we present Proba, a feedback-directed SMS-based prefetcher that integrates probabilistic pattern updates, marginal accuracy decision-making, and pattern accumulation over several trigger features to achieve fine-grained accuracy-coverage trade-offs. When accuracy deteriorates, Proba moderates its aggressiveness to prioritize accurate prefetches; conversely, when accuracy rises, it expands its coverage. Proba achieves higher speedups than any other SMS-based prefetcher while being vastly more efficient in DRAM traffic. This culminates in a large performance gap between Proba and other techniques in multicore and DRAM-constrained scenarios without harming single-threaded throughput.

items.title: Physical Reservoir Computing Using Microelectromechanical Systems
items.abstract: The growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) and edge computing has motivated the need for alternative computational frameworks such as neuromorphic computing, which can efficiently handle data‐intensive tasks. Reservoir computing (RC) is a neuro‐inspired approach for processing complex temporal data using a fixed network (the reservoir) and a simple trainable readout layer. To reduce the complexity of computation and energy consumption, physical reservoir computing (PRC) extends this concept to dynamical physical systems by exploiting their intrinsic nonlinearities and memory effects. Among the different substrates that have been proposed for PRC, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) have shown promise due to their nonlinear mechanical behavior and direct interaction with physical stimuli. Also, being compact and scalable, MEMS devices are widely used as sensors and transducers in commercial applications, making them a suitable choice for low‐power in‐sensor computing and edge intelligence applications. This review discusses recent progress in MEMS‐based PRC with a focus on its underlying principles, device architectures, and the potential of MEMS in neuromorphic computing applications.

items.title: Oxygen vacancy impacts on phase stabilization in ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide thin films with interfacial engineering
items.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide (HZO) thin films have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for nonvolatile memory and logic applications. The ferroelectricity of HZO film stems from the non-centrosymmetric orthorhombic phase, which is metastable and can be stabilized via the introduction of oxygen vacancies (Vo). To modulate Vo behaviors, a variety of processing strategies, including doping engineering, thermal annealing, and interfacial engineering, have been demonstrated to be effective in promoting phase stabilization and performance enhancement of HZO films. Nevertheless, despite the effectiveness of these approaches in enhancing ferroelectricity, the underlying mechanisms, especially the role of Vo, remain unclear. In this study, we employed capping-layer-based interfacial engineering via the deposition of Al 2 O 3 capping layers with varying thicknesses on HZO films to construct Al 2 O 3 /HZO capacitor devices. First-principles calculations based on density functional theory were carried out to calculate the interfacial energies, Vo formation energies, and Vo migration barriers, with the aim of investigating the influences of Vo on phase stabilization and ferroelectric polarization. The calculation results reveal that both the Al 2 O 3 thickness and the Vo concentration requires precise tailoring for optimizing the ferroelectric performance. These theoretical findings are in good agreement with our experimental observations. This work provides an alternative solution to facilitate the advancement of high-performance HZO-based ferroelectric devices.

items.title: Optimizing gate voltage of SiC MOSFETs to enhance the lifetime and reliability of an H-ANPC inverter
items.abstract: SiC MOSFETs offer significant advantages over their silicon counterparts, including higher breakdown voltage, faster switching speed, and better thermal conductivity, making them well-suited for high-frequency, high-voltage, and high-temperature applications in power electronics. Nevertheless, the long-term reliability of SiC MOSFETs remains a major challenge, as device failures can lead to system-level malfunctions, unplanned outages, and elevated safety risks, particularly in mission-critical applications. To assess their reliability under typical converter stresses, a hybrid-active neutral point clamped (H-ANPC) inverter is used. The H-ANPC inverter efficiently balances switching losses and thermal stress, providing higher efficiency and better thermal management, making it ideal for high-power applications requiring robust, long-term reliability. This article proposed an active gate voltage control (AGVC) technique, which is used to develop a scheme for optimizing gate voltage to improve the reliability and lifetime of SiC MOSFETs within the H-ANPC inverter. To determine the lifetime models of SiC MOSFETs in the H-ANPC inverter, two accelerated tests (ATs), the inverter-like accelerated test (IAT), and the time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) test are applied. Although the IAT-based lifetime model indicates SiC MOSFET reliability, gate voltage variations make it crucial to assess impacts on gate oxide degradation by the TDDB-based lifetime model. The article includes detailed explanations of the experimental setups for IAT, TDDB, and the H-ANPC inverter, along with an analysis of the results and lifetime modeling. Also, the AGVC scheme (AGVCS) is tested within the IAT framework, and results are provided. Together, these insights highlight strategies for enhancing the reliability and lifetime of SiC MOSFETs in H-ANPC inverter applications.

items.title: Monolithic Vertically Stacked Carbon Nanotube Transistor with Emergent Negative Transconductance for Ternary Logic
items.abstract: Abstract Vertical integration offers an opportunity to engineer transistor responses as well as device placement. Here, we demonstrate negative transconductance (NTC) using two carbon nanotube (CNT) network channels monolithically integrated on opposite sides of a common gate. The vertically stacked NTC transistor connects the channels internally through a via and retains three external terminals. Sequential processing yields a lower channel that is electron-dominant ambipolar under top-gate operation after HfO 2 deposition, while the subsequently deposited upper channel remains p-type. Their contrasting gate responses shift the current bottleneck between layers, producing a local current peak. Channel geometry and upper-layer CNT density tune this response, yielding an extracted peak-to-valley current ratio above 10 4 at a drain-voltage magnitude of 0.1 V. Paired with an n-type CNT pull-down transistor, the device enables a ternary inverter at a 3 V supply, with three output states and two voltage-gain peaks exceeding maximum 6. Comparisons across fabricated variants link the NTC profile to intermediate-state formation and reveal a trade-off between static noise margins. These results establish vertical stacking as a route to single-semiconductor transfer-function engineering for ternary logic.

items.title: Low‐Flicker‐Noise MoS 2 Transistors Enabled by High‐ κ Rare‐Earth Oxychlorides for Mixed‐Signal Electronics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The trade‐off between gate dielectric constant and interface quality limits two‐dimensional (2D) analog and mixed‐signal electronics because trap‐mediated 1/ f noise from amorphous oxides degrades signal fidelity. Here, single‐crystalline rare‐earth oxychlorides (REOCl; LaOCl and GdOCl) are employed as Cl‐terminated crystalline high‐ κ dielectrics that form atomically abrupt van der Waals interfaces with MoS 2 . MoS 2 /REOCl transistors exhibit near‐thermal‐limit switching, with minimum one‐decade‐averaged subthreshold swings of 65.7 and 63.2 mV dec −1 for LaOCl and GdOCl, with ultralow hysteresis and suppressed low‐frequency noise. Carrier‐number‐fluctuation analysis of two independently measured devices per dielectric yields effective noise‐derived interface trap densities of 1.15–1.94 × 10 10 cm −2 eV −1 , approaching the hexagonal boron nitride regime while retaining high‐ κ electrostatic coupling. Channel‐area‐scaled normalized 1/ f noise remains up to two orders of magnitude below amorphous SiO 2 /Al 2 O 3 /HfO 2 controls, with on‐state S I / I D 2 reaching ∼10 −10 Hz −1 . A Samsung 28 nm high‐ κ /metal‐gate reference process design kit sensitivity analysis, with only the flicker‐noise coefficient varied, indicates reduced voltage‐controlled oscillator phase noise and phase‐locked‐loop jitter and an effective‐number‐of‐bits improvement of up to 1.45 bits in passive noise‐shaping successive‐approximation‐register analog‐to‐digital converters. These results establish REOCl as a trap‐poor high‐ κ dielectric platform for low‐noise 2D electronics and illustrate the mixed‐signal relevance of reduced transistor flicker noise.

items.title: Label-free detection of biomolecules using a triple stacked source tunnel field-effect transistor (TSS-TFET) based biosensor: proposal and sensitivity analysis
items.abstract: Abstract A triple stacked source tunnel field-effect transistor (TSS-TFET) based biosensor incorporating a dielectric-modulated nano-cavity is proposed and numerically investigated for highly sensitive label-free biomolecule detection. The sensing mechanism exploits variations in nano-cavity dielectric constant induced by biomolecule immobilization to modulate the tunneling junction electrostatics. DC and RF performance are analyzed for a 10 nm × 2 nm nano-cavity under different drain biases, dielectric constants, and nano-cavity filling ratios. Numerical results reveal that increasing the dielectric constant from K = 1 (air) to K = 12 (Gelatin) significantly enhances device performance. At V ds = 0.5 V, the threshold voltage decreases from 0.649 V to 0.538 V, subthreshold swing improves from 52.98 mV dec −1 –22.66 mV dec −1 , and the ON-current increases by nearly seven orders of magnitude, while maintaining ultra-low OFF-current (∼10 −18 A). A high I o n / I o f f ratio of 4.66 × 1 0 11 and transconductance of 4.76 × 1 0 − 6 A V −1 are achieved, indicating excellent switching and sensing capability. Sensitivity analysis under partial nano-cavity filling demonstrates reliable detection even at low biomolecule coverage, with current sensitivity reaching 2.68 × 1 0 6 . Additionally, RF performance evaluation shows that higher dielectric constants improve gate control and carrier transport, leading to increased cut-off frequency and reduced transit time, confirming faster device response for real-time biosensing applications. The strong dependence of DC and RF parameters on biomolecule dielectric constant and nano-cavity occupancy validates the proposed TSS-TFET as a promising candidate for next-generation ultra-low-power, high-sensitivity, and high-speed biosensors.

items.title: High-speed FPGA implementation of the CORDIC algorithm using carry lookahead adders
items.abstract: This paper presents an efficient hardware architecture for sine and cosine generation using the CORDIC (Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer) algorithm. The design employs a pipelined scale-free CORDIC datapath integrated with a carry look-ahead adder (CLA) to reduce critical path delay and improve computational speed compared to conventional ripple-carry adder (RCA) implementations. To achieve an optimal balance between performance and hardware cost, hybrid CLA–RCA configurations are introduced, where CLAs are selectively used in timing-critical stages while RCAs are retained in non-critical paths. Furthermore, mutually exclusive micro-rotation techniques are utilized to reduce the number of iterations and eliminate the need for scale-factor compensation, thereby enhancing efficiency. The proposed architecture is implemented and synthesized on both FPGA and ASIC platforms to validate its performance and portability. FPGA implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 confirms accurate sine and cosine outputs with low power consumption of 0.175W, while a standard-cell ASIC realization on the open SkyWater 130 nm (Sky130) PDK using the Yosys–OpenROAD flow further demonstrates a core area of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$0.88 \textrm{mm}^{2}$$\end{document}, an achievable clock frequency of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$32 \textrm{MHz}$$\end{document}, and a total power of \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$10.2 \textrm{mW}$$\end{document}, confirming successful timing closure with zero violations across all sign-off corners.

items.title: High Energy Photon Induced Defect Engineering in Ultra‐Thin Indium Oxide Transistors for BEOL‐Compatible Logic Circuits
items.abstract: ABSTRACT As oxide semiconductors are increasingly considered for BEOL (Back‐End‐of‐Line)‐Compatible logic applications, aggressive channel scaling is required to improve electrostatic control and mitigate short‐channel effects. However, realizing ultrathin oxide channels with high uniformity and controllable electrical characteristics remains challenging, particularly under a limited thermal budget. In this work, we fabricated 1‐nm‐thick In 2 O 3 thin‐film transistors using atomic layer deposition at 150°C and subsequently tuned their electrical properties by xenon flash lamp annealing (XFLA). The XFLA treatment systematically shifted the threshold voltage in the negative direction while improving switching stability and device uniformity. Optimized devices exhibited reduced hysteresis from 1.5 to 0.76 V and improved positive‐bias‐stress stability, with the threshold‐voltage shift decreasing from 4.4 to 2.1 V after 3600 s. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed an increase in the oxygen‐vacancy‐related component from 28.4% to 33.8% after XFLA, indicating that high‐energy photon irradiation effectively modulates defect states in the ultrathin In 2 O 3 channel. Finally, by combining pristine and XFLA‐treated transistors, we demonstrated NMOS inverter operation at both 5 and 40 V, achieving a maximum voltage gain of 30. These results suggest that high‐energy‐photon‐induced defect engineering provides an effective route for threshold‐voltage control and circuit implementation in ultrathin oxide transistors for BEOL‐Compatible logic applications.

items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. To address this, we propose HAWK, a transfer mechanism that enables rapid KV cache transfer across heterogeneous devices. HAWK establishes a remote direct memory access (RDMA) path for direct cross-device transfers while handling inter-device tensor layout discrepancies as part of the transfer process. In particular, HAWK allocates tensor-layout-aware RDMA buffers on the NPU side to match the target tensor layout. Leveraging these buffers, HAWK orchestrates data transfer from a conventional contiguous GPU RDMA buffer to the corresponding NPU buffers, allowing transferred tensors to be consumed directly without additional data rearrangement while maintaining transfer efficiency. We implement and evaluate HAWK on a system built with commercially available GPUs and NPUs, demonstrating performance within 7.88% of a GPU-only system under the same SLO constraints while achieving up to 1.26$\times$ higher power efficiency and 1.72$\times$ higher cost efficiency.

items.title: Gallium‐Content‐Dependent Optical Synaptic Plasticity in Amorphous Ga‐Zn‐Sn‐O Thin‐Film Transistors
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Optoelectronic synaptic transistors integrate optical sensing with history‐dependent conductance modulation for neuromorphic information processing. Here, ultraviolet‐responsive synaptic transistors were fabricated using indium‐free amorphous Ga‐Zn‐Sn‐O (a‐GZTO) films deposited from targets with nominal Ga contents of 0.5, 1, and 2 wt.%. The devices exhibited graded composition‐dependent electrical, photoresponsive, and synaptic characteristics, with 1 GZTO generally showing intermediate behavior. O 1s peak fitting indicated that the defect‐related component decreased with increasing Ga content, consistent with the observed photoresponse and retention trends. Under 365 nm stimulation, the devices demonstrated excitatory postsynaptic current, paired‐pulse facilitation, and spike‐number‐, duration‐, and rate‐dependent plasticity. Peak‐normalized transients showed greater retention at lower Ga contents. Electrical and single‐pulse optical characteristics were evaluated across five devices per composition to assess device‐to‐device variation. For 10 UV pulses of the same width and intensity, increasing the repetition frequency enhanced the relative EPSC gain, consistent with high‐pass‐filter‐like temporal processing at the device level. These findings establish nominal Ga content as a materials‐design parameter for tuning UV response, retention, and relaxation in planar a‐GZTO transistors.

items.title: Forensic Chip-Off Acquisition of NOR Flash Memory in Router's & DVR's
items.abstract: Chip-Off Acquisition offers great feasibility to the investigator, with such technique the data recovery has been made easy to extract from the devices, which are physically damaged, burned, encrypted or password protected.After a review of available literature, limited publications were found to be discuss on data recovery of NOR Flash Memory from Router's and DVR using Chip-Off Acquisition.This study presents a detailed application of Chip-Off technique for data recovery of NOR Flash Memory from Router's & DVR's.The process involves the physical removal of NOR chip from the device, followed by cleaning, chip reading, extracting and analyzing the data using Binwalk for Router's and Bulk Extractor for DVR's.Performing Wireshark to analyze the resolved address.The Chip Off method has some difficulties such as heat control, hot enough to melt the solder but not too much to damage the chip, chip reader, software for extracting the data etc.Our findings shows how data can be extracted from the devices using Chip-Off Acquisition along with the use of Software, Binwalk, Bulk Extractor, and Wireshark.
items.venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

items.title: Ferroelectric control of Rashba spin splitting in Janus Sb2Se2Te/In2Se3 heterostructure
items.abstract: The integration of Janus two-dimensional materials with ferroelectric layers provides a promising platform for electrically tunable spintronic and nanoelectronic devices by enabling simultaneous control of charge, polarization, and spin degrees of freedom. In this work, we investigate the electronic and spintronic properties of a van der Waals heterostructure consisting of a Janus Sb 2 Se 2 Te monolayer coupled with a ferroelectric In 2 Se 3 monolayer using first-principles calculations. The intrinsic structural asymmetry of Janus Sb 2 Se 2 Te combined with the reversible polarization switching of In 2 Se 3 induces significant modulation of the electronic structure, including the bandgap, work function, and interfacial charge redistribution. Furthermore, the ferroelectric polarization provides an effective approach for controlling spin-orbit coupling and Rashba spin splitting near the conduction-band minimum. The Rashba coefficient ( ) can be reversibly tuned by polarization switching, reaching a maximum value of 1.543 , demonstrating strong electrically controllable spin splitting. These results reveal that the Janus Sb 2 Se 2 Te/In 2 Se 3 van der Waals heterostructure is a promising multifunctional platform for nonvolatile spintronic applications, including electrically programmable Rashba devices and next-generation low-power nanoelectronic systems.

items.title: Counter‐Anion‐Engineered Solid‐State Polymer Electrolytes for Vertically Stacked Artificial Synapses With Configurable Plasticity
items.abstract: Neuromorphic hardware requires artificial synapses (ASs) with configurable plasticity to support diverse signal‐processing functions while employing device architectures that minimize interconnect complexity among functional components. Electrolyte‐gated synaptic transistors enable low‐voltage conductance modulation, tunable synaptic plasticity, and mechanical flexibility through ion‐mediated operation. However, the use of gel or liquid electrolytes often compromises mechanical robustness and processability. Here, we report ASs based on solid‐state cationic polyurethane (cPU) gate dielectrics, in which Li + mobility is regulated by the counter‐anion of the cPU. Compact Br − counter‐anions suppress Li + transport and redistribution, thereby enabling long‐term synaptic plasticity. In contrast, bulky BPh 4 − counter‐anions weaken Li + coordination and facilitate Li + transport through anion exchange with Tf 2 N − , resulting in short‐term synaptic plasticity. The counter‐anion‐dependent Li + transport mechanism is validated by first‐principles calculations and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We further integrate these counter‐anion‐engineered devices into vertically stacked, array‐level architectures that implement reconfigurable AND/OR logic and in‐memory computing via multiply‐accumulate operations. This strategy establishes a foundation for future neuromorphic hardware by engineering solid‐state ion dynamics to achieve configurable plasticity, vertical integration, and multifunctional array‐level operation.

items.title: Charge-Trapping Memory Characteristics and Stability Testing of Gd2O3-Based MOS Capacitors
items.abstract: Ag/Gd2O3/Si metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) capacitors incorporating RF-magnetron-sputtered Gd2O3 dielectric layers were fabricated to investigate the influence of dielectric thickness on their structural, optical, interfacial, and electrical properties. Films deposited for 2 and 4 h produced Gd2O3 layers of 16.57 and 33.46 nm, respectively. Increasing deposition time promoted partial structural ordering and increased surface roughness, while the optical bandgap decreased slightly from 5.1 to 5.0 eV. The thicker film’s greater roughness correlated with a higher interface-state density (∼1.02 × 1011 eV–1 cm–2) compared with the thinner film (9.07 × 1010 eV–1 cm–2). Frequency-dependent C–V and G–V measurements revealed clear deep-depletion, depletion, and accumulation regions for both devices; oxide thickness strongly influenced accumulation capacitance, series resistance, and interface behavior. Clockwise C–V hysteresis in both capacitors indicates electron trapping in the Gd2O3 layer. As the sweep voltage increased from ±1 to ±5 V, the memory window widened from 0.66 to 3.05 V for the thinner film and from 1.62 to 3.51 V for the thicker film. The thicker dielectric also had better charge retention, with an extrapolated charge loss of only 3.92% compared to 6.06% for the thinner film. These findings show that tuning Gd2O3 thickness via deposition time is an effective way to optimize interface properties and improve the memory performance of high-k MOS capacitors for future nonvolatile memory applications.

items.title: AnalogPortBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Analog Circuit Porting
items.abstract: Analog circuit design still relies heavily on expert knowledge, and porting proven designs to new process nodes is a recurring bottleneck. As a lower supply reduces available voltage headroom, a working topology may require redesign or fail to meet specifications. While large language models (LLMs) have begun to generate and optimize analog circuits, existing benchmarks focus on one process node and assume feasible specifications. To bridge this gap, we introduce AnalogPortBench, a benchmark of 54 tasks for porting ten circuits, from current mirrors to telescopic amplifiers, from a 0.18 $μ$m process to the open-source SKY130 PDK. Tasks range from a direct port through a reduced supply and harder specifications to infeasible ones, and every feasible task has a reference design verified at five process corners. Evaluating six frontier LLMs at two reasoning levels, with and without simulation feedback, we find that models port simple circuits but rarely re-design headroom-sensitive amplifiers, seldom recognize infeasible specifications, and gain more from simulation feedback than from more samples or reasoning. Code and data are available at https://github.com/saeidrajabii/AnalogPortBench.

items.title: Wafer-to-Wafer bonding: Part: I - The coupled physics problem and the 2D finite element implementation
items.abstract: Wafer-to-wafer (WxW) bonding is a key enabler for three-dimensional integration, including hybrid bonding for fine-pitch Cu–Cu interconnects. During bonding, wafer deformation and the air entrapped between the wafers interact through a strongly coupled, time-dependent fluid–structure interaction (FSI) that can produce non-intuitive bonding dynamics and process sensitivities. This paper develops a mathematically consistent reduced-order model for WxW bonding by deriving a Kirchhoff–Love plate equation for wafer bending from three-dimensional linear elasticity and coupling it to a Reynolds lubrication equation for the inter-wafer air film. The resulting nonlinear plate–Reynolds system is discretized and solved monolithically in the high-performance FEniCSx framework using a C 0 interior-penalty formulation for the fourth-order plate operator, standard continuous Galerkin discretization for the pressure field, implicit time integration, and a Newton solver with automatic differentiation. Simulations reproduce experimentally reported wafer displacement histories for multiple initial gaps and verify force equilibrium at the bond front, where the Reynolds pressure acts as an effective contact reaction. Parametric studies reveal nonlinear, and in some cases non-monotonic, sensitivities of bonding-front kinetics to the initial gap, air viscosity, and interfacial energy, providing actionable trends for process optimization.
items.venue: Finite Elements in Analysis and Design

items.title: Sliding Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions with Ultrahigh Tunneling Electroresistance
items.abstract: Sliding ferroelectricity in van der Waals materials offers an appealing route to compact, nonvolatile, atomically thin ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) with low switching energy, but achieving a large resistance contrast in such devices remains challenging because the weak out-of-plane polarization provides limited electrostatic modulation of the tunneling barrier. Here, using bilayer rhombohedral MoS2 as a sliding ferroelectric barrier, we demonstrate room-temperature sliding FTJs with tunneling electroresistance (TER) values exceeding 3.2 × 105. We show that this giant contrast arises from a height-width hybrid tunneling mechanism, in which polarization reversal simultaneously modulates the tunnel barrier height and switches a nanoscale interfacial depletion width, yielding exponential amplification of the tunneling contrast. Spatially resolved tunneling, piezoresponse, and Raman measurements reveal that local strain, rather than ferroelectric domain walls, dominates spatial variations in the TER by modulating the sliding ferroelectric dipole strength, the OFF-state depletion width, and the resulting TER amplification. Finally, planar 3R-MoS2 FTJs further validate this mechanism by exhibiting a TER above 105, a switching energy density of several fJ μm-2, and projected endurance beyond 106. These results provide fundamental insight into the nanoscale electrostatics in sliding ferroelectric-based tunnel junctions while pointing toward low-energy, high-contrast nonvolatile memory applications.

items.title: Simulated Annealing-Based Resource Binding for Reliability Enhancement in High-Level Synthesis under Aging and Process Variations
items.abstract: This study addresses the growing challenges in digital circuit design due to aging and process variation, particularly in the context of nanoscale semiconductor technology. As transistor dimensions shrink, reliability issues such as Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) and Hot Carrier Injection (HCI) have a more significant impact on performance and longevity. Traditional High-Level Synthesis (HLS) methods, optimized primarily for power, area, and delay, have overlooked long-term reliability. This paper proposes a reliability-driven HLS binding methodology using Simulated Annealing (SA) and AI-assisted prediction models to integrate reliability considerations into the HLS design process. By simulating aging effects and process variation, this approach allows for better resource allocation, balancing performance, power, and reliability. The proposed methodology utilizes a synthetic dataset to model delay prediction under stress factors, employing a Random Forest regressor for accurate aging predictions. The simulation-based optimization is computationally efficient and provides reliable, degradation-aware designs. The results demonstrate that the methodology improves latency, power efficiency, and system lifetime across benchmarks, with the stream_alu benchmark showing the most significant improvements. Notably, this framework introduces reliability-aware decisions without adding area overhead, making it a practical solution for designing future digital circuits.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Robust Representation Learning for Spiking Neural Networks based on Conditional Information Bottleneck
items.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have shown great potential for low-power neuromorphic computing due to their event-driven processing and spatiotemporal sparsity, but they remain vulnerable to input perturbations, hardware-intrinsic noise, and adversarial attacks in real-world deployment. We attribute this vulnerability partly to input-specific hidden representations learned by standard SNNs trained with conventional cross-entropy loss, as our information-plane analysis empirically shows that substantial input-related information can still be retained after label-predictive information becomes stable. To address this issue, we propose SCIB, a simple yet effective robust learning objective for SNNs based on the Conditional Information Bottleneck. Different from conventional variational IB methods, SCIB replaces the mutual information compression term $I(X;S)$ with the conditional mutual information $I(X;S|Y)$ and derives a tractable variational upper bound. Moreover, it introduces a learnable class-conditional prior instead of a label-agnostic isotropic Gaussian prior, improving the expressiveness of variational compression and encouraging class-structured representations when combined with the supervised classification objective. Systematic experiments on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 under external environmental noise, neuromorphic hardware noise, and adversarial attacks show that SCIB improves robustness over standard SNNs and IB-based baselines under most evaluated noise conditions, improves adversarial accuracy under the evaluated attacks without using adversarial training, and reduces the SynOps-based single-sample inference energy consumption by 24.9% relative to an unconstrained SNN baseline.

items.title: Moore's Law: Fundamental and Technological Challenges
items.abstract: This paper discusses the fundamental and technological challenges for continuing the shrinking of transistor size under Moore's Law. Over the past few decades, making transistors smaller has boosted chip performance, reduced the cost per transistor, and supported the development of integrated circuits. However, as transistors become smaller and smaller, the traditional method of scaling is facing increasingly significant limitations. On the physical side, quantum tunneling, short-channel effects, material limits, and heat dissipation all impair the stability and reliability of transistors. On the technological side, lithography limits, manufacturing errors, yield problems, and the complexity of 3D integration have made further chip development more difficult and costly. Facing these challenges, the future of semiconductor technology should not solely depend on simply reducing transistor size. Instead, it requires the combined development of Tao's Law, alternative materials, and 3D integration. In conclusion, faced with obstacles including physical objective limitations and technical limitations, the future of Moore's Law is more likely to depend on progress in materials, structures, and manufacturing technologies, rather than only on traditional size scaling.

items.title: Monolithic GaAs Nanowires on Silicon with TiO2/MoS2 Surface Engineering for Efficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Hydrogen Evolution
items.abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting is a promising route to meet the escalating demand for clean energy and to mitigate its associated environmental impact. III–V semiconductors possess excellent optical properties and hold the record for solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency. However, their photocorrosion in aqueous electrolytes remains a major challenge. In this work, self-catalyzed GaAs nanowire (NW) photocathodes, grown monolithically on silicon (Si) substrates by molecular beam epitaxy, were protected with an amorphous titanium dioxide (TiO2) layer deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and decorated with a conformal, ∼5.5 nm polycrystalline MoS2 co-catalyst grown by plasma-enhanced ALD. The TiO2 thickness was varied (15, 37, and 47 nm), where the 37 nm layer delivered the best performance: a saturated photocurrent density of 20 mA/cm2 at –0.54 V versus RHE and an onset potential of –0.30 V in 1.0 M H2SO4 under one-sun illumination, together with stable hydrogen evolution for more than 2 h of continuous operation. Growing the GaAs NWs directly on large-area Si substrates provided a scalable route toward high-performance PEC devices and low-cost multijunction solar-fuel systems.

items.title: Monolithic 3D Stacked Carbon Nanotube/Indium–Tin–Oxide Complementary Transistors for High-Frequency Logic and Sense Amplifier Integration with Memory
items.abstract: Complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) maximize 3D integration density but face two fundamental bottlenecks: the stringent thermal budget of silicon-based sequential stacking and the inherent electrical mismatches in homogeneous material systems. To overcome these challenges, we demonstrate a monolithic 3D-stacked heterogeneous CFET architecture integrating back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible p-type carbon nanotube (CNT) and n-type indium-tin-oxide (ITO) channels. Both materials exhibit high carrier mobility and low-temperature process, which simultaneously resolve the bipolar transport disparity and mitigate thermal degradation. Consequently, the resulting CFET inverters exhibit favorable statistical uniformity and symmetric transfer characteristics, enabling the fabrication of versatile logic gates. Besides, a 5-stage ring oscillator (RO) achieves a high frequency of 334 MHz, with a 0.3 ns stage delay, demonstrating potential applications of CFET in high-speed digital circuits. Furthermore, bridging logic and memory, a CFET-based sense amplifier (SA) is integrated with an ITO-based planar capacitorless (2T0C) dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) cell. This hybrid system achieves data write/read operations and signal amplification, providing an architectural platform for next-generation ultradense 3D logic and memory systems.

items.title: Mitigating Permittivity–Charge Cross-Sensitivity in Biomolecular Sensing: Electrostatic Decoupling and Feedforward Biasing in an Asymmetric Dual-Gate a-IGZO FET
items.abstract: Abstract Permittivity-based biomolecular identification is inherently ambiguous in real-world sensing environments because analyte charge also influences the measured electrical response. Different combinations of charge and permittivity can produce similar electrical responses, so a change in the measured response cannot be uniquely attributed to permittivity. This work combines electrostatic decoupling through device engineering with charge-conditioned feedforward biasing to mitigate this cross-sensitivity and recover both analyte properties through direct drain-current readings from a single transistor. We provide a proof of concept through technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations of an asymmetric dual-gate, dual-nanogap amorphous indium– gallium–zinc oxide (a-IGZO) transistor. Gate-insulator dielectric engineering and nanogap optimization establish complementary drain-current responses, with the bottom gate pre-dominantly sensing analyte charge and the top gate predominantly sensing permittivity. Feedforward biasing further suppresses residual charge interference in the top-gate response. First, the bottom-gate drain current provides an estimate of analyte charge. This estimate and a preliminary top-gate current reading are used to select the voltage for the final top-gate measurement. The drain current measured at that voltage then determines permittivity. Three sequential current readings thus provide permittivity-based biomolecular identification without prior knowledge of analyte charge, alongside complementary charge measurement. Mean charge and permittivity extraction errors remain below 1.8% and 0.6%, respectively, across the calibration and independent test datasets. Abstract Figure

items.title: Local learning with imperfect analog synapses
items.abstract: Analog in-memory computing delivers efficient neural network inference at the edge, but systems deployed in non-stationary environments may need to adapt in situ to locally acquired data. Backpropagation faces two structural obstacles here. Its global error transport lets stochastic write errors compound across layers, and its backward pass demands bidirectional, high-precision peripheral circuitry absent from inference-oriented crossbar arrays. We introduce Channel-wise Spatial Gradient learning (CwSG), a strictly local, forward-only rule that trains each convolutional layer by rewarding spatial variation in its feature maps. In simulations replaying the measured trajectories of 1,189 phase-change memory and 1,268 filamentary memristor devices, CwSG learns with single, unverified, sub-1 V pulses. It matches backpropagation on phase-change memory with 59-fold fewer pulses and outperforms it by 53 percentage points on highly variable filamentary memristors, with 8-bit forward converters and without transposed crossbar reads or network-wide activation storage. Analog training thus becomes a problem of credit assignment, in which algorithmic design rather than hardware compensation alone overcomes severe programming noise.

items.title: Heterogeneous Integration and Thermal Management in Advanced Electronic Packaging
items.abstract: This review examines the evolution of advanced electronic packaging from monolithic integration toward heterogeneous architectures, with particular emphasis on the thermal, mechanical, materials, and manufacturing challenges that accompany higher functional density. A structured critical review method was adopted, synthesising scholarly evidence on chiplets, system-in-package configurations, multi-chip modules, 2D, 2.5D and 3D integration, interposers, through-silicon vias, hybrid bonding, thermal-interface materials, cooling technologies, modelling approaches, reliability mechanisms, and industrial implementation. The analysis shows that heterogeneous integration enables process-node optimisation, modular design, intellectual-property reuse, reduced interconnect length, improved bandwidth, and compact multifunctional systems. However, these benefits are constrained by non-uniform heat generation, hotspot interaction, vertical thermal resistance, thermomechanical stress, warpage, interfacial delamination, electromigration, solder fatigue, and material mismatch. The review further identifies co-design as the decisive requirement for balancing electrical performance, heat removal, structural integrity, manufacturability, and lifecycle reliability. Passive heat spreaders, advanced substrates, thermal-interface materials, liquid microchannels, thermoelectric devices, embedded cooling, and high-conductivity composites were found to offer complementary rather than universally interchangeable solutions. Multiphysics simulation, validated characterisation, statistical process control, digital twins, and condition monitoring are therefore essential for predictive package design and qualification. This synthesis also clarifies priority research gaps for emerging high-power and miniaturised applications. Industrial adoption additionally depends on interoperable chiplet standards, resilient supply chains, automated manufacturing, skilled personnel, and robust quality assurance. The study concludes that future progress requires integrated electro-thermal-mechanical optimisation, low-temperature bonding, embedded sensing, hotspot-targeted cooling, circular material strategies, and design-for-disassembly. Coordinated research among foundries, packaging houses, equipment manufacturers, universities, and end-use industries is recommended to accelerate reliable, sustainable, and economically scalable deployment across computing, telecommunications, automotive, energy, medical, and industrial electronics
