Electrical measurements confirm that paired‐pulse programming improves post‐disturbance resistance retention from 85%, demonstrating thermal‐budget engineering as an effective strategy for enhancing the reliability of vertically integrated 3D vertical PCM devices.

items.title: Twist-Induced Out-of-Plane Ferroelectricity in Bilayer Hafnia
items.abstract: Ferroelectric HfO2 is a promising candidate for next-generation memory devices due to its CMOS compatibility and ability to retain polarization at nanometer scales. However, the polar orthorhombic phase responsible for ferroelectricity is metastable and requires extrinsic stabilization, complicating integration with silicon. Here, we predict that twist-induced symmetry breaking in bilayer 1T-HfO2 enables robust, switchable out-of-plane (OOP) polarization. First-principles density functional theory shows that monolayer 1T-HfO2, cleaved from the (111) surface of cubic HfO2, is dynamically stable. Twisting two aligned monolayers forms a moiré superlattice that breaks interlayer symmetry and yields bistable OOP polarization. At a twist angle of 7.34°, the bilayer exhibits ∼16 μC/cm2 polarization, primarily from polar displacements within AB stacking domains. The polarization can be switched via interlayer sliding with a low energy barrier (∼8 meV per formula unit), enabling electric-field tunability in atomically thin ferroelectric devices.

items.title: Thickness‐Defined Transport Regime Toward Near‐Ideal Area‐Type Switching
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Area‐type memristors are attractive for analog in‐memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non‐pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near‐ideal area‐type switching emerges within a tunneling‐governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging‐related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta 2 O 5 /Pt in a range of 3–10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near‐short‐circuit transport with two gradual‐switching modes with different readout stability. The 5–6 nm thickness window suppresses non‐pinched hysteresis and short‐time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity‐symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near‐linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap‐assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized‐state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine‐state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi‐static I–V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse‐width‐dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog‐A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime‐defining design rule for near‐ideal area‐type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi‐state memristors for in‐memory computing applications.

items.title: Thermal Management, Packaging, and Electro-thermal Co-design of Wide- and Ultra-Wide-Bandgap Power Devices
items.abstract: Background: Wide- and ultra-wide-bandgap (WBG/UWBG) power devices offer higher blocking-field capabilities and faster switching, but increasing power density presents significant thermal management and packaging challenges. Heat dissipation depends on semiconductor properties, thermal interfaces, package geometry and cooling conditions. However, translating material- and interface-level thermal improvements into reliable device and converter performance remains challenging because of differences in operating conditions and electro-thermal constraints. Aims: To assess thermal transport, packaging and electro-thermal co-design constraints in WBG/UWBG power devices. Study Design: Focused narrative review. Methodology: Thirty journal articles were compared by structure, measurement or modelling methods, operating conditions and evidence limitations. The search was updated on 7 August 2026. Findings: Interfaces, anisotropy, package geometry and duty cycle can outweigh bulk conductivity advantages. Thermal improvements can coexist with electrical degradation. Interface measurements, simulations and pulsed demonstrations do not establish continuous converter performance or service life. Conclusion: Coupled thermal, electrical and packaging assessment is essential. The priority gaps are matched-condition comparisons, manufacturing variability and durability under representative converter operation.

items.title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
items.abstract: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under indepen dent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.

items.title: Re‐Thinking Electronic Circuit Design Through Emerging Reconfigurable Field Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Reconfigurable field-effect transistors, short RFETs, are a unique class of emerging electronic devices that merge n-type, p-type, and ambipolar operation modes into a single element. Unlike conventional MOSFETs, the dominant carrier type in RFETs is purely defined by electrostatics and can be dynamically changed at runtime. This enables new design possibilities by enabling post-fabrication functionality definition, thereby increasing circuit density and adaptability without requiring additional feature-size scaling. However, the added value of the devices requires a reassessment of classical design paradigms to unlock their full potential. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the state of the art in RFET circuit design. Starting from the underlying device physics and material systems, such as group-IV and two-dimensional (2D) materials, the manifold circuit design possibilities in digital, analog, and post-Shannon computing are introduced. We highlight how RFETs aim to enable simplified, energy-efficient, and reusable hardware for edge computing, hardware security, bio-sensing, and cryogenic electronics. Thereby, device- and circuit-level results are exemplified by measurements of transistors fabricated in an industrial 22 nm FDSOI technology. The paper also provides an overview of future key challenges in reliability, BEOL integration, and electronic design automation, offering an outlook on the path towards scalable, sustainable reconfigurable electronics.

items.title: ReHGNN: A Digital-Analog Processing-in-Memory Architecture for Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication in Hypergraph Neural Networks
items.abstract: Resistive random access memory (ReRAM) based analog processing-in-memory (APIM) architectures have been extensively explored for accelerating matrix multiplication in various artificial neural networks (ANNs). However, since the emerging hypergraph neural network (HGNN) generally encompasses large and highly-sparse weight matrices, they usually results in a significant waste of ReRAM resource for zero values when HGNNs are processed with APIM. This paper presents ReHGNN, the first hybrid digital/analog PIM architecture for HGNN inference. We abstract most operations in the aggregation phase of HGNN as sparse-dense matrix multiplication (SpMM), and explore a digital PIM (DPIM) to accelerate these SpMMs. First, we map only non-zero values of sparse matrices to DPIM arrays compactly to minimize the ReRAM resource consumption while improving computational parallelism. Second, we exploit heterogeneous crossbar arrays to accommodate the irregular distribution of sparse matrices. Third, we propose a greedy heuristic algorithm to further improve the utilization of ReRAM resource. Experimental results show that ReHGNN can improve the performance of HGNN inference by a factor of 3.4, 9.2, 15.3, 31.4, 41.3, and improve energy efficiency by a factor of 4.6, 14.1, 17.2, 363.8, and 473.4, compared with ReGNN, ReGraphX, FloatPIM, Hypergef, and GPUs, respectively.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization (TACO)

items.title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
items.abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. The asymptotic classical covariance further yields the uncertainty-based consistency criterion kBT≥ℏω0/2, which identifies regimes in which the classical equipartition covariance is incompatible with a physical quantum state. The pole construction is also generalized to finite sums of exponential memory kernels, providing an analytic treatment of environments with multiple relaxation times. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. A deterministic atomic force microscope drive translates the Wigner distribution without changing its integrated negative part, whereas environmental fluctuations suppress nonclassical interference. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.

items.title: Piezoelectric and Dielectric Enhancement in Orientation‐Engineered Freestanding Epitaxial Ba(Ti,Sn)O 3 Membranes
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterogeneous integration of freestanding single‐crystalline ferroelectric membranes offers a promising route to leverage their dielectric, piezoelectric, and nonlinear optical behavior in adaptive electronics. Crystallographic orientation engineering in these membranes further enables tuning of strain states, domain characteristics, and resulting functional properties. While orientation‐engineered Pb‐based piezoelectric membranes have been demonstrated, similar studies on Pb‐free systems remain limited. Here, single‐crystalline BaTi 0.97 Sn 0.03 O 3 (BST) membranes along three different crystallographic orientations are fabricated via an epitaxial layer lift‐off process on Indium Tin oxide (ITO)‐coated glass substrates to investigate the anisotropic dielectric, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Relaxation of substrate‐induced compressive strain promotes enhanced in‐plane and out‐of‐plane domain nucleation, yielding superior piezoelectric and dielectric responses across all orientations. An enhanced piezoelectric response in all BST membranes (61–113 pm/V) is observed. Dielectric analysis further reveals a significant enhancement in permittivity for all the freestanding membranes compared to their clamped counterparts, at frequencies above ∼10 5 Hz (∼150 at 5 MHz), indicating faster polarization relaxation dynamics. Overall, this study demonstrates the influence of crystallographic orientation on domain evolution in freestanding membranes and paves the way for their integration into next‐generation high‐frequency dielectric and microelectromechanical devices.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing with Interfacial Dynamics in Electrolytic Memristive Synapse
items.abstract: Brain‐inspired computing demands devices that operate at biological voltages and embody biological principles. Existing liquid‐based memristors offer ion‐mediated computation yet exceed physiological levels and require rigid matrices. Here, we report a hydrogel‐confined electrolytic memristive synapse (EMS) that leverages reversible Ag/AgCl interfacial electrochemistry for synaptic modulation and reservoir‐state encoding at only 100 mV. The device exhibits chloride‐ion‐dependent memristive hysteresis and emulates fundamental synaptic learning rules. Such dynamics provide the short‐term memory and nonlinearity used in a simulated reservoir‐computing framework, achieving 95.05% accuracy in handwritten‐digit classification and exhibiting good performance under noise and mechanical deformation. The device conformability and the design flexibility of the electrochemical interface offer new opportunities toward bio‐integrated systems, promising for adaptive human‐machine computing architectures.

items.title: Multilevel resistance states in van der Waals multiferroic tunnel junctions based on In 2 Se 3 /CuInP 2 S 6 ferroelectric heterostructures
items.abstract: Multiferroic tunnel junction (MFTJ) integrating magnetic electrodes with semiconducting ferroelectrics (FEs) as central tunneling barrier holds great promise for next-generation nonvolatile memory. The emergence of room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnets (e.g., Fe3GaTe2) and FEs (e.g., α-In2Se3, CuInP2S6) renders the possibility of all-vdW MFTJ under ambient conditions. Here, we employ first-principles calculations combined with nonequilibrium Green’s function methods to explore spin-dependent transport in Fe3GaTe2/α-In2Se3/CuInP2S6/Fe3GaTe2 junctions. The α-In2Se3/CuInP2S6 dual FE heterojunction introduces an additional degree of freedom for band alignment and interfacial charge modulation under external electric field, dramatically enhancing tunneling electroresistance. We find that polarization reversal leads to a giant tunneling electroresistance exceeding 6.2 × 104 %, far surpassing conventional tunnel junction with a single barrier. Furthermore, adjusting the relative magnetization of Fe3GaTe2 electrodes yields a colossal tunneling magnetoresistance up to 5.8 × 106 % upon polarization reversal. These results demonstrate the feasibility of multiple resistance states in MFTJ through coupled electric and magnetic field control, establishing ferroelectric heterojunctions as a powerful route toward high-density, multifunctional memory technologies.

items.title: Multi-channel shielding induced trap robust plasma wave rectification in AlGaN/GaN HEMT THz detectors
items.abstract: This work investigates trap-induced degradation in multi-channel (MC) GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) terahertz (THz) detectors operating in the non-resonant plasma-wave rectification regime. The THz detection characteristics of MC-HEMTs are systematically compared with conventional single-channel (SC) architectures to evaluate responsivity, transient response, and stability under surface and buffer trap conditions. The results demonstrate that the MC-HEMT achieves enhanced responsivity of 12 500 V W−1 compared with 10 000 V W−1 for the SC-HEMT under trap-free conditions due to improved carrier transport and stronger nonlinear rectification behavior. Systematic trap analysis further reveals that surface donor traps have minimal influence on the THz response after saturation of the two-dimensional electron gas density, whereas buffer acceptor traps strongly suppress plasma-wave rectification in SC devices. In contrast, the MC-HEMT exhibits significantly improved robustness against buffer-trap-induced degradation even at high trap densities ranging from 5× 1016 to 1× 1019 cm−3. Numerical physics-based simulations further shows that trap activation is primarily confined to the lower channel while the upper conducting channel remains electrostatically shielded from trap-induced carrier modulation. The results identify a channel-shielding mechanism intrinsic to MC configurations that preserves stable plasma-wave rectification under trap-loaded operating conditions.

items.title: Insights into the S-Curve Engineering in Ferroelectric-on-Top Negative-Capacitance CFET for Ultra-Low Power Computing
items.abstract: The growing demand for energy-efficient computing has intensified interest in highly scalable device technologies such as complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs). In this work, we investigate Scurve engineering for a unique ferroelectric-on-top (FE-o-T) negative-capacitance (NC) CFET through calibrated numerical simulations to assess its potential for ultra-low-power computing and supply-voltage scaling. Our results reveal that proper design of the CFET-to-ferroelectric aspect ratio and ferroelectric thickness is critical for capacitance matching and internal voltage amplification. By employing an aspect ratio of 8 with a ferroelectric thickness of 6 nm, the proposed hysteresis-free FE-o-T NC-CFET achieves a room-temperature subthreshold swing of ~30 mV/dec, a ~55% reduction in supply voltage compared with the baseline CFET, and effectively suppressed short-channel effects including drain induced barrier lowering and off current. The presented design insights may facilitate the development of energy-efficient logic technologies for future computing.

items.title: Hyper-NA EUV lithography: challenges and opportunities for advanced interconnect patterning
items.abstract: BackgroundContinued device scaling beyond high numerical aperture (NA) EUV (NA=0.55) resolution motivates the exploration of “hyper-NA” EUV lithography systems (NA≥0.75), which promise improved contrast and resolution but introduce stronger mask 3D effects, increased polarization sensitivity, and reduced depth of focus (DoF).AimWe assess whether 0.75 NA EUV can provide manufacturable imaging for post-2030 logic interconnect patterning and identify the principal ecosystem constraints on masks, depth of focus, and photoresists.ApproachWe analyze the consequences of NA scaling on the EUV scanner architecture, including mask-side angle distributions, and we model multilayer and absorber effects. Imaging performance is quantified through rigorous simulations with source mask optimization (SMO), comparing 0.55 and 0.75 NA under unpolarized illumination and central-obscuration constraints. Two representative use cases are studied: (i) a CFET Metal0 (M0) layer with 16-nm pitch lines/spaces and line-end structures, and (ii) 2D interconnect blocks down to 16-nm pitch. Photoresist effects are included via a simplified blur and absorption model, and local EPE tail behavior is assessed using ±20% dose contours with NA-scaled defocus.ResultsModest multilayer period adjustments are sufficient to support the larger mask-side angles at 0.75 NA with limited average reflectivity impact, while low-n/high-k mask absorbers improve contrast and reduce mask-3D penalties relative to standard Ta-based absorbers. Hyper NA consistently increases the image log slope (ILS)—with the largest gains observed for dark-field masks on the most critical CFET interconnect features—and reduces local EPE extremes compared with 0.55 NA in the evaluated patterns. The Rayleigh DoF at 0.75 NA decreases to ∼20 nm, indicating the need for thinner resist films and improved focus/wafer topography control.ConclusionsUnder the modeled assumptions, 0.75 NA hyper-NA EUV offers significant contrast and EPE-tail improvements for CFET-relevant interconnect layers without revealing fundamental imaging limitations, provided that mask multilayer/absorber optimization, scanner focus control, and thin-film resist performance advance in a coordinated manner.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: High-performance p-type two-dimensional transistors enabled by weak disorder engineering
items.abstract: High-performance field effect transistors (FETs) demand efficient charge doping alongside superior charge transport, which has proven challenging for p-type two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. Conventional substitutional impurity doping often induces severe lattice damage and deep-level acceptor states within 2D semiconductors, severely deteriorating carrier transport. Here, we demonstrate weak disorder engineering (WD)—a mild two-step procedure involving sulfur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation—to simultaneously achieve efficient hole doping and exceptional hole transport in 2D semiconductors (e.g., MoS2 and WS2, collectively denoted as MS2). First-principles calculations reveal that oxygen-passivated sulfur vacancies suppress deep trap states while preserving near-valence-edge occupied states (NVOS), rationalizing the simultaneous hole doping and high hole mobility. Photoelectron spectroscopy indicates the Fermi level (EF) of WD-MS2 is shifted by ~ 240 meV toward the valence band. Structural and Raman characterizations show that the mild process preserves the lattice integrity of 2D semiconductors and introduces compressive strain. Owing to NVOS‑induced efficient hole doping, suppressed deep‑trap states, preserved lattice integrity, and engineered compressive strain, the p‑type 2D WD‑MS2 FETs deliver high hole mobilities, high on/off ratios, and large current densities. Furthermore, high‑gain, low‑power 2D Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) inverters are constructed by integrating p‑type WD-WS2 FETs. Stable p-type doping of 2D semiconductors remains an important challenge towards the development of complementary 2D electronics. Here, the authors report a procedure involving sulphur vacancy creation and subsequent oxygen passivation to realize high-performance 2D MoS2 and WS2 p-type transistors.

items.title: General model and physical principles of memristor neurons
items.abstract: Locally active memristors (LAMs), owing to their excellent intrinsic brain-like properties, have become fundamental building blocks for constructing spiking neurons and implementing brain-inspired computing. Although a variety of LAM-based neurons and their computational networks have been reported, the diversity of internal physical mechanisms and neuronal structural principles makes it challenging to establish a unified theoretical framework for memristive neurons starting from microscopic physical mechanisms. This difficulty hinders the unified analysis and quantitative characterization of neural behaviors across different material systems, and restricts the widespread application of LAMs in the field of neuromorphic computing. To address this issue, this work circumvents the intricate microscopic material details and physical processes inside LAMs, and instead starts from their macroscopic electrical port characteristics and mathematical models to extract the inherent neuron-like behavioral features of the devices themselves. On this basis, we construct a general memristive neuron model applicable to different material systems and physical mechanisms, and provide the physical structural principles and parameter calculation principles underlying the model construction. This generic neuron model features a minimal topology and is capable of realizing all eight possible combinations of second-order and third-order memristive neuron designs, thereby overcoming the long-standing trial-and-error approach to determining circuit topology and parameters. Furthermore, taking a modified Chua Corsage Memristor (CCM) as an illustrative example, the theoretical design and calculations of second- and third-order memristive neuron circuits are validated. Typical brain-like behaviors, including resting states, periodic spiking, burst spike firing and chaotic spiking, are reproduced, and the formation mechanisms of different firing patterns are elucidated. This paper provides a rigorous theoretical methodology for the design and analysis of memristive spiking neurons in future brain-inspired computing, as well as for other memristive circuits such as chaotic circuits.

items.title: Electrode-Dependent Phase Stabilization and Polarization Response in Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Thin Films
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide-based ferroelectrics have emerged as a leading candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory devices, yet the relationships between fabrication conditions and ferroelectric response remain poorly understood. The structural complexity of hafnium oxide and the constraints associated with nanoscale dimension and multilayer device geometry make conventional characterization methods unsuitable for resolving detailed microstructure characteristics. Here, we use four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy to perform phase and orientation mapping and quantitatively examine the impact of electrode materials on the microstructure and remnant polarization of ferroelectric hafnium-zirconium oxide capacitors. We show that the observed remnant polarization is correlated with the polar phase fraction and alignment of the polar axis with respect to the growth direction. We also demonstrate that the interfacial oxide layer and the nonpolar polymorphs of hafnium oxide play a critical role in determining the ferroelectric polarization, as these structures give rise to depolarization fields.

items.title: Dynamic On-resistance and Charge Trapping in Gallium Nitride Power Devices
items.abstract: Aims: This review examines how charge trapping and electrical stress history influence dynamic on-resistance in gallium nitride power devices and considers the implications for measurement and converter-loss estimation. Study Design: A focused narrative review synthesising device-level mechanisms, pulsed and continuous-switching measurements, and converter-oriented interpretation. Methodology: Published journal studies were compared according to device architecture, stress conditions, measurement timing, reported findings and limitations on transferring results. Targeted literature searches were updated on 8 August 2026. No new device experiments or pooled quantitative analysis were undertaken. Findings: The reviewed evidence associates dynamic on-resistance with charge trapping in buffer, surface and gate-related regions, together with temperature and preceding bias conditions. Reported resistance changes depend on the applied blocking voltage, gate bias, pulse sequence, sampling delay and reference-resistance definition. Double-pulse tests reveal responses after defined stress intervals, whereas continuous-switching measurements examine the effects of repeated electrical histories. The relationship with voltage or switching frequency is not necessarily monotonic and cannot be assumed to be transferable between device architectures. Measurement artefacts and thermal effects can also influence the reported resistance ratio. Consequently, a single dynamic-resistance multiplier does not adequately represent all converter operating conditions. Conclusion: Dynamic on-resistance should be characterised using reproducible, device-specific procedures that document electrical history, measurement uncertainty and thermal conditions. Converter-loss estimates should reflect the relevant current waveform and switching sequence rather than relying exclusively on static resistance values.

items.title: Dissociative electron attachment dynamics in pulsed Cl2 plasma process: characteristic pulse-OFF time on chamber diameter
items.abstract: Abstract Pulsed-plasmas are widely used in semiconductor dry etching because of lower plasma-induced damage compared with continuous-wave (CW) operation. Notably, in electronegative gases such as Cl, significant amounts of negative ions form in the afterglow, producing an ion-ion plasma that enables the transport of low energy ions to the surface and thereby reducing defects of etch patterns. This work studies the impact of the chamber size on plasma loss characteristics and the resulting timescale for ion-ion plasma formation using time-resolved Langmuir probe measurements applied to plasma systems with two different diameters. Relative to the large diameter chamber, the small diameter chamber exhibited more than twice the radial electron diffusion loss and ion loss to the wall during the discharge. In the pulse-OFF phase, the plasma diffusion rates were ∼1.4 × 10 4 s − 1 and ∼2.9 × 10 3 s − 1 , demonstrating that chamber geometry strongly governs diffusion-driven losses and transient plasma behavior during upscaling. GaN etching revealed a chamber-size-dependent optimal OFF time: the etch rate peaked at 1.8 nm/min at 200 μs using the large diameter and 5.5 nm/min at 100 μs using the small diameter. These results provide practical guidance for pulse-OFF time optimization and establish a foundation for large diameter pulsed-plasma modeling toward mass manufacturing.

items.title: DC‐to‐RF Optimization of a Charge‐Plasma Cylindrical Gate‐All‐Around Nanowire TFET Under Interface Trap Charge Variation
items.abstract: A detailed study of a charge plasma cylindrical gate‐all‐around (CP‐GAA) vertical nanowire (NW) tunnel field‐effect transistor (TFET) based on technology computer‐aided design (TCAD) is presented with effects of interface trap density ( D it ) on the device DC, analog, and RF characteristics. The device relies on an intrinsic silicon nanowire of 5 nm radius and 50 nm gate length and platinum and hafnium contacts to create hole‐ and electron‐rich charge‐plasma regions through work‐function engineering rather than conventional devices. The simulated results show that the positive interface trap charge can increase the electrostatic field and improve the source‐channel band alignment; thus, the band‐to‐band tunneling probability is increased. For D it = +1 × 10 13 cm −2 , the ON‐state current is 1.82 µA (compared to 1.20 µA for the neutral condition), and the average subthreshold swing improves from ~35 to 26 mV/dec. The same positive‐trap condition leads to a peak transconductance of about 165 µS/µm and a cut‐off frequency of about 600 GHz. The gate dielectric study shows that the ON current increases with increasing dielectric constant, giving the highest current of about 1.62 µA among the four dielectrics. All interface‐trap conditions show an average subthreshold swing lower than 40 mV/dec for the proposed TFET.

items.title: CktHGVAE: A Symmetric Design/State Heterogeneous Graph Variational Autoencoder for Transistor-level Analog/Mixed-signal Circuit Design and Analysis
items.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. With a single hyperparameter configuration without topology-specific tuning, comparison between model-generated and SPICE-simulated circuit operational states gives median R2 values above 0.9 for typical single-ended voltage amplifiers and the CMOS inverter, and 0.81-0.96 for differential amplifiers with larger datasets. Latent-space optimization in the PCA-reduced latent space with Bayesian optimization, evolutionary search, random search, and quasi-exhaustive search is demonstrated for a common-source voltage amplifier with NMOS input and resistive load, where the objective function is defined as a penalty for deviation from required circuit specifications. For each search strategy, 93.3 - 100% of all design candidates suggested by the model satisfy the required circuit specifications at the decoder output, and SPICE simulations verify that 90 - 100% of them indeed satisfy the requirements. The model pretrained on a batch of topologies can be transferred to unseen topologies without retraining at all, with zero-shot reconstruction median R2 values of 0.72-0.90 in three of four scenarios, including transfer from single-ended to differential topologies, although the transfer fidelity depends on the choice of pretraining topologies. Our demonstrations suggest that the proposed model can potentially serve as a basis for AMS CMOS circuit design automation.

items.title: Charge‐Domain In‐Memory Computing With NAND‐Compatible Ferroelectric Memcapacitor Crossbar
items.abstract: Rapid growth in artificial intelligence has intensified the need for energy-efficient computing architectures beyond the conventional von Neumann paradigm. While memristive in-memory computing has attracted significant attention, its low cell resistance causes static power consumption, IR-drop-induced errors, and scalability limitations. Here, we demonstrate a NAND-compatible ferroelectric memcapacitor crossbar for scalable and energy-efficient in-memory computing. The proposed architecture employs charge-domain operation with intrinsically high cell resistance, strongly suppressing static conduction and reducing energy consumption. Optimized device design enables a large charge memory window, reliable multilevel storage, and non-destructive readout. Experimental vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) exhibits highly linear behavior due to displacement-current-based computation, which alleviates IR-drop effects. Circuit-level validation confirms practical sensing feasibility, while parasitic-aware SPICE simulations based on a 3D NAND architecture verify robust operation under deeply stacked conditions. Finally, CIFAR-10 image classification and spiking neural network inference highlight the strong potential of ferroelectric memcapacitor arrays as a scalable platform for energy-efficient neuromorphic and in-memory computing applications.

items.title: CMOS‐Compatible Hybrid Silicon and Strontium Barium Niobate Mach‐Zehnder Modulators
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence demands unprecedented speed and capacity in data communication and computing, placing stringent requirements on electro‐optic modulators—the critical components for high‐speed optical interconnects. Conventional silicon photonic modulators, limited by the plasma dispersion mechanism, struggle to meet the needs of next‐generation high‐speed, low‐power systems. While thin‐film lithium niobate offers superior electro‐optic properties, its reliance on complex wafer bonding hinders fabrication efficiency, cost‐effectiveness, and compatibility with standard CMOS processes. Here, we demonstrate a promising approach: the first design and experimental realization of a Mach–Zehnder electro‐optic modulator monolithically integrating strontium barium niobate (SBN) thin films with silicon waveguides. The SBN film exhibits a large electro‐optic coefficient ( r 33 = 145 pm/V), several times greater than that of lithium niobate. The fabricated device achieves a half‐wave voltage–length product of 2.3 V·cm. Crucially, the SBN film can be preferentially grown directly atop silicon waveguides via magnetron sputtering, eliminating the need for wafer bonding. This synergistic innovation in material and fabrication greatly simplifies the process flow, enhances compatibility with silicon photonics, and offers a viable pathway toward scalable, low‐cost photonic integrated circuits for future optical communication and computing systems.

items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. CAFE introduces C$^2$AM, a bit-significance-weighted conducting-cell activity metric that predicts output deviation and inference accuracy degradation under FeFET device variation. Guided by C$^2$AM, CAFE applies differential weight and activation encoding to eliminate sign-extension-induced conducting-cell amplification. To balance robustness and cost, CAFE performs type-wise encoding enumeration, layer-wise NSGA-II search, and post-GA pruning to allocate robust encodings where the robustness-cost trade-off is favorable. Across representative vision and language workloads, CAFE reduces C$^2$AM by up to $28.6\times$; in the main deployment study, it improves accuracy over two's-complement CIM by more than 87 percentage points and approaches full-differential robustness at $1.86$-$2.78\times$ normalized cost, compared with $3.06\times$ for uniform full-differential encoding.

items.title: Analysis of leakage current in ScAlN thin films grown on GaN/sapphire substrates by sputtering epitaxy at various temperatures
items.abstract: The leakage current of ScAlN thin films grown on n + -GaN/sapphire substrates by sputtering epitaxy at growth temperatures of 420 °C, 550 °C, and 600 °C was investigated. As the growth temperature decreased, the device-to-device variation in leakage current was suppressed, and the average breakdown field increased from 3.3 to 4.8 MV cm −1 . The measured leakage current far exceeded that predicted by Fowler–Nordheim tunneling. The temperature-dependent current–voltage characteristics exhibited an exponential increase in leakage current with increasing temperature under both positive and negative bias. Arrhenius analysis revealed that the activation energy depended on the applied electric field, with values typically ranging from approximately 0.4–0.6 eV. This field dependence suggests that multiple transport processes may contribute to the leakage current.

items.title: Access Rate-Dependent Endurance Behavior of Ferroelectric Hafnium Zirconium Oxide Capacitors
items.abstract: Fluorite-structured ferroelectrics, such as hafnium zirconium oxide ($Hf_{1-x}Zr_{x}O_{2}$), are among the most promising materials for developing the next generation of low-power nonvolatile memories. Emulating realistic operating scenarios for ferroelectric memories requires performing access rate-dependent endurance tests. The access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization cannot be described as a mere superposition of fatigue and imprint effects, which are observed in conventional endurance and retention tests, respectively. The interplay between these degradation mechanisms and its correlation with the delay time in between the programming pulses remains unclear. Combining electrical testing through voltage pulses with ab initio and drift-diffusion simulations provides a comprehensive perspective on the microscopic origin of the access rate-dependent reduction of the switched polarization of ferroelectric capacitors based on product-relevant 5 nm thick $Hf_{0.5}Zr_{0.5}O_{2}$ films. The role of oxygen vacancy defects accumulating at the electrode-ferroelectric interface with delay time in reducing the fraction of switchable domains is elucidated considering electron transfer processes which change the defect charge state. Building upon this theoretical understanding, a physics-based model to extrapolate the long-term access rate-dependent endurance performance is developed and experimentally verified for temperatures up to 135°C and delay times up to 2 ms.

items.title: A strain-aware electromechanical framework for III-nitride axial nanowire heterostructures toward an energy-efficient high-frequency tunnel FET
items.abstract: A polarization-engineered III-nitride nanowire tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) is investigated for low-energy, high-frequency operation under strain relaxation. Unlike approaches that optimize polarization-assisted tunneling primarily from an electrical perspective, the proposed framework introduces mechanical strain retention and critical structural dimensions as explicit constraints before electrical optimization. A coupled Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin tunneling analysis and finite-element electromechanical framework evaluates multiple heterostructures in terms of critical thickness, strain relaxation, polarization degradation, and tunneling strength. The InN/In \(_{0.65}\) Ga \(_{0.35}\) N/InN axial nanowire is identified as a balanced structure with strong tunneling under both coherent and relaxed strain conditions. Device simulations show steep switching with a subthreshold swing of 11.3 mV/dec at 300 K, suppressed leakage, and transconductance of 723–997 \(\upmu \) S over 225–400 K. Femtofarad-scale gate capacitance enables cutoff frequencies of 268–76 GHz, indicating potential for millimeter-wave operation. Zero-bias rectification is enabled by polarization-induced built-in electric fields, which enhance band-to-band tunneling without an externally applied DC bias. The device exhibits high intrinsic gain, low noise, and high power gain across the Ka-, V-, and early W-band ranges. System-level operation is validated using a non-quasi-static compact model for a differential power detector with high-responsivity drain-biased detection and polarization-driven zero-bias rectification, demonstrating strain-aware polarization control for strain-tolerant millimeter-wave TFET operation.

items.title: A novel analytical current model for hexagonal shaped double gate JLFET
items.abstract: A fully analytical mathematical model for drain current for the junctionless field effect transistor (JLFET) with a hexagon-shaped body has been developed and reported in this work. The model is designed to be valid in the four modes of operation- Subthreshold, bulk current, flat band, and accumulation modes. The model is based on channel resistance. Resistance for each of the three-layer types—neutral, depletion, and accumulation layers is determined first, and then the equivalent channel resistance. The subthreshold region comprises only the depletion layer, while in the bulk current mode, the overall resistance will be the parallel combination of the neutral layer and depletion layer resistances. In accumulation mode, the total resistance is derived by combining the accumulation and neutral resistances in parallel, whereas in flat band mode, only the neutral layer is present. After calculating the body's equivalent resistance, the potential model and Ohm's law were used to generate the drain current expression. The model is appropriate for compact modeling and has a completely analytical nature. The analytical drain current model is validated with technology computer-aided design (TCAD) numerical simulator and experimental results by comparing the device’s output and transfer characteristics acquired from the mathematical expressions with those computed by TCAD simulations and experimental results. The model seems to agree well with the results obtained from both TCAD simulations and experiments.
items.venue: International journal of nanoelectronics and materials

items.title: A low-voltage half-select free static memory with hybrid inverters for low-power and reliable WSN-based IoT architecture
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of wireless sensor network (WSN)-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems increases the necessity of designing SRAM cells with very low power dissipation, excellent stability, and reliable low-voltage operation. Nevertheless, traditional SRAM cells have problems of insufficient read/write stability, half select disturb, and higher susceptibility to process variations in nanometer technology nodes. In this paper, a CNTFET-enabled 10T SRAM cell with independent read/write paths, Schmitt trigger storage inverter, virtual ground write assistance, and half select disturb free operation is proposed to enhance the stability and energy efficiency. The new design is analysed in HSPICE by using the Stanford 32 nm CNTFET model and compared with the state-of-the-art CNTFET SRAM cells. Simulation results show that the proposed cell has 81% increase in read static noise margin (RSNM), 94% increase in write static noise margin (WSNM), 80% reduction in write power, 76% reduction in read power, 74% reduction in leakage power, 29% reduction in minimum operational voltage, and 109% increase in critical charge over the traditional 6T SRAM cell. Also, the RSNM and WSNM yields of the 1000 samples in Monte Carlo analysis are the largest, indicating immunity to process variations.

items.title: A BDPR-Feedback-Based LNA with Programmable RF Metrics in Real-World Settings for Wideband Wireless Communication Systems
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents a low-voltage (0.6 V), low-power Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA) operating in the $1.8-4.0$ GHz wide-band wireless communication standards. The proposed LNA, implemented in the Cadence simulation environment using a standard 45 nm PDK, integrates a tunable bulk-driven pseudo-resistor (BDPR) feedback network with the conventional architecture. Simulation results show a noise figure of 1.66 dB, a forward gain of 14.18 dB, and an input return loss of $33.7$ dB at 3.6 GHz, and almost the same can be achieved across the $1.8-4.0$ GHz wide-band by tuning the bulk bias voltage, (\(V_{bulk}\). Closely matched RF metrics achieved by the post-layout simulation validates the robustness of the proposed LNA against the parasitics. PVT analysis demonstrates its less sensitivity against the process corner variations, supply voltage fluctuations and temperature changes, whereas, Monte Carlo analysis reveals its high yield against the device-mismatches during fabrication. Moreover, the \(V_{bulk}\)-tuning leads to achieve almost the same RF metrics in these real-world scenarios, and hence, offers an effective and simple on-chip programming mechanism in real-world scenarios. Finally, low power consumption (only 6 mW) and compact design (active area is $\approx 0.080$ mm$^2$) makes the proposed LNA well-suited for 5G, IoT, and wearable RF front-ends.

items.title: Stacking-factor-integrated production planning for 3D-Stacked high-bandwidth memory manufacturing: an optimization approach
items.abstract: As AI-driven computing accelerates, demand for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) manufactured through 3D DRAM stacking and Through-Silicon-Via (TSV) technology has surged, yet existing production-planning models risk overestimating package-level capacity by treating multi-layer stacking conversion linearly. We develop a mixed-integer optimization framework that explicitly incorporates a stacking factor ( S j ) for 4-, 8-, 12-, and 16-layer HBM structures and refines turn-around-time logic to preserve physical flow consistency across extended lead times. Applied to a 6-month, three-line, fourteen-configuration case study solved via CPLEX, the baseline model produced 554,163 chips over the planning horizon while accurately converting die-level output into package-level demand fulfillment; a demand-stabilizing extension substantially reduced production disruption for high-volume configurations relative to low-volume configurations under simulated demand fluctuation. These results indicate that explicitly modeling commercial stacking constraints prevents capacity overestimation at the die-to-package conversion stage and supports more reliable production planning for high-performance, multi-layer semiconductor manufacturing.

items.title: Screening of Deep Ultraviolet Plasmonic Materials for Enhanced High-Order Harmonic Generation in the Extreme Ultraviolet
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense deep ultraviolet (DUV) pulsed lasers provides a bright, narrow-line width source of vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), extreme ultraviolet (EUV), and soft X-ray light. Its spectral and temporal properties are distinct and complementary to the radiation produced by infrared-driven HHG. Plasmonic nanostructures that can confine electromagnetic energy tightly enable the enhancement of weak nonlinear optical effects and are therefore promising for boosting the efficiency of HHG in solid-state nonlinear media. However, the DUV plasmonic nanostructures for enhanced HHG are rarely explored. We identified DUV plasmonic materials through dielectric function analysis of 19 elemental candidates and proposed a DUV plasmonic nanostructure-enhanced HHG strategy to efficiently produce coherent EUV light. Our finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations on nanodisks and nanodisk dimers revealed that Al, Mo, and Si nanostructures are superior for the confinement of DUV optical fields. Further calculations demonstrated that employing a dual-step HHG approach, involving the conversion of 810 nm light to 270 nm using a commercially accessible nonlinear crystal, followed by further conversion to 90 nm EUV through DUV plasmonic nanostructure-enhanced HHG, could result in a theoretical EUV HHG conversion enhancement of up to 107 times compared to direct ninth-harmonic generation at the surface of the solid medium. Moreover, we evaluated the thermal stability of various DUV plasmonic nanostructures under the illumination of DUV laser light. We found that Al nanobowties exhibit the strongest local electric field enhancement but suffer from the lowest thermal stability, while their Mo and Si counterparts with high material melting points are able to maintain structural integrity at the same laser intensity. We believe that our work will provide an accessible methodology to boost the development of coherent EUV light sources with improved brightness and narrow line width, which will facilitate their applications in coherent diffractive imaging as well as advanced EUV lithography.

items.title: Saliency-Guided Replay for Continual Learning in Deep Spiking Neural Networks
items.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are promising for energy-efficient neuromorphic computing, but they still suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially. This work investigates the integration of Experience Packing and Replay (EPR) as a memory-efficient continual learning strategy for deep SNNs under low-latency constraints. The proposed framework combines Batch Normalization Through Time stabilized VGG9 SNNs with Spike Activation Maps (SAM), which provide forward-only explanations based on spike activity. These explanations are temporally aggregated into spatial attention maps and used to select the most informative image patches for replay, instead of storing full images. Experiments on Split CIFAR10 and Split CIFAR100 show that SAM-guided EPR improves the accuracy-memory trade-off under tight memory budgets, and remains competitive while requiring substantially less storage.

items.title: Neuromorphic Devices for Extreme Environments: State‐Variable Reliability and Stabilization Strategies
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic devices are increasingly considered for edge‐intelligence systems operating in spaceborne, aerospace, nuclear, cryogenic, and other harsh environments, where local decision‐making is constrained by limited power, communication bandwidth, and latency. Reliable operation in these environments requires more than the preservation of basic electrical functionality because neuromorphic computation is physically encoded in material and interfacial state variables. Environmental stress can reshape these variables and alter analog modulation, plasticity, memory retention, threshold dynamics, and readout stability. This review discusses neuromorphic devices for extreme environments from the perspective of state‐variable reliability and stabilization. Radiation, temperature extremes, and vacuum or low‐pressure conditions are examined as major stressors that perturb defect generation, ionic and electronic transport, interfacial chemistry, switching pathways, and signal readout. Emerging space‐relevant factors, including microgravity‐assisted fabrication and mechanical loading, are also considered with respect to device formation, structural integrity, and long‐term reliability. Stabilization strategies are organized across material‐level design, environmental boundary control, and programming or readout compensation. By connecting device‐level degradation to neuromorphic metrics, array operation, soft‐error response, and inference accuracy, this review provides a framework for evaluating and designing reliable neuromorphic hardware under realistic environmental constraints.

items.title: Network-on-Chip Technology for Chiplet Integration Architecture
items.abstract: In today's era, the marginal benefits of transistor scaling are continuously decreasing, and Chiplet heterogeneous integration has become the mainstream path for scaling AI chip computing power. Meanwhile, on-chip interconnect performance is increasingly becoming the key factor limiting system computing power and energy efficiency. This paper focuses on on-chip network technology for Chiplet-integrated AI chip architectures, providing a systematic review and analysis of its technical principles, research status, existing limitations, and development directions. The study first breaks down the on-chip network's dual-layer architecture of 'physical architecture layer - protocol mechanism layer,' clarifying the functional roles of each core hardware unit and protocol mechanism and the complete data transmission logic. Next, from the perspectives of topology, routing algorithms, switching mechanisms, and flow control mechanisms, it summarizes the evolution of on-chip network technology and the customized research results for AI computing features and Chiplet heterogeneous scenarios. It then identifies two core current issues—inter-chiplet interconnect performance bottlenecks and lack of cross-layer collaborative design, as well as insufficient dynamic load adaptation and lagging industry standards — and outlines the key paths for future technology optimization. This research can provide clear insights into the technological development path for researchers in the field and offer theoretical support and direction for the interconnect architecture design and industrial implementation of the next-generation highly integrated AI chips.

items.title: MultiBranchFusionNet: A Lightweight Attention-Guided Dual-Branch Framework for Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Using Heterogeneous Field and Public Images
items.abstract: Tomato foliar diseases reduce yield, degrade fruit quality, and cause major economic losses, especially in regions such as Nigeria where diagnosis still relies largely on manual visual inspection. Although deep learning has improved automated plant disease recognition, many models are trained on controlled datasets that do not capture field variability. This study presents an attention-guided multi-branch transfer learning framework for tomato leaf disease classification using a heterogeneous dataset of 20,245 images from South-West Nigerian farms and public sources, spanning ten disease categories. Field-acquired labels were assigned through visual symptom assessment with expert adjudication of uncertain cases and should therefore be interpreted as symptom-based classifications rather than pathogen-confirmed diagnoses. During preliminary backbone screening, MobileNetV2 was selected as the pretrained feature-extraction pathway because it combined strong recorded classification performance with a compact model profile. MultiBranchFusionNet integrates a frozen ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV2 branch enhanced with Squeeze-and-Excitation attention and a custom convolutional branch, with feature-level fusion used to improve discrimination among visually similar disease classes. Under the evaluated mixed-source image-level protocol, the proposed model achieved 97.28% test accuracy, with macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1-score values of 96.75%, 96.69%, and 96.66%, respectively. Calibration and qualitative Grad-CAM analyses were used to examine model behaviour. The image-level partitioning strategy, together with the absence of systematically retained plant- and acquisition-group identifiers, prevented verification of independence at the plant, farm, acquisition-session, state, collection-phase, or source level. Although combining field-acquired and public images increased acquisition diversity within the assembled dataset, it did not constitute source-independent external validation. The reported performance should therefore be interpreted as internal mixed-source image-level performance rather than evidence of independent field-domain generalisation. The model has a compact size of approximately 15.28 MB, supporting its characterisation as architecturally lightweight; however, practical mobile or edge deployment remains to be established through direct device-level evaluation.

items.title: Modeling spin-orbit torque driven magnetization dynamics in emerging magnetoresistive devices: a finite element method approach
items.abstract: We present a versatile three-dimensional finite element simulation framework that couples a charge and spin drift-diffusion formalism, extended to include interfacial spin-orbit coupling, with the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. The resulting solver provides an efficient and accurate platform for modeling magnetization dynamics in emerging magnetoresistive devices such as SOT-MRAM. Its capabilities are demonstrated through simulations of current-induced magnetization switching with spin-orbit torques in a representative SOT-MRAM cell.

items.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
items.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.

items.title: Leakage-aware wide fan-in domino logic architecture using controlled keeper and stacked footer for low-power high-speed CMOS with tag comparator design
items.abstract: Abstract Wide fan-in domino logic circuits are widely used in high-speed applications such as tag comparators; however, their performance is degraded by contention, leakage and dynamic node instability in scaled CMOS technologies. A new wide fan-in domino logic circuit is presented to improve power efficiency, reduce contention and increase robustness. The proposed design employs a conditionally controlled keeper with a stacked footer network to regulate PDN, thereby suppressing leakage, reducing contention and minimizing unnecessary switching at the dynamic node. This results in lowering effective capacitance and improving evaluation speed. Simulation results in 90 nm CMOS technology for 8-64 input OR gates demonstrate up to 20% reduction in power consumption, 19% improvement in PDP and up to 1.8× improvement in noise immunity, along with 1.86× improvement in FOM and reduced variability under Monte Carlo analysis. A tag comparator implemented using the proposed circuit achieves up to 29% reduction in power consumption and 23% reduction in delay, while maintaining robust operation across PVT variations.
items.venue: Analog Integrated Circuits and Signal Processing

items.title: Integrated GaN HEMT-based terahertz metasensor with q-BIC spectral modulation for thin-film molecular fingerprinting
items.abstract: Terahertz molecular fingerprinting of thin films is limited by weak absorption and the bulky free-space paths commonly required for spectral readout. We propose a vertically integrated metasensor that combines a gap-tuned quasi-bound-state-in-the-continuum (q-BIC) metasurface with a GaN high-electron-mobility-transistor (HEMT) self-mixing detector. Radiative interference between an LC mode and a dipole mode produces a finite-linewidth q-BIC resonance, providing a frequency-selective sampling channel. The sector-antenna HEMT provides broadband electrical response. To account for electromagnetic coupling between the metasurface and antenna layers, we introduce an interlayer-corrected cascaded model that captures the effect of antenna loading on the q-BIC response. Full-wave simulations confirm that this correction preserves the designed spectral ordering and reproduces the integrated-device response with high fidelity. The resulting 36 electrical sampling channels cover 700– 1200 GHz. Within the 750– 1100 GHz analysis window, the device-encoded fingerprint features of L-tyrosine, L-arginine, and sucralose show spectral-shape correlations of 0.984, 0.976, and 0.970 with their reference absorption trends, respectively. Further loading analysis and mixture decoding show that the multichannel electrical features support thin-film thickness estimation and binary or ternary composition recovery. These results indicate that a coordinated architecture in which q-BIC pixels perform molecular spectral encoding and GaN HEMTs provide electrical transduction offers a feasible route toward compact terahertz molecular fingerprint sensors with transistor-based readout.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: In Vacuo X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Insights into the Chemical Selectivity of MgO ALD
items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) holds great promise for many applications, such as microelectronics and catalysis, due to its capability to achieve precise material deposition on targeted regions while leaving others uncoated. However, direct observation of the surface chemistry during selective deposition, a critical aspect of AS-ALD, remains limited. In this work, we utilize an integrated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)-ALD system, enabling in vacuo XPS measurements after each half or full ALD cycle to monitor elemental and chemical state evolution. Both homogeneous metal and oxide films (i.e., Ni, SiO2 and Al2O3) and heterogeneous samples consisting of metal nanoparticles on oxide supports (i.e., Ni/SiO2 and Ni/Al2O3) are employed as substrates to investigate the inherent chemical selectivity of MgO ALD from Mg(EtCp)2 and H2O at different deposition temperatures in the range of 100 to 250 °C. These MgO/Ni materials are particularly relevant for CO2 conversion catalysis. In vacuo XPS confirms the thermal reduction of native Ni oxide in high vacuum prior to MgO deposition, with supported Ni nanoparticles requiring higher temperatures than blanket Ni films. Monitoring the growth of MgO with in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry reveals differences in nucleation behavior on homogeneous blanket Ni, SiO2 and Al2O3 films during the initial ALD cycles. The inhibition of MgO ALD growth on Ni and Al2O3 at 100 °C is attributed to the presence of adventitious carbon species on the substrate surfaces, as confirmed with in vacuo XPS. However, the chemical selectivity observed on blanket SiO2 films is not fully replicated on heterogeneous Ni/SiO2 samples, underscoring the complexity of inherent AS-ALD on nanostructured substrates. Overall, this study demonstrates an effective approach for characterizing surface chemistry during (AS-)ALD and provides critical insights into the mechanisms governing inherently selective MgO deposition.

items.title: Heterogeneous Computing Systems: A Review of Architectural Evolution and Design Methodologies
items.abstract: Heterogeneous computing has emerged as an important architectural response to the slowdown of conventional semiconductor scaling, particularly in the post-Moore era. This review follows the shift from homogeneous multicore processors toward integrated platforms that place CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and domain-specific accelerators on the same die. The transition is closely related to two long-standing technology constraints, namely the slowing of Moore's Law and the breakdown of Dennard scaling, while Amdahl's Law still limits the speedup that can be obtained from parallel acceleration. From the system perspective, the review focuses on three recurring obstacles: the memory wall, cache coherence in shared-memory heterogeneous architectures, and on-chip communication supported by Network-on-Chip (NoC) designs. I also reviewed low-power VLSI approaches, especially clock gating and low-swing flip-flop designs, together with design methodologies such as SystemC-based high-level synthesis (HLS), the Catapult HLS flow, and latency-insensitive design. Based on these 24 research contributions, I organize the discussion into a multi-level technical framework for heterogeneous SoC design in AI and IoT applications.

items.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
items.abstract: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.

items.title: From Soldering to Sintering: Novel Interconnection Technology for SiC Power Device Package
items.abstract: As new energy vehicles and wide-bandgap semiconductor power devices have been used more widely, higher requirements have been put forward for packaging interconnections, above all under repeated thermomechanical loading, at high operating temperature, and at high current density. Conventional solder joints do not perform well in such a situation, since intermetallic compounds grow, voids form, and fatigue damage develops during long service, and the long-term reliability is thus weakened; therefore, three typical interconnection technologies of next-generation power devices are reviewed in this paper, that is, transient liquid-phase sintering/bonding, silver sintering, and copper sintering. Their bonding mechanisms, processing characteristics, mechanical properties, electrical and thermal performance, and major challenges are compared. TLPS can achieve low-temperature bonding and high-temperature service, but its reliability is restricted by brittle intermetallic compounds and void evolution. Ag sintering provides excellent thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity, bonding strength, and high-temperature stability, but high cost, electrochemical migration, and large-area bonding remain important concerns. Cu sintering offers low cost, good conductivity, and better resistance to electrochemical migration, while oxidation sensitivity and pressure-dependent densification limit its practical application. Finally, this review suggests that future interconnection design should balance performance, cost, process compatibility, and long-term reliability for high-power semiconductor packaging.

items.title: Fabrication and Electrical Characterization of ZnO Thin-Film Transistors Using Anodized Aluminum Oxide as Gate Dielectric
items.abstract: This study reports the deposition and characterization of zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films and the fabrication of a ZnO thin-film transistor (TFT) employing anodized aluminium oxide (AAO) as the gate dielectric. Profilometric analysis revealed a ZnO film thickness of 1,308.14 nm and an AAO dielectric thickness of 15,414.41 nm. The optical properties of the ZnO film were investigated using absorbance, transmittance, reflectance and direct optical band-gap measurements. The film exhibited stronger absorption in the short-wavelength region and increasing optical transmission toward longer wavelengths, indicating the characteristic wide band-gap optical response of ZnO. The direct optical band gap was determined to be 3.20 eV. Electrical characterization of the fabricated ZnO/AAO TFT demonstrated clear gate-voltage dependent drain-current modulation, consistent with n-channel ZnO TFT operation. The threshold voltage was approximately 6.20 V, while the maximum drain current reached 2.864 mA. An off-state current of 17.37 µA resulted in an on/off current ratio of approximately 164.84. The maximum transconductance was 3.002 mS, and the subthreshold swing was approximately 206 mV/decade. The extracted field-effect mobility was 4.15 cm²/Vs, indicating measurable charge transport and effective gate modulation in the ZnO channel. The results demonstrate that the ZnO/AAO structure possesses the essential optical and electrical characteristics required for thin-film transistor applications. Further optimization of ZnO microstructure, defect concentration, dielectric/interface quality and deposition conditions could improve carrier transport and switching characteristics.
items.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY

items.title: Emergent Phenomena in Wurtzite Ferroelectric Semiconductors
items.abstract: The emergence of ferroelectricity in wurtzite-structured semiconducting materials broadens the material landscape beyond traditional perovskites, introducing design rules for scalable nanoelectronic devices with an inherent thermal robustness. These materials combine large spontaneous polarization, ultrathin scalability, and compatibility with back-end-of-line processing. This review discusses the state-of-the-art and recent progress in understanding their ferroelectric behavior, from atomic-scale switching pathways and proximity-triggered, electrically controlled polarization states to charged yet intrinsically stable domain walls. Progress in compositional tuning, strain and interface engineering, heterostructure design, and advanced synthesis strategies is highlighted, including key material and device challenges for the integration of wurtzite ferroelectrics into next-generation memory, logic-in-memory, and neuromorphic computing systems.

items.title: Device Design Implications on RON×QOSS FOM in p-GaN Power HEMTs: A Simulation Study
items.abstract: In this paper, we analyze by means of numerical simulations the device design implications on the RON×QOSS Figure of Merit (FOM) in p-GaN power HEMTs to be employed in soft-switching converters. During switching, p-GaN power HEMTs experience dynamic RON increase but also dynamic QOSS reduction, effectively establishing a trade-off between the two device parameters. This trade-off stems from the physical mechanism of hole redistribution within the C-doped buffer. Device design choices such as field plate length, channel and buffer thickness as well as C-doping concentration influence both parameters; however, the relative variation of the two parameters is not necessarily symmetric. Simulations are therefore carried out to identify the best device design choices depending on the target trade-off between RON and QOSS.

items.title: Crystallographic Parity and Inverse Area Scaling in Two-Dimensional Perovskite Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
items.abstract: Ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for next-generation high-density non-volatile memory; however, conventional polycrystalline oxide FTJs face issues with defect-induced leakage and degraded ferroelectricity at nanometer scales. Here, we demonstrate atomically defined nanocrossbar FTJs based on single-crystalline two-dimensional (2D) Dion-Jacobson perovskite nanosheets designed to address these scaling challenges. Electrical transport measurements reveal crystallographic-parity-dependent switching behavior: odd-layered (m = 3, 5) homologs exhibit hysteretic switching consistent with ferroelectric tunnel barriers, whereas even-layered (m = 4, 6) homologs show non-switching behavior consistent with paraelectric controls. Simmons-model analysis supports direct tunneling as the dominant transport mechanism through the atomically uniform nanosheet barriers, even at the smallest junction area of 520 nm2. Notably, the tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio increases as the junction area decreases, reaching approximately 35, consistent with the suppression of defect-induced OFF-state current inhomogeneity under nanoconfinement. These FTJs show strong non-volatile retention (extrapolated to 10 years) and reliable switching endurance (100 cycles) at room temperature. These results highlight that crystallographic layer parity and nanoconfinement-enabled defect avoidance serve as key design principles for scalable 2D ferroelectric tunnel devices and facilitate pathways toward ultra-dense post-Moore memory and neuromorphic computing architectures. This favorable scaling behavior aligns lateral miniaturization with improved memory contrast and, together with the metal-electrode nanocrossbar architecture, provides a promising basis for high-density integration if wafer-scale nanosheet assembly and reproducible interface control can be established.

items.title: Analysis on Optoelectronic Properties of ZnO/TiO₂ Heterostructure-Based Phototransistors with Semiconductor Process and Device Characterizations
items.abstract: Wide-bandgap oxide semiconductors such as ZnO and TiO₂ are traditionally limited to ultraviolet photodetection due to their bandgaps exceeding 3.0 eV. This paper examines the optoelectronic properties of a visible-light phototransistor based on the heterostructure of ZnO and TiO₂, fabricated through atomic layer deposition (ALD) of TiO₂ onto spin-coated ZnO films. The study demonstrates that oxygen-related subgap states introduced within the TiO₂ layer enable visible-light absorption through trap-assisted photocurrent generation, circumventing the intrinsic bandgap limitation. Photoelectron spectroscopy measurements confirm the presence of these subgap states and reveal a favorable conduction band offset of approximately 0.08 eV between TiO₂ and ZnO, facilitating efficient electron transfer. The optimized TiO₂/ZnO phototransistor, achieved by controlling the titanium isopropoxide purge time during ALD to 10 seconds, exhibits a photoresponsivity of 99.3 A W⁻¹ and photosensitivity of 1.5 × 10⁵ under 520 nm illumination. This approach offers a viable pathway for developing visible-light photodetectors using environmentally stable, all-oxide heterostructures.

items.title: AiSAQ-in-Filtering for DRAM-free Filtered Information Retrieval
items.abstract: Filtering search is one of the crucial applications of approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). In filtering search, label information is used in conjunction with unstructured vector data. ANNS provides efficient similarity search in large-scale datasets, however, the memory footprint of storing both vector data and their associated label becomes a significant cost factor as dataset sizes grow. To address this problem of increasing DRAM usage, we propose AiSAQ-in-Filtering, with a novel quantization method called LiPQ (Label-inclusive Product Quantization). LiPQ combines unstructured data and structured labels into a single representation, leading no growth of encoded data. Our proposal increased recall@1 of single-label searches by up to 55% and fewer disk I/Os compared with existing methods. This also retains the main advantages of AiSAQ, which can reduce DRAM footprint by up to 1/78 and index switching time comparing with existing methods. This proposal can also be applied to sparse-dense hybrid search beyond label filtering such as semantic and keyword search of documents.

items.title: A Variational Neural-Field Interpretation of the Stereo-CeNN Architecture in Light of Disparity-Tuned Cortical Organization
items.abstract: Stereoscopic vision relies on the ability of the visual system to estimate binocular disparity across the visual field. In computational models, stereo matching can be represented through multiple candidate disparity hypotheses defined over retinotopic position. In this work, we reinterpret the Stereo Cellular Neural Network, here referred to as Stereo-CeNN, within a continuous variational framework and introduce a neural-field representation defined over the joint domain of retinotopic position and disparity. In this interpretation, the discrete activities of the Stereo-CeNN are regarded as samples of a continuous activity field r(x,d,t), where different disparity layers correspond to populations tuned to different disparity preferences. The binocular input drives these populations according to local matching evidence, while spatial interactions within each disparity channel promote coherent activity across neighboring retinotopic locations.
