The final disparity estimate is obtained, consistently with the original Stereo-CeNN architecture, by selecting the disparity channel with the largest steady-state response at each retinotopic position. We show that the layer-wise organization and local spatial dynamics of the Stereo-CeNN admit a continuous neural-field counterpart, establishing an explicit structural and variational correspondence between the discrete retinotopy–disparity lattice and a population-level representation of stereopsis. This formulation provides a conceptual bridge between the independently developed Stereo-CeNN architecture and the mesoscale organization of disparity-selective populations observed in visual cortex, without implying a one-to-one anatomical or physiological correspondence. Because Cellular Neural Networks are locally connected dynamical systems originally conceived for analog and mixed-signal VLSI implementation, the same organization is also compatible with general neuromorphic principles of local, parallel, and distributed computation.

items.title: Voltage-weighted effective charge as a statistical damage coordinate for time-dependent dielectric breakdown in 1.2-kV SiC MOSFET gate oxides

items.title: Toward Partitioned Reference Readout for Four-Level IGZO Memory: Device Statistics, Confusion Matrices, and INT4 Error Propagation
items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. We analyze 107 measured DC transfer curves from 37 isolated IGZO transistors (W/L = 3/0.5 micrometers). Four gate-bias operating points inferred from the first sweep are evaluated on later sweeps of 35 devices. Device-resolved operating points reduce second-sweep across-device current standard deviation by 49.4-52.4%, yet retaining initial thresholds increases misclassified points from 37/140 to 55/140. Leave-one-device-out reference estimation gives 0/140 on the second sweep; freezing second-sweep thresholds yields 6/140 on the third. Sampling eight reference transistors on the third sweep gives a mean held-out error fraction of 0.15% over 2,000 selections, versus 4.33% with frozen thresholds on matched held-out devices. We present conditional confusion matrices, a counterfactual common-gain sensitivity, and an INT4 error-propagation proxy. A simultaneous four-state bank with eight reference cells per state requires at least 32 physical reference cells, 12.5% of a proposed 256-cell data bank before peripheral overhead. A charge-conservation model and a partitioned hierarchical error model specify the pulse, retention, and array measurements needed to test transfer from DC device statistics to pulsed 2T0C operation.

items.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Parameter Optimization of Oxide-Based Memristor Characteristics Using Genetic Algorithms
items.abstract: Abstract We present a multiobjective, physics-informed optimization framework for oxide-based memristive devices that jointly minimizes forming voltage (Vf) and maximizes memory contrast (HRS/LRS). The proposed approach integrates COMSOL Multiphysics with MATLAB through a genetic algorithm (GA), enabling self-consistent electrothermal simulations and systematic exploration of a high-dimensional design space encompassing geometrical, electrical, thermal, and operational parameters. By optimizing 13 key variables, the GA efficiently identifies optimal trade-offs between switching efficiency and resistance ratio. The optimization results demonstrate a substantial enhancement in device performance, with the high-resistance-state to low-resistance-state ratio (HRS/LRS) improved by up to 21× relative to the reference device, while alternative optimized configurations achieve a reduction in Vf down to 0.7× of the reference value. A parameter-importance analysis based on a random forest model highlights oxide thickness and effective electrical and thermal conductivities as influential parameters. Importantly, the optimization further reveals nontrivial multiparameter trade-offs, demonstrating that reductions in Vf and enhancements in HRS/LRS can be simultaneously achieved through coordinated tuning of geometrical, material, and pulse-related parameters beyond simple intuitive design rules. Overall, the MATLAB–COMSOL co-optimization strategy provides a scalable and generalizable computational design methodology for next-generation low-power, high-contrast RRAM devices, and offers quantitative insights into the coupled physical mechanisms underlying filament formation and rupture.

items.title: LATCH: LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness for Post-Route FPGA Optimisation
items.abstract: Post-route FPGA timing closure remains expert-dependent and computationally expensive. We present LATCH (LLM-Assisted Timing Closure Harness), a two-layer framework that separates large language model (LLM) orchestration from deterministic FPGA implementation and evaluation. Across sixteen designs and seven LLMs, a single-iteration study compares three agent control granularities - expert-written recipes, direct EDA operations and LLM-constructed procedures - to ask how much control an agent needs per attempt. Functional-pass rates are 98.2%, 71.4% and 17.9%, respectively; yet direct operations give slightly larger 3.4% median Fmax gains when passing, versus 3.2% for recipes. This exposes a trade-off between execution reliability and timing improvement. Informed by this trade-off, a multi-iteration study fixes the action tier at expert recipes to ask how repeated attempts are best organised, comparing a fitted deterministic heuristic with sequential LLM reasoning, branching exploration and knowledge base-guided exploration within 12 checkpoints per run. Branching raises mean maximum-frequency improvement from 10.5% (sequential) to 16.0%, and the knowledge base to 20.3%, improving 15 of 16 designs. Characterisation across 2,421 recipe attempts profiled their gain and validation rates, showing hard-block re-placement gives the largest cumulative mean gain at 41.4MHz.

items.title: Indium gallium zinc oxide channel-integrated crystallization for wake-up-free HfZrO x metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor gate stacks
items.abstract: Multilevel programming in ferroelectric neuromorphic hardware benefits from a well-defined initial polarization state; wake-up-induced polarization evolution can cause the same programming pulse to produce different polarization states during early operation. Here, we identify the semiconductor/ferroelectric integration sequence as a critical materials-design variable and demonstrate an indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) channel-integrated crystallization route for HfZrOₓ metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor (MFS) gate stacks. The 10-nm-thick IGZO channel is deposited on 16-nm-thick HfZrOₓ before annealing and retained during crystallization, enabling completion of the MFS gate stack with a single anneal and without sacrificial-metal removal. The completed stack exhibits a well-developed as-fabricated polarization–voltage (P–V) loop and only a 2.3% change in switchable polarization after 105 bipolar cycles. By contrast, a complete sacrificial-TiN reference route shows a 39.0% wake-up increase followed by a 20.9% post-wake-up decrease. Starting from this well-defined as-fabricated polarization state, pulse amplitude, pulse width, and displacement-current compliance provide controlled access to intermediate polarization, including 16 current-controlled polarization levels. Ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) fabricated from the same gate stack convert the programmed polarization into four ordered threshold-voltage states. By linking the integration sequence to wake-up-free initialization, multilevel programming, and transistor-level readout, this work establishes a direct materials-to-function pathway relevant to oxide-semiconductor neuromorphic applications.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: High-mobility enhancement-mode thin-film transistors with 1.5 nm-thick ALD-grown Sn-doped In2O3 channels
items.abstract: Aggressive channel thickness scaling to the sub-2 nm regime is essential for strengthening electrostatic gate control in monolithic three-dimensional electronics, but it causes severe carrier depletion and transport degradation in In2O3 thin-film transistors (TFTs). Here, we demonstrate enhancement-mode TFTs with 1.5 nm-thick Sn-doped In2O3 (ITO) channels prepared by inhibitor-assisted atomic layer deposition. At the same physical channel thickness, the ITO TFT exhibits a field-effect mobility of 25.7 ± 1.4 cm2V−1s−1, a subthreshold swing of 129 ± 31 mV/dec, and a threshold voltage of 0.2 ± 0.2 V, whereas the undoped In2O3 TFT undergoes severe transport degradation. The ITO TFT also shows markedly improved positive-bias-stress stability, with a threshold voltage shift of 0.37 V after 3600 s, whereas the thickness-matched In2O3 TFT reaches 2.07 V within 1000 s and fails before 3600 s. Analysis of the effective mobility and sheet carrier density indicates that Sn doping mitigates carrier depletion in the sub-2 nm channel. The resulting carrier replenishment improves on-state transport and strengthens electrostatic screening against positive-bias-induced trap charging, thereby improving the mobility–positive-bias-stress stability balance. These results establish controlled Sn doping as an effective strategy for realizing high-mobility ultrathin In2O3 TFTs with positive-bias-stress stability for monolithic three-dimensional electronics.

items.title: FlashT2S: GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators for Heterogeneous Neuromorphic LLM Backends
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence faces two growing challenges: computational bottlenecks and energy inefficiency inherent to the von Neumann architecture. Neuromorphic computing offers a promising alternative, yet its immature ecosystem still relies on conventional systems for data supply, requiring efficient conversion between tensor and spike dataflow. We observe a clear mismatch, where data conversion is slow while downstream computation is fast. As data size grows quadratically with large language models, this mismatch becomes a major bottleneck. In this work, we examine the data-conversion components that appear on the critical path of training and inference in neuromorphic LLMs. The work presents FlashT2S (Flash Tensor-to-Spike): GPU-Accelerated Tensor-to-Spike Conversion Operators, which applies architecture-aware and data-centric optimizations to reduce conversion latency. Experimental results show that FlashT2S delivers an average speedup of 850.78x over the native operators across individual operators and 802.83x in realistic workloads. Additionally, compared with GPU kernels automatically generated by torch.compile, our kernels achieve 5-11x speedups. Notably, it achieves near-optimal absolute performance: large-scale conversions are reduced to tens of microseconds (10-99 us), while small-scale conversions reach single-digit microsecond levels (less than 10 us). Furthermore, its standardized output enables seamless integration across heterogeneous backends, including diverse neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: FPGA-based Power & EM Side-Channel Cryptanalysis on GIFT-128 and Development of secure Trojan-free physical design for GIFT-128 with minimized transistors
items.abstract: The rapidly evolving field of the Internet of Things revolves around the transmission of data through wired or wireless networks. A crucial aspect within this domain is ensuring the security of the data being transmitted within optimal timeframes. PRESENT is a well-known lightweight cryptosystem for wireless communication. GIFT is an improved version of it. It is designed to optimize throughput. This paper presents the hardware implementation of the GIFT cipher on an FPGA, including simulation with a testbed. The process involves the generation of random plaintext and keys, which are inputs to the cipher, followed by conducting power leakage analysis and electromagnetic (EM) leakage analysis on GIFT. Subsequently, based on these analyses, a secure Trojan-free VLSI Physical design of GIFT has been presented. The paper also outlines the schematic designs of the GIFT cipher, along with the verification of layout and simulation results.

items.title: Evolution mechanism of damage locations in drift region of SiC MOSFETs under heavy ion irradiation
items.abstract: This paper investigates the evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations in the drift region of the SiC MOSFETs under different applied drain voltages (VDS(irra)) during heavy ion irradiation using 587 MeV 36Kr ions. It is interesting to find from the post-irradiation blocking I–V curves that the drain–source leakage current increases significantly at about 500 V for the case under relatively low VDS(irra) (175–300 V) and increases rapidly at low voltage for the case under relatively high VDS(irra) (350 V). To explain this phenomenon, a local damage-related lifetime-model along the ion track is proposed and validated by technology computer-aided design simulations. The model indicates that thermal damage will develop near the p-base/n-drift junction once the damage near the n-drift/n-sub junction along the ion track becomes sufficiently serious with increasing VDS(irra). The proposed evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations can help analyze mechanisms of single-event leakage current and single-event burnout in SiC devices and guide radiation-hardening designs for SiC devices.

items.title: Engineering Ag+ flux via PMMA incorporation for stable threshold switching and temporal neuromorphic processing in flexible SnO2 quantum dot memristors
items.abstract: In this work, flexible Ag/SnO2 quantum dots (QDs):PMMA (1:0, 1:0.5, 1:1, and 1:1.5)/ITO memristors were fabricated by blending SnO2 QDs and PMMA at different volume ratios. The polymer-assisted Ag+ migration engineering strategy enables effective regulation of conductive filament evolution, inducing a controllable transition from unstable nonvolatile resistive switching to highly stable threshold switching (TS). The Ag/SnO2 QDs:PMMA (1:1)/ITO device exhibits a switching window of ∼25, stable TS over 104 cycles, and excellent mechanical reliability after 104 bending cycles at a bending radius of 4 mm. The polymer matrix modulates Ag+ migration kinetics, facilitating the formation of uniformly distributed metastable. Benefiting from these characteristics, the Ag/SnO2 QDs:PMMA (1:1)/ITO device enables leaky integrate-and-fire and adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire neuron functions. Furthermore, the intrinsic volatile conductance relaxation enables time-dependent image feature extraction by dynamically modulating convolutional weights through Ag filament evolution. This work demonstrates that polymer-assisted Ag+ migration engineering provides an effective strategy for developing flexible volatile memristors toward compact neuromorphic computing hardware.

items.title: Energy constraints in large scale artificial intelligence and insights from human cognition for efficient large language models
items.abstract: Large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) systems, especially large language models (LLMs), face growing constraints related to energy use, power delivery, memory traffic, experimentation, and infrastructure capacity. These pressures are often studied separately, which makes it difficult to understand how they interact across the full AI lifecycle. This review develops a cross-layer framework that brings these constraints together and examines whether resource-allocation strategies observed in human cognition can inform more sustainable AI design. We compare human and artificial systems by function rather than anatomy, focusing on how each allocates limited resources to learning, search, memory, external support, optimization, and inference. Using a systematized narrative-review approach, we identified 6284 records, screened 898 at the full-text stage, and selected an initial set of 150 focal studies for detailed synthesis. We organize the evidence into seven interacting regimes covering scaling, experimentation, hardware power limits, data movement, infrastructure, evaluation incentives, and inference allocation. The framework extends Green AI by linking these layers and translating insights from human cognition into testable design hypotheses and measurable evaluation criteria. The strongest near-term opportunities include data selection, energy-aware experimentation, hardware-supported low-precision computation, and demand-adaptive inference. However, most reported gains are based on proxy measures such as operations, memory, latency, or data volume rather than direct end-to-end energy measurements. Near- and in-memory computing show longer-term promise, while retrieval, tool use, distributed experts, and multi-agent systems may shift or increase energy costs through communication and repeated inference. These findings support cross-layer co-design and end-to-end evaluation at matched capability, reliability, latency, and service quality.

items.title: Emerging Nanoelectronic Technologies for Next-Generation VLSI: Devices, Challenges, and Prospects
items.abstract: The continuous scaling of CMOS technology enables significant progress in performance and integration density in VLSI. However, due to short-channel effects, leakage currents, interconnection delays, variability effects, and power-density limitations, at the current sub-5 nm feature size, the conventional scaling down of CMOS is becoming more and more challenging. This research work discusses a few promising nanoelectronic devices beyond the conventional CMOS, such as CNTFETs, TFETs, nanowire FETs, SETs, graphene-based devices, and spintronic devices. The principle of operation, characteristics, scalability, CMOS compatibility, and perspectives of VLSI application of the devices under consideration are comparatively analyzed. Possible problems related to the integration of the devices, including fabrication scalability, device variability, process complexity, cost, reliability, and thermal issues, are discussed. It is shown that heterogeneous and monolithic 3D integration can be effective methods for combining special-purpose nanoelectronic devices with traditional CMOS technology. Perspectives related to the application of 2D materials and negative-capacitance devices are discussed.

items.title: EXPERIMENTAL STUDY OF THE DEAD-TIME COMPENSATION ALGORITHM FOR GAN HEMT BASED INVERTER FOR AC ELECTRIC DRIVES
items.abstract: This paper presents the experimental evaluation of a dead-time compensation algorithm based on the instantaneous directions of phase currents in a voltage source inverter (VSI). The mechanism by which dead time affects the accuracy of stator voltage vector reproduction is analyzed. The compensation algorithm is implemented in the stationary (a-b) reference frame by introducing a corrective voltage vector whose magnitude and polarity are determined by the dead-time interval and the signs of the motor phase currents. The algorithm was investigated through both experimental testing and mathematical simulation for six dead-time values using two induction motors with different power ratings. The results demonstrate a high level of agreement between simulation and experimental data and confirm that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the nonlinearity of the inverter input-output characteristic and mitigates phase-current waveform distortion over the entire range of investigated dead-time values. The greatest improvement is achieved in the low-output-voltage region, where the influence of dead time is most pronounced.

items.title: Decoupling Trap States in Amorphous Oxide Semiconductor Transistor Using a Conductive-Semiconducting-Conductive MOS Structure
items.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. In conventional test structures, non-ideal metal-AOS contacts convolute the conductance loss generated by various trap states. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. Our results yield bias-resolved trap profiles and reveal three distinct regimes: (1) In the depletion region, interface states dominate the conductance loss. These states exhibit sub-microsecond time constants and their density increases slightly with deeper depletion, which is associated with donor-like states. (2) From weak to moderate accumulation, shallow states become the primary contributor, displaying a Gaussian-like volumetric density-of-states distribution with response times spanning from microseconds to nanoseconds. (3) In the strong accumulation regime, interface states regain dominance with an increased state quantity, while their time constants remain invariant. These bias-resolved profiles clarify how different trap populations impact AOS transistors under distinct operating conditions, providing intuitive metrics for understanding reliability degradation. Consequently, the CSC structure offers a simple, scalable, and robust platform for trap characterization in AOS transistors.

items.title: Decoupled Multiplicative Physics-Guided Neural Network for Extrapolative Modeling of GaN HEMT
items.abstract: Rapid direct-current (DC) surrogate modeling of gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) requires accurate prediction of the current-capability, conduction-loss, and self-heating indicators used in geometry screening. This work presents an electrothermal decoupled multiplicative physics-guided neural network (ET-DM-PGNN) for this task. It combines a gray-box backbone, separate high- and low-field polarization channels, a latent DC self-heating update, and bounded target-specific multiplicative residuals. A two-stage strategy first calibrates the complete surrogate and then refines the current branch while preserving resistance and temperature. On 32 interstitial samples, ET-DM-PGNN achieves R2>0.997, with mean absolute percentage errors of 0.13%, 0.15%, and 0.04% for Imax, Ron, and Tmax, respectively. The corresponding errors on nine external cases are 1.46%, 0.94%, and 0.74%. A leakage-controlled, three-seed level-held-out audit yields errors of 0.44-6.40% in four composition and lateral-geometry directions, whereas holding out the 0.015 µm barrier level produces errors of 12.41-21.21% under the tested training protocol. Across 365 geometries, 4 updates differ from a 12-step reference by at most 0.0076%. Numerically validated at Vgs=3 V using TCAD DC sweeps extending to Vds=15 V, the surrogate supports rapid fixed-protocol geometry screening and identifies the ultrathin-barrier direction as the least reliable tested extrapolation regime.

items.title: Competing Hysteresis Mechanisms in HZO/MoS2 Transistors with a Metal-Ferroelectric-Metal-Insulator-Semiconductor Gate Stack
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors based on hafnium oxide offer a versatile platform for advanced memory concepts. Here, we demonstrate a proof-of-concept top-gated Hf0.5Zr0.5O2-based transistor integrating a metal-ferroelectric-metal-insulator-semiconductor (MFMIS) gate stack with a two-dimensional MoS2 channel. The implementation of such an architecture is particularly challenging in MoS2, where the strong sensitivity of the channel to trapped charge can further complicate the balance between ferroelectric switching and charge redistribution within the MFMIS stack. By varying the MFM-to-MIS area ratio and the applied gate-voltage amplitude, we observe a systematic evolution of the transfer hysteresis consistent with competing ferroelectric polarization switching and trap-related contributions. Temperature-dependent measurements, zero-bias write/read experiments, and compact SPICE modeling provide additional support for this interpretation. Despite the non-optimized gate stack, a substantial ferroelectric contribution to the device response is retained, while retention measurements reveal limitations associated with depolarization and trapping. These results demonstrate the feasibility of MFMIS ferroelectric transistors based on MoS2 and provide a basis for further optimization of their gate-stack design and memory performance.

items.title: Bipolar Hot Carrier‐Driven Switchable Photocurrent Polarity in Plasmonic‐Functionalized Phototransistor for All‐Optical‐Configured Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocarrier engineering in semiconductors is critical for developing advanced optoelectronic devices. Plasmonic hot carriers enable effective modulation of the photocarrier behavior in semiconductor systems, yet their full potential is restricted by the exploitation of unipolar charges. Herein, by integrating a plasmonic Ag nanoplate layer with an asymmetric MoS 2 transistor, we introduce a plasmon‐enabled photocarrier engineering strategy that achieves vertical bipolar‐hot‐carrier (both hot electrons and hot holes) harvesting and utilization in an n‐type 2D material device for the first time. Hot electron injection into the MoS 2 channel leads to a maximum 50‐fold photoresponsivity enhancement, while hot hole diffusion to the MoS 2 ‐Au electrode interface enables the barrier‐controllable regulation of photoconductivity polarity triggered by optical intensity and wavelength. The multiple‐stimuli‐responsive polarity‐switching characteristic of the hybrid architecture allows for the hardware implementation of an artificial plasmonic neuromorphic system capable of simulating different neural plasticity and performing logical operations with enhanced accuracy. This work presents an innovative framework for the rational design of plasmonic bipolar‐hot‐carrier engineered semiconductor devices with novel functionalities and highlights opportunities for the development of next‐generation optoelectronic intelligence applications.

items.title: AlGaN Barrier Thickness Dependence of Ferroelectric Switching and Interface-Trap Effects in AlScN/HfO2 Gate Stack HEMTs
items.abstract: We investigate the effect of AlGaN barrier thickness (23, 15, and 7 nm) on the transport and switching characteristics of AlScN/HfO2/AlGaN/GaN ferroelectric high-electron-mobility transistors (FeHEMTs). While the 7 nm device exhibits the largest apparent memory window (MW) under quasi-static DC conditions, it suffers from degraded transport, increased leakage, and pronounced trap-induced effects. Pulsed measurements, which reduce the contribution of slower interface-trapping processes, yield representative MWs of 1.6, 3.4, and 2.8 V for the 23, 15, and 7 nm devices, respectively, under their respective program/erase conditions. Prolonged pulse-width measurements demonstrate MW closure and inversion, indicating dominant electron trapping rather than polarization fatigue. Under the present experimental conditions, including a fixed 70 nm AlScN layer, the 15 nm barrier provides the most favorable balance among electrostatic coupling, channel transport, and trap-related effects.

items.title: Activated clotting time in cardiac surgery, cardiological interventional procedures, vascular surgery, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and haemodialysis
items.abstract: The activated clotting time (ACT) is a point-of-care test used to monitor unfractionated heparin (UFH) in acute care settings. Although widely recommended in cardiac surgery, interventional cardiology, vascular surgery, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and haemodialysis, important uncertainties remain regarding its use. Given the lack of interchangeability between ACT devices and consumables, clear information on targets and analytical systems is essential. We reviewed guideline documents published before November 1, 2025, as well as recommendations from major scientific societies, to assess ACT use, thresholds, and reported levels of evidence. Studies cited within these guidelines were also analysed, and the characteristics of ACT devices were compared with those currently available. A total of 24 guideline documents were identified, of which 17 specified ACT target values and only two mentioned the device or reagent used. The level of evidence was generally low or not graded. For example, during cardiopulmonary bypass, recommended ACT thresholds vary (e.g., 480 s without heparin-coated circuits or 400 s with the so-called maximal activation), without specification of the analytical system. Guidelines often rely on outdated studies using devices no longer available. Moreover, ACT analysers differ substantially in consumables, clot detection methods, blood volume, and reagents, which are rarely considered in recommendations. In conclusion, current guidelines provide limited guidance on ACT measurement despite significant inter-device variability. We recommend that future guidelines specify devices and consumables, or at least their sensitivity to UFH, to ensure reliable interpretation. Further studies are needed to optimise UFH monitoring in clinical practice.
items.venue: European Journal of Anaesthesiology Intensive Care

items.title: Vertical NAND Flash Memory‐Based Bayesian Neural Networks With Intrinsic Gaussian Weight Sampling
items.abstract: Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) provide improved robustness and well‐calibrated uncertainty estimates compared with deterministic networks, but their hardware realization remains challenging because Gaussian weight sampling typically requires random number generators, substantial memory overhead, or additional circuitry. Here we experimentally characterize commercial vertical NAND (V‐NAND) flash memory and show that a fully hardware‐compatible BNN can be realized without modifying the native array structure. We demonstrate that although individual ISPP‐programmed V‐NAND cells exhibit non‐Gaussian conductance distributions, the differential current between adjacent cells naturally forms a zero‐mean Gaussian distribution. The variance of these Gaussian weights can be tuned using only the read voltage, introducing no extra storage or peripheral circuitry. Using this hardware‐aware mapping, we construct a Bayesian last‐layer on top of a ResNet‐34 classifier and evaluate it in hardware‐calibrated simulations on the Tiny‐ImageNet‐C dataset. The resulting V‐NAND BNN achieves up to a 9.0% point improvement in accuracy over a deterministic counterpart under severe corruptions, along with enhanced calibration, ROC/PR performance, and separation of epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. These results establish V‐NAND flash memory as a practical and scalable platform for uncertainty‐aware in‐memory computing and provide a blueprint for hardware BNNs.

items.title: SpikeOcc: Towards Resilient Multimodal 3D Occupancy Perception via Spiking Experts
items.abstract: Multimodal 3D occupancy prediction underpins safe autonomous driving through comprehensive scene understanding. However, existing methods have largely pursued higher accuracy through sophisticated fusion, leaving resilience to missing sensors underexplored. In this paper, we investigate spiking neural networks (SNNs) as a means of building more resilient multimodal perception. Still, the discrete nature of spiking neurons makes optimization challenging. To overcome this difficulty, SpikeOcc is introduced with two complementary components, a Spiking Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) and Sensor Availability Learning (SAL). Specifically, SMoE organizes RGB, LiDAR, and joint fusion into specialized pathways, enabling full-width unimodal representations while retaining the original multimodal features via a bounded residual. Beyond sensor dropout, SAL employs a staged curriculum with explicit routing supervision, progressively improving robustness under severe sensing conditions. Remarkably, SAL also yields notable gains for conventional models, highlighting its broader potential for resilient multimodal learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpikeOcc maintains competitive full-sensor accuracy while markedly raising the performance floor under sensor outages. SpikeOcc illustrates the promise of neuromorphic computing, pointing toward more reliable and energy-efficient autonomous driving.

items.title: Spatially Complementary In‐Plane Lattice Strain Engineering for Reduced Contact Resistance and Enhanced Ferroelectric Switching in Van Der Waals α‐In 2 Se 3 Ferroelectric Semiconductor Field‐Effect Transistors
items.abstract: ABSTRACT α‐In 2 Se 3 ferroelectric semiconductor field‐effect transistors (FeS‐FETs) offer attractive non‐volatile memory characteristics but are limited by high source/drain (S/D) contact resistance and inefficient ferroelectric polarization switching. Here, we demonstrate a low‐temperature, CMOS‐compatible strain‐engineering strategy based on region‐dependent in‐plane (IP) lattice strain. A silicon nitride stress layer induces tensile strain in the S/D regions and compressive strain in the channel, producing spatially differentiated effects within a single device. The contact‐side tensile strain modifies the interfacial electronic structure and reduces contact resistance, whereas the channel‐side compressive strain facilitates ferroelectric polarization switching. Consequently, the strained α‐In 2 Se 3 FeS‐FET achieves a 12.03‐fold reduction in S/D contact resistance, a 19.21‐fold increase in on‐state current, a 4.4%p increase in normalized memory window, and a 22.4‐fold enhancement in the ferroelectric resistance switching ratio. Raman characterization and finite‐element method simulations establish the region‐dependent strain distribution, while interface‐pinning analysis and first‐principles calculations provide mechanistic support for the distinct contact‐ and channel‐side effects. These results establish region‐dependent IP lattice strain as a unified device‐engineering framework for jointly controlling contact transport and ferroelectric memory functionality in vdW α‐In 2 Se 3 FeS‐FETs.

items.title: High-Performance Uncooled Infrared Photodetection Based on van der Waals Metallic FePd2Te2 Nanoflakes
items.abstract: Uncooled infrared photodetectors that combine high sensitivity, low power consumption, and broad spectral coverage remain highly desirable. However, they are still hindered by the complex epitaxial processes and cooling requirements of mainstream semiconductor technologies. Here, we demonstrate a high-performance infrared photodetector based on FePd2Te2 nanoflakes, a van der Waals metallic material that enables efficient photothermal conversion. The device operates at room temperature under a bias of 0.1 V and exhibits a broadband photoresponse spanning from the visible to the long-wave infrared. Across the measured infrared range, a wavelength-independent responsivity (R) above 50 A/W, a noise equivalent power (NEP) below 2.83 × 10−16 W/Hz1/2, and a specific detectivity (D*) exceeding 3.86 × 1012 cm Hz1/2/W are achieved. The photoresponse appears to arise from the photobolometric effect, in which the temperature rise at the contact interface is considered to modulate the contact resistance and thereby amplify the photocurrent. These results establish FePd2Te2 as a promising platform for room-temperature, low-power, and highly sensitive infrared detection.

items.title: An optimized majority-feedback QCA D-latch and SET/RESET-enabled SRAM cell for compact, low-latency nanoelectronic memory design
items.abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata is a contender to replace the scaling of semiconductor technology as it hits physical limits of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology, with its ability to switch faster, take up less space and consume less power. In this study, the design and functional verification of compact QCA data latch circuit and a memory cell suitable for SRAM operation are presented, which are designed, implemented and simulated in the QCA designer (QCAD) 2.0.3 software. The main contribution is a single-layer 14-cell D-latch with a 0.007 µm 2 footprint, reducing the layout area, latency and QCA cost compared with a similar design previously reported in the literature. Another 15-cell variant is proposed, incorporating SET and RESET control, for SRAM-type applications, reducing peak energy dissipation by approximately 22% from the 14-cell baseline. The circuits are found to be compact, low-latency circuits for next-generation nanoelectronics memory and different logic circuit design applications with reduced power dissipation. The power dissipation and polarization map of proposed circuits are implemented in QCAPro Software.

items.title: Air-gap engineering enabled ultrafast 9-bit ferroelectric semi-gate transistor array for high-efficiency image denoising
items.abstract: Abstract The insufficient lateral electric field gradient limits the programming/erasing speed of conventional semi-floating gate transistors, while charge leakage leads to poor data retention and compromised operating characteristics. Here we design a ferroelectric semi-gate (FSG) transistor featuring a triangular air gap adjacent to the drain region. The device exhibits an as-programmed on–off ratio exceeding 107, remaining above 105 after 11 weeks, and a memory window of approximately 6 V. The localized lateral electric field accelerates program and erase operations to 60 ns and 75 ns, respectively. The spontaneous polarization field of the ferroelectric HfZrO layer strengthens charge retention in the HfO2 charge-trapping layer, enabling robust nonvolatile memory performance with a retention time exceeding 106 s. This synergistic integration of air-gap engineering and ferroelectric polarization yields an optimal trade-off between speed, retention and multilevel operation. By exploiting its superior multilevel capability with 9-bit distinguishable current states, we realize Ising-model-based image denoising using a 32 × 32 transistor array. These FSG transistors show promising potential for high-speed, low-power random-access memory applications.

items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Rather than committing to a single representation, TileCas allows an agent to transfer and refine candidates across levels through Cross-Level Diagnosis, which maps correctness and performance feedback to actionable controls at different abstraction levels; Abstraction Scheduling, which selects both the candidate and representation from which subsequent refinement should proceed; and a Heterogeneous Search Tree, which preserves and revisits alternative search trajectories spanning multiple representations. We integrate TileCas with two code agents AKO and KDA, and evaluate both integrations on 50 end-to-end KernelBench Level 3 workloads across two accelerator platforms and two language models. Giving equal weight to the four accelerator-model configurations, AKO with TileCas achieves an arithmetic-mean speedup of $4.84\times$, compared with $3.75\times$ for the strongest evaluated baseline without TileCas, an improvement of 29.0%. Integrating the same interface with KDA improves its mean speedup by 69.2%, with gains in every configuration. These results show that allowing coding agents to navigate across programming abstractions can improve machine-driven software development and can be reused across different base workflows.

items.title: Scalable Ion‐Electron Coupled Poly(Benzodifurandione) Inks Enabling Biosignal Amplification and Neuromorphic Memory
items.abstract: Printed organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising for next‐generation biosensing and neuromorphic computing, owing to their high transconductance, low operating voltage, mechanical flexibility, and efficient volumetric ionic–electronic coupling. Yet, printable n ‐type OECTs have lagged their p ‐type counterparts due to limited stability and poor printability. The key challenge lies in achieving high electronic conductivity, efficient ionic accessibility, and rheological properties compatible with scalable printing. To address this, we developed a screen‐printable, air‐stable, n ‐type OECT channel by blending high‐conductivity poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) with poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO). Devices fabricated using 5wt.% PEO blend and a gelatin‐based electrolyte exhibited tunable transient responses (turn‐on time; 9.6 to 419 ms, turn‐off time; 4.3 ms to 17.8 ms), stable operation (92.4% ON current retained over 1,000 cycles), and high uniformity across 50 devices (I ds, ON = 2.47 ± 0.29 mA and transconductance g m = 3.55 ± 0.57 mS). PEO transforms low‐viscosity PBFDO solutions into shear‐thinning pastes suitable for screen printing, while enhancing film wettability and electrolyte infiltration. This dual role promotes efficient ion penetration and improves printability, enabling devices with improved transient speeds and rheological properties optimized for scalable fabrication. By controlling channel thickness, thin devices enable electrocardiogram signal acquisition while thick devices act as artificial synapses, highlighting PBFDO‐based inks as versatile platforms for integrated bioelectronic interfaces.

items.title: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration
items.abstract: Chiplet technology is a key approach for extending Moore's Law. However, its design process is constrained by two primary challenges: the scarcity of early-stage platforms for rapidly evaluating chiplet-based heterogeneous systems, and the complex relationships between design parameters and optimization metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with Bayesian Optimization (BO), enabling architectural-level simulation and automated optimization for the 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplets. We extend the open-source chiplet simulator to evaluate 3D designs by supporting graph topologies. Further, to enhance the exploration efficiency of BO, we introduce an LLM that generates high-quality policies to guide the optimization process, enabled by our proposed adaptive directional policy reasoning (ADPR) and an exploration gain-aware fine-tuning method. Finally, we use the policy-guided BO to perform an automated and efficient exploration of the complex chiplet design space. Experiments on 2.5D and 3D chiplet reveal that our framework improves design space exploration efficiency.

items.title: HADES: A Programmable Processing-Near-Memory Engine for Binary Similarity Search
items.abstract: Moving operands to a processor can cost more than the arithmetic performed on them, and for small binary similarity and search workloads data movement can dominate. We present HADES, a programmable processing-near-memory engine built around one shared 32x32-bit 2R1W register-file macro that holds both data and program. Twelve 16-bit opcodes, three working registers and a 32-slot program express ten search workloads in 8 to 19 slots, and SCANP and SCANSEL shorten dual-row and selected scans. A post-layout 2x2 Tiny Tapeout implementation closes timing at 40 MHz with 26,968 square microns of standard cells beside a 15,744 square microns macro. All HADES results come from RTL or gate-level simulation of this implementation, and HADES energy is estimated. Against ESP8266 and ESP32 microcontrollers running plain C, and with an ideal host, HADES answers a resident query 10x to 32x and 2.2x to 11x faster, respectively. End to end, it wins at the evaluated batch sizes of B = 16 and B = 256 against both boards and loses the single-query (B = 1) runs to the ESP32. An Arduino Nano runs a restricted subset. Kernel power stays within about 2% of a spin loop on all three boards. These results hold for plain-C baselines under the evaluated conditions. At this scale the control and instruction storage fit around a shared memory macro, while the byte-wide interface and the loading path remain significant costs.

items.title: Comparative Electro-Thermal Evaluation of IGBT- and SiC MOSFET-Based Bidirectional DC-DC Converters for Supercapacitor Energy Storage Systems
items.abstract: Bidirectional DC-DC converters are key interfaces between supercapacitor energy storage systems and DC networks in applications requiring rapid bidirectional power exchange, particularly regenerative braking and acceleration support. This paper presents a like-for-like comparison of IGBT- and SiC MOSFET-based implementations of the same 125 kW rated non-isolated bidirectional buck–boost converter platform. The novelty lies in a controlled system-level comparison in which the semiconductor technology is changed, while the converter architecture, control structure and operating conditions are retained, enabling the electro-thermal impact of the device technology to be assessed in both directions of power flow. Both semiconductor technologies are evaluated in buck and boost operation through analytical loss calculations, manufacturer-based electro-thermal simulations, and laboratory measurements. The laboratory measurements reached approximately 50 kW in buck mode and 38 kW in boost mode for both semiconductor implementations; the 125 kW results are analytical/manufacturer tool projections rather than rated-power experimental validation. The results obtained from the manufacturer tool simulations show that the relative benefit of SiC depends on both the switching frequency and power flow direction. In particular, the SiC implementation provides a substantially greater thermal margin in boost operation, while the buck-mode comparison reveals a frequency-dependent crossover for the selected devices. The partial-power experimental results support the electro-thermal trends observed in the analysis and simulations, particularly the reduced thermal stress of the SiC implementation. These results highlight the importance of considering both the switching frequency and power flow direction when selecting the semiconductor technology for high-power bidirectional supercapacitor converters.

items.title: Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor based Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier with Enhanced Analog Performance
items.abstract: This article describes how to develop and operate a Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier (CNTFET-VDIBA) using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistors (CNTFETs). It utilizes the superior characteristics of CNTFETs to facilitate enhanced transconductance, a wideband range of operation, and a low power demand compared to conventional CMOS alternatives. The effect of increasing numbers of CNTs on device performance was thoroughly studied and characterized. Simulation results specify that by increasing the number of CNTs significantly improves transconductance. The proposed VDIBA, CNT has the highest transconductance of around 1.32mS, while maintaining the high BW. The 3-db BW was observed to be 7.9 GHz, enabling this proposed VDIBA to apply for high-frequency analog signals. These results demonstrate that CNTFET-based VDIBA is a feasible substitute to CMOS, providing ultra-low power consumption, scalability, and high-performance analog building blocks for future integrated circuits.
items.venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

items.title: Unveiling Phosphorus Vacancy-Mediated Resistive Switching in Cu/HfO2/BP/Pt Memristors: Experimental and First-Principles Investigations
items.abstract: Memristors integrating 2D materials are promising for neuromorphic computing, yet their microscopic resistive switching mechanisms require further clarification. In this study, a Cu/HfO2/BP/Pt memristor was fabricated to investigate its electrical characteristics and conductive filament (CF) dynamics. The device exhibits compliance-dependent behavior, enabling unipolar volatile switching at 100 μA and bipolar nonvolatile switching at 200 μA. In nonvolatile mode, it demonstrates a concentrated switching voltage distribution (Vset ≈ −1.491 V, Vreset ≈ 1.669 V), stable endurance exceeding 150 cycles, and an ON/OFF ratio of ∼104. The low- and high-resistance states follow ohmic conduction (a hybrid ohmic conduction of electron capture/decapture under negative bias) and Schottky emission, respectively. Furthermore, first-principles CI-NEB calculations indicate that intrinsic phosphorus vacancies (Vp) within the BP layer facilitate directional Cu+ migration (1.54 eV barrier) and spontaneous Pt atom trapping (0.1 eV barrier). This defect-mediated interfacial interaction promotes stable orbital hybridization, anchoring localized CFs. This work provides experimental and theoretical insights for designing oxide/2D material-based neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips
items.abstract: We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips. Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant. Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop. Our results have important implications for HBM-based system design and validation. Relying solely on JEDEC- or vendor-specified test loops to bound HBM power could cause system failures and/or thermal throttling in real-world high-power AI/ML workloads. To improve 3D-stacked DRAM power modeling in open source architectural simulation infrastructures, we develop a new HBM power model. Our model predicts the power of 36 real HBM2 chips across diverse workloads (including a real LLM decode workload) with 7.6 -- 8.1% mean absolute percentage error, substantially more accurately than state-of-the-art HBM power models. The power consumption predicted by our model for a power-intensive microbenchmark closely matches (with 2.4% to 5.3% error across HBM3E's specified supply voltage range) the average HBM3E memory power consumed by three tested NVIDIA H200 GPUs. We publicly release our power model at https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/HBM-Power.

items.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
items.abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

items.title: Trap engineering in InP/ZnSe/ZnS colloidal quantum-dot memristors for neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are attractive memristive materials because their electronic structure and interfaces can be engineered to control charge transport and trapping for neuromorphic synaptic devices. However, many QD-based memristors exhibit resistive switching based on filament formation via silver migration, without utilizing the unique properties of QDs. In this presentation, we combine mechanism-guided engineering of device architecture and material properties to achieve non-filamentary resistive switching in InP/ZnSe/ZnS QDs. Based on device-architecture engineering, we found that interlayers adjacent to QDs have an important role in charge trapping and detrapping governing hysteresis and retention characteristics. Guided by these insights, a multilayer stack of metal oxide nanoparticles and QDs promotes spatially uniform areal trapping, while oxide nanoparticle interlayers enhance electron transport, suppress hole injection, and create interfacial trap sites via controlled interfacial chemistry. The strategies enabled robust resistive switching and synaptic plasticity for neural network operation.

items.title: Thickness scaling in hafnium ferroelectrics: insights into oxygen vacancy clustering and its impact on ferroelectricity and reliability
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium-based ferroelectrics have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation non-volatile memory technologies owing to their excellent complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) compatibility and exceptional thickness scalability. However, the defect mechanisms governing the evolution of ferroelectricity and reliability during thickness scaling remain poorly understood. In particular, the role of oxygen-vacancy-related defects has primarily been discussed from the perspective of defect concentration, while their spatial organization has received far less attention. Here, we systematically investigate the impact of thickness scaling on the ferroelectric properties and reliability of Hf 0.5 Zr 0.5 O 2 (HZO) capacitors. Although thinner HZO films exhibit reduced remanent polarization due to enhanced dead-layer effects, increased depolarization fields, and stabilization of nonpolar phases, they surprisingly demonstrate superior breakdown tolerance and endurance performance. Notably, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis revealed a higher oxygen vacancy concentration in thinner films, indicating that defect concentration alone cannot explain the observed reliability evolution. Time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB) analysis using the time-dependent clustering model, together with density functional theory (DFT) calculations and atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterization, suggests that thickness scaling modifies the spatial organization of oxygen-vacancy-related defects. Grain refinement in ultrathin films increases the grain-boundary density, thereby suppressing severe defect clustering and promoting a more dispersed defect organization, which delays breakdown and improves long-term reliability. These findings identify defect organization as a critical factor governing the thickness-scaling behavior of hafnium ferroelectrics and provide new insights for the design of highly scaled and reliable ferroelectric memory devices.

items.title: The role of various scattering mechanisms on electron velocity in Al0.21Ga0.79N/GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: In the present study, the mobility corresponding to various scattering mechanisms under low-field conditions was calculated. Among all scattering mechanisms, polarization Coulomb field (PCF) and polar optical phonon (POP) scattering exhibited the highest mean momentum relaxation rates under low-field conditions. Sentaurus technology computer-aided design (TCAD) coupled Monte Carlo (MC) simulations were employed to calculate the electron drift velocity (ve) of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under high-field conditions. Individual scattering mechanisms were removed sequentially in the MC framework. The impact of each mechanism on ve under high-field conditions was quantified. The results reveal that under high-field conditions, PCF scattering can reduce ve of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs by 20%–30%. Meanwhile, a method based on the mean momentum relaxation rate was proposed. It can be used to approximate scattering strength and to rank the contributions of different mechanisms in the MC simulations. The highest mean momentum relaxation rate was also obtained for PCF and POP scattering. PCF and POP scattering are, therefore, identified as the dominant carrier-scattering mechanism in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs. Further, a correlation between device geometry and the mean momentum relaxation rate of PCF scattering was further established. Devices with a larger ratio of source-spacing (drain-spacing)-to-gate-length [Lgs(gd)/Lg] exhibited stronger PCF scattering strength.

items.title: The Effect of Passive Substrate Terminations on RON Degradation in GaN Bidirectional Switches
items.abstract: In this paper, four passive terminations are considered for the substrate biasing of Gallium Nitride (GaN) bidirectional high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). These substrate networks are analyzed via switching simulations and by adopting a physical model for the bidirectional transistor based on the well-known Advanced SPICE Model (ASM) for GaN HEMT, including an enhanced formulation of back-gating phenomena. The most promising network, which exploits resistances and diodes in the common anode configuration, was implemented with discrete components and tested. The measurement data turned out to be in line with the simulations results in terms of substrate voltage, which is pushed toward zero at low resistance values, thus reducing the back-gating effect. Consequently, a remarkable reduction in the on-resistance (RON) degradation compared to the floating substrate configuration is observed, with a proper trade-off between RON drift and off-state leakage current. Finally, some considerations about the partial recovery of on-resistance due to the substrate termination are discussed.

items.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
items.abstract: The growing diversity of domain-specific architectures and microarchitectural designs demands fast and accurate evaluation methods during early design stages. However, existing approaches suffer from a fundamental trade-off: high-level simulators offer speed but lack fidelity, while RTL-based tools provide accuracy at the cost of significant simulation overhead. This gap limits efficient pre-RTL microarchitecture exploration. Therefore, we propose Transaction-Pruned Cycle Simulation (TPCS), a novel modeling and simulation framework. It serves as a unified intermediate abstraction spanning microarchitecture modeling, cycle-accurate simulation, and synthesizable RTL implementation. TPCS organizes combinational logic as transaction-based function invocations and leverages host CPU control flow to naturally prune inactive logic, eliminating the need for explicit event scheduling or signal tracking. This enables cycle-accurate simulation with significantly improved performance. TPCS preserves structural correspondence with RTL and supports automatic generation of synthesizable designs. TPCS achieves 36$\times$-42$\times$ speedups over parallel Verilator on SMP systems and 3.4$\times$-7.2$\times$ over single-threaded Verilator on accelerators, with cycle-level waveform agreement on the evaluated traces. The generated RTL demonstrates comparable timing and area to handcrafted implementations, with relative changes of -4.7\% to +2.6\% in clock period and -3.3\% to +4.0\% in standard-cell area. By bridging the abstraction gap between high-level modeling and RTL design, TPCS enables a unified and agile pre-RTL workflow, allowing efficient microarchitecture exploration with both high performance and implementation fidelity.

items.title: Role of lateral surface conduction in barrier modulation of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs under optical illumination and elevated temperature
items.abstract: Optical and thermal excitation are known to enhance OFF-state leakage and modify the electrostatics of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), yet the role of lateral surface conduction in mediating these effects remains insufficiently understood. In this work, a geometry-defined ring-break architecture is introduced to probe the interplay between lateral surface conduction and channel electrostatics. Simultaneous measurements of gate leakage current ( IG) and floating channel potential ( Va) reveal correlated transport and electrostatic responses together with a characteristic transition at a critical gate bias, Vcrit. Under optical illumination and elevated temperature, both ring-break and conventional HEMTs exhibit systematic evolution of IG and Vcrit, supporting a common field-dependent lateral surface-conduction mechanism. However, the illumination-induced Va response differs qualitatively between the two geometries: |Va| decreases in the conventional structure but increases in the ring-break structure. This opposite response is attributed to the geometry-dependent balance between positive surface charging, which reduces |Va|, and negative virtual gating associated with distributed surface resistance, which increases |Va|. These results establish lateral surface conduction as an important contributor to barrier modulation and OFF-state leakage in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs and demonstrate the ring-break architecture as a geometry-controlled platform for probing surface transport, charge redistribution, and the influence of surface passivation.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-transport framework treats the source, drain, and gate as current-carrying quantum-mechanical contacts and resolves the local current density throughout the device. The spatially resolved current density shows that gate-injected carriers tunnel through the high-$k$ dielectric preferentially near the drain side of the gate, where the dielectric barrier is most strongly lowered by the drain bias, and are collected by the drain. This provides a direct real-space picture of the DIDBL-driven gate-drain leakage mechanism.

items.title: Phase imaging of vortex laser beams in antiresonant and hollow waveguides for high harmonic generation and telecommunications in the IR-to-x-ray regime
items.abstract: We interrogate experimentally the conservation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) of laser beams in the VIS–IR spectral range propagating in anti-resonant waveguides for next-generation high harmonic generation in the soft and hard x-ray region, and telecommunication applications. Vortex beams with effective fractional OAM of 0.6–1.3 are coupled to hollow-core or anti-resonant waveguides of 30–150μm inner diameters, sharing an identical revolver substructure of 6–12 hollow-core capillaries. First, using holography, we interfere the fractional OAM beams with a Gaussian reference beam, yielding characteristic multi-spiral phase patterns in Fourier space. Experimental analyses and theoretical beam propagation show excellent quantitative agreement, suggesting conservation of OAM for large bandwidths of at least ~400nm. This enables structured laser pulses of extended femtosecond bandwidth to be combined with waveguides optimized for high transmission, especially relevant for the near-IR–mid-IR regimes. Second, ptychographic coherent diffractive imaging can detail the phase topology with near-wavelength resolution across a vortex beam. We demonstrate enhanced OAM characterization using structured light with quantum properties combined with ptychography — which we term quanthography — further confirming that OAM is preserved. In perspective, guided twisted laser beams with large bandwidth can produce ultrahigh harmonics in the IR-to-x-ray region with inherently large OAM of 10–1000, as well as multiply data transmission capacity using structured IR light in novel anti-resonance fiber-optic telecommunication systems. Furthermore, highly structured EUV–soft x-ray light can greatly enhance phase contrast in coherent diffractive imaging using tabletop apparatus at the sub-1–10 nm spatial scale for semiconductor metrology.
items.venue: Unconventional Imaging, Sensing, and Adaptive Optics

items.title: Performance modeling of photonic accelerators for attention kernel
items.abstract: In modern machine learning models such as Transformers, the attention kernel serves as the core computational kernel and is typically accelerated using transistor-based systems. Photonic in-memory computing offers a promising alternative by leveraging high optical bandwidth and operating frequencies for efficient multiply-accumulate operations. However, photonic compute arrays, such as photonic-SRAM (pSRAM) in-memory compute arrays, cannot support the large on-chip storage required for intermediate data in the attention kernel, necessitating integration with conventional electronic external memory. In addition, non-linear operations such as softmax require electronic execution. These constraints require a hybrid photonic-electronic architecture for attention acceleration. Developing such an accelerator requires understanding how hybrid photonic-electronic system parameters influence sustained performance. Therefore, a system-level performance model is necessary to identify and tune parameters and guide the design decisions required to achieve the target performance. We address this need by developing a system-level performance model for photonic accelerators that quantifies the impact of pSRAM compute arrays and electronic external memory on sustained performance (TOPS) for the attention kernel. We decompose the attention kernel into computation primitives and map them onto pSRAM-based compute arrays fabricated using GlobalFoundries’ standard silicon photonics process. We evaluate pSRAM configurations with 256x64 array size, 4-16-bit precision, 40-200 WDM channels, and electronic external memory such as HBM3E. Using our system performance model, we identify operating regions where photonic acceleration yields significant performance gains with sustained performance reaching up to 85 PetaOps/s at 200 WDM channels, as well as regions where memory overhead dominates.

items.title: Neural bolometers: designing next-generation infrared thermal imagers with in-pixel neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Emerging applications like Heat-Assisted Detection and Ranging and thermal LIDAR necessitate a shift toward high-resolution, information-rich infrared perception. However, conventional infrared detectors face challenges in area, latency, and power consumption. To address these limitations, we demonstrated a Spintronic Poisson Bolometer that operates in a Poisson-counting regime, where infrared detection is achieved through thermally activated transitions between discrete magnetization states. Building on this platform, we present the concept of a neural bolometer that integrates spintronic poisson bolometers with artificial neural network architectures. Leveraging their tunable stochastic response, nanoscale footprint, and CMOS compatibility, these devices enable in-pixel computation. Our approach enables long-wave infrared (LWIR) detectors to function as both imaging sensors and stochastic computing units. The system achieves LWIR MNIST classification with 92.5% accuracy, 2.82μs inference time, and 1.9μW power consumption. The proposed approach can usher-in a new generation of thermal imagers with in-pixel computing for next-generation of thermal vision.
items.venue: Unconventional Imaging, Sensing, and Adaptive Optics 2026

items.title: Morphotropic Phase Boundary Engineering in HfO2-Based High-k Dielectric Nanosystems for Dynamic Random-Access Memory Capacitors: A Review
items.abstract: Abstract HfO2-based dielectrics engineered into an MPB-like regime have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) capacitors because they offer enhanced dielectric permittivity while preserving the wide bandgap and CMOS compatibility of fluorite-structured oxides. At the nanometer-scale film thicknesses and grain dimensions relevant to DRAM, surface and interface energies, electrode confinement, stress, and defect distributions strongly reshape the relative stability and accessibility of fluorite-derived phases. However, the physical origin of the high-k response and its relationship with leakage current and reliability remain under active discussion. In this review, we summarize recent progress in HfO2-based MPB dielectrics from three perspectives. First, we discuss two complementary interpretations of dielectric enhancement: spatial phase coexistence between orthorhombic and tetragonal phases at the MPB, and dynamic nonlinear dielectric response associated with low transition barriers and field-induced structural evolution. Second, we review major engineering strategies for achieving MPB-like behavior, including stoichiometric and oxygen-vacancy control, advanced annealing processes, doping, bilayer and superlattice heterostructures, and electrode/interface engineering. Third, we evaluate the practical performance and reliability requirements for DRAM applications, with emphasis on the coupled trade-offs among dielectric constant, leakage current, equivalent oxide thickness, and time-dependent dielectric breakdown. Representative reports include k ≈ 67 with a leakage current density of 3 × 10−8 A/cm2 at 0.8 V and, in a separate ultrathin HZO device, an EOT of approximately 2.42 Å with k ≈ 64.24. Finally, we highlight that the optimization of MPB HfO2-based dielectrics requires a holistic design framework that simultaneously considers phase stability, defect dynamics, interface quality, and realistic low-voltage benchmarking conditions.

items.title: Low-resistance ohmic contacts: a strategy for ideal 2D semiconductor transistors
items.abstract: The rapid development of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) field-effect transistors (FETs) highlights the critical need to reduce the contact resistance for the future of Moore’s law using 2D complementary metal-oxide semiconductors. Electrical metal contacts with 2D TMDs-based FETs remain a critical challenge because of their high contact resistance, which primarily results from the Schottky barrier, poor interface quality, and Fermi level pinning. In this study, we report a significant reduction in the contact resistance of 2D TMDs using several strategies including plasma knowledge based polymorphic engineering, controllable doping, band matching, phase engineering and insertion buffer layer.

items.title: LightZK: An Efficient GPU Acceleration Framework for Large-Scale Zero-Knowledge Proofs
items.abstract: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), particularly zk-SNARKs, have become a cornerstone for privacy-preserving protocols and blockchain scalability. However, the generation of proofs remains computationally prohibitive due to the immense overhead of underlying cryptographic primitives, namely Multi-Scalar Multiplication (MSM) and Fast Number Theoretic Transform (NTT). As applications scale up to billion-scale constraints, conventional GPU-accelerated frameworks tailored for smaller instances suffer from overwhelming memory usage, invalid architectural assumptions, and suboptimal end-to-end orchestration. Driven by the motivation to complete massive proof generation on a single memory-constrained node, this paper presents LightZK, an efficient GPU acceleration framework for large-scale zero-knowledge proofs based on a tile-based execution model. LightZK not only aims to support ultra-large-scale ZKP generation, but also strives to improve the practical performance of proof generation. LightZK contributes a micro-architectural diagnosis of MSM on GPUs: hardware performance counters expose the register-pressure and low instruction-level-parallelism mismatches that under-utilize the GPU during bucket-merge computation, and targeted kernel optimizations derived from this diagnosis yield a 1.5 × –2.5 × MSM speedup over the SOTA baseline. LightZK further makes large-scale NTT executable where the SOTA GPU baseline fails, via storage and structural optimizations that deliver nontrivial acceleration (2.2 × –2.5 × over a functional baseline). At the systemic level, LightZK builds on a data-dependency graph (DDG) analysis of the Groth16 proving flow to drive a three-tier pipeline orchestration: a hand-crafted DRAM-VRAM pipeline for Poly-phase that overlaps sparse matrix operations with data transfer, and a producer-consumer disk-DRAM-VRAM pipeline for Group-phase that treats each MSM tile as an independently schedulable unit. Experimental results demonstrate that LightZK achieves a 2.8 × end-to-end performance improvement over the leading executable GPU baseline at standard scales. Crucially, while existing GPU frameworks exceed available memory at billion-scale, LightZK successfully sustains 230-scale proof generation with near-linear scalability on a single node.
items.venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization (TACO)

items.title: Laser plasma x-ray sources for semiconductor metrology
items.abstract: This paper discusses the development of compact laser-driven ultrabrilliant microfocus x-ray sources (LPXSs) and their application to semiconductor micro-XRF metrology. LPXSs also offer significant advantages in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, x-ray microscopy, and x-ray imaging applications. The LPXSs employ mJ laser pulses with tens of kHz repetition rate. These pulses are focused onto liquid metal targets, generating characteristic line emissions in the soft, tender, and hard x-ray regimes (200eV to 24keV). LPXSs offer a significant potential enhancement over typical microfocus X-ray tubes because they offer x-ray source brightness that exceed that of tubes. LPXS data from bismuth and gallium-based targets have been measured. The LPXS spectra were used for highly sensitive quantification of germanium on silicon wafers. These results establish a credible pathway to elevate micro-XRF from a near-line analytical technique to a viable inline metrology solution for Ge detection and depth profile measurements during the production of GAA and CFET semiconductor nodes.
items.venue: Advances in X-Ray/EUV Sources, Optics, and Components

items.title: Introducing Hardware Neurotechnology: A Non-Reconfigurable, Monolithic Transistor-as-a-Perceptron Architecture for Instantaneous AI Inference
items.abstract: Modern artificial intelligence is structurally constrained by the von Neumann bottleneck, which enforces an energy-intensive physical separation between arithmetic logic circuits and memory storage banks. This paper formalizes the architectural paradigm of Hardware Neurotechnology, an invention authored by Dr. Nitnem Singh Sodhi, wherein the physical silicon lattice natively embodies the artificial neural network graph, completely eliminating algorithmic instruction cycles and memory access overhead. By utilizing multi-input floating-gate (MIFG) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors operating in the subthreshold (weak-inversion) regime, the fundamental mathematical operations of a perceptron—linear synaptic weighting, multi-input accumulation, bias offset, and non-linear sigmoidal activation—are mapped directly onto single semiconductor device pairs. To overcome the catastrophic interconnect scaling, parasitic routing overhead, and silicon area expansion that have historically stalled analog neuromorphic engineering, the proposed architecture abandons dynamic reconfigurability in favor of a strictly hardwired, application-specific monolithic topology. Sacrificing field reconfigurability eliminates routing crossbar switches, SRAM routing memory, and intermediate analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), realizing an Application-Specific Neuromorphic Integrated Circuit (ASNIC) that executes complex inference tasks near-instantaneously at sub-femtojoule energy dissipation per synaptic operation.
items.venue: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology

items.title: Interface-Engineered Diffuse Morphotropic Phase Boundary in Hafnia–Zirconia Nanolaminates for DRAM Capacitors
items.abstract: Abstract The morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) in Hf₁₋ ₓ Zr ₓ O₂ enables enhanced dielectric permittivity through the energetic competition between tetragonal and orthorhombic phases, yet its strong compositional sensitivity imposes stringent requirements on stoichiometric control in scaled DRAM capacitors. Here, we show that this limitation can be mitigated by converting a composition-defined MPB into an interface-defined one using tetragonal/orthorhombic HfO₂–ZrO₂ nanolaminates. First-principles calculations reveal that the lattice-distorted heterointerface reduces the tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition barrier from approximately 50 to 7 meV per formula unit relative to composition-matched bulk HZO. The interfacial structural distortion and local cation coordination further modify the lattice polarization response, producing an extended region with MPB-like dielectric susceptibility across the interface. The calculated interfacial region extends over approximately 1.3–1.5 nm, substantially broader than the corresponding transition region in compositionally homogeneous HZO. Guided by this prediction, nanolaminates with sublayer thicknesses near 1.2 nm exhibit the highest dielectric response.
