Based on this analysis, a thermal-limited power-capacity boundary is derived under junction-temperature and efficiency constraints, accounting for the combined effects of operating conditions and device thermal stress. To further enhance the achievable power capacity, a cost-effective device-rating configuration methodology is proposed by introducing the relative capacity of SiC mosfets as a key design variable. The proposed method redistributes power losses and thermal stress between Si IGBTs and SiC devices, improving thermal utilization without proportionally increasing device count. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a 100% increase in power capacity with a peak efficiency of 98.7%, while reducing system cost by 24% compared with conventional approaches. This article provides a practical and systematic solution for enhancing the power capacity of hybrid Si/SiC ANPC converters under thermal and efficiency constraints.

items.title: Testing of Chiplet-Based Packages Based on Advanced Heterogeneous Integration
items.abstract: Editor’s notes: With 3-D chips becoming main-stream to address the growing demands of heterogenous integration, their test has moved from research to practical necessity and adoption. This article provides a comprehensive overview of what causes defects and anomalies due to imperfections in complex integration, and different methods to detect them at time zero and in the field. —Rubin Parekhji, Texas Instruments, India

items.title: Temperature‐Dependent Conduction and Gate‐Tunable Photoresponse in Graphene Photodetectors
items.abstract: Graphene photodetectors are promising candidates for broadband and high‐speed optoelectronics, yet tunable photoconductive behavior without junction engineering remains elusive. Here, we report gate‐controlled switching between positive and negative photoconductance in graphene field‐effect transistors (GFETs) fabricated on Si/SiO2 with Si3N4 passivation using a CMOS‐compatible process. Temperature‐dependent transport measurements (77–327 K) reveal impurity‐limited mobility at low temperatures and phonon‐dominated scattering at elevated temperatures, alongside pronounced hysteresis attributed to interfacial charge trapping and adsorbates. Under illumination, the devices exhibit a sublinear photocurrent dependence on incident power and saturation at higher intensities, consistent with a charge trap‐mediated photogating effect. Remarkably, the application of a back‐gate voltage induces a reversible transition from positive to negative photoconductance in the absence of heterojunctions. This behavior is attributed to the interplay of photogenerated carrier trapping at the graphene/SiO2 interface, adsorbate‐mediated charge transfer, and gate‐induced Fermi level modulation, which collectively govern carrier density and scattering. These results establish a simple platform for electrically tunable photoconductance in graphene and provide new insights into interfacial effects governing photogating, enabling low‐power and multifunctional optoelectronic devices.

items.title: Temperature-Dependent Analytical Modeling of Switching Loss and Time Intervals for SiC MOSFETs With Channel and Capacitance Dynamics
items.abstract: This article presents an improved analytical model for switching loss and time intervals of SiC MOSFETs. A physics-based model of static and dynamic stray capacitances is first developed. Then, an MOS channel-dependent equivalent transconductance model is proposed. The dynamic transfer characteristics are considered. At the turn-off transient, the MOS channel current can turn off either synchronously with or before the drain current, and both cases are addressed in this study. The impacts of low/high common source inductance and unipolar/bipolar high-side operation on switching are also included. Based on the improved understanding, an analytical model of switching loss and time intervals is proposed. Temperature-dependent characteristics of the SiC MOSFETs are modeled, with a simple method to assess temperature sensitivity of switching loss. The good agreement of experimental and simulated losses and time intervals validate the model accuracy.

items.title: TSV-W for 2.5-D IC Wireless Interconnects
items.abstract: This article introduces the use of through silicon vias (TSVs) connected to electrical switches as waveguides for wireless interconnects on 2.5-D interposer-based integrated circuits (ICs). The resulting wireless interconnect can be controlled at run-time with electrical switches on the TSVs forming the TSV-W(aveguide) (TSV-W). This run-time control allows for creating or blocking wireless interconnects based on the demands of the applications mapped to a multicore computing system. The 3-D finite element method (FEM) simulations of 2.5-D IC floorplans are utilized to demonstrate the utility of TSV-Ws when deployed with wireless interconnects built with TSV-A(ntenna)s (TSV-As). The wireless channel between two TSV-As at a communication distance of 15 mm, representative of distant cores on a $6\times 6$ multicore 2.5-D system, is improved from a 3.6-dB loss without proposed TSV-Ws to a stronger link with only a 2.6-dB loss with TSV-Ws ( $3.125\times $ improvement in bandwidth at −10 dB), primarily due to the directionality imposed by TSV-Ws. Also shown in FEM simulations is a configuration of an orthogonally bent wireless channel on a multicore 2.5-D IC system.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: TSR-Q-1: A Preregistered Experimental Protocol for Testing Structured Quantum-Coherence Residuals in Superconducting Qubits
items.abstract: TSR-Q-1 presents a preregistered and falsifiable experimental protocol designed to test for structured late-time coherence residuals in superconducting transmon qubits. The protocol does not treat generic recoherence, non-exponential decay, or non-Markovian behavior as evidence for the proposed framework, since such phenomena may arise from conventional open-system mechanisms. Instead, it targets a specific normalized temporal scaling law, tₙ/T₂ = nᵏ, with the preregistered theoretical value k* = 1.4706, corresponding to the first two target locations t₂/T₂ = 2.7714 and t₃/T₂ = 5.0310. If the associated amplitude-scaling hypothesis is retained, the predicted ratio is A₃/A₂ ≈ 0.551. The accompanying computational validation package develops the analysis pipeline through five stages: preliminary signal injection, blind null testing, blind injection-recovery, multi-qubit global-k inference, and sensitivity mapping. The synthetic null models include stretched-exponential decay, 1/f^α correlated noise, random-telegraph/TLS-like contributions, slow drift, white noise, and device-to-device variability. These simulations validate the detectability, specificity, and sensitivity of the proposed analysis procedure under the tested synthetic noise families. They do not constitute experimental evidence for the existence of the predicted physical effect. The next stage is a preregistered hardware implementation using superconducting qubits, with device-specific null calibration, blind analysis, systematic controls, held-out replication, and, ultimately, independent experimental replication.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: TEF-CIM: Heterogeneous Tri-Flow Training CIM Macro With Exponent-Exclusive Addend-Compression and Adder-Free Arithmetic Enabling Fused Weight Update
items.abstract: This article reports a heterogeneous tri-flow compute-in-memory (TEF-CIM) macro that enables end-to-end edge DNN training operations, including forward propagation, error backpropagation (EBP), weight gradient calculation (WGC), and weight update (WU). It features several techniques that enhance the area/energy efficiency and reduce the external memory access: 1) a bit-polarity-interleaved 4T/12T/14T addend-compression matrix-vector-multiplication (MVM) CIM core with complementary 5T-SRAM for hardware-efficient exponent-exclusive 8b (EF8) operation; 2) A vector-outer-product (VOP) CIM core with adder-free bit-select SRAM signed ripple counter, reducing the partial sum access of WGC by $37.3\times $ in ResNet-50; 3) a heterogeneous tri-flow data loading system fusing EBP, WGC, and WU, which reduces the total external memory access by $2.7\times $ in ResNet-50. The proposed TEF-CIM macro prototyped in 28-nm CMOS reaches a peak energy efficiency of 208.6 TFLOPS/W, and an area efficiency of 3.81 TFLOPS/mm 2 .
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: TCAD-assisted analysis of large-signal dynamic trap effects in GaN HEMT power amplifiers
items.abstract: The HB-POLITO TCAD tool is exploited to simulate the effect of Fe traps on power amplifier stages based on a GaN HEMT from a 150 nm technology, focusing in particular on the large signal behavior of the active device. The dispersive effects of traps lead to pronounced differences between Class A and deep Class AB amplifiers in terms of dynamic load lines, DC power consumption, and output power. Low frequency large signal simulations with varying loads have been carried out to identify possible ways to include these large signal trap dynamic effects in GaN HEMT models.

items.title: Surrogate-assisted DTCO for 1T1C FeMFET Bitcells: A Comparative Study on Model Choice and Data Sampling
items.abstract: Design–Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) of emerging memory technologies requires efficient exploration of large and highly nonlinear design spaces, making exhaustive simulation computationally expensive. Surrogate modeling provides an attractive alternative by learning the mapping between design parameters and circuit-level metrics from a limited set of simulations. However, the impact of the modeling paradigm and training dataset generation strategy remains under-explored, particularly for multi-input multi-output problems with heterogeneous target scales. In this work, we evaluate three machine learning surrogate approaches: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Random Forest (RF) for bitcell-level modeling of a 1T1C FeMFET. We compare datasets generated using Design of Experiments (DoE) and genetic algorithms and assess model accuracy, scalability with training size, and suitability for surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization. The resulting Pareto fronts define the feasible trade-off space at the bitcell level, which serves as the input design space for subsequent array-level exploration in crossbar architectures for in-memory computing.
items.venue: IFIP/IEEE International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration

items.title: Study on the Low-Power Transient Current Behavior in Scalable MIS Tunnel Diodes by Gear-Shaped Coupling Gate and High--Low Oxide Structures
items.abstract: Metal–insulator–semiconductor tunnel diode (MISTD) transient memory with designed coupling gates and high–low (HL) oxide structures was presented for capacitor-less dynamic memory. It was found that the quintuple gear-embedded arched structure reduces the device area by approximately 85% compared with the conventional concentric-circle structure and increases the transient memory window to about 104. This improvement is attributed to enhanced fringing electric fields at the high-curvature gear edges and the spatial concentration of process-induced oxide charges, which strengthen lateral carrier exchange. In addition, the dual-thickness HL oxide structure, featuring an inner-thick/outer-edge-thin dielectric profile, suppresses vertical tunneling leakage while maintaining lateral electrostatic coupling near the electrode edges. Multilevel cell (MLC) operation and reduced power consumption are also demonstrated, suggesting the feasibility of the proposed fully CMOS-compatible MISTD structure for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) applications.

items.title: Study on 3-D 1T1R Resistive Random Access Memory and Stacked Array for Chiplet Integration by Parallel Electrothermal Field-Circuit Co-Simulation
items.abstract: One-transistor-one-resistor (1T1R) structure plays a crucial role in chiplets for in-memory computing (IMC), offering significant advantages in terms of its integration density, energy efficiency, and scalability. This study at first introduces a 3-D massively parallel solver for electrothermal field-circuit co-simulation of 1T1R devices and stacked arrays. The multiphysics coupled processes in the 1T1R are described by circuit equations, Poisson’s equation, electron, hole, and oxygen vacancy transport equations, as well as the current continuity and heat conduction equations. The accuracy of our model is verified in comparison with experimental data and numerical results. By systematically investigating both resistor and transistor parameters, we demonstrate effective strategies for improving the resistance ratio, which is a critical performance metric for resistive random access memory (RRAM) applications. Additionally, we explore the impact of stacking layers in the 1T1R arrays, highlighting the thermal challenges caused by self-heating effects (SHEs) as the number of stacked layers increases. Different operating modes are also studied for reducing thermal crosstalk effects, among which a specialized multiline write operation mode is proposed for enhancing the operational efficiency.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Steady-State Dynamic $R_{\text{ON}}$ Measurements of GaN HEMTs: Role of Voltage- and Temperature-Dependent Time Constants
items.abstract: Steady-state measurements of the dynamic ON-resistance ( $R_{\text{ON}}$ ) in GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) are crucial due to the presence of slow charge trapping processes. This is often overlooked by most circuit-level studies, which fail to represent realistic steady-state operations and hinder direct comparison between different GaN technologies. In this work, we propose a steady state, time-resolved dynamic $R_{\text{ON}}$ characterization methodology spanning the microsecond-to-minute scale, enabling accurate evaluation of Schottky-type (GaN-1) and Ohmic-type (GaN-2) $p$ -GaN gate HEMTs under realistic hard- and soft-switching conditions up to 200 kHz. We reveal the role of different trapping time constants, which can exceed 10 min, along with their voltage and temperature dependencies. For GaN-1, we identify two off -state trapping processes: a fast $\mu$ s-scale process correlated with drain-bias-induced threshold voltage shift and its partial recovery; a slow, thermally activated process with an activation energy of 0.34 eV that closely follows off -state leakage behavior. Finally, fast detrapping processes in GaN-2 driven by gate-side and drain-side hole injection are identified, explaining its superior steady-state performance. These findings clarify the distinct trapping time scales and are important for understanding and optimizing GaN HEMT performance for efficient power conversion.

items.title: SpinTran: A Spintronic Transformer Accelerator Using Full-Precision Computing in Memory With Approximate Softmax Functions
items.abstract: Transformer models have made remarkable contributions to various artificial intelligence (AI) applications. However, high energy consumption and delay caused by matrix multiplication (MM) and softmax are bottleneck for hardware to implement transformer models. Computing in memory (CIM) is a promising architecture to solve these problems by reducing data movement and enabling highly parallel data processing. In this work, we propose a software-hardware co-design SpinTran accelerator using the full-precision spintronic CIM and approximate softmax functions for performing energy-efficient transformer models. First, a full-precision CIM scheme (FPCIM) based on toggle spin torque magnetic random-access memory (TST-MRAM) is proposed to realize fast MM operation. Second, we build a highly-reconfigurable array by utilizing the characteristic of TST-MRAM, which can write multiple bits into a column simultaneously to significantly reduce write-back cycles for dynamic matrix in transformer models. Third, we design an efficient Taylor expansion method that adopts approximation and range reduction techniques to achieve rapid convergence, thereby improving the computational efficiency of softmax function. Results show that the delay and energy efficiency of the proposed SpinTran accelerator are 3.5 ns and 56.7 TOPS/W in INT8 MAC operation, respectively. Meanwhile, the energy consumption is 4.71 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ μ J/token, 12.82 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ μ J/token, and 4.32 $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ μ J/token when executing Bert-base, Bert-large, and ViT-small models, respectively, which achieves 2.81 to 4.30 $\boldsymbol{\times}$ × energy reduction compared to other state-of-the-art works.

items.title: Spatially Varying Partial Polarization Switching Dynamics in Negative Capacitance FETs: Insights From Fully Numerical Simulations
items.abstract: In this study, we present a novel simulation framework for negative capacitance field-effect transistors (NCFETs), rigorously incorporating position- and gate-bias-dependent partial polarization behavior in ferroelectric (FE) layers. While previous theoretical approaches primarily assumed fully polarized FE (FPFE) states, our method integrates Poisson’s equation, the nonequilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism, and a minor loop FE polarization model to accurately simulate partially polarized FE (PPFE) states, which occur frequently under realistic operating conditions. Our results demonstrate that NCFETs operating under PPFE states demonstrate worsened subthreshold swing (SS) and drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) compared to the FPFE case. Specifically, we reveal that FPFE assumptions tend to overestimate the steepness of the switching behavior and illustrate how the magnitude of polarization distinctly affects the gate control and spatial conduction band profile. We further investigate and compare the impact of FE thickness and channel length on DIBL in FPFE- and PPFE-NCFETs, offering critical insights for the optimization of FE-based ultralow-power electronics.

items.title: Software-defined Significance-Driven Computing
items.abstract: Approximate computing has been an emerging programming and system design paradigm that has been proposed as a way to overcome the power-wall problem that hinders the scaling of the next generation of both high-end and mobile computing systems. Towards this end, a lot of researchers have been studying the effects of approximation to applications and those hardware modifications that allow increased power benefits for reduced reliability. In this work, we focus on runtime system modifications and task-based programming models that enable software-controlled, user-driven approximate computing. We employ a systematic methodology that allows us to evaluate the potential energy and performance benefits of approximate computing using as building blocks unreliable hardware components. We present a set of extensions to OpenMP 4.0 that enable the programmer to define computations suitable for approximation. We introduce task-significance, a novel concept that describes the contribution of a task to the quality of the result. We use significance as a channel of communication from domain specific knowledge about applications towards the runtime-system, where we can optimise approximate execution depending on user constraints. Finally, we show extensions to the Linux kernel that enable it to operate seamlessly on top of unreliable memory and provide a user-space interface for memory allocation from the unreliable portion of the physical memory. Having this framework in place allowed us to identify what we call the refresh-by-access property of applications that use dynamic random-access memory (DRAM). We use this property to implement techniques for task-based applications that minimise the probability of errors when using unreliable memory enabling increased quality and power efficiency when using unreliable DRAM.

items.title: Simultaneous Enhancement of Performance and Stability in Dual‐Gate a‐IGZO Thin‐Film Transistors via Single‐Step Laser Annealing for Capacitor‐Less DRAM (Adv. Funct. Mater. 84/2026)
items.abstract: Laser-Tailored Oxide Transistors A 532 nm CW laser heats the W top gate of a dual-gate a-IGZO TFT, driving oxygen redistribution at the Al2O3/IGZO interface and improving W/IGZO contacts. This single-step process enhances channel stability and contact properties, showing promise for capacitor-less DRAM read transistors. More details can be found in the Research Article by Hyuk-Jun Kwon and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77445).

items.title: Side-channel aware design of FeFET based memory for cryptographic SBox implementation
items.abstract: Among promising non-volatile emerging technologies that can tackle the von Neumann bottleneck of computing architectures, CMOS-compatible ferroelectric transistors (Fe-FETs) offer a large design space for exploring new computing paradigms. FeFETs can be used to create dedicated non-volatile logic gates where operands are stored inside the computing structures but also non-volatile and reconfigurable logic circuits and innovative memories, such as ternary content addressable memory.In this article, we explore how to scale the 1-bit Ternary Content addressable and MEMory (TC-MEM) circuit to multi-bit memory cells, with a particular attention to energy consumption to assess vulnerability to side-channel attacks of the proposed circuits. Then, we discuss the advantages and drawbacks of various implementations in terms of control logic, complexity, and attack countermeasures at array level.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Self-Heating Induced Differential Resistance in Complementary FET: The Role of Dielectric Insulation in Thermal Dynamics
items.abstract: The heat flux confined within the sheets or channels, that is, between the gate dielectric and across the dielectric sidewall ( ${D} _{\text {SW}}$ ), engenders a severe self-heating effect (SHE) in stacked transistors like complementary FETs (CFETs). This heat accumulation due to SHE reduces the velocity and mobility of charge carriers in the channel region, resulting in the negative differential resistance (NDR). This article extensively provides insight into SHE in CFETs using a first-principles approach, that is, from the fundamental current equation. In a conventional case, the carrier mobility, carrier concentration, velocity, and threshold voltage are temperature-dependent parameters; however, with SHE, the current ( ${I} _{\text {DS}}$ ) is also drain-voltage ( $V$ DS )-dependent. Using well-calibrated TCAD models, we demonstrate the electrical and thermal characteristics of the CFET by extracting the $I$ DS gradient as a function of temperature. We also investigated the CFET performance of the device under various parametric conditions, including channel width ( $W$ CH ), channel thickness ( ${T} _{\text {CH}}$ ), and extension length ( $L$ EXT ), and explained the significance of the dielectric layer in heat coupling across $D$ SW . The design guidelines for optimal $W$ CH , $T$ CH , and $L$ EXT are presented, considering $I$ ON / $C$ gg and intrinsic RC delay, as a figure of merit. Henceforth, the proposed work underscores the importance of integrated electrical and thermal evaluations in establishing a robust framework for reliable and energy-efficient CFET architectures.
items.venue: IEEE transactions on dielectrics and electrical insulation

items.title: Secure and Energy-Efficient Hardware Design for Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms in IoT Edge Devices
items.abstract: The impending advent of cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) threatens the fundamental security posture of modern Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems by invalidating public-key infrastructure (PKI) based on RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). In response, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has standardized Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) primary algorithms, including ML-KEM (CRYSTALS-Kyber) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) for digital signatures. However, transitioning PQC algorithms to resource-constrained IoT edge devices introduces severe hardware overheads in energy consumption, memory footprint, operational latency, and vulnerability to Physical Side-Channel Attacks (SCA) and Fault Injection Attacks (FIA). This paper presents a holistic hardware design methodology for integrating PQC algorithms into ultra-low-power IoT edge processors. We investigate domain-specific vector coprocessors, domain-optimized Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) multipliers, hybrid SRAM-eMRAM memory architectures, and Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) frameworks. Furthermore, we evaluate lightweight hardware countermeasures against power analysis (DPA/CPA) and electromagnetic leakage (EMA), demonstrating a zero-latency masking unit that preserves energy efficiency. Experimental evaluations on 22nm FD-SOI and 45nm CMOS technology nodes show a 7.8x speedup in NTT polynomial multiplication and a 64% reduction in overall energy per execution cycle, achieving robust quantum security under a 15 mW energy budget.
items.venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

items.title: Search-Space Efficient Optimization of Karatsuba Multipliers for ECDSA Hardware Accelerators
items.abstract: The elliptic-curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) has emerged as a secure, computation-efficient successor to the traditional digital signature algorithm (DSA), leveraging the hardness of elliptic-curve arithmetic to meet the demands of modern, resource-limited hardware platforms. This article presents a hardware-centric exploration of ECDSA architectures, in which GF( $2{^{{163}}}$ ) Karatsuba-based finite-field multipliers are systematically refined using fast-converging multiobjective optimization techniques. In contrast to conventional NSGA-II-driven methodologies, the adopted optimization strategies significantly reduce convergence time while yielding higher quality design solutions. The optimized multiplier hierarchies were embedded in ECDSA signature generation and verification engines and implemented on a Kintex Ultrascale FPGA, followed by an ASIC evaluation using OpenROAD with the Nangate 45-nm standard-cell library. Comparative analysis against state-of-the-art (SOTA) implementations reveals substantial efficiency gains with different multiplier sequences in terms of area, delay, and area-delay product (ADP). By coupling a fast-convergence multiobjective optimization algorithm and hierarchical Karatsuba multiplier optimization with accelerated design-space exploration, this work delivers ECDSA hardware architectures that significantly improve efficiency while preserving the correctness of ECDSA operations. To encourage reuse and further investigation, all hardware source files and experimental data are released publicly for the research community.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: Scalable Small-Signal Modeling of 20-nm InGaAs HEMTs Using a DC-Biased Backside Field Plate
items.abstract: We present a scalable small-signal model for III–V HEMTs featuring a DC-biased nanostructured backside field plate and an extended gate–drain recess to enhance breakdown voltage and enable higher millimeter-wave output power. The model extends a classical Common-Source shell topology by adding intrinsic elements that capture the capacitances and leakage paths between the backside field plate, the channel, the gate, and the drain, enabling accurate prediction of the associated small-signal behavior. The framework is experimentally validated using InGaAs HEMTs with a 20-nm gate length on 100-mm silicon substrates, where the backside field plate is implemented locally beneath the center of the gate–drain access region via wafer bonding and electron-beam lithography. The model describes unit gate widths from 5 μm to 30 μm, including 2- and 4-finger configurations. Bias-dependent parameters (as functions of IDS, VDS, and VBS) are extracted and verified over a wide operating range. The model consistently reproduces measured S-parameters from 1 GHz to 225 GHz under low-noise and power-amplifier bias conditions. The proposed approach provides a physically meaningful, scalable compact model that captures the impact of an advanced localized nanostructured DC-biased backside field plate.

items.title: Robust Extrinsic Parasitic Extraction for GaN HEMTs Using Full Bias-Range Cold-FET Optimisation
items.abstract: This work proposes a fully automated equivalent circuit extraction method that optimises over a larger cold-FET gate bias range than the isolated extreme points commonly used in the literature. It optimises the parastic element values using singular value decomposition (SVD) as a measure of linearity of admittance fits across frequency. Applied to both simulated and measured GaN HEMT device S-parameter datasets, the method shows improved parasitic extraction accuracy compared to existing techniques. Validation on synthetic GaN HEMT datasets indicates notable reductions in capacitance and S-parameter error metrics.

items.title: RoboPIM: A ReRAM-Based Accelerator for LLM-Based Robotics Applications via Dynamic Task Slicing
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant potential in improving robotics applications through natural language processing capabilities. Matrix multiplication dominates the computational workload in these LLM-based robotics systems, and resistive random access memory (ReRAM) provides notable performance benefits due to its inherent parallelism and energy efficiency. However, matrix multiplications in these applications pose dual heterogeneity challenges, encompassing both structural and scale heterogeneity. Structurally, these applications involve both standard dense matrix operations and block-structured sparse multiplications, where sparsity patterns vary significantly with robot topology. In terms of scale, matrix sizes range from just a few to thousands of dimensions, making large ReRAM crossbars designed for LLM inefficient for small-scale robotics computations. Existing acceleration approaches fail to address this dual heterogeneity, limiting their effectiveness for LLM-based robotics applications. In this work, we propose robotics applications-processing in memory (RoboPIM), the first low-energy ReRAM-based accelerator tailored for LLM-based robotics applications. robotics applications-processing in memory (RoboPIM) adapts to the diverse matrix multiplication requirements across robot platforms and LLM configurations. Our design features a ReRAM architecture with various crossbar sizes and implements a dynamic task slicing scheme that allocates matrix slices to appropriately sized crossbars. To maximize ReRAM’s parallel processing capabilities, we develop a two-stage scheduling strategy that efficiently manages matrix multiplications while enhancing hardware utilization. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that RoboPIM achieves $2.85\times $ and $6.85\times $ speedup across diverse robotic platforms and LLMs, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art domain-specific solutions.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Reliable HCI-based programming in V-NAND flash memory: co-optimization of SWL waveform and trap-cut architecture
items.abstract: Abstract Hot carrier injection-based programming has emerged as a high-efficiency alternative to conventional Fowler–Nordheim (FN) tunneling for next-generation vertical NAND (V-NAND), yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by coupled physical reliability trade-offs: program disturb, Z-interference, and retention degradation. This study investigates these bottlenecks through technology computer-aided design simulations calibrated to experimental PN junction and V-NAND reference data, and proposes a co-optimization framework combining switch word-line (SWL) waveform engineering with a trap-cut storage-node architecture. We demonstrate that the severe program disturb observed during the hold phase originates from localized lateral electric field crowding and subsequent impact ionization. This can be electrostatically mitigated by applying the negative SWL bias only during the set-up phase and returning the SWL to 0 V during the hold phase, achieving a 46.3% reduction in disturb under the most stringent victim-state conditions. Furthermore, we show that the aggravated Z-interference and lateral charge migration stem from the spatial spreading of hot electrons into the continuous spacer charge trap layer beyond the gate boundaries. By implementing a physically segmented trap-cut structure, the lateral charge transport path is severed, eliminating spacer charge trapping and yielding a 37.3% improvement in Z-interference over the conventional FN baseline while improving long-term retention. The proposed approach decouples the performance-reliability trade-offs and provides physical insight and an architectural solution for high-density V-NAND scaling. Experimental validation of the proposed scheme is a subject for future work.

items.title: Reliable Bi-Layer HfO2/Zr-Doped ZnO Memristive Synaptic Devices
items.abstract: Oxide-based memristive synaptic devices are promising hardware elements for neuromorphic computing, but stochastic resistive switching caused by uncontrolled defect distributions and localized conductive paths remains a critical challenge. Here, we demonstrate Zr-doped ZnO memristive synaptic devices fabricated using an atomic layer deposition (ALD) super-cycle process to regulate both defect states and surface morphology. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a decrease in the V O -related O 1s component from 34.9% to 23.2%, while atomic force microscopy showed a reduction in RMS surface roughness from 0.7532 to 0.2603 nm with less distinguishable surface-grain features. These results suggest that Zr incorporation suppresses V O -related defects and reduces grain-boundary-assisted localized conduction. Compared with the undoped device, the Zr-doped device exhibited improved switching uniformity, reduced resistance-state variation, stable pulse endurance, and retention for over ${10}^{{4}}$ s at 25, 50, and $75~^{\circ }$ C. The regulated defect distribution and surface morphology enabled gradual and reproducible conductance modulation during long-term potentiation and depression, resulting in improved synaptic linearity. Neural network simulations using experimentally extracted LTP/LTD nonlinearity parameters further demonstrated enhanced recognition accuracy in ANN and CNN classification tasks.

items.title: Reliability Improvement of Top-Gate ITO Transistors by Post-Metal Annealing at 450 °C
items.abstract: In this letter, we present significant reliability improvement of top-gate indium-tin-oxide (ITO) transistors through an optimized two-step post-metal annealing (PMA) conducted in an oxygen atmosphere at $450~^{\text {o}}$ C. By effectively suppressing oxygen-vacancy-related traps and interfacial defects, the optimized devices achieve exceptional bias temperature stability. Under a high electric field of ±6 MV/cm at room temperature, the threshold voltage shift ( $\Delta $ V ${}_{\text {th}}\text {)}$ is minimized to 9.9 mV for positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) and 2.2 mV for negative bias temperature instability (NBTI) after 1,000 s. Furthermore, the devices maintain robust stability under simultaneous high-field of ±5 MV/cm and high-temperature of $105~^{\circ }$ C stress, exhibiting a $\Delta $ V th of less than 50 mV after 3,000 s. These results demonstrate superior reliability under extreme operating conditions, establishing top-gate ITO transistors as viable candidates for next-generation back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible electronics.

items.title: Reliability Enhancement of Ga2O3 Heterojunction Diodes Due to Space-Charge Modulation
items.abstract: This work substantially improves the understanding of stability in p-NiO/n-Ga 2 O 3 heterojunction diodes (HJDs) under high forward bias stress, demonstrating that space-charge modulation via deep-level gallium vacancy (V ${}_{\text {Ga}}\text {)}$ states significantly enhances device reliability. Key results are: 1) two sequential charge-trapping (CT) processes are identified under sustained high stress, evidenced by distinctly opposing space-charge-limited current (SCLC) behaviors; 2) dynamic secondary ion mass spectrometry (D-SIMS) and capacitance–voltage ( $C$ – ${V}\text {)}$ analysis reveal that the CT processes involve V Ga -related space charge modulation: initial negative charge accumulation at V Ga states extending ~100 nm from the interface into the Ga 2 O 3 bulk, followed by neutralization via self-trapping of holes at adjacent oxygen sublattice sites (O ${}_{\text {I}}\text {)}$ ; and 3) remarkably, once both CT processes are complete, degradation is effectively suppressed and device reliability is markedly enhanced. These findings reveal a novel reliability physics in Ga 2 O 3 -based p-n heterojunctions, providing practical guidelines for fully exploiting their high-performance potential.

items.title: Recent Advances and New Directions in Superconductor Electronic Design Automation Tools
items.abstract: The successful completion of the intelligence advanced research projects activity (IARPA) SuperTools project, which significantly advanced the state-of-the-art in superconductor electronic design automation (EDA) tools, enabled superconductor electronics (SCE) designers to synthesize and verify complex circuits, such as 64-bit reduced instruction set computer processors. Advances under SuperTools included technology computer-aided design, logic and clock synthesis, place-and-route and compact model extraction directly from layouts. A recent defense advanced research projects agency (DARPA) project on homomorphic encryption with SCE circuits demanded improvements in high-level synthesis, place-and-route and timing extraction tools. New lumped-element transmission line models were introduced to simulation tools to handle not just reflections, but also cross-coupling, dispersion and loss on intergate transmission lines in very large digital systems. Despite the maturity of large-scale digital circuit design and analysis tools, recent developments in the field have exposed a need to add EDA capabilities for superconductor quantum computing (SQC) design, analysis, and verification. SQC end-user demand for tools that model and process flux trapping, vortex displacement, noise, high-precision extraction of weak magnetic coupling, and microwave frequency analysis for resonance and impedance has driven new directions in tool development. In this presentation, we discuss EDA advances post-SuperTools, including the new research and development efforts demanded by SQC applications.

items.title: Read Performance Optimization Strategies for Temporary Read Error in High-Density 3-D nand flash memory
items.abstract: Temporary read error (TRE) is a transient reliability issue uniquely observed in 3-D nand flash memory, and its impact has become increasingly significant in high-density multilevel stacked nand flash devices, such as 3-D triple-level cell (TLC), quad-level cell (QLC), and penta-level cell (PLC) technologies. TRE reduces the already limited reliability margin inherent to high-density storage, complicating efforts to further enhance device reliability. However, TRE can mislead threshold voltage (Vth) decision algorithms and read-retry algorithms, potentially causing incorrect threshold judgments and misguiding retry attempts. Such misdirection not only increases read latency but may even lead to uncorrectable errors (UECC). Although currently most TREs in nand flash memory can be effectively corrected by error correction code (ECC), the available ECC correction margin diminishes considerably at higher cell densities. Consequently, proactive management of TRE has become increasingly critical and urgent, as it offers significant potential to enhance both reliability and read latency performance in high-density nand flash systems. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive page-type-based reliability analysis throughout the entire lifespan of flash memory devices, systematically modeling and quantitatively analyzing idle-access-triggered occurrences of TRE and their effects on raw bit error rate (RBER), as well as read latency characteristics. Based on this analysis, we propose two lightweight system-level strategies—adaptive re-read (ARR) and preventive re-read (PRR)—designed to effectively mitigate read performance degradation caused by TRE. The proposed strategies are implemented in a TLC solid-state drive (SSD) simulator and evaluated using real-world enterprise workloads. The results demonstrate that, compared to the traditional error correction scheme without mitigation, ARR and PRR reduce the average read latency by 23.9% and 20.7%, respectively, while also reducing the average tail latency at the 99th and 99.9th percentiles by 42.1% and 63.5%, respectively. Our results validate the effectiveness of the proposed TRE management strategies and demonstrate that management of TRE at the system level can substantially improve overall read performance and enhance the quality of service (QoS) in high-density 3-D nand flash memory systems.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Rate-Compatible Protograph Low-Density Parity-Check Codes With Transfer Learning-Based Decoding for Spin-Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory
items.abstract: Spin-transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) is a promising non-volatile memory. However, fabrication process variations lead to diversity in raw bit error rates (BERs) across memory dies, making conventional fixed-rate error correction codes (ECCs) inefficient due to high coding redundancy and reduced memory storage density. Furthermore, the existing deep learning (DL)-based decoding approaches for ECCs are limited to fixed-rate codes and require retraining for each code rate, which consumes extensive training data and is costly in practice. In this work, we first propose an efficient approach for designing a new class of rate-compatible protograph low-density parity-check (RCP-LDPC) codes for STT-MRAM, which substantially outperform existing codes under the same channel conditions. We further develop a neural network (NN)-based min-sum (Neural MS) decoding algorithm for RCP-LDPC codes with parallel edges in the base graph. Building upon this decoder, we then propose a transfer learning (TL)-based decoding scheme to efficiently adapt neural decoders across different code rates. The simulation results show that the TL approach efficiently adapts the decoder to other code rates, requiring only 8% of the training data compared with a fully trained decoder while retaining comparable error-rate performance.

items.title: RF Stress-Induced Degradation Characteristics and Mechanism Analysis of AlGaN/GaN HEMTs at Different Compression Points
items.abstract: This article investigates the performance degradation of AlGaN/gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) under long-term radio frequency (RF) stress at different compression points and verifies the corresponding failure mechanisms using various characterization methods. Experimental results show that the DC and RF characteristics of the devices degrade severely under continuous over-drive stress for 100 h at P ${}_{\text {3 {dB}}}$ , P ${}_{\text {4. {5} {dB}}}$ , and P ${}_{6~ \text {dB}}$ . All stressed devices exhibit negative threshold voltage shift, degraded gate control capability, on -resistance increase, and prolonged gate hysteresis, and the saturated output power of the devices decreases by 0.22, 0.88, and 1.69 dB under the three over-drive conditions, respectively. In addition, low-frequency noise (LFN) measurements further confirm that the interface defect state density near the 2-D electron gas (2DEG) channel increases from ${2}.{10}{\,}\times {\,}{10} ^{{18}}$ cm ${}^{-{3}}~\cdot $ eV ${}^{-{1}}$ to ${1}.{91}{\,}\times $ ${10} ^{{19}}$ cm ${}^{-{3}}~\cdot $ eV ${}^{-{1}}$ . A physical model is established via TCAD simulation to analyze the high-electric-field stress mechanism. Unlike previous studies mainly focused on short-term RF stress or single characterization techniques, this work systematically correlates gate leakage evolution, gate-lag behavior, LFN characteristics, and TCAD electric-field analysis under long-term RF stress at different compression levels.

items.title: RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM
items.abstract: Processing-using-memory (PUM) architectures perform computation directly within DRAM to reduce costly data movement between memory and processors. Because charge-sharing operations are confined to individual bitlines, existing DRAM-PUM architectures reorganize data into column-oriented, bit-serial representations. This organization is fundamentally incompatible with the row-oriented, word-parallel layouts used by conventional processors and accelerators, requiring expensive data-layout transformations whenever computation transitions between PUM and conventional execution. In this paper, we present RAPID, a Row-parallel Arithmetic Processing-In-DRAM architecture. RAPID augments the DRAM subarray with two lightweight extensions: migration cells that enable localized horizontal data movement between neighboring bitlines and inversion cells that provide efficient in-array logical inversion. These primitives enable RAPID to operate directly on row-parallel, bit-parallel data, preserving CPU-compatible layouts while exploiting the massive parallelism of the DRAM subarray. In particular, RAPID demonstrates that localized horizontal communication is sufficient to realize shallow arithmetic networks and efficient parallel reduction for multiplication, reducing arithmetic latency while preserving throughput and eliminating costly data-layout transformations, all while maintaining the conventional DRAM array organization. We demonstrate the feasibility and overhead of augmenting DRAM subarrays with migration and inversion cells through detailed transistor-level layout and SPICE-validated circuit simulations. Using the RAPID compiler it is possible to evaluate the performance and data reorganization tradeoffs to ensure the best execution across combined CPU and PUM. Evaluating RAPID on 19 MLPerf benchmarks, there is a 5.9x higher end-to-end performance compared to SIMDRAM for DDR4 PUM execution.

items.title: Pushing the Limits of Computing: Transistor-to-Processor Benchmarking at 77 K With Self-Heating Effect
items.abstract: Owing to increased power density with each newer technology node, transistors suffer from increased Self-Heating (SH) at room temperature, which is a daunting challenge for circuits and processors’ reliability. Given the increasing interest in leveraging cryogenic temperatures to enhance the performance and energy efficiency of computing systems, understanding SH effects at cryogenic temperatures is critical for the reliability and optimization of such systems. This work presents a comprehensive investigation of SH effects from the transistor to the processor level on the advanced 5 nm FinFET node under cryogenic conditions, specifically at 77 K. Further, it presents a pioneering comparison of SH effects between 5 nm FinFET and 28 nm FDSOI transistors at 77 K. Our findings reveal that FinFET devices on bulk substrate, despite their 3D-confined structure and reduced scale to extreme 5 nm, exhibit better thermal characteristics compared to FDSOI devices at 77 K. This is primarily attributed to the inherent design of FDSOI devices, where the buried oxide layer acts as a thermal barrier, thereby significantly restricting heat dissipation. Further, we explore the standard cell libraries and a processor core operating at 77 K with and without i) SH effect and ii) scaled parasitic resistance using 5 nm FinFETs. The exploration undertaken in this study not only demystifies the thermal behavior of a cutting-edge 5 nm technology under extremely low temperatures but also establishes a new paradigm in selecting technologies for future high-performance computing applications at cryogenic temperatures. It opens new avenues for the development of more efficient and reliable computing systems, paving the way for future innovations in cryogenic computing.

items.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network for PGM Operation of 3-D CT-NANDs Under Data-Scarce Environments
items.abstract: For the first time in modeling the operation of 3-D charge trap (CT)-based nand flash memories, we demonstrate a physics-based model integrated with a physics-informed machine learning (ML) framework capable of both transient behavior prediction and inverse profiling of device parameters (SIPS-PINN). The constructed neural network (NN) is shown to successfully provide an automatic search for an optimal solution with high precision, and the parameter inverse profiling result shows that it is capable of reasonable tracking of physical conditions. The proposed framework is anticipated to lead to automation of cell behavior predictions and efficient cell design with a wide chance of further advancements and applications on different processes and operations, or data augmentation.

items.title: Performance Improvement of 3-D Si/IGZO Hybrid Circuits With Top-Tier Threshold Voltage Optimization Technology
items.abstract: The increasing demand for compact and energy-efficient artificial intelligence (AI) edge computing hardware necessitates advanced 3-D heterogeneous integration of silicon (Si) and oxide semiconductor (IGZO) devices. However, achieving precise threshold voltage (V ${}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ ) matching between bottom-tier Si transistors and top-tier indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs) remains challenging. This article presents an annealing-driven top-tier V ${}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ optimization technology that tunes the top-tier IGZO transistor’s electrical characteristics after interlayer metal interconnect formation, achieving an intertier V ${}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ difference below 0.1 V, enabling seamless monolithic 3-D integration with bottom-tier Si devices. Compared to other heterogeneous hybrid circuits using traditional technology, the proposed approach significantly enhances the performance of various 3-D Si/IGZO hybrid circuits, such as the inverter (INV) gain, ring oscillator (RO) frequency, and SRAM noise margin. In addition, the annealing-driven process provides a low-cost and flexible postfabrication approach for adjusting the V ${}_{\mathbf {\text {th}}}$ of top-tier IGZO devices, which may be useful for process-window optimization in Si/IGZO heterogeneous monolithic 3-D integration.

items.title: PDAcc: A Prefill-Decode Disaggregated MCM-Based Accelerator for Multi-Task Large Language Model Applications
items.abstract: Prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation has emerged as a promising serving paradigm for large language models (LLMs), as it decouples prompt processing (prefill) from autoregressive token generation (decode) to reduce inter-task interference and improve quality of service (QoS). However, disaggregation also amplifies stage imbalance: the prefill cluster (P-C) can become compute-limited, the decode cluster (D-C) is often bandwidth-limited, and the required cross-device KV cache transfer introduces additional communication overhead. This work presents PDAcc , a four-chiplet multi-chip-module (MCM) accelerator optimized for PD-disaggregated LLM inference. PDAcc employs reconfigurable chiplets that can be dynamically assigned to prefill or decode according to workload ratios. It further introduces three techniques: copy-less float hybrid-LUT multiply (CFHM) to repurpose idle on-chip SRAM for prefill acceleration, hybrid compressed weight gather (HCWG) to utilize prefill-side bandwidth and improve inter-chip weight delivery for decode, and cross-cluster attention dataflow (CCAD) to reduce dependency traffic by shifting part of attention computation across clusters. Implemented in 22-nm technology as a four-chiplet MCM, PDAcc sustains 541–4727 effective tokens/s on GPT-2, OPT, and Llama 3.2, achieving $5.76\times $ higher prefill throughput and $12.42\times $ higher decode throughput than a single chiplet, and further delivering an additional 1.50– $3.24\times $ improvement over a four-chiplet PD-aggregated baseline with the same MCM scaling.

items.title: PCB-Embedded SiC MOSFET Packaging Using Shield to Suppress Near-Field Magnetic Radiation
items.abstract: Wide bandgap semiconductor printed circuit board (PCB)-embedded packaging offers a small size and low parasitic parameters, potentially improving the power density and switching performance of power electronic converters. However, due to the high switching frequency and fast speed of wide bandgap semiconductors, coupled with the high device density of PCB-embedded packaging, reducing electromagnetic interference (EMI) poses a critical challenge. This article newly proposes a shielded PCBembedded packaging that utilizes a copper layer in the PCB to shield the near-field magnetic radiation induced by silicon carbide devices. Finite element analysis shows that the proposed shielded PCB-embedded packaging reduces magnetic field interference significantly by 96.2% compared with an unshielded PCB-embedded packaging.

items.title: Origin of positive bias stress-induced threshold voltage shifts in amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O thin-film transistors
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding the origin of bias-stress instability is critical for the reliable operation of amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (IGZO) thin-film transistors (TFTs). Here, we investigate the mechanism of positive bias stress (PBS)-induced threshold-voltage ( V th ) shifts in bottom-gate IGZO TFTs through electrical, chemical, and electronic structural analyses. The devices exhibit typical n-type characteristics with a field-effect mobility of 5.2 cm 2 /V∙s and an on/off ratio exceeding 10 4 . Under PBS, a significant positive V th shift is observed, whereas the mobility and subthreshold swing remain nearly unchanged. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density-of-states analyses reveal no detectable changes in the chemical states or electronic structure of the IGZO layer after PBS. In contrast, frequency-dependent capacitance measurements show a reduced resonance frequency and increased trap density in the SiO 2 dielectric. These results indicate that dielectric electron trapping, rather than semiconductor degradation, is the dominant origin of PBS-induced V th shifts in IGZO TFTs.

items.title: Open-Source Multi-Wire SPI Readout for Wearable Ultrasound Probes
items.abstract: Wearable ultrasound probes must transfer increasingly large acquisition payloads while maintaining compact, low-power electronics. In TinyProbe, the current bottleneck in data transfer occurs between the acquisition FPGA and the wireless system controller. This work presents an open-source, multi-wire SPI readout interface that uses serial command and address phases followed by a build-time-selectable dual- or quad-lane payload phase that is intended to address this bottleneck by increasing the potential bandwidth over the wifi limit while retaining compatibility with the Microcontroller-centric wearable US architecture. The interface emulates a serial flash memory, enabling compatibility with a broad range of microcontroller families and their existing peripheral interfaces. On the FPGA, the data path connects the existing acquisition FIFOs to the SPI interface through clock-domain crossing, sample reshaping, and packing into 32-bit words. Dual-SPI readout is integrated into the existing IGLOO2/SiWG917 TinyProbe architecture and verified at an SCLK frequency of 5 MHz. A separate Kria K26 testbed is used to characterize the FPGA SPI interface independently of the acquisition and wireless subsystems, demonstrating error-free transfers at SCLK frequencies up to 66 MHz. These measurements identify the SiWG917 multi-lane SPI implementation as the next bandwidth-limiting component and motivate a future upgrade of the system controller. The HDL and MCU implementations are released under a permissive open-source license.

items.title: Novel Unipolar Stacked FET (USFET) Architecture Enabled by Tri-Layer Dummy Gate, Quasi-GAA SD Process, and Interconnect Innovations
items.abstract: In this work, a novel unipolar stacked FET (USFET) is proposed, featuring nFET-on-nFET or pFET-on-pFET stacking with split gate (SG). From the perspective of process complexity, USFET shows a distinct advantage over complementary FET (CFET) by adopting a quasi-gate-all-around (GAA) source/drain (SD) process. Furthermore, a tri-layer dummy gate (TDG) process is proposed to simplify the SG process. This process can also be extended to CFET to facilitate the integration of heterogeneous channels and different gate stacks. From the perspective of interconnect design, a common-SD (CSD) structure can be incorporated in USFET, and its area efficiency and routing complexity can be optimized simultaneously. By integrating these innovations, USFET shows superior performance in both area scaling and electrical performance. Additionally, the USFET enables wider bit-line (BL)/BLB for further optimization. Compared to CFET, USFET static random access memory (SRAM) with wider BL/BLB (USFETWBL) delivers a 23.1% area reduction, a $2.8\times $ higher write margin (WM), and decreases read and write delays by 19.1%/25.1% (frontside/backside) and 32.4%, respectively, proving its potential for advanced nodes.

items.title: NCMemSim: Nanocrystal Memory Simulation Platform
items.abstract: A modular Python framework for simulation and design-technology co-optimization of Ge/GeSn nanocrystal non-volatile memories, including multi-floating-gate state dynamics, compact electrostatics, local fields, WKB tunnelling, charge redistribution, retention, optical and electro-optical programming, experimental-data handling, deterministic parameter fitting, uncertainty diagnostics, calibration qualification, deterministic design-space sweeps, Pareto and grid sensitivity analysis, bounded independent uncertainty propagation, explicit robust objectives, reproducible nominal and Robust DTCO reports, immutable scientific workflow evidence, fitted evaluator contexts, linked workflow exports, opt-in trap-assisted transport with image-force barrier corrections, mechanism-resolved diagnostics and reports, reproducible stochastic nanocrystal ensembles, population statistics, feasibility and failure accounting, variability-aware DTCO, ensemble Pareto analysis, and integrity-checked ensemble reports, explicit model/TAT-density variability, isolated model execution, source-linked population and Pareto analysis, strict MODEL report bundles, opt-in reference-anchored Si and Ge temperature properties, isolated thermal simulation contexts, thermal DTCO, source-linked thermal report bundles, validation, and reproducibility tools.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: N+ Ring Shaped Pocket CY-GAA-TFET Architecture for Low-Power High Speed RF Application
items.abstract: An N+ ring pocket Cylindrical Gate All Around (CY-GAA) TFET is proposed in this work to improve on current. The analytical modeling of the N+ ring pocket at the source-channel interface shows that it significantly increases electrostatic potential, electric field and thus reduces tunneling barrier and finally results in increased drain current. The proposed structure achieves an on current of 1.1×10-3 A/µm and an Ion/Ioff ratio of 2.6×1010 for a ring radius of 10 nm, shows a significant improvement over the conventional CY‑GAA TFET. The transconductance (gm) and cutoff frequency (Ft) are enhanced by 48% and 36%, respectively. Further, an inverter and a three-stage ring oscillator are designed using Cadence Virtuoso tools by using its Verilog-A model. The inverter exhibits a 27% reduction in propagation delay and 33% lower power consumption, while the ring oscillator achieves an oscillation frequency of 4.4 GHz with improved spectral purity.
items.venue: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology

items.title: Monolithic Integration of Hybrid 2T0C DRAM/FeRAM With In-Situ Weight Transfer
items.abstract: In this work, we demonstrate a monolithically integrated hybrid memory that stacks 2T0C DRAM on FeRAM and enables in-situ weight transfer within a single cell. Leveraging an MIS stack enabled by the monolithic all-ALD process, the 2T0C DRAM achieves an off-state leakage of $8.48\times 10^{-{14}}$ A/ $\mu $ m, retention >200 s, endurance $\gt 10^{{11}}$ cycles, and stress immunity >10000 s. Meanwhile, the all-ALD TiN/HZO/TiN FeRAM exhibits 2P ${}_{\text {r}} \gt 50~\mu $ C/cm 2 , with projected retention >10 years and endurance $\gt 10^{{10}}$ cycles. Beyond co-integration, bidirectional in-situ transfer is realized without external circuits. Specifically, the large read window (high I ON /I ${}_{\text {OFF}}\text {)}$ of the 2T0C DRAM programs its “0”/“1” states into distinct FeRAM polarization states via controlled polarization reversal, while the large displacement current during FeRAM switching is exploited to reload the FeRAM state back into the 2T0C DRAM. This hybrid cell enables in-cell bidirectional volatile–nonvolatile transfer, serving as a compact primitive for hybrid memory hierarchies, compute-in-memory, and energy-efficient AI with rapid updates and persistent storage.

items.title: Moisture-Accelerated Gate-Oxide Failure in 1200-V SiC MOSFETs Under Repetitive Avalanche Stress
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs are increasingly adopted in high-efficiency power systems where avalanche events are prevalent. However, the coupled impact of environmental humidity and repetitive avalanche stress is not well understood, which complicates reliability assessment under realistic mission profiles. In this work, the repetitive-avalanche characteristic lifetime to catastrophic gate-oxide breakdown is found to decrease markedly with humidity, even though the single-pulse avalanche ruggedness remains comparable at 25% RH and 85% RH; within the investigated range, the characteristic lifetime is reduced by about 15.7% for every 10% increase in RH. To clarify the underlying degradation process, fixed- and step-change-humidity unclamped inductive switching (UIS) experiments are combined with interrupted-device emission microscopy (EMMI), failure analysis, TCAD simulation, and capacitance–voltage ( $C_{G}$ – $V_{G}$ ) characterization. The results support a two-stage degradation scenario in which a localized precursor gate-leakage path first forms under repetitive avalanche with only weak humidity dependence, whereas the subsequent charge buildup and propagation to final breakdown are strongly accelerated by humidity. Based on these findings, a semi-empirical lifetime model is established to support humidity-aware repetitive-avalanche reliability assessment of the investigated 1200-V planar-gate SiC MOSFET platform.
items.venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics

items.title: Modeling and design of energy-efficient dependable memory sub-systems
items.abstract: The rapid increase of processed data is driving the aggressive scaling of DRAM for meeting the needs of higher memory density and bandwidth. As a result of the high memory demand, projections forecast that the memory sub-system will be responsible for a considerable portion of the overall power consumption within most multicore systems. However, the DRAM scaling is hampered by the adoption of pessimistic circuit parameters, that are selected based on the worst-case conditions for reliable operation. Such an approach might guarantee error-free storage of data, but the incurred power and performance overheads raise doubts about its efficiency in the future. This dissertation is focused on characterization and modeling of the DRAM behaviour under non-nominal DRAM circuit parameters, and design of energy-saving techniques in real systems to ensure the reliable operation of the system. Initially, we present the characterization of the DRAM reliability under relaxed circuit parameters and various conditions. We are able to understand the major effects of the workloads on the DRAM error behaviour under realistic conditions. In order to achieve this, we have developed an experimental framework on two server systems and a thermal testbed to control the DRAM temperature. We analyze the correlation between the DRAM error behavior, and the circuit parameters, temperature and workload-depended features. We apply supervised learning methods to construct a prediction model of the DRAM error behaviour based on the main features identified by our characterization. The prediction allows us to relax the DRAM circuit parameters just enough to avoid errors while having the maximum energy savings possible. We develop a benchmark that is able to stress the system even when the server is in the field. Furthermore, we propose a heterogeneous-reliability memory framework that enables allocation of critical data in a reliable memory domain, while the rest of the data are allocated on a variably-reliable memory domain. This ensures the reliable operation and storage of critical data in memory that is operating under nominal circuit parameters. While data that can tolerate errors are stored in memory that is operating under relaxed circuit parameters and is more energy-efficient. We introduce a programming interface to expose the capabilities of the framework to the users and a governor for scaling the DRAM circuit parameters dynamically. We extend the system with a checkpoint and restart mechanism to ensure even in the worst-case that data can be restored. We further enable the user of the framework to evaluate the fault tolerance and approximate techniques of their applications by implementing it on a real system. Finally, we devise software techniques to enable the exploitation of the refresh-by-access property of DRAM. We modify the scheduling order of accesses to the memory controller by re-ordering of the tasks in an application to minimize the duration of data residing in memory. This results eventually in decreased probability of errors. We extend our methodology in an application specific compiler to bound the access interval for all application data. We achieve this by controlling the size of each task and the order, while tracing the data accessed for each task. In the process to understand the refresh-by-access property, we develop a simulator for fast measurement of the interval between accesses through binary instrumentation. We use the outputs of the simulator to better understand the refresh-by-access property and to improve the existing DRAM fault injection schemes. By taking into consideration of the real duration that the data were stored in memory, we have more representative error fault injection when DRAM is operating under relaxed circuit parameters.

items.title: Mixed-Signal Fractional-N Frequency Synthesis Building Blocks in 45 nm CMOS: Differential DTMOS VCO, Multi-Modulus Divider, and MASH 1-1-1 Controller
items.abstract: This paper presents transistor-level building blocks for fractional-N frequency synthesis in 45 nm CMOS. The main contribution is a five-stage differential current-starved ring VCO using gate-to-body-connected dynamic-threshold MOS devices and sleep-stack transistors placed only in alternate stages to limit the added delay and capacitive loading. The digital section includes an eight-stage multi-modulus frequency divider based on push-pull cascode logic divide-by-2/3 cells and a MASH 1-1-1 sigma-delta controller. All circuits are implemented in Cadence Virtuoso with a nominal 1.0 V supply. Post-layout simulation of the VCO gives an oscillation frequency of 9.24 GHz, phase noise of −124.38 dBc/Hz at a 1 MHz offset, and power consumption of 59.4 µW, corresponding to an FoM of −215.96 dBc/Hz. At Vctrl=0.5 V, the extracted VCO remains oscillatory over 60 combined process, supply voltage, and temperature conditions, with the oscillation frequency ranging from 6.43 to 10.96 GHz. The MMFD, MASH controller, and their integrated fractional-division path are evaluated under the reported nominal operating conditions; PVT robustness of the combined digital path is not established in this work. The digital-path validation includes analysis of fractional-divider command convergence, edge-count consistency, output line spectra, and characterization of the third-order noise-transfer response. The work focuses on the design and validation of individual frequency-synthesis building blocks rather than a complete closed-loop fractional-N PLL.

items.title: Memristive In-Memory Computing for AI: Neural Network Acceleration, Adaptive Learning, and System Integration
items.abstract: Moving data between memory and processing units has become a major cost in neural network computing. Memristive crossbars address this cost by retaining model parameters as conductance states and performing parallel multiplication and accumulation within the array. This review examines how that physical operation is translated into numerical formats, peripheral circuits, neural-network mappings, heterogeneous accelerators, local learning, compilation, and calibration. Fabricated chips have demonstrated substantial parallelism and lower weight traffic. Their application performance, however, is determined just as strongly by utilization, data conversion, unsupported operations, programming overhead, and device variation. Representative heterogeneous systems combine memristive arrays with static random-access memory (SRAM), digital logic, and software, assigning each resource the work it handles most efficiently. Current hardware evidence is strongest for inference and limited adaptation. Continuous monitoring, remapping, and recovery remain largely runtime design goals. Peak array efficiency alone is therefore insufficient; comparisons should use measured workloads and clearly stated system boundaries.

items.title: Market Risk Connectedness and Tail Risk in the Global High-Bandwidth Memory Oligopoly
items.abstract: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) is a critical AI-semiconductor bottleneck concentrated among Micron, Samsung Electronics, and SK Hynix. Using 1,895 aligned daily USD log returns (2018–2025), this study combines asymmetric GARCH, rolling Diebold-Yilmaz connectedness, and 99% Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). The five-variable network has a total connectedness index (TCI) of 38.1%, versus 20.0% for the memory-only triad. Contrary to the initial hypothesis, post-AI connectedness falls from about 43% to 39%. HBM suppliers are net receivers—especially SK Hynix—while SOX and NVIDIA transmit risk. The equal-weighted HBM portfolio's tail risk rises in the AI regime but remains below SOX. HBM firms are therefore best interpreted as downstream risk-absorbing nodes with a supplier-specific connectedness component.

items.title: MRAM-Based CiM Architecture for Backpropagation-Free Training of Neural Networks Using DFA and DRTP
items.abstract: Conventional backpropagation’s (BP) sequential nature limits its efficiency on compute-in-memory (CiM) architectures. To address this challenge, this work proposes the first CiM accelerator framework for training neural networks using direct feedback alignment (DFA) and direct random target propagation (DRTP) implemented on magnetoresistive random access memory (MRAM)-based CiM crossbars. By exploiting the inherent parallelism of these learning rules, the proposed design enables concurrent error propagation and weight-gradient computation for all layers. A CiM-aware mapping strategy is developed for forward computation, error projection, and gradient evaluation on crossbar arrays, along with hierarchical organization and pipelining to improve hardware utilization. The architecture is evaluated across fully connected and convolutional neural networks. Results show an average of 36% and 50% improvement in area and energy efficiency compared to BP-based training, while pipelining further reduces iteration latency and improves throughput. In particular, DRTP enables inter-iteration pipelining and achieves more than 100% higher throughput than BP in spin-orbit torque (SOT)-MRAM-based CiM architectures, demonstrating an efficient approach for scalable and energy-efficient on-chip neural network training.

items.title: MOMAT: Mixture of Multiple Atlases for Low-Power Jailbreak Defense of Quantized LLMs
items.abstract: Quantized large language models are increasingly deployed on edge devices for their low latency and energy efficiency. However, model quantization weakens alignment safeguards, leaving qLLMs (quantized large language models) highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. To address this challenge, we present MOMAT (Mixture of Multiple Atlases), a hardware-enhanced safety framework that combines structured knowledge retrieval with low-power defense acceleration. Each atlas represents a semantic cluster of harmful or benign sample sets and policy templates, enabling domain-localized Retrieval-Augmented Generation guarding that mitigates the curse of dimensionality and the resulting semantic sparsity problem in large, heterogeneous safety databases. MOMAT retrieves top-$k$ similarity features from all atlases for each prompt and evaluates them using a lightweight MoE (Mixture of Experts) detector, while a CiM (Compute-in-Memory)-accelerated similarity engine performs fast, low-power atlas-local retrieval. MOMAT's CiM-based retrieval accelerates a 100-query batch from 15,052.44 ms to 3,207.21 ns (a $4.69 \times 10^6\times$ speedup) and reduces energy from $8.1 \times 10^7$ $\mu$J to 3.32 $\mu$J, yielding an approximately $2.5 \times 10^5\times$ energy reduction over DRAM-based (Raspberry Pi) baselines. Red-team evaluations across standard benchmarks show that MOMAT matches the defense performance of state-of-the-art methods while avoiding benign overkill and providing substantial efficiency gains, demonstrating that CiM-based modular defenses can make edge-deployed qLLMs both safer and more energy-efficient. We will release the full 223.2k-sample dataset to foster future research.

items.title: Low-Bit-Error-Rate Cross-Temperature Compensation in 3-D TLC NAND Flash Memory: Observations, Modeling, and Solutions
items.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) and edge systems is driving continuous advances in nand flash capacity and performance. However, large and rapid temperature fluctuations in these scenarios cause threshold voltage distribution (TVD) shifts, leading to reduced reliability and degraded performance. Conventional analog temperature compensation circuits provide linear voltage compensation only within a limited temperature range, and subsequent models built upon these circuits show poor generality. To overcome these limitations, we construct an intrinsic cross-temperature model that captures the relationship between TVD shift and cross-temperature amplitude at the chip level, excluding the effects of circuit compensation and mitigating short-term retention loss effects, thereby ensuring strong generality. Based on this model, we propose a model-based adaptive temperature compensation (MB-ATC) scheme, which adaptively applies either circuit-based compensation or model-based operating voltage adjustment according to the operating temperature range. This approach achieves high reliability and performance across the wide temperature range of $- 40~^{\circ }$ C to $120~^{\circ }$ C. The experimental results show that, under extreme cross-temperature conditions, the proposed scheme reduces the raw bit error rate (RBER) by up to 61.34%, approaching the 68.40% upper bound of read-retry, and decreases read latency by up to 67.44% compared with the baseline.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe2 monolayers
items.abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance p-type monolayer transistors is critical for extending two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors beyond silicon in sub 1-nm technology nodes for complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits. However, insufficient doping and metal-induced gap states (MIGS) during metal deposition lead to high contact resistance, greatly limiting p-type on-state currents. Here, we demonstrate high-performance ballistic p-type monolayer tungsten diselenide (WSe 2 ) transistors by oxygen p-doping. The controllable oxygen doping greatly reduces the number of Se vacancy defects in as-grown WSe 2 , and thus increases the hole mobility from 55 to 218.3 cm 2 V −1 s −1 —approaching the theoretical limit. Moreover, this approach also induces a heavily hole-doped contact region in p-type monolayer WSe 2 devices and decreases the contact resistance from 1869 Ω·μm down to 104 Ω·μm. Consequently, a 16-nm-channel WSe 2 p-type field effect transistor (pFET) delivers a saturation current of up to 1635 μA μm −1 at a drain voltage of −1.2 V and a ballistic ratio as high as 81% at room temperature.

items.title: Location-Selective Dual Work-Function Engineering for DRAM Vertical Cell Transistors
items.abstract: As dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) technology approaches the scaling limit of conventional 6F2 buried-channel array transistor (BCAT) structures, vertical cell transistors (VCTs) have emerged as promising candidates for future 4F2 DRAM architectures. In this work, a location-selective Dual Work-Function (DWF) engineering scheme is proposed to co-optimize leakage and drive-current characteristics in VCT devices. Using calibrated three-dimensional TCAD simulations, lower-work-function n+ polysilicon regions were selectively introduced into the front-gate (FG) and back-gate (BG) electrodes. In the buried contact (BC)-side DWF implementation, the local gate electrostatics near the BC junction were modulated, thereby reducing the peak electric field responsible for gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL). The FG_BC DWF reduced GIDL current by up to 66% while maintaining a threshold voltage (V ${}_{\text {T}}\text {)}$ shift below 10 mV and less than 1% variation in ON-current. In the bit line (BL)-side DWF implementation, the reduced work function lowered the electron injection barrier near the BL-side carrier-injection region, leading to ON-current enhancement of up to 12.6% while maintaining nearly unchanged VT and subthreshold swing (SS). In addition, a combined FG_BC+BG_BL structure demonstrated concurrent GIDL suppression and ON-current enhancement without additional WL resistance overhead. These results indicate that location-selective DWF engineering, enabled by the vertically separated BC-side and BL-side junctions, provides a promising design guideline for low-leakage and high-performance 4F2 DRAM VCTs.
