items.title: Life Cycle Assessment and Circularity Strategies of GaN-on-SiC Substrates for RF
items.abstract: The resource consumption of semiconductors for modern electronics is of growing concern, particularly in the context of sustainable development. It is well known that semiconductor production consumes critical amounts of materials, energy and water, but detailed data remain scarce. Using the life cycle assessment method, this study assesses the environmental impact of GaN-on-SiC for high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) devices. GaN-HEMTs offer high efficiencies, enabling smaller chip footprints and lower operational energy consumption. Following the 9R-framework of circular economy, potential circularity strategies reduce, reuse and recycle are discussed. The results demonstrate that switching to renewable energies or by implementing a lift-off method, the impact can be reduced drastically. By providing detailed data on the production of power and radio frequency devices, and presenting circularity strategies, this work supports informed and sustainability-oriented decision-making.

items.title: Layer-by-layer growth of highly aligned MoS$_2$ nanoribbon arrays
items.abstract: One-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) nanoribbons (NRs) offer a promising route to aggressive channel-width scaling in nanoscale transistors. However, controlling their layer number, a key determinant of device performance, has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) approach for layer-by-layer growth of MoS$_2$ NRs on a low-symmetry sapphire surface. This approach enables the oriented growth of single-crystalline bilayer NRs with a 2H stacking configuration, while maintaining widths below 20 nm. Increasing the MoO$_3$ precursor supply was found to be crucial for promoting the growth of the second and subsequent layers. By controlling the growth time and precursor supply, the layer number of MoS$_2$ NRs can be increased up to four layers. This method can also be extended to the growth of vertical MoS$_2$/WS$_2$ hetero-NRs. The average carrier mobility and current density of bilayer NR field-effect transistors (FETs) are two- and three-times higher than those of monolayer counterparts, respectively, and a maximum mobility of 86.7 cm$^2$V$^{-1}$s$^{-1}$ was attained with a bilayer NR-FET. These results highlight layer number as a key parameter for optimizing NR device performance. Our thickness-controlled growth strategy provides a general route towards TMD NR-based transistors with enhanced scalability and performance.

items.title: K/Ka−band load-pull performance of AlGaN/GaN/AlN HEMTs on free-standing AlN substrates
items.abstract: We demonstrate first K/Ka band CW load-pull (LP) measurements of AlGaN/GaN/AlN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) on free-standing AlN substrates at 20GHz and above. The AlN buffer on AlN shows a much lower dislocation density compared to the same epitaxial stack grown on SiC substrates. The devices with a gate length of 220 nm exhibit an off-state leakage current below 100 µA mm−1 and a maximum Ids of around 1 A mm−1. Measured with passively-tuned LP equipment at 10 (20) GHz the devices with a gate width of 8× 75µm reveal up to 58 (40) % maximum power added efficiency, 14 (9) dB gain and 4.1 (2.8) W mm−1 Pout, where higher drain voltages lead to an increase in Pout. For 30GHz 33%, 7 dB and 2.6 W mm−1 were measured with an actively-tuned equipment for 4× 50µm devices. The 20 and 30 GHz measurements are to the best of our knowledge the first reported so far for GaN HEMTs on AlN substrates underlining the potential of this material system.

items.title: JTAG You’re It: A Scalable JTAG Network in Chiplet Arrays via Fabric-Reuse
items.abstract: As chiplet-based architectures push systems towards using larger numbers of smaller dies, the area overhead of dedicated I/O becomes increasingly important, as pad geometries do not scale with Moore’s law. We introduce a transaction-based framework that enables capabilities beyond conventional IEEE 1149.1 JTAG, including dynamic re-routing and selective broadcasting. The presented fabric-reuse eliminates the need for dedicated JTAG pads by embedding test access into packets on an existing Die-to-Die link. This technique supports independent power-gating and configuration of chiplets while maintaining system-level debug access through dynamic routing. A 22nm FDSOI silicon proof-of-concept validates the reconstruction of IEEE 1149.1-compatible JTAG signals from out-of-band packets on the die-to-die link, providing extended IEEE 1149.1 capabilities.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Investigation of Frequency-Reliant Dielectric Constant-Dependent Drain-Engineered Ferroelectric Gate Tunnel FET for Biosensing in Glioblastoma Multiforme
items.abstract: A ferroelectric (Fe) gate dielectric-modulated (DM) drain-engineered (DE) tunnel field-effect transistor (Fe-DM DE TFET) biosensor for detecting and differentiating brain tissues, in particular glioblastoma, meningioma, white matter, and gray matter, based on their frequency-dependent permittivity, is presented in this article. According to the study, tumor tissues show distinct permittivity peculiarities compared to normal brain matter. This investigation analyses the impact of dielectric dispersion in specific tissues on device performance. Higher dielectric constants associated with tumor tissues enhance tunneling and gate coupling, thereby increasing the on-state current, altering gate capacitance and transconductance, and improving the sensor’s sensitivity. Comprehensive Sentaurus TCAD simulations demonstrate that the proposed biosensor exhibits high drain current sensitivity in the $10^{{5}}$ range. A low detection limits across a wide range of frequencies (1, 5, and 10 GHz), making it ideal for label-free, noninvasive biomedical diagnostics. The suggested Fe-DM DE TFET that relies on a dielectric-constant biosensor is a suitable platform for detecting and differentiating early-stage brain tumors.

items.title: Investigating the behavior of hydrogenated amorphous silicon under UHDR proton beam
items.abstract: Radiation-based therapies are crucial treatments in the fight against malignant cancers. Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) proton therapy promises a higher radiobiological advantage and increased effectiveness in targeting tumor cells while sparing healthy cells by providing the total dose in a short time at a rate higher than 40 Gy/s. This work aims to characterize a hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) pixel under UHDR proton beams. A-Si:H gains particular interest due to its capacity to produce large-scale and high-resolution flat panel detectors at an affordable cost with high radiation hardness. A test board of a 2.4 × 2.4 mm2 a-Si:H pixel array was acquired and bonded to test at MedAustron in Wiener Neustadt. The test plan was to irradiate using a single spot of constant dose at different spill lengths and spill numbers to test the behavior from conventional to flash regimes for dose rate dependence measurements. Additionally, an ionization chamber for proton measurements (IBA PPC05) was placed at the isocenter for dose and spill length verification. The chamber was connected to the IBA DoseX electrometer equipped with an API measuring at a rate of 1 kHz. To analyze dose rate dependence, measurements were normalized twice by the dose measured via the PPC05 and the average of the specific measurement group. The integration time was kept the same at 10 s for all measurements. At higher dose rates and the same doses, the normalized charge increases until it reaches a plateau, then saturates in the flash regime. This is expected since, at higher current, charge traps get filled the higher the dose rate, until all the charge traps saturate. To test for radiation hardness, dose sensitivity was measured before and after heavy irradiation of 3 kGy using a clinical map. The sensitivity was reduced by 10%. The results were reproducible and linear with dose.

items.title: Interface Chemistry Modulation and Reliability Enhancement of ErTixOy/Si Gate Stacks Using an ALD-Derived HfAlO Passivation Layer
items.abstract: In this work, an ErTi ${}_{x}$ O ${}_{y}$ /hafnium aluminum oxide (HfAlO)/Si gate-stack structure was designed and fabricated. The modulation effect of atomic layer deposition (ALD)-derived HfAlO passivation layer thickness on interface chemistry, electrical properties, and their reliability was systematically explored. The results reveal that the HfAlO passivation layer restrains interfacial oxidation and reduces interface trap density. The sample with ten ALD cycles (2.2 nm HfAlO) presents an interfacial Si ${}^{{4}+}$ /Si ${}^{{2}+}$ total fraction of 21.8% and a surface rms roughness of 0.40 nm. It delivers excellent electrical performance, including a dielectric constant of 22.37, a low leakage current density of ${3}.{72}\times {10}^{-{8}}$ A/cm 2 , and an interface state density of ${2}.{98}\times {10}^{{12}}$ cm ${}^{-{2}}\cdot $ eV ${}^{-{1}}$ , along with the maximum accumulation capacitance and negligible frequency dispersion of capacitance–voltage ( $C$ – $V$ ) and conductance–voltage ( $G$ – $V$ ) curves. Moreover, this moderate-thickness passivation layer greatly improves the thermal stability and time-dependent stability of the gate-stack. This work offers experimentally supported guidance for optimizing the high- $k$ gate dielectric and its interface in CMOS devices.

items.title: In-situ measurement for drain current of SiC-MOSFET using optical-probe current sensor with half-open loop magnetic yoke
items.abstract: In recent years, the switching frequency of power converters has increased significantly with the widespread adoption of wide-bandgap power semiconductors. Conventional sensors, such as current transformers and Rogowski coils, are limited by their size and frequency bandwidth, making accurate current measurement difficult. The optical probe current sensor developed by the authors is effective for high-frequency current measurements due to its compact sensor head and wide bandwidth (DC to 150 MHz). Although this sensor can measure magnetic fields in narrow spaces, measuring wideband current in wide conductors like busbars or copper traces remains challenging due to skin and proximity effects. In this study, we improved the frequency response of the sensor by integrating it with a half-open loop magnetic yoke that homogenizes the magnetic field around the conductor. Finally, we report the in-situ measurement results of the drain current flowing through a SiC-MOSFET during a double-pulse test using the proposed sensor.

items.title: In situ identification and oxygen-assisted suppression of residual-fluorocarbon-induced instabilities in purgeless atomic layer etching of SiO 2
items.abstract: Abstract Purgeless atomic layer etching (ALE) of SiO 2 has been proposed to simplify the conventional ALE process by eliminating the purge steps, and its feasibility for achieving self-limiting etching has been experimentally demonstrated. However, subsequent investigations revealed that the process suffers from non-ideal behaviors: ‘dragging decrease’ caused by residual fluorocarbon species, and ‘over-etching’ that may cause etch-per-cycle drift. These phenomena weaken the self-limiting nature essential for ALE yet have not been mechanistically studied in the purgeless ALE regime. In this study, simultaneous in situ ellipsometry and residual gas analysis are used to directly track residual gas-phase CF x species and examine their temporal relationship with dragging decrease and continuous over-etching in purgeless ALE. Oxygen is introduced into the etching step to scavenge residual species and suppress the instabilities, and the process monitoring confirms that O 2 addition effectively reduces residual CF x radicals, leading to the simultaneous suppression of dragging decrease and over-etching. According to the results, application of the oxygen-assisted approach in purgeless ALE successfully restores the self-limiting characteristics and ensures process stability. By mechanistically identifying the instabilities and demonstrating their suppression, this work supports the practical implementation of purgeless ALE.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: Imprint Effect on Polarization Fatigue in Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 Thin-Film Capacitors
items.abstract: Ferroelectric HfO2-based thin films have aroused great interest in logic and memory applications. However, the progressive loss of the remanent polarization occurs during repetitive write/read cycles. The underlying physics of fatigue is unknown yet. Here we observed the gradual generation of positive and negative imprint fields that distort the dielectric displacement–electric field hysteresis loop during low-field cycling. During the high-field wakeup process, the imprint fields gradually disappear. The two processes of charge trapping and detrapping into the regions in opposite domain orientations are believed to be pertinent. Once the fatigue field is close to the coercive field, dielectric breakdown seldom occurs. Finally, the equations to calculate the numbers of dielectric breakdown and polarization fatigue are provided to tradeoff write voltages of the memory.

items.title: Impact of Total Ionizing Dose on 128-Layer 3-D TLC NAND Flash Memory: Endurance, Read Disturb, and Data Retention
items.abstract: This article evaluates the postirradiation degradation of the endurance, read disturb, and data retention characteristics in a 128-layer 3-D triple-level cell (TLC) nand flash memory. Both fresh and P/E-cycled memory chips were exposed to a total ionizing dose of 10 krad(Si) using a Co-60 gamma-ray source. Subsequently, a random data pattern was programmed into the irradiated chips to investigate the degradation behaviors of these three characteristics. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to unirradiated chips, the irradiated devices exhibit significant degradation in both endurance and retention characteristics. The endurance characteristics of the irradiated devices are degraded by approximately 30% upon reaching a program/erase (P/E) cycle count of 5k. Furthermore, cells in different programmed states exhibit distinct responses regarding the direction of their threshold voltage shifts during postirradiation P/E cycling tests. In addition, both the order in which P/E cycling stress and irradiation are applied and the storage state of the chip during irradiation profoundly affect the severity of the data retention degradation. The data retention characteristic under the most severe stress condition was 94% higher than that under the least severe condition after 12 h of high-temperature bake.

items.title: Impact of Programming Pattern Strategy on ReRAM Relaxation and Retention Stability
items.abstract: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) is a promising candidate for next-generation non-volatile memory. However, relaxation-induced conductance drift limits programming stability, particularly in multi-level operation and time-dependent analog computing applications. This work presents an experimental study of multi-pulse programming and its impact on memory window, short-term low-resistance state (LRS) drift, retention, and endurance. We systematically analyze three regimes: short-term relaxation (≤1s), accelerated retention using post-bake stress (≈10-year equivalence), and endurance over 10,000 cycles. Our results show that the inter-pulse interval (IPI) critically governs drift dynamics. Short IPIs exacerbate short-term relaxation, whereas longer IPIs significantly constrain conductance variations, reducing LRS drift by up to 20% compared to single-pulse programming. The optimized multi-pulse scheme improves short-term stability while preserving both post-bake memory window and cycling endurance. Furthermore, these improvements are achieved with less than 10% energy variation compared to single-pulse programming, with double-pulse operation achieving lower energy consumption. These results demonstrate that time-engineered programming strategies provide an effective path to enhance ReRAM stability without compromising long-term reliability.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Impact of Dual-Channel Communication for Wireless Interconnects of Chiplet-Based Architectures
items.abstract: The increasing demand for scalable and energy-efficient computing has driven the widespread adoption of chiplet-based architectures, where multiple smaller chiplets are integrated within a single package to overcome the limitations of monolithic system-on-chip (SoC) designs. However, a key challenge in these architectures is designing high-performance interconnects capable of efficiently handling both intrachiplet and interchiplet communication. This letter studies the impact of wireless interconnects against the wired counterpart in realizing reliable and efficient communication in chiplet-based architectures. We also compare the advantages of the dual-channel (DC) wireless interconnect over the single-channel (SC) wireless interconnect. Our study reveals that a token-passing protocol for wireless communication employs a hybrid router (HR) equipped with two wireless transceivers that provide better efficiency over an HR equipped with a single wireless transceiver. We evaluate the average packet latency across varying intrachiplet traffic (ICT) loads ranging from 20% to 80% and injection rates to determine the saturation thresholds. Our simulation results demonstrate that the DC communication consistently outperforms the SC setup, achieving significantly lower latency and supporting up to $2\times $ higher injection rates before saturation. While DC communication effectively mitigates the wireless contention, it introduces the area and power overheads due to the additional wireless transceiver. However, the performance gains outweigh these overheads, making DC wireless interconnects a more scalable and performance-efficient solution for next-generation multichiplet platforms.

items.title: Hyper NA: a system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75
items.abstract: BackgroundEUV scanners with a numerical aperture (NA) of 0.55 have recently been introduced into the market and are now on their way to high-volume production. Given the long product development cycles for EUV scanners, the question of a successor to the NA 0.55 scanners already arises.AimWe present the concept of an EUV scanner with an NA of at least 0.75, named hyper NA.ApproachHyper NA should enable reuse of as much of the present lithography infrastructure as possible, such as masks, sources, and production equipment for manufacturing those scanners.ResultsHyper NA can support an NA of 0.75 within practically the same volume claim as the current NA 0.55 scanners. The current light source can be reused as-is, and modern mask absorbers such as low-n or high-k are also sufficient for hyper NA.ConclusionsAn increase in NA, hence the introduction of hyper NA, is the preferable successor to the current NA 0.55 scanner as it offers an infrastructure-compatible path.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: Hydrogen plasma-assisted atomic layer epitaxy of superconducting titanium nitride
items.abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) offers precise, conformal control of thin-film growth and is a workhorse for semiconductor manufacturing, but its use in superconducting quantum circuits is constrained by the need to simultaneously control crystallinity, stoichiometry and interfacial disorder at cryogenic temperatures. Here we develop hydrogen plasma assisted ALD to epitaxially grow superconducting titanium nitride (TiN) thin films, using a hydrogen plasma step to modify the surface chemistry to suppress precursor-derived impurities during each deposition cycle. Synchrotron X-ray scattering reveals semi-coherent epitaxy of TiN on c-plane sapphire, with discrete crystallographic domains and minimal long-range structural disorder. Complementary X-ray spectroscopy and neutron reflectometry show negligible oxygen-related disorder throughout the film and no substantial hydrogen incorporation. The resulting TiN films exhibit a superconducting transition at 2.2 K, a kinetic inductance of 15 pH/sq and a superconducting coherence length of 14.6 nm, comparable to the measured crystal coherence length. These results establish hydrogen plasma assisted ALD as a route to structurally ordered superconducting TiN thin film epitaxy and demonstrate that the nanoscale control of ALD can be extended to materials suitable for cryogenic quantum technologies.

items.title: Humidity-Modulated Flexible Chitosan-Based Memristor With Synaptic Behavior
items.abstract: A flexible Cu/Ti/chitosan:sodium chloride (CS:NaCl)/indium tin oxide (ITO)/polyimide (PI) memristor was evaluated at controlled relative humidity (RH) levels of 30% and 60% to investigate what RH-dependent changes occur in nonvolatile switching and short-term synaptic responses. Across five independently fabricated devices, the mean SET voltage (V ${}_{\text {SET}}\text {)}$ increased from $2.128~\pm ~0.046$ to $3.152~\pm ~0.046$ V, whereas the RESET voltage (V ${}_{\text {RESET}}\text {)}$ showed greater cycle-to-cycle and device-to-device variability. Higher RH enhanced the excitatory postsynaptic current, paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), and low-voltage conductance modulation. A 30% $\to 60$ % $\to 30$ % RH sequence showed a recovery trend in the SET voltage, and bipolar switching remained observable in all five devices after 200 bending cycles at R = 6 mm. Based on the measured conductance modulation, MNIST recognition exceeded 92% at both RH levels. Fusing I–V and PPF classifier outputs enabled proof-of-concept RH-state classification. These results reveal differentiated RH modulation of nonvolatile SET and short-term synaptic responses in a flexible chitosan-based memristor.

items.title: High-entropy enabled two-dimensional ferroelectricity and memristive synapses in van der Waals layered materials
items.abstract: Two-dimensional ferroelectric materials offer opportunities for ultrathin non-volatile electronics, but their development is limited by stringent structural requirements for intrinsic polarity. Here we show that high-entropy engineering can induce switchable polarization in centrosymmetric van der Waals materials. By introducing configurational disorder into layered metal phosphorus trisulfides, we synthesize (MnFeCoNi)1−xCdxPS3 single crystals exhibiting electric-field-induced polar states and ferroelectric-like switching at ±0.5 V, with a transition temperature up to 523 K. Combined calculations and characterizations reveal that polarization originates from electric-field-driven Cd2+ migration enabled by lattice distortions and heterogeneous coordination environments. This migration-mediated mechanism differs from conventional ferroelectric models and enables non-volatile neuromorphic functions, including long-term potentiation and bidirectional weight modulation. This work establishes high-entropy engineering as a strategy for manipulating ion migration dynamics in two-dimensional layered materials, opening a pathway toward emergent ferroelectric-like states beyond the conventional requirement of non-centrosymmetric structures. Two-dimensional ferroelectrics are often constrained by stringent structural requirements for intrinsic polarity. Sun et al. demonstrate that high-entropy engineering enables switchable polarization in centrosymmetric van der Waals materials, offering a potential pathway toward emergent ferroelectric-like states.

items.title: High-Throughput LDPC Decoder for nand Flash: Turbo Two-Bit Gradient Descent Bit-Flipping Algorithm and VLSI Architecture
items.abstract: In this article, we propose a turbo two-bit gradient descent bit-flipping (TTGDBF) algorithm for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes in nand storage systems. The TTGDBF algorithm introduces an additional bit at each variable node (VN) to represent its “strength,” which is further combined with the turbo flipping mechanism to improve the error-correction capability. To fulfill the high-throughput requirement, the proposed algorithm breaks the separation between the maximum-finding phase and the flipping phase in conventional gradient descent-based algorithms, allowing the codeword bit to be flipped at any time during the decoding process, thereby accelerating the convergence speed and decoding performance. Furthermore, a VLSI architecture is proposed for efficient hardware implementation of the TTGDBF algorithm, which achieves a 55.5% reduction in logic area and a 75.6% increase in throughput compared to the unified penalty GDBF (UPGDBF) decoder. Implemented in the TSMC 65 nm process, the proposed 4KB LDPC decoder can achieve a throughput of 15.87 Gbps with an area of 0.992 mm2, demonstrating high efficiency for high-speed nand storage applications.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: High-Frequency Performance AlN/GaN HEMTs with sub-100 nm Gate Lengths
items.abstract: Ultra-thin AlN barrier AlN/GaN high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with scaled gate dimensions were realized using a hybrid metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) and plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy (PA-MBE) growth approach. The heterostructure consisted of an MOCVD-grown AlN nucleation layer and GaN buffer, followed by a PA-MBE-grown GaN channel, a 4.1 nm AlN barrier, and a 2 nm GaN cap. Mushroom gate devices with gate lengths down to 30 nm were fabricated using electron beam lithography. DC and RF characterization demonstrated promising device performance, with extrinsic cutoff frequency (fT) up to 160 GHz at VDS = 3 V and 154 GHz at VDS = 11 V, while the extrinsic maximum oscillation frequency (fmax) increased from 182 to 296 GHz at the same biases. These results show the potential of ultra-thin PA-MBE-grown AlN barriers for scalable high-frequency GaN-HEMTs.

items.title: High-Density Staggered Cylindrical TSV Layout With Shielding for Crosstalk Mitigation and Area Efficiency
items.abstract: In the post-Moore’s Law era, the semiconductor industry is increasingly focusing on modular 2.5D and 3D integration due to its significant advantages. These 2.5D and 3D chips leverage Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs) to enable vertical stacking and ensure high-throughput communication between chiplets. In this paper, we propose a staggered layout of cylindrical TSVs with appropriate shielding to achieve higher density while maintaining acceptable crosstalk levels. The primary objective of this work is to exploit the unused spaces in the conventional cylindrical-grid TSV pattern by employing a staggered orientation, thereby accommodating the continued increase in transistor density. Furthermore, cylindrical geometry is retained to avoid the fabrication complexity associated with new geometries. A shielding strategy is introduced to mitigate crosstalk with minimal area overhead, and the transmission performance is evaluated in comparison with the industry-standard TSV arrangement. The proposed layout achieves a 17.37% higher density than the standard cylindrical-grid pattern and a 10.88% improvement over the high-density triangular-hexagram structure. Moreover, both the cylindrical-grid and cylindrical-staggered layouts exhibit near-identical transmission characteristics. The proposed shielding approach significantly reduces crosstalk, achieving a worst-case crosstalk level of 8C with area overheads ranging from 9.09% to 22.93% depending on the chip shape, while never exceeding 25% in worst cases. Additionally, a 7% delay reduction is observed in the victim TSV from circuit-level analysis. Overall, the proposed TSV layout demonstrates strong potential to meet the growing demand and align with the industry roadmap for higher-density interconnect development.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: High-Density 3-D-DRAM Architecture With Folded Capacitor for Sub-10-nm Scaling
items.abstract: In this letter, a novel 3D-DRAM process architecture based on a folded capacitor is proposed to enhance the bit-cell density of 3D-DRAM, one of the most promising candidates for sub-10 nm DRAM technology nodes. This work comprehensively introduces a manufacturable solution that includes bit-cell layout design, structural configuration, and a process integration scheme, ensuring design-to-fab applicability. To conduct a rigorous evaluation, structural characteristics of the proposed memory cell are precisely calibrated through Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations and BSIM-CMG modeling, using silicon-verified hardware data. As a result, the proposed cell exceeds a ${3}.{3}\times $ increase in storage capacitance ( ${C}_{\text {S}}$ ) within the same footprint compared to state-of-the-art 3D-DRAM with horizontal capacitor. Moreover, it secures over a 28% improvement in bit-cell density within the operational margin that guarantees reliable memory performance, highlighting its potential as a next-generation DRAM architecture.

items.title: High frequency performance of GaN HEMT with thin InAlGaN barrier
items.abstract: In this study, the optimization of the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure and the fabrication of RF high-electron-mobility-transistors (HEMTs) on a SiC substrate are reported. Owing to the outstanding 2DEG properties of the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure, the InAlGaN/GaN HEMT achieved a high on-current of 1280 mA/mm and a transconductance of 482.8 mS/mm with a low off-state leakage current of 5 × 10−4 A/mm. Furthermore, the InAlGaN/GaN HEMT exhibited a high fT/fmax of 93/154 GHz and a breakdown voltage of 56 V, resulting in a Johnson’s figure of merit value of 5.2 THz V. These distinguished characteristics of the device demonstrate that the InAlGaN/GaN heterostructure is a promising candidate for high power and high frequency applications.

items.title: HFLSM: A Hybrid Flattened LSM-Tree for Write-Efficient Key-Value Stores
items.abstract: Log-structured merge (LSM)-trees are widely used in write-intensive key-value stores, but compaction can cause write stalls and write amplification, especially when overlapping SSTables at level 0 ( $L_{0}$ ) trigger costly $L_{0}$ – $L_{1}$ compactions. This letter presents Hybrid Flattened LSM-Tree (HFLSM), a hybrid flattened LSM-tree for non-volatile memory solid-state drive (NVM-SSD) storage systems. HFLSM places frequently compacted upper levels on NVM, expands level capacities to reduce compaction frequency, and restructures $L_{0}$ based on SSTable overlap to limit $L_{0}$ – $L_{1}$ compaction. Preliminary results show that HFLSM improves random-write throughput by up to $2.71\times $ over LevelDB-NVM and reduces the write amplification factor (WAF) from 11.12 to 9.1, demonstrating improved write efficiency for NVM-based LSM-tree key-value stores.

items.title: Gate-Current-Dominated Positive Threshold Voltage Shift Under PBTI Stress in Schottky p-GaN Gate HEMTs
items.abstract: While positive bias temperature instability (PBTI)-induced threshold voltage (V ${}_{\text {th}}\text {)}$ instability is a major bottleneck in gallium nitride (GaN) power electronics, the role of gate current remains poorly understood and is often confounded by temperature effects. In this work, the role of gate current in threshold voltage instability is investigated using short-term PBTI stress to isolate the positive shift component before the counteracting component becomes pronounced. The positive shift decreases with increasing gate current, even at the same temperature. Moreover, nearly identical positive shifts are observed at different temperatures when the gate current is comparable. These results suggest that the positive shift is not determined by temperature alone but is associated with gate current. C–V and recovery analyses suggest that this current-dependent positive shift is associated with electron trapping. Arrhenius analysis of the secondary recovery transient of the positive shift yields an activation energy of 174 meV, suggesting trap states associated with the p-GaN/AlGaN interface.

items.title: Fully Phase-Change Artificial Neural Networks Based on Phase-Change Memory With Reconfigurable Activation Functions
items.abstract: We demonstrate an all-phase-change artificial neural network in which phase-change memory (PCM) devices simultaneously realize synaptic plasticity and reconfigurable activation-function artificial neurons. Precise control of the voltage-amplitude step size during the SET and RESET processes enables gradual conductance modulation, thereby realizing synaptic long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). More importantly, threshold switching behavior induced by larger pulse widths and larger voltage steps allows the realization of reconfigurable activation functions, including ReLU, sigmoid, and softplus. System-level simulations on the MNIST dataset demonstrate recognition accuracy exceeding 98%, comparable to those achieved using ideal software-defined activation functions, thereby validating the robustness and reliability of the all-PCM neural network. These results highlight the strong potential of PCM devices for highly integrated and multifunctional neuromorphic computing systems.

items.title: Frequency-Dependent Magnetic Flux Density Attenuation in Aluminum-Steel Hard Disk Drive Enclosures: Mesh Refinement Guidelines for Degaussing Analysis
items.abstract: The rapid transition from hard disk drives (HDDs) to solid-state drives (SSDs) results in massive HDD decommissioning, raising data security and environmental challenges. Before recycling, data sanitization through magnetic degaussing is required; however, HDDs’ composite aluminum-steel casing significantly attenuates the applied magnetic field. This article presents a 3-D finite element method (FEM) study investigating frequency-dependent magnetic flux density attenuation through aluminum-steel HDD cases and establishing mesh granularity guidelines, while quantifying the frequency ranges in which local attenuation predictions achieve convergence. The study employed an open-source FEM toolchain (NETGEN, ELMER FEM, and GNU Octave) and first-order (linear) Whitney/Nedelec H(curl)-conforming edge elements to analyze frequency-dependent attenuation for different mesh resolutions and field orientations. Results reveal that coarse meshing leads to underestimated shielding effects, especially above 1 kHz, potentially causing false predictions in degaussing efficiency. This article formalizes frequency-aware meshing guidelines linking the maximum element size to the electromagnetic skin depth, verifies global energy convergence using energy-norm indicators, and identifies the frequency ranges in which local attenuation predictions remain mesh-sensitive. The framework supports the design of secure HDD sanitization systems, which can be reproduced with free software.

items.title: Ferroelectric α- Bi 2 O 3 films derived from β- Bi via ultraviolet ozone oxidation
items.abstract: Abstract Bismuth-based oxides are well known for their high Curie temperature and excellent fatigue resistance, which have attracted extensive researches and various applications. In this work, we successfully fabricated pure phase α -Bi 2 O 3 films by a novel ultraviolet ozone oxidation method from β -Bi. The obtained α -Bi 2 O 3 exhibits room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity, as confirmed by both piezoelectric force microscopy measurements and hysteresis loops obtained from out-of-plane ferroelectric tunnel junctions. Density functional calculations predict that the ferroelectricity of α -Bi 2 O 3 arises from a synergistic interplay between electric-field-induced structural deformation and charge redistribution within films. Our results demonstrate that such a thin room-temperature ferroelectric α -Bi 2 O 3 film could be a promising candidate for future multifunctional electronic devices.

items.title: Ferroelectric domain walls: new 2D functional materials for conventional and neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Neuromorphic computing seeks to perform data-centric computational tasks in an energy-efficient manner by mimicking the way living systems process information. Artificial synaptic devices are key building blocks for this emerging technology. Many efforts have been made to realise biological synaptic behaviour using different device technologies. Among these, ferroelectric tunnel junction-based devices have been prominent, partly due to their purely electrical switching mechanism, without oxygen vacancy/metal ion migration or Joule heating. This has made them attractive in terms of device reliability and power consumption. An alternative approach to generate synaptic behaviour using ferroelectrics (that does not rely on tunnel currents) is by using a system that exhibits enhanced electrical conductance along domain walls compared to the bulk domains. Recently, it has been shown that a thin film LiNbO3 (LNO) memristor device, with conductance levels spanning almost 12 orders of magnitude, could be realised by altering the domain wall microstructure with different applied electric fields. Different from ferroelectric tunnel junctions, the memristive response in these simple ferroelectric capacitor structures was controlled by altering the total number of conducting domain walls that straddle the interelectrode gap and by altering their inclination angle with respect to the polarisation axis. Early signs of conduction plasticity have been seen in these devices, in which there is a gradual increase in conductivity, induced by applying multiple voltage pulses of equal magnitude. These findings led us to investigate neuromorphic aspects of domain wall transport in this ferroelectric system. Building on the knowledge established in the earlier reports, this thesis explores the neuromorphic properties of domain wall conductivity in 500 nm thick LNO capacitors and investigates how neuromorphic functions and operating voltages change as ferroelectric film thickness decreases. Two-probe current-voltage measurements supported by atomic force microscopy (AFM) characterisation have shown that the domain wall conductivity in LNO thin films is a complex history-dependent function of electric field and time. Field-time kinetics of microstructural change in this system can replicate important features of synaptic response such as potentiation & depression, spike-rate-dependent plasticity and spike-time-dependent plasticity. Measurements on samples prepared by tomographic AFM (TAFM) and dimple grinding have demonstrated that operating voltages scale almost linearly with film thickness in the 50-500 nm regime. Similar neuromorphic behaviours have been observed in ≈100 nm thick capacitors at about five times lower voltages. Local variations in wall inclination angle resulted in diode-like behaviour in the dc conductance response, enabling half-wave rectification at low frequencies. Boolean "AND" and "OR" logic gates have been experimentally demonstrated using domain wall diodes and resistors. Results show that ferroelectric domain walls in lithium niobate thin films might be useful not only for neuromorphic but also for conventional computing systems.

items.title: FedSRAM-PUF: Federated Bit-Error Correction for Reliable SRAM PUF Authentication
items.abstract: The static random access memory (SRAM)-based physical unclonable functions (PUFs) provide a lightweight hardware primitive for device authentication in embedded systems. However, their practical deployment is limited by noise-induced bit instability, which degrades response reproducibility across repeated power-up measurements. The existing reliability-enhancement methods typically rely on centralized processing, error-correcting codes, or helper data, which may introduce additional overhead or expose sensitive device-specific information. This letter presents a federated learning (FL)-based framework for improving SRAM PUF reliability through distributed bit-error correction. A lightweight multilayer perceptron model is trained collaboratively across devices to learn bit-level instability patterns while keeping raw SRAM responses local to each device. In addition to clean-response evaluation, we examine robustness under emulated noise-induced drift to assess the effect of persistent bit perturbations on correction performance. The experimental results on SRAM measurements from eight ESP32 devices show that the proposed approach reduces average BER by 46.49% in the clean setting and by 36.19% under emulated noise-induced drift, while improving response stability for downstream authentication.

items.title: FALCON: A Triple-Port FeFET LUT Architecture for CNN Acceleration
items.abstract: Editor’s notes: Edge deployment of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is constrained by the computational and energy costs of multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations. This article presents FALCON, a sparsity-aware LUT-based accelerator that combines a triple-port split-gate FeFET cell architecture with algorithm-driven storage reduction to enable efficient CNN inference at the edge. —Partha Pratim Pande, Washington State University, USA

items.title: Exploration and Analysis of Biomolecule Incorporated GaN Based Cylindrical Gate All Around FET for High Performance Biosensing Applications
items.abstract: Abstract GaN cylindrical gate-all-around (GAA) field effect transistors are explored for high performance biosensing applications incorporating biomolecules. The device structure employs a conformal high-k dielectric wrapping the 2nm gate underlap to achieve enhanced electrostatic control and nanocavity for biomolecule implants in gate stack oxide for surface interaction with analytes. Electrical performance under varying biomolecular environments are analyzed using biotin, glucose and blood biomolecules having distinct dielectric properties. The dielectric constant variations, directly affect the gate capacitance and channel potential leading to measurable shifts in the biosensor behavior. The biosensor device C 3 demonstrates an on current of 40.13µA/µm and an off current of 0.13pA/µm resulting in an elevated switching ratio of 3.09×108. Subthreshold swing approaches 61.87mV/decade indicating superior gate controllability and reduced short channel effects. Biomolecular sensing is quantified through modulation in threshold voltage and drain current where the maximum current sensitivity reaches ~ 20.5% and voltage sensitivity attains 122mV with blood producing the highest signal response due to its high permittivity. These results confirm the effectiveness of dielectric modulation as a detection mechanism for biosensing. In blood detection, the device demonstrates enhanced threshold-voltage, on-current, and drain-current sensitivity, highlighting its potential for ultra-low-concentration biomolecule sensing. The GaN cylindrical GAA FET offers high signal integrity, low-power operation, and label-free analyte detection. The compact structure and high sensitivity of the GaN GAA makes it a promising candidate for next generation implantable biosensing device for possible real time bioelectronic applications.

items.title: Equivalent-Voltage Translation for Slow-Trap Quantification in GaN MOS Capacitors
items.abstract: Quantitative analysis of slow traps in gallium nitride (GaN) devices remains challenging because many capacitance-based extraction methods rely on an absolute conversion from $C$ – $V$ data to surface potential. In GaN devices, this conversion can be unreliable in the presence of dispersion, nonquasi-static response, leakage, and series/access resistance. In this work, we develop a series-resistance ( ${R} _{\text {s}}\text {)}$ -corrected equivalent-voltage translation (EVT) method for Al 2 O 3 /GaN MOS capacitors (MOSCAPs). Instead of reconstructing the absolute surface potential, EVT maps the capacitance transient, after series-resistance correction, onto a premeasured capacitance-voltage reference curve and extracts an equivalent gate-voltage shift. This measurement-based translation yields the time-dependent slow-trap sheet-density change $\Delta $ N st (t) and an effective time constant from the same transient. For the piranha + SC-1 split, EVT gives $\Delta $ N st (1 s) $= 1.07\times 10^{{11}}$ ${\mathrm {cm}}^{-{2}}$ after 60 s filling at 4.8 V. This value is close to the hysteresis-based consistency check of $1.12\times 10^{{11}}$ ${\mathrm {cm}}^{-{2}}$ and higher than the value obtained from a surface-potential (SP)-based benchmark on the same corrected dataset. Under an identical transient protocol, EVT also captures the effect of substrate pre-clean, with $\Delta $ N st (1 s) increasing to $2.07\times 10^{{11}}$ ${\mathrm {cm}}^{-{2}}$ for the HCl split. These results support EVT as a matched-frequency, measurement-based framework for quantitative slow-trap benchmarking and standardized process screening in Al 2 O 3 /GaN gate stacks.

items.title: Enhancing PDK Accuracy Through Advanced Modeling of 0.15-μm GaN Transistors
items.abstract: This work presents an enhanced nonlinear modeling approach for 0.15-μm AlGaN/GaN HEMTs aimed at improving Process Design Kit (PDK) accuracy under multi-bias operating conditions. Starting from a conventional nonlinear model extracted using standard DC, pulsed I–V, and RF measurements, an advanced nonlinear model is developed by incorporating dispersion-aware formulations to account for thermal and trapping effects. The advanced model identification is based on time-domain load-pull measurements at low frequency (2 MHz) across multiple bias conditions, enabling accurate tracking of dynamic knee behaviour. The models are validated against large-signal measurements up to microwave frequencies (1–6 GHz). While both the models show comparable accuracy at nominal bias, the advanced model demonstrates significantly improved predictive capability under varying drain voltage and current conditions, ensuring consistent estimation of output power, efficiency, and load-pull characteristics. The proposed approach enables robust multi-bias design for GaN-based RF amplifiers.

items.title: Enhanced 2Pr in 5-nm HZO Capacitors Under 300 °C RTP via Nb Electrode Engineering
items.abstract: In this letter, Nb electrode engineering is proposed to enable low-temperature crystallization of ultrathin HZO, thereby extending its BEOL compatibility. Large $2{P}_{\text {r}}$ values of 53.6/ $56.4~\mu $ C/cm 2 at 3/3.5 MV/cm are achieved by the positive-up-negative-down (PUND) method in 5-nm HZO with Nb electrodes (NHN) after $300~^{\circ }$ C annealing, together with wake-up-free, negligible fatigue to 1E10 cycles (3 MV/cm, 100 kHz), and an extrapolated retention of 10 years at $85~^{\circ }$ C. Specifically, the bottom Nb tends to form an Nb 2 O 5 cap layer during the ALD process owing to its more negative oxide formation enthalpy, which suppresses oxygen scavenging and serves as an oxygen reservoir, thereby mitigating the redistribution and generation of interfacial oxygen vacancies ( ${V}_{\text {O}}\text {)}$ . Meanwhile, the top Nb provides uniform nucleation sites due to the smaller Nb/HZO interfacial mismatch (~6%), promoting O-phase formation at ultra-low temperature. The synergy of above effects enables excellent ferroelectricity at a thermal budget as low as $300~^{\circ }$ C, which is of great interest for BEOL-compatible FeRAM applications.

items.title: Energy-Efficient Stochastic Spiking Neural Network Hardware With 8T SRAM Array Utilizing Sub-Threshold Cascaded Current Mirrors and Stochastic CMOS Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neurons
items.abstract: Brain-inspired computing mechanisms are characterized by two primary features: 1) Sparse event-driven processing with spatio-temporal dynamics which result in low power consumption, and 2) Stochastic phenomena occurring between pre- and post-synaptic neurons, enhancing the stability and robustness of data processing. This paper introduces an 8T SRAM-based Compute-In-Memory (CIM) architecture that capitalizes on these two key principles of brain-inspired computing. 1) By exploiting the inherent sparsity of spiking activity in SNNs, the architecture significantly improves energy efficiency in typical SNN applications by employing a cascaded current mirror that operates in sub-threshold region and dynamic latch-based Stochastic Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron. 2) The noise characteristics inherent to CMOS comparators are effectively leveraged to implement stochastic activations within the SNN computations. Furthermore, the benefits of stochastic computing in enhancing the fault tolerance of neural networks, along with the associated trade-offs, are discussed. Fabricated using a 180nm CMOS process, the proposed SNN hardware exhibits high energy efficiency, achieving 0.1 pJ per synaptic operation (SOP). The SNN chip has been fully validated through on-chip classification tasks using the complete 10,000-sample MNIST test dataset. With 16 × 16 downsampled input images, the chip achieves an on-chip classification accuracy of 86.26%.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Artificial Intelligence

items.title: Energy-Efficient Checkpointing for IMC-Based AI Accelerators Using 3.5 D Packaging
items.abstract: In-memory computing (IMC) techniques provides an energy-efficient way to train artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models. Furthermore, 2.5-D integration made it possible to store the weights of a large AI model on the compute system itself. However, resistive random access memory (ReRAM)-based IMC devices may fail abruptly due to frequent memory writes during training, coupled with their low endurance. Since the training of an AI model is an iterative process, abrupt failure of memory devices results in wasted of compute energy and time. In this work, we propose a probability-based energy-efficient checkpointing mechanism utilizing the device characteristics of ReRAM. We further leverage a 3.5 D packaging strategy to improve its efficiency. Extensive experimental results show that the proposed checkpointing frequency and the workflow effectively save 61% of the recovery energy on average and increase the possible number of epochs by up to 32.53%. We also observe an average improvement of 76.60% in checkpointing latency, 77.03% in checkpointing energy, and 4.51% in end-to-end training latency with just 0.4% overhead in packaging cost and a minimal increase of $4~^{\circ } $ C in temperature due to 3-D stacking.

items.title: Electron Beam Lithography for Back-End-of-Line Integration of Emerging Technology on Foundry Coupons With Dummy Fill
items.abstract: The insertion of dummy metal features in the dielectrics of foundry processes at the 130 nm node and smaller introduces errors in electron-beam lithography (EBL) alignments on foundry coupons. This is because the accuracy of the electron beam edge detection is degraded by electron backscatter from dummy fill (DF) metals. Here, we show a process that corrects for edge detection errors and enables alignment marks (AMs), which then suppress backscatter from the dummy metal features. This process is then used to integrate submicrometer ferroelectric memory in the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of 40-nm-node foundry coupons, with successful alignment to foundry vias as small as $40\times 40$ nm 2 . Repeatability and reproducibility are characterized by polarization–voltage, capacitance-voltage, and current–voltage measurements on submicrometer W/hafnium zirconium oxide (HZO)/W ferroelectric capacitor (FeCap) arrays. Scanning electron microscopy shows clear connection of submicrometer FeCaps to foundry metal M4 vias. Pulsed measurements of polarization switching (SW) are in good agreement with SPICE simulations and prove the functionality of the 1T1C transistor–capacitor memory. Polarization SW in 1T1C memory is measured on FeCaps as small as ${\mathrm {(0.8)}}^{{2}} ~\mu $ m 2 .

items.title: Electrical Degradation and Trapped Charge Evolution in SiC MOSFETs Under Power-Cycling Stress
items.abstract: The reliability of SiC mosfets under repetitive power cycling is a critical concern for power converter design. This article investigates the degradation behavior in SiC mosfets under power-cycling stress, and the trap analysis is carried out based on transient current method. Five samples are stressed under forward conduction with load current from 52.5 to 73.2 A. An inverse relationship is observed between the applied current and the number of cycles, determined by a 5% increase in the on-state voltage under hot conditions. Poststress electrical characterizations reveal the positive threshold voltage shift and increased drain leakage current, with the degradation being more pronounced with an increasing number of cycles. Based on the actual transient current variations of samples, the trapping behaviors governed by exponential decay are extracted using Bayesian deconvolution. Three trap levels are identified with increased amplitudes under larger cycle count, and the activation energies are almost unchanged after power-cycling by the temperature-dependent measurements. It can be attributed to the increase in traps near the SiC/SiO2 interface and within the gate oxide especially under higher cycle count. By directly linking macroscopic degradation to the evolution of microscopic traps, it provides profound insights for the reliability assessment of SiC mosfets in power electronic systems.

items.title: Efficient and Low Power VLSI Implementation of Lifting based 3-D DWT
items.abstract: The research presented here introduces a lifting-based 3-D Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) architecture optimized for video input frames with hardware efficiency and high operational speed. The proposed design employs four concurrent spatial and temporal DWT modules to deliver sixteen results per clock cycle. Two parallel spatial processors minimize frame memory for temporal conversion, and a novel dual Z-scan addressing scheme eliminates internal transposition buffers and wait cycles. Implemented on Xilinx Artix 7 (xc7a100t) FPGA using VHDL and synthesized at 150 MHz, the design achieves 150 Mpixels/s throughput, 280-cycle end-to-end latency, and 0.98 W dynamic power—improvements of 66.7%, 33.3%, and 46% respectively over the convolution-based baseline. Experimental hardware measurements confirm deviations under 4.1% from reported values. Timing closure is achieved with a worst negative slack of +1.367 ns.
items.venue: International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications

items.title: Dynamic Landau–Khalatnikov Modeling of Ferroelectric Hafnium–Zirconium Oxides Across Volatile and Non‐Volatile Switching
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The design of energy‐efficient neuromorphic devices demands compact, physically grounded models that seamlessly connect microscopic ferroelectric dynamics to macroscopic circuit behavior. Hafnium–zirconium oxides (, HZO) are compelling candidates owing to their CMOS compatibility, scalability below 10 nm, and tunable transition between ferroelectric and volatile responses. Yet, conventional first‐order Landau–Khalatnikov (LK) formulations cannot capture key experimental features such as negative differential capacitance, pseudo‐inductive transients, and leakage interplay. Here we introduce an extended LK framework incorporating inertial second‐order terms, nonlinear charge‐dependent damping, and a modular leakage branch. This unified, simulation‐ready model quantitatively reproduces experimental Q–V characteristics across Hf‐rich, equiatomic, and Zr‐rich HZO compositions, defining operational regimes from non‐volatile memory to volatile, reservoir‐like dynamics. By linking free‐energy landscapes to compact circuit representations, the approach establishes a predictive device–model–circuit co‐design framework that connects atomistic energetics with system‐level simulation, enabling composition‐specific design rules for scalable, low‐power neuromorphic architectures.

items.title: Duty-cycle-aware empirical modeling of BTI-induced delay degradation in FPGA LUTs
items.abstract: As Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) adopt advanced CMOS nodes, Bias Temperature Instability (BTI) becomes an important threat to timing reliability. This paper investigates aging-induced delay degradation in SRAM-based FPGA Look-Up Tables (LUTs), with emphasis on stress duration and signal duty cycle. A representative transmission-gate LUT topology is analyzed through SPICE simulations to identify NBTI- and PBTI-sensitive timing paths, and a 65 nm Cyclone III FPGA is characterized for 3000 h under an accelerated core-voltage condition. An aggregate empirical model, expressed using path-level coefficients A – H , static-path terms X and Y , and a common time exponent n , is calibrated to the measured rise- and fall-delay shifts. The same 3000-hour dataset is used for both parameter estimation and fit assessment; consequently, the reported error metrics quantify in-sample goodness of fit rather than independent predictive validation. The measurements show a pronounced duty-cycle-dependent asymmetry between rise and fall degradation, consistent with PMOS-dominated NBTI stress and recovery. The resulting framework connects transistor-level path interpretation to a compact circuit-level description under the tested accelerated condition; extrapolation to other voltage and temperature conditions requires additional characterization.

items.title: Different Single-Event Burnout Behavior in p-GaN HEMTs Under Zero and Negative Gate Bias
items.abstract: High-energy heavy-ion-induced single-event burnout (SEB) in p-GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) under zero and negative gate bias was investigated. Under negative gate bias, simultaneous transient surges occur in both drain and gate currents during irradiation, whereas only a drain current surge manifests under zero gate bias conditions. This distinct behavior indicates bias-dependent SEB mechanisms. Through technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations, we reveal that the redistribution of heavy-ion-induced charge critically governs poststrike electric field evolution. Electron cluster accumulation combined with the back-channel effect caused the high electric field near the drain, resulting in the SEB under zero gate bias. Furthermore, analysis of the p-GaN gate energy band structure demonstrates that partial turn-on of the metal/p-GaN Schottky diode caused the high electric field within the p-GaN layer. Negative gate bias intensifies this electric field, thereby promoting breakdown beneath the gate electrode. Simulation results align with the experimental observations. This study provides new physical insights into SEB mechanisms in p-gallium nitride HEMTs (GaN HEMTs).

items.title: Dielectric Nanolensing: How a Wavelength-Scale Lens Carries Hidden Detail into an Ordinary Microscope and What Chemistry Should Build Next
items.abstract: Dielectric nanolensing has evolved from a wavelength-scale molecular lens into a broad family of microsphere, particle-lens, scanning, arrayed, and computational platforms. Breakthrough advances now include white-light nanoscopy, immersed high-index imaging, large-field scanning, nondestructive semiconductor metrology, living-cell optics, nanolithography, and substrate-free Raman analysis. This Perspective explains, in accessible terms, how a lens placed in the specimen's near field can redirect otherwise inaccessible spatial information into light collected by an ordinary objective. It then reconciles curvature, solid immersion, nanojets, Mie and whispering-gallery modes, and Fano interference as condition-dependent contributions rather than competing universal explanations. The central opportunity is forward-looking: chemistry can control complex refractive index, shape, assembly, environment, and the nanometre-scale lens-specimen gap, while quantitative transfer measurements can replace incomparable resolution claims. Together, these developments point toward scalable, calibrated nanolenses for imaging, metrology, and chemical analysis.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

items.title: DfT-Assisted Testing of Resistive Short Defects in SRAM-Based In-Memory Computing Architectures
items.abstract: In-Memory Computing (IMC) architectures accelerate neural networks by performing computation within memory arrays, alleviating the von Neumann bottleneck and reducing energy consumption. SRAM-based IMC leverages mature, high-speed technology but introduces testing challenges in detecting and localizing manufacturing defects. While conventional SRAM memory sub-cells are well studied, the computational sub-cells enabling IMC remain less explored. In this paper, we investigate resistive short defects in the computational sub-cell of SRAM-based IMC topologies performing analog-domain MAC operations. Such defects may lead to computational errors, bit-flips in the memory sub-cells, and increased static power consumption, resulting in hot spots. We propose a Design-for-Testability (DfT) and diagnosis scheme that supports a Differential Analysis–based testing approach with a complexity of 2N write operations and 4×N×M compute-read operations, where N and M denote the number of rows and columns in the memory array. Experimental results show that, under process variations, the proposed DfT enables 100% defect detection and 87.5% localization coverage for critical resistive short defects, with minimal delay, area, and power overhead.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Device‐to‐System Perspectives on Scalable Ising Machines for Physics‐Driven Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) are fundamental to numerous applications but remain challenging due to their exponentially large solution spaces and the limitations of conventional computing architectures. Ising machines have emerged as a promising alternative by mapping optimization problems onto the energy minimization of the Ising Hamiltonian. Various hardware implementations, including quantum annealers, digital annealers, and coherent Ising machines, have been explored based on distinct physical mechanisms. More recently, emerging device‐based approaches have gained significant attention for their potential to enable scalable and energy‐efficient optimization. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of Ising machines from both theoretical and hardware perspectives, with particular emphasis on three emerging‐device‐based platforms: crossbar array‐based, stochastic p‐bit, and oscillator‐based Ising machines. We establish a comparative device‐to‐system perspective that traces how distinct physical and device properties translate into computational primitives, hardware architectures, and ultimately system‐level scalability. Platform‐specific bottlenecks, including array nonidealities and peripheral overhead in crossbar‐based systems, device variability and probability‐generation overhead in p‐bit systems, and synchronization and coupling‐network complexity in oscillator‐based systems, are quantitatively and qualitatively analyzed. Finally, we discuss future directions toward scalable and energy‐efficient Ising hardware through device‐to‐system co‐optimization across devices, circuits, architectures, and algorithms.

items.title: Design and performance optimization of an asymmetric dual-gate MoSi 2 N 4 /α-In 2 Se 3 ferroelectric heterostructure FET
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional semiconductors and ferroelectrics offer complementary routes to scaled electrostatic control and embedded nonvolatility. This work evaluates an asymmetric dual-gate ferroelectric heterostructure field-effect transistor that combines a monolayer MoSi 2 N 4 channel, an α -In 2 Se 3 ferroelectric top-gate layer and an h-BN bottom gate. The framework couples a Landau–Ginzburg–Devonshire description anchored to reported α -In 2 Se 3 polarization, coercive-field and permittivity data, including depolarization, coercive-field thickness scaling and Curie–Weiss temperature dependence, to a two-dimensional finite-volume electrostatic solution of the gate stack and a charge-based transport kernel with velocity saturation. The spatial solution shows that a 6 nm ferroelectric over a 12 nm gate permits strong drain-field fringing through the high-permittivity layer, and that a 1 nm h-BN bottom gate removes most of the top-gate control. A design criterion fixed in advance (SS ⩽ 75 mV dec − 1 , DIBL ⩽ 50 mV V − 1 , retained bottom-gate threshold tuning) selects a 2.5 nm ferroelectric and a 10 nm h-BN bottom dielectric at L G = 12 nm, giving SS = 71.4 mV dec − 1 , DIBL = 45.7 mV V − 1

items.title: Design and Verification of Miniaturized High-Power Pulsed Laser Trigger System for Optically Controlled Multigate Thyristors
items.abstract: Optically controlled multigate thyristors (OCMGTs) face challenges in high-voltage series applications, specifically requiring high-power triggering and synchronous turn-on of multiple gates. To address these issues, this article proposes a compact, high-power nanosecond pulse laser trigger system based on the field-induced nonlinear trigger mode (Mode C), targeting a benchmark of 4.5-kW peak optical power. The drive circuit utilizes a SiC MOSFET capacitor-direct-drive topology with a compact, low-inductance package, achieving a peak current of 146.6 A and an 80 ns rise time. Furthermore, the optical system employs a passive arrayed fiber combining and homogenization method alongside a transmissive-reflective beam-splitting mechanism, keeping the energy deviation among the three sampled optical paths within ±5%, which serves as a representative indication of the seven-spot uniformity. Experiments on a 42-kV high-voltage series assembly validate the design, achieving synchronous turn-on with a peak current of 20.15 kA, a di/dt of 19.89 kA/ $\mu $ s, and a measured interstage absolute delay of 413–436-ns relative to the master trigger (channel-to-channel skew $\approx$ 23 ns). Consequently, no turn-on delay or local overvoltage occurs across any stage, establishing a highly reliable engineering path for all-solid-state pulsed-power systems.

items.title: Design and Analysis of a Three-Port Bidirectional DC--DC Converter With Low-Voltage Stress and Flexible Power Flow Control for DC Microgrid Applications
items.abstract: Nonisolated bidirectional DC–DC converters (BDCs) are widely used for power flow management in energy storage systems, DC microgrids (DC-MGs), and electric vehicles (EVs); however, many existing topologies suffer from limited voltage gain, narrow duty-cycle range, high component count, bulky structure, and high-voltage stress on power devices. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes a nonisolated three-port high-gain BDC for the integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), energy storage units (ESUs), and DC-MGs. The proposed converter supports multiple power flow paths, including battery-to-DC-MG, photovoltaics (PVs)-to-DC-MG, and DC-MG-to-battery operation. It operates in boost mode for power transfer from Port-A to Port-B and in buck mode for reverse power flow. A wide voltage conversion ratio with reduced voltage stress across most switches is achieved, improving efficiency and reliability. A 200-W SiC MOSFET-based prototype was developed and experimentally validated. The converter achieves a peak efficiency of 96% and exhibits stable operation under both open-loop and closed-loop control. Moreover, operation in both continuous conduction mode (CCM) and discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) demonstrates the flexibility and robustness of the proposed topology across a wide operating range.
items.venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics

items.title: Design Space Exploration of Backside Clock Meshes for 2 nm GAAFET BSPDN Technology
items.abstract: Clock meshes are used in high-performance VLSI designs to minimize skew and tolerate on-chip variation, but they spend scarce routing resources on premium metal layers. Backside power delivery creates a new option: it adds thick, low-resistance metal layers on the back of the wafer, and the power grid does not consume all of them. Flip-flops remain on the frontside; a backside mesh therefore cannot drive them directly, and every connection passes through a through-silicon via. We present the first design-space exploration of backside clock meshes, implemented in OpenROAD on GT2N, a 2 nm nanosheet technology. Four benchmarks (1,938 to 15,311 flip-flops) are explored with multi-objective Bayesian optimization, and every design point is verified by transistor-level SPICE simulation, since the cyclic mesh cannot be evaluated by static timing analysis. Across all four designs, the backside mesh consistently outperforms an identical frontside mesh, with on average 45% lower skew, 25% lower sink slew, 4.5% lower power, and 28% less frontside clock wiring, and its skew spread under 10,000-sample Monte Carlo is a third of the frontside mesh's.

items.title: Demonstrating Novel Interbridge Complementary FET: Capacitance Extraction Using Dielectric Permittivity Suppression and Conformal Mapping
items.abstract: Complementary FET (CFET) is an astonishing transistor architecture that comprises a self-aligned nFET over pFET separated by a dielectric sidewall ( ${D}_{\text {SW}}$ ), or vice versa, designed to obtain the optimal gate pitch. To facilitate an enhanced effective channel width without altering the gate pitch, we propose a novel interbridge (IB) CFET (IB-CFET) structure in this article, in which a laterally branched fin-shaped IB layer is appended between the self-aligned vertical sheets. The additional IB layer offers a potential improvement in ${I}_{\text {ON}}$ / ${C}_{\text {gg}}$ , ${g}_{\text {m}}$ / ${C}_{\text {gg}}$ , and RC delay due to an increased overall channel area and reduced capacitance. We developed an analytical model framework for extracting the capacitance and RC delay using conformal mapping (CM) and the permittivity suppression technique to capture the gate electrostatics, including IBs. Considering only nFET is on , in IB-CFET, the total gate capacitance ( ${C}_{\text {gg}}\text {)}$ is contributed: 40% by spacer capacitance ( ${C}_{\text {spr}}\text {)}$ , 43% by channel ( ${C}_{\text {ch}}\text {)}$ , 4% by outer fringing ( ${C}_{\text {OF}}\text {)}$ , 6% by IB ( ${C}_{\text {IB}}\text {)}$ , and ~7% by the cumulative capacitance of pFET and dielectric sidewall. IB-CFET shows ~8% lower ${C}_{\text {gg}}$ than the conventional CFET, i.e., without IB; thereby offering ~9.95% lower RC delay. Using well-calibrated TCAD models, we extracted the capacitance and RC delay, which is further validated by our proposed model with a tolerable error of ~4%. The extracted ${I}_{\text {ON}}$ / ${C}_{\text {gg}}$ and g m / ${C}_{\text {gg}}$ of the proposed IB-CFET are improved by 11.40% and 4.08%, respectively, compared to the baseline CFET. Thus, the proposed IB-CFET proves its potential as a promising candidate beyond the 3-nm technology node.
items.venue: IEEE transactions on dielectrics and electrical insulation

items.title: Degradation Mechanisms in Die-to-Wafer Hybrid Bonding Governed by Surface Activation Lifetime and Moisture Evaporation
items.abstract: While direct placement die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonding is essential for advanced packaging, its performance is often compromised by an extended storage time between surface activation and bonding. However, the underlying chemical degradation mechanisms have not been fully elucidated because of the challenge of correlating macroscopic bond strength with molecular-scale interfacial changes. Here, we introduce a comprehensive analytical approach, combining a novel, highly accurate bonding energy measurement with multimodal surface spectroscopy. This method reveals that degradation is governed by a dual-factor mechanism: the loss of interfacial water and the depletion of surface silanol groups. The direct correlation between these interfacial changes and the reduction in bonding energy was quantitatively confirmed by thermal desorption and sum-frequency generation spectroscopy. This study provides the first quantitative insight into the degradation kinetics during storage, offering a clear scientific basis for optimizing D2W hybrid bonding processes.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging, and Manufacturing Technology

items.title: Defect-Engineered PECVD-Grown hBN Enabling Effective Charge Trapping in IGZO Synaptic Transistors
items.abstract: Neuromorphic devices require reliable charge trapping mechanisms to emulate synaptic functionalities such as hysteresis, memory retention, and weight modulation; however, conventional oxide semiconductor-based devices often suffer from limited stability due to the absence of well-defined trapping layers. Here, we demonstrate that defect-engineered hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) grown by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) can serve as an effective charge-trapping interlayer in indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) synaptic transistors. The PECVD-grown hBN exhibits significant structural disorder, oxygen-related bonding, increased Urbach energy, and reduced film density, indicating the presence of abundant defect-induced localized states that provide energetically favorable sites for charge trapping and retention. When the hBN film is integrated with the IGZO semiconducting channel layer, it significantly enhances the charge trapping efficiency, resulting in a pronounced increase in the hysteresis window from 0.8 to 4.7 V, along with improved synaptic characteristics such as enhanced potentiation/depression behavior and stable long-term memory retention. These results highlight the potential of PECVD-grown defect-rich hBN as a functional charge-trapping layer for high-performance oxide semiconductor-based neuromorphic devices.

items.title: Cryogenic RF Characterisation of FD-SOI Passive and Active Devices for LC-VCO Measurement-Based Design and Simulation
items.abstract: This paper presents a measurement-driven design methodology for a cross-coupled LC-VCO in 28-nm FD-SOI technology, targeting cryo-CMOS applications for qubit readout. Conventional design flows are limited by the lack of reliable compact models at cryogenic temperatures. To address this, each oscillator component (inductor, accumulation-mode MOS varactor, NMOS transistor) is characterised at both room temperature and 4.2 K. Small-signal S-parameters are used to reconstruct the differential admittance at the VCO output, enabling direct evaluation of oscillation startup without compact models. The approach reveals how cryogenic operation enhances transistor transconductance, improving startup speed and allowing supply voltage reduction beyond room-temperature limits. These results provide practical guidelines for designing oscillators in pulsed qubit readout systems, demonstrating that measurement-based modelling can effectively substitute for unavailable cryogenic compact models.

items.title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Based Optoelectronic Memristors: Structural Design, Optoelectronic Modulation and Neuromorphic Applications
items.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a tunable platform for optoelectronic memristors by coupling light absorption with history‐dependent conductance, yet their potential remains underexplored. This review systematically examines how structural features, including linkage chemistry, donor–acceptor organisation, dimensionality, layer stacking, photochromic groups, redox centres and pore environments, govern the generation and stabilisation of excited, charged, isomeric and ionic states. It then traces the translation of these states into device‐level conductance modulation via molecular switching, photoredox reactions, charge trapping, interfacial photogating and ion or filament motion, with special emphasis on film quality, electrode contacts and semiconductor heterointerfaces. Functional capabilities such as temporal plasticity, bidirectional programming, spectral encoding, adaptive vision, denoising, motion recognition and task‐specific sensing are critically assessed, distinguishing genuine device responses from software simulations and physically integrated arrays. From this analysis, three design rules emerge: charge separation must operate within a reversible kinetic window, the stored state should be identifiable independently of conductance, and framework architecture must align with the device current path. The primary opportunity lies in linking chemically defined state variables to optically addressable conductance, whereas major challenges include incomplete mechanistic validation, limited device statistics, environmental instability and the lack of fully integrated addressable COF arrays. The review concludes with priorities for mechanism‐resolved characterisation, scalable processing and circuit integration.

items.title: Coupled TCAD and 3D ANSYS Thermal Simulation for Hotspot Analysis in GaN HEMTs
items.abstract: This paper presents an electro-thermal methodology for hotspot temperature estimation in a GaN HEMT by coupling TCAD electrical simulation with 3D thermal simulation in ANSYS. First, TCAD is used to compute the electric field distribution and extract the corresponding Joule heating profile along the active region between source and drain. This non-uniform heat source is then transferred into a 3D geometrical model of the device in ANSYS, which offers a more physically representative thermal description of the device structure. The simulated temperatures are compared with experimental results obtained from several characterization techniques probing different regions of the transistor, including gate-related, surface, and electrically averaged temperatures. Although the hotspot itself cannot be directly measured, a good coherence is obtained between simulation and measurements. The proposed TCAD-to-ANSYS approach therefore provides a relevant framework for analyzing self-heating and estimating hotspot temperature in GaN HEMTs.

items.title: Control of Flatband Voltage via Ge Oxide-Involved Dipole Modulation in Low-Temperature Fabricated SiO 2 /GeO 2 /Ge Gate Stacks
items.abstract: Understanding and controlling the flatband voltage ( V FB ) of gate stacks is critical for the low-temperature fabrication of advanced Ge-based devices. In this study, we investigate the mechanism of V FB modulation in SiO 2 /GeO 2 /Ge gate stacks formed by an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) plasma process at 130 °C, followed by post-deposition annealing (PDA) at 210 °C–450 °C. Electrical characterization revealed that V FB and hysteresis strongly depend on annealing time. A systematic analysis of capacitance–voltage characteristics indicates that both the interface dipole ( δ dipole ) and fixed charge ( Q fix ) change dynamically during annealing, including polarity inversion of Q fix and gradual weakening of δ dipole . To clarify the origin of these modulations, structural analyses were performed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry.
