The results reveal the formation of Ge suboxides and the outward diffusion of Ge oxide species toward the SiO 2 . These phenomena are attributed to the generation and migration of oxygen vacancies within the GeO 2 layer. The oxygen vacancies simultaneously act as positive Q fix and modulate the δ dipole by redistributing charge at the SiO 2 /GeO 2 interface. These findings provide a comprehensive model linking chemical reactions, defect dynamics, and electrical properties, offering a pathway to precise V FB control in low-temperature Ge-based device technologies.
items.venue: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology

items.title: Continuous Bayesian Machine Learning for High-Dimensional Analog and Mixed-Signal Circuit Yield Analysis and Optimization
items.abstract: Traditional yield analysis for analog and mixed-signal (AMS) circuits relies heavily on Monte Carlo (MC) methods, which suffer from a fundamental information inefficiency: they reduce rich, continuous circuit performance metrics to binary pass/fail indicators. As process variations scale into high-dimensional spaces with advanced technology nodes, this inefficiency creates an insurmountable computational barrier. This paper proposes a Continuous Bayesian Inference framework that fundamentally transforms circuit yield analysis from discrete counting to probabilistic integration over the performance landscape. We introduce a Sparse Gaussian Process (SGP) model augmented with Deep Kernel Learning (DKL) to effectively capture the non-stationary correlations in high-dimensional variation spaces, reducing the computational complexity from $\mathcal{O}\mathbf{(}\boldsymbol{n}^\mathbf{3}\mathbf{)}$ O ( n 3 ) to $\mathcal{O}\mathbf{(}\boldsymbol{nm}^\mathbf{2}\mathbf{)}$ O ( n m 2 ) . Furthermore, we propose an information-theoretic active learning strategy based on convolutional entropy, which exploits the smoothness of circuit performance to optimally select samples that maximize uncertainty reduction. Experimental validation on benchmark circuits, including a 569-dimensional SRAM column, demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves a 34.30 $\mathbf{\times}$ × -320.14 $\mathbf{\times}$ × end-to-end speedup over standard MC. Furthermore, compared to state-of-the-art yield analysis baselines, it demonstrates 1.0 $\mathbf{\times}$ × –5.24 $\mathbf{\times}$ × end-to-end speedup. Additionally, SBYA can be seamlessly extended to yield optimization tasks, delivering comparable or even superior optimization efficacy while consuming merely one-quarter of the simulation budget required by existing methodologies.

items.title: Comprehensive Variation Model of Hafnium-Based Ferroelectric Capacitors for High-Sigma Memory Window Simulation
items.abstract: The polycrystalline nature of emerging ferroelectric materials introduces inherent variability in switching behavior, which poses a fundamental challenge for future high-density memory arrays. Predicting and mitigating this variability, particularly the worst-case “tail bits,” is critical for performance yet difficult with conventional approaches. Here, we present FEVAR, a synergistic framework that integrates multiscale material characterization with a physics-based modeling pipeline to accurately predict the performance distribution of hafnium-based ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) arrays. Leveraging this approach, we further delineate how material properties govern array-level performance. This work not only provides guidance for optimizing FeRAM but also establishes a generalizable methodology for linking material structure to device performance in the face of intrinsic variability.

items.title: Comparison of Direct Filtering and Channel Splitting in the Context of Digital Beamforming Chiplets
items.abstract: Two processing architectures for digital beamforming (DBF) and sub-band filtering, namely direct filtering and channel splitting, are compared in terms of complexity for the first time in the context of DBF integrated circuits. By exploiting the fact that reconstruction of processing channels can be performed at array-level instead of element-level, the channel splitting approach is shown to reduce processing complexity. A comparison is conducted for a wideband K-band satellite communication receiver use case. It is demonstrated that both architectures achieve equal performance in terms of error relative to the ideal matched transfer function. In processing, the channel splitting architecture exhibits a base complexity of 9.54 complex multiplications per input sample (cmps), while direct filtering has none. However, its scaling per color is significantly lower at 0.64 cmps/color compared to 7.36 cmps/color, making it more efficient for multi-beam, multi-frequency communication systems.

items.title: Comparative Scaling Analysis of Charge-Trap TFET and MOSFET Synapses for IR-Drop-Aware Analog Vector-Matrix-Multiplication
items.abstract: This study compares the scalability of charge-trap metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (CT-MOSFETs) and charge-trap tunnel field-effect transistors (CT-TFETs) for high-accuracy analog vector-matrix-multiplication (VMM) operations for the first time. Featuring stronger gate-controllability, CT-TFETs demonstrate better channel length modulation ( $\lambda \text {)}$ and analog weight level difference ratio ( $\Delta {I}_{\text {W}}$ / ${I}_{\text {W{0}}}\text {)}$ than those of CT-MOSFETs in both long and short gate length ( ${L}_{\text {G}}\text {)}$ cases (500 and 65 nm), maintaining low VMM error in the scaled case. Consequently, CT-TFETs show ~6.25× higher tolerable IR drop range and 11-% higher MNIST classification accuracy than CT-MOSFETs in the 65-nm ${L}_{\text {G}}$ case.

items.title: Compact and energy-efficient MRL-based approximate adder for image processing
items.abstract: Abstract Energy-efficient arithmetic circuits are crucial for modern computing applications, particularly in energy-constrained systems such as image and video processing. This paper introduces hybrid memristor-MOS approximate full-adders (MAFAs), namely MAFA1, MAFA2, and MAFA3. The proposed MAFAs are implemented using the memristor-ratioed logic (MRL) method and optimized the logic operations using the pruning technique. Moreover, the author proposed an 8-bit approximate adder that used a 4-bit MRL-based exact full adder (MEFA) for the most significant bits and an MAFA for the remaining 4 least significant bits. The proposed designs reduce circuit complexity, power consumption, delay, and area while maintaining acceptable error levels for media processing applications. Circuit performance parameters are analyzed using the LTspice simulator and 45 nm predictive technology model parameters for Metal–Oxide–Semiconductor transistors, and the voltage threshold adaptive memristor model model for the memristor. The proposed circuits are used to implement image-processing applications, including image addition and edge detection. The proposed designs are more energy-efficient and show clear performance improvements over earlier versions. They use fewer components and achieve lower power consumption and delay. In particular, the new MAFA designs reduce power consumption by up to 95.70% and delay by 64.07% compared to previous studies.

items.title: Chip-Agnostic Hardware-Aware Training for ADC-Efficient BNNs in SOT-MRAM Crossbars
items.abstract: Analog in-memory computing using SOT-MRAM crossbars is a promising approach for energy-efficient acceleration of Binary Neural Networks (BNNs). However, analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) remain a major latency and power bottleneck, forcing a direct trade-off between ADC precision and model accuracy. Furthermore, crossbars and their peripherals suffer from process variations, introducing noise that further degrades accuracy. To address this, we propose a SPICE-based hardware-aware training framework that injects end-to-end crossbar non-idealities directly into the BNN training flow. Our methodology supports both chip-specific training for precise device-level adaptation, and a novel chip-agnostic training for robust, generalized deployment across varying hardware instances without per-chip retraining. On ImageNet, scaling down to 4-bit ADCs reduces inference energy by ~30%. Despite this aggressive quantization and compounded hardware noise, our chip-agnostic and chip-specific frameworks bridge the hardware-software gap, limiting the Top-1 accuracy drop of a 4-bit MeliusNet22 to 2.7% and 0.9%, respectively, compared to an FP32 software baseline.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Characterization of Sub-6-GHz Carbon Nanotube Transistor-Based Resistive Mixer
items.abstract: This letter presents the fabrication and characterization of carbon nanotube (CNT) transistors and demonstrates their feasibility for high-linearity sub-6-GHz single-ended resistive mixer applications. Randomly oriented CNT FETs with a gate length of 200 nm were realized, delivering a current-gain cutoff frequency of 9.6 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency of 21.9 GHz. To evaluate their performance in practical RF environments, the CNT FETs were integrated onto a Rogers 4003 PCB via wire bonding, enabling characterization under realistic interconnect and fixture parasitics without de-embedding. Under zero-bias operation, the proposed gate-pumped resistive mixer achieves a conversion gain (CG) of −17.8–−21 dB over the 1.4–5 GHz band. An input third-order intercept point (IIP3) of 16 dBm is obtained, indicating good linearity. These results demonstrate the feasibility of CNT FETs for passive mixer applications in sub-6-GHz RF front ends.
items.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters

items.title: CTLIM: A 1.92 Mb/mm2 4T1C eDRAM Macro for Area-Efficient Cryogenic Ternary Logic-in-Memory
items.abstract: Cryogenic ternary logic-in-memory (LIM) is a promising solution to improve storage density and computation efficiency for data-intensive applications by performing ternary operations directly within memory. However, most previous ternary logic implementations rely on binary-encoded processing at room temperature, making it difficult to achieve the density benefits of true ternary operation for both compute and memory at cryogenic temperatures. To address this issue, this work presents a 28 nm $128\times 128$ cryogenic true ternary LIM (CTLIM) macro. First, we propose a compact four-transistor one-capacitor (4T1C) cryogenic ternary cell (CTC) capable of storing a trit, featuring a full-swing write path for stable ternary data storage and a decoupled dual-transistor readout for reliable sensing and efficient LIM operations. Second, we develop a true ternary write–read scheme comprising a ternary write driver (TWD), a charge-sharing-based bitline reference voltage configuration (BRVC), and a voltage-latched ternary sense amplifier (TSA). Third, we implement true ternary LIM operations, including one-operand [standard ternary inverter (STI), negative ternary inverter (NTI)] and two-operand [MIN, MAX, consensus (CONS), accept-anything (ANY)] ternary operations, enabled by the TSA and BRVC. Measurement results of our test chip in a 28-nm bulk CMOS process demonstrate that the CTLIM macro achieves a macro density of 1.92 Mb/mm2 and ternary LIM energy consumption of 23.63–31.27 fJ/bit at 77 K. Moreover, it also achieves a retention time of 18 ms, demonstrating area-efficient true ternary storage and LIM operations at cryogenic temperatures.

items.title: CFET-FP: Complementary FET Standard Cell Synthesis With Optimal Transistor Folding and Placement for Design and Technology Co-Optimization
items.abstract: It has been widely accepted that the complementary-field-effect transistor (CFET) is a promising technology, which stacks P-FET on N-FET or vice versa, to achieve this objective. In comparison with synthesizing the conventional FET-based standard cells, two prominent optimization tasks in CFET-based multirow cell synthesis that significantly affect the cell quality, in terms of area and routability, are as follows: 1) determining transistor folding shapes and 2) determining placement order of transistors with feasible routability. In this work, we propose an optimal solution to the combined problem of tasks 1 and 2. Precisely, we develop a search tree-based area-optimal method of transistor folding and placement, in which we accelerate the cost computation of partial solutions by formulating it into dynamic programming while performing a strict feasibility checking of the routability of partial solutions. In the meantime, through experiments with benchmark circuits, it is shown that the CFET cells produced by our cell synthesizer are 6% smaller in size on average, even with 28% shorter total metal length and 62% less use of metal 2 for in-cell routing over the cells produced by the recent state-of-the-art CFET cell generator. In addition, we conduct a study on design and technology co-optimization (DTCO) by exploring the CFET cell architecture for an open-source 64-bit RISC-V CPU block with a 7-nm node.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: Building Minimum-Power Digital Circuits With Sub-Femtowatt Dynamic Leakage-Suppression Logic Standard Cells
items.abstract: This article investigates dynamic leakage-suppression (DLS) logic for minimum-power operation in digital circuits. The DLS logic family uses a strong intrinsic subthreshold leakage reduction technique and is an emerging approach for computing applications that prioritize low active power at or beneath the nW-level. We analytically model the key operating characteristics of DLS logic and show that a minimum-power point exists at an optimal $V_{\mathrm {dd}}$ that balances various sources of leakage current. We discuss available knobs for DLS logic and present a general design methodology for targeting minimum-power operation while also considering robustness. A fabricated test chip in 65-nm CMOS validates our models and design methodology with several unique DLS standard cell libraries, and measurements of traditional static-CMOS logic are included for comparison. Measurement results demonstrate a minimum DLS leakage power of 0.26 fW per inverter at 0.35 V, over $350\times $ lower than CMOS inverters at the same supply voltage. At 1.2 V, this leakage reduction increases to $\gt$ $ 1000\times $ . The library implementation of the proposed DLS libraries is validated with synthesized 8-bit DLS multiply-accumulate (MAC) circuits.

items.title: Breaking the Drivability-Threshold-Voltage Trade-off in 40 nm Vertical Gate-All-Around Oxide FETs via Spacer-Defined Offset Engineering
items.abstract: Spacer-defined offset engineering is presented as a structural strategy to enhance the on-state current (ION) of vertical gate-all-around (VGAA) amorphous indium-gallium oxide (IGO) field-effect transistors (FETs) while preserving threshold-voltage (VTH) control. Increasing the indium fraction in the IGO channel improved ION but simultaneously caused a pronounced negative VTH shift, revealing an observed trade-off in composition-based channel engineering. To circumvent this limitation, the SiO2 spacer thickness was scaled from 100 to 30 nm while maintaining the optimized IGO 6:3 channel composition. For IGO FETs with a gate length of 40 nm, the average ION increased from 1.24 ± 0.54 to 9.5 ± 1.94 μA as the spacer thickness was reduced from 100 to 30 nm, without inducing a negative VTH shift. For twenty 30-nm-spacer devices, the average VTH and subthreshold swing were 0.29 ± 0.05 V and 71.4 ± 4 mV/dec, respectively, with an apparent drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) factor of 3.7 mV/V. Y-function analysis, temperature-dependent measurements, and Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations revealed that the performance enhancement originated from reduced access resistance and electrostatic modulation of the source-side access region, while no statistically distinct spacer-dependent change in the effective source-side injection barrier was resolved. The optimized device also exhibited VTH shifts of only +79 and -26 mV under positive and negative bias-temperature stress, respectively, at 95 °C for 3600 s under effective gate fields of ±3 MV/cm, while the VGAA-based two-transistor zero-capacitor dynamic random-access memory (2T0C DRAM) cell exhibited a retention time exceeding 100 s. These results establish spacer-defined offset engineering as an effective structural design approach for oxide-semiconductor memory transistors that require both high ION and stable VTH operation.

items.title: Bias- and Frequency-Dependent Optimization of Gate Length for Efficiency in GaN-on-SiC HEMTs With a Fit Predictive Model
items.abstract: The efficiency of GaN-on-SiC high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) is limited by the combined influence of the trap-induced current collapse, knee-voltage walkout, and parasitic capacitances. While the gate-length scaling is known to affect these mechanisms, the optimum geometry for maximum power-added efficiency (PAE) under the realistic bias and frequency conditions has remained unclear. Here, we investigate the gate length impacts on efficiency. Comprehensive DC, pulsed-IV, small-signal, and large-signal measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of efficiency, from which a bias-frequency regime map for gate-length optimization has been established, and a predictive model that links PAE to small-signal fmax and applied bias was introduced. The model reproduces measured data with high accuracy and offers a compact route to efficiency prediction from routine RF characterization. Together, the regime map and predictive model provide a physically grounded framework for bias- and frequency-aware design of GaN HEMTs for millimeter-wave power amplification.
items.venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters

items.title: Backside Signal Intracell Routing Beyond Backside Power Delivery for Angstrom Nodes
items.abstract: This study extensively examines the power, performance, and area benefits of backside signal intracell routing for Angstrom nodes. For effective backside signal implementation, wrap-around contact (WAC) is applied to reduce contact resistance. Since backside metal layers with narrow widths substantially increase process cost, only a single MB1 layer is used for backside intracell routing. As the backside power linewidth decreases, parasitic capacitance is reduced, improving single-cell performance, while the IR drop remains sufficiently low at a small micro-bump pitch. Because the proposed scheme keeps cell pins on the frontside, only cells containing relocatable nonpin metals can benefit; thus, cells such as INVx1 show no benefit. The proposed routing reduces Miller capacitance and improves the cell-level energy-delay product (EDP), with more pronounced benefits in complex cells such as DFF. At the chip level, backside intracell routing alleviates routing congestion, reducing frontside intercell wire length by 4.1%–6.8%. The wire-length reduction is more pronounced in macro-containing designs, such as the Rocket benchmark, due to their higher routing complexity. In the Rocket benchmark, the conventional design exhibits 19–73 short violations, whereas backside signal intracell routing reduces them to nearly zero. Backside intracell routing also decreases the number of inserted repeaters. Furthermore, backside signal intracell routing provides a thermal benefit by mitigating the chip temperature. Overall, backside signal intracell routing improves the power-delay product by 4.3%–14.2% across all benchmarks by combining cell-level optimization with routing-congestion and chip temperature reduction. This study provides practical guidelines for the characteristics and benefits of backside signal intracell routing.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: Avalanche Failure Mechanism of SiC MOSFETs After Total Ionizing Dose Irradiation
items.abstract: This brief reports the impact of total ionizing dose (TID) irradiation on the avalanche behavior of SiC MOSFETs. Experimental results show that the avalanche energy ( ${E}_{\textit {av}}\text {)}$ decreases by 5.99% and 13.83%, while the threshold voltage ( ${V}_{\textit {TH}}\text {)}$ shifts negatively by 34.14% and 76.34% after 50 krad and 100 krad TID irradiation, respectively. Both microscopic analysis and TCAD simulation results indicate that the diversion of avalanche current from the body diode to the MOS channel underlies this degradation. Due to the irradiation-induced accumulation of positive charges in the gate oxide, ${V}_{\textit {TH}}$ exhibits a negative shift with increasing irradiation dose. As a result, the margin for fully turning off the MOS channel under a fixed gate-off voltage ( ${V}_{\textit {GS}\_{\textit {off}}}\text {)}$ during avalanche is reduced, and a portion of the avalanche current is redirected from the body diode to the adjacent MOS channel. As channel mobility is low in SiC MOSFETs, this current diversion generates substantial Joule heating and triggers a rapid temperature rise along the channel path. Ultimately, premature burnout occurs in SiC MOSFETs after TID irradiation during avalanche. This finding provides insights into reliability assessment and radiation hardening of SiC MOSFETs for space applications.

items.title: AutoSDC: Shielded Neuro-Structural SDC Repair with Matched Ablations and Post-Route Verification
items.abstract: An edit to a Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) file proposed by artificial intelligence (AI) can be legal Tcl and still hide a real timing path. AutoSDC therefore divides authority: a learned policy only ranks typed repair operators against a signed scenario contract, while deterministic structural checks and measured timing evidence control every mutation and promotion. A 16-unit tanh layer maps ten structural features onto ten repair actions; a 26-feature critic supplies value feedback. In matched leave-one-design-out tests (18 held-out arms, 30 seeds), a rule-based selector, a supervised multilayer perceptron, and reinforcement-learning proposers trained by proximal policy optimization - cold-started or warm-started via behavior cloning - all repair 18/18 arms; warm-starting cuts median convergence from four updates to one without improving accuracy. Across the 24-mutant dual-timer campaign, all typed outputs are byte-identical to signed targets, semantic counters plus endpoint-universe preservation expose all 24 hazards, and only 6/24 outputs clear the absolute gate because 18 targets retain prior findings. Fresh OpenROAD runs add physical evidence: a 26,242-cell TinyRocket with two SRAM macros routes with zero design-rule-check violations, contract repair cuts unconstrained endpoints from 165 to 40, and a narrow constant-cone proof discharges all 40 without false paths. A matched GCD control under a four-times-relaxed clock looks clean there yet shows 44 failing endpoints against the signed contract, versus 17 for the signed flow; the signed flow is repeated on ASAP7. This is a reproducible pre-signoff repair-and-triage study, not multimode multi-corner signoff, multi-GPU execution, or SoC-scale validation.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: Area-Efficient and High-Performance 3T CFET Cells Enabled by an Embedded Interconnect Layer (EI-CFET) With Sequential Integration
items.abstract: Complementary FET (CFET) architectures are promising for logic scaling, especially when combined with backside power delivery networks (BSPDNs). In this work, we propose a CFET architecture featuring an embedded interconnect (EI) layer (EI-CFET), enabled by sequential process integration. By redistributing signal and power routing across the frontside (FS), EI layer, and backside (BS), the proposed architecture enables a 3T standard-cell height (CH) and reduces the cell area by approximately 25% and 20% relative to the 4T and 3.75T FS-/BS-routed reference CFET cells, respectively. The EI layer alleviates routing-induced parasitic penalties by shortening critical connections and improving routing flexibility, leading to more pronounced performance benefits in cells with denser internal routing. Meanwhile, connection failures induced by top-to-bottom misalignment can be effectively mitigated by an optimized EI handoff structure, and the performance variation is suppressed to below 0.5%. In addition, independent crystallographic optimization of stacked devices provides additional performance gains exceeding 6% over the reference design. These results demonstrate that the EI-CFET is a promising candidate for high-density and high-performance 3-D CMOS technologies.

items.title: Analog Hardware Trojans: An Overlooked Threat
items.abstract: Editor’s notes: Hardware Trojan attacks represent a critical integrity threat in the modern microelectronics supply chain. This article sheds light on vulnerability of analog/mixed-signal circuits to Trojan attacks and presents several interesting case studies. —Swarup Bhunia, University of Florida, USA

items.title: An Extendable Wideband Band-Divided SPnT Switch Topology Based on a Reconfigurable Pole-to-Throw Network
items.abstract: This article presents an extendable wideband band-divided SP $n$ T switch topology based on a reconfigurable pole-to-throw network (RPTN). Compared to conventions, it mitigates the loss degradation resulting from complex signal routing in advanced RF front-ends. This is enabled by the RPTN, which divides the throws into low-/mid-/high-band (HB) groups and reshapes the pole-to-throw interaction in different operating modes. It allows off -state parasitics to be incorporated into mode-dependent matching networks or bypassed. To demonstrate the scalability and technology portability of the proposed topology, two wideband switch chips in SP3T and SP6T configurations are implemented in different processes. The SP3T prototype is fabricated in a 0.25- $\mu $ m GaN HEMT process with a modest figure of merit (FoM) of 500 fs. Measurements show an insertion loss (IL) of 0.42–1.47 dB, a return loss (RL) of better than 14.6 dB, and a P0.1dB of 35.2–40 dBm over a DC–18 GHz frequency range. The SP6T prototype is fabricated in a 0.15- $\mu $ m GaAs pHEMT process with a favorable FoM of 240 fs. Measurements demonstrate an IL of 0.34–1.18 dB, an RL of higher than 15.0 dB, and a P0.1dB of 25.6–29.7 dBm over a DC–18 GHz. The measured results of both prototypes verify the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed topology.

items.title: An Efficient Optimization Design Method for Signal Integrity of 3-D Integrated Circuits With Quasi-Coaxial TSV Arrays
items.abstract: Due to the crosstalk and electromagnetic interference (EMI) in 3-D integrated circuits, signal integrity degradation remains a critical bottleneck. To address the inefficiency of full-wave electromagnetic simulation and optimization design, the high-efficiency optimization design method for quasi-coaxial through-silicon via (TSV) arrays is proposed to enhance signal integrity in interference-prone environments. To replace time-consuming full-wave electromagnetic simulations, a stacked autoencoder (SAE) surrogate model is developed and trained on 2401 orthogonal HFSS datasets, achieving a prediction R2 of 0.93 and a 150 $000\times $ speedup. Then, the SAE model is integrated into a two-step global–local particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to perform multiobjective optimization under three representative scenarios (balanced, low-frequency prioritized, and high-frequency prioritized). The simulation verifications indicate a maximum relative error of 2.38% compared with the full-wave HFSS simulation. In addition, the experimental results across three fabrication batches indicate an overall R2 of 0.9825 for the S-parameter predictions from the SAE model. Moreover, the compatibility with 12-in TSV manufacturing has been confirmed. Therefore, the proposed method combines accuracy and efficiency, which is suitable for 3-D integrated circuits design in uncrewed systems, aerospace, robotics, and 6G applications.

items.title: An Analytical Model of the SiC MOSFET Body Diode Over a Wide Range of Operating Conditions
items.abstract: The temperature-dependent reverse recovery characteristics of the SiC MOSFET body diode are comprehensively investigated in this article. Initially, the switching transient of the SiC MOSFET body diode is divided into eight phases, and the switching behavior in each phase is discussed. The analysis of the diode reverse recovery charge and its dependency on temperature and load current reveals the unipolar and bipolar characteristics of the body diode, which are modeled analytically. Based on device physics, the minority carrier build-up during the dead time and the minority carrier recombination during the current falling time are modeled. To model the minority charge dynamics, a charge equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is introduced, and its analytical expression is derived. The simulation results are compared with test data, and good agreement is achieved.
items.venue: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics

items.title: Amorphous boron nitride as a low-k dielectric for next-generation BEOL interconnects
items.abstract: As back-end-of-line (BEOL) scaling pushes porous low-k dielectrics toward their reliability limits, nonporous dielectrics that combine a low dielectric constant (k) with mechanical, thermal, and interfacial robustness are increasingly needed. Among nonporous low-k candidates, amorphous boron nitride (aBN) has attracted attention for advanced BEOL interconnects owing to its low-k value (k ≈ 2) and high mechanical robustness, as reflected by a Young's modulus of ~50 GPa. In this review, we discuss aBN from a BEOL process-integration perspective, focusing on the origin of its low-k behavior, process-dependent structure-property relationships, and its potential roles in BEOL interconnects and hybrid-bonding interfaces. Finally, we discuss remaining issues and future directions for validating aBN as a nonporous low-k dielectric/interface material under BEOL and hybrid-bonding integration.

items.title: Additive solid immersion lenses for enhanced collection efficiency of shallow NV centers by pulsed laser deposition and structurization of high-k amorphous oxides
items.abstract: The negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy ($\mathrm{NV}^-$) defect in diamond can be used for quantum information processing via the readout of the radiative decay of the excited state into the ground state. The large refractive index mismatch of diamond and air causes low photon extraction efficiency due to total internal reflection losses. Here, we investigate the photon extraction numerically and report additive solid immersion lenses (SILs) consisting of the high-k dielectric yttria-stabilized-zirconia (YSZ) for surface modification and enhanced light extraction of shallow implanted nitrogen-vacancy centers. We demonstrate an average increase of 63% in saturation intensity using a scalable bottum up room temperature pulsed laser deposition and photolithography structurization process. The average necessary laser intensity for saturation is reduced by 33% by the SILs.

items.title: Achieving 0.82-dB NFmin in High-Drain-Bias GaN HEMTs via Buffer and Field-Plate Engineering for High-Linearity LNA Applications
items.abstract: In this letter, minimum noise figure ( NF ${}_{\text{min} }$ ) of GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) under high-drain bias ( $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}} \gt \text{20}$ V) is investigated and optimized for high-linearity low noise amplifier (LNA) applications. By employing a $\text{1}~\mu $ m Fe-doped GaN buffer and a non-overlapping source field plate (SFP), the device achieves a NF min of 0.82 dB at 3 GHz and a $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}}$ of 24 V, while delivering an associated gain ( $\textit{G}_{\text {a}}$ ) of 16.61 dB and an output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of 31.8 dBm. Experimental comparison and a physics-based noise model identify the sharp increase in gate leakage current ( $\textit{I}_{\text {G}}$ ) as the dominant cause of NF min degradation under high $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}}$ , and confirm its suppression using $\text{1}~\mu $ m Fe-doped buffer scheme. Moreover, a non-overlapping SFP suppresses the device’s thermal noise by lowering the intrinsic resistances ( $\textit{R}_{\text {i}}$ , $\textit{R}_{\text {gd}}$ ). This work provides a novel design optimization strategy for high-bias, low-noise GaN HEMTs tailored for high-linearity LNA applications.

items.title: AI-Assisted Full-Field Warpage Prediction and Optimization for Advanced Packaging
items.abstract: Advanced packages often exhibit complex and nonuniform warpage because of heterogeneous materials, diverse structural layouts, and multiple manufacturing processes. These characteristics make conventional global warpage metrics alone insufficient for design decision-making and require full-field prediction to identify different warpage patterns. In addition, the enlarged design space and modeling complexity increase the computational burden of optimal design exploration to reduce the warpage. This study proposes an AI-assisted package design approach that combines conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN)-based full-field warpage prediction with multiobjective optimization based on the nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II). The cGAN model predicts spatially resolved warpage distributions from design variables, with informative warpage features embedded in the conditional input to guide nonlinear mapping. The prediction model achieved 97.0% prediction accuracy in terms of full-field prediction, confirming its suitability as a surrogate model for large-scale design exploration. The trained model was then coupled with NSGA-II to identify warpage-reducing design candidates. The optimized design reduced warpage by more than 88% compared with reference designs, while completing the optimization process within a few seconds. The proposed method is particularly suitable for accelerating the design exploration and optimization of complex advanced packages.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging, and Manufacturing Technology

items.title: A photolithography-compatible method for transferring full-device constituents on silicon substrate
items.abstract: Transfer printing offers a promising route to integrate pre-fabricated device components with two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors, yet most existing approaches rely on deliberately deposited buffer layers or specialized substrates, adding complexity and limiting compatibility with standard silicon fabrication. Here, we report a simple and photolithography-compatible strategy that leverages the ultrathin lift-off-resist (LOR) residue, which naturally retains on a commercial silicon substrate after standard photolithography, as a sacrificial release layer. This ~2 nm-thick residue allows selective water intercalation at the LOR/Si interface, enabling damage-free delamination of various pre-fabricated metal electrodes, high-κ metal gate (HKMG) stacks, and even entire device stacks directly from the Si substrate. Besides, the top-gated MoS2 transistor was fabricated by one-step laminating the full-device stack onto the MoS2 flake, yielding a clean van der Waals interface, small subthreshold swing and negligible gate hysteresis. Our method eliminates the need for additional sacrificial layer deposition or specialized handling substrates, offering a facile method to transfer full-device constituents on industry-compatible Si substrate.

items.title: A neuromodulable current-mode silicon neuron for robust and adaptive neuromorphic systems
items.abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic engineering makes use of mixed-signal analog and digital circuits to directly emulate the computational principles of biological brains. Such electronic systems offer a high degree of adaptability, robustness, and energy efficiency across a wide range of tasks, from edge computing to robotics. Within this context, we investigate a key feature of biological neurons: their ability to carry out robust and reliable computation by adapting their input responses and spiking patterns to context through neuromodulation. Achieving analogous levels of robustness and adaptation in neuromorphic circuits through modulatory mechanisms is a largely unexplored path. We present a novel current-mode neuron design that supports robust neuromodulation with minimal model complexity, compatible with standard complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technologies. We first introduce a mathematical model of the circuit and provide tools to analyze and tune the neuron behavior; we then demonstrate both theoretically and experimentally the biologically plausible neuromodulatory adaptation capabilities of the circuit over a wide range of parameters. All theoretical predictions were verified in experiments on a low-power 180 nm CMOS implementation of the proposed neuron circuit. Thanks to the underlying analog feedback structure, the proposed adaptive neuromodulable neuron exhibits a high degree of robustness, flexibility, and scalability across operating ranges of currents and temperatures, making it a perfect candidate for real-world neuromorphic applications.

items.title: A memory-adaptive Karma–Dharma optimizer for global optimization and VLSI design
items.abstract: While many recent metaheuristics rely on elaborate biological or physical metaphors, their underlying mathematical mechanics often remain obscured. This paper introduces the Karma–Dharma Optimizer (KDO), a transparent, memory-adaptive metaheuristic designed for continuous and constrained engineering optimization. KDO couples two complementary phases: a memory-guided exploration phase that utilizes a historical success archive (the Dharma operator) and a structured exploitation phase (the Karma operator). An adaptive stagnation-recovery mechanism, termed Nirvana Reset, is further incorporated to help the search escape locally stagnant regions. The global search capability and dimensional scalability of KDO are extensively evaluated on the CEC-2017 and CEC-2022 benchmark suites across dimensions up to \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$D=50$$\end{document}. Furthermore, KDO is applied to four constrained analog, RF, and VLSI circuit design problems: a two-stage Miller operational amplifier, an RF CMOS cascode LNA, a low phase-noise LC-VCO, and a 6T FinFET SRAM cell. These circuits are evaluated under both closed-form analytical surrogates and an automated, physics-driven MATLAB–ngspice-in-the-loop simulation framework accounting for process–voltage–temperature (PVT) variations and Monte Carlo yield constraints. Non-parametric statistical analyses alongside component-wise ablation studies, reveal a problem-dependent performance profile for KDO. It achieves the best overall rank on the constrained VLSI design problems under both analytical and physics-based evaluations, while remaining competitive against strong mathematical optimizers (DE, GBO) on the standardized CEC benchmarks.

items.title: A Wideband and Highly Accurate Electrical Model of Arbitrary TSV Arrays and RDL Interconnections With Partial Inductance Method for 3-D ICs
items.abstract: In this article, a wideband and highly accurate electrical model of arbitrary through silicon via (TSV) arrays and redistribution layer (RDL) interconnections using the partial inductance method is proposed for 3-D integrated circuits (3-D ICs). Coupling matrices associated with partial inductances are employed to characterize the coupling effects and electromagnetic behaviors among TSV arrays and within RDL interconnects. Moreover, to characterize the nonlinear effect introduced by the mutual coupling among TSVs, the parasitic capacitance of TSV arrays is calculated by quasi-transverse electromagnetic (quasi-TEM) field theory. In addition, the conformal mapping method is used to characterize the complex parasitic effects of RDL in multilayer dielectrics. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed electrical model of the TSV-RDL interconnections is validated by the simulated and measured results.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Components, Packaging, and Manufacturing Technology

items.title: A Wide Memory Window of 10.3 V With Ferroelectric AlScN Layer In2O3 FeFET
items.abstract: This work presents the operation and reliability test of field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with ferroelectric AlScN films and In 2 O 3 channels. For a 45-nm-thick AlScN FeFET with an Al 2 O 3 interfacial layer, a large memory window (MW) of 10.3 V and a high on / off ratio of $10^{{10}}$ are obtained. Thickness scaling of AlScN films down to 15 nm has also exhibited FeFET operation. A 4-bit operation is confirmed by applying different programming (PRG) and erasing (ERS) pulses. A switching cycle endurance of $10^{{5}}$ cycles and a retention characteristic of $10^{{4}}$ s were confirmed. The gradual retention loss was modeled by electron trapping and de-trapping in the Al 2 O 3 layer. The FeFET results are highly promising for the next generation of analog memory applications.

items.title: A Universal Photodiode-Based Optical Gate Driver for GaN Power Devices
items.abstract: Optically controlled power devices hold promise for achieving minimal triggering delay, simplified control for device stacking, and high electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity. Although gallium nitride (GaN) devices are rapidly advancing power electronics applications, optically controlled high-voltage switching has rarely been reported in GaN. This work addresses this gap by presenting a universal, optically controlled gate driver based on two photodiodes (PDs) in a totem-pole structure capable of switching GaN power devices with fast speed and low optical power. The two reverse-biased PDs are controlled by complementary optical signals to provide gate current, emulating a current-source gate driver. The proposed driver is demonstrated on both voltage- and current-driven GaN transistors, including a 650 V GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) and a 1200 V vertical GaN junction-gate field-effect transistor (JFET). The GaN HEMT achieves some of the fastest switching speeds and lowest required optical powers reported for optically controlled power devices. For the current-driven GaN JFET, the PD’s intrinsic properties provide both transient and steady-state gate current, simplifying the driving circuitry and reducing driver losses. An analytical model is further developed to describe the switching dynamics of both devices under PD-based optical control. These results reveal the potential of PD-based optical gate driving schemes for advancing GaN power electronics.
items.venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)

items.title: A Study of Schottky Gate Diode Noise in 10 GHz GaN HEMT Oscillators
items.abstract: This paper presents a phase noise study of two HEMT-based cross-coupled oscillators, with focus on the noise generated by Schottky gate diode. A simple method to improve the phase noise performance by reducing the gate diode current is implemented in one of the oscillators. The two oscillators are designed in a 150nm GaN HEMT technology and they operate at 10.8 GHz and 10 GHz, respectively. Phase noise calculations based on impulse sensitivity function and measurements show a good match and confirm that the proposed method can significantly improve phase noise performance. The oscillator with improved performance reaches phase noise of -132.6 dBc/Hz and -156.7 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz and 10 MHz offsets from the carrier, with corresponding FOMs of 189.3 dBc/Hz and 193.5 dBc/Hz.

items.title: A Self-Supervised and Cross-Design Netlist Power Model for Time-Based Layout Power Analysis
items.abstract: Accurate power prediction in very large scale integration (VLSI) design is crucial for effective power optimization, especially as designs get transformed from gate-level netlist to layout stages. However, traditional accurate power simulation requires time-consuming back-end processing and simulation steps, which significantly impede design optimization. To address this, we propose ATLAS, which can predict the ultimate time-based layout power for any new design in the gate-level netlist. In addition, we extend ATLAS to support power prediction using only register-transfer level (RTL)-stage toggle information, further increasing its applicability and efficiency. To the best of authors’ knowledge, ATLAS is the first work that supports both time-based power simulation and general cross-design power modeling. It achieves such general time-based power modeling by proposing a new pretraining and fine-tuning paradigm customized for circuit power. Targeting golden per-cycle layout power from commercial tools, our ATLAS achieves the average mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of only 5.41%, 3.79%, and 7.51% for the clock tree, register, and combinational power groups, respectively, without any layout information. Overall, the average MAPE for the total power of the entire design is 3.05%, and the inference speed of a workload is significantly faster than the standard flow of commercial tools. Furthermore, ATLAS can bypass the time-consuming signal propagation process, and when using only RTL-stage toggle information, it achieves a total power MAPE as low as 5.00%.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A Self-Recoverable Nonvolatile Magnetic Latch with High-Speed SEU-Tolerant Backup Module
items.abstract: With the continuous scaling of transistor technologies, single event upset (SEU) induced by space radiation particles has become a critical reliability challenge for aerospace digital circuits. This paper proposes a radiation-hardened self-recoverable nonvolatile (NV) latch, termed the SRHS-STBM latch, which integrates magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with CMOS circuitry. To achieve complete recovery from SEUs, the proposed latch employs four cross-coupled dual-input standard C-elements (DSCs) forming a robust feedback structure. In addition, a novel SEU-tolerant backup module is developed to address a key limitation of prior NV latches, where backup operations are vulnerable to radiation-induced data corruption. The proposed module ensures reliable backup operation while significantly improving backup speed. Using a physics-based STT-MTJ compact model and a commercial 40 nm CMOS design kit for simulations, the proposed SRHSSTBM latch achieves a D-Q delay of 60.85 ps, a restore delay of 43.60 ps, and a static power consumption as low as 0.16 μW. Monte Carlo simulations further reveal that, even in the worst case with a deposited charge of Qinj = 2 pC, the backup delay is only 3.73 ns and the internal nodes can fully recover from SEUs.
items.venue: IEEE/IFIP International Conference on Very Large Scale Integration of System-on-Chip

items.title: A Rugged 40 V 0.12-μm GaN HEMT Technology Platform for Single Chip RF Front-Ends
items.abstract: This paper describes a versatile 40 V 0.12-μm GaN-on-SiC technology platform (NP12-0B) optimized for high-performance RF front-end applications. By leveraging an optimized device structure, the operational drain bias is extended from 28 V to 40 V, significantly enhancing power density while maintaining fmax of 150 GHz, with excellent noise figure and antenna switch performance. A pre-matched PA cell operating at 40V provides Psat of 7.9 W/mm with over 13dB gain at 18 GHz. For receiver applications, this technology demonstrates 18GHz NFmin of 0.9 dB using a 10 V bias. To enable single chip frontends, a broadband SPDT switch measured from DC to 20 GHz exhibits a input P1dB of 40 dBm at 18 GHz. Preliminary reliability results for 500-hour HTOL, 1000-hour HTRB and HTGB stress tests show negligible parametric drift. These results confirm the NP12-0B platform provides a rugged, versatile high-performance solution for next-generation integrated RF front-end modules.

items.title: A Process-Tolerant, Decoupled 8T SRAM Configuration for Ultralow-Power IoT Caches: Comparative Statistical Analysis
items.abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things edge devices requires cache memories that balance low power consumption with robust process variation immunity. While traditional six transistor SRAM cells suffer from high static power dissipation, compact five transistor options compromise the Read Static Noise Margin (SNM, dropping stability to 102.7 mV. To address this multiparametric trade-off, this paper presents a process tolerant, decoupled eight transistor SRAM configuration for ultra-low power Internet of Things (IOT) caches. By utilizing a dedicated, isolated two transistor read path, the architecture shields internal storage nodes from bit line noise during read sweeps, eliminating read disturb mechanisms. Simulations in 45 nm CMOS technology demonstrate that the proposed cell maintains high efficiency while elevating stability. Compared to a standard six transistor cell, it reduces total power loss by 90.62 percent to 4.16 nanowatts, cuts static leakage by 75.78 percent to 3.02 picowatts, and improves operational delay to 167.6 ps. A 1,000-sample Monte Carlo analysis and multi-corner process evaluation confirm tight statistical tracking with a standard deviation of 1.11 nanowatts for total power and uncompromised data integrity at worst case corners, proving its suitability for resilient Internet of Things cache architectures.
items.venue: International Conference on Innovative Mechanisms for Industry Applications

items.title: A Nonvolatile AI-Edge Processor With Lossless-Compressed-Computing STT-MRAM Near-Memory-Compute Macro Using Dynamic Floating-/Fixed-Point Accumulation
items.abstract: Nonvolatile AI-edge processors based on near-memory-compute (nvNMC) enable energy-efficient multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) operations with short wakeup latency for edge inference operations. Lossless compression is required for floating-point (FP) neural network (NN) models under on-chip memory capacity constraints; however, this imposes several challenges: 1) data decompression overhead due to lossless FP weight encoding; 2) a read-yield–energy tradeoff due to near-far effects in large nonvolatile memory arrays; 3) a MAC-accuracy–energy tradeoff in FP accumulation within the multi-level adder tree; and 4) inefficient layer fusion due to feature-map (FM)–weight mapping in nvNMC. This article addresses these challenges by presenting a nonvolatile AI-edge processor featuring four system–circuit co-design schemes: 1) delta-exponent lossless compression computation (DELC ${}^{2}$ ); 2) near-far-aware bias-and-mapping (NFABM); 3) dynamic floating-/fixed-point (FXP) accumulation (DF2PA); and 4) nvNMC-friendly hybrid-layer-fusion weight-mapping (CIM-HLF-WM). A test chip fabricated using foundry-provided 22-nm spin-transfer-torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) achieved an energy efficiency of 24.6 TFLOPS/W and a wakeup-to-response latency of 428.58 $\mu $ s under BF16 input and weight, verifying its effectiveness for capacity- and energy-constrained AI-edge applications.

items.title: A Nonuniform Frequency Dithering Technique to Minimize the EMI Noise and Input Filter in a SiC-MOSFET Based DC–DC Converter
items.abstract: The wide-bandgap device-based power electronic converters pose the challenge of electromagnetic interference (EMI). The EMI attenuation is largely achieved through input-side EMI filters, which reduce the power density and increase cost. The frequency dithering technique (FDT) is widely used to reduce filter size. However, the existing FDTs do not consider the resolution bandwidth (RBW) of 9 kHz mandated by international standards. Additionally, the practicability of filter size reduction has not been validated. This article proposes a nonuniform FDT with 15 switching frequencies, each with a 1 kHz frequency step, ranging from 32 to 46 kHz. The persisting time of each switching frequency is adjusted to maximize the EMI attenuation with a lower frequency variation range. The persistence of switching frequencies within the dithering time is made nonuniform, considering the effect of a 9 kHz RBW, sidebands arising from FDT, and the noise floor, which have been largely neglected in the literature. Additionally, this article validates the achieved filter size reduction through the proposed FDT. The proposed nonuniform FDT achieves an EMI attenuation of as high as 10 dB compared to single-frequency operation, resulting in a significant filter size reduction of $\mathbf{58\%}$ in volume. The proposed technique is experimentally validated on a 1 kW SiC-MOSFET-based DC–DC converter prototype.
items.venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)

items.title: A Multifunctional 28-nm 4-Kb 9T1C SRAM-CIM Macro With Bidirectional Read/Write, Full-Array Self-Cycling Boolean Logic, and MAC Operation
items.abstract: This article presents a 28-nm 4-Kb 9T1C SRAM-CIM macro that unifies bidirectional read/write, full-array self-cycling Boolean logic operations, and charge-domain multiply–accumulate (MAC) operation within a compact bit-cell structure. The proposed cell supports both row- and column-wise access, where the row-wise read path effectively suppresses read disturbance and improves read stability. In addition, and, or, and IMP operations are executed directly in memory through a self-cycling mechanism, while MAC operation is realized by charge-domain accumulation using the embedded capacitor. Simulation results show that the proposed cell maintains stable data-holding capability under different temperatures and process corners, and the row-wise RSNM is significantly higher than that of column-wise read and conventional 6T read. The proposed Boolean logic operations exhibit stable energy behavior under process and voltage variations, and 2000 Monte Carlo simulations verify 100% correctness for representative cases. The MAC outputs also show near-linear behavior, with the absolute INL within 0.026–0.08 LSB, and stable output distributions under process variation. The proposed macro achieves logic energy as low as 1.218 fJ/bit, Boolean logic energy efficiency of 821 TOPS/W, and Boolean logic throughput of 1024 GOPS/Kb, while the MAC throughput reaches 1170.3 GOPS with an energy efficiency of 696–1323.5 TOPS/W. These results indicate that the proposed design provides a compact and efficient multifunctional SRAM-CIM solution for both logic-centric and MAC-oriented applications.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (vlsi) Systems

items.title: A Low-Dark-Current 4H-SiC MOS UV Photodetector With a Charge-Trapping Gate Stack by Electric Field Modulation Operation
items.abstract: A 4H-SiC metal–oxide–semiconductor ultraviolet photodetector featuring an Al 2 O 3 /AlO ${}_{x}$ /SiO 2 charge-trapping gate stack is demonstrated for highly sensitive ultraviolet intensity monitoring. A high-quality SiO 2 /SiC interface formed by intermittent spray hydrated oxidation suppresses interface defects, resulting in an ultralow dark current density ( ${3}.{96} \times {10}^{-{10}}~\text {A}/ {cm}^{{2}}$ ) under a reverse bias of -5 V. Subsequently, the upper gate dielectric layers are fabricated using thermal evaporation followed by a multi-step anodic oxidation process. Under ultraviolet illumination, photogenerated holes tunnel through the ultrathin SiO 2 layer and are stored in the oxygen-deficient AlO ${}_{x}$ layer, where the accumulated positive charges redistribute the internal oxide electric field. The continuously increasing oxide field drives a carrier transport transition from Poole–Frenkel emission to Fowler–Nordheim tunneling. The device achieves a photo-to-dark current ratio of ${8}.{0} \times {10}^{{4}}$ at an ultraviolet power density of 400 W/m 2 and exhibits excellent linearity with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) exceeding 0.997. These results demonstrate a highly promising electric-field-modulation approach for robust charge-trapping-assisted ultraviolet sensing and precision intensity monitoring applications.

items.title: A High-Reliability and High-Performance Nonvolatile Magnetic Radiation-Hardened Latch Based on Approximate C-Elements
items.abstract: With the continuous advancement of transistor manufacturing processes, soft errors induced by space radiation particles have become a critical challenge in digital circuit design. This paper proposes a fully double node upset (DNU) tolerant nonvolatile magnetic (FDNUT-NVM) latch by using magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) and CMOS. DNU tolerance is provided by six cross-coupled PMOS dual-input approximate C-elements (PDACs) and a clock-gated three-input standard C-element (CG-TSC). Compared to the dual-input standard C-element (DSC), the PDAC reduces the number of transistors in the discharge path, thereby improving the speed and increasing the differential current. Furthermore, we propose an improved backup and restore module with higher reliability and lower power consumption than prior design. The proposed FDNUT-NVM latch achieves an optimal trade-off between speed and power consumption while maintaining high reliability. Using a physics-based STT-MTJ compact model and a commercial 40 nm CMOS design kit for simulations, the results show that under a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 150% and a supply voltage of 1.2 V, the proposed FDNUT-NVM latch achieves a D-OUT delay of only 7.59 ps, a restore delay of 85.92 ps and a total power consumption of only $50.48 \;\mu \mathrm {W}$ . Monte Carlo simulations further reveal that the error rate of restoration (ERR) from MTJs is as low as 0.7%. Moreover, the proposed FDNUT-NVM latch can fully tolerate DNU even in the worst case with a deposited charge $Q_{\text {inj}}$ of $\pm 2 \;{\text {pC}}$ .
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A High-Linearity Hybrid-Domain SRAM-CIM Macro With Wide-Margin Voltage-to-Time Interface and Process-Adaptive TDC
items.abstract: SRAM-based computing-in-memory (SRAM-CIM) alleviates the memory-wall bottleneck of the von Neumann architecture, enabling energy-efficient AI edge computing. Current-domain CIM schemes suffer from degraded linearity at low supply voltages, whereas time-domain CIM schemes are highly sensitive to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations. This paper presents a hybrid-domain SRAM-CIM macro featuring enhanced linearity and process-adaptive quantization. Specifically, a current mirror discharge and inverting Schmitt trigger (CMD-IS) module converts bit-line voltage-signals into time-signals, alleviating discharge nonlinearity while ensuring a uniform slew rate. Additionally, guided by statistical analysis of the column-wise multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) value probability distribution, a resolution-tunable stepwise-encoded time-to-digital converter (RTSE TDC) reduces quantization overhead, while a process corner detection and delay regulation (PDDR) module adaptively calibrates TDC quantization steps to compensate for process corner variations. Implemented in 28 nm CMOS technology, the macro achieves peak energy efficiencies of 29.88 TOPS/W and 36.88 TOPS/W in signed and unsigned CIM modes, respectively, with area efficiencies of 6.00 TOPS/mm2 and 5.88 TOPS/mm2. For the ResNet-20@CIFAR-10 and ResNet-20@CIFAR-100 datasets, the macro achieves inference accuracies of 91.33% and 67.43%.

items.title: A High-Efficiency Doherty Power Amplifier with Enhanced Back-Off Performance
items.abstract: This paper presents a high-efficiency asymmetric Doherty power amplifier (DPA) designed for sub-6 GHz 5G n78 applications with extended output power back-off (OBO) capability. The proposed amplifier achieves improved efficiency across the Doherty region, particularly at mid-level back-off, by incorporating a three-state matching technique to better control the load modulation across the entire back-off region. The design is implemented using commercially available 10-W and 30-W GaN HEMT devices. Experimental results demonstrate that the fabricated DPA achieves a drain efficiency exceeding 45% at 9.5dB OBO over the 3.3–3.8 GHz frequency band. At saturation, the amplifier delivers an output power of 46–47.3 dBm with a peak drain efficiency ranging from 60.5% to 68.5%. These results confirm that the proposed DPA provides an effective solution for achieving high efficiency over a wide back-off range in next-generation 5G base station applications.

items.title: A High-Density RRAM Memory Architecture With IO-Assisted-Core-Transistor 1T1R Array and Two-Level Encoding for Edge AI Models
items.abstract: The deployment of AI on edge devices requires high-capacity on-chip memory to mitigate the performance and energy overhead of frequent off-chip data movement. Resistive random access memory (RRAM) has emerged as a promising candidate owing to its nonvolatility, high storage density, and low read cost. However, its adoption faces several challenges, including reliability concerns at high density, insufficient scalability for increasingly large AI models, and lower access frequency compared to CMOS-based units. In this work, we present a high-density and reliable RRAM memory architecture enabled by algorithm–hardware co-design. On the hardware side, a 1T1R array leveraging small core-voltage transistors for density and peripheral IO transistors for program reliability is introduced, together with a 16-step tunable current source for robust readout. On the algorithm side, a two-level encoding scheme is proposed to compress AI model storage with low implementation cost, while a burst-mode read strategy alleviates the frequency disparity with CMOS processors. Our experiments show a storage density of 17.4 MB/mm 2 @ 28 nm, with $1.23\times $ to $4.15\times $ compression rate, $4.99\times $ read-out energy reduction compared to SRAM baseline, and $4\times $ higher read frequency. System-level evaluation further confirms the performance and efficiency improvements of the proposed design.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems

items.title: A Fast Characterization Methodology of Multicorner Thermal Library for Thermal Signoff
items.abstract: As the thermal issue in integrated chips becomes increasingly severe, thermal sign-off and thermal management become more important for performance and reliability. Thermal libraries provide an offline approach to avoid time-consuming real-time thermal simulations. However, thermal library characterization under multicorner scenarios for thermal sign-off is a computationally expensive task. This work decouples the thermal resistance of a standard cell into two components: the thermal critical transistors that dominate heat generation and dissipation, which are corner-invariant and determined by the cell topology, and the transistor thermal resistances, which are corner-dependent. Based on this insight, we propose a fast multicorner thermal library characterization methodology, which significantly enhances efficiency through the reuse of thermal-critical transistor information. The characterized thermal library can be seamlessly integrated into mature electronic design automation (EDA) toolchains, enabling rapid full-chip, standard cell-level thermal assessment in both steady-state and transient conditions, while accounting for thermal coupling and thermal relaxation effects. The proposed methodology reduces the thermal library characterization time for multicorner thermal libraries from several weeks to 1 h. The accuracy of the proposed thermal assessment methodology has been validated through finite element simulation, and its full-chip thermal evaluation speed is 3.8 times faster than HotSpot.

items.title: A Dual-Slope Adaptive Feedback Strategy for Dynamic Voltage Balancing of Series-Connected SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Silicon carbide metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (SiC MOSFETs) can enhance the voltage withstand capability when operated in series. However, dynamic voltage imbalance caused by mismatches in parasitic parameters of devices or circuits is an inherent issue in series operation, which significantly degrades the service life of series-connected devices. Existing active schemes suffer from either a long voltage balancing period or a significant degradation of the inherent fast switching speed of SiC MOSFETs. In contrast, existing passive schemes are plagued by either considerable energy loss introduction or complex structures that are difficult to implement. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel passive voltage balancing strategy for dual-slope drain-source voltage (vds) of SiC MOSFETs. By employing simple components to enforce equal vds slew rates and controlling the circuit’s operation time, the proposed scheme minimizes the impact on switching speed as much as possible while achieving effective voltage balancing. Comparisons with the conventional gate drive (CGD) through experiments and with the existing best active scheme have verified that the proposed method can effectively achieve dual-slope vds driving and significantly reduce the impact of the voltage balancing circuit on switching speed (restricting the turn-off time to ∼120 ns compared to the ∼80 ns baseline, substantially outperforming the ∼300 ns required by the benchmark active scheme).
items.venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)

items.title: A Defect-Detection Graph-Based Methodology for Cell-Aware Model Generation
items.abstract: As modern integrated circuits (ICs) incorporate increasingly smaller transistors, the occurrence of manufacturing defects within standard cells (intracell defects) has risen. Detecting and localizing these defects is essential for ensuring a rapid yield ramp-up and maintaining a low-test escape rate. To address intracell defects, cell-aware (CA) methodology was introduced, but it relies on time-consuming analog SPICE simulations for standard cell characterization. This article introduces transistor undetectable defect eliminator (TrUnDeL), a graph-based methodology designed to expedite the CA model generation process. TrUnDeL identifies undetectable (UD) defects for each stimulus applied to cell inputs, excluding them from required analog simulations. TrUnDeL was tested on two FD-SOI standard cell libraries (P28 and C28) from STMicroelectronics. The results show that, for combinational cells, the CA model generation process time was reduced by a factor of three compared to standard analog-based methods without compromising accuracy. To efficiently address sequential cells, modifications to the classical TrUnDeL flow were implemented, resulting in a 30% reduction in CA model generation time for sequential cells, again without compromising accuracy. TrUnDeL was also tested on a $4\times 4$ SRAM case study, maintaining accuracy across all memory modules. Finally, this article introduces Layout-TrUnDeL (La-TrUnDeL) for addressing layout defects, proving effective on 8 test-case cells without misclassification.
