items.title: A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling
items.abstract: Accurate thermal analysis of heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC packages is essential yet computationally prohibitive. A single full-package FEM simulation can take hours, while AI-based surrogates treat the entire stack as a monolithic prediction target and must be retrained whenever the die count or topology changes. To address this limitation, this work proposes Domain-Decomposed AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for Thermal Analysis (DAIST), a composable thermal solver that decomposes the global package simulation into block-level subdomain problems, replaces subdomain solvers with neural operators, and couples them through iterative exchanges of interfacial temperature and heat flux. This local-to-global architecture eliminates the topology lock-in of monolithic models: block-level neural operators can be directly reused in unseen package assemblies without retraining. The iterative coupling strategy further provides a controllable accuracy-runtime tradeoff, where the iteration budget can be adjusted to trade accuracy for runtime. Evaluated on a multi-chiplet system and an advanced packaging system, DAIST achieves up to $178\times$ speedup over traditional FEM solvers with mean temperature errors of 0.068% and 0.323%, respectively, while demonstrating cross-topology reuse of block-level models across structurally distinct package assemblies.

items.title: A Chip-Package Multilevel Coupled Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Modeling for SiC MOSFETs and Package-Level Avalanche Ruggedness Enhancement
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) mosfets face critical challenges in avalanche ruggedness under repetitive low-energy stresses, yet the underlying failure mechanisms and reinforcement strategies remain underexplored. This study investigates the degradation of a 1200 V/40 mΩ planar-gate SiC mosfet through stepped single-pulse and multipulse unclamped inductive switching (UIS) tests. Experimental results demonstrate a 20.18 mΩ increase in on-resistance (Rdson) after 30 000 repetitive avalanche cycles, attributed primarily to bond wire aging and solder delamination. A chip-package multilevel coupled electro-thermo-mechanical model is developed, bridging carrier dynamics and package-level electro-thermo-mechanical coupled stress. The calibrated model reproduces the electrical characteristics and transient thermal response (<1.5% error) of the real device. Simulations highlight that localized electric fields exceeding 15 MV/m at bond pads and cyclic thermo-mechanical strain accelerate package-level degradation. Guided by these findings, two reinforcement strategies—increased bond-pad contact area and higher wire count—are proposed. Experimental validation over 50 000 UIS cycles demonstrates reductions in ${{R}_{\rm dson}}$ degradation of 30.1% and 36.4%, respectively, prolonging predicted fatigue life from 16 000 to 24 000 cycles. The combined experimental–simulation framework offers a scalable design methodology for extending the avalanche safe-operating area of SiC mosfets without compromising static performance.

items.title: A Cascade-Breakdown Model for Heavy-Ion-Induced Oxide Failure Mechanisms in 4H-SiC Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (MOS) Capacitors
items.abstract: Single-event gate rupture (SEGR) remains a critical limitation for deploying silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs in space environments, due to the comparatively poor oxide quality and a limited process window for forming a robust, defect-lean dielectric on SiC bulk. This article systematically investigates the mechanism of heavy-ion-induced oxide breakdown in 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) capacitors. Conventional physics-based analyses of oxide breakdown typically rely on peak electric field criteria at a single point. To overcome this limitation and elucidate the local gate-oxide breakdown physics relevant to SEGR in SiC MOSFETs, we propose a novel cascade breakdown model comprising four sequential stages: electric field distortion induced by residual hole accumulation (Stage I), oxide thinning triggered by localized breakdown (Stage II), a reduction of the effective oxide thickness coupled with electric field superposition (Stage III), and ultimately, electric field runaway leading to the cascade breakdown behavior (Stage IV). An analytical expression for the peak electric field in the oxide during the thinning process is derived, yielding a refined SEGR failure criterion. In particular, by comparing the minimum peak electric field during oxide thinning with the intrinsic breakdown field, the recombination coefficient $\alpha $ was calibrated to be $3 \times 10 ^{-6}$ cm3/s. Furthermore, by incorporating energy deposition fluctuations into the proposed model, it is demonstrated that the calculated failure probability distribution of breakdown voltages agrees remarkably well with the experimental results obtained under Ta and Kr ion irradiation. Collectively, these findings deepen the microscopic understanding of the evolutionary mechanism of SEGR, providing critical insights for the radiation-hardened SiC MOS devices.

items.title: A 915-MHz 1-kW High-Efficiency Continuous-Mode GaN Power Amplifier with In-Package Matching and Diamond-Copper Heat Dissipation
items.abstract: This paper presents a 915-MHz 1-kW high-efficiency gallium nitride (GaN) power amplifier (PA) for industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band applications. Fulllink optimization is implemented from 40-mm gate-width GaN HEMT die design, input harmonic-controlled, in-package matching, diamond-copper high-thermal-dissipation packaging, to PCB circuit and water-cooled structure design. The fabricated PA achieves 1100 W saturated output power with 80% peak drain efficiency (DE) and 22 dB linear gain under continuous wave (CW) condition, and 1240 W saturated output power with 83% peak DE under 10% pulse condition. The proposed PA shows superior comprehensive performance over state-of-the-art works.

items.title: A 6T--11T In-Memory Computing Architecture for Near-Sensor Pipelined Binary Neural Network
items.abstract: This brief presents the fabrication and experimental validation of an interlaced 6T-11T CMOS in-memory computing circuit designed for low-silicon-area pipelined binary neural networks. The circuit implements a weight-stationary architecture in which input activation values are sequentially stored in 6T SRAM columns, while 11T cells retain the convolution weights and perform binary XNOR-based multiply-and-accumulate operations, naturally aligning with the column-parallel readout topology of CMOS image sensors. The circuit has been fabricated in a 180 nm standard CMOS process and experimentally characterized. Measured results on a binary convolutional layer demonstrate operation at 1 MHz with a simulation-assisted energy efficiency of 18.53 TOPS/W. The interlaced organization embeds the line-buffer functionality required for streamed convolution within the IMC array itself, so that image rows are processed as they are read out from the sensor.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems - II - Express Briefs

items.title: A 492.8-TOPS/W STT-MRAM Sparsity-Adaptive Compute-in-Memory Macro for Edge AI Inference
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of intelligent sensors has led to increased latency and privacy risks when processing data on a remote server. This work proposes a spin-transfer torque magnetic random access memory (STT-MRAM) compute-in-memory (CIM) macro to enhance inference efficiency for an artificial intelligence (AI) model on the edge device. A sparsity-adaptive design is presented, featuring coupled-1T1M (c-1T1M) computing cells to eliminate bit-level activation computing power overhead and suppress pattern-dependent deviations in the result. An activation-aware voltage comparator array (AA-VCA) reduces power consumption by up to $56{\times }$ and improves sensing margin by $13{\times }$ . At the system level, a hybrid-granularity sparsity workflow accelerates inference and aligns well with compact analog CIM architectures. In addition, a hardware-implemented variational autoencoder (VAE) is deployed to enhance processing capabilities. The test chip is fabricated in 28-nm CMOS with 60-nm MTJ, achieving energy efficiencies of 712 TOPS/W for image classification and 492.8 TOPS/W for anomaly detection, along with an accuracy of 96.3% and an $F1$ score of 0.97.

items.title: A 40 %-PAE Power Amplifier with 2.35 W/mm 2 power density for Ka-Band SATCOM in 55 nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
items.abstract: This paper presents a two-stacked Ka-band neutralized power amplifier (PA) using a 55 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. This PA achieves a maximum output power (Pout) of 24.9 dBm and a maximum power added efficiency (PAE) of 40 % at 19 GHz, with a –3 dB bandwidth of 34 % and a state-of-the-art power density of 2.35 W/mm2. This paper presents the different design techniques used to improve overall performance and details a theoretical approach for interstage matching regarding stacked neutralized transistors.

items.title: A 4-W 38 GHz High Efficiency Power Amplifier Using 0.12 μm GaN HEMT Technology
items.abstract: The proposed Ka-band power amplifier is implemented using WIN’s 0.12-μm GaN HEMT process. It adopts a two-stage common-source configuration with a two-way power-combining architecture. The power stage is biased in class-A to improve large signal linearity, while the driver stage employs class-AB biasing to reduce DC consumption. Transmission-line and capacitor-based matching networks are employed to realize a compact layout. The measurement results show that the amplifier achieves a maximum small-signal gain of 20.7 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth extending from 36.5 to 40 GHz. Under large-signal conditions, the circuit delivers a saturated output power of 36.2 dBm with a power-added efficiency of 31.3% at 38 GHz, and a measured two-tone OIP3 of approximately 44 dBm. The total chip area is 5 mm2.

items.title: A 3-D Stackable 1T2C DRAM With Sidewall Storage Capacitors for High-Density Memory
items.abstract: This work proposes a 3D Stackable 1T2C DRAM architecture for high-density memory applications. Unlike conventional 1T1C DRAM with large lateral storage capacitors, the proposed structure integrates capacitors along the sidewalls of the vertically stacked cells. The device is implemented with a NAND-like process flow based on alternating metal/insulator stacks, lateral replacement, and a vertical common bit-line connection, enabling compact multilayer integration. An amorphous oxide semiconductor channel is employed to suppress off-state leakage. TCAD simulations verify the write, hold, and read operations of the proposed cell. A bit-line sensing margin exceeding 350 mV and retention time exceeding 100 s is obtained with a bit-line load capacitance of 10 fF. In addition, a two-layer stacked cell simulation demonstrates independent write and read operations without observable crosstalk. With hexagonal close packing, the projected storage density can reach 0.024 Gb/mm2 per layer. These results indicate that the proposed 3D 1T2C DRAM is a promising candidate for high-density memory.

items.title: A 28-nm Versatile TinyML SoC With Flexible Hetero-Fabric Dataflow Orchestration and Compute/Storage-Density-Adjustable CIM
items.abstract: Tiny machine learning (tinyML) brings machine intelligence to numerous extreme edge scenarios under battery-powered and always-on constraints, which imposes demands on tinyML processors for ultra-low power and versatile support for diverse applications and tinyML models. A heterogeneous-computing-fabric (hetero-fabric) architecture that incorporates compute-in-memory (CIM) core and multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit-based digital core (Dcore) can combine high energy efficiency and flexibility to meet such demands. However, the dataflow flexibility in the hetero-fabric architectures has not been well explored. Besides, previous CIM macros are limited by the inherently fixed compute-storage ratio, facing the dilemma of balancing compute and storage density requirements from shallow to deep layers in neural network models. This work presents a versatile tinyML SoC for diverse extreme edge ML tasks. Firstly, we propose a tightly-coupled hetero-fabric architecture for tinyML processing, where the CIM core (Ccore) and Dcore are tightly coupled through the reconfigurable data-streaming network (RDSN). Flexible inter-/intra-core dataflow orchestration for various tinyML models with reduced L1 memory access is further proposed. We also propose a layer-wise dynamic frequency scaling (DFS) scheme for hetero-fabric performance balance with adjustable inter-core clock frequency ratios. Further energy savings can be achieved when combined with dynamic voltage scaling (DVS). Besides, we propose a three-mode reconfigurable-LUT (R-LUT) CIM macro, which breaks the inherent compute-storage limitations and enables dynamically adjustable compute and storage density. A compact Twin-10T SRAM cell featuring lower read power is also proposed to construct the LUT array. Finally, we design a flexible Dcore featuring intra-core fine-grained workload partition and elaborate scheduling to coordinate with the Ccore for dataflow orchestration. The fabricated 28nm chip achieves $2.14\times $ higher SoC energy efficiency than state-of-the-art CIM-based tinyML SoC. It supports all MLPerf Tiny tasks, achieving practical performance (e.g., no less than 30 fps) with no more than 0.5mW power.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 28-nm Soft Error Tolerant SRAM With Design-Layout Co-Optimized 14T Cell and Double Mode Redundant Peripheral Circuit for Space Application
items.abstract: This work presents a radiation-hardened 28 nm SRAM with Design-Layout Co-Optimized 14T cell (DLCO-14T) and double mode redundant peripheral circuit for space applications. The proposed architecture exhibits strong resilience to single-event effects (SEE), withstanding laser irradiation at a linear energy transfer (LET) of up to 60 MeV $\cdot $ cm2/mg. The memory cell achieves a normalized critical path distance (NCPD) of 67%, approximately twice that of conventional rad-hard designs. By integrating a dual-mode decoding strategy, dual-port cell configuration, and a DICE-latched sense amplifier (DL-SA), the SRAM remains functional at operating frequencies above 500 MHz under radiation. A mixed-mode redundancy (MMR) delay chain in the sense amplifier control circuitry achieves single-event transient (SET) immunity with an area overhead of 140%. Experiment results confirm no failure at laser injecting at hardened zone and an 87.9% soft error rate reduction at laser injecting at non-hardened zone, demonstrating high reliability for space systems.
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems Part 1: Regular Papers

items.title: A 27-Gb/s/pin Inverter-Based Delay-Matched PAM-3 Transceiver With Pattern-Selective Switching Jitter Compensation for Die-to-Die Interfaces
items.abstract: This article presents a 27-Gb/s/pin inverter-based delay-matched three-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-3) transceiver for short-reach die-to-die (D2D) interfaces. The proposed design uses two parallel, identical offset-programmable transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) to independently generate two finely tunable PAM-3 reference levels with minimal parasitic loading, enabling multi-level signaling within a compact, energy-efficient inverter-based architecture. A pattern-selective switching-jitter compensation (PS-SWJC) technique is further proposed, which selectively removes switching jitter (SWJ) only at switching-jitter events, thereby recovering the horizontal margin that conventional SWJ compensation (SWJC) schemes cannot restore. Measurements show that the proposed PS-SWJC improves the horizontal margin from 0.25 to 0.41 UI (a 64% enhancement) and maintains a stable 0.31-UI margin even with 0.94-0.95-UI peak-to-peak recovered-clock jitter under 60-Hz, 10-MHz, and 100-MHz supply ripple, demonstrating strong robustness to power-supply-induced jitter (PSIJ). These features make the proposed architecture a robust solution for high-density, low-power chiplet and D2D interfaces. The prototype transceiver is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process and achieves an energy efficiency of 0.399 pJ/bit at the DQ channel and 0.55 pJ/bit including the forwarded clock channel at 27 Gb/s/pin.

items.title: A 10 W, 4–20 GHz SPDT Switch Using Stacked Transistors in a 100-nm GaN-on-SiC Technology
items.abstract: This paper presents a reflective-type wideband single-pole double-throw switch, implemented in a 100-nm GaN-on-SiC semiconductor technology. The design achieves a relative bandwidth of more than 130%, spanning over the frequency range from 4 to 20GHz. The measured ON-state insertion loss varies between 1.2dB and 1.7dB, the OFF-state isolation is better than 35dB. Stacked transistors are used for the series and shunt switch elements to enhance the linearity of the SPDT. The input-related P0.1dB compression point is measured above 34dBm over the entire frequency range. The input-related P1dB compression point is simulated to exceed 40dBm, thus offering power handling capabilities of the switch beyond 10W.

items.title: 4-Transistor IGZO Ternary Content Addressable Memory Enabling Large-Scale Array Integration for In-Memory Computing
items.abstract: We report a 4-transistor (4T) Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) that significantly reduces the physical footprint by employing dual-gate IGZO transistors. High-density TCAMs are essential components for memory augmented neural networks and advanced computing systems; however, the large physical footprint remains a significant limitation in conventional designs. The proposed TCAM unit cell adopts a simplified structure, reducing the transistor count to four, which is substantially lower than previous SRAM-based (16T) and oxide semiconductor-based (6T) counterparts. Moreover, connecting the search line directly to the gate electrode effectively mitigates IR drop, enhancing the design’s suitability for large-scale memory applications. Experimental results validate the proposed design, demonstrating accurate Hamming distance computations (155.9 nA/bit), high endurance ( $\gt$ $10^{{10}}$ cycles), and fast operation with 350 ps search latency and 220 ns write time.

items.title: 15 W/mm Output Power Density AlGaN–GaN HEMTs on the Epitaxy with Ultra Thin Buffer for X-Band Applications
items.abstract: This work demonstrates an ultra-thin-buffer (UTB) AlGaN/GaN HEMT epitaxy on 4H–SiC enabled by a strain-relaxed AlN nucleation layer and a carbon-rich high-resistivity GaN layer, eliminating the conventional micrometer-scale Fe-doped GaN buffer. Hall measurements indicate improved sheet transport, with a 2DEG density of 1.41 × 1013 cm−2 and a sheet resistance of 230 Ω/sq. DC and RF characterization was performed on fabricated 8×125 μm HEMTs with Lg = 0.25 μm. Relative to a standard Fe-doped baseline, the UTB devices achieve an approximately twofold increase in breakdown voltage, from 90–100 V to 180–190 V. Despite this improvement, only ~1 dB reduction in maximum available gain is observed over 8–12 GHz, while large-signal operation at VDS = 65 V delivers 15 W/mm output power density. These results indicate that the proposed UTB epitaxy provides a favorable breakdown–RF tradeoff with reduced buffer complexity.

items.title: Controlling Switching Evolution in Lead-Free Perovskite-Inspired Chalcogenide Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Memristors have emerged as key building blocks of neuromorphic computing architectures due to their ability to integrate data storage and processing. While metal halide perovskites have recently shown significant promise owing to their mixed electronic-ionic conduction and low-cost solution processability, their reliance on toxic lead and limited stability presents critical challenges. Here, we report environmentally friendly, low-toxicity AgBiS2-based solution-processable memristors exhibiting an ultra-low SET voltage of ~0.08 V and a high ON/OFF ratio of >104. First-principles calculations identify Ag interstitials as the energetically most favourable native defect and reveal low migration barriers within the Ag sublattice, for both interstitials and vacancies, facilitating ionic transport in the AgBiS2 lattice. Through interface and thickness engineering, the resistive switching behaviour can be systematically tuned from abrupt digital to gradual analog modes. Notably, thicker switching layers promote the evolution of stable conductive pathways through intermediate metastable states, revealing a controllable filament evolution process. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals pronounced negative capacitance (inductive) behaviour at low bias voltages, arising from coupled electronic-ionic dynamics. Consistent with this behaviour, pulse measurements demonstrate gradual conductance modulation under pulse trains, emulating synaptic responses relevant for neuromorphic computing. Finally, post-operando structural analysis reveals substantial morphological evolution of the switching layer driven by repeated filament formation and rupture. Linking structural dynamics to switching variability provides important design principles for achieving reliable and durable sustainable memristors.

items.title: Variability-Aware Memristor Circuit for Hierarchical Bayesian Temporal Sampling
items.abstract: Abstract Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) require hardware capable of storing and sampling probabilistic synaptic weights. While population coding exploits device-to-device (D2D) variability to encode weight distributions, temporal sampling instead requires controlled and reproducible stochastic fluctuations, making its hardware implementation particularly challenging. Here, we demonstrate a memristor-based temporal-coding circuit that combines three analog memristor devices per synaptic weight to encode its mean and standard deviation with an externally injected white-noise source for sample generation. A dedicated fluctuation-amplification stage provides controllable temporal stochasticity, while a hierarchical training algorithm explicitly models device-to-device variability and temporal noise to ensure robust Bayesian inference under hardware non-idealities. On the MIT-BIH arrhythmia classification task, the proposed approach achieves a 2.7-fold reduction in memory footprint compared with an equivalent population-coding implementation, while preserving Bayesian inference accuracy and uncertainty estimates.

items.title: Two‐Dimensional Flash Memory: Materials, Interfaces, and Storage–Computing Convergence
items.abstract: Flash memory remains the dominant nonvolatile storage technology, yet its continued scaling is increasingly constrained by the coupled requirements of fast programming, low operating energy, and long-term reliability. Recent advances in 2D materials and van der Waals heterostructures provide an opportunity not merely to miniaturize flash cells, but to reconfigure the charge-programming physics itself. In this Review, we introduce interface-controlled charge programming as a unifying framework for understanding and designing 2D flash memories. We discuss how atomically thin channels, clean van der Waals interfaces, engineered tunneling barriers, controllable trap states, and contact modulation regulate charge injection, transport, trapping, and confinement. This framework connects device-level metrics, including nanosecond-to-subnanosecond programming, low-energy operation, long retention, and high endurance, with emerging system-level functions such as multilevel storage, in-memory computing, sensing-memory-computing integration, and CMOS-compatible heterogeneous integration. We further identify critical challenges in wafer-scale synthesis, device variability, reliability benchmarking, and array-level implementation. By shifting flash memory design from bulk-field-driven tunneling to interface-programmed charge control, 2D materials may enable a new class of nonvolatile devices for storage-computing convergence beyond conventional silicon flash.

items.title: Top-down fabrication of TiN nanogap electrodes via lithographic patterning and plasma-assisted dimensional transfer
items.abstract: Controlled fabrication of titanium nitride nanogap electrodes is critical for advancing molecular, bio-, and hybrid nanoelectronic interfaces, where device performance depends strongly on interelectrode gap geometry. Despite recent advances, top-down fabrication of titanium nitride nanogap electrodes remains challenging because final nanogap dimensions result from coupled lithographic pattern definition and plasma-assisted dimensional transfer rather than lithographic resolution alone. This work investigates these effects using a two-stage fabrication approach for titanium nitride nanogap electrodes, including maskless photolithography and Cl 2 /Ar inductively coupled plasma reactive ion etching to define microscale electrodes, followed by high-resolution electron-beam lithography and a second etching step to define interelectrode nanogap spacing. Selected process conditions were varied across the fabrication sequence, and their effects on resulting nanogap geometry were evaluated using scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and electrical characterization. Results demonstrate that plasma chemistry can substantially influence nanogap dimensions during pattern transfer, with final nanogaps extending below nominal lithographic resist opening, yielding sub-lithographic nanogaps relative to the resist-pattern definition. Within the investigated electron-beam lithography stable transfer region (190–250 pC/cm), final nanogap dimensions are influenced predominantly by plasma-etching conditions. Under an Ar-rich Cl 2 /Ar (10/40 sccm, 290 s) plasma condition, transferred gaps were narrower than or comparable to corresponding resist openings, with the narrowest gaps observed measuring below 20 nm at the lowest electron-beam lithography dose tested (130 pC/cm). Structural and electrical characterization revealed a tapered nanogap profile and high interelectrode resistance ( ∼ G Ω cm). These results provide a potentially CMOS-compatible approach for sub-50 nm titanium nitride nanogap electrode fabrication.

items.title: Technical Bottlenecks and Process Optimization Pathways for AI Chip Wafer Manufacturing under Advanced Semiconductor Nodes
items.abstract: With the rapid growth of AI workloads, there is now a high demand for high-end node wafer manufacturing, and at the same time, better power efficiency and higher yield are required. Identify the main technical bottlenecks in AI chip wafer manufacturing at advanced semiconductor nodes and put forward feasible process optimisation paths based on manufacturing integration. AI chips are not only the result of new-generation architecture but also depend on factors such as lithography technology, device structure, defect management, interconnect reliability, process fluctuation and yield optimisation to some extent in their actual performance and economic feasibility. Based on the theory of classical scaling, research in semiconductor manufacturing and recent reports on advanced-node processes have shown that the main problem is how to align performance scaling with manufacturability. Optimisation strategies based on design-technology co-optimisation, critical-layer process control, yield-oriented defect management and adaptive fab collaboration are also proposed. Therefore, the construction of advanced-node AI chip manufacturing will require the parallel development of device structure, process integration and manufacturing governance in the semiconductor industry.
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Engineering and Technology Research

items.title: Strain-regulated deep trap engineering in polyethylene terephthalate electrets
items.abstract: Emerging technologies in sensing, filtration, and energy harvesting demand polymer electrets with highly stable and long-lasting electric fields. While most approaches improve charge stability by increasing trap density through heterogeneous structures, controlling trap depth through morphology engineering remains largely unexplored. Here, strain programming is employed to regulate trap depth in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) electrets. Uniaxial and sequential biaxial stretching induce chain orientation and strain-induced crystallization, producing increasingly oriented and constrained semicrystalline morphologies. Structural characterization confirms progressive increases in crystallinity and molecular orientation. Thermally stimulated depolarization current measurements show that the apparent activation energy for trapped charge release increases from 1.28 to 2.12 eV, accompanied by a shift of the depolarization peaks to higher temperatures. Surface-potential decay measurements further confirm a strong correlation between activation energy and long-term charge retention, with biaxially oriented PET exhibiting approximately threefold greater retained potential than weakly oriented PET after 3000 h. The results demonstrate that strain-induced changes in semicrystalline morphology strongly influence charge-trap energetics and are consistent with increased restriction of amorphous-chain mobility at crystalline-amorphous interfaces. These findings identify strain programming as an effective and scalable approach for intrinsic deep trap engineering in polymer electrets.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics

items.title: Source Code for Machine Learning Framework for Threshold Voltage Prediction and Design Optimization of Ground Select Transistor in Vertical Channel 3D NAND Flash Memory
items.abstract: This repository contains the dataset and Python code supporting the manuscript above (submitted to Scientific Reports). It includes: (1) the 768-point dataset of GST threshold voltage (VT) values digitized and reconstructed from published TCAD simulation results, along with raw digitized-curve data and the merge script for three of the seven source figures; (2) a data-cleaning and resampling pipeline (binning, Savitzky-Golay smoothing, cubic-spline interpolation); (3) feature-engineering and model-training code for Gradient Boosting and XGBoost regressors using a physics-informed 11-term feature vector derived from a Two-MOSFET analytical model of the device; (4) SHAP feature-importance analysis; and (5) figure-generation scripts for the learning-curve and partial-dependence plots reported in the paper. A README documents how to run each script and reproduce the paper's results, along with known reproducibility caveats.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Quantum Materials Defect Detection and Characterization System
items.abstract: Abstract: Quantum-materials inspection requires reliable identification of atomistic and mesoscale defects from observations that are noisy, heterogeneous and often only indirectly connected to structure. This monograph develops a coherent design for a defect detection and characterization system integrating spectroscopy, microscopy, physically informed inverse problems, statistical uncertainty, graph-based learning, hybrid quantum–classical signal analysis and reproducible industrial data engineering. The proposed research architecture treats defect identity, charge state, geometry and functional consequence as distinct inferential targets. It specifies experimental controls, cross-instrument calibration, causal process–structure analysis, selective prediction and active measurement policies. An end-to-end implementation is developed from specimen provenance and synchronized acquisition through constrained reconstruction, validation, release gating and governance. Ten research themes synthesize a screened reference corpus, while five chapters translate the themes into testable models, protocols, engineering artifacts and sector-oriented applications. Five original schematics and five comparison tables organize the analytical workflow. The concluding design offers illustrative system and method claim concepts, together with a prior-art and enablement checklist; no legal conclusion of patentability is implied. The resulting framework supports laboratories and industrial users seeking interpretable, calibrated and scalable characterization rather than unqualified automated labels. Keywords quantum materials, point defects, crystal disorder, vacancy, dislocation, photoluminescence, Raman spectroscopy, spin resonance, hyperspectral microscopy, defect ontology, Bayesian inference, inverse problems, causal identification, uncertainty quantification, graph neural networks, persistent homology, physics-informed learning, quantum machine learning, calibration, multimodal fusion, digital twins, MLOps, semiconductor metrology

items.title: Process Technologies and Device Applications of Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD)-Based Two-Dimensional Semiconductors: A Review
items.abstract: With the continuous miniaturization of semiconductor devices, the limitations of conventional Si-based devices—including short-channel effects, increased leakage current, and elevated power consumption—have become more pronounced, drawing increasing attention to atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors as candidate channel materials for next-generation devices. Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) exhibit electronic and optical properties that vary with layer number; in particular, monolayer MoS2 possesses a direct bandgap and excellent electrostatic gate control, making it a promising material for ultrascaled transistors and optoelectronic devices. In this review, we examine the structural and electrical properties of TMDs, focusing on phase engineering for crystal-phase control, semimetal electrodes, and van der Waals contacts for reducing contact resistance at metal/TMD interfaces. We further analyze wafer-scale TMD growth via chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and metal–organic CVD (MOCVD), as well as recent progress in epitaxial growth for controlling grain boundaries and growth orientation. From a device perspective, we review TMD transistors with 1 nm and sub-1 nm physical gate lengths and discuss their extension toward high-frequency devices and three-dimensional integration. These findings demonstrate that TMDs are promising channel materials capable of overcoming the scaling limitations of conventional Si-based semiconductors; however, challenges remain for practical implementation, including large-area material uniformity, contact resistance, defect and interface control, process reproducibility, and compatibility with existing CMOS processes.

items.title: Photonic-computing error correction through optical encoder and decoder calibrations
items.abstract: Photonic processors have emerged as an attractive platform for fast and energy-efficient matrix-vector multiplication. However, they are susceptible to error due to their analog nature. Here, we present an error-correction technique that implements a correction offset to the optical en-/decoders of photonic processors. Our proposed method is general-purpose, does not require introducing any additional components to the photonic network, and can address errors stemming from unbalanced losses, 50/50 beamsplitter deviations, digital-to-analog conversion inaccuracies, and any unknown sources. In particular, we show that our method is highly effective in mitigating unbalanced-loss errors, a problem that has not previously been addressed by any error-correction technique. Using this approach, we achieve over 90% error reduction in large triangular meshes, overcoming a key obstacle to highly accurate photonic processors for information processing.

items.title: Performance Analysis of Arduino DHT11 Sensor Libraries for Resource-constrained IoT/WoT Edge Nodes.
items.abstract: Efficient sensing remains critical in low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) and Web of Things (WoT)-enabled edge nodes, even when the sensor itself is inexpensive and widely used. The DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor employs a single-wire digital protocol and relies on Arduino libraries for data acquisition, timeout handling, and scheduling behavior. In this paper, eight Arduino DHT11 libraries are benchmarked on an Arduino Uno R3 using six criteria: flash memory usage, SRAM consumption, average measured call duration, timing variability, maximum CPU blocking time, and failure-recovery behavior. The results reveal substantial performance trade-offs. Average measured call durations ranged from 5,588 µs for the asynchronous DHT Sensors Non-Blocking implementation to approximately 1.04 s for DHT11; however, these measurements reflect different execution semantics and should not be interpreted as directly equivalent end-to-end acquisition latencies. Flash usage ranged from 4,288 to 5,244 bytes, while SRAM consumption ranged from 238 to 266 bytes. TroykaDHT and SDHT delivered the most stable low-latency readings, DFRobot_DHT11 minimized SRAM usage, and DHT Sensors Non-Blocking was most suitable when asynchronous execution and reduced continuous CPU occupation were required. This study does not directly benchmark application-layer protocols or cloud services, such as HTTP, MQTT, REST, or WebSocket; instead, it characterizes sensing-layer behavior that can influence data freshness, task scheduling, and overall responsiveness in re-source-constrained IoT/WoT edge deployments.
items.venue: Zanin Journal of Science and Engineering

items.title: Patent Infringement Liability and Countermeasures in Chiplet-Based Heterogeneous Integration Structures
items.abstract: Chiplet integration combines functional dies through advanced packaging by separate design, fabrication, and assembly firms. It challenges patent rules built for a single actor’s complete practice. A semi-finished product made in Korea directly infringes only if final processing is minor and the product realizes the invention. Chiplet cases thus depend on when claimed features arise. The 2025 addition of “export” to Article 127 raises indirect-infringement issues for products dedicated to overseas completion. If it removes the double domestic nexus requirement, dedicated use becomes central, although open-standard compatibility alone should not defeat it. Multi-tier outsourcing also requires claim-specific analysis of exhaustion, intermediate-product embodiment, and whether later packaging practices another patented invention. This article proposes functional divided-practice liability, a dedicated-use test for standard parts, and IP-contract guidance on ‘manufacturing and packaging licensing’ and KGD data.

items.title: OBIRCH Hotspot Detection via MH-to-WL Biasing for 3D NAND Memory Hole Defect Isolation
items.abstract: Abstract In Flash semiconductor technology, NAND-type 3D Flash memory continues to stack up more Word-Line (WL) layers e.g. 2XX for 8th and 9th generation 3D NAND. The complexity of interconnect structures and the density of metal layers have increased dramatically. This evolution introduces new failure modes that are difficult to detect and isolate using conventional techniques. This paper presents a novel biasing approach that enhances OBIRCH sensitivity by targeting Memory Hole (MH)-to-WL interaction. Experimental results on advanced NAND-type 3D Flash memory devices demonstrate that this technique enables repeatable hotspot detection after destructive sample preparation. The finding established a robust and novel solution for detecting MH defects in highly scaled memory technologies.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Nonvolatile Ferroelectric Control of Diffusive Spin Transport at Room Temperature in Graphene/CuInP 2 S 6 Heterostructures
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonvolatile electric control of spin transport is important for low‐power spintronic applications, but remains challenging to realize. While prior work has highlighted the significance of ferroelectric control in spintronics—primarily through magnetoelectric switching, spin–charge conversion, or spin‐dependent tunnelling—direct nonvolatile control of the diffusive spin current itself at room temperature has not been demonstrated. Here, we demonstrate a graphene lateral spin valve incorporating a van der Waals ferroelectric top gate, CuInP 2 S 6 , that enables bistable, nonvolatile modulation of diffusive spin transport at 300 K. At an identical applied gate bias, opposite ferroelectric polarization states produce distinct spin signals, demonstrating retained‐state control beyond ordinary electrostatic gating, and yielding a maximum modulation exceeding 100% under optimized operating conditions. Hanle spin‐precession measurements further reveal distinct effective spin‐transport states for the two remanent ferroelectric states, consistent with nonvolatile ferroelectric modulation of spin transport. These results highlight a promising route toward room‐temperature, nonvolatile electrical control of spin transport by using van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Non-Markovian dissipation as a resource for quantum reservoir computing
items.abstract: The control of open-system dynamics provides a powerful mechanism for using quantum information to process sequential tasks. While quantum reservoir computing typically relies on Markovian dissipation to process sequential data, the computational role of non-Markovian memory effects remains largely unexplored. We introduce a framework for quantum reservoir computing where non-Markovianity is explicitly modeled and regulated using fractional derivatives. By employing fractional time subordination, we generate tunable, heavy-tailed relaxation dynamics that govern the information backflow between the system and its environment. Non-Markovian information backflow regulates the overall temporal retention of the system, maximizing short-term linear memory capacity. Within an optimal operating regime, fractional non-Markovianity redistributes the reservoir memory towards recent inputs, improving both linear memory capacity and nonlinear prediction accuracy at short delays, at the expense of long-range temporal retention. System-environment interaction proves being not merely a requirement for quantum reservoir computing, but an active resource that embeds memory retention directly into the quantum evolution.

items.title: Noise-aware fine-tuning as a hardware noise margin: Cross-layer co-design for robust low bit RRAM in-memory computing toward space-borne edge inference
items.abstract: Resistive Random Access Memory (RRAM)-based Computing in-memory (CIM) accelerators promise orders of magnitude energy savings for space-borne edge inference. At the low bit precision imposed by tight power budgets, however, device-level conductance noise competes directly with the quantization signal margin. While conventional Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) can adapt neural networks to low bit hardware, it remains insufficient against physical conductance fluctuations, often leading to severe accuracy degradation in regression tasks. We therefore introduce noise-aware fine-tuning as a cross-layer robustness primitive, a three-stage pipeline (PQAT-FT) in which sparse regularization and noise injection reshape the weight distribution to carve unused conductance headroom, interrupting layer-by-layer error propagation. Measured on a fabricated 8K RRAM CIM test chip over five programming rounds (mean +/- SD), PQAT-FT consistently reduces the 4-bit inference error across both bounded and unbounded activations, lowering the RMSE for Tanh, Sigmoid, Leaky ReLU, and ReLU by 64.2%, 18.7%, 25.3%, and 36.8%, respectively. Notably, Tanh exhibits the largest relative improvement over its QAT baseline. These findings establish noise-aware fine-tuning as an effective primitive for low bit RRAM CIM across the four activations and bit widths tested on this hardware platform, toward future space-borne edge systems.
items.venue: ITU Journal on Future and Evolving Technologies

items.title: N-bit ferroelectric tunnel junctions via all‑van‑der‑Waals stacking
items.abstract: Abstract We present a scalable design for multi-bit ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) by vertically stacking N van der Waals (vdW) ferroelectric layers. Crucially, despite the inherent challenges of interlayer coupling in such heterostacks, the weak vdW interactions are shown to preserve the independent switching of each layer, yielding 2N physically stable resistance states and achieving an exponential scaling of information density. We demonstrate this concept in a five-layer stack of lattice-matched vdW ferroelectrics. First-principles calculations confirm 32 stable polarization states, and quantum transport simulations resolve all 32 distinct resistance levels. Weak interlayer coupling preserves all polarization configurations, while built-in electrostatic asymmetry generates a giant tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio exceeding 105 without asymmetric metal electrodes. Beyond the specific materials modeled here, our framework is directly applicable to any vdW ferroelectric stack. Once the layer-resolved coercive fields are experimentally calibrated, the same recursive switching rule governs all resistance-state transitions, making this design principle universal for arbitrary N-bit FTJs. This study establishes a scalable all-vdW platform for ultracompact multi-state memory, where information capacity scales exponentially with layer number.

items.title: Memory in Behavioral Models as Motion on a Slow Invariant Manifold
items.abstract: A single-tone large-signal operating point of a nonlinear two-port is a periodic orbit of a periodically forced circuit. When the device has memory, the Floquet exponents of that orbit separate into fast (electrical) and slow (thermal and trapping) modes, and long-term memory is motion on the invariant manifold attached to the slow modes. Existence and uniqueness of that manifold follow from the parameterization method of Cabr\'e, Fontich and de la Llave, applied to the stroboscopic map at the orbit; the manifold is the spectral submanifold of Haller and Ponsioen, without a small-forcing parameter. The manifold is a bundle over the circle of drive phase, its fiber dimension the number of slow exponents, and the dynamic X-parameter kernel of Verspecht et al. identifies its reduced dynamics from the transient after a step in drive amplitude. An exact reduced model has one memory state per slow exponent, the memoryless X-parameter surface is the fixed-point family of the reduced dynamics, and the envelope-domain model is the reduced dynamics driven by the envelope. The hypotheses are verified and the manifold constructed for a GaN HEMT compact model with thermal and trap memory: the trap's time constant at the operating point, $14 \mu$s, is set by the linearization, not by its $6$ ms emission time, and the trap's nonlinearity confines a polynomial representation of the manifold to a few millivolts of drive, so trap memory must be represented over the operating range, by tables or a fitted network, not by an expansion about the operating point.

items.title: Investigation of LVI Application for Nanosheet Devices
items.abstract: Abstract Laser Voltage Imaging (LVI), also known as Electro Optic Frequency Mapping (EOFM), maps transistor switching activity at a selected frequency within a device under test (DUT). It can trace periodic signal propagation through circuits such as scan chains or any logic that can be driven with a toggled input. LVI works by scanning a laser across the DUT and detecting electro optic modulation of the reflected beam caused by space charge region changes near drains and/or free carrier density variations in channels. LVI has become a workhorse for fault isolation in planar and FinFET technologies. For Nanosheet devices, however, the gate all around (GAA) architecture—with high k/metal gate (HKMG) wrapping the channel and vertically stacked sheets at different focal planes, poses new challenges. This work has investigated LVI applicability on 2 nm Nanosheet devices across several circuit types and demonstrates that LVI remains viable, provided experimental parameters are carefully optimized. The dominant parameters affecting the LVI signal to noise ratio have also been discussed.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Implementation of Filter Structures in VLF Band for Remote Sensing Systems Using MCFOA
items.abstract: This paper presents analogue current-mode filter circuits for the very low frequency (VLF) band (3–30 kHz), intended for remote sensing applications. The proposed designs include first-order low-pass, high-pass, and all-pass filters, together with a single-input, three-output universal filter providing simultaneous low-pass, high-pass, and all-pass responses. Each structure employs a single modified current feedback operational amplifier (MCFOA) and only four grounded passive components, enabling a simple and compact implementation. Designed at a cut-off frequency of 10 kHz, the filters achieve a total harmonic distortion (THD) of ≤1.5%, a dynamic range (DR) greater than 60 dB, and power consumption below 1 mW with a 2.5 V single supply. Frequency and gain can be adjusted through passive component selection. Moreover, the use of a 100 pF capacitance supports VLSI and low-voltage/low-power implementations. The proposed circuits are verified through PSpice simulations.
items.venue: Celal Bayar Universitesi Fen Bilimleri Dergisi

items.title: Impact of Proton Irradiation on the TDDB Reliability of SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Abstract The present work aims to evaluate the impact of 200 MeV proton irradiation on Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown in SiC MOSFETs using Constant Voltage Stress (CVS) measurements. After proton irradiation, commercial SiC MOSFET devices were classified based on the occurrence of catastrophic Single-Event Burnout (SEB). Constant Voltage Stress (CVS) measurements were then employed to evaluate the Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) characteristics of the surviving population. A comparison between the electrical behavior of radiation-induced failures and TDDB of irradiated but survived devices, is proposed.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: High Energy-Storage Density in Ferroelectric La:HfO2-Based Thin-Film Capacitors
items.abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric and antiferroelectric hafnium and zirconium oxides have attracted considerable attention for the development of next-generation energy-storage capacitors owing to their high energy-storage density (ESD), high power density, moderately high efficiency (η), and scalability down to the ultrathin limit. Most research on dielectric energy-storage capacitors focuses on antiferroelectric hafnium oxide- and zirconium oxide-based capacitors, while ferroelectric hafnium oxide-based capacitors have been less extensively investigated. This work highlights the enhancement of the energy-storage characteristics of epitaxial ferroelectric orthorhombic lanthanum-doped hafnium oxide-based two-dimensional capacitors by introducing a thin dielectric amorphous alumina capping layer. It is revealed that the inclusion of a dielectric layer influences both the ESD and η of the fabricated capacitors due to the increased depolarization effect resulting from the presence of the alumina layer. The best balance between ESD and η is achieved through the insertion of a 2.3 nm-thick alumina layer, providing an ultra-high ESD of 142 J/cm3, with an η of 69% for an electric field of 7.7 MV/cm. Additionally, the capacitor displays an ESD greater than 120 J/cm3 after 106 cycles and a stable performance up to 120 °C. Therefore, this work foresees the potential of ferroelectric epitaxial hafnium oxide-based capacitors in energy-storage technologies.

items.title: Ge Composition Modulation of NBTI-TID Coupling Effects in Strained SiGe PMOSFETs
items.abstract: In this paper, TCAD simulation is adopted to investigate the coupling degradation mechanism between Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) and Total Ionizing Dose (TID) in strained SiGe PMOS field-effect transistors. By adjusting the germanium (Ge) composition, the coupling damage is suppressed, which provides a theoretical basis for the design of radiation-hardened and high-reliability devices. The data respectively illustrate the introduction of stress and its influence on the electrical properties of devices. Under Negative Bias Temperature (NBT) stress, both elevated temperature and increased gate voltage aggravate the generation of interface trap charges, thereby worsening the degradation of threshold voltage shift. The effects of total ionizing dose on devices and the coupling effects of NBTI and TID under different stress sequences are also analyzed. Finally, it is found that increasing the Ge content can effectively suppress the synergistic coupling degradation induced by NBTI and TID.

items.title: Failure Analysis Methods to Localize Defects in Data Path on 3D Flash Memory Products
items.abstract: Abstract For 3D Flash memory products, competitiveness depends not only on die size but also on how quickly data can be programmed into and read from the memory cells. Achieving high performance requires minimizing delay throughout the entire data path— from the I/O interface, through buffers and sense amplifiers, to the memory array itself. As data-path speeds continue to increase, failure analysis of the associated circuits becomes increasingly challenging. In this paper, we examine several analytical techniques used to identify root-cause defects within the NAND data path.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: FROM PMOS TO CFET: A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF MOSFET-BASED DEVICE ARCHITECTURES FOR NEXT-GENERATION VLSI SYSTEMS
items.abstract: The relentless drive toward transistor miniaturization that has sustained Moore's Law for over five decades has forced the semiconductor industry through a succession of device-architecture transitions, each addressing the electrostatic and parasitic limitations of its predecessor. This paper presents a systematic review and comparative analysis of MOSFET-based device architectures spanning the foundational planar PMOS/NMOS transistor and complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) circuit, the FinFET/tri-gate transition commercialized in 2011, gate-all-around (GAA) nanowire and Nano sheet field-effect transistors now in high-volume manufacturing, the fork sheet architecture, and the emerging complementary FET (CFET). Technical literature and primary industry disclosures from IEEE Xplore, arXiv, and semiconductor foundries and research consortia (imec, Intel, TSMC, Samsung) covering 2011–2026 were reviewed and synthesized using a PRISMA-inspired methodology adapted for engineering and technology sources. Each architecture is evaluated against a consistent set of criteria: gate electrostatic control, short-channel-effect suppression, area and density scaling, power–performance trade-offs, and manufacturing readiness, and the findings are consolidated into a comparative summary table. The review finds that GAA nanosheet transistors have now entered high-volume production across three major foundries, while the CFET architecture — in which n-type and p-type devices are stacked vertically — is positioned as the leading contender to extend logic scaling into the sub-1 nm regime, contingent on resolving wafer-bonding, contact-yield, and thermal-crosstalk challenges. The paper concludes with an assessment of open research gaps and beyond-CFET directions, including two-dimensional channel materials and monolithic three-dimensional integration.
items.venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

items.title: Engineering Grain Boundary Commensurability for Ferroelectric Stabilization in Hafnia-Based Films
items.abstract: Grain boundaries fundamentally dictate the macroscopic properties of polycrystalline materials by breaking long-range symmetry. In ferroelectrics, these structural discontinuities are conventionally considered as detrimental features that induce depolarization fields and accumulate defects, thereby suppressing or pinning local polarization. Here, we demonstrate that the commensurability of grain boundaries inherently governs the polar-orthorhombic phase stability in polycrystalline Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) thin films. Using depth-resolved multislice electron ptychography, we map the three-dimensional (3D) phase distribution across diverse boundaries with atomic resolution, revealing that highly commensurate grain boundaries effectively suppress the nonpolar-tetragonal phase by compensating for lattice mismatch while mitigating geometric frustration. Monte Carlo simulations uncover the atomistic and energetic origins of polar-phase stabilization, showing that commensurate grain boundaries favor the polar-orthorhombic phase more strongly than other grain boundaries. Guided by this principle, we epitaxially engineer HZO thin films to promote the preferential formation of commensurate grain boundaries, resulting in an approximately 60% enhancement in the remanent polarization of ferroelectric devices. These findings provide direct 3D experimental and theoretical evidence that establishes grain boundary commensurability as a critical degree of freedom for designing functional interfaces, guiding the construction of novel ceramics and polycrystalline ferroelectrics.

items.title: Energy-Optimized Multiplier-Less FIR Filter for Reconfigurable Biomedical Systems
items.abstract: Low-power reconfigurable finite impulse response (RFIR) filters are important in portable biomedical signal-processing systems, where area, power consumption, and timing overhead must be minimized. This paper presents a multiplier-less RFIR filter architecture based on shared input decoding and coefficient multiplication block (CMB)- based shift-add realization. In the proposed architecture, the input sample is decoded into selection, shift, sign, and nonzero control signals, and coefficient multiplication is performed using multiplexer-assisted shift-add operations instead of conventional multipliers. This reduces redundant decoding hardware, arithmetic complexity, and switching activity in the product-generation stage. The architecture is implemented in Verilog HDL and synthesized using Synopsys Design Compiler with the SAED 32 nm standard-cell library. For 32-tap and 64-tap RFIR implementations, the proposed design achieves up to 85.19% reduction in area-delay product (ADP) and up to 82.64% reduction in powerdelay product (PDP) compared with selected existing programmable FIR filter architectures. Standard FIR benchmark filters are also evaluated to verify the behavior of the proposed architecture across different coefficient sets and tap lengths, where ADP and PDP reductions of up to 62.40% and 59.51%, respectively, are obtained. The reduced PDP values indicate improved energy-oriented performance under the same synthesis conditions. An ECG denoising case study is included to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed RFIR architecture for biomedical signal-processing applications.
items.venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers

items.title: Diëlektrische betrouwbaarheid van Al:HfO MIM ontkoppelingscondensatoren in de BEOL
items.abstract: In advanced integrated circuits, continued interconnect scaling has made stable power delivery a critical challenge. In particular, the reduced interconnect pitches and increased routing complexity amplify fluctuations in the supply voltage and high-frequency noise. The relocation of the power delivery network to the backside of the wafer (back-side power delivery network, BSPDN) is a promising approach to alleviate these limitations. In this context, metal-insulator-metal (MIM) decoupling capacitors are essential to stabilize the power supply and suppress noise induced by transistor switching. While shrinking the area dedicated to the capacitors is necessary to keep up with the continuous device down-scaling, maintaining high capacitance densities remains crucial for the decoupling performance. HfO2 is widely employed for decoupling capacitors due to its favorable balance between high permittivity, chemical stability, bandgap, and band offset. Doping HfO2 with elements such as Al allows tuning of its structural and electronic properties, thereby directly affecting the leakage behavior and reliability. In this study, the structural analysis of the dielectrics reveals partial crystallinity of 20 nm thick HfO2 films with low Al concentrations, while they remain amorphous at higher Al concentrations. Higher permittivity values are found for partially crystalline HfO2, although this phase is also prone to increased leakage currents due to grain boundaries. While grain-boundary-assisted leakage can be suppressed in amorphous dielectrics, this comes at the expense of a reduced permittivity, thereby limiting the decoupling performance. Furthermore, scaling toward thinner dielectric layers can introduce reliability challenges, such as time-dependent dielectric breakdown (TDDB). Dielectric breakdown is a reliability issue that has been studied by academia and industry for more than 60 years. Despite extensive research, a unified understanding linking defect generation, charge transport mechanisms, and the breakdown behavior in high-k dielectrics is still lacking. A fundamental investigation of the degradation processes is therefore essential for the reliable integration of Al:HfO2 dielectrics in emerging 3D technologies. This PhD work aims to investigate the degradation mechanisms in Al-doped HfO2 thin films integrated in MIM capacitors through a combination of experimental reliability studies and physics-based modeling. First, the structural and electronic properties of the Al:HfO2 dielectrics are characterized, including the extraction of pre-existing trap concentrations. The concentration of trapped electrons in the studied Al:HfO2 dielectrics are found to be largely independent of the Al-doping concentration, suggesting that the traps are intrinsic to the HfO2-matrix. Second, a time-zero conduction model is developed to characterize the dominant conduction mechanisms over a wide temperature range (77 K to 448 K) and electric field range (up to 10 MV/cm). Uniform trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) is employed at elevated temperatures, while the transport mechanisms shift from thermally activated TAT to electron-tunneling processes below room temperature. It was further found that the fundamental conduction mechanisms in Al:HfO2 are independent of the Al-doping concentration. The framework is extended to model the stressed-induced leakage current (SILC) in degraded dielectrics, revealing distinct conduction regimes for amorphous and partially crystalline Al:HfO2 dielectrics. The conduction mechanisms are associated with (quasi-)uniform TAT due to trap clustering and filamentary conduction, respectively. Finally, the impact of the conduction and degradation mechanisms on the dielectric breakdown characteristics is analyzed. The activation energies extracted from temperature-dependent TDDB measurements indicate that the breakdown characteristics are consistent with the generation of oxygen vacancy-interstitial defect pairs (so-called Frenkel pairs) and Hf-O bond weakening due to electron trapping after injection from the electrode into the oxide. It is shown that partially crystalline films exhibit reduced lifetimes compared to amorphous Al:HfO2 dielectrics, which is likely associated with enhanced defect concentrations and conductive filament formation at grain boundaries. Overall, this dissertation establishes comprehensive relationships between the structural properties of the dielectrics, the dominant conduction and degradation mechanisms, and the breakdown characteristics.

items.title: Determining Optimal FIB Access Points Using DFT-Guided Simulation Data
items.abstract: Abstract The adoption of backside power delivery (BPD) for advanced semiconductor integrated circuit (IC) chips introduces significant electrical fault isolation (EFI) challenges. The lack of direct optical access to the device's FET layer severely impacts techniques such as laser voltage probing and imaging (collectively, LVX), photon emission microscopy (PEM), and dynamic and static laser stimulation (DLS, SLS). Electron beam probing (EBP) is actively being developed to replace LVX for BPD ICs. It offers a small spot size, narrow probe geometry, long working distance, and, crucially, the ability to measure voltage signals from both nets and cells. EBP, however, requires direct line of sight access to any nets/cells of interest, so its usefulness is heavily dependent on the ability to reach those nets/cells using focused ion beam (FIB) created holes. Most high-performance compute ICs will have more than 10 frontside metal layers. With local routing confined to the lowermost levels, reaching most signals of interest will be difficult. As a result, EBP on BPD ICs will require careful planning and searching for the best locations to create FIB access holes. In this work, we present a novel methodology that leverages design for test (DFT) data and simulation to identify optimal frontside FIB access points. Locations with access unobstructed by signal nets are preferred, but rare, with <20% for the designs that were analyzed thus far. The main new development in this work is the capability of differentiating between relevant nets for the test in question vs. nets that can be safely removed while maintaining the ability to stimulate the faulty logic for EBP. This increases the chances for FIB access upto 45%. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed technique for enabling scalable and practical EBP in the era of BPD.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Reliability Assessment Methodology for Total Ionizing Dose Effects in FDSOI MOSFETs
items.abstract: This work investigates the effects of total ionizing dose (TID) on 22 nm FDSOI MOSFET devices through combined technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations and actual TID irradiation experiments, establishing a comprehensive dataset of radiation-induced degradation characteristics. By utilizing both simulated and experimental radiation data as training foundations, this research developed and optimized a deep neural network (DNN) capable of conducting efficient and accurate reliability analysis of TID effects under various radiation conditions, with demonstrated effectiveness in predicting device performance degradation across different TID ranges. The methodology integrates physical simulations with deep learning approaches, where TCAD simulations and irradiation experiments capture fundamental device physics under radiation exposure, while the DNN enables rapid performance prediction. The resulting framework achieves superior prediction accuracy while significantly reducing computational costs compared to conventional simulation methods, providing a powerful solution for evaluating electronic device reliability in complex radiation environments.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based ROI Alignment for Automated SEM Workflows
items.abstract: Abstract Over the past several years, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) based automated acquisition workflows have been widely used in semiconductor analysis to rapidly inspect fine patterns and defects in advanced memory and non-memory devices. In particular, during repetitive high-magnification imaging across multilayer structures, pattern alignment that stably maintains the region of interest (ROI) is a critical factor governing metrology reliability and throughput. However, most automated SEM workflows rely on rule-based methods such as intensity-profile peak finders or template matching, whose fixed configuration cannot accommodate the full diversity of imaging conditions. This imposes two coupled costs that grow as conditions diversify: the lower success rate forces repeated reacquisition that consumes instrument time, while restoring accuracy requires repeated manual re-tuning that consumes operator time. In this study, a deep learning ROI recognition framework based on a one-stage object detection model and a semantic segmentation model was evaluated within the Thermo Fisher iFast automation workflow for a NAND SEM workflow, and was compared with a conventional rule-based edge-finder baseline (intensity-profile peak detection) under the same Test-set and operational-specification conditions. The evaluation tasks consisted of (i) word-line (WL) nitride-layer-band alignment and (ii) channel-hole (CH) centering using adjacent word-line-cut patterns as recognition references. Approximately 200 SEM images were collected per task, and evaluation was performed on a fixed Test set of 30 images while varying training-set size (N_train) from 10 to 136 (step 10). On the 30-image Test set, both deep learning models substantially improved operational metrics over the edge-finder baseline (WL: success rate 74.8% → 98.1-99.4%, F1 72.5% → 98.7-99.7%; CH: success rate/F1 100%, FP/FN = 0). Together with single-image end-to-end inference latency below 20 ms for both models, these results confirm that both models provide alignment reliability and real-time feasibility sufficient for deployment in automation workflows.
items.venue: Proceedings - International Symposium for Testing and Failure Analysis

items.title: Current Status and Challenges of Defense Semiconductor Test and Evaluation Standards: Focusing on the Linkage of Defense Testing and Qualification to Measurement Quality
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between common test standards and technology-specific testing and measurement in defense semiconductor testing and verification, and examines the need for linkage between defense qualification and measurement-quality functions. Academic literature, military standards, international standards, and guidance on testing, calibration, accreditation, and metrology were reviewed through literature and institutional analysis. Reliability and lifetime evaluation of gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) and high-frequency performance measurement of GaN radio-frequency (RF) devices and monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) were examined as technical cases. Institutional analysis examined qualification and Laboratory Suitability practices of the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) and Defense Logistics Agency (DLA), together with the ISO/IEC 17025-based Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme (KOLAS) and related measurement-quality guidance. The case analysis shows that common test standards provide a baseline for consistent application of test items and procedures, but additional technology-specific conditions also require consideration. For GaN HEMT lifetime evaluation, relevant conditions include actual RF operating conditions, channel-temperature measurement methods, thermal paths involving packages, mounting, and fixtures, and failure criteria. For high-frequency measurement of GaN RF devices and MMICs, reference planes, calibration methods, test configurations including probes, mounting, grounding, and biasing, and measurement uncertainty can affect the consistency and comparability of results. Taken together, the findings indicate that functions for specifying technology-appropriate test conditions and acceptance criteria and functions for supporting the reliability of measurement results serve different purposes but need to be used together in actual testing processes. Therefore, improving the reliability of defense semiconductor testing and verification requires an approach that retains common test standards, specifies technology-specific testing and measurement conditions requiring additional control, and links the test capabilities needed to implement those conditions with measurement-quality functions.
items.venue: Society for Standards Certification and Safety

items.title: Characterizing High Bandwidth Flash for LLM Serving
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving requires substantial memory to store model weights and KV caches. As models grow larger and contexts become longer, memory capacity and bandwidth increasingly become bottlenecks for serving performance. Agentic workloads compound this pressure through repeated interactions over growing contexts, making it increasingly important to retain KV state for reuse. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers a way to expand accelerator memory capacity for large language model (LLM) serving, but its access costs and limited write endurance complicate its use. We evaluate HBF for high-throughput agentic serving across system design and scheduling choices to understand when additional capacity improves serving performance and energy efficiency. We introduce an HBM-HBF-host hierarchical storage system and buffered cache-aware scheduling, and use trace-driven simulations to analyze their effects on performance, energy consumption, and HBF write lifetime. Across the evaluated workloads, the fastest HBF-augmented systems reduce completion time by 36.1-87.7% relative to HBM-only systems. Modeled energy savings reach 59.1%, with benefits depending on the workload and weight placement. Buffered cache-aware scheduling extends estimated HBF write lifetime from 1.21 to 14.82 years in the evaluated configuration. These results demonstrate the importance of coordinating data placement and scheduling to improve serving efficiency while sustaining a practical HBF write lifetime.

items.title: Bridging a Gap between Physical and Electrical Failure Analysis: Fault Localization on TEM Lamellae Enabled by Workflow Redesign and optional Probing Pads
items.abstract: Abstract As FinFET and Gate-All-Around devices grow more three-dimensional, the gap between electrical and physical failure analysis is widening. Defects such as fin nano-cracks, dopant variations, interface traps, and resistive anomalies may show clear electrical signatures yet elude conventional TEM workflows. Once a TEM lamella is extracted, electrical access is lost, leaving analysts reliant on diffraction, material contrast, and spectroscopy, often in a different plane than the electrical evidence. This paper presents a TEM preparation method that preserves electrical access to planar-view and cross-section lamellae. Replacing the initial conductive deposition with an insulating dielectric keeps selected areas electrically isolated after lift-out; the standard protective layer is applied on top. Full device-level measurements are then possible on the lamella, optionally via FIB-fabricated probe pads for out-of-plane terminals. The approach supports high-precision endpointing and integrates nanoprobing, e-beam localization, and TEM analysis within a single sample. Case studies demonstrate planar-view defect localization, cross-section P-N junction mapping, and full device characterization. Probe-pad series resistance and Ga-FIB implantation, which can increase leakage, must be accounted for. The method links electrical and physical analyses in a semi-reversible manner and provides a localization pathway for backside power delivery and 3D-stacked devices, where optical fault isolation lacks line of sight.

items.title: Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition for Next-Generation Semiconductor Processing: Mechanisms of Selectivity Breakdown and Process Integration Strategies
items.abstract: As device miniaturization and three-dimensional integration progress, thin-film processes for semiconductor devices increasingly require atomic-level control not only of thickness and composition but also of growth location. Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) is a bottom-up process that exploits differences in surface reactivity between growth and non-growth areas to form thin films only at the intended locations. Because it enables self-aligned patterning and can reduce subsequent etching steps, AS-ALD has drawn attention as a candidate technology for next-generation semiconductor manufacturing. However, the high initial selectivity obtained on planar substrates is not always retained on real patterned or high-aspect-ratio structures. This review examines the process applicability of AS-ALD based on studies published through 2026, focusing on the selectivity window, the maximum selectively deposited thickness, the nucleation density in the non-growth area, and the preservation of pattern shape. Across the literature, the turning point of selectivity breakdown converges on the moment at which the first stable nucleus forms in the non-growth area. Residual surface defects and pinholes in the inhibition layer, together with precursor physisorption, penetration, thermal degradation, and lateral diffusion, all act to bring this transition forward in time. Molecular design strategies (inherent selectivity, self-assembled monolayers, small-molecule inhibitors, surface pretreatment, and combined precursor-inhibitor design) and process control strategies (inhibitor regeneration, ALD/ALE supercycles, and reactor control) are compared according to which stage of the nucleation pathway they intervene in. Pattern- or device-level demonstrations have accumulated for back-end-of-line interconnects and resistive random-access memory, whereas for DRAM, 3D NAND, and gate-all-around transistors most of the evidence remains at the level of material and process concepts. The performance of AS-ALD is difficult to judge from the initial selectivity value alone; a more direct criterion is whether the selectivity window-defined with respect to the target thickness and the tolerable defect level of the actual device structure-can be secured.

items.title: Area Scaling of Nanosecond Switching Delay in HZO Capacitors with an Ultrathin ZrO2 Interlayer
items.abstract: Interfacial engineering can modify the electrical response of hafnium zirconium oxide capacitors, but separating polarization dynamics from circuit charging remains essential. We compare approximately 10 nm thick Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) capacitors with otherwise identical capacitors containing an additional approximately 1 nm thick ZrO2 bottom interlayer (hereafter HZO–ZrO2 capacitors). Polarization–voltage measurements, cross-sectional scanning transmission electron microscopy, capacitance–voltage characterization, and switching/non-switching pulse measurements were combined across electrode areas of 25–10,000 μm2. Both stacks exhibit ferroelectric hysteresis and butterfly-shaped capacitance curves. At 2.5 V and 100 kHz, the HZO–ZrO2 capacitors have 10–15% higher capacitance. Their measured switching-onset delays are nevertheless lower at areas ≥ 400 μm2: 2.1, 5.6, and 23.0 ns at 400, 2500, and 10,000 μm2, compared with 3.2, 7.7, and 30.9 ns for HZO; the largest relative reduction is 34.4%, observed at 400 μm2, where the delay decreases from 3.2 ns to 2.1 ns. At 25 and 100 μm2, the measured differences (0.1 ns) are within the ≈0.1 ns timing resolution of the single-record measurement and are reported as descriptive values.
